Job Description:
About the Role
We are seeking a highly motivated and results-oriented Advocate to join our growing legal practice. The successful candidate will be responsible for handling a diverse portfolio of legal matters, providing strategic legal advice, representing clients in various forums, and contributing to the firm's commitment to delivering exceptional legal services.
Key Responsibilities
Represent clients in courts, tribunals, and other legal proceedings.
Draft, review, and negotiate legal documents including pleadings, contracts, agreements, and legal opinions.
Provide timely and practical legal advice and develop effective legal strategies for clients.
Conduct legal research and analysis to support litigation, advisory, and transactional matters.
Prepare, organize, and manage case files to ensure efficient handling of legal matters.
Liaise and maintain professional relationships with clients, courts, government agencies, regulatory bodies, and other stakeholders.
Attend client meetings, court sessions, negotiations, and other legal engagements as required.
Ensure compliance with legal and professional standards while safeguarding clients' interests.
Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor of Laws (LL.B) degree from a recognized university.
Admission to the Roll of Advocates of the High Court of Kenya.
Possession of a valid Practicing Certificate.
Minimum of three (3) years' post-admission experience in active legal practice.
Demonstrated experience in litigation, legal advisory, and legal drafting.
Strong legal research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational and time-management abilities with keen attention to detail.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
High level of professionalism, integrity, and client-service orientation.

Job Description:
What You Can Expect:
At EABL, interns are more than observers. We are looking for curious individuals who are ready to learn, ask questions, contribute ideas, and gain practical experience in a fast-paced environment.
During your internship, you will have the opportunity to:
Gain hands-on experience working on real business projects.
Learn from experienced professionals and leaders across the organisation.
Develop practical skills that complement your academic learning.
Build your professional network and workplace confidence.
To apply for the internship program:
Only students in their 3rd year or final year of study are eligible to apply. Applicants should intend to continue their education upon completion of the internship or be awaiting graduation. Candidates who completed their studies more than 12 months ago are unfortunately not eligible for this programme.
Be enrolled in a public or accredited private academic institution pursuing a Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification.
You must be on break/ holiday from school during the internship period.
What you will need:
A successful intern has a desire to gain professional experience and is exceptionally eager to learn and explore possibilities.
Strong listening skills are also required to perform this role.
Oral and written communication skills, the ability to understand instructions, as well as not being afraid to ask questions will ensure a productive internship.
Excellent knowledge in use of Microsoft applications is needed.
Very articulate with fluent English.
Patient, attention to detail, fast learner, committed, able to understand directions, can work quickly and accurately under pressure.
Keen to learn about the markets and also with a high attention to detail and pride in their work at this initial stage of their career development.
A dedication to completing the 3 months internship program.
Mandatory Requirements:
Letter from your institution indicating you are a student there and/or require internship as part of requirement for course completion.
Personal Accident insurance cover for the duration of the internship.
Bank account details.
Copy of National Identity Card.
Copy of KRA Pin Certificate
NSSF and SHA numbers.

Job Description:
Job Summary
NestVest is a property investment platform helping local and diaspora investors in Kenya make smarter real estate decisions through curated investment properties, mortgage affordability tools, area rankings and market insights. We are looking for an experienced Real Estate Sales Manager to lead and grow our sales team in Nairobi.
You will be responsible for building a high-performing sales team, driving lead-to-deal conversion, setting sales targets, and ensuring our sales processes align with our data-driven property platform. This is a hands-on leadership role — you will coach, motivate and manage the team while also closing deals when required.
Key Responsibilities
Team Leadership & Management
Recruit, train and manage a team of property sales consultants
Set individual and team sales targets (viewings, offers, deals)
Run daily/weekly sales stand-ups, pipeline reviews and performance coaching
Build a performance culture with clear KPIs, incentives and accountability
Sales Process & Conversion
Own the full sales funnel: lead → consultation → viewing → offer → deal
Work closely with the Growth and Marketing teams to ensure leads are followed up within 24 hours
Monitor and improve conversion rates at every stage of the funnel
Ensure CRM discipline: accurate records, follow-ups and reporting
Market & Product Knowledge
Deep understanding of Nairobi property market (Kilimani, Westlands, Lavington and investment hotspots)
Knowledge of mortgage, off-plan, and diaspora investment sales
Use NestVest data tools (area rankings, affordability calculator) to support clients' decisions
Reporting & Strategy
Prepare weekly/monthly sales reports for management
Analyse team performance and identify training needs
Feed market intelligence back to the product and marketing teams
Qualifications & Requirements
Must-have:
3+ years of real estate sales experience in Kenya, with at least 1–2 years in a sales leadership/management role
Proven track record of meeting and exceeding sales targets
Strong coaching, motivation and team management skills
Excellent English communication (written and spoken); Kiswahili is an advantage
Customer-focused, resilient and self-driven
Proficiency with CRM tools and basic reporting (Excel/Google Sheets)
Nice-to-have:
Experience selling to diaspora and international investors
Knowledge of mortgage/financing processes in Kenya
Experience with off-plan/new development projects
Valid PSV/land-buying agent certifications or estate agency experience
Personal qualities we value:
Punctual, reliable and professional
Honest with strong ethics — we never tolerate misrepresentation of properties
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, data-driven startup environment
What We Offer
Competitive salary + strong commission structure
Opportunity to build and lead a growing team
Training and development support
A modern office in Kilimani, Nairobi

Job Title: Customer Success Representative – Interior Design & Construction
Job Description:
Salary: KES 50,000–60,000 per month, depending on experience and capability
Valentori Group is seeking a mature, confident and highly organized
Customer Success Representative
to take ownership of the client experience throughout the project journey.
This is more than a customer-care role. The successful candidate will become the client's
primary coordination point from the moment a site visit is paid for through design, planning, execution, snagging and final project handover
.
We are looking for someone who can keep clients informed, coordinate internal teams, anticipate concerns, solve problems and ensure that commitments, approvals and project decisions do not fall through the cracks.
The Role
Once a client enters our project process, you will help ensure that they experience a
professional, organized and well-communicated journey
.
You will coordinate closely with
Sales, Interior Design, Quantity Surveying, Project Management, Procurement and Site Teams
, while maintaining clear and professional communication with the client.
You will not replace the Project Manager or technical teams. Your responsibility is to
own the customer journey and ensure information flows effectively between the client and the people responsible for delivery.
Key Responsibilities
Take over client coordination once a
site visit has been confirmed and paid for
.
Coordinate site-visit scheduling and ensure clients understand the next steps.
Maintain consistent communication with clients throughout design, quotation, approvals, execution and handover.
Coordinate communication between clients and
Sales, Design, QS, Procurement and Project Management teams
.
Track client decisions, selections, approvals, variations and outstanding requirements.
Ensure commitments made to clients are properly documented and communicated to the responsible team.
Provide clients with timely, accurate project updates rather than waiting for them to request information.
Follow up internally on outstanding actions affecting the client's project.
Identify potential client concerns early and coordinate resolution before they escalate.
Manage complaints professionally and remain composed in difficult conversations.
Attend project sites when necessary to understand issues, meet clients and support resolution.
Coordinate snagging, client feedback, project handover and post-handover follow-up.
Maintain accurate client records, communication history, approvals and follow-up actions in the company's designated systems.
Identify opportunities for additional services, referrals and repeat business without compromising the customer relationship.
Collect structured client feedback and help management identify recurring service-delivery weaknesses.
What We Are Looking For
The successful candidate should demonstrate:
Exceptional communication skills
– Able to communicate confidently and professionally with homeowners, developers, consultants, contractors, fundis and internal teams.
Excellent English and Kiswahili
– Strong spoken and written communication in both languages is required.
Strong organization and follow-through
– Able to manage multiple clients, deadlines, meetings, approvals and outstanding actions without losing track of commitments.
Exceptional problem-solving ability
– We need someone who does not merely forward problems. You should be able to understand an issue, establish the facts, coordinate the appropriate people and actively drive it toward resolution.
Composure under pressure
– Construction and renovation projects can involve delays, changes, complaints and unexpected site conditions. You must remain professional, objective and solution-oriented.
Proactive communication
– Clients should not consistently have to chase the company for information. You should anticipate the information they require and communicate early.
Strong ownership mentality
– Once an issue enters your responsibility, you should follow it through to closure rather than assuming that forwarding it to another department completes your responsibility.
Good judgement and emotional intelligence
– Ability to distinguish between matters you can resolve, matters requiring technical input and matters that should be escalated to management.
Commercial awareness
– Understand that excellent customer experience should contribute to client retention, referrals, repeat business, additional sales and protection of the company's reputation.
Industry Knowledge
Previous experience in
interior design, construction, renovations, fit-outs, property development, architecture, cabinetry or a related built-environment business
will be strongly preferred.
The ideal candidate should understand, or be capable of quickly understanding, concepts such as:
Site measurements
Design approvals
BOQs
Material selections
Variations
Project schedules
Procurement
Installation
Snagging
Practical completion
Handover
You do not need to be the technical designer or Project Manager, but you must understand projects well enough to
communicate intelligently with both clients and technical teams.
Personal Attributes
We are particularly interested in someone who is:
Mature
Confident
Presentable
Highly organized
Proactive
Calm under pressure
Accountable
Persuasive
Detail-oriented
Sales-driven
Collaborative
Solution-oriented
You must be a genuine
team player
capable of coordinating different departments without creating unnecessary conflict or confusion.
The successful candidate must also be
willing and able to travel to project sites
as required.
How Success Will Be Measured
This role will ultimately be measured by outcomes such as
timeliness and consistency of client updates, closure of client concerns, documentation of approvals and decisions, reduction in avoidable escalations, client satisfaction, successful handovers, referrals, repeat business and opportunities converted into additional revenue.

Job Title: Human Resources and Organizational Development Officer
Job Description:
Job Summary
The Human Resources and Organizational Development Officer (HROD Officer) provides operational and administrative support to the Human Resources and Organizational Development function at AAIK. The role supports the implementation of HR policies, procedures and people processes across the employee lifecycle and provides timely HR services to staff and management. The role maintains accurate personnel records and HRIS entries and supports recruitment, onboarding, performance management, learning and development, employee benefits, staff welfare and separation processes. The role works under the guidance of the HROD Manager and ensures that HR activities are implemented in accordance with the AAIK Human Resources Manual and applicable employment legislation in Kenya.
Supervisory Responsibilities
None. The role may coordinate activities with staff, service providers and other stakeholders as delegated by the HROD Manager.
Duties/ Responsibilities
Human Resources and Organizational Development
Support the implementation of key Human Resource (HR) and Organizational Development (OD) activities, ensuring that AAIK complies with internal HR policies and procedures and relevant employment laws and regulations, including but not limited to:
Supporting the employee life cycle within AAIK, including recruitment and induction, work permits, pay and benefits, performance management, employee wellbeing, retention and separation.
Maintaining accurate and confidential personnel records, HR files and HRIS entries and ensuring that employee information is updated promptly.
Supporting recruitment processes, including vacancy documentation, interview coordination, reference checks, pre-employment documentation and onboarding arrangements.
Supporting the administration of probation, confirmation, contract renewals, transfers and other employee lifecycle processes.
Supporting the annual performance management cycle, including communication of timelines, documentation, tracking and follow-up.
Supporting staff learning and development initiatives, including training coordination, attendance records and evaluation.
Providing accurate and timely HR information required for payroll processing and supporting administration of employee benefits, insurance and staff welfare schemes.
Responding to routine employee HR requests and enquiries in a timely and professional manner and escalating complex or sensitive matters to the HROD Manager.
Supporting HR compliance activities, including maintenance of compliance trackers and preparation of documentation for HR reviews and audits.
Supporting HR and OD projects, staff engagement activities, surveys, workshops and other people-related initiatives as delegated by the HROD Manager.
Coordinating routine communication with HR-related service providers, including insurance, medical, payroll and other providers, as delegated.
Maintaining confidentiality and appropriate handling of employee information and reporting suspected breaches of HR policy, safeguarding requirements or applicable law through the appropriate channels.
Other Duties
Support organization and coordination of relevant staff and organizational activities as assigned.
Undertake other reasonable HR/OD-related tasks assigned by the HROD Manager.
Re
quired skills/ abilities.
Good working understanding of human resource principles, practices and procedures.
Good verbal and written communication skills.
Good interpersonal, people and relationship-management skills.
Good organizational skills and attention to detail.
Good time management skills with proven ability to meet deadlines.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive employee information with discretion.
Ability to work effectively in a busy, multicultural and at times stressful environment.

Job Description:
Role Overview
The Procurement Assistant will support the Procurement and Administration function in ensuring timely, efficient, transparent, and compliant procurement and administrative processes.
The position will assist with processing procurement requests, purchase orders, invoices, supplier documentation, travel arrangements, inventory management, record keeping, and procurement reporting. Invoice Review and Verification
Review pending invoices to ensure accuracy, completeness, and availability of required supporting documentation.
Verify that goods and services have been received in accordance with approved purchase orders.
Check that prices, quantities, and other invoice details correspond with approved purchase orders and agreed terms.
Identify and follow up on discrepancies and missing documentation.
Support the timely processing of invoices and payment documentation.

Receive and process approved purchase requests from programmes and other departments.

Verify purchase order details, including specifications, quantities, prices, delivery dates, and supplier information.
Request quotations from suppliers and support the preparation of bid analyses.
Assist in obtaining and maintaining supplier documentation.

Support programme and departmental procurement requirements.

Records Management and Online Filing
Maintain accurate and complete records of invoices, purchase orders, quotations, contracts, agreements, and related correspondence.
File procurement documentation systematically in both electronic and physical filing systems.
Ensure procurement records are easily accessible for reference, reporting, and audit purposes.
Support the maintenance of an organized online filing system.
Invoice and Consultancy Trackers

Update the consultancy tracker and monitor the status of consultancy-related procurement processes.
Follow up on outstanding invoices and documentation.

Payment Processing Support

Submit complete and approved payment documentation to Finance/Accounts Payable.
Follow up on outstanding payments and discrepancies as directed.
Supplier Statement Reconciliation
Assist in reconciling supplier statements with internal procurement and payment records.
Identify discrepancies, outstanding invoices, or payment issues.
Follow up with relevant suppliers and internal teams to support resolution of discrepancies.
Maintain appropriate records of reconciliations and follow-up actions.
Travel and Administrative Support
Assist in arranging local and international flights and hotel bookings for staff, consultants, and guests.
Assist visitors to AAIK offices and provide general administrative support as required.
Support programme and departmental administrative requirements.
Assist in organizing meetings, workshops, and other activities where required.

Assist in receiving and inspecting delivered goods to confirm that they meet approved specifications and quantities.
Monitor stock levels and notify the relevant officer when supplies need replenishment.
Ensure goods and supplies are properly stored to prevent damage, loss, or deterioration.
Assist with issuing and distributing goods and maintaining appropriate records.
Conduct stock checks as required and report shortages or discrepancies.
Communicate stock shortages and replenishment requirements to the relevant team members.
Reporting and Compliance
Assist in preparing reports on pending invoices, procurement activities, payments, and outstanding issues.
Maintain accurate procurement records for reporting and audit purposes.
Ensure procurement activities are undertaken in accordance with AAIK procurement policies and procedures.
Report potential instances of non-compliance to the Procurement and Administration Coordinator.
Support implementation of corrective actions where required.

Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Purchasing and Supplies Management, or a related field.

Demonstrable experience in procurement processes, including requesting quotations, preparing purchase orders, processing invoices, and maintaining procurement records.

Knowledge or experience in fleet and facilities management is an added advantage.

Strong commitment to AAIK’s vision, mission, values, and rights-based approach.
Commitment to equal opportunity and the principles outlined in the AAIK Code of Conduct.
Strong commitment to feminist leadership principles and safeguarding, including prevention of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, child abuse, and abuse of adults at risk.
High level of integrity, dependability, confidentiality, and accountability.
Excellent planning, organization, prioritization, and time-management skills.
Strong attention to detail and ability to complete tasks accurately and within deadlines.
Good interpersonal and communication skills.
Good analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated initiative and ability to take responsibility for assigned tasks.
Ability to work effectively as part of a team and interact professionally with suppliers, staff, partners, and visitors.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Microsoft Excel, Word, and Outlook.
Ability to maintain accurate electronic records and use online filing and document-management systems.

Job Description
Reporting to the Group Chief Corporate & External Affairs Officer, the Lead Fintech Oversight & Governance is accountable for leading Safaricom’s regulatory strategy and institutional engagement framework across its digital financial services and fintech ecosystem, ensuring sustainable innovation, regulatory resilience, and long-term license to operate within an increasingly complex financial services landscape.
The role shapes and executes a forward-looking regulatory agenda covering digital payments, credit, savings, interoperability, open banking, data governance, AI-enabled financial services, and emerging fintech models. It drives proactive, structured engagement with the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) and other domestic, regional, and global financial regulators to secure timely approvals, influence policy direction, and manage systemic regulatory risk.
The role embeds regulatory foresight into product design, commercial strategy, and platform expansion by partnering closely with M-Pesa, Financial Services, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Strategy, and Innovation teams. It ensures that regulatory considerations are integrated early in innovation cycles, accelerating time-to-market while safeguarding prudential integrity and consumer protection standards. Through disciplined horizon scanning, regulatory scenario planning, and fintech intelligence capability, the role anticipates shifts in prudential regulation, financial inclusion policy, digital identity, cross-border payments, embedded finance, and platform governance. It translates early signals into structured engagement strategies that protect revenue continuity, unlock new growth opportunities, and strengthen Safaricom’s credibility as a trusted financial ecosystem player.
The Lead Fintech Oversight & Governance safeguards Safaricom’s financial services license to operate while enabling strategic growth ambitions, positioning Safaricom as a responsible fintech leader within Kenya and across its subsidiary markets.
The Lead Fintech Oversight & Governance is accountable for shaping Safaricom’s external regulatory strategy, influencing policy direction and maintaining strategic relationships with financial regulators to secure and sustain the Group’s licence to operate. The role anticipates regulatory change, secures regulatory approvals, influences policy outcomes and provides regulatory guidance to the Financial Services business and regulated subsidiaries. It does not own operational execution of regulatory requirements within Financial Services.
Therefore, the Lead Fintech Oversight & Governance is strategically accountable for:
Fintech Regulatory Strategy & Framework: Lead the development and execution of Safaricom’s end-to-end fintech regulatory strategy, ensuring alignment with commercial ambitions, evolving financial sector policy, and prudential requirements across digital financial services.
Regulatory & Central Bank Engagement: Drive structured, senior-level engagement with the Central Bank of Kenya and other financial regulators to secure approvals, shape regulatory interpretation, and proactively manage systemic regulatory risk.
License to Operate & Prudential Governance: Safeguard Safaricom’s financial services license to operate by ensuring robust compliance positioning, regulatory readiness, and alignment with consumer protection, capital, and operational risk expectations.
Fintech Policy Shaping & Industry Influence: Influence national and regional fintech policy development through evidence-based submissions, coalition building, and structured stakeholder engagement to enable innovation and financial inclusion.
Product & Innovation Regulatory Enablement: Embed regulatory foresight into product design, commercial planning, and new fintech initiatives to accelerate time-to-market while mitigating regulatory exposure.
Horizon Scanning & Regulatory Intelligence: Establish forward-looking regulatory intelligence capability to anticipate shifts in digital finance, open banking, interoperability, AI-driven services, and cross-border financial models.
Cross-Functional Regulatory Integration: Partner with M-Pesa, Financial Services, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Strategy teams to ensure regulatory considerations are integrated into enterprise decision-making and transformation initiatives.
Subsidiary Oversight, Governance & Enablement: Provide structured oversight and strategic support to subsidiaries, ensuring alignment to Group standards while enabling effective local execution within market context.
Risk, Governance & Control Ownership: Embed and maintain effective risk, governance, compliance, and control practices within the function by proactively identifying and mitigating operational, regulatory, financial, people, technology, and reputational risks. Ensure adherence to internal policies, regulatory requirements, audit actions, and enterprise governance frameworks while driving accountability, ethical practices, and a strong controls environment across all areas of responsibility.
Anchored in Safaricom’s ambition to lead Africa’s digital financial services evolution, the role ensures Safaricom engages regulators from a position of credibility, preparedness, and strategic influence, enabling growth with regulatory confidence rather than constraint.

Health and Safety

All employees have a responsibility to adhere to safety, health, and wellbeing policies, guidelines and procedures in all actions and decisions.

Develop and continuously refine Safaricom’s integrated fintech regulatory strategy aligned its ambitions and digital financial services expansion.
Define the regulatory positioning across payments, credit, savings, interoperability, open banking, embedded finance, and emerging fintech models.
Translate regulatory obligations into structured operating frameworks that enable innovation while maintaining prudential integrity.

Ensure alignment between regulatory strategy and commercial growth priorities across M-Pesa and broader DFS portfolios.

Develop policy position papers that align commercial objectives with public interest and financial inclusion goals.

Job Description:
Scope of Work:
Daily supervision, execution management, and people performance ownership for all stores, dispatch, and production operations. The Supervisor ensures that the policies, standards, and plans set by the Manager are implemented correctly, accurately, and on time every day, without exception. Beyond operational execution, the Supervisor owns the full performance cycle for all direct reports from setting KPIs and goals at the start of each cycle, through to conducting formal appraisals at the close and is personally accountable for the development, conduct, and performance of every person under direct supervision.
JOB PURPOSE
To ensure that all stores, dispatch, and production activities are executed accurately and on time through direct, hands-on supervision of the operational team, while owning the full performance management cycle for all direct reports and enforcing all stores policies and standard operating procedures across the department. The Stores Supervisor owns daily execution from morning briefing to end-of-day reporting and is personally accountable for stock removal accuracy, dispatch integrity, production quality, bin card compliance, stock take planning, sample and gifts management, SOP compliance, and the structured development, goal setting, and formal appraisal of every person under direct supervision.
MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Daily Task Assignment & Team Briefing
Receive all incoming orders each morning and assign them to the correct team members based on order priority, staff skills, and availability ensuring no team member is idle and all work is covered.
Conduct a structured morning briefing with the full team each day: communicate the day's order priorities, production jobs, any special instructions from the Manager, and safety or compliance reminders.
Prepare and issue production job cards for all conversion orders, ensuring each card specifies the correct client, product, quantity, specifications, and target completion time before the team begins.
Monitor workload throughout the day, reallocating team members when bottlenecks arise or priorities shift, ensuring all commitments remain achievable.
Stock Removal Accuracy & Dispatch Verification
Verify every order removal personally before it leaves the shelves; confirming the correct product, correct quantity, and correct variant against the authorized Delivery Note and Sales Order.
Conduct pre-dispatch verification for every outgoing order: physically counter-check items staged in the dispatch yard against the Delivery Note and Sales Invoice before authorizing loading.
Enforce the dispatch schedule: all confirmed orders must be picked, verified, and staged at least 20 minutes before the scheduled departure time.
Communicate immediately with the Stores & Logistics Manager when any order cannot be dispatched on time providing the reason and a proposed solution, not a problem alone.
Coordinate delivery routes with the Stores & Logistics Coordinator and Driver to ensure efficient sequencing and on-time client delivery.
Stock Take Planning, Coordination & Execution
Plan, schedule, and coordinate all monthly full physical stock counts and weekly cycle counts by category, ensuring the team is briefed, adequately assigned, and the count is completed accurately within the agreed timeframe.
Brief all team members participating in stock takes on counting methodology, zone assignments, and documentation requirements before each count begins.
Supervise the stock count in progress, ensuring accuracy of counting and resolution of discrepancies identified during the count before results are submitted to the Stock Controller.
Receive the Stock Controller's variance report and immediately investigate discrepancies within the Supervisor's area of oversight, reporting findings and corrective actions to the Stores & Logistics Manager.
Sample Management & Oversight
Maintain active oversight of all sample movements; dispatched, pending return, and returned ensuring every sample is tracked in the sample log at all times.
Enforce the rule that no sample leaves the stores without a system entry (Material Out) raised by Stores Assistant I and without the Supervisor's authorization.
Follow up proactively on outstanding sample returns that have exceeded the agreed return timeline, escalating persistent non-returns to the Stores & Ensure returned samples are assessed against condition standards before re-entry into stock, rejecting any item that has deteriorated below an acceptable standard.
Gifts Planning, Coordination & Dispatch
Plan and coordinate all client and partner gifts dispatches proactively. Begin annual gift planning at least 30 days before the anticipated dispatch period, coordinating quantities, recipient lists, packaging requirements, and dispatch scheduling with the Stores & Logistics Manager.
Maintain a Gifts Dispatch Register covering all gifts sent, recipient names, quantities, dispatch dates, and documentation, updated after every dispatch and submitted to the Stores & Logistics Manager monthly.
Ensure all gift dispatches are processed with the correct system entries (Tally) and documentation, including authorization from the Manager, before release.
Alert the Manager immediately if gift stock is insufficient to meet planned dispatch requirements, with sufficient lead time to enable replenishment.
Production Floor Supervision & Quality Compliance
Supervise the production team throughout the working day, monitoring output pace, quality, and adherence to job card specifications, and intervening immediately when any deviation is identified.
Inspect all finished production items before sign-off: personally verify that every item meets the client specification on the job card. No non-conforming item is passed to stores for dispatch.
Ensure all stock transferred to the production floor is accompanied by the correct job card and documentation before the production team begins work.
Make correct voucher entries in Tally for all conversion jobs and external branding assignments, and ensure completed converted goods are fully documented on return to stores.
Stores Policies, SOPs & Operational Compliance
Take personal accountability for the implementation, communication, and enforcement of all stores policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) across the entire team; every staff member under the Supervisor's oversight must know, follow, and be held to each applicable SOP.
Conduct structured SOP induction for every new team member before they work independently, and provide refresher briefings for the full team whenever a policy or procedure is updated, amended, or introduced by the Manager.
Carry out weekly SOP compliance spot checks across all stores, dispatch, and production functions; verifying adherence to FIFO, stock removal procedures, bin card protocols, documentation standards, and production job card requirements and recording findings in the weekly report to the Manager.
Identify any SOP gap, ambiguity, or breach and escalate immediately to the Stores & Logistics Manager with a written account of the finding, the staff member involved, and the corrective action taken or proposed.
Ensure the stores environment, production floor, and dispatch yard meet all housekeeping, health and safety, and physical organization standards at all times treating any deviation as a compliance failure requiring immediate correction.
Reinforce a culture where standards are non-negotiable. No team member operates outside a defined procedure without prior written authorization from the Manager.
Bin Card & Documentation Compliance Enforcement
Enforce bin card discipline across the entire team through daily spot checks; every stock removal must be entered on the bin card on the same transaction, without exception.
Conduct random documentation audits throughout the week, verifying that Delivery Notes, Sales Orders, sample records, and production logs are correctly completed, signed, and ready for filing.
Escalate any bin card discrepancy, FIFO breach, or documentation irregularity to the Stores & Logistics Manager that cannot be resolved at operational level.
Ensure that all daily stores documentation is complete, filed, and submitted to the Stores & Logistics Coordinator within 24 hours of the transaction.
Performance Cycle Management — KPI Setting, Goal Setting & Formal Appraisals
Own the full performance management cycle for all direct reports; set documented KPIs and performance goals with each direct report at the beginning of every performance cycle, in alignment with the department objectives set by the Stores & Logistics Manager.
Conduct formal one-on-one performance reviews with each direct report using documented evidence from daily reports, dispatch records, production logs, and weekly observations; scoring performance against the agreed KPIs and recording findings in the appraisal system.
Prepare formal appraisal documentation for each direct report at the close of every performance cycle, submitting completed forms to the Stores & Logistics Manager for validation and sign-off before submission to the HR Department.
Recommend salary reviews, grade progressions, or additional training investment to the Stores & Logistics Manager based on completed review cycle evidence.
Daily & Weekly Reporting
Submit a written daily, weekly and monthly operational report to the Stores & Logistics Manager by end of each working day covering; orders dispatched, production completed, stock issues, team conduct, SOP compliance observations, and any outstanding matters.
Report immediately to the Stores & Logistics Manager any critical operational failure; dispatch error, missing stock, production quality failure, SOP breach, or team conduct issue with full context, facts, and corrective action already initiated.
Maintain a written issues and actions log for all outstanding matters: every unresolved issue from a daily or weekly report must have an owner, a timeline, and a status update in the following day's report until closed.
Coaching, Development & Team Conduct
Conduct structured weekly coaching sessions with each direct report, providing specific, actionable feedback on performance observed during the week; both positive reinforcement and corrective guidance and logging the session and outcome.
Support the onboarding and initial training of new team members: brief them on all SOPs and procedures, supervise their early work closely, and confirm readiness to the Stores & Logistics Manager before they are permitted to work independently.
Monitor attendance, timekeeping, and conduct for all direct reports — documenting concerns with specific dates, incidents, and observed behaviours, and reporting formally to the Stores & Logistics Manager before any disciplinary process is initiated.
ROLE SPECIFICATIONS
Minimum Qualifications & Experience
Diploma or Bachelor's Degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum 4 years of experience in a warehouse, stores, or production environment — with at least 2 years in a supervisory role with direct people management accountability.
Demonstrated experience in conducting performance reviews and setting team KPIs.
Proficiency in Tally or equivalent warehouse management software.
Working knowledge of stores management SOPs, FIFO principles, and documentation controls.
Key Skills
Strong operational coordination — able to manage simultaneous dispatch, production, and receiving activities without losing accuracy.
People performance management — capable of setting goals, conducting structured reviews, and managing performance formally and fairly.
High precision in documentation verification, picking accuracy confirmation, and production sign-off.
Clear, direct communication — capable of briefing the team concisely and escalating issues to the Manager with full context.
Planning and scheduling skills for stock takes, gifts coordination, and production job card management.
SOP enforcement discipline — implements standards consistently and holds the team to them without exception.
Proficiency in Tally for voucher entries, manufacturing journals, and sample management.

Job Description:
Job Summary
This position provides dedicated administrative and personal assistant support to the Women's Health Thematic Lead, and administrative support to the projects under her portfolio, starting with the GBS-SITE landscaping study. The role combines project administration, including scheduling and correspondence with collaborators and funders, consultant and payment documentation, and travel logistics, with direct personal assistant duties such as diary management, correspondence handling, and communications support. The appointee will also act as the point person for interactions with AKU Supplies and Procurement, Finance, and other administrative teams within COEWCH on behalf of the Thematic Lead's projects and will represent the Thematic Lead and the Centre professionally in dealings with collaborators, funders, and county stakeholders.
The position reports to the Centre Manager for administrative supervision and to the Women's Health Thematic Lead for day-to-day direction of work.
He / She will be the face of the study to the larger health facility and will be required to communicate to health facility team and other stakeholders as appropriate and at all times to display a professional attitude.
The position is based in Kilifi, Kenya, with travel to Mariakani, Malindi, Rabai and other project sites as required (please confirm base location).
Responsibilities
Project and Grant Administrative Support
Coordinate scheduling and communication with project collaborators, researchers, and funders on the GBS-SITE study and other projects under the Thematic Lead's portfolio.
Draft correspondence, including items of a confidential nature, with international collaborators and funder contacts for review, and send approved communications.
Act as a communication link between the Thematic Lead's projects and other facilities, departments, and administrative teams within COEWCH, to exchange information and coordinate support on key activities.
Maintain project meeting calendars, arrange meetings and calls across time zones, and circulate materials in advance.
Take minutes at project meetings and circulate action points.
Support consultant engagement: draft consultant contracts and agreements for review, track deliverables, and follow up on invoices.
Process consultant and vendor payment requests: prepare payment documentation, route for approvals, and follow up with finance until payment is confirmed.
Manage allowance documentation for county team members and other partners engaged in project activities.
Maintain organized project files, electronic and paper, for grant correspondence, contracts, and financial documentation.
Personal Assistant Support to the Women's Health Thematic Lead
Manage the Thematic Lead's calendar: schedule and prioritize meetings, resolve clashes, and send reminders.
Screen, sort and prioritize incoming correspondence (email, mail, calls), flagging urgent items and drafting routine responses for approval.
Prepare briefing notes and materials ahead of meetings.
Prepare minutes and follow up on agreed action points afterward.
Maintain contact lists and follow up on behalf of the Thematic Lead with collaborators, funders, and internal AKU departments.
Support the Thematic Lead's professional social media presence (for example LinkedIn), drafting and scheduling content for review and approval.
Undertake other personal assistant duties as reasonably required to support the Thematic Lead's work.
Travel Coordination
Arrange local and international travel for the Thematic Lead and project team members: flights, accommodation, visas, and ground transport.
Prepare travel itineraries and ensure all travel documentation (invitation letters, visa support letters, insurance) is in place ahead of departure.
Reconcile travel expenses and prepare travel claims and support documentation for finance.
Maintain travel logs and monthly transport requirement summaries and track travel budgets against project allocations.
Meetings, Workshops and Events
Organize logistics for meetings, workshops, and training sessions: venue, catering, participant invitations, and materials.
Support the Thematic Lead and project managers during meetings and events, including note taking and follow up.
Receive and direct visitors and guests appropriately.
Data Management and General Office Administration
Develop and maintain an up to date, well-organized filing system for project and administrative records.
Update contact directories (phone, email, postal, and physical addresses) for collaborators and funders.
Monitor and advise on office and project supply needs.
Support other COEWCH administrative tasks as directed by the Centre Manager.
Handle office petty cash and expenses
Facilitate project procurement needs by raising required requisition documents including non-stock purchasing requisition (NSPR), and ensuring that the necessary approvals are timely obtained and submitted
Follow up with all departments approving requisitions made and ensure timely delivery of expected deliveries
Handle all project dispatch as and when need arises and follow up for confirmation of delivery
Maintains office petty cash and facilitates any necessary requisitions and documentation according to AKU petty cash policy
Prepares orders for office supplies in the system as needed, billings for payment of purchases by providing required information to MMD.
Management of allowance documents for the county team and other partners, processes expense claims in a timely fashion and maintain related records
Requirements
Minimum: Diploma in Business Administration, Office Administration, Secretarial Studies, Communication, or a related field. OR
At least 2 years of relevant experience in an administrative, secretarial, or personal assistant role.
Proficient in computer applications, particularly MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), email and calendar tools, and comfortable learning new digital tools such as video conferencing platforms and cloud document storage.
Excellent communication skills in English and Kiswahili, spoken and written.
Background or work experience in a health-related setting (for example a hospital, clinic, or health research institution) is an added advantage, to support quick understanding of the research environment.
Additional relevant training is an advantage but not required, for example a certificate or diploma in secretarial studies or office administration, a personal or executive assistant course, minute taking training, or a communications course.
Personal Characteristics & Behaviours
High level of confidentiality and discretion, given regular exposure to sensitive research, financial, and personal information.
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Demonstrated initiative and the ability to produce high-quality work with minimum supervision.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to work well with a wide range of people, including international collaborators and funders.
Attention to detail, particularly for scheduling, documentation, and financial paperwork.
Flexibility and willingness to work outside standard hours when required, for example around travel or deadlines.
Professional manners and presentation, representing the Thematic Lead and the Centre well in all interactions.
Adaptability, comfortable working across shifting priorities in a research environment.
Ability to work flexible/long hours when required
Well groomed, courteous and respectful

The Finance Officer – Grants delivers high-quality financial management and reporting services for restricted grants, ensuring accuracy, compliance with CIFOR-ICRAF and donor requirements, timely support to project teams, and effective internal controls to safeguard organizational resources. The position will work closely with the Finance Unit and other units and will be based at the Bogor office.
Duties and responsibilities
Provide financial oversight for restricted grants through budget review, expenditure verification, partner financial monitoring, reconciliation, and timely internal and donor reporting, ensuring accurate budgets, strong compliance, audit-ready records, effective use of donor funds, and sound project cash-flow management
Budget Monitoring and Control
Maintain complete and accurate records of all project financial documentation to ensure alignment with grant agreements.
Collaborate with Principal Investigators (PIs), project teams, implementing partners, and donors to ensure financial implementation aligns with project requirements. Clarify financial issues, answer queries, and provide updates on the budget status of the project.
Review and verify project expenditures to ensure compliance with approved budgets and donor requirements.
Liaise with the Program Management Unit (PMU) on Letters of Agreement (LoAs), project start-up, budget updates, and project tracking in MyTree.
Budget Planning and Updates
Support annual and rolling budget preparation in coordination with Principal Investigators (PIs).
Review planned staff-time allocations and ensure proper updates in the planning system (OCS Planner).
Collaborate with project teams to plan project costs based on available funding.
Review overall annual budgets of assigned grants to ensure accuracy and alignment with funding.
Donor Financial Reporting
Prepare financial reports in compliance with grant agreements, donor requirements, and CIFOR-ICRAF standards.
Prepare and submit accurate financial reports, invoices, and payment requests in accordance with the terms, schedules, and requirements of grant agreements.
Submit the financial reports through MyTree.
Review financial reports from Country Offices before submission for approval.
Follow up on donor queries and feedback related to submitted financial reports.
Grant Budget Development and Amendments
Support the preparation of budgets for new projects and grant amendments.
Review and discuss revised budgets with PIs, budget holders, and Country Offices.
Ensure full cost recovery, including proper allocation of overheads.
Provide guidance to ensure budgets are accurate and compliant with donor requirements.
Grant Agreement Review
Review the financial provisions of new grant agreements and amendments, including budgets, reporting schedules, payment terms, audit requirements, eligible costs, and foreign-exchange provisions, to ensure clarity, accuracy, operational feasibility, and compliance with CIFOR-ICRAF and donor requirements.
Internal Financial Reporting
Prepare monthly summaries of restricted projects, including multi-year budgets and cumulative expenditures.
Report staff-cost forecasts and allocation.
Audit Management
Coordinate with supervisor on the selection and engagement of external auditors for donor-required project audits.
Provide supporting documentation and respond to audit queries during the audit process.
Review draft audit reports and partner audit reports to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Financial Operations and Monitoring
Monitor donor receivables and payables, ensuring timely collection and follow-up.
Review significant donor receivable and payable balances (more than USD 50,000) and provide explanations based on treasury reports.
Inform PIs of monthly spending rates and follow up on low spending.
Identify incoming donor funds and provide coding details to Treasury.
Monitor actual timesheet recording and variances.
Ensure completeness and accuracy of supporting documents, including mandatory timesheets.
Provide financial insights and recommendations to support decision-making by project teams and management.
Implementing Partner Financial Management
Review partner Letters of Agreement (LoAs) and budgets in coordination with Grants Management Unit.
Monitor partner compliance with donor and CIFOR-ICRAF financial requirements.
Analyze partner expenditures and provide insights on spending trends and variances.
Review partner financial reports, monitor balances, and ensure collection of unused funds.
Other Responsibilities

The Internal Auditor plans and independently executes end-to-end audits across the organization, covering Finance, Settlements and Reconciliations, Operations, Technology, IT systems, ISMS/Information Security, AML/CFT, Risk, Compliance, and other business functions.

Key Responsibilities
Internal Audit Execution
Develop and execute a risk-based internal audit plan covering key financial, operational, technology, compliance and information security risks.
Personally conduct audits from planning and scoping through testing, analysis, reporting and follow-up.
Evaluate the design and effectiveness of internal controls, policies, processes and risk mitigation measures.
Conduct special, investigative and ad hoc audits as required by Management or the Board Audit C Risk Committee.
Financial, Operational C Compliance Audits:
Audit financial processes including revenue, expenditure, treasury, settlements, reconciliations, payroll, procurement and financial reporting.
Evaluate operational processes to identify control weaknesses, inefficiencies, and fraud risks, and recommend corrective actions.
Assess compliance with all regulatory laws, regulations, internal policies and delegated authorities.
Audit AML/CFT, fraud prevention, sanctions and other financial crime controls.
Technology C Systems Audits:
Conduct IT and systems audits covering access controls, system changes, application controls, backups, data integrity, system availability and IT operations.
Review system configurations, logs, reports, data and other technical evidence to validate control effectiveness.
Identify technology, cybersecurity and information security risks arising from systems, processes and integrations.
Evaluate business processes to pinpoint opportunities for IT system upgrades and acquisitions.
Audit Reporting C Remediation:
Prepare clear, concise and evidence-based audit reports identifying findings, root causes, risk implications and practical recommendations.
Discuss findings with process owners and management and facilitate agreement on appropriate corrective actions.
Maintain an audit issues register and independently follow up on agreed actions to confirm effective and timely remediation.
Escalate significant, overdue or unresolved high-risk issues to Management and the Board Audit C Risk Committee.
External Audit C Assurance Coordination:
Act as the key liaison between the Company and external auditors, coordinating audit requests, information requirements, meetings and access to relevant documentation.
Coordinate responses to external audit findings and track management actions arising from external audits.
Support effective coordination between internal and external assurance activities and minimize duplication of audit work.
Provide relevant internal audit reports and insights to support external audits and other independent assurance reviews.
Key qualifications:
BCom degree specializing in Accounting/Finance, Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Computer Science, Risk Management or a related field.
Professional certification such as CIA, CPA/ACCA, CISA, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or equivalent.
5–7+ years' relevant experience in internal audit, external audit, IT audit, risk or assurance.
Demonstrated experience conducting both financial/operational audits and technology/systems audits.

Job Description:
Key Responsibilities
As our Security Officer, you will:
Maintain a safe and secure environment for guests, staff and visitors.
Respond promptly and professionally to security incidents and emergencies.
Complete clear, accurate and timely incident reports.
Control access to restricted areas and sensitive locations.
Conduct scheduled security patrols across the property and identify potential risks.
Monitor CCTV and identify, investigate and report suspicious or unusual activity.
Maintain proper control and accountability of master, emergency and restricted area keys.
Safeguard hotel property, equipment and guest belongings.
Ensure lost and found items are properly handled, recorded and secured.
Support the effective response to fire, medical, evacuation and other emergencies.
Identify and promptly report safety and security hazards.
Monitor parking areas, loading zones and vehicle movements.
Ensure visitors, contractors and service providers comply with hotel access procedures.
Monitor staff adherence to established hotel security procedures.
Work closely with Front Office, Food & Beverage, Housekeeping, Engineering, Finance and other departments to maintain a secure operating environment.

Technical security knowledge is important. How you think and behave is equally important to us.
INQUISITIVE
You are naturally observant. You question assumptions, investigate irregularities and actively seek information before reaching conclusions.
RESOURCEFUL
You think on your feet and find practical solutions, even when resources, information or time are limited.
EFFICIENT
You work systematically, prioritise effectively and respond with pace without compromising standards or attention to detail.
DETERMINED
You take ownership. You follow issues through, maintain focus under pressure and do not leave important matters unresolved.
EXPRESSIVE
You communicate confidently and respectfully. You bring warmth and personality to the role while knowing when discretion and firmness are required.
What We're Looking For
You should have:
A Diploma in Security Management, Criminology or a related security discipline.
Certification in Basic First Aid and Firefighting.
Basic training in investigations, incident management and crime scene preservation.
Hands on experience in security operations, preferably within the hospitality industry.
Working knowledge of hotel security systems, procedures and access control processes.
Proven experience responding to and managing emergencies in a busy and complex operating environment.
Experience conducting regular property inspections, identifying security and safety risks and preparing detailed reports for management action.
Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact professionally with guests, colleagues and external stakeholders.
A high level of integrity, confidentiality and professional conduct.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify potential risks, unusual behaviour and irregularities.
The ability to remain calm, alert and professional during incidents and high pressure situations.
Good observation, judgement and problem solving skills.
The ability to collaborate effectively across hotel departments.
Flexibility to work nights, weekends, public holidays and rotational shifts.

Learn guest preferences and use that information to create more personalised experiences.
Give guests a genuine and warm farewell when they leave.

Manage waiting lists and provide realistic wait times rather than leaving guests uncertain.

Excellent spoken communication and confidence engaging guests face to face and over the telephone.
A polished and professional personal presentation.
A naturally warm, outgoing and expressive personality.
Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
The ability to remember faces, names and guest preferences.
Confidence managing reservations, walk ins, waiting lists and busy restaurant periods.
Ability to make quick decisions while remaining composed under pressure.
Strong teamwork and communication skills.

Genuine interest in food, restaurants, people and hospitality.

Job Description:
WHAT YOU WILL DO
As Front Office Agent, you will:
Welcome arriving guests genuinely and warmly, making direct eye contact and recognising returning guests whenever possible.
Complete check in and check out processes accurately and efficiently.
Create a personalised arrival experience rather than simply handing over a room key.
Brief arriving guests on the House, our restaurants, experiences, facilities and services.
Handle room reservations, amendments and guest enquiries.
Monitor room status information and work closely with Housekeeping to support smooth room readiness and guest arrivals.
Maintain accurate guest profiles within the Property Management System.
Capture and update guest preferences and relevant history to support more personalised future stays.
Identify duplicate guest profiles and maintain accurate guest records.
Process guest payments accurately and securely.
Handle cashiering, invoices, PDQ transactions and other Front Office financial responsibilities in accordance with company procedures.
Handle approved foreign currency transactions in accordance with company procedures.
Maintain accurate records, reports and supporting documentation.
Respond promptly to telephone calls and guest enquiries.
Coordinate guest requests with Housekeeping, Maintenance, Food & Beverage, Security and other departments.
Follow up on requests rather than assuming someone else has handled them.
Identify guest concerns early and take appropriate action.
Resolve reasonable guest concerns within your authority and escalate appropriately when additional intervention is required.
Record guest feedback and ensure important information is communicated during shift handovers.
Maintain an organised, professional and welcoming Front Desk environment.
Protect guest information and maintain strict confidentiality.
TURN GUESTS INTO RAFIKIS
This is an important part of the job.
We don't want every conversation to sound like:
“Good afternoon. Passport please. Here is your key. Breakfast is at 7.00am.”
That is a transaction.
We want you to create genuine relational conversations.
Learn names.
Remember faces.
Understand preferences.
Notice birthdays and anniversaries.
Ask guests about their stay.
Follow up on yesterday's conversation.
Remember the restaurant they enjoyed.
Recognise them when they walk through the House again.
A guest should not have to introduce themselves to us repeatedly.
The more we know our guests, the better we can host them.
YOU ARE ALSO COMMERCIAL
Exceptional hospitality and commercial awareness should work together.
You should be comfortable identifying opportunities to increase guest spend without turning every conversation into a sales pitch.
This may include:
Upselling appropriate room categories.
Promoting relevant hotel packages and experiences.
Recommending our restaurants and dining experiences.
Encouraging appropriate room extensions or late check outs where available.
Identifying opportunities for future stays.
Understanding current promotions well enough to recommend them naturally.
Contributing towards Front Office and hotel revenue targets.
The objective is not to push products.
Understand the guest first, then recommend something relevant.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You should bring:
A Diploma in Hotel Management, Front Office Operations or another relevant qualification from a recognised hospitality or tourism institution.
A relevant degree will be an added advantage.
Proven experience as a Front Office Agent, Guest Service Agent, Receptionist or similar guest facing hotel professional.
Previous experience in a 4 or 5 star hotel, lifestyle hotel, boutique hotel or premium hospitality environment is strongly preferred.
Hands on experience using a Property Management System such as Opera.
Experience handling guest check ins, check outs, reservations and room enquiries.
Experience with cashiering, invoices, cash handling and PDQ payment terminals.
Basic bookkeeping and numerical accuracy.
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel.
Confidence using multi line telephone systems and standard Front Office equipment.
Excellent spoken and written English.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
A warm, expressive and naturally engaging personality.
Strong organisational ability and attention to detail.
The ability to remain composed and productive during busy arrival and departure periods.
Confidence dealing with guest complaints and difficult situations.
Commercial awareness and willingness to contribute towards revenue targets.
High standards of honesty, integrity and confidentiality.
Flexibility to work shifts, including evenings, weekends and public holidays.

Job Description:
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
As Executive Pastry Chef, you will:
Lead and oversee the entire pastry and bakery operation, setting high standards for quality, taste, texture, presentation and consistency.
Develop a distinctive French inspired pâtisserie offering for The Social House and The Living Room.
Create signature pastries and desserts that guests begin to associate specifically with The Social House.
Develop exceptional croissants, viennoiserie, laminated pastries, artisan breads, cakes, tarts, entremets, petits gâteaux, chocolate products and plated desserts.
Balance classical French pastry techniques with contemporary flavours, presentation and locally relevant ideas.
Develop seasonal collections, festive ranges, celebration cakes, afternoon experiences and limited edition pastry concepts.
Continuously explore pastry trends, techniques, ingredients and leading pastry houses locally and internationally.
Create, implement and maintain standard recipes, production specifications, photographs, yields, portion sizes and presentation standards.
Build production systems that deliver the same exceptional quality every day, regardless of who is on shift.
Plan production requirements and maintain appropriate par levels and stock availability.
Monitor ingredient usage, wastage and portion control while maintaining strong food cost discipline.
Work closely with Procurement on ingredient quality, supplier performance and product specifications.
Lead, coach, train and develop Pastry Chefs, Commis Chefs, Bakers and other members of the pastry team.
Build the technical capability of the pastry team so that knowledge and standards are transferred rather than concentrated in one person.
Work closely with the Executive Chef and wider culinary team on menus, promotions, special events and seasonal offerings.
Partner with the commercial and marketing teams to create pastry products and experiences that generate excitement, guest traffic and revenue.
Ensure all pastry production complies with food safety, hygiene and health and safety standards.
Maintain exceptional standards of cleanliness, organisation and operational discipline within the pastry kitchen.
Monitor the condition and performance of pastry equipment and promptly address maintenance and safety concerns.
Drive continuous improvement, innovation and efficiency throughout the pastry operation.
Act as a role model for professionalism, teamwork, discipline and culinary excellence.
WE ARE PARTICULARLY INTERESTED IN YOUR FRENCH PASTRY CRAFT
You should have strong practical knowledge of classical and contemporary French pastry.
We are particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate excellent work in areas such as:
Croissants and laminated doughs
Pain au chocolat and viennoiserie
Brioche
Choux pastry and éclairs
Mille feuille
Macarons
Tarts and tartlets
Entremets and petits gâteaux
Mousses, crémeux, ganaches and glazes
Chocolate and praline work
Celebration and speciality cakes
Artisan breads and premium bakery products
Contemporary plated desserts
We are interested not only in where you have worked, but also in what you can actually create.
THE PERSON WE ARE LOOKING FOR
INQUISITIVE
You are curious about your craft.
You study what leading pastry chefs and pâtisseries are doing. You ask why a product works, how it could be improved and what guests might want next.
You experiment intelligently and never assume yesterday’s success guarantees tomorrow’s relevance.
RESOURCEFUL
Not every challenge requires more money, more people or more equipment.
You know how to work intelligently with ingredients, people, equipment and available resources.
When something goes wrong, you look for solutions rather than excuses.
EFFICIENT
Beautiful pastry must also make commercial sense.
You understand production planning, yields, portion control, food cost, wastage, labour productivity and stock management.
Your kitchen is organised because you understand that creativity performs better when supported by discipline.
DETERMINED
You have high standards and the stamina to maintain them.
You understand that becoming recognised for exceptional pastry requires repetition, refinement, training and relentless attention to detail.
You finish what you start.
EXPRESSIVE
Pastry should have personality.
So should its leader.
You communicate clearly, teach confidently, receive feedback well and can explain the story and thinking behind your creations.
You bring energy and character to your kitchen while maintaining discipline, professionalism and respect.
WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING
A recognised qualification in Pastry & Bakery, Culinary Arts, Hotel Management or a related discipline.
Significant experience as an Executive Pastry Chef, Head Pastry Chef, Pastry Sous Chef or equivalent senior pastry leader within a luxury hotel, premium pâtisserie, high end restaurant or comparable hospitality operation.
Strong practical expertise in French pâtisserie and viennoiserie.
Demonstrable experience creating and launching new pastry products rather than simply reproducing an existing menu.
Strong technical knowledge of pastry, bakery, desserts and chocolate production.
Experience developing recipes and establishing production and presentation standards.
Strong understanding of recipe costing, food cost, portion control, inventory management and waste reduction.
Experience leading a pastry team and developing junior chefs.
Strong production planning and organisational capability.
Excellent knowledge of food hygiene, safety and quality standards.
An exceptional eye for presentation and attention to detail.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Commercial awareness and an understanding that a successful pastry operation must deliver both exceptional products and sustainable financial performance.
The ability to remain calm, organised and consistent in a demanding hospitality environment.
Genuine passion for craftsmanship, innovation and creating memorable guest experiences.

Job Description
Strategy/Planning
Performs duty with minimum amount of supervision and is responsible for effectively planning his or her time during the shift
Reviews the production schedule for the day, works with the planner to understand where he/she should be positioned to capture all relevant process or product checks and measurements.
Ensure all production is being carried out in line with Quality Control, HACCP requirements, operating procedures including visual inspections audits, QC line checks as required.
Implementation
Uses a series of tools (ingredient specifications, product recipes/formulas, product specifications, manufacturing procedures, sampling program, GMP requirements, in process analysis/records e.tc.) and devices to check process or product condition and compares to standard to compare actual versus tolerable limits.

Acts as an independent body from the manufacturing team, and engages as if he/she was the eyes of the final customer to ensure consistency and integrity throughout.
Uses documentation or digital means to record checks and measures.
Authorized to quarantine ingredients, products or a process should any such checks and measure yield out of limit results.
Continuously monitor product quality at all stages of the raw material intake, packing, positive release and dispatch process.
Reporting and Evaluation
Completes checks and measures against predetermined scope, completes documentation during each activity
Refers to specific product or process name, work order number and decision at each level being pass or fail.
Escalates failed processes or products immediately to shift manager and quality supervisor on duty, citing details and reasons for such quarantine.
Qualifications
Food science based degree or Diploma from a recognized institution
Experience
2 years working in a QC related position in a FMCG environment.
Computer literate.
Qualification or experience in ISO 22000/HACCP.
Actively demonstrate the following behaviors : consultative ,collaborative, analytical, pro-active, change-orientated and structured with the ability to be flexible when required.
Results driven, able to find solutions when faced with adverse results or conditions to achieve objects.

YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
ESSENTIAL CRITERIA:

Job Description:
The Role
The role holder will provide full-time investment and programme leadership for AECF's circular economy portfolio, with primary responsibility for structuring, appraising and managing investments in private sector enterprises, and secondary responsibility for ensuring those investment decisions are informed by sound circular economy principles. Leading a small team and working closely with the sector head, advisory and programme teams, the Programme Manager will manage the circular economy investment pipeline, portfolio, work plan, budget and donor reporting.
The incumbent will lead investment due diligence and structuring, oversee portfolio management and results verification under the results-based financing mechanism, and represent the programme with ecosystem stakeholders to strengthen circular economy financing and enterprise growth across the programme countries.
This role will report to the Associate Director - Energy.
Key Responsibilities
Investment Leadership and Portfolio Management
Lead end-to-end investment due diligence on prospective portfolio companies, assessing business models, financial viability, commercial scalability, management capacity and risk, alongside circular economy performance.
Structure and recommend appropriate financing instruments — results-based repayable grants, blended finance and other risk-sharing mechanisms — tailored to enterprise needs and investment risk.
Present investment recommendations to the investment committee and manage the approval-to-disbursement process.
Oversee active portfolio management, including monitoring financial and operational performance, covenant compliance, and results verification under the results-based financing mechanism.
Programme Management and Coordination
Manage the planning, budgeting, work planning and reporting of the circular economy programme.
Supervise and provide guidance to programme team members and consultants, including technical circular economy specialists supporting the portfolio.
Coordinate with donors on work plans, deliverables, timelines and reporting requirements.
Monitor programme and portfolio risk, ensuring timely, quality delivery of investment and programme outputs.
Enterprise Advisory and Investment Readiness
Oversee the design and delivery of technical assistance and investment readiness support to strengthen portfolio companies' performance and bankability.
Work with technical circular economy specialists and the Advisory team to ensure enterprises receive appropriate guidance on cleaner production, eco-design, sustainable packaging, recycling, repair and refurbishment, reverse logistics, material recovery and resource efficiency.
Work closely with the ESG team to support enterprises in improving investment readiness, operational performance, and ESG practices.
Market Development and Knowledge Management
Lead engagement with financial institutions, industry associations, government agencies and development partners to strengthen circular economy financing ecosystems and pipeline development.
Contribute to market research, investment case development, knowledge products and programme learning.
Oversee monitoring, evaluation and reporting, developing investment and technical indicators and validating financial, environmental and circularity results.
Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate should:
Hold a postgraduate qualification in Finance, Investment, Business Administration, Economics, Development Finance or a related discipline; a background or additional qualification in Circular Economy, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Sciences, Sustainable Manufacturing or a related discipline is an added advantage but not a requirement.
Have at least ten (10) years' experience in investment, fund/portfolio management, private equity, venture capital, blended finance or development finance, including experience investing in or supporting private sector enterprises in Africa.
Have substantial experience conducting investment due diligence, structuring financing instruments (grants, results-based financing, guarantees or similar), and managing an investment portfolio.
Have at least three (3) years' experience in a programme management or team leadership role, including budget and plan management.
Prior knowledge of or exposure to circular economy business models — plastics and packaging, electronic waste, recycling systems, resource recovery, eco-design or industrial symbiosis — is preferred but not required; candidates without direct circular economy experience but with strong investment credentials and a demonstrated ability to build sector knowledge quickly are encouraged to apply.
Experience working on donor-funded programmes involving blended finance, results-based financing or challenge funds will be an added advantage.
Required Competencies
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Strong investment and financial analysis skills, including due diligence, deal structuring and portfolio management.
Proven programme and team management skills, including work planning, budgeting and donor reporting.
Good understanding of blended finance, results-based financing and enterprise development; working knowledge of circular economy principles and business models is preferred.
Excellent analytical, communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to translate technical and financial concepts into practical business solutions and work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.
