Job Description:
About the role:
This role oversees the supply chain operations underpinning Sun King's PAYG LPG business in Kenya. The scope spans commercial relationships with bulk LPG vendors, safe and efficient product movement, inventory planning across the warehouse and depot network, and the full lifecycle management of cylinder assets deployed to customers and riders. The role also ensures effective loss governance, capital efficiency, and compliance with Sun King's safety, quality, and regulatory standards.
The role holder manages vendor performance and credit terms alongside physical stock, ensuring accurate goods receipt, account reconciliation, SLA compliance, and reliable supply continuity. The position balances service availability with working capital efficiency at every stage, from unissued stock in depots to cylinders circulating in the field. A consistent, reliable performance-reporting framework provides visibility across the supply chain.
As PAYG LPG expands into new markets, effective management of the vendor base, inventory network, and cylinder assets will be essential to ensuring safe, compliant, and capital-efficient growth.
What You Will Be Expected to Do
LPG Supply Management:
Oversee bulk LPG transportation from vendor facilities to refilling points or bulk storage locations.
Ensure the safe and timely movement of bulk LPG across the supply network.
Monitor real-time supply flows and stock-in-transit visibility to maintain operational continuity.
Identify and resolve operational bottlenecks, including transport delays, facility capacity constraints, and routing issues.
Improve bulk transportation costs and routing efficiency.
Ensure accurate goods-receipt verification through dual-weighing at refilling points and bulk storage facilities, identifying discrepancies against vendor dispatch records.
Maintain continuous, safe, and reliable physical LPG movement throughout the Sun King network.
Inventory Planning & Replenishment
Manage inventory flows for cookstoves, cylinders, FMCDs, accessories, and LPG from suppliers and depots into the warehouse network before field deployment.
Establish and monitor warehouse and depot stock levels in line with demand.
Develop and maintain safety stock policies across the warehouse and depot network.
Minimize stock-outs while optimizing working capital tied up in unissued warehouse and depot inventory.
Establish a replenishment planning framework aligned with customer demand and operational requirements.
Coordinate with Sales on demand forecasting and inventory requirements.
Maintain product availability across the warehouse and depot network while optimizing pre-deployment working capital.
Asset Lifecycle Management
Maintain end-to-end tracking and visibility of deployed cylinders across markets, including assets held by customers, riders, or in transit.
Improve monthly working capital efficiency across deployed cylinders by addressing idle, unreturned, or uncollected units in the field.
Manage the cylinder recertification pipeline, including scheduling and tracking cylinders due or overdue for recertification.
Establish and maintain loss and shrinkage governance processes for unaccounted cylinders, covering declarations, recovery tracking, and write-off approvals.
Maintain a consolidated reporting framework covering supply, inventory, vendor SLAs, and asset KPIs to enable informed, data-based operational assessments.
Improve deployed-cylinder productivity and capital efficiency across the field fleet, backed by accurate and reliable performance reporting.
Safety, Quality & Regulatory Compliance
Ensure LPG storage, refilling, and bulk transportation operations comply with Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) licensing and safety requirements.
Maintain depot and facility licences, permits, and inspection readiness, including EPRA, county government, fire safety certification, and NEMA requirements, where applicable.
Maintain cylinder quality standards covering leak testing, valve and regulator integrity, and dent or corrosion checks, in line with KEBS cylinder standards and recertification requirements.
Ensure compliance with weights and measures requirements for gas dispensed by weight, including dual-weighing procedures at facility and shop level.
Establish and audit safety protocols for bulk transportation, depot handling, and last-mile cylinder exchange, including PPE, fire safety, and hazardous-material handling, in line with DOSH requirements.
Coordinate incident investigations and reporting for safety events, including leaks, accidents, and near-misses, and ensure corrective actions are completed.
Ensure transporters, distributors, depots, and refill centres maintain full compliance with applicable EPRA requirements.
Maintain a safe operating environment, prevent major safety incidents, and ensure regulatory compliance across the depot and shop network.
Vendor & Partner Relationships
Manage commercial relationships and intake coordination with LPG bulk vendors and other supply chain partners.
Monitor and uphold vendor credit terms, including payment due dates and invoicing cycles, and address any breaches.
Conduct regular vendor statement-of-account (SOA) reconciliations, covering invoiced, consumed, and paid volumes.
Establish, monitor, and uphold vendor SLAs covering refill turnaround times, dispatch timelines, and quality standards.
Conduct periodic vendor performance reviews and maintain performance scorecards.
Negotiate commercial terms, including pricing, credit terms, SLAs, and volumes, as business scale and market conditions evolve.
Manage vendor risk, supplier diversification, and onboarding of new vendors as the business expands into new markets.
Act as the escalation point for vendor disputes and facilitate timely resolution.
Maintain reliable vendor relationships that ensure uninterrupted supply, cost efficiency, and compliance with contractual credit terms and SLAs.
You Might Be a Strong Candidate If You:
A bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Administration, Finance, IT, or a related field.
Experience in LPG, downstream oil and gas, or FMCG distribution.
Strong project management capabilities, with experience delivering process improvement initiatives.
The ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with minimal supervision.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships across teams and partners.
Experience coordinating and managing cross-border teams.
Strong financial skills and data interpretation capabilities, with experience using insights to inform operational and commercial assessments.
Familiarity with regulatory bodies such as energy regulatory authorities, preferably within the LPG or energy sector.

Job Title: Digital Growth Expert & Online Business Owner — Kenya
Job Description:
Own a webshop. Sharpen a European engine. Prove everything before it travels.
Moyee Coffee is a FairChain coffee company. We roast at origin in Ethiopia and Kenya, we sell directly to the people who drink our coffee across Europe, and we run a roastery and café in Nairobi. Not fair trade with a certificate — fair chain, with the value staying where the coffee grows.
We're looking for someone to own our online business in Kenya, and to be the digital expert in our European growth team. One person. One Odoo platform. Two markets.
Why this role exists
Most digital roles are one of two things: a strategist who briefs an agency, or a specialist who runs one channel. This is neither.
In Kenya, you are the
owner
. The Odoo website and webshop for the Kenyan market are your business — the pages, the product catalogue, the checkout, the payments, the campaigns, the revenue. Not a maintainer. An owner with a number.
In Europe, you are the
expert
. You optimise paid, CRM and conversion across our pan-European rollout, alongside our paid specialist and our technical lead.
The connection between the two is the point. Because you own the Kenya shop completely, you can test at full speed on a live shop — no committee, no ticket queue, no waiting. New page designs, checkout flows, subscription mechanics and campaign formats get built and proven in Nairobi first. What works travels to Europe with results attached.
Test it in Kenya. Prove it in Kenya. Roll it out in Europe. You run both ends of that loop.
What you'll do
Own the Kenya webshop, end to end
Full ownership of the Kenya Odoo website and shop: structure, content, products, pricing, promotions
Design and build the pages yourself in Odoo Website Builder — mobile-first, fast, and built for the phones Kenyan customers actually use
Own the sales flow from product page to confirmation, including local payment methods and delivery options that fit how Nairobi buys
Run the local growth calendar: campaigns, offers and launches connected to the café, the roastery and our microlot programme
Build subscriptions and repeat purchase for a Kenyan audience — not a copy-paste of what works in Amsterdam
Kenya online revenue is your number.
Be the digital expert in Europe
Run and optimise paid campaigns (Google Search, Display, Meta) together with our paid specialist
Build and improve the CRM and lifecycle flows in Odoo: welcome, repeat purchase, winback, subscription journeys
Own conversion optimisation on the European webshop — landing pages, product pages, checkout, account flows
Support new market launches with working campaigns and pages
Build the dashboards that connect Odoo, Google Ads and Meta, so every channel has one number everyone agrees on
Run the laboratory
One deliberate test per week on the Kenya shop, documented with result and decision
Keep a living playbook: what was tested, what won, what Europe should copy
Propose and implement the transfers — minimum one Kenya-proven improvement live in Europe per quarter
What this role is not
Not an agency-management role.
There's nobody to brief and wait for. You build it.
Not a strategy role without hands.
If you can't open Odoo and change how a page looks and sells before lunch, this isn't the right fit.
Not a content role.
Our content pod makes the stories and the reels. You tell them what the funnel needs and show them what performed.
Not two half-jobs.
The shop you own is the proving ground for the platform you optimise.
Who you are
Odoo web expert.
Deep, hands-on experience with Odoo Website and eCommerce: building and styling pages, templates, product configuration, payment providers, sales flows.
You've run growth yourself.
Personally managed paid campaigns (Google / Meta) and email/CRM flows — and you know how to read what the numbers actually say.
Design and flow instinct.
Pages that look like the brand and sell like a funnel.
Data discipline.
Dashboards and attribution are how you decide, not how you decorate.
Owner's mindset.
You want a business to run, not a queue of tickets to close.
Let's-do-it mentality.
You test something every week, learn from it, and go again.
A plus: experience with European e-commerce and how those markets tick.
Your first 90 days
Phase
Focus
What's done by the end
Days 1–30
Own & audit
Full ownership and access to the Kenya Odoo shop. Kenya shop audited as a customer experiences it — on a phone, on Kenyan networks, through payment and delivery. European paid and CRM audited. Baselines set for both markets. First quick fixes live.
Days 31–60
Improve both sides
Redesigned homepage, key product pages and checkout live in Kenya. First local campaign running. European paid restructured. Core CRM flows improved. Weekly testing rhythm and dashboards live.
Days 61–90
Close the loop
Kenya improvements measured against baseline. First Kenya-proven improvement live on the European shop. Playbook v1 written. 90-day review and Year 1 plan.
What we offer
Real ownership from day one — the Kenya online business is yours: the shop, the flows, the campaigns, the results
A double stage almost no digital role offers: an online business of your own at home, and the expert seat in a European growth team, with your wins travelling onto a much larger platform
Freedom to build and test at full speed on a live shop, with no committees between an idea and its result
Founding membership of the Kenya digital team — built at the source, not bolted onto Europe — with regular working sessions with the European team

Digital Content Production & Platform Management
Translate annual communication strategies and editorial priorities into actionable content plans and platform-specific messaging.

Repurpose high-performing assets across multiple platforms to maximize reach and value.
Social Media & Audience Engagement

Identify digital trends and opportunities to strengthen the Academy’s online visibility.
Promptly escalate sensitive comments, complaints, or reputational risks to the Brand Communications Manager.

Coordinate photography, videography, live coverage, and same-day storytelling packages (reels, highlights, recap articles).
Manage on-site media requirements, press logistics, and interviews during institutional functions.
Performance Analytics & Insights
Track and report monthly performance metrics across digital channels, including reach, engagement, audience growth, and website traffic.
Maintain analytics dashboards, conduct quarterly competitor content audits, and present data-backed recommendations.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Brand Stewardship
Work with the Graphic Designer & Website Specialist to build integrated visual assets.
Partner with Admissions on recruitment content and support internal communication channels (e.g., weekly staff bulletin).
Maintain a secure, organized Digital Asset Management system and enforce 100% compliance with media consent and child safeguarding protocols.
Mentorship & Student Development

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Digital Engagement & Reach:
Consistent month-on-month growth across official social media channels, website traffic, and campaign conversions.
Content Delivery & Live Coverage:
100% delivery of same-day event media packages, weekly staff bulletins, and scheduled editorial calendars.
Brand Compliance & Safeguarding:
0 violations of child safeguarding protocols; 100% signed media release compliance prior to asset publication.
Operational Efficiency:
Demonstrable workflow optimization using AI tools and regular update of digital media archives.
CORE COMPETENCIES
Communication & Copywriting:
Exceptional written English and ability to translate complex topics into engaging narratives.
Multimedia Storytelling:
Proficiency in mobile journalism, press photography (DSLR/drone), and short-form video production.
Digital Literacy & AI Integration:
Confident application of social media analytics, management suites, and AI-assisted creation tools.
Live Event Journalism:
Capability to deliver high-quality, polished assets under high-pressure, live deadlines.
Safeguarding & Ethics:
Unwavering commitment to ethical reporting and safety standards for minors.

Minimum of three (3) years’ professional experience in digital content development, journalism, corporate communications, or social media management.

Job Purpose
The Production Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the production operations in the factory, ensuring that all processes run efficiently, safely, and in compliance with company standards. This role involves supervising the production team, managing resources, ensuring product quality, maintaining safety standards, and optimizing production output to meet company targets.
Key Responsibilities
Production Planning and Coordination:
Coordinate and schedule production activities to ensure that production targets are met in a timely manner.
Monitor the daily production processes and ensure that production schedules are adhered to.
Communicate with the production team to ensure they have the resources and materials needed for their tasks.
Optimize production processes by minimizing downtime, improving efficiency, and reducing waste.
Team Supervision and Leadership:
Supervise a team of production operators and assistants, providing guidance and direction to ensure smooth operations.
Train and mentor production staff on equipment usage, safety protocols, and quality standards.
Conduct regular performance evaluations, provide feedback, and recommend training opportunities to improve team performance. Ensure that staff follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and working efficiently.
Quality Control and Compliance:
Ensure that all products are manufactured according to quality standards and specifications.
Perform regular inspections of production output and processes to identify any defects or quality issues.
Work with the quality control team to implement corrective actions when production issues arise.
Monitor and enforce compliance with environmental, health, and safety regulations during all production activities.
Resource Management and Inventory Control:
Ensure that raw materials, chemicals, and production resources are available and properly stored to prevent shortages or contamination.
Track material usage and assist in maintaining accurate inventory records.
Report on raw material consumption and assist with the ordering of materials to ensure no production delays.
Ensure the proper maintenance and operation of production equipment, machinery, and tools.
Health, Safety, and Environmental Management:
Maintain a safe working environment by enforcing safety procedures, conducting regular safety checks, and promoting a culture of safety.
Ensure all workers wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE) and follow safety protocols.
Respond to safety concerns and incidents promptly, conducting investigations and reporting findings.
Ensure compliance with environmental regulations related to waste management, emissions, and factory operations.
Performance Monitoring and Reporting:
Monitor production performance through key performance indicators (KPls) such as efficiency, output quality, and adherence to schedules.
Prepare and submit regular production reports to senior management, highlighting production output, challenges, and areas for improvement.
Identify trends in production performance and suggest improvements to optimize processes.
Troubleshooting and Problem Resolution:
Identify production bottlenecks and address issues related to machinery, materials, or labor.
Resolve any production-related issues promptly to avoid delays or quality problems.
Work closely with maintenance teams to ensure that any equipment malfunctions or breakdowns are addressed quickly.
Continuous Improvement:
Encourage and participate in continuous improvement initiatives to increase productivity, reduce costs, and enhance product quality.
Suggest new techniques or technologies to improve production efficiency or product consistency.
Implement lean manufacturing principles and other methodologies to optimize production workflows.
Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor's degree or Diploma in Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering or a related field.
At least 3 years of experience in production or manufacturing, with at least 2 years in a supervisory role, preferably in a chemical or manufacturing industry
Strong understanding of production processes, equipment, and chemical safety regulations.
Knowledge of quality control and inventory management systems.Proficiency in computer applications (e.g., Microsoft Office, production software).
Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
A solid understanding of safety and environmental regulations in manufacturing.

Company Details: The Vision and Mission It is our vision to find creative solutions to offer a continuum of emotional, spiritual, physical and educational care for Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVCs), youths and their families in Kenya. Emotional and spiritual care includes mentorship, counseling, professional...read moreguidance and life skills education. Physical support includes but is not limited to; family unification, kin care, provision of food and adult transitional support. Educational care includes sponsorship for primary, secondary, university and vocational education. The Beneficiaries We work closely with orphans, vulnerable children and youths, parents, guardians and community members who care for our population. It is our belief that simply because a childs life circumstances lead them to be born into poverty, doesnt mean that their story has to end there. It is paramount to our relationship that these children know hope for their futures. The Plan We believe in empowering local leadership in our organization. We acknowledge Kenyans know best the cultural, political and environmental background of their own country, and we believe they know the best solution to providing improvement in the lives of their children. We act in partnership with our Kenyan leadership to provide additional ideas, support and resources to refine Kenyan identified solutions to Kenyan identified problems. In partnership with our Kenyan leadership we work closely with guardians and community members to find loving community based solutions to poverty and care for OVCs. We collaborate to find solutions to keep OVCs in their community connected to their families and living in healthy and safe homes. This includes family unification efforts, provision of food, healthcare, educational and career development opportunities. Additionally, Light Up Hope is keenly aware that once an OVC reaches the age of 18 they continue to be in need of support to make the transition to adulthood without returning to a life of suffering. When an OVC turns 18, they are expected to leave the safety of the care environment they have known and join the Kenyan society. For some this means their education is finalized and they hope to enter the job market with little professional training. In most cases, these young adults do not have the skills, knowledge, resources, or training to do this with success. Our transitional program exists to provide the opportunity for these young adults to gain life skills, resources and university education so they can become contributing members of the Kenyan society and break the cycle of poverty into which they were born.

Job Title: Programme Specialist, Climate Change, Population and Development Branch, Programme Division (PD)
Company Address: New York, NY
Company Details:
UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe and every young person's potential is fulfilled.

UNFPA expands the possibilities for women and young people to lead healthy and productive lives.

Since UNFPA started working in 1969, th...read moree number - and rate - of women dying from complications of pregnancy or childbirth has been halved. Families are smaller and healthier. Young people are more connected and empowered than ever before.

Too many left behind

But too many are still left behind. Nearly a billion people remain mired in extreme poverty. Sexual and reproductive health problems are a leading cause of death and disability for women in the developing world. Young people bear the highest risks of HIV infection and unintended pregnancy. More than a hundred million girls face the prospect of child marriage and other harmful practices, such as female genital mutilation.

Much more needs to be done to ensure a world in which all individuals can exercise their basic human rights, including those that relate to the most intimate and fundamental aspects of life.

Ensuring every pregnancy is wanted
Few things have a greater impact on the life of a woman than the number and spacing of her children. That’s why international agreements going back decades affirm that individuals should have the right (and the means) to freely decide when (or if) to start a family and how many children to bear. Yet, in this new century, some 225 million women who want to avoid or delay childbearing still lack access to the quality services and supplies needed to manage their fertility.

Supporting maternal health
We know how to save almost all women who die giving life. The first step is to ensure they can plan their pregnancies and space their births. Skilled birth attendance at delivery, with backup emergency obstetric care and essential supplies in place, is also critical.

Perhaps the most challenging aspect of reducing maternal death and disability is finding ways to reach all women, even those in the poorest, most remote areas, or in times of natural or man-made disasters. This involves bolstering health systems. It is also critical that pregnant women are able to access all the care they need, from prenatal HIV testing to post-natal care for newborns, at the same clinic or health centre. This approach saves money and saves lives.

Helping young people fulfil their potential
Young people from age 10-24 constitute a quarter of the world’s population (2014). Their reproductive choices will shape future demographic trends.

UNFPA advocates for the rights of young people, including the right to accurate information and services related to sexuality and reproductive health. Empowered with knowledge and skills to protect themselves and make informed decisions, they can realize their full potential and contribute to economic and social transformation.

Investing in young people, especially adolescent girls, is one of the smartest investments a country can make. As parents, teachers and leaders of the next generation, they can help break the cycle of poverty, strengthen the social fabric and create a sustainable future.

Description
The Finance Manager runs the day-to-day operations of the Finance Department, directing the Revenue & AR Accountant, Cost & AP Accountant and Tax & Treasury Accountant so that the work of the department is planned, completed on time and delivered to the standard set by the Head of Finance. It holds the team to the reporting, payment and statutory calendar, keeps internal controls and segregation of duties working in daily practice, coordinates the department in its dealings with auditors, suppliers, customers and other functions, and refers accounting, tax and reporting judgements to the Head of Finance.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Supervise, coach and performance-manage the Revenue & AR Accountant, Cost & AP Accountant and Tax & Treasury Accountant; plan and allocate their workload, agree deadlines and hold each portfolio to them.
Run the monthly reporting cycle from start to finish, checking that the management accounts prepared by the direct reports are complete and submitted to the Head of Finance by the agreed date.
Maintain the departmental calendar covering reporting, payment, filing and audit deliverables; track each item to completion and raise slippage early.
Ensure journals, accruals, prepayments and closing entries are prepared, checked and posted within the agreed timetable, referring questions of accounting treatment to the Head of Finance.
Ensure the AR, AP, bank and tax control account reconciliations are completed on schedule and that reconciling items are chased and cleared rather than carried forward.
Track cash position, collections and payment commitments with the Tax & Treasury Accountant, and give the Head of Finance early warning of funding pressure.
Check supplier payment runs, customer collections and payroll and statutory remittances prepared by the direct reports against the authorisation matrix before they go to the Head of Finance for sign-off.
Keep the company current on tax and statutory filings (VAT, withholding tax, PAYE, NSSF, SHIF/SHA, NITA, corporate income tax, eTIMS) by holding the Tax & Treasury Accountant to the filing calendar and confirming that returns and payments are made on time.
Coordinate the annual budget and periodic forecasting exercise, collecting inputs from the direct reports and from other departments and packaging them for the Head of Finance.
Enforce internal controls, segregation of duties and the authorisation matrix in daily practice across revenue, payables and treasury processes, and report breaches or weaknesses to the Head of Finance.
Follow up escalated queries, disputes, variances and long outstanding items to conclusion, drawing on the Head of Finance where technical input is needed.
Coordinate internal, external, stock and tax audits, scheduling the input of the team, assembling the schedules requested and tracking audit findings through to closure.
Compile and present the periodic operating reports required by the Head of Finance and the management team, covering collections, AR and AP ageing, cash position and compliance status.
Deputise for the Head of Finance on operational matters in their absence, including approvals within the authorisation matrix and day-to-day liaison with other departments.
Improve finance processes and the use of SAP Business One, and build depth in the team through cross-training and documented procedures.

A monthly reporting cycle closed on time, with management accounts submitted to the Head of Finance by the agreed date.
Reconciliations of AR, AP, inventory, bank and tax accounts completed to schedule with reconciling items cleared.
A well-led, cross-trained team of Accountants meeting reporting deadlines with no disruption to service delivery.
Controls, segregation of duties and the authorisation matrix applied consistently, with no repeat audit findings.
Statutory and tax returns and remittances made within the deadlines set out in the compliance calendar.
Operating reports on cash, collections, payables and compliance available to the Head of Finance and management when required.
Professional Qualifications, Knowledge, and Experience
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field from a recognised institution.

Training in supervision, management or business process improvement is an added advantage.
Experience:

Demonstrated ability to run a team through a monthly reporting and payment cycle, holding several portfolios to deadline at the same time.
Practical experience with SAP (Business One) or a similar ERP, and strong working proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

Proven experience leading, coaching and performance-managing accounting or administrative staff.

Ability to plan, allocate and follow up the work of a team so that deadlines are met without prompting from above.

Targeted process and performance improvement

Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.
Reporting and documentation
Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
You will lead internal investigations at M-KOPA end-to-end — from intake through to case closure — across all five operating markets (Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, and South Africa). You will engage stakeholders internally with discretion and sound judgement, safeguard the integrity of the whistleblower and grievance programme, and keep the Board informed through regular, well-evidenced reporting. This role demands not just technical investigative skill but strong personal character — the trust placed in this role by complainants, subjects, and the business depends on it.
Key Responsibilities
Investigation Lifecycle Management
Lead internal investigations end-to-end: intake and triage, planning, evidence gathering, interviews (complainants, witnesses, and subjects), analysis, and final reporting.
Apply consistent, defensible investigative methodology across fraud, misconduct, harassment, safeguarding, and policy-violation cases.
Maintain a clear, well-documented evidence trail for every case, sufficient to withstand scrutiny (including in disciplinary or legal proceedings).
Recommend proportionate, well-reasoned outcomes and remediation actions, including control weaknesses exposed by the investigation.
Stakeholder Engagement & Board Reporting
Engage confidently and sensitively with stakeholders across HR, Legal, Risk, and country leadership throughout the life of a case.
Prepare monthly and quarterly investigation reports for the Head of Internal Audit & Risk and the Board Audit & Risk Committee, summarising case volumes, themes, outcomes, and emerging risk signals.
Manage sensitive conversations with complainants and subjects with empathy, fairness, and absolute discretion.
Whistleblower & Safeguarding Programme
Support the day-to-day operation of the whistleblower and grievance programme, ensuring reported concerns are triaged, tracked, and actioned in line with policy and IIA/ACFE good practice.
Own and maintain the case management platform (tracking, evidence storage, and reporting), ensuring data integrity and confidentiality at all times.
Identify recurring themes or systemic control gaps from case data and feed these into audit planning and risk reporting.
Audit Innovation & Function Development
Champion adoption of M-KOPA’s technology and AI capabilities to enhance audit planning and execution (e.g., risk sensing, scoping, testing, and reporting) while maintaining independence, governance, and confidentiality.
Embed data analytics and continuous monitoring approaches into audit delivery to strengthen coverage, increase efficiency, and enable earlier identification of emerging risks across markets.
Drive standardisation and quality uplift through modern audit tooling (e.g., audit management platforms, workflow automation, and digital working papers), including clear controls over evidence, versioning, and review.
Build capability within the Internal Audit team through coaching and knowledge transfer on analytics- and AI-enabled audit techniques, and contribute to the development of related methodology/standards.
Support the Head of Audit & Risk on strategic projects and function development initiatives as required.
Continuous Improvement & Governance
Contribute to strengthening investigation methodology, templates, and standard operating procedures.
Maintain strict confidentiality and independence, managing conflicts of interest appropriately.
Keep abreast of evolving fraud typologies, investigative techniques, and relevant regulatory requirements across M-KOPA’s markets.
Experience, Skills & Qualifications
Education
Degree in a business-related field, law, criminology, or a related field from a recognised university.
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) required.
Other certifications (e.g., CIA, CISA, forensic accounting, or investigations-specific credentials) are an added advantage.
Experience
Minimum of 8 years’ experience, with in-depth, hands-on experience conducting internal investigations (fraud, misconduct, harassment, or safeguarding-related), ideally within financial services, fintech, or a comparably regulated, multi-market environment.
Demonstrated experience preparing investigation findings and reports for senior management and/or Board-level audiences.
Skills
Unimpeachable personal integrity and sound ethical judgement — this role requires trust from all sides of a case.
Strong interviewing skills: able to build rapport, ask probing questions, and remain composed and neutral under pressure.
Excellent written communication — able to produce clear, factual, defensible case reports.
Discreet and calm under pressure; able to handle emotionally difficult and highly confidential matters with maturity.
Strong stakeholder management across HR, Legal, Risk, and country leadership.
Ability to manage a caseload independently, prioritising sensitively and appropriately across concurrent investigations.
Comfortable operating across multiple markets and cultures, with willingness to travel.

Job Description:
Job Overview
The Computer Management Assistant (CMA) shares responsibility for support of all equipment, applications, and cloud services at Embassy Nairobi. A senior member of the 17-person Information Systems Center, the CMA provides leadership and guidance to agile teams as a frequent technical project manager and lead. Additional duties include managing physical and virtual servers, routers, switches, cloud-based applications and services, mass data storage devices, virtual private network (VPN) connections, digital signage, audio visual solutions, and various other hardware and software which together provide access to one of the largest and most complex Embassies in the world. CMA also manages all forms of computer peripherals and networks host devices such as workstations, providing technical expertise and support to all users locally and remotely.
System Administration and Management – 25%
The incumbent proactively looks at potential network problems and ensures that the network continues to operate while maintaining a maximum possible uptime. The position coordinates with ENM, the ITSC, other relevant Washington offices, and the Nairobi CIS team to configure VPN devices, troubleshoot network latency, monitor line availability and client switch configurations and coordinates failover to VPN alt route, as necessary.
User Support - 25%
Computer Management Assistant provides advanced support to the IRM Help Desk Support Team and as such is responsible for the 'second and third tier' troubleshooting of all hardware, including PCs, printers, etc., and software, including support for post SharePoint office file shares, OneDrive and Office 365 tickets assigned by help desk coordinator. Once a ticket or task has been assigned, the position is expected to take responsibility for the issue, resolve it in a timely manner, write the steps taken in the Help Desk comments field and close the ticket, all while providing outstanding customer service.
The CMA analyzes user requests and provides technical guidance and suggest appropriate solutions to the end user, pointing the user to the best available tools of trade.
IT Consulting and Technical Project Management - 20%
The position is one of the lead IT consultants working closely with end users to identify gaps and provide customized solutions to their needs; introduces customers to new and better computing tools and solutions, conducting tech-talks sessions where necessary to bring users up to speed on the technology; and also serves as an advocate and champion for new tools and will help manage change with our user base, driving efficiencies, greater management oversight and transparency, and better collaboration across the interagency.
Mobile Computing Support - 15%
In support of an increasingly mobile workforce, the position sets up and configures smart mobile computing devices for use on different government system. Devices include tablets, smart phones, laptops, virtual and augmented reality headsets, mobile internet routers, public address systems, internet of things devices, and other gadgets as they emerge. The incumbent sets up these devices, registers and activates users on Department information platforms, and creates and maintains user accounts and authentication services to enable access to applications and services via Virtual Private Network (VPN). Such services include but not limited GO Mobile, GO Desktop and GO Virtual, and FAN.gov.
Systems Engineering and Design - 10%
The position is responsible for engineering and design of various systems for Nairobi. These systems include Audio Visual systems, virtual meeting rooms, conference centers, digital signage, DIN network architecture, and Public Diplomacy American Center spaces to name a few. The Computer Management Assistant also provides back-end technical support for these system on an ongoing basis; gathers user requirements and work with the IRM management in putting together scope of work (SOW) and bills of materials (BOM) for procurement actions. The position makes recommendations and provides guidance on appropriate technology considering that such system, component, or equipment are approved by Information Technology Configuration Control Board (ITCCB) or relevant office with the Department of State, for use on various networks, within Government facilities and are in strict compliance with Department security guidelines. Part of the duties include preforming constant reviews and evaluations of system and where necessary recommend upgrades, refreshes, or system re-engineering.
Other duties as assigned – 5%
This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by incumbent. The employee will be required to perform other duties as assigned by the agency.

Requirements:
All selected candidates must be able to obtain and hold a:
Security clearance.
Education Requirements:
A university degree in the field of Computer Science or Information Technology is required.

Under the supervision of the Senior Facility Manager, the Electrical Engineer Supervisor leads a team of skilled tradespersons and is responsible for maintaining all the New Embassy Compound (NEC) Electrical Power Distribution Systems, both interior and exterior. Operations and Maintenance Support (50%)
Serves as the Subject Matter Expert and oversees the operations and maintenance of large, complex, electrical systems and equipment including emergency generators and power generation equipment, medium and low-voltage switchgear, motor control centers; distribution panelboards and sub-panels; transformers; voltage regulators; automatic transfer switches; feeder wire and cabling; branch circuit wiring; lighting and power outlets, the fire alarm system and components, and uninterruptable power supply systems.
Resolves complicated complex electrical problems with minimal disruption to the NEC operations and restores these systems to their designed operating parameters and efficiency. Oversees an aggressive and comprehensive preventative maintenance program for critical and non-critical equipment and systems by directing subordinate electrical technicians from the facility maintenance staff, and/or monitoring contracted service providers, ensuring they use KPIs to analyze equipment and system performance, and that their repair and service techniques are code and life safety compliant.
Maintains; monitors; troubleshoots; configures; identifies; isolates and corrects faults; performs diagnostic tests; ensures the proper operations of designated equipment and systems.
Oversees the electrical operations and maintenance of Operating Leased properties to include large, complex, electrical systems and equipment including emergency generators and power generation equipment, medium and low-voltage switchgear, motor control centers; distribution panel boards and sub-panels; voltage regulators; automatic transfer switches; feeder wire and cabling; branch circuit wiring; lighting and power outlets, and uninterruptable power supply systems.
Resolves complicated electrical problems with minimal disruption to operating leased operations and restores these systems to their designed operating parameters and efficiency.
The value of oversight by the incumbent will be approximately $3 million.
Management and Logistic Support (35%)
Focused on all components of the electrical systems, the Electrical Engineer provides budget input for operating, maintenance and repair, and replacement costs to include all tools, special equipment and spare parts required to maintain all systems within the designed operational performance requirements and within operating budget limits.
Assist the Senior Facility Manager in briefing post management on work and project status. Attends senior level staff meetings, as delegated, to provide justifications for equipment/system outages for preventive maintenance, minor repairs, major overhauls, or replacement.
This position will assist in maintaining post’s Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) for the electrical department, in conjunction with post’s Work Control Clerk to ensure that planned preventative service events and unscheduled events are recorded/documented in the CMMS and closed out when they are completed.
Ancillary/Collateral Duties (15%)
Assists the Post Occupational Safety and Health Officer (POSHO) in the day-to-day management of the safety program. Provides weekly safety training to subordinate staff on various topics such as use of personal protective equipment (PPE), lock-out/tag-out procedures, ladder safety, and confined space entry safety.
Conducts daily inspections of facilities to ensure fire and life safety practices are in compliance with Department of State (DOS) fire and life safety requirements.
Develops deficiency reports with recommendations for solutions along with independent government cost estimates to bring facilities, especially electrical equipment and systems, into compliance.
Ensures that Overseas Buildings Operations (OBO) Fire and SHEM deficiency reports and action items are corrected in a timely manner, and that online reporting (SMARTS) requirements are kept up to date.

Job Description:
Purpose
The Cyber Security Administrator is responsible for safeguarding Kenya Airways' information systems, digital assets, and supporting infrastructure through offensive security operations primarily conducting penetration testing, red team simulations, adversary emulation, and vulnerability assessments to proactively identify and exploit weaknesses before malicious actors do. The role demands a hands-on, attacker-minded professional who can think creatively, adapt to evolving threat landscapes, and translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable remediation guidance that strengthens the organization's overall security posture.
Responsibilities
Identify, assess, and manage cybersecurity risks through defensive analysis and offensive testing. This includes evaluating both internal and external threats and vulnerabilities.
Develop risk mitigation strategies informed by threat monitoring and incident analysis, prioritizing security investments to protect critical assets against evolving threats.
Develop and implement the system-wide Information Security function of the information security program to ensure information security risks are identified and monitored.
Continuously identify, assess, and monitor information security risks across the organization and escalating emerging threats to inform defensive priorities.
Collaborate with developers, Systems engineers, database engineers, security engineers, project managers, cybersecurity administrators and SOC analysts.
Implement and fine tune security monitoring solutions, including SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) systems, to detect and respond to security incidents.
Collaborate with internal teams to investigate and mitigate security breaches.
Triage, investigate, contain, eradicate, and recover from security incidents while coordinating with internal teams and external partners as required.
Lead incident investigations using data-driven analysis, coordinate response efforts, and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence
Maintain and continuously improve incident response plans and playbooks for common attack scenarios.
Consume and operationalize threat intelligence feeds and adversary TTPs to proactively update detection rules, block emerging IOCs, and inform defensive priorities.
Deploy and maintain SOAR workflows to automate alert triage, enrichment, and routine response tasks reducing response times and analyst fatigue.
Oversee the deployment, configuration, and maintenance of security technologies, including EDR/XDR and encryption solutions among others.
Ensure all defensive systems are patched, updated, and operating at optimal performance with high availability.
Assist in executing vulnerability assessments, penetration tests, and adversary emulation exercises mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework to validate and stress-test defensive controls.
Collaborate with SOC analysts in purple team exercises and translate offensive findings into actionable defensive improvements.
Work with Internal Audit and External Audit consultants as appropriate on required security assessments and audits
Ensure all projects and systems are subjected to security checks to avert possible security threats pre and post go-live
Respond promptly to all system and network security breaches, ensuring containment, eradication, and recovery in line with documented procedures.
Implement automation (SOAR) within the organization to enable efficient alert triage, incident response workflows, and routine security operations.
Evaluate the organization's security needs and establish defensive best practices, hardening baselines, and configuration standards accordingly.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
Installer is a service professional who affix and position equipment in a designated location and complete the set-up process so the equipment is ready for operation or can serve its service purpose.
Their primary objective is to ensure the equipment is installed in a safe manner that doesn’t present any hazards while also supporting functionality to allow for the best possible performance.
They review and explain operation and maintenance information to the user or customer.
They will also provide ongoing support, maintenance, and repairs.Installers have a minimum of a high school diploma and may have completed a trade school program or training course. Hands-on experience installing and adjusting the particular equipment involved is preferred.
These roles are often physically demanding and may involve working in strenuous conditions.
Responsibilities
Coordinate with dispatch for daily appointments
Wear all identification, safety and courtesy equipment at all times.
Test electrical equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning of routers and service.
Carry material and stage for installer at the customer’s’ premises.
Guide, coordinate and oversee fellow installers.
Educate customers about benefits and up-sell to customers’ add-on sales products.
Evaluate and monitor the performance and quality standards of sub-contractors within their infrastructure boundaries.
Maintain installation tools and equipment in safe working order.
Educate customers on the features and functionality of installed products.
Assist with the completion of tasks within the allotted time frame.
Assist with parts, shipping, receiving and inventory as needed.
Review paperwork with customers where needed.
Assist in the removal and installation of materials in customer’s premises.
At times, crawl into small spaces, work in all climates and remain physically fit.
Qualifications
At least a certificate/diploma holder
Completion of a trade school program or technical training course is an added advantage.
Practical experience in installing and adjusting internet equipment (routers, cabling, electrical systems).
Familiarity with testing electrical equipment and ensuring safe functionality.
Ability to troubleshoot routers and service systems.
Knowledge of installation tools, electrical safety, and maintenance procedures.
Capable of working in strenuous conditions, crawling into small spaces, and handling installations in all climates.

Job Title: Driver S1, British Defence Staff East Africa
Job Description:
Job Description (Roles and Responsibilities)
Main purpose of job:
To provide transport services for the Defence Section, British Defence Staff, and related visitors to the Defence Section. On occasion, the post holder may be required to provide driving services in support of the British High Commission (BHC) and, more widely, on a case-by-case basis. Journeys will be to and from assigned destinations within Kenya.
Driving duties must be carried out in a safe, efficient, and courteous manner, with strict adherence to road traffic regulations, Ministry of Defence Transport Policy, Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) Transport Policy, British High Commission Transport Policy, and Post security regulations. Where there is any disparity between policies or regulations, the more stringent requirement will apply.
This is an exciting opportunity to work in one of Nairobi's largest diplomatic missions, providing all-round logistical support to the Defence Section. The successful applicant must hold a clean driving licence with Category C1 entitlement and have a minimum of five years' driving experience. Applicants are also required to have a good working knowledge of Nairobi, its surrounding areas, and other regions of Kenya.
The successful candidate will need to be highly organised and efficient in managing their time within a dynamic environment that is subject to change at short notice. They should be able to plan ahead, identify and select the most suitable routes for each journey, demonstrate initiative, and maintain the highest levels of discretion and professionalism. The individual must also be courteous in all interactions with internal and external stakeholders, acting as a representative of the Defence Section at all times.
Roles and responsibilities:
Work as part of a two-person Driver team supporting the Defence Section and British Defence Staff.
Ensure the cleanliness, maintenance, and professional presentation of Defence Section vehicle(s) at all times.
Conduct routine maintenance checks on Defence Section vehicles in accordance with the prescribed schedule. Ensure vehicles are roadworthy before commencing any journey by carrying out checks on tyres, fuel, oil levels, lubricants, spare tyres, jacks, and all mandatory safety equipment.
Report vehicle defects, incidents, and accidents promptly using the prescribed reporting procedures, documentation, and systems.
Drive both armoured and non-armoured Defence Section vehicles as required.
Meet and transport authorised passengers to and from airports, meetings, official engagements, and functions.
Accurately complete all official documentation relating to Defence Section vehicle journeys, including Expressway credit management records.
Work in accordance with an agreed shift pattern, including periods of being on call and occasional weekend working. There may also be a requirement to undertake occasional multi-day trips. Maximum driving hours will be in accordance with Ministry of Defence policy.
Ensure the safety and security of passengers by confirming that seat belts are worn and, where armoured vehicles are used, that passengers receive an appropriate safety and security brief.
Prepare and maintain a documented journey plan for long-distance travel. Be familiar with the operation of issued tracking devices, radios, and satellite telephones where applicable.
As directed, maintain communication with the Defence Section and/or British High Commission using the provided communications equipment and ensure that installed dashboard cameras are operated correctly.
Maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion with regard to all passengers, journeys, destinations, and official information.
Undertake other duties as agreed with the Defence Section, including, but not limited to, providing cover for colleagues during periods of authorised absence.
Essential qualifications, skills and experience
Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing.
Valid Police Clearance Certificate issued by the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Kenya.
Hold a clean and valid driving licence with the appropriate endorsement for driving Category C vehicles.
Good knowledge of Nairobi's road network, the locations of government offices, and the principal routes to other parts of Kenya.
Minimum of a Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) or equivalent secondary school qualification.
At least five years' experience working as a driver within a government, non-governmental organisation (NGO), corporate, or office environment.
Desirable qualifications, skills and experience
Experience driving civilian armoured vehicles (CAVs).
Working knowledge of the Kenyan military and the Ministry of Defence.
Experience of working with UK Government organisations, such as British Peace Support Team (Africa) (BPST(A)), British Army Training Unit Kenya (BATUK), and the British High Commission (BHC) Nairobi.
At least two years' experience working in, or in support of, a diplomatic mission, international organisation, or non-governmental organisation (NGO).
Experience of working with UK Five Eyes partners.
Good IT and computer skills would be advantageous.
A recognised First Aid certificate.
Required behaviours
Changing and Improving, Making Effective Decisions, Managing a Quality Service, Working Together

Job Description:
Role Summary
We are looking for a high-energy, technically strong Sales Engineer to support distribution growth across assigned East Africa markets, including Ethiopia, while being based in Nairobi, Kenya. The role will focus on market intelligence, distributor enablement, technical product support, customer relationship development, and opportunity identification.
Key Responsibilities
Market Development and Planning
Developing regional market development plans for Ethiopia and assigned surrounding markets, aligned with Timken’s regional growth objectives as directed by the manager.
Identify and map target customers, end users, distributors, engineering companies, mining operations, cement plants, power generation facilities, manufacturing companies, and other industrial prospects across assigned markets.
Collect market intelligence on customer needs, competitor activity, industry trends, importation considerations, and distributor capability to support regional planning.
Prepare non-binding account insights, opportunity summaries, and recommended actions for review and decision by the Manager.
Customer and Distributor Engagement
Build and maintain professional relationships with distributors, end users, maintenance teams, engineering teams, procurement stakeholders, and other industrial contacts.
Conduct planned customer and distributor visits to understand technical needs, application requirements, and potential product fit.
Support distributor development through technical guidance, product knowledge sharing, joint visits, and coordination of approved marketing activities.
Coordinate with internal teams, including Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Customer Service, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain, to support customer and distributor responsiveness.
Escalate all commercial matters, including pricing, discounts, terms, quotations, purchase order acceptance, and contract-related discussions, to the Manager.
Technical Support
Provide technical presentations, product information, product demonstrations, and application support for Timken bearing and power transmission product portfolios.
Support distributors and customers with technical product understanding, application considerations, and troubleshooting guidance within approved Timken processes.
Read and interpret technical mechanical drawings, specifications, and application information to support accurate internal recommendations.
Provide internal and external technical training on Timken products and applications where approved by the Country Manager.
Pipeline, Reporting and Compliance
Maintain accurate CRM records, visit reports, opportunity notes, customer requirements, and distributor engagement records.
Maintain pipeline visibility, demand planning, market feedback, and opportunity prioritisation.
Monitor competitor activity and communicate insights to the Manager for review and agreed response planning.
Follow Timken policies, local legal requirements, anti-bribery and anti-corruption standards, trade compliance requirements, and delegated authority limits at all times.
Track all cross-border travel and ensure travel activity remains aligned with approved business, tax, immigration, and legal guidance.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related Engineering discipline.
Minimum 4 years’ sales experience within industrial sectors such as bearings, mining, metals, cement, power generation, heavy industry, or industrial distribution.
Proven experience in technical sales, business development, distributor management, and customer relationship management within industrial markets.
Fluent in English, both written and verbal.
Fluent in Amharic, both written and verbal, with the ability to engage confidently with engineering, maintenance, and technical personnel in Amharic.
Valid, unendorsed driver’s license.
Valid passport with the ability and willingness to travel extensively into Ethiopia, including fly-in/fly-out travel where required.
Must be legally authorized to work in Kenya and be based near the Timken Kenya, Nairobi office – State house road.
Technical Skills
Strong understanding of mechanical engineering principles, rotating equipment, and industrial product applications.
Ability to read and interpret technical mechanical drawings and specifications.
Proficient in industrial product application, troubleshooting, and customer technical support.
Ability to conduct technical presentations, product demonstrations, and product training for customers and distributors.
Experience working with distributor/channel partner business models.
Understanding of industrial procurement processes, customer decision-making structures, and sales cycles.
Familiarity with pricing models, sales forecasting, reporting tools, and CRM systems.
Good command of Microsoft Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint.
Understanding of import/export processes, customs requirements, duties, tariffs, and logistics impacting business into Angola would be advantageous.
Preferred Experience
Previous business exposure to Ethiopia or experience supporting sales, distribution, or technical customer engagement in the Ethiopian market will be advantageous.
Existing network of contacts within Ethiopian industrial markets, distributor channels, engineering companies, mining, cement, power generation, manufacturing, or heavy industry would be beneficial.
Experience developing new territories, markets, distributors, or channel partner relationships across East Africa or similar emerging markets.
Familiarity with mining, cement, power generation, manufacturing, heavy industry, or industrial distribution sectors within Ethiopia and surrounding regional markets will be beneficial.
Experience working across multiple African countries, cultures, and distributor-led market environments.
Experience supporting the launch or expansion of business activity in a new or developing market, while operating within defined commercial authority and approval frameworks.
Personal Attributes
High-energy, self-motivated hunter mindset.
Entrepreneurial and self-starting approach.
Strong prospecting and business development capability.
Comfortable working independently in a developing territory.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
Problem-solving mindset with strong customer focus.
Proactive approach to market development.
Culturally adaptable, relationship-oriented, and resilient in challenging market conditions.
Strong team player who can collaborate effectively with Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and other internal stakeholders.
Company Details: The Timken Company is a global industrial leader with a growing portfolio of engineered bearings and power transmission product brands. With more than a century of knowledge and innovation, we continuously improve the reliability and efficiency of global industries to move the world forward. We w...read moreork with NASA to explore the mysteries of Mars. We partner with renewable-energy companies to power some of the world’s largest wind turbines. We help engineers improve global transportation, including drilling the world’s longest rail tunnel.To strengthen our position as a global industrial leader, we have grown our portfolio of product brands purposefully. Engineered bearing products continue to be core to our business and reflect our long-standing innovative power in moving global industries forward. Power transmission products are adjacent to our core business and increase our ability to serve the needs of global industries more fully. To leverage our portfolio’s potential and create additional growth, our strategy is threefold: outgrow markets, operate with excellence and optimize capital deployment.

Company Details:
Our purpose is to unlock value in Africa. We use our analytical capabilities to improve decision-making and, through better decisions, to unlock substantial value for our clients and society. While we are the largest economics-based consulting firm in Africa, we use a large number of techniques and...read moreapproaches to achieve clarity for decision-makers.

We work across various domains. 

Early specialisations were competition and regulatory economics, and then financial services strategy.

Since then we have added: agriculture and agribusiness, applied behavioural economics, infrastructure, health, monitoring and evaluation and shared value. We often combine our areas of expertise to craft services that recognise the multifaceted nature of our clients’ challenges and opportunities.

How does our work unlock value? 

How our work unlocks value depends on the challenge posed. We do it by figuring out the mobile entry strategy for a bank operating in a fast-growing market. By equipping a regulator with litigation-proof analysis to reduce mobile-phone termination rates, saving low-income consumers hundreds of millions of dollars a year. By devising a horticulture strategy for a large East African country that can create a hundred thousand jobs. By demonstrating how a climate-resilient water scheme can be restructured to serve thousands more households in needier areas.

Four convictions that infuse our work:

A focus on analytical strength. While economics is a core tool, we apply many other tools - financial, strategic and evaluative - to improve decisions and unlock value. We do this across a wide range of sectors and services, as is evident from the site. We pride ourselves on the quality of our analysis. Every professional in Genesis is equipped and indeed required to wield our analytical tools with rigour, imagination and - when called for - courage.

At home in both the private and public sectors - and especially where they meet. At Genesis, the same teams service both the corporate and the public sectors. Experience in the one, we believe, enriches our work in the other. As a result of this cross-learning, we are often asked to work in the zone where the market meets the state. One example is helping a financial services firm build competitive advantage in a harsh new regulatory environment. Another is devising a donor-funded intervention to enable catfish farmers in the Niger Delta to service their markets more effectively.

Ethics above expedience. The zone where the state meets the market is crowded with many actors, from the ethical to the expedient. We work hard to earn and maintain a reputation for rigour, ethics and fairness. We are also dedicated to improving the system we work and live in. These convictions add to our effectiveness for clients, as what we do and say is taken seriously by state and non-state entities alike. When we err, we own up to it and act swiftly to recover lost ground for our client.

A focus on the decision and how it is made. We aim to improve a wide range of decisions ranging from a regulatory process in a multi-billion-dollar industry to the nutrition decisions of a young woman in rural Rwanda. In all these cases there is much to understand about the decision-makers: their assumptions, their priorities, their constraints, their blind spots, their language, their way of thought. The better we understand the decision context, the more effective our advice.

Once a decision has been made, the real work begins. The decision needs to be communicated and coalitions for change built. Our work gathers the evidence, crafts the insights and anticipates likely objections to ease the next stages of communication, persuasion and implementation. We increasingly assist in implementation. 

A brief history
Stephan Malherbe founded Genesis Analytics in February 1998 with a staff of two in a 59 square-metre office in the Johannesburg suburb of Blairgowrie. The firm was the first specialist microeconomics consultancy in South Africa, microeconomics being the study of product, labour and capital markets.

The word 'genesis’ is derived from the ancient Greek word, which means to be born. Despite the strong biblical associations today, the word entered the English language only in the 17th century via Latin. Stephan called the firm Genesis because it was founded at a time of two beginnings: a rebirth for South Africa -just four years into democracy - and a new phase of growth for Africa. The hope was that the firm, small as it was, would be able to apply economic logic and would therefore be a catalyst for further growth and expansion in the region.
Making a positive impact

From the start, Genesis was an avowedly for-profit firm with the purpose of making a positive impact in South Africa. The idea was to use the disciplines of a business and an ability to reinvest earnings in order to work effectively in areas that have traditionally been the preserve of government or non-profit organisations.

Due to a combination of skills and circumstance, the firm’s work from the beginning has tended to be where the state meets the market and to this day state/market interface remains an important focus. Our earliest projects included developing strategies to increase investment, designing policy for a financial centre in Africa, and undertaking detailed work on a competition policy regime for South Africa. An important early project involved drafting a key report for the International Organisation of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) on the causes and implications of the 1998 emerging-market financial crisis.
Work in public and private sectors

Another early feature was a roster of clients split fairly equally between the public and private sectors. This is still the case today, and is embodied in our methodology of using the same teams for both public and private work. We believe that understanding the one sector enables Genesis to better advise the other. While this approach has proven to be beneficial for both corporate and government clients, it has also necessitated absolute clarity and consistency on ethics and conflicts of interest. This, too, has become a cornerstone of our ongoing approach. 

Stephan was joined by banking and financial specialist Richard Ketley in 2003 and industrial organisation and trade specialist James Hodge in 2005. Their arrival led to the launch of our financial services strategy and competition and regulatory practice areas. Another prominent early director, who joined in 2002, was Hennie Bester. He built up the firm’s capabilities in financial inclusion and is today a prominent independent consultant in financial inclusion and development strategy. 
Largest economics-based firm in the region

Within six years, Genesis had become the largest firm of its kind in the region, which it remains to this day. Its growth reflected the versatility of economic tools for understanding commercial, societal and political dynamics.

As a result, Genesis has become proficient in an ever larger number of domains. To our start in policy design we added financial deepening and inclusion, bank strategy, competition economics, utilities regulation, challenge fund design, development programme evaluation, infrastructure strategy and evaluation, programme design, behavioural economics and stakeholder strategy.

In the last three years, practice areas and teams have been established in infrastructure, agriculture and agribusiness, energy, health and behavioural economics. In 2015, a large team was split off from other development work to focus on monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and this is one of the most rapidly expanding and internationally active areas of the firm.

With its roots still firmly in South Africa, Genesis has rapidly internationalised in recent years. Approximately half of our revenue is generated outside South Africa and this proportion is increasing steadily. The African specialists operating out of the Johannesburg and Nairobi offices offer expertise in competition, regulation development and finance that we believe is unparalleled in the region. The firm is intent on building a cadre of African professional expertise that matches and exceeds international benchmarks of quality.
Educational fund for black economists

We are also proud of our South African roots. We have been a direct beneficiary of South Africa’s democratisation and of the historic compact that accompanied it. More than a decade ago, we therefore donated a 20% ownership stake in our South African operation (then the only one) to a purpose-created foundation in order to fund the education of black South African economists. Including current students, the foundation has funded graduate studies for more than 30 specialists in the field. Alumni of this programme have filled senior positions in the National Treasury, the Reserve Bank and the Competition Commission, among others. Many alumni have also worked for, or continue to work for, Genesis on a number of different teams.

Although Genesis is no longer solely an economics firm, we still employ many economists and work extensively in the area. Our economics roots have therefore formed our identity. Clarity of thought, analytical rigour, an evidence-driven approach, a thirst for getting to the truth of the matter: these parts of our DNA come from our grounding in economics.

The firm, which is still jointly owned by the founding partners and the foundation, has grown to include 15 partners and more than a hundred full-time staff
