Job Title: Head of AI & Program Technology Engineering
Job Description:
J
ob Overview:
This is a senior technical leadership role for someone who wants to build at the frontier of applied AI in service of humanitarian impact. You will lead a team of engineers and AI specialists designing and shipping AI-powered, program-facing solutions — primarily agentic systems, predictive analytics, and AI diagnostics deployed in low-resource and high-stakes settings.
You will own three things:
Technical strategy and direction for IRC's program-facing AI portfolio.
You will help translate IRC's AI ambitions into a clear technical roadmap, make build-vs-buy-vs-partner decisions, and set the architectural direction for systems that need to work reliably in some of the hardest operating environments on earth — including AI that runs offline on low-cost smartphones, agentic systems with high safety standards, and diagnostic models trained on populations the major datasets ignore.
A high-performing engineering team.
You will manage and grow a team of engineers, applied AI engineers, and QA specialists; raise the bar on engineering quality; and build the kind of culture that attracts top technical talent to mission-driven work.
Deep partnership with program leaders and strategic partners.
You will be a true thought partner to IRC's program experts in health, education, protection, resettlement, and emergency response — co-designing solutions with them rather than receiving requirements. You will also help us get maximum value from our flagship partnerships with Anthropic, OpenAI, and other frontier labs, with direct access to frontier models, early features, and the researchers building them.
Major Responsibilities

AI Strategic Leadership
Translate IRC's AI strategy and program priorities into a prioritized technical roadmap, in close partnership with program leaders, the SVP for Research, Innovation, AI, and People & Culture, and the T4P demand pipeline.
Stay at the edge of AI/ML advances — particularly in agentic systems, multimodal models, and edge/on-device inference — and bring promising approaches to IRC's programs.
Serve as a core member of IRC's AI leadership, helping shape organizational direction alongside the SVP for Research, Innovation, AI, and People & Culture and other senior leaders.
Champion responsible, human-centered AI deployment in some of the most sensitive humanitarian contexts in the world, with the safety standards those contexts demand.
Represent IRC in technical discussions with partners, peer organizations, donors, and the broader humanitarian and AI sectors.

Team Leadership and Management
Manage and develop a team of engineers, applied AI engineers, and QA specialists. Hire well, raise the bar, and build a culture that strong technical people want to be part of.
Establish engineering quality standards, development practices, and documentation protocols.
Maintain a prioritized backlog of program innovations and manage team capacity against demand.
Mature the team's AI development and DevOps practices and grow stakeholder buy-in across the organization.

About the Role
FinAgra is looking for a Chief Operating Officer – Kenya, to lead execution of our operating model as we scale our network of farms and REPs (Rural Entrepreneurial Partners) across the country.
This is a broad COO role responsible for translating company strategy into disciplined execution on the ground. The COO will directly lead Agronomy, Agricultural Operations, and the REP Program, while coordinating closely with Procurement, Finance, Commercial, Product, Technology, and other functions.
The role combines operational leadership, cross-functional coordination, organisational development, and execution discipline. A key part of the mandate is to build the systems, standards, and culture required for FinAgra Kenya to scale effectively.
This is a Kenya-based leadership role requiring full-time relocation. We welcome candidates currently based internationally who are ready to build and lead operations on the ground.
What You Will Do
Operational Leadership
Translate company and seasonal priorities into executable plans across teams, regions and farms.
Identify operational bottlenecks, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and ensure issues are escalated and addressed quickly.
Build scalable processes that allow FinAgra to grow across more REPs, farms and regions without losing execution quality.
Cross-Functional Execution
Lead Agronomy, AgOps, and the REP Program, and ensure these functions operate as one integrated system.
Coordinate execution across Operations, Procurement, Finance, Commercial, Product and Technology.
Ensure operational requirements are clearly defined and communicated to supporting functions.
Drive strong seasonal planning and alignment across functions.
Establish management routines, KPIs, reporting and escalation processes that provide visibility into execution.
Standards, Safety & Culture
Establish high standards of operational discipline, safety, ethics, transparency and accountability.
Build and enforce clear SOPs, management standards and operational controls.
Ensure strong standards around worker safety, machinery use, chemical handling and responsible farm operations.
Develop local managers and create a culture of ownership, problem-solving and professional management.
Build an organisation that can operate with increasing independence and consistency as FinAgra scales.
What We Are Looking For
7+ years of operational leadership experience, ideally as a COO, General Manager, Head of Operations, or similar.
Strong experience managing complex, distributed or multi-site operations.
Proven ability to build management systems, processes and operational discipline in a growing organisation.
Experience leading multiple functions and coordinating execution across teams.
Strong understanding of agriculture, and commercial farming operations.
Sufficient understanding of agronomy, mechanisation, and irrigation to effectively lead specialists and make informed operational decisions.
Sufficient experience in working with digital systems like ERP, farm management systems, etc.
Strong people leadership, performance management, and problem-solving skills.
Highly structured and execution-oriented, while able to operate at a strategic leadership level.
High standards of integrity, accountability, and professionalism.
Experience working across cultures, and in complex operating environments is highly desirable.
Willingness to relocate to Kenya, and spend significant time across FinAgra’s operating regions and farms.

Job Description:
About the role
This Senior Data Scientist role is broad – we are looking for someone who can sit at the intersection of data engineering, ecological data science, and technical product ownership. As Senior Data Scientist, you will be responsible for day-to-day data management and the building of automated data processing pipelines and visualizations. You will also be involved in applying discriminative machine learning and ecological modeling approaches to processing and analyzing biodiversity data and designing and building ecological decision support tools within our Natural State Analytics platform.
This role owns data pipeline design, requirements, testing, and validation. Pipeline implementation may be carried out by you, the Technology team, or collaboratively depending on the project. This will include designing dynamic, structured field survey forms (in ODK) and data ingestion pipelines that ensure raw field data are cleaned, processed, and joined correctly to become analysis-ready datasets that can be exported for different end users. Your role will also include analyzing field datasets into decision-support metrics that can be displayed on platform dashboards and be used to generate project reports, under guidance from Project Delivery and Biometrics.
Our Project Delivery and Biometrics teams decide how data collection should be done, what quality checks matter, and what data dashboards need to show. You will turn these requirements into precise, buildable specifications for the Technology team to implement on the platform and then verify what gets built. You will not need to write all the backend code yourself, Natural State's Technology team owns most implementation, but you do need to be comfortable building data pipelines (in SQL) and writing and executing data analysis functions (in Python or similar). Most importantly, you need to understand the Natural State science database and principles deeply enough to specify exactly what should be built, ask the right questions before it's built, independently check the result once its built, and communicate that information clearly to external technical and non-technical audiences.
There is a lot of scope for growth within this role. We envision the first 6-12 months to be heavily focused on creating and improving data management pipelines. Once those systems become less time consuming to maintain, we hope you will bring your imagination and expertise to help us build data tools within the Natural State Analytics platform that inform better decision making and help us achieve our mission of Restoring the Natural World.
This role is for you if...
You have a strong technical background and are wanting to use your skills on real-world, applied biodiversity conservation and restoration projects.
You have ideas about how biodiversity data can be leveraged to make better decisions and you are excited to implement these.
You are detail-oriented and diligent, with a keen understanding of the importance of well-curated data and a passion for creating pipelines to support this.
You thrive in a remote work environment and are able to effectively manage your own workload without needing too much top-down direction.
You enjoy working in a small, high-performance team and pitching in where you’re needed.
Requirements
Must have: 5+ years of work experience and a degree in data science, computer science, statistics, mathematics, quantitative ecology or a related field plus experience working with ecological/biodiversity data (e.g. camera trap images, passive acoustic monitoring recordings, vegetation surveys, animal surveys, species lists, soil carbon, biomass, remote sensing observation, climate etc.).
Must have: Strong Python for scientific data work - pandas or polars for data handling, plus the analysis stack (numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn or equivalent). Comfortable writing validation scripts that catch schema mismatches early and explain clearly what broke.
Must have: Strong statistical reasoning, including an understanding of concepts such as confidence intervals, uncertainty estimation, GLMs, and discriminative machine learning models.
Must have: Confident in SQL, joins, CTEs, window functions.
Must have: Comfortable investigating data issues independently in pgAdmin, DBeaver, or similar.
Strongly desired: Able to handle spatial data in PostGIS, QGIS, and GeoPandas - raster algebra, coordinate reference systems and reprojection, vector versus raster, and the common ways location data breaks.
Strongly desired: Experience working with remote sensing data.
Nice to have: Experience with ODK, KoboToolbox, Survey123, or a comparable field data collection platform (ODK Central admin experience is a plus).
Job Field: Data, Business Analysis and AI,ICT / Computer

Job Description:
We are looking for a detail-oriented and reliable Finance Assistant to join our team in Nairobi, Kenya.
In this role, you will be responsible for overseeing daily financial operations, including cash flow monitoring, banking transactions, foreign currency management and accurate financial record-keeping.
You will play a key role in ensuring regulatory compliance, maintaining strong relationships with financial institutions, and supporting the smooth execution of payments and treasury activities. The ideal candidate should have a strong understanding of Kenyan financial regulations, a proactive approach to internal controls, and the ability to support audit readiness and uphold overall financial integrity.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Cash and Bank Management: Oversee daily bank and cash operations including reconciliations, monitoring liquidity, managing petty cash and preparation of regular cash position reports to ensure accurate and timely financial visibility.

Regulatory Compliance and Reporting: Ensure adherence to Kenyan tax laws and financial regulations, support statutory filings and contribute to the implementation of controls and reporting improvements across finance functions.
Foreign Currency and Exchange Management: Manage foreign currency transactions by securing favourable exchange rates, accurately updating system rates, and executing compliant currency purchase transactions with local banks.
Cross-Functional Support: Collaborate with banks, suppliers, auditors, and internal teams to support smooth financial operations, budgeting and ad hoc tasks assigned by Management.

Hands-on experience with ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite, SAP or Oracle) and strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel for data analysis and reporting.
Results-oriented with ability to maintain a high standard of service level.
Trustworthy and able to deal with confidential information in an appropriate and sensitive way; does not divulge the company's sensitive information.
Highly developed interpersonal and communication skills coupled with the ability to negotiate and influence at all levels within the business.

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE STATEMENT
The job holder is responsible for managing the overall all end-to-end customer experience within the Group through all channels and touchpoints using well defined standards and processes. The role oversees and leads the improvement of all aspects of the customer journey, ensuring satisfaction and loyalty throughout the customer lifecycle with a focus on creating positive customer impact and hence a positive impact on the company’s bottom line. These includes:
Developing and implementing customer experience strategies and initiatives.
Analyzing customer feedback and data to identify improvement opportunities.
Ensuring consistent and positive customer interactions across all touchpoints.
Collaborating with cross functional teams to enhance customer satisfaction.
Monitoring customer metrics and reporting on CX performance.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Customer Experience Standards
Define, implement and review the organization’s customer experience standards and guidelines and align them to overall corporate strategic goals.
Review the standards and guidelines in line with changing regulations and market dynamics.
Create strategic alignment for Customer Experience KPIs and ownership throughout the organization.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align customer experience efforts with business goals and objectives.
Customer Service Excellence Management
Be the voice of the customer and drive processes to identify and close gaps in the customer experience based on direct and indirect customer feedback.
Monitor and measure key performance indicators (KPIs) related to customer satisfaction, retention, and loyalty, providing regular reports and insights to senior management and stakeholders.
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to drive internal customer satisfaction and build strong customer relationships.
Collect, collate and analyze customer feedback and data to provide insights into customer needs, identify pain points and improve the customer journey.
Business Process Management
Establish and manage key customer experience processes, including customer contact facilities, interaction models and complaint tools.
Monitor customer retention trends and manage performance metrics.
Compile and analyze monthly reports to track customer service performance, including metrics such as customer satisfaction and conversion rates.
Ensure regulatory and risk-related compliance of all processes at all times.
Manage change related to customer experience processes and systems.
Customer Feedback Management and Reporting
Collect customer feedback and data via surveys and all other feedback channels.
Communicate findings to relevant stakeholders and design interventions to create a positive customer experience.
Monitor and report on the implementation of intervention initiatives.
Identify customer pain points and recommend ways to improve the customer journey.
Continuous Improvement
In collaboration with business leadership, develop and implement initiatives to improve customer interactions across multiple touchpoints and channels for all business units.
Follow up on implementation of improvement initiatives, report on progress and analyze impact.
Review and continuously improve on initiatives.
People Management
In collaboration with HR, recruit, train, coach and mentor the customer service team.
Evaluate and monitor effectiveness of training programs.
Develop, assign, monitor and review team member targets.
Manage team discipline, build and motivate the team for optimal performance, and drive organizational culture.
Other duties assigned from time to time
QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS
University degree or equivalent in Business Administration, Business Management, Communications, Public Relations, Marketing or a related field. An MBA will be an added advantage.
Minimum of 10 years’ experience in Customer Experience or Business Operations, 5 of which should have been in a leadership/supervisory capacity.
Relevant experience in the Service Industry, Telecommunications, Banking, Insurance or similar customer-centric industries.
Customer Experience or Service Excellence certification will be an added advantage.
Experience leading change and inspiring teams with an exciting future vision.
Proven ability to define and implement CX standards, manage feedback systems and drive continuous improvement across multiple channels and touchpoints.
COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS
Excellent communication, interpersonal and negotiation skills.
Strong leadership and people management skills.
Business acumen and commercial awareness.
Team working and collaboration skills.
Knowledge and experience of business process review to provide guidance on strategic / continuous improvement.
Technical skills to effectively perform and guide performance of Business and Operations teams’ activities to consistently achieve high quality standards.
Ability to analyze customer data, identify insights and translate them into actionable improvements.
Strong stakeholder management and change management capabilities.

Job Description:
Code for Africa (CfA) is recruiting a bilingual full-time
Digital Security Engineer
to lead
technical incident response and security assessments
at
TrustLab
, our nonprofit digital security lab working to safeguard frontline human rights defenders (HRDs), journalists and civil society organisations across Africa and the majority world.
Candidates should possess a strong background in endpoint security and incident response, with demonstrable experience in providing support, conducting security assessments, investigating breaches, and implementing hardening measures across various devices and operating systems. Ideally, you have a deep understanding of the threat landscape in Africa and experience working with non-profit organisations or in the development sector.
This is both an engineering and a duty-of-care role. The people who contact TrustLab may be non-technical, under significant stress, or facing threats that extend well beyond their devices. We practise consent-first, victim-centred and trauma-informed incident response: we explain what we propose to examine, respect the limits of the client’s consent, minimise what we collect, and communicate the confidence and limitations of our findings honestly.
Candidates must be fluent in English and French, and candidates who are fluent in an additional international language, such as Arabic or Portuguese, will have an advantage.
Required
: minimum requirements include:
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity, and similar technology degrees, or equivalent technology experience,
Demonstrable experience supporting high-risk users like journalists and activists.
3+ years experience in security engineering, or a similar role, with a strong focus on incident response and endpoint and application security,
Experience with endpoint security tools and techniques, such as Mobile Device Management and anti-malware,
Hands-on experience investigating and responding to security incidents, including triage, forensic analysis, evidence preservation, containment, recovery and post-incident review, using SIEM, EDR or comparable security tools where appropriate,
Experience conducting risk-based security assessments using techniques such as secure configuration review, vulnerability assessment, threat modelling or authorised penetration testing, and translating findings into practical, prioritised remediation,
Experience with identity and access management such as MFA, SSO, least-privilege provisioning and deprovisioning,
Experience with scripting languages for security automation (Python and shell scripting).
Deep practical knowledge of macOS and iOS, including secure configuration, endpoint management, incident investigation and relevant security tooling, together with demonstrated ability to assess and support mixed-device environments,
Passion for using technology to empower and protect civil society organisations,
Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities and tasks, and deliver results within deadlines,
Excellent technical documentation and presentation skills, and
Proven ability to work and communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Preferred
: candidates who can demonstrate the following will have an advantage:
Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, or similar technology postgraduate degrees,
Expertise in one or more of the following domains is highly desirable: Penetration Testing, Cloud Security, and Cryptography,
Familiarity with security risks involving generative-AI or agentic systems, and with the responsible, privacy-preserving use of AI-assisted tools in security workflows,
Working knowledge of Windows, Linux and Android, including their secure configuration, common security controls and relevant investigation tooling,
Hold one or more relevant security certifications such as eJPT, Security+, GCIH, CySA+, OSCP,
Extensive knowledge of digital security issues and threat vectors in the African context,
Experience working with non-profit organisations or in the development sector is a plus, and
Experience working in a fully remote environment.
Language and Location Requirements:
Location: Remote. Candidates must be able to maintain at least four hours of overlap with the team’s core collaboration hours of 09:00–17:00 GMT+1.
Timezone: GMT-1 to GMT+5
Languages: English and French
Nice to have: Arabic or Portuguese.
Company Details: Code for Africa (CfA) uses technology and #OpenData to empower citizens. We give citizens actionable information for better-informed decision making and digital tools to amplify their voices, so that they can hold the authorities (both governmental and corporate) to account. We do this in a numbe...read morer of ways: firstly, by liberating the data currently locked up in governments and corporations, and using this information to build open data / open government digital "backbone""‹ infrastructure. Job Title: Experienced Zoomlion Concrete Pump Truck Operator
Job Description:
We are seeking one highly experienced, competent and safety-conscious Concrete Pump Truck Operator to operate a ZOOMLION concrete pump mounted on a SITRAK / SINOTRUK 3-axle chassis. This is a specialized equipment-operator position, not a general truck-driving position. The successful candidate must have practical concrete pump operating experience, understand boom deployment and stabilization, concrete pumping procedures, hydraulic systems and construction-site safety. Applicants without genuine concrete pump operating experience are unlikely to be considered.
Responsibilities and Duties
Safely drive and position the concrete pump truck at construction sites.
Assess ground and site conditions before setup.
Correctly deploy stabilizers or outriggers and the 5-section boom.
Operate the concrete pump and boom within manufacturer safety limits.
Coordinate concrete supply with mixer-truck drivers and site teams.
Monitor concrete flow, pumping pressure and equipment performance.
Safely manage concrete delivery pipes, hoses, clamps and connections.
Recognise and respond appropriately to blockages and abnormal pressure.
Maintain safe clearance from workers, structures, excavations and overhead hazards.
Conduct pre-operation and post-operation equipment inspections.
Clean and secure the pump, boom and delivery system after operations.
Identify mechanical, hydraulic and electrical faults.
Report defects, incidents, breakdowns and safety hazards immediately.
Maintain accurate equipment and operational records.
Follow all site safety procedures and PPE requirements.
Minimum Requirements
Hold a valid Kenyan driving licence appropriate for the vehicle being operated (Class CE).
Have substantial heavy-commercial-vehicle and specialized equipment experience.
Have demonstrable experience operating truck-mounted concrete pumps.
Understand concrete pumping, boom operation and stabilization procedures.
Have practical mechanical and hydraulic troubleshooting skills.
Be capable of working around heavy machinery and demanding site conditions.
Comply fully with Kenyan law, NTSA requirements and company procedures.
Direct experience with ZOOMLION concrete pumps.
Experience with SITRAK / SINOTRUK heavy vehicles.
Experience operating 40m+ concrete pump booms.
Heavy diesel, hydraulic or plant-equipment experience.
Experience on major construction projects.
Clean and verifiable professional driving record.
The operator must comply with applicable Kenyan traffic laws, NTSA requirements, commercial-vehicle regulations, occupational safety requirements, manufacturer operating procedures and company policies. The operator must never compromise personnel safety, vehicle stability, boom safety, concrete-line safety or equipment integrity for speed of operation. Safety, professionalism and responsible equipment operation are non-negotiable.

Job Description:
Summary of the job title
The Project Coordinator is being recruited initially to coordinate the implementation of the WAHAFA-supported Building Early Action Capacity through local Ownership and cross-border Networks (BEACON) Omo-Turkana project. The project focuses on the Omo River-Lake Turkana cross-border corridor, with work in Turkana County in Kenya and the adjoining South Omo area of Ethiopia. Its central objective is to coordinate the participatory development, testing and validation of one locally owned, operational and protection-sensitive cross-border Early Action Protocol (EAP) for drought and flooding.
Reporting to the Country Representative - Kenya, the Project Coordinator will initially be fully dedicated to the BEACON Omo-Turkana project and will provide strong day-to-day coordination, leadership, grant and project management, monitoring and evaluation, documentation, learning and reporting. The Coordinator will work closely with SoH Kenya and Ethiopia teams, SoH Germany, the relevant cross-border programme team and structures, local implementing partners, government and technical stakeholders, and other actors involved in anticipatory action. While the initial primary focus is the BEACON project, the Coordinator may, subject to organizational needs, workload and applicable donor requirements, be assigned to support other SoH humanitarian and development projects in Kenya and the wider region.
Core duties
Project Coordination and EAP Development
Coordinate day-to-day implementation of the BEACON Omo-Turkana project in accordance with the approved proposal, workplan, budget, donor requirements and SoH policies and procedures.
Coordinate the participatory development, testing and validation of the cross-border Early Action Protocol for drought and flooding, ensuring that the Kenya and Ethiopia workstreams progress as one coherent process.
Maintain and regularly update the Project Implementation Plan, milestone and deliverables tracker, and follow up agreed actions, responsibilities and deadlines with the project teams and partners.
Coordinate key technical and implementation processes, including risk and vulnerability analysis, stakeholder mapping, forecast and indicator review, trigger development and validation, early action prioritization, readiness planning, scenario exercises, simulation and final EAP validation.
Coordinate project meetings, field missions, community consultations, technical workshops and validation processes, ensuring that required inputs and follow-up actions are completed on time.
Identify implementation challenges and emerging risks, facilitate timely corrective action and escalate issues requiring management or technical decisions.
Ensure project activities and outputs are delivered to the required quality standard and remain aligned with the project’s cross-border design and intended results.
Support preparation and consolidation of the final cross-border EAP and its country-specific operational annexes, ensuring that technical and community inputs are reflected clearly.
Cross-Border Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as the principal day-to-day coordination link between SoH Kenya, SoH Ethiopia, SoH Germany, the Diocese of Lodwar, Catholic Caritas Ethiopia-Soddo and relevant cross-border programme structures.
Coordinate and, where required, serve as secretariat to the Cross-border EAP Steering Committee/Coordination Group, including preparation of meetings, documentation of decisions and follow-up of agreed actions.
Facilitate effective engagement with county, regional, zonal, woreda and local authorities, disaster risk management structures, meteorological and hydrological institutions, sector departments, technical working groups and other relevant anticipatory action actors.
Maintain clear and timely communication and information flow across the Kenya and Ethiopia workstreams, ensuring technical, community and partner inputs are consolidated consistently into project outputs.
Work closely with SoH cross-border programmes and other relevant humanitarian and development initiatives to strengthen complementarity, institutional relationships, coordinated learning and efficient use of existing structures.
Grants, Financial and Operational Management
Coordinate implementation of the institutional donor grant and ensure compliance with agreed objectives, contractual conditions, timelines, donor regulations and SoH internal procedures.
Work closely with Finance to monitor budget utilization and project expenditure, review budget-versus-actual performance, identify variances and support timely corrective measures or budget revisions where required.
Coordinate partner workplans, budgets, reporting schedules and grant deliverables, and follow up with partners to ensure timely and compliant implementation.
Work with procurement, logistics, finance and administration colleagues to ensure timely operational support for project activities, field missions, workshops and other implementation requirements.
Maintain complete and well-organized project and grant documentation and contribute to donor reporting, grant reviews, audits, compliance checks and any approved project modifications.
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, Learning and Documentation
Coordinate project monitoring systems and tools, including indicator tracking, activity monitoring, milestone tracking and consolidation of monitoring information from the Kenya and Ethiopia workstreams.
Undertake and coordinate regular field monitoring, project review and reflection processes, and ensure that findings are used to improve implementation quality and decision-making.
Ensure high-quality documentation of consultations, technical decisions, implementation progress, challenges, adaptations, lessons learned and good practices throughout the project cycle.
Prepare and coordinate timely, accurate and high-quality narrative, technical and management reports, learning products, case studies, presentations and other project documentation as required by SoH and the donor. Promote systematic learning and information sharing between SoH, partners, government and technical stakeholders, and ensure lessons from the Build phase inform future anticipatory action and wider humanitarian and development programming.
Capacity Strengthening and Wider Programme Support
Identify capacity-strengthening needs among project teams and partners and coordinate appropriate technical, project management, grant management, monitoring, documentation and learning support.
Promote adherence to humanitarian principles, relevant humanitarian standards, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, protection mainstreaming and conflict-sensitive programming.
Contribute, as assigned, to assessments, project design, proposal and concept-note development, reporting, reviews and other programme quality processes relevant to SoH humanitarian and development work. Subject to organizational priorities, workload and donor requirements, provide coordination, grant management, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, documentation and learning support to other SoH humanitarian and development projects in Kenya and the wider region.
The duties and responsibilities set out above are not exhaustive. The Project Coordinator may be required to undertake other reasonable assignments consistent with their skills and experience. Although the initial assignment is centred on the BEACON Omo-Turkana project, the post holder should be prepared to support other SoH humanitarian and development projects when requested and where this is compatible with donor requirements and agreed priorities.
Candidates’ profile
A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Risk Management, International Development, Project Management, Humanitarian Action, Development Studies, Climate Change, Natural Resources Management, Social Sciences, Public Health or another relevant field.
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in project or programme coordination/management, preferably in humanitarian, resilience, disaster risk reduction or development programming.

JOB PURPOSE
Sitting within the Evidence Lab, the Investigator, Arms and Armed Conflict will work with research teams across Amnesty International, including regional and thematic specialists, to proactively lead and support investigations into lethal and less-lethal weapons, operations by militaries, police, and other security-forces, arms transfers and the changing nature of armed conflict, with a focus on their human rights and international humanitarian law (IHL) implications.
Combining advanced expertise in weapons and armed conflict with strong investigative, open-source research and writing skills, the postholder will design and conduct multidisciplinary investigations, and produce rigorous, accessible and visually compelling research outputs.
A central part of the role will be to help develop Amnesty International's work on new warfare, investigating the human rights impacts of evolving technologies and systems in armed conflict and other crises, including hybrid warfare, remote and autonomous weapons, targeting and other AI enabled military technologies.
The role will contribute to Amnesty International's efforts to produce specific findings about responsibility for grave violations, including identifying relevant individuals, military and security-force and law enforcement units, corporate actors, suppliers and other entities based on rigorous research and strong evidence.
The role will also provide specialist analysis and advice to Amnesty International research teams responding to conflicts, protests and other crises, including on weapons identification, remote battle damage assessments and post-blast analysis, attribution and responsibility, the conduct of hostilities and use of force, weapons transfers and supply chains and other relevant topics.
LOCATION
The preferred location location for this role is London, however we will also consider Mexico City, Dakar, Nairobi and Johannesburg.
The salary on offer will be dependent on the location.
MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES
Work with regional offices, thematic programmes and researchers to proactively identify research opportunities and lead or support multidisciplinary investigations relating to weapons, military, security-force and law enforcement operations, arms transfers and changing forms of warfare, drawing on monitoring of conflicts, technological developments, digital evidence and emerging human rights concerns.
Lead or substantially contribute to reports, briefings, press releases and multimedia outputs, translating complex findings into clear and accessible language for non-technical audiences.
Work with researchers, legal and policy advisers to ensure findings are well supported and grounded in relevant international human rights and humanitarian law standards.
Bring a strong editorial and communications vision to investigations, combining rigorous research, compelling writing and powerful visual evidence
Work with communications, campaigns and design colleagues to translate findings into media, multimedia, and social media content that reaches and resonates with diverse audiences.
SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
Substantial professional experience conducting complex investigations relating to weapons, armed conflict, military,security-force or law enforcement operations, arms transfers, ideally in the context of human rights documentation, investigative journalism or another closely related public-interest field.
Strong portfolio of advanced digital investigations/ research projects that demonstrate the ability to carry out complex research and produce high-quality outputs, showcasing advanced expertise in a digital investigations field.
Demonstrable advanced expertise in firearms, explosive ordnance, and less-lethal weapons, including practical experience identifying weapons and ordnance from visual and documentary evidence and a strong understanding of weapons employment, explosive effects and relevant military and law-enforcement doctrine.
Experience investigating weapons use and attack reconstruction, attribution and responsibility, military operations, arms transfers and supply chains, or emerging military technologies.
Experience investigating the trade in and misuse of law enforcement equipment, including identifying common types of lethal and less lethal weapons and their use in human rights violations.

Job Description:
Job Summary
Provide dedicated finance and accounting support for the project “Accelerating Adaptation Action Through Faith-Led Advocacy in Africa”, ensuring accurate project accounting, close monitoring of expenditure against the budget, compliance with donor and ACT Alliance requirements, timely financial reporting and complete supporting documentation. The position will work closely with project and finance colleagues to monitor expenditure and compliance and to support effective financial management throughout the project cycle.
Key Responsibilities
Common Accountabilities
Contribute to one integrated ACT Alliance, operating under shared strategic direction, annual workplans and ways of working.
Promote accountability, dignity, inclusion, non-discrimination, gender equity and locally led approaches in line with ACT values and policies.
Work collaboratively with project, programme and finance colleagues to strengthen quality, accountability, compliance and learning.
Ensure compliance with ACT Alliance policies, including the Code of Conduct, safeguarding, conflict of interest, complaints, safety and security, travel, environmental and finance-related policies
Contribute to planning, monitoring, reporting, learning and risk management processes of the Secretariat and relevant project teams.
Role-Specific Responsibilities
Project accounting: Maintain accurate project financial records, accounting codes and supporting documentation in accordance with donor requirements and ACT Alliance financial procedures.
Budget monitoring: Closely monitor project expenditure against the approved donor budget, identify variances and emerging underspend/overspend risks, and provide timely analysis to project management.
Donor compliance: Review project expenditure to ensure costs are eligible, reasonable, appropriately authorised and supported in accordance with donor rules and approved project arrangements.
Financial reporting: Prepare timely and accurate financial information and donor financial reports, ensuring consistency between accounting records, project budgets and reported expenditure.
Expenditure review: Review invoices, contracts, payment documentation and other supporting records, ensuring expenditure is properly documented, correctly coded and appropriately allocated to the project.
Project management support: Work closely with the project team to provide budget monitoring information, explain variances and support informed financial decision-making.
Sub-grants, partners and reconciliations: Monitor the financial aspects of sub-grants and implementing partner expenditure, including financial reports, supporting documentation and compliance. Reconcile project financial records, investigate discrepancies and ensure identified issues are followed up and resolved.
Audits and budget revisions: Prepare financial documentation for donor audits and reviews, support responses to audit queries and contribute financial inputs to donor budget revisions and amendments as required.
Supervision & Accountability
Finance Officer reports to the Project Manager as line manager & Finance Manager as technical manager and works closely with the project team and relevant finance colleagues. Key working relationships include: Project Manager; Finance Manager; project and programme colleagues; implementing partners; and donor representatives/auditors as required.
Skills and experiences
Education: University degree or professional qualification in finance, accounting, business administration, grants management or a related field.
Experience: At least 3–5 years of relevant finance and project accounting experience, preferably within an international NGO, donor-funded project or similar environment.
Demonstrated experience in project accounting, budget monitoring, donor financial reporting and compliance.
Good knowledge of donor financial requirements and experience checking expenditure eligibility against donor rules and approved budgets.
Experience monitoring project expenditure, reviewing supporting documentation, reconciling accounts and investigating variances.
Experience working with sub-grants or implementing partners and reviewing partner financial reports is desirable.
Strong Excel skills and experience with accounting or financial management systems.
Languages: Excellent written and spoken English; knowledge of relevant local languages is an asset.
Core Competences and behaviours
Commitment to ACT Alliance’s faith-based, rights-based and locally led humanitarian and development mission.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate, timely and well-documented financial management.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work constructively with finance, programme and project colleagues.
Sound judgement, integrity and ability to identify and raise financial, compliance and documentation issues appropriately.
Ability to work independently, manage deadlines and maintain effective financial controls within a part-time project role.

Job Title: Tax Manager for Professional Services Firm
Job Description:
Job Summary
We are a mid-sized, full-service professional firm offering audit, book-keeping, tax, company secretarial, and advisory services. To support our expanding tax services division at our Kisumu office, we are seeking a proactive and dynamic Tax Manager. Reporting directly to the Managing Partner, you will oversee a full range of tax engagements, drive KRA dispute resolutions, publish client tax updates, build high-level stakeholder relationships, and actively mentor our growing team.
The Opportunity
We are a fast-growing, high-quality professional audit, tax, company secretarial, and advisory firm with offices in Nairobi and Kisumu, Kenya. We are a meritocratic firm committed to training our staff and encouraging knowledge sharing among team members. In line with our rapid expansion, we are seeking a highly motivated, experienced, and talented
Tax Manager
to join our dynamic leadership team.
This role offers an exceptional career progression opportunity for the right candidate, with direct reporting to the Managing Partner, oversight of high-value tax engagements, and key leadership responsibilities.
Key Responsibilities
Tax Advisory, Compliance & Risk Management
Oversee a full range of tax services provided to clients, including drafting tax opinions and managing engagements across direct and indirect taxation (Income Tax, Transfer Pricing, Value Added Tax, Customs & Excise).
Provide high-level tax advisory services, review complex corporate and individual income tax returns, identify potential tax risks, and implement robust mitigation strategies.
Lead engagement teams undertaking tax due diligence and tax health check engagements.
Continuously improve internal processes by developing and implementing best practices to optimize our tax services.
KRA Management, Dispute Resolution & Stakeholder Relations
Oversee the handling of KRA tax audits, in-depth investigations, objections, and formal appeals.
Assist clients to prepare, navigate, and defend tax disputes before the Tax Appeals Tribunal (TAT).
Actively follow up with the revenue authority on client issues, including client tax status, ledger reconciliations, tax clearance applications, and compliance reviews.
Build, maintain, and strengthen professional relationships with key external stakeholders, including clients, the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), and The National Treasury.
Thought Leadership & Client Communication
Author and distribute regular tax articles, technical briefs, and client newsletters detailing emerging tax laws, court rulings, and Finance Act changes.
Proactively keep clients, internal departments, and firm partners updated on current tax developments, legislative shifts, and potential tax risks.
Organize and lead client workshops, webinars, or tax alerts to establish the firm as a thought leader in tax advisory.
Team Leadership, Mentorship & Capacity Building
Drive the growth of the tax division by actively mentoring, coaching, and "bringing up" junior tax associates and seniors to handle complex engagements.
Conduct structured internal training sessions to ensure audit and tax staff remain updated on tax laws, compliance changes, and internal best practices.
Provide strong personnel management to foster a high-performing, motivated tax team capable of taking on new clients and expanded service offerings.
Client Engagement & Audit Coordination
Serve as the primary engagement liaison with clients, including agreeing on engagement timeframes, deliverables, and operational logistics.
Coordinate seamlessly with the audit department to ensure statutory deadlines and reporting schedules are met without conflict.
Deliver exceptional client service, building long-term, trust-based client relationships to support business development.
Qualifications & Requirements
Experience:
Minimum of 5 years of proven work experience as a Tax Manager in a busy professional audit/tax firm.
KRA & Regulatory Relations:
Demonstrated experience directly dealing with the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) in all tax matters, audits, and dispute resolution processes.
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Law or Business-related field (Finance, Accounting, Economics) from an accredited university.
Professional Qualifications:
Must be a CPA-K or ACCA member in good standing.
Technical Mastery:
Excellent, deep knowledge of Kenyan law, accounting standards (IFRS), tax compliance, and all tax types (direct, indirect, transfer pricing, customs).
Leadership & Communication:
Exceptional leadership, personnel management, analytical, and writing skills (with a focus on drafting clear technical articles and newsletters).
Work Ethic:
Self-driven, proactive, and able to work hard and smart to deliver exceptional client results under pressure.
Why Join Us?
Career Growth:
Meritocratic culture offering clear pathways for professional advancement and direct access to firm leadership.
Dynamic Environment:
Collaborative workspace committed to knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and diverse advisory work.
Competitive Package:
Attractive remuneration package aligned with experience and industry benchmarks.

The Strategic Communications Manager leads communications for Amref Health Africa in Kenya. The purpose of the role is to protect and build trust in Amref among government, county, community, partner and donor audiences, and to turn that trust into influence that advances the organization’s advocacy, programme, partnership and resource mobilization priorities. The manager leads the country communications strategy, advises the Country Director and Senior Management Team on positioning, reputation and stakeholder engagement, and keeps Kenya’s communications aligned with Amref’s global strategy and brand. Success is measured on outcomes rather than outputs. The function is deliberately lean: the manager both leads the strategy and personally produces its flagship communications products.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
Strategic Leadership and Advisory
Lead the implementation, monitoring and periodic review of Amref Kenya’s communications strategy and project-level communication plans, aligned with the Kenya Country Strategy and Amref’s global communications priorities.
Advise the Country Director and Senior Management Team on organisational positioning, stakeholder engagement, emerging opportunities and reputational risk, and recommend responses.
Translate organisational and programme priorities into clear messages and campaigns for defined audiences.
Prepare the function’s quarterly report to the board’s Resource Mobilisation, Partnerships and Communications Committee and complete the actions the Committee assigns.
Media Relations, Reputation and Misinformation Readiness
Build and maintain relationships with editors, journalists, health correspondents and producers across national, county, community, Kiswahili and vernacular media, including radio.
Pitch stories, opinion articles, expert commentary and research findings; coordinate interviews, briefings and field visits; and serve as Amref Kenya’s primary media contact.
Equip Ministry, county and Amref spokespeople, and community messengers, to speak in the languages their audiences use, rather than producing every product in-house.
Monitor coverage for message accuracy, positioning and sentiment, and provide leadership with regular media intelligence.
Maintain crisis communications preparedness and lead responses to reputational issues, in coordination with the Country Director and Group communications.
Keep light-touch social listening for health misinformation affecting priority programmes and support rapid, evidence-based responses, with the Ministry of Health leading and coordination through WHO’s Africa Infodemic Response Alliance and Group.
Government and Public-Sector Communications
Support the Ministry of Health and county governments with communications for joint engagements, launches and milestones, always positioning the Ministry or county as the lead and Amref as the supporting partner.
Coordinate Amref Kenya’s communications contribution to national platforms such as health summits and technical working groups, and prepare materials for engagements with government principals with the Country Director’s office.
Thought Leadership and Advocacy
Coordinate a thought leadership agenda that positions Amref Kenya’s technical experts as credible voices on priority health issues, with domestic audiences first.
Place the Country Director and subject-matter experts through media interviews, opinion pages, keynote speeches, podcasts and policy platforms, and draft or edit speeches, talking points, opinion articles and briefing notes.
Lead communications for Amref Kenya’s advocacy and policy priorities, including policy briefs, position statements and key national policy moments.
Content, Storytelling and Community Voice
Maintain, with programme teams, a pipeline of impact stories, human-interest stories, innovations and research findings, and produce the annual report, newsletters, factsheets and advocacy materials.
Practise participatory storytelling in which communities help shape and approve the stories told about them, with informed consent, dignity and fair representation throughout.
Work with the Impact, Data & Insights function to turn programme evidence into accurate, data-driven stories of measurable change.
Build programme teams’ communications capacity through training, tools and templates.
Digital Communications and Owned Audiences
Oversee Amref Kenya’s digital presence, including the website, social media and digital campaigns, using analytics and audience insights to guide decisions.
Build audiences Amref can reach directly, growing an email newsletter and WhatsApp broadcast and community lists, measured on genuine engagement rather than follower counts.
Apply AI tools responsibly under Group policy and recognised professional guidance: disclose meaningful AI use, verify accuracy, and never publish synthetic imagery or content that could mislead.
Donor Visibility and Resource Mobilisation Support
Lead donor visibility planning so that every funded project meets its branding, marking and acknowledgement requirements.
Produce funder-facing products, including capability statements, project profiles and impact summaries, with the Business Development & Partnerships function, and coordinate communications for donor visits and co-branded moments.
Brand, Ethics and Communications Governance
Act as custodian of Amref’s brand in Kenya, assure the quality of key products before publication, and ensure compliance with ethical storytelling, informed consent, safeguarding, data protection, copyright and image-use requirements.
Adapt and implement in Kenya the communications policies and standards owned by Amref’s global communications function, and share country lessons to strengthen them.
Internal Communications and Staff Messengers
Keep staff informed and engaged through internal communications, and support the Country Director and Senior Management Team with leadership communications and organisational announcements.
Develop staff, technical experts and community health workers as credible messengers for Amref’s work, with simple guidance, talking points and practice.
Team and Resource Management
Supervise, coach and develop communications staff, setting clear performance expectations and annual workplans.
Manage the communications budget, assets, external agencies and service providers in line with organisational policies.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Success in this role is measured on outcomes; advertising value equivalence is not used. Five indicators, agreed annually with the Country Director:
Stakeholder trust and reputation. An annual perception pulse of government, county, partner, community, donor and staff audiences, designed and run with the Impact, Data & Insights function; baseline in year one, then tracked.
Quality and message alignment of media coverage. The share of coverage that carries key messages accurately, quotes a credible spokesperson and positions the Ministry or county as lead where relevant, with sentiment; coded quarterly from media monitoring and reported to the board committee.
Owned-audience growth and engagement. Newsletter subscribers, WhatsApp list members and returning website visitors, measured quarterly on growth and genuine engagement rather than follower counts.
Documented contribution to advocacy, policy, partnership and resource mobilisation outcomes. A quarterly outcome log validated with the Business Development & Partnerships function and programme directorates, synthesised annually; contribution, not sole attribution.
Donor visibility and ethical-content compliance.
The proportion of active projects meeting branding and acknowledgement requirements, and of published human-interest content with documented consent and ethical sign-off, tracked quarterly.
Qualifications
Education
Master’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Marketing, Development Communications, or a related discipline, with at least 8 years’ progressive communications experience; OR
Bachelor’s degree in Communication, Public Relations, Journalism, or a relevant discipline, with at least 10 years’ progressive communications experience.
Experience
Minimum of 8-10 years’ progressive communications experience, including
at least three years in a managerial or leadership capacity.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing communications strategies and measuring their outcomes.
Strong track record in media relations, thought leadership, digital communications, executive communications and reputation management; experience with county, community or vernacular media an advantage.
Experience in public health or international development desirable.
Technical Skills
Exceptional writing and editing; strategic storytelling; digital communications and analytics; building owned audiences (email and WhatsApp); media measurement aligned to the AMEC framework; crisis and misinformation response; brand management; responsible use of AI tools.
Leadership Competencies

Job Description:
Rationale/Objective for Position
The Corporate Sponsorship Acquisition Specialist is responsible for providing specialist expertise and lead the acquisition of corporate sponsorship for MSF Eastern Africa’s priority fundraising events. The role will own the corporate sponsorship acquisition cycle from prospect identification and relationship access.
This position will be hierarchically and functionally accountable to the Donor Relationship Manager.
Tasks & Responsibilities
Corporate Sponsorship Strategy and Pipeline Ownership
Support in developing and implementing the corporate sponsorship acquisition strategy for the Charity Gala Dinner, Charity Golf Tournament and Charity Run & Walk.
Build and own a prioritised pipeline of corporate prospects, including anchor and premium prospects, based on sponsorship potential, decision-maker access, giving capacity, strategic fit and event relevance.
Map sponsorship opportunities against sectors and corporate budgets, including marketing, brand, CSR/ESG, employee engagement, customer engagement and corporate affairs.
Determine the most appropriate sponsorship assets, levels and prospects for each event and continuously refine the pipeline based on market response.
Set clear prospecting, meeting, proposal, negotiation and closure milestones against agreed sponsorship income targets.
High-Value Corporate Prospecting and Senior Stakeholder Access
Lead proactive prospecting through established networks, warm introductions, business forums, direct approaches and existing MSF relationships.
Secure meetings with CEOs, Managing Directors, Marketing Directors, Corporate Affairs leaders, CSR/ESG heads, HR leaders and other corporate budget holders.
Use professional networks and market knowledge to open doors to organisations that may not be accessible through conventional fundraising approaches.
Develop and maintain trusted relationships with senior corporate stakeholders and position MSF’s events as credible platforms for humanitarian impact, brand visibility, employee engagement and corporate purpose.
Represent MSF professionally in high-level corporate and business networking environments to originate sponsorship opportunities.
Sponsorship Proposition Development and Commercial Packaging
Lead the design and refinement of commercially compelling sponsorship packages for each event, including title/presenting sponsorship, premium tiers, corporate tables, golf foursomes, hole sponsorships, brand activations, prizes and in-kind partnerships.
Advise on sponsorship pricing, benefits, exclusivity, branding, hospitality and activation opportunities based on market expectations and the profile of each event.
Tailor sponsorship propositions to individual corporate objectives and decision-makers rather than relying solely on standard packages.
Prepare high-quality sponsorship proposals, pitch decks and presentations that clearly articulate both the humanitarian value and corporate proposition.
Ensure that proposed benefits are realistic, deliverable and aligned with MSF’s principles and approval requirements.
Sponsorship Sales, Negotiation and Closing
Lead sponsorship pitches and commercial conversations with prospective sponsors from initial engagement through to commitment.
Lead negotiations on sponsorship value, contribution levels, benefits, branding, activation, hospitality and other commercial terms within approved parameters.
Use strong sales judgement to overcome objections, manage competing priorities and move prospects towards timely decisions.
Create and manage a clear closing strategy for priority prospects, particularly anchor and high-value sponsors.
Secure signed sponsorship agreements/MOUs and confirmed financial or in-kind commitments within agreed event timelines.
Escalate matters requiring organisational, financial, legal or policy decisions while retaining ownership of the commercial relationship and acquisition process.
Event-Specific Sponsorship Acquisition
Charity Gala Dinner:
lead acquisition of title/presenting sponsors, premium sponsors, corporate tables, hospitality partnerships, brand partners and other high-value revenue opportunities.
Charity Golf Tournament:
lead acquisition of title/presenting sponsors, corporate foursomes, premium hospitality, hole sponsorships, prizes, gifts, activations and other sponsorship assets.
Charity Run & Walk:
lead acquisition of title/presenting, gold, silver and other sponsorship levels, corporate/team participation, activation partners and in-kind sponsors.
Prioritise anchor sponsorships and high-value opportunities that can materially contribute to the financial success of each event.
Work with relevant MSF colleagues to ensure sponsor commitments can be delivered, while retaining primary responsibility for sponsorship acquisition and closure.
Sponsor Stewardship and Relationship Conversion
Maintain senior-level relationships with confirmed sponsors and ensure a professional transition from commitment to fulfilment.
Capture and document key relationship intelligence, decision-maker information, commitments and future opportunities.
Identify opportunities to convert event sponsors into repeat sponsors, annual event partners or broader corporate partnerships with MSF.
Advise MSF on prospects with potential for longer-term strategic corporate relationships beyond the immediate event.
Reporting, Accountability and Compliance
Provide regular, concise updates to the Head of Fundraising on pipeline value, senior meetings, proposals, negotiations, commitments and income secured.
Maintain accurate records of prospects, corporate contacts, proposals, agreements and financial commitments in relevant MSF systems.
Ensure all sponsorship engagements proceed through MSF due diligence, gift acceptance, ethical fundraising and brand approval processes.
Provide a complete handover of active relationships, negotiations, signed agreements, outstanding actions and future opportunities at the end of the assignment.
OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES
Integrate EDI & Safeguarding aspects in area of work responsibility, including policies and practices.
Recognize, respond, and document any form of abuse or inappropriate behavior and alert the safeguarding unit of any suspected potential abuse.
Proactively participate in the individual performance management process including objective setting, performance monitoring and performance evaluation.
Qualifications
Education:
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Business, Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Fundraising, Sales or a related field.
Experience:
Minimum 5 years of proven experience in corporate sponsorships, sponsorship sales, partnership development, business development, fundraising or event commercialization.
Local market experience working closely with corporates and specific on events sponsorships.
Competencies:
Technical Competencies
Demonstrable track record of personally securing and closing corporate sponsorships or partnership deals, particularly for high-value or high-profile events.
An established network among Kenyan corporate decision-makers and organisations with marketing, CSR/ESG, corporate affairs, employee engagement or sponsorship budgets.
Proven ability to access senior stakeholders and convert relationships into sponsorship commitments within short, deadline-driven sales cycles.
Strong commercial, negotiation, influencing and closing skills.
Excellent presentation, proposal-writing and relationship-management skills.
Ability to operate independently as a subject matter expert and provide specialist advice to MSF colleagues.
Strong understanding of the corporate sponsorship, events and CSR/ESG landscape in Kenya; experience with premium charity, golf, gala, run or comparable events is highly desirable.
Highly target-driven, resilient and comfortable managing multiple high-value negotiations under significant time pressure.
Behavioral/General Competencies
Commitment to MSF’s Principles
Excellent writing and editing skills in English and Swahili
Results and Quality Orientation
Service Orientation
Initiative and Innovation
Teamwork and Cooperation
Leadership
People Management and Development
Networking and Building Relationships
Security awareness and Management
Ethics: High ethical standards and a commitment to protecting the data of individuals and furthering MSF mandate.

Company Details: Médecins sans frontières (MSF) or Doctors Without Borders, is an international humanitarian-aid non-governmental organization (NGO) and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, best known for its projects in war-torn regions and developing countries facing endemic diseases. It was founded in Fra...read morence in response to the Biafran War. Job Description:
THE OPPORTUNITY & RESPONSIBILITIES
The IT Service Delivery Manager will be responsible for ensuring that Inkomoko's IT services are reliable, responsive, consistent, secure and aligned with the needs of our teams and country operations.
The role will lead the day-to-day service management function, oversee the Service Desk and coordinate IT operations across countries and sites. The position will work closely with Infrastructure, Information Security, Software Engineering, Product, Project Management and country leadership to ensure that technology services translate into an effective and consistent experience for users.
The role will also drive continuous improvement of IT services through effective service management processes, performance measurement, standardization, automation and user-focused improvements.
Key Responsibilities
IT Service Delivery
Lead the effective delivery of IT services across Inkomoko.
Ensure IT services meet agreed service levels, performance standards and business requirements.
Define consistent service delivery standards and practices across countries and locations
Maintain visibility of IT service performance, risks and operational issues.
Develop and maintain the IT service catalogue in collaboration with relevant technology owners.
Ensure users understand available IT services and appropriate support channels.
Coordinate dependencies between Service Delivery, Infrastructure, Information Security and Software Engineering.
Ensure service delivery processes align with Information Security policies and requirements.
Service Desk & User Support
Manage and develop the Service Desk function.
Ensure timely and effective resolution of incidents and service requests.
Monitor ticket volumes, response times, resolution times and backlog.
Improve first-contact resolution and overall user experience.
Ensure appropriate categorization, prioritization and escalation of tickets.
Establish and maintain knowledge management and self-service capabilities.
Identify recurring user issues and initiate appropriate corrective actions.
Country IT Operations
Provide functional coordination and performance oversight to the Country IT Ops.
Ensure consistent IT support standards across all countries and geographically dispersed sites.
Coordinate country-level technology priorities and operational issues.
Monitor country IT service performance and identify areas requiring improvement.
Drive standardization of IT support processes, equipment and operating practices.
Ensure appropriate coverage and support arrangements across locations.
Consolidate country-level service issues, risks and performance for management reporting.
Support Country IT Ops in effectively engaging with Country MDs/CDs and Operations Managers.
Incident & Problem Management
Establish and maintain effective incident and problem-management processes.
Coordinate response to major incidents and significant service disruptions.
Ensure appropriate stakeholder communication during major incidents.
Coordinate resolution with Infrastructure, Information Security, Software Engineering and other relevant teams.
Ensure root-cause analysis is completed for significant and recurring incidents.
Maintain a problem register and track corrective and preventive actions.
Identify opportunities to eliminate recurring incidents and improve service reliability.
Service Performance & SLA Management
Define, monitor and report on IT service KPIs and SLAs.
Produce regular service-performance reports for the Head of IT Infrastructure & InfoSec and relevant stakeholders.
Monitor trends in service performance and identify areas of degradation.
Drive corrective actions where SLAs or service standards are not being met.
Track service performance across countries and identify systemic issues.
Monitor user satisfaction and use feedback to improve service delivery.
Support budget planning and cost-efficiency tracking for Service Desk staffing and tooling,
Change & Release Management
Coordinate operational readiness for technology changes and releases.
Participate in the Change Advisory Board (CAB).
Assess operational impact and support requirements for proposed changes.
Ensure appropriate communication, testing, support and rollback plans are in place.
Monitor the impact of changes on IT services.
Ensure failed or disruptive changes are reviewed and corrective actions implemented.
Coordinate service readiness for major technology projects transitioning into operations.
Service Improvement & Standardization
Establish a continuous service-improvement agenda.
Identify opportunities to automate, simplify and standardize IT services.
Reduce repetitive manual support activities and recurring incidents.
Improve IT processes, workflows and knowledge management.
Identify opportunities for self-service and automation.
Drive adoption of consistent IT service practices across countries.
Track and report the benefits of service-improvement initiatives.
Vendor & Service Provider Management
Monitor performance of IT service providers against agreed SLAs.
Coordinate vendor resolution of incidents and service issues.
Track vendor performance, recurring issues and escalations.
Participate in service reviews with key technology vendors.
Escalate material vendor performance issues to the Head of IT Infrastructure & InfoSec.
Provide service-performance information to support procurement and contract reviews.
IT Service Governance & Reporting
Maintain effective IT service-management processes and documentation.
Participate in relevant Digital Transformation governance forums.
Provide accurate and timely service-performance reporting.
Maintain service risks, issues and improvement actions.
Support audits and compliance activities relating to IT service delivery.
Ensure operational procedures are documented, maintained and followed.
Requirements
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Information Technology or a related field.
ITIL 4 foundation certification required.
Relevant certifications in service management, project management or technology operations are an advantage.
Professional Experience
6–8+ years of experience in IT service management, IT operations or technology service delivery.
At least 3 years of experience in a service-management or technology leadership role.
Demonstrated experience managing IT services across multiple locations or geographically distributed operations.
Experience managing Service Desk and IT support functions.
Strong experience with incident, problem, request and change management.
Experience defining and managing IT SLAs and service KPIs.
Experience coordinating infrastructure, application, security and business teams.
Experience managing IT service providers and vendors.
Demonstrated experience implementing service improvements and standardization.
Experience working in a multi-country or distributed organizational environment is an advantage.
Benefits
WHAT YOU’LL GET
This role is inside a high-growth, mission-driven social enterprise. By joining, you’ll access:
Competitive salary, and potential Goal-based bonus
Incredible company culture, including deep investment in your learning and growth
Diverse colleagues and policies that show our commitment to equity and inclusion
Talented, passionate, and committed team colleagues across the region
Ability to make a significant social impact to your community
Generous health insurance, staff savings, parental leave, sabbatical, and more benefits.

Job Description:
Duties and Responsibilities for the Audit Committee Chair
The Chairperson shall provide leadership to the Audit Committee and shall be responsible for:
Providing strategic leadership to the Audit Committee in the execution of its mandate.
Overseeing the integrity of financial reporting and financial management processes.
Providing oversight over governance, risk management and internal control systems.
Overseeing the effectiveness and independence of the Internal Audit function.
Monitoring implementation of recommendations arising from internal and external audit reports.
Overseeing compliance with applicable laws, regulations, Government policies and ethical standards.
Setting the agenda of the committee meetings in consultation with the other members and committee secretary.
Presiding over Audit Committee meetings and ensuring effective discharge of the Committee’s responsibilities.
Facilitating effective engagement between the Committee, Management, Internal Audit, External Auditors and other oversight institutions.
Perform such other duties and responsibilities as provided under the Public Finance Management Act, 2012, the Public Finance Management Regulations, 2015 and the Audit Committee Guidelines.
Qualifications for the Audit Committee Chairperson
Bachelor’s degree in any of the following: -Accounting, Audit, Risk Management, Finance, Economics, Human Resource Management, Law or any other related field.
Bachelor’s degree from a university recognized in Accounting, Auditing, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, Human Resource Management, Law or another relevant discipline.
Possession of a Master’s degree in any of the above fields will be an added advantage.
Membership in a relevant professional body in good standing.
Experience for the Audit Committee Chairperson
At least ten (10) years’ professional experience, five (5) of which must be in a senior management position in the relevant fields;
Thorough understanding of relevant legislation, best practices and emerging issues in the relevant professional field;
Good understanding of the Council of Governors’ mandate, public sector governance and public financial management.
Be a person of integrity with demonstrated professional competence and strong interpersonal skills;
Must not be an employee of the Council of Governors, and shall not have served as an employee or agent of a business organization which has carried out any business with CoG within the preceding two years.
Terms and Conditions of Service
Chair of the Committee shall:
Be appointed for a term of three (3) years, renewable for one further term subject to satisfactory performance;
Serve on a part-time basis;
Be paid allowances at rates determined by the Salaries and Remuneration Commission (SRC).
Successful candidates shall be required to submit valid clearance certificates in fulfillment of the requirements of Chapter Six of the Constitution of Kenya: Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC), Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Higher Education Loans Board (HELB), and a Credit Reference Bureau (CRB).
