Job Description:
Assignment
Each trainer will be responsible for delivering sixteen (16) training sessions, with two (2) sessions conducted in each assigned county. Each session will comprise five (5) contact hours. The training will focus on building participants’ understanding of gender-responsive circular economy principles and strengthening their ability to apply relevant practices and business approaches within their enterprises and communities.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare and deliver the assigned circular economy training sessions in accordance with the approved curriculum and programme schedule.
Facilitate practical learning on circular economy principles, circular business models, resource efficiency, waste-to-value opportunities, sustainability, and relevant environmental governance and compliance requirements.
Apply the training content to the three priority waste streams, specifically plastic waste, organic waste and textile waste, using relevant local examples and business cases.
Use participatory and experiential methods, including demonstrations, practical exercises, case studies, group problem-solving, peer learning and field-based activities, as appropriate to the training context.
Adapt delivery to the needs and circumstances of MSMEs, community groups and informalsector actors, while ensuring meaningful participation of women, youth and other groups that may face barriers to participation.
Administer pre- and post-training assessments and use the results to assess learning gains and participants’ ability to apply the knowledge acquired.
Maintain accurate training records and submit session reports, assessment results, lessons learned and other required documentation within the agreed timelines.
Training Content
The approved Gender-Responsive Circular Economy Curriculum will cover the following areas:
Circular economy principles and the business case for transitioning from linear to circular models.
Resource efficiency, waste reduction, and sustainable use of water and energy.
Circular business models and opportunities for value addition.
Value-chain-specific practices in plastic waste, organic waste, and textile waste.
Environmental governance and regulatory compliance, including relevant requirements under the Sustainable Waste Management Act, 2022, Extended Producer Responsibility Regulations, 2024, NEMA, and KEBS.
Product development, human-centered design, prototyping and testing of circular solutions, where relevant.
Qualifications and Experience
A Bachelor’s degree in environment, environmental science, natural resource management, sustainability, waste management or another relevant field.
Demonstrated professional experience in training, facilitation, or adult learning.
A strong understanding of environmental sustainability and gender-responsive, gender responsive circular economy principles and practices.
Demonstrated experience delivering practical and interactive training to MSMEs, communities, informal-sector actors, or other adult learners.
Experience applying participatory, experiential, and problem-based learning approaches.
Experience administering or using pre- and post-training assessments or other learning assessment tools.
Strong communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.

Job Description:
Assignment
Each trainer will be responsible for delivering sixteen (16) training sessions, with two (2) sessions conducted in each assigned county. Each session will comprise five (5) contact hours. The training will focus on building participants’ understanding of gender-responsive circular economy principles and strengthening their ability to apply relevant practices and business approaches within their enterprises and communities.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare and deliver the assigned circular economy training sessions in accordance with the approved curriculum and programme schedule.
Facilitate practical learning on circular economy principles, circular business models, resource efficiency, waste-to-value opportunities, sustainability, and relevant environmental governance and compliance requirements.
Apply the training content to the three priority waste streams, specifically plastic waste, organic waste and textile waste, using relevant local examples and business cases.
Use participatory and experiential methods, including demonstrations, practical exercises, case studies, group problem-solving, peer learning and field-based activities, as appropriate to the training context.
Adapt delivery to the needs and circumstances of MSMEs, community groups and informalsector actors, while ensuring meaningful participation of women, youth and other groups that may face barriers to participation.
Administer pre- and post-training assessments and use the results to assess learning gains and participants’ ability to apply the knowledge acquired.
Maintain accurate training records and submit session reports, assessment results, lessons learned and other required documentation within the agreed timelines.
Training Content
The approved Gender-Responsive Circular Economy Curriculum will cover the following areas:
Circular economy principles and the business case for transitioning from linear to circular models.
Resource efficiency, waste reduction, and sustainable use of water and energy.
Circular business models and opportunities for value addition.
Value-chain-specific practices in plastic waste, organic waste, and textile waste.
Environmental governance and regulatory compliance, including relevant requirements under the Sustainable Waste Management Act, 2022, Extended Producer Responsibility Regulations, 2024, NEMA, and KEBS.
Product development, human-centered design, prototyping and testing of circular solutions, where relevant.
Qualifications and Experience
A Bachelor’s degree in environment, environmental science, natural resource management, sustainability, waste management or another relevant field.
Demonstrated professional experience in training, facilitation, or adult learning.
A strong understanding of environmental sustainability and gender-responsive, gender responsive circular economy principles and practices.
Demonstrated experience delivering practical and interactive training to MSMEs, communities, informal-sector actors, or other adult learners.
Experience applying participatory, experiential, and problem-based learning approaches.
Experience administering or using pre- and post-training assessments or other learning assessment tools.
Strong communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE
To act as a strategic partner to the business, supporting the implementation of HR strategies across departments. The role bridges business needs and HR initiatives, focusing on talent management, performance management, learning and development, recruitment, employee relations, policy review, reporting, and organisational development to drive performance. The HR Business Partner collaborates closely with key stakeholders, including Functional and Departmental Heads.
DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Talent Acquisition
Partner with hiring managers to identify staffing needs, develop job descriptions, and create recruitment strategies.
Manage the full recruitment cycle, from sourcing and interviewing to onboarding, ensuring a positive candidate experience.
Implement best practices for attracting high-quality talent.
Onboarding
Lead the onboarding process to integrate new hires smoothly into the culture and their roles.
Develop and facilitate orientation programmes to educate new employees on policies, values, and expectations.
Monitor the onboarding experience to ensure early-stage employee engagement and retention.
Performance and Talent Management
Support the performance management cycle, including goal-setting, mid-year and year-end reviews, and ongoing feedback.
Provide coaching to managers on effective performance management and employee development techniques.
Support talent management programmes, including succession planning, career pathing, and high-potential employee development.
Strategic Initiatives
Support leadership and business units to implement key strategic initiatives related to employee engagement, diversity and inclusion, and organisational development.
Align HR strategies with Imara Hospital's strategic objectives to drive organisational change and improve performance.
Collaborate on initiatives to improve operational efficiency and foster a culture of continuous improvement.
Employee Engagement
Design and implement employee engagement programmes that promote a positive work environment and strengthen organisational culture.
Conduct employee surveys, analyse results, and partner with managers to create action plans for engagement and retention.
Organise events, recognition programmes, and initiatives that enhance employee morale and satisfaction.
Learning and Development
Work with line managers to identify training needs and design and deliver training programmes.
Support leadership development programmes to ensure a strong talent pipeline for future leadership roles.
Facilitate workshops and training sessions to enhance employee skills, including soft skills and technical competencies.
Employee Relations
Serve as a trusted advisor to managers and employees on employee relations matters, including conflict resolution, grievances, and disciplinary actions.
Conduct investigations and ensure fair, consistent handling of employee concerns in compliance with policies and legal requirements.
Promote a culture of fairness, respect, and transparency by upholding policies and HR best practices.
Organisational Development and Change Management
Support organisational change initiatives by working with leadership to align structure, culture, and talent with evolving healthcare needs.
Implement training programmes to enhance employee skills, ensure compliance, and improve service quality.
Compensation and Benefits
Provide support on compensation strategies, job evaluations, and pay equity to keep the facility competitive in the healthcare market.
Support the development of staff welfare and employee benefit programmes.
HR Metrics
Track and analyse key HR metrics, including turnover rates, time-to-hire, employee engagement scores, and performance outcomes.
Provide data-driven insights to inform decision-making and identify trends or areas for improvement.
Prepare reports and dashboards to present HR metrics to senior management and recommend HR strategy enhancements.
QUALIFICATIONS
Education
Bachelor's degree in Human Resource Management or a related field.
Professional qualification such as a Higher Diploma in Human Resource Management or Certified Human Resource Professional of Kenya, CHRP(K).
Experience
Minimum of Three (3) years in Human Resources or equivalent.
Knowledge of all HR functions as an HR generalist.
Strong understanding of HR laws and regulations, with the ability to handle employee relations matters effectively.
Payroll processing is an added advantage.
Membership
Membership with the Institute of Human Resource Management (IHRM) of Kenya.

Job Description:
Position Purpose
Pesapal is seeking a commercially driven Credit Manager to grow our merchant lending book. This is a growth and origination role, not a back-office control role: your job is to convert Pesapal's proprietary transaction data and credit scores into more merchants borrowing, borrowing more, and borrowing again — safely. We already sit on a rich data ecosystem of POS flows, e-commerce volumes, reservation data and digital spend, and a large number of merchants are creditworthy today and simply not borrowing. You will own that gap.
Importantly, we lend in partnership. Pesapal originates, scores and services merchant credit alongside licensed Digital Credit Providers (DCPs) and banks, who bring the lending licence, the balance sheet, or both. We bring what partners cannot easily replicate: the merchant relationship, the daily transaction data, the credit score built on it, and the distribution. This makes the role dual-sided — you will grow the book on the merchant side and make the partnerships work on the lender side, keeping partner appetite, pricing and limits aligned with the volume of good merchants our data identifies.
Critically, you will scale the book through the platform, not through headcount. Every lesson you learn in the market — which merchant profiles repay, which signals predict trouble, which limits and tenors get taken up — must end up codified in our digital origination platform as decision rules, eligibility criteria and limit logic. Your success is measured not by how many deals you personally wrote, but by how much of your credit judgement now runs automatically, at volume, without you in the loop. You will not manage Credit Operations, Data Science or Collections; you will work side by side with them and with our lending partners.
Key Responsibilities
Loan Book Growth & Origination
Own the Growth Number: Carry the disbursement, active borrower and outstanding loan book (OLB) targets for your markets and segments, across all partner lending programmes.
Build the Origination Engine: Design and run the end-to-end funnel — from identifying eligible merchants in the pre-scored base through offer, application, partner approval and disbursement — and lift conversion at every step.
Activate the Dormant Base: Systematically work the population of merchants who already qualify but have never drawn down, and diagnose why they don't.
Drive Repeat & Deepening: Grow repeat borrowing, top-ups, limit utilisation and graduated limit increases, and run pre-approved offers and seasonal working-capital campaigns with Marketing, Product and the relevant partner.
Enable the Frontline: Equip Sales, Relationship and Merchant Success teams to position credit confidently — talk tracks, eligibility rules, objection handling and referral routes.
Lending Partnerships with DCPs & Banks
Own the Commercial Relationship: Act as Pesapal's day-to-day counterpart to our lending partners, running the joint pipeline, performance reviews and the working relationship at credit and product level.
Negotiate & Expand Appetite: Use portfolio evidence to secure larger allocations, higher limits, broader eligibility criteria, better pricing and faster decisioning.
Keep the Joint Machinery Running: Work with Credit Operations, Finance and the partner on data exchange, decisioning integration, disbursement and repayment flows, reconciliation and revenue share, escalating blockages before they cost volume.
Report with Credibility: Own the portfolio narrative our partners see — vintage performance, funnel metrics, NPL and recovery trends — so Pesapal is consistently the partner they want to allocate more capital to.
Codifying Credit Learning Into the Platform
Turn Judgement Into Rules: Translate what you learn originating in the market — merchant behaviour, decline patterns, repayment signals, exception cases — into credit policy expressed as decision rules, eligibility criteria, and limit and pricing logic.
Own the Credit Strategy in the Decision Engine: Define and continuously refine the cut-offs, scorecard bands, limit-assignment and step-up rules that govern automated decisions, working with Product, Engineering and Data Science to get them built and released.
Raise Straight-Through Processing: Grow the share of merchants who receive an instant, fully automated decision, and treat every recurring manual exception as the specification for the next platform rule — so volume grows without growing the credit team.
Commercialise the Score: Work with the Lead Data Scientist to turn model output into commercial decisions — who receives an offer, how large, at what price, over what tenor — and run champion/challenger tests that quantify volume gained against risk taken.
Close the Feedback Loop: Feed origination intelligence — partner decline reasons, funnel drop-off points, thin-file and underserved segments — back into scoring and policy, and monitor the vintage performance of the cohorts you write.
Credit Assessment, Policy & Collaboration
Assess & Recommend: Make sound credit decisions within delegated limits, and prepare well-argued cases for exposures above your threshold or requiring partner sign-off.
Shape Policy With Evidence: Recommend changes to credit policy, limits and eligibility criteria — internally and with partners — supported by portfolio data, knowing when to loosen to capture safe share and when to tighten.
Respect the Firewalls: Grow the book within the approved risk appetite of Pesapal and each partner, maintaining clear separation between origination, underwriting and collections.
Work Across Functions: Partner with Credit Operations on clean handover and fast disbursement, Data Science on model design and rollout, Collections on early-warning feedback, and Finance and Compliance on pricing, revenue share, provisioning, Central Bank requirements, data protection and AML/KYC.
Candidate Profile & Experience
Required Qualifications
Experience: 3–6 years in credit, SME or commercial lending, digital lending or credit analytics, with a clear record of growing a loan book rather than only managing or monitoring one — evidenced by volumes disbursed, borrowers acquired, book grown or conversion improved.
Partnership Exposure: Experience working across institutional counterparties — banks, DCPs, microfinance institutions, fintech partners or funders — and comfort holding a commercial relationship with a lender rather than simply reporting to one.
Credit & Systems Fundamentals: Ability to assess an MSME, size a limit sensibly and defend a decision to a partner credit committee, together with experience translating credit policy into the rules, criteria and limit logic that a decision engine or loan origination platform executes.
Data Fluency: Comfort interrogating dashboards and working with scorecard output, preferably with the ability to write your own SQL queries or build your own analysis in Excel.
Market Knowledge: Deep familiarity with the Kenyan MSME and merchant ecosystem and how DCPs and banks in this market think about credit. Experience in a digital lender, fintech or a bank's MSME / cash-flow lending unit, and exposure to alternative-data underwriting, is highly desirable.
Key Competencies & Traits
Commercial Drive With Credit Discipline: You chase growth, but you understand that a book grown badly is worse than no growth at all — and that a partner's trust, once lost, is expensive to rebuild.
Data-Driven Credit Mindset: You accept that a merchant's daily POS consistency can tell you more than a three-year audited financial statement, and you can prove it to a sceptical bank.
Influence Without Authority: You get results through peers in Operations, Data Science, Collections and Sales, and through partner institutions, without managing any of them.
Systems Thinker, Not a Deal Doer: When you solve a credit problem once, your instinct is to make sure the platform solves it every time after that.
Bias to Experiment: You would rather run a controlled pilot on 200 merchants this month than write a strategy paper about it, and you understand what an MSME actually needs working capital for, and when.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Loan Book Growth: Value disbursed and outstanding loan book against target, across all partner programmes.
Take-Up & Conversion: Proportion of eligible merchants who accept and draw down, funnel conversion at each stage including partner approval, and growth in active borrowers, repeat borrowing and limit utilisation.
Partnership Performance: Funding capacity secured and utilised, expansion of partner appetite and eligibility, and successful onboarding of new lending partners.
Quality of Originated Business: First-payment default and vintage NPL on the cohorts you write, within budgeted and partner-agreed boundaries.
Automation & Speed: Straight-through processing and automated approval rates, reduction in applications needing manual review, and time from eligibility to disbursement.

Job Description:
Job purpose
The Programme Development Manager will support a portfolio of Saferworld’s teams in co-designing and mobilising funding for peace, security and justice programmes alongside Saferworld’s partners. The successful applicant will have a focus of 3-4 countries, which will be decided based on the candidate’s experience and preference.
Working closely with Regional Directors, Country Managers, and programme and grant management colleagues, the post-holder will lead on: coordinating and facilitating programme co-design processes (including taking the lead in facilitating co-design, processes, drafting high quality concept notes and proposals, theories of change, logical models, risk matrixes and budgets); developing and supporting the implementation of long-term country funding strategies; and supporting new donor engagement and sustaining relationships with current donors.
The post-holder will be responsible for managing funding portfolios across institutional and non-institutional donors in our programmes.
The post-holder will have a successful track record in developing programmes and leading new business development efforts with institutional donors such as Global Affairs Canada (GAC), the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), the European Union (EU), UN agencies and European Governments such as Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida). Additional experience in mobilising resource from trusts and foundations and other non-traditional funding mechanisms is desirable.
Strong applicants will have proven programme experience, such as in project management or programme support, which equips them to lead and inform high-quality programme design. They will be skilled in coordinating complex processes, facilitating participatory co-creation with partners, and ensuring proposals are robust, contextually relevant, and strategically aligned.
Key areas of responsibility
Programme design and proposal development
Work with country teams and partners to make informed go/no go decisions on calls for proposals and invitations to submit funding applications.
Lead participatory, partner-centred programme co-design and development of programme concept notes and proposals that link to Saferworld’s organisational theory of change and enable delivery of country strategies. This includes coordinating across teams, facilitating locally informed ideas from country teams and partners, and leading the drafting of high-quality funding applications (including narratives, budgets, theories of change, MEL frameworks and risk matrices).
Ensure programme design and proposal development processes are non-extractive and non-hierarchical, in line with Saferworld’s values and guidelines, including meaningful partner leadership throughout the full design cycle, participatory budget development, equitable budget sharing, and transparent communication of donor requirements and obligations.
Ensure strong gender and conflict analysis, informed by local partner knowledge and contextual expertise, is integrated into programme design and proposal development.
Provide guidance and capacity strengthening to country teams and partners on donor policies, strategies and funding opportunities, supporting high-quality programme design and proposal development through coaching, joint drafting and shared reflection.
Support efforts to diversify funding sources from trusts and foundations within country portfolios, with a focus on flexible, long-term funding suited to locally led approaches.
Support due diligence processes when entering into partnerships with INGOs and new or deepened funding relationships with donors, ensuring processes are proportionate, transparent and partnership-focused.
Strategic development
Support country teams and partners, where appropriate, to develop, plan and implement resource mobilisation plans to fund country strategies, including coordinating efforts to cultivate and maintain strong donor relationships.
Track donor priorities and opportunities for engagement, and work with country teams and partners to cultivate and influence donor relationships, including advocating for less top-down and less hierarchical funding approaches, greater flexibility, and increased funding flowing directly to local partners and civil society actors.
Monitor country resource mobilisation plans and analyse fundraising performance, including proposal success rates, while conducting learning on the effectiveness and quality of programme co-design and partnership processes.
Ensure cross-organisational collaboration by working closely with colleagues across the Funding Team to align country and regional resource mobilisation plans with global donor outreach and cultivation efforts.
Keep up to date with donor policy developments and funding trends, maintaining relevant funding intelligence to inform country strategies and organisational positioning.
Participate in and support negotiations with donors related to new and/or existing grants, advocating for flexible, equitable and partnership-friendly terms wherever possible.
External representation
Represent Saferworld at relevant donor conferences, seminars and other fundraising events, actively promoting Saferworld’s partnership-centred and locally led approach to programme design.
Engage with the wider NGO and fundraising community, particularly on funding trends related to locally led peacebuilding, co-design, equitable partnerships and shifting power within the aid system.
Key working relationships
Regional directors, country managers and country teams – working together on programme design, proposal development, and the development of resources mobilisation plans to enable the implementation of country and regional strategies.
Programme support – working closely together to ensure proposal development and programme design is of the utmost quality and in line with organisational approaches to partnership, gender, climate, MEL and advocacy.
Colleagues in the fundraising team – regularly coordinating to ensure country and regional resource mobilisation plans are connected to global outreach and donor cultivation plans, ensure approaches to institutional and non-institutional donors are coordinated with other parts of the organisation and leverage donor research support, support global efforts to diversify Saferworld funding basis in collaboration with Saferworld affiliate offices in the US and Brussels.
Colleagues in the finance team – working collaboratively to develop programme budgets, ensuring effective cost recovery and budget sharing with partners.
Colleagues in the policy team - ensuring linkages between donor trends and policy developments, and supporting the integration of policy insights into programme design and resource mobilisation approaches.
Knowledge and Experience
Essential
:
Demonstrable experience of co-designing, developing and implementing international development programmes, preferably in conflict-affected contexts, that deliver community-led change and influence policy and practice.
Experience leading collaborative design processes alongside civil society partners and a strong understanding of partner-led approaches in programme design.
Demonstrable experience of writing successful funding proposals – including developing theories of change, MEL frameworks, risk matrixes and complex budgets.
Proven experience of financial design, including programme budgeting and development of budget narratives.
Demonstrable experience of leading proposal development processes, including facilitating design workshops, coordinating inputs from multiple stakeholders, and managing remote relationships with country offices and local partners to produce successful concept notes and funding proposals.
Demonstrable experience in building and maintaining relationships with donors, and understanding of donor requirements, particularly for donors relevant to Saferworld such as GAC, the FCDO, EU, UN agencies and Sida (among others).
Demonstrable experience of working with teams and partners in ways that reflect the principles of power-sharing, solidarity and accompaniment.
Experience in mainstreaming gender-sensitivity/responsiveness/transformation in programme design and proposal development.
Desirable
:
Strong understanding of key political, development and humanitarian trends and debates on, and/or experience working in, focus countries/regions for Saferworld.
Experience of designing peacebuilding, security and justice, and/or conflict prevention programmes.
Proven experience in programme management or programme support roles, including planning, coordinating, and monitoring projects, which informs and strengthens high-quality programme design.
Experience in mobilising resources from trusts and foundations and non-traditional donors.
Skills/Abilities
Excellent written and spoken English; knowledge of a second language is desirable (such as Russian, Arabic, or Swahili).
Ability to work flexibly, independently and on own initiative.
Experience in developing strategies, and translating strategy into practice.
Ability to negotiate and understand priorities of colleagues, applying a problem-solving supportive approach.
Excellent communication skills, with clear strategies for working remotely with colleagues and partners, including experience of communicating effectively across cultures and with diverse audiences, both verbally and in writing.
Ability to work to tight deadlines, multiple priorities, and prioritise and manage workload.
Excellent participatory workshop facilitation skills.
Personal qualities
Self-motivated and persistent in the face of complex challenges.
Able to manage multiple and complex priorities at once and prioritise work to deliver on objectives effectively.
Personable, empathetic and able to develop excellent working relationships and collaborate with staff around the world.
Commitment to and compliance with Saferworld’s safeguarding principles.
Commitment to gender equality, respect and value equality and diversity, and understanding of how this applies to own area of work.
Commitment to the vision, mission and values of Saferworld.
Other requirements:
Willingness to travel (dependent on security assessments and project funding and aligned to our aim of working differently and reduce environmental impact).

Job Description:
About the Role
The Project Operations Officer supports the efficient coordination, documentation, and operational delivery of projects within the Project Operations Department. Reporting to the Manager, Project Operations & Busara ISERC, and receiving day-to-day task direction from the Research Ethics and Compliance Officer, the role provides structured administrative and operational support that strengthens project management execution, ethics and compliance administration, knowledge management systems, and operational follow-through across teams.The role addresses operational workload gaps, improves documentation quality, and strengthens compliance monitoring, freeing senior team members to focus on leadership, technical decision-making, and project oversight.
Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities
Ethics & Compliance Operational Support (Busara ISERC)
Submission & Protocol Management
Support the administrative procedures related to Busara ISERC, including the acceptance, verification, and distribution of submitted proposals for review.
Check protocol completeness against the submission checklist before routing to reviewers.
Follow up on outstanding documents or clarifications from applicants.
Log new protocols in the Busara ISERC tracker.
Send acknowledgment-of-receipt emails to Principal Investigators.
Maintain version control on protocol documents and amendments.
Reviewer Coordination
Manage reviewer assignments, and track turnaround against the 7-day / 21-day deadlines, escalating persistent delays to the Manager.
Send reminder notices for overdue reviews.
Collate reviewer comments into a single feedback document for the committee.
Maintain the reviewer roster: contact details, areas of expertise, Conflict of Interest declarations, and appointment letter expiry dates.
Monthly Committee Meetings
Support the drafting and circulation of meeting agendas.
Take and format minutes when the ISERC Secretary is on leave.
Distribute meeting packs (protocols and reviewer feedback) ahead of the sessions.
Follow up on action items from previous meetings.
Correspondence & Compliance
Draft approval, conditional approval, and rejection letters for review by the Research Ethics and Compliance Officer ahead of Manager/Chair sign-off.
Send renewal and continuing-review reminders as approvals near expiry.
Log protocol deviations, adverse events, and complaints as they arise.
File signed COI forms, NDAs, and appointment letters.
Financial & Administrative
Invoice applicants for review fees and track payment status.
Reconcile honoraria records against meeting attendance.
Records & Reporting
Keep the master tracker(s) updated: status, dates, assigned reviewers, decisions.
Produce periodic summary reports for management (submission volumes, approval rates, turnaround times).
Archive closed protocol files per the retention policy (refer to SOP).
Support NACOSTI and other regulatory reporting requirements.
Research & Advisory Division Support
Support the planning, coordination, and follow-up of project kick-off, review, and closure meetings, ensuring high-quality documentation and action tracking.
Provide project management administrative support, including scheduling, reminders, and stakeholder coordination.
Support improvements to project management systems and processes.
Monitor and support compliance with knowledge management practices, including correct use of Google Drive and other shared systems.
Track RA Division subscriptions (e.g., SurveyCTO, Zoom), including renewal timelines and usage coordination.
Document emerging project development needs to inform project development resources and support structures.
Knowledge Management & Project Database Support
Maintain and regularly update a centralized project database, including completed and closed projects, to support efficient project tracking across key indicators.
Support the knowledge management strategy, including organizing repositories of past projects and maintaining reference materials for recurring operational questions.
Ensure project documentation is properly named, stored, and accessible in line with internal standards, in coordination with relevant teams.
Maintain a centralized repository of data collection firms and log feedback on their performance to build organizational knowledge.
Support adherence to knowledge management processes and flag emerging challenges to the Manager.
Subscriptions, Payments & Operational Tracking
Follow up on platform subscriptions and licenses to ensure continuity of access.
Raise payment requests through the hub as instructed, in line with established procedures.
Track pending payments and follow up across systems to minimize delays.
Maintain simple operational trackers for subscriptions, renewals, and payment status.
Ensure invoices, contracts, and related documentation are accurately filed and easy to retrieve.
Project Operations Team Administration
Support monitoring of progress against Project Operations team tasks and priorities.
Maintain well-organized Project Operations documentation and shared folders.
Manage meeting schedules for the Project Operations team, including cross-functional meetings.
Coordinate logistics for meetings, workshops, and other team activities.
Support submission of team payment and travel requests.
Provide additional administrative and coordination support as required.
Role Boundaries and Accountability
The Project Operations Officer does not lead projects or make strategic decisions.
The role provides operational and administrative support, receiving day-to-day task direction from the Research Ethics and Compliance Officer and overall direction from the Manager, Project Operations & Busara ISERC.
Ethics and compliance technical decisions and committee-level approvals remain with the Manager, Project Operations & Busara ISERC, supported by the Research Ethics and Compliance Officer.
The role is accountable for timely follow-up, accurate documentation, and well-organized operational records that support effective project delivery.
Knowledge, Skills, and Experience: Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Social Sciences, Business Administration, Public Health, or related discipline).
At least 2 years' experience in an administrative, operations, or coordination role, ideally within a research, academic, or development organization.
Strong organizational skills with proven ability to manage multiple trackers, deadlines, and follow-ups simultaneously.
Excellent written communication skills, with experience drafting professional correspondence (emails, letters, minutes).
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets).
Close attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and record-keeping.
Ability to work under supervision while managing routine tasks independently.
Strong interpersonal skills and professionalism in handling correspondence with external stakeholders (e.g., applicants, reviewers, partners).
Desired Qualifications
Prior exposure to research ethics review processes, regulatory compliance, or IRB/ethics committee administration.
Experience with protocol or case management platforms (e.g., RHInnO, or similar systems).
Familiarity with Kenyan regulatory frameworks (e.g., NACOSTI, Kenya Data Protection Act) or international research ethics standards (Belmont Report, Declaration of Helsinki, CIOMS).
Experience supporting project management functions (scheduling, action tracking, meeting coordination) in a research or donor-funded environment.
Familiarity with subscription/license management and basic budget or invoice tracking.
Experience maintaining knowledge management systems or document repositories.
A proactive, detail-oriented working style with a demonstrated ability to anticipate needs and follow through without close supervision.
Time Allocation
Ethics & Compliance Operational Support (Busara ISERC): 20%
Research & Advisory (RA) Division Support: 30%
Knowledge Management & Project Database Support: 20%
Subscriptions, Payments & Operational Tracking: 15%
Project Operations Team Administration: 15%

Job Summary
IPA’s Right-Fit Evidence (RFE) Unit is a global advisory team that helps development and humanitarian organizations use data and evidence more effectively to achieve greater impact. The Associate Director will lead a portfolio of evidence and learning advisory engagements for funders, implementers, and governments, helping these organizations turn data into decisions by designing learning strategies, building M&E systems, and connecting evidence to real-world outcomes. The Associate Director will also join RFE’s global leadership team, contributing to its strategy and public presence, and will report to an RFE Director, working alongside the Senior Director and five other Associate Directors/Directors across the unit’s 40-plus person team.
Responsibilities
Leading the delivery of a portfolio of advisory engagements (65–75%)
Serve as a senior point of contact for a wide range of clients—including implementers, funders, and government agencies—leading multiple project teams to develop tailor-made solutions for their evidence, learning, and M&E needs and supporting their implementation; manage several engagements at any time (e.g., 3–5), some large and complex, with a high level of autonomy in delivery, across sectors such as education, health, technology, agriculture, finance, social protection, and livelihoods
Oversee various types of external evidence-, learning-, and M&E-related workshops, such as theory of change and learning plan design, and other written advisory deliverables
Provide technical assistance to implement learning plans and strengthen MEL systems, support technical activities such as cost-effectiveness analyses and A/B testing, and build organizational capability to use data and evidence for decision-making
Lead implementer communities of practice, in collaboration with funders
Provide support to a wide array of funders, from high-net-worth individuals to major global foundations and bilateral aid agencies, on issues such as internal learning systems, initiative design, grantmaking processes, grant implementation, grantee technical assistance, and portfolio-level learning
Occasionally lead the design, analysis, and write-up of mixed-methods evaluations and other studies
Advise and support IPA policy and country office teams worldwide on their own technical assistance engagements, often with government partners
Provide performance management to multiple Managers, and possibly Advisors, working on various engagements, and support their professional development
Contributing to new business development, public presence, and external relationship management (15–20%)
Lead the development of a portfolio of new potential engagements, both self-initiated and assigned, often in collaboration with other IPA teams (e.g., sectors, policy, country offices)
Interface with active or potential funders, occasionally representing RFE and IPA more broadly at conferences and other events
Contribute significantly to RFE thought leadership and global influence through the production and dissemination of public goods

Take a proactive role in the innovation and implementation of methodological products and services
Lead at least one stream of RFE’s annual strategic plan (assignments based on skills and interest)
Strengthen internal management systems
Encourage a positive work environment rooted in IPA values, well-being, and sustainability
Provide expertise and mentorship to the team in one or more specific areas (e.g., sector, methodology)

Master’s degree in international public policy, (development) economics, or a related field, with coursework in quantitative methods; PhDs and MBAs also welcome

Superior analytical, quantitative, structured problem-solving, and conceptual thinking skills
Experience translating business questions into analytical frameworks and appropriate metrics
Significant exposure to the design and management of evidence, learning, monitoring, and evaluation strategies and systems

Entrepreneurial self-starter mindset; highly adaptable and versatile, with strong multitasking skills

Passion for making data-driven decision-making a reality in the development sector
English fluency (verbal and written)

Company Details: ABOUT US BECOMING ALIGHT We are and always have been about amazing global citizens taking action to change our world. Forty years ago, Chicago businessman Neal Ball recruited a volunteer relief team who deployed to the Thai-Cambodian border. Even in the face of terrible tragedy, that first team w...read moreas characterized by their incredible energy and belief that anything was possible. In 2019, we took the next big step on a journey to unleash and put into action that same abundant belief. American Refugee Committee became Alight. Were the same organization with the same people doing the same critical work providing health care and clean water, shelter, protection, and economic opportunity to more than 3.5 million people in 19 countries each year. But in solidarity with the people we serve who are too often defined by a single dark moment in their lives, weve dropped the label refugee. Alight sees and helps every person make meaningful change in the world from displaced and marginalized communities in Africa, Asia and the Americas toanyone, anywhere. OUR PURPOSE Alight exists to inspire and unleash the abundance in every person. Were becoming an organization that sees possibility instead of scarcity, that provides services truly worthy of human beings instead of just good enough. From the people we serve to the people who serve alongside us, our purpose is to unlock limitless potential, together. Thats when abundance happens. WHAT WE DO We build a meaningful life for and with the displaced. When we find people displaced from their homes, countries, or lives, our instinct may be to focus only on their basic needs. And that is essential. But its also not a life. A life is filled with joy, dignity, connection, and purpose. And thats what we aim to build. We are an open family of organizations that works closely with refugees, trafficked persons, and economic migrants, to co-design solutions that help them build full and fulfilling lives lives that are Alight.

Job Description:
About the Role
The Head of Market Research owns BURN’s consumer insight capability. The role turns field research, user feedback, and product data into evidence that shapes decisions across new product development, commercial strategy, carbon programs, and market expansion. The role leads the full research lifecycle — from framing the question, through fieldwork, to the insight that changes a decision — and builds the team, standards, and methods to do this consistently across all BURN markets.
Key Responsibilities
Research strategy and methodology
Own BURN’s research agenda: work with stakeholders to identify what the organization needs to learn, prioritize studies collaboratively against upcoming product and commercial decisions, and advise on the most cost- and time-efficient methodologies, techniques, and approaches for each question.
Take leadership of the entire research process end to end — needs assessment, study design, sampling, data acquisition, analysis, and reporting — to consistent quality standards across markets.
Field execution
Spearhead the preparation and execution of field activities, including focus groups, household surveys, in-person interviews, home visits, usability sessions, and remote or phone-based surveys across BURN’s operating markets.
Build and quality-control field research capacity — in-house enumerator teams and third-party agencies — with rigorous training, supervision, and research ethics standards.
Insight and decision support
Produce reports and briefings that clearly and compellingly summarize results, draw out insights, and drive data-driven decisions — insight delivery, not just data delivery.
Triangulate primary research with BURN’s connected-product data (cooking telemetry, app engagement, PAYGO repayment behavior) to build a complete picture of the customer.
Lead evaluations of completed projects and studies, and feed lessons on best practice back to management and the research team to sharpen future project execution.
Stakeholder partnership
Serve as the voice of the customer for internal client departments — new product development, commercial, expansion, and carbon — playing a leading role in relaying user feedback and embedding research in their decisions.
Work closely with country teams to localize research design to each market’s context, language, and channels.
Team leadership
Provide thought leadership in addressing emerging challenges, developing the team’s skills, and continuously improving the quality and impact of the department’s output.
Provide strategic input and direction on restructuring and building up the team over the first six months to achieve the organization’s planned goals.
Perform any other duties reasonably assigned by the manager.
Candidate Profile
Required
8+ years’ experience in market research, consumer insights, or applied social research, including 3+ years leading a research team.
Deep command of quantitative and qualitative methods: survey design and sampling, focus group moderation, in-home and ethnographic research, and statistical analysis.
Proven track record managing multi-country field operations in African or comparable emerging markets, including management of third-party research agencies.
Strong analytical toolkit — advanced Excel plus at least one of SPSS, Stata, R, or Python — and hands-on experience with digital data collection platforms (e.g., SurveyCTO, KoboToolbox/ODK).
Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn complex data into clear, decision-ready recommendations for senior leadership.
Bachelor’s degree in statistics, economics, social sciences, marketing, or a related field.
Willingness to travel regularly across BURN’s markets.
Desirable
Experience researching clean cookstoves, household energy, PAYGO/asset finance, or last-mile distribution.
Experience combining primary research with behavioural or product data (IoT telemetry, app analytics, transaction data).

Job Description:
Job Outline:
The Bid Manager owns the end-to-end bid lifecycle for GardaWorld's security services opportunities across assigned African markets.
This includes leading capture activities to qualify opportunities, defining win strategies, coordinating technical and commercial inputs, ensuring compliance and quality of submissions, and managing post-submission and post-award reviews to capture lessons learned and support operational handover.
The role balances strategic thinking, governance and commercial decision-making with hands-on proposal leadership and content development. The Bid Manager routinely engages country leadership, executive sponsors and subject matter experts to strengthen pursuit strategies, improve win probability and ensure proposals accurately reflect customer requirements, operational capability and commercial objectives.
The Bid Manager is expected to leverage data, market intelligence, competitor insights and bid analytics to continuously improve win rates, proposal quality, decision-making and overall bid function maturity.
Key Responsibilities:
Capture & Opportunity Qualification
Lead early-stage capture activities for medium to high-value pursuits, including stakeholder mapping, customer intelligence gathering, competitor analysis and win-theme development.
Partner with Sales and Business Development teams to understand customer priorities, procurement drivers, pain points and evaluation criteria.
Apply a data-driven bid/no-bid qualification framework, assessing opportunities against strategic fit, probability-to-win, profitability, operational capacity, compliance requirements and risk profile.
Analyse historical bid performance, win/loss trends and market intelligence to support pursuit decisions.
Coordinate executive sponsor and country leadership engagement to shape and approve pursuit strategies.
Maintain visibility of future opportunities and proactively support pursuit readiness activities.
Win Strategy & Proposal Leadership
Define and guide the win strategy with the opportunity owner, help clarify value proposition and differentiators for each pursuit.
Translate win strategies into compelling, customer-focused technical and commercial responses.
Lead cross-functional win strategy workshops and sprint-based response plans.
Establish pursuit themes, customer value messaging and executive positioning.
Act as the primary author/editor for executive summaries, compliance matrices and key proposal content.
Ensure proposal narratives clearly demonstrate GardaWorld's operational capability, customer understanding, value creation and delivery confidence.
Manage proposal resources and workload allocation to ensure priority pursuits are adequately supported.
Proposal Management & Quality Assurance
Manage the end-to-end proposal process, including planning, scheduling, content development, reviews, approvals, clarifications and final submission.
Establish and maintain bid plans, responsibility matrices and submission schedules.
Facilitate structured proposal reviews at key stages of the bid lifecycle, including compliance reviews, peer reviews, red-team reviews and executive approval reviews.
Implement strict pre-submission quality assurance processes, including compliance checks, formatting reviews, pricing alignment and document control.
Ensure all submissions comply with customer instructions, tender requirements and GardaWorld brand standards.
Maintain and continuously improve proposal templates, response libraries, boilerplate content, case studies, CV repositories and evidence playbooks.
Commercial & Risk Coordination
Liaise with Managing Directors, Operations Directors, Country Managers and Business Development teams to ensure alignment across technical, operational and commercial elements.
Identify contractual, commercial, operational, financial and reputational risks associated with pursuits and coordinate mitigation actions.
Work closely with Legal, Finance and Operations teams to ensure risk acceptance and approval requirements are understood and documented.
Support pricing reviews, commercial negotiations and executive approval processes.
Escalate material risks, resource constraints and approval dependencies to senior leadership as appropriate.
Governance, Compliance Tools & AI Enablement
Lead bid governance activities and ensure compliance with delegated authority requirements and approval frameworks.
Maintain transparent approval trails and ensure audit readiness across all pursuits.
Ensure compliance with applicable procurement regulations, licensing requirements, contractual obligations and country-specific operational requirements.
Ensure proposals accurately reflect GardaWorld's certifications, accreditations, compliance obligations and security service capabilities.
Champion the effective use of CRM systems, proposal management platforms and bid analytics tools.
Promote responsible use of AI-assisted drafting and automation technologies by implementing appropriate controls around accuracy, confidentiality, version control and data privacy.
Ensure secure document management and confidentiality across all bid activities.
Post Submission Learning & Continuous Improvement
Own the post-submission feedback process, including customer debriefs, win/loss reviews and internal lessons-learned sessions.
Conduct structured post-mortems to identify key improvement opportunities.
Analyse bid metrics and performance data to improve win rates, proposal quality and process efficiency.
Develop and implement action plans arising from lessons learned.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen bid capability, governance and response quality.
Contract Award & Operational Handover
Support contract award transition activities and ensure a structured handover process to operational delivery teams.
Ensure all bid commitments, assumptions, risks, pricing mechanisms and contractual obligations are clearly documented and communicated.
Participate in operational mobilisation and handover meetings where required.
Work with delivery teams to ensure continuity between proposed solutions and operational execution.
Stakeholder Management & Communications
Coordinate inputs from Operations, Finance, Legal, HR, Procurement, Technical Services and Country Leadership teams.
Secure timely reviews, approvals and decisions throughout the pursuit lifecycle.
Present bid/no-bid recommendations, bid status updates and strategic insights to senior management and executive sponsors.
Build and maintain productive relationships with customers, partners and subcontractors.
Facilitate collaboration across geographically dispersed teams and multiple countries.
People & Process Leadership
Mentor and upskill proposal contributors and subject matter experts.
Promote bid management best practices and proposal excellence across the business.
Drive standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, templates and playbooks.
Support capability development initiatives and training programmes.
Contribute to the maturity and scalability of the Commercial Support Team function.
Key Performance Indicators
Win Rate: Identify opportunities to improve win rate across assigned pursuits by effective review of previous win/loss results from bids submitted.
Submission Compliance: Percentage of bids submitted with full compliance to customer requirements.
On-Time Submission Rate: Percentage of bids submitted within agreed timelines.
Proposal Quality Score: Percentage of submissions passing first-line quality assurance reviews.
Qualification Effectiveness: Percentage of pursued opportunities meeting established qualification criteria and strategic objectives.
Risk Management Effectiveness: Number and value of material risks identified and mitigated before submission.
Time-to-Submission: Reduction in bid cycle times while maintaining quality standards.
Stakeholder Satisfaction: Internal feedback scores relating to responsiveness, coordination and process effectiveness.
Knowledge Management: Currency and utilisation of proposal libraries, templates and reusable content.
Continuous Improvement Delivery: Implementation of agreed improvement actions arising from bid reviews and lessons learned.
Accountability:
Accountable to the Senior Manager, Commercial Support Team for the successful delivery of bids, proposals, governance activities and continuous improvement initiatives.
Authority:
Authority to coordinate cross-functional contributors, enforce bid timelines, lead bid governance processes, manage proposal reviews and escalate commercial, contractual, operational or compliance risks to the Senior Management Team.
Required Skills & Experience:
Minimum 3-5 years' experience in bid management, proposal management, capture management or commercial support roles.
Strong commercial awareness and ability to translate business strategy into compelling customer-focused responses.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional projects under tight deadlines.
Excellent written communication, editing and proposal development skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with the ability to interpret bid data and performance metrics.
Experience conducting bid/no-bid assessments and supporting strategic pursuit decisions.
Strong stakeholder engagement and executive communication skills.
High attention to detail and strong organisational capability.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, together with CRM, document management and proposal management platforms.
Experience working within multi-country, matrix or international business environments.
Knowledge of procurement processes, tendering environments and contract structures.
Security industry experience is desirable but not essential.
Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in business, Marketing, Commercial Management, Communications, Project Management or a related discipline.
APMP Certification (Foundation, Practitioner or Professional) or equivalent bid/capture certification.
Experience with proposal automation platforms and AI-assisted drafting technologies.
Knowledge of public procurement regulations and tendering frameworks within African markets.
Relevant project management, commercial or contract management certifications would be advantageous.

Job Description:
Overall Purpose
The Systems Auditor provides independent assurance and advisory on the adequacy, effectiveness, and security of information systems, IT governance, and technology controls across the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) commercial entities, including Boma Hotels, Eplus, Switch TV, and Boma International Hospitality College (BIHC). The role supports business continuity and operational efficiency by evaluating IT risks, cybersecurity, ERP controls and compliance with information systems policies and standards.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Planning & Execution
Conduct financial, operational, compliance, investigative, IT, and systems audits in line with approved audit plans and professional standards.
Identify operational inefficiencies, control gaps, process improvement opportunities and recommend corrective actions.
Governance, Risk & Internal Controls
Evaluate governance, risk management, internal controls and IT controls to identify weaknesses and improvement opportunities.
Review controls to ensure the accuracy, integrity, security and availability of organizational information.
IT & Systems Audit
Review IT governance, cybersecurity, information security, business continuity, disaster recovery and change management controls.
Review ERP systems, application controls, user access, system configurations and automated controls.
Review IT projects, system implementations, upgrades, and integrations to ensure adequate controls are in place.
Use data analytics and CAATs to identify anomalies, control weaknesses, fraud risks, and unusual transactions.
Compliance & Investigations
Assess compliance with policies, laws, regulations, contractual obligations, ICT requirements, software licensing, and data protection standards.
Conduct fraud and investigative audits and report suspected irregularities or policy violations.
Reporting, Follow-Up & Advisory
Prepare audit reports, communicate findings and follow up on implementation of agreed recommendations.
Advise management on internal controls, risk management, cybersecurity, IT governance and emerging technology risks.
Person Specifications
Academic Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer Engineering or a related field.
Professional Qualifications
CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor) is required.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor/Implementer, or CPA(K) will be an added advantage.
Membership in ISACA or another relevant professional body.
Experience
Minimum of four (4) years' experience in IT audit
Experience auditing ERP systems and business applications such as Sun Systems, Navision, Opera, Microsoft Dynamics or similar platforms.
Experience with data analytics, IT general controls (ITGCs), application controls and systems implementation reviews.
Competencies, Skills and Knowledge
Strong knowledge of IT auditing standards, COBIT, ISO 27001, IT General Controls (ITGCs), cybersecurity and risk management.

Job Description:
About The Role
The Head of Lending is a pure business role. You own the commercial strategy, the credit strategy, and the P&L for Moniepoint's lending business in Kenya. You are not a product leader: Product is responsible for building the lending experience and underwriting infrastructure, Data Science builds and tunes the credit models, Risk and Compliance set the risk appetite and regulatory guardrails, and Finance manages funding and capital. Your job is to decide who we lend to, on what terms, at what price, and to run that business profitably, working closely with each of these functions to get there.
You report to the Head of Business, Kenya, and you sit within the Business function: you own the commercial health of the lending product, with the added weight of a full P&L and direct accountability for portfolio performance and credit outcomes.
The mandate starts with SME lending, the segment with the best fit with Moniepoint's existing merchant base. As the business matures, the scope may extend to other lending products, but your first job is to build a profitable, well-run SME lending business from the ground up.
Your responsibilities:
Own the lending P&L. You are accountable for the full economics of the lending business: interest and fee revenue, cost of funds, credit losses, and operating costs. You build the budget, the forecast, and the reporting cadence that gives you and the Head of Business clear visibility into portfolio health and profitability.
Set the commercial and credit strategy. You decide which SME segments to prioritise, what loan products and terms to offer, and how to price for risk. Pricing and risk tolerance sit with you, but neither is set in isolation: risk thresholds are agreed jointly with Risk and Compliance, and any change in pricing or risk appetite is shared with Product, since it changes what customers experience, and with Growth, since it changes what a segment can expect.
Grow a portfolio with healthy unit economics. You are responsible for building the SME lending book from zero into a significant, profitable portfolio, growing disbursement volumes and revenue while keeping default rates and portfolio quality within agreed limits.
Drive distribution for lending. You define how lending reaches SME customers, whether through direct sales effort, or partner channels. You work with Growth on which segments to prioritise and how lending fits into the broader customer acquisition motion, without owning segment growth yourself.
Partner closely with Product, Data Science, Finance, Risk, and Compliance. You do not own any of these functions, but the lending business cannot run without them. You bring the commercial view to Product's roadmap so the right features get built in the right order. You work with Data Science to define what a good underwriting decision looks like and to keep tightening it. You work with Finance on the cost and availability of lending capital. You work with Risk and Compliance to make sure the business is prudent and compliant with Kenyan lending regulation.
Build and lead the commercial lending team. You will hire and manage the people who run the lending business day to day: portfolio and relationship management, credit operations, and collections.
Build strategic partnerships. You identify and negotiate relationships with strategic partners who can extend our reach into the SME segment.
Who You Are
At least 8 years of experience in lending, and lending specifically, not general banking, general commercial leadership, or a broader financial services career with lending as one part of it. You should have spent your career originating, underwriting, pricing, and managing loan portfolios, and be able to speak fluently and specifically about how a lending business actually makes or loses money.
Direct, demonstrable ownership of a lending P&L. Not a contribution to one, and not an advisory role around one. You should be able to describe the full economics of a portfolio you ran: revenue, cost of funds, credit losses, and how you managed the trade-off between growth and portfolio quality.
A track record of building or meaningfully scaling an SME (or comparable) lending book, ideally in a market with real credit risk challenges and thin credit history data, where good underwriting is a genuine differentiator rather than a solved problem.
Comfort operating cross-functionally without owning the functions around you. You will depend daily on Product, Data Science, Risk, Compliance, and Finance, and you need to be effective at shaping their work through influence and a clear commercial point of view, not through authority over their teams.
Strong quantitative and analytical ability. You should be genuinely comfortable with the unit economics of lending, portfolio performance metrics, and credit risk concepts, able to interrogate a model's output rather than simply consume it.
Exposure to the Kenyan or East African lending market is an advantage but not a requirement. What matters most is that you have built real depth in lending somewhere, and can apply that depth with genuine curiosity to a new and different market.
Cultural Alignment
As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.
Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets.
Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality.
Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality.
Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early.
Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders.
No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes.
Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not.
Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.

Collect feedback from teams and propose improvements to both content and systems.
Help organize knowledge-sharing forums or sessions where teams exchange lessons learned and best practices.

Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple tasks.

Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to build trust and collaborate across teams.
Proactive, curious, and motivated by a strong sense of ownership.
Commitment to Food for Education’s mission and values.

The entire organisation has defined and adapted a knowledge management taxonomy.

c.Ensuring that content which depicts, contain scenes or are of the language intended for adult audience are not aired during the watershed period
d.Giving consumer advise by empowering film and broadcast content consumer with knowledge to make informed choices
ii.Registering and licensing film agents, local and international filmmakers, distributors and exhibitors.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
You will lead internal investigations at M-KOPA end-to-end — from intake through to case closure — across all five operating markets (Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, and South Africa). You will engage stakeholders internally with discretion and sound judgement, safeguard the integrity of the whistleblower and grievance programme, and keep the Board informed through regular, well-evidenced reporting. This role demands not just technical investigative skill but strong personal character — the trust placed in this role by complainants, subjects, and the business depends on it.
Key Responsibilities
Investigation Lifecycle Management
Lead internal investigations end-to-end: intake and triage, planning, evidence gathering, interviews (complainants, witnesses, and subjects), analysis, and final reporting.
Apply consistent, defensible investigative methodology across fraud, misconduct, harassment, safeguarding, and policy-violation cases.
Maintain a clear, well-documented evidence trail for every case, sufficient to withstand scrutiny (including in disciplinary or legal proceedings).
Recommend proportionate, well-reasoned outcomes and remediation actions, including control weaknesses exposed by the investigation.
Stakeholder Engagement & Board Reporting
Engage confidently and sensitively with stakeholders across HR, Legal, Risk, and country leadership throughout the life of a case.
Prepare monthly and quarterly investigation reports for the Head of Internal Audit & Risk and the Board Audit & Risk Committee, summarising case volumes, themes, outcomes, and emerging risk signals.
Manage sensitive conversations with complainants and subjects with empathy, fairness, and absolute discretion.
Whistleblower & Safeguarding Programme
Support the day-to-day operation of the whistleblower and grievance programme, ensuring reported concerns are triaged, tracked, and actioned in line with policy and IIA/ACFE good practice.
Own and maintain the case management platform (tracking, evidence storage, and reporting), ensuring data integrity and confidentiality at all times.
Identify recurring themes or systemic control gaps from case data and feed these into audit planning and risk reporting.
Audit Innovation & Function Development
Champion adoption of M-KOPA’s technology and AI capabilities to enhance audit planning and execution (e.g., risk sensing, scoping, testing, and reporting) while maintaining independence, governance, and confidentiality.
Embed data analytics and continuous monitoring approaches into audit delivery to strengthen coverage, increase efficiency, and enable earlier identification of emerging risks across markets.
Drive standardisation and quality uplift through modern audit tooling (e.g., audit management platforms, workflow automation, and digital working papers), including clear controls over evidence, versioning, and review.
Build capability within the Internal Audit team through coaching and knowledge transfer on analytics- and AI-enabled audit techniques, and contribute to the development of related methodology/standards.
Support the Head of Audit & Risk on strategic projects and function development initiatives as required.
Continuous Improvement & Governance
Contribute to strengthening investigation methodology, templates, and standard operating procedures.
Maintain strict confidentiality and independence, managing conflicts of interest appropriately.
Keep abreast of evolving fraud typologies, investigative techniques, and relevant regulatory requirements across M-KOPA’s markets.
Organisation Structure
Reports to Head of Internal Audit & Risk
Experience, Skills & Qualifications
Education
Degree in a business-related field, law, criminology, or a related field from a recognised university.
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) required.
Other certifications (e.g., CIA, CISA, forensic accounting, or investigations-specific credentials) are an added advantage.
Experience
Minimum of 8 years’ experience, with in-depth, hands-on experience conducting internal investigations (fraud, misconduct, harassment, or safeguarding-related), ideally within financial services, fintech, or a comparably regulated, multi-market environment.
Demonstrated experience preparing investigation findings and reports for senior management and/or Board-level audiences.
Skills
Unimpeachable personal integrity and sound ethical judgement — this role requires trust from all sides of a case.
Strong interviewing skills: able to build rapport, ask probing questions, and remain composed and neutral under pressure.
Excellent written communication — able to produce clear, factual, defensible case reports.
Discreet and calm under pressure; able to handle emotionally difficult and highly confidential matters with maturity.
Strong stakeholder management across HR, Legal, Risk, and country leadership.
Ability to manage a caseload independently, prioritising sensitively and appropriately across concurrent investigations.
Comfortable operating across multiple markets and cultures, with willingness to travel.

Job Summary
Our client is seeking to recruit a competent and detail-oriented Declaration Officer to support operations within their bonded warehouse. The successful candidate will be responsible for preparing and processing customs declarations, coordinating the receipt, storage, and release of bonded cargo, maintaining accurate customs and warehouse documentation, and ensuring compliance with applicable customs regulations and bonded warehouse procedures.
The role requires strong knowledge of customs clearance processes, import and export documentation, cargo tracking, and inventory reconciliation. The successful candidate will work closely with KRA customs officers, clearing agents, shipping lines, and warehouse personnel to facilitate efficient cargo movement and ensure that all bonded goods are properly accounted for and handled in accordance with regulatory requirements

Prepare, submit, and process customs declarations for goods entering and leaving the bonded warehouse in accordance with applicable customs regulations.

Monitor customs duties, taxes, and other applicable charges, ensuring that payments and supporting documentation are properly coordinated.
Prepare regular reports on customs declarations, cargo clearance status, warehouse stock movements, outstanding entries, and related activities.

Ensure confidentiality of company, client, and customs-related information.

At least 6 years of relevant experience in customs declarations, clearing and forwarding, or bonded warehouse operations.

Strong knowledge of KRA customs procedures, bonded warehouse regulations, and import and export documentation.
Proven experience in preparing customs entries and processing cargo release, transfer, and re-export documentation.
Familiarity with customs declaration systems and warehouse management systems.
Strong knowledge of cargo documentation, inventory reconciliation, and customs compliance.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
Excellent organizational, communication, and record-keeping skills.
Ability to work under pressure and meet strict cargo clearance deadlines.
High level of integrity, accuracy, and attention to detail.

Customs declaration and documentation management.
Bonded warehouse operations and inventory control.
Customs compliance and regulatory knowledge.
Attention to detail and accuracy.
Problem-solving and analytical skills.
Communication and stakeholder coordination.
Time management and ability to meet deadlines.
Integrity and accountability.
