Job Description:
Role Summary
We are looking for an experienced and dependable Deputy Lead – Security to support the Head of Security in overseeing day-to-day security operations and safeguarding the Company’s people, assets and premises.
The role will work closely with the Head of Security in overseeing security operations and will deputise when required, supporting manpower deployment, access control, surveillance, incident management, investigations and emergency response.
This role requires a hands-on security professional with strong leadership skills, sound judgement, integrity and the ability to manage security teams effectively while maintaining high standards of operational discipline.
Key Responsibilities
Security Operations & Manpower Management
Support the Head of Security in coordinating day-to-day security operations and deputise in their absence.
Plan and coordinate security manpower deployment to ensure adequate coverage across designated security points.
Prepare and manage duty rosters, shifts, officer replacements and redeployment.
Conduct regular patrols, perimeter inspections and manpower audits to ensure officer alertness, discipline, grooming and performance.
Ensure effective protection of Company people, assets and premises against theft, intrusion, vandalism, fire and other security threats.
Oversee security controls relating to receipt and dispatch of goods, offloading of raw materials, waste disposal and movement through designated factory entry and exit points.
Ensure security personnel are properly deployed, briefed and compliant with established security procedures.
Access Control & Surveillance
Oversee the entry and exit of employees, visitors, contractors, vehicles and other persons accessing Company premises.
Ensure searches and access-control procedures are conducted professionally and in accordance with Company requirements.
Monitor CCTV, access control, alarm and other security systems and ensure exceptions or suspicious activities are promptly addressed.
Identify security vulnerabilities and recommend appropriate preventive and corrective measures.
Team & Performance Management
Supervise, guide and motivate security personnel to maintain high standards of discipline, professionalism and performance.
Conduct regular security briefings and ensure officers understand their responsibilities and deployment requirements.
Monitor security personnel performance and escalate conduct, discipline or performance concerns for appropriate action.
Promote accountability, teamwork and adherence to Company standards across the security function.
Incident Management & Investigations
Respond promptly to security incidents, emergencies and operational challenges and ensure appropriate escalation.
Conduct preliminary security investigations and gather relevant information and intelligence as required.
Ensure incidents, irregularities, property damage, theft and unauthorised activities are accurately recorded in the Occurrence Book and other relevant records.
Prepare timely, factual and confidential investigation and incident reports for management review.
Support emergency preparedness and response to security-related threats and incidents.
Reporting & Compliance
Maintain accurate security records including Occurrence Books, deployment registers, duty rosters, incident reports and equipment records.
Monitor proper use, custody and accountability of security equipment and resources.
Ensure security operations comply with Company policies, procedures and applicable security standards.
Prepare periodic security reports and operational updates for the Head of Security and Management.
Identify recurring security risks and recommend measures to strengthen controls and improve security operations.
Requirements
Ideal Candidate Profile
Education & Professional Training
Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Criminology or a related field will be an added advantage.
Relevant professional security training is required.
Experience
Minimum 10 years of relevant security experience, including at least 5 years in a supervisory or security leadership role, with proven experience managing security teams and operations within the manufacturing or FMCG industry.
Previous experience in corporate security, law enforcement or the military is desirable.
Practical experience with CCTV surveillance, access control systems and alarm systems.
Good understanding of manpower planning, rostering, investigations, incident management, emergency response and security risk management.
Experience preparing security reports and maintaining operational security records.
Skills & Competencies
Strong leadership and team-management capability.
Sound judgement and decision-making.
Strong investigation and problem-solving skills.
Good written and verbal communication skills.
Strong report-writing and documentation skills.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel.
High level of integrity, confidentiality, discipline and accountability.
Ability to remain calm and make appropriate decisions during security incidents and emergencies.
Flexibility to work shifts, weekends and public holidays where operationally required.
What Success Looks Like
Effective security coverage and manpower deployment across assigned operations.
Strong discipline, accountability and performance within the security team.
Effective access control and protection of Company people, assets and premises.
Security incidents responded to, investigated, documented and escalated promptly.
Improved identification and mitigation of security risks and vulnerabilities.
Accurate and timely security reporting to support management decision-making.
Effective continuity of security leadership when deputising the Head of Security.

Job Description:
Position Summary
InformAction is inviting applications for the position of Driver & Logistics Support Officer.
The successful candidate will be responsible for providing safe and reliable transportation while also supporting the organisation with basic logistics, field activities, workshops and other operational requirements.
Please provide accurate information in all sections of this form. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.
Key Responsibilities
Driving and Transportation
Provide safe, reliable and timely transportation for InformAction staff, consultants, partners and other authorized passengers.
Drive staff to and from official meetings, field activities, workshops, trainings and other assignments as authorized.
Undertake local and out-of-town travel, including travel to rural and difficult-to-access locations when required.
Plan routes in advance and consider traffic, road conditions, weather, security and expected travel times.
Ensure that passengers are transported safely and professionally at all times.
Maintain punctuality and communicate promptly where delays or changes to travel arrangements arise.
Comply with all applicable traffic laws and organizational requirements relating to official travel.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality and discretion regarding information obtained while transporting staff and other passengers.
Vehicle Management and Maintenance
Conduct routine checks of the assigned vehicle before and after journeys.
Check essential items including tires, oil, coolant, fuel, lights, brakes and other basic vehicle requirements.
Report mechanical faults, damage or other concerns immediately to the supervisor.
Ensure that vehicle servicing and repairs are undertaken as scheduled and properly documented.
Keep the assigned vehicle clean and in good working condition.
Maintain required vehicle documents and ensure that they are available and valid.
Ensure that the vehicle has the necessary emergency equipment, tools, and spare tire.
Maintain accurate vehicle log sheets, fuel records, mileage records, and other required documentation.
Report accidents, incidents, traffic violations or vehicle damage promptly and in accordance with organizational procedures.
Logistics and Field Activity Support
Provide basic logistical support during workshops, trainings, meetings, field visits, and other organizational activities.
Assist with the collection, transportation, loading, unloading and arrangement of equipment and materials required for activities.
Support venue preparation, including arranging materials and basic equipment before activities begin.
Assist with transportation and coordination of participants where required and authorized.
Collect and deliver documents, supplies, equipment and other materials as assigned.
Support staff in ensuring that logistical requirements are confirmed before field activities commence.
Assist with purchasing or collecting approved supplies and ensure that relevant receipts and supporting documentation are submitted.
Support the movement and safe handling of organizational assets and equipment.
Provide practical support to program and administrative teams during field activities as required.
Planning and Coordination
Confirm transport and logistical requirements with the relevant staff member before an assignment.
Plan journeys and logistical activities to ensure that tasks are completed within the required timelines.
Communicate effectively with staff, participants, suppliers, venues and other relevant persons when carrying out assigned duties.
Inform the supervisor of any logistical challenges that may affect an activity and propose practical solutions where possible.
Prioritize tasks appropriately when handling multiple assignments.
Maintain flexibility when program activities or travel arrangements change.
Safety and Security
Prioritize the safety of passengers, staff, equipment and other organizational assets at all times.
Follow InformAction’s security and safety procedures during travel and field assignments.
Exercise appropriate judgment when driving in unfamiliar, remote or challenging locations.
Report security concerns, road incidents, and other risks to the relevant supervisor.
Avoid driving when conditions or the vehicle present an unreasonable safety risk and immediately report such concerns to the supervisor.
Support staff in following applicable security and safety procedures during field activities.
Accountability and Compliance
Maintain accurate records relating to vehicle use, fuel, mileage, servicing and other assigned logistical activities.
Account for any funds provided for authorized purchases or logistical activities and submit the required receipts and balances.
Ensure that organizational vehicles, equipment, and other resources are used only for authorized purposes
Comply with InformAction’s policies and procedures, including those relating to safeguarding, PSEAH, fraud prevention, whistleblowing, data protection, security and occupational health and safety.
Maintain professional conduct when representing InformAction during official travel and field activities.
Report any suspected misuse, loss, damage or unauthorized use of organizational resources through the appropriate channels.
General Support
Provide reasonable administrative and operational support to the organization when required and where such duties are consistent with the position.
Work collaboratively with programme, finance, administration and other teams to support smooth implementation of organizational activities.
Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor that are consistent with the objectives of the position.
Qualifications
A valid Kenyan driving license appropriate for the vehicles assigned to the position.
A diploma in social sciences or related fields. A degree would be an added advantage.
A minimum of three years’ professional driving experience, preferably within an NGO, development organization, private sector company or other institution.
Demonstrated experience driving, including rural and difficult road conditions, preferably a resident in one of the focus counties with extensive knowledge of the road network.
Basic knowledge of vehicle maintenance and troubleshooting.
Basic computer literacy.
Basic understanding of logistics and administrative support.
Experience supporting workshops, trainings, meetings, field activities or similar events is an added advantage.
A valid Certificate of Good Conduct may be required at the appropriate stage of the recruitment process.
Knowledge of Kenya’s road network
Basic knowledge of occupational health, safety and security practices relevant to driving and field travel.

The successful candidate will be responsible for providing safe and reliable transportation while also supporting the organisation with basic logistics, field activities, workshops and other operational requirements.
Please provide accurate information in all sections of this form. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.
Key Responsibilities
Driving and Transportation
Provide safe, reliable and timely transportation for InformAction staff, consultants, partners and other authorized passengers.
Drive staff to and from official meetings, field activities, workshops, trainings and other assignments as authorized.
Undertake local and out-of-town travel, including travel to rural and difficult-to-access locations when required.
Plan routes in advance and consider traffic, road conditions, weather, security and expected travel times.
Ensure that passengers are transported safely and professionally at all times.
Maintain punctuality and communicate promptly where delays or changes to travel arrangements arise.
Comply with all applicable traffic laws and organizational requirements relating to official travel.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality and discretion regarding information obtained while transporting staff and other passengers.
Vehicle Management and Maintenance
Conduct routine checks of the assigned vehicle before and after journeys.
Check essential items including tires, oil, coolant, fuel, lights, brakes and other basic vehicle requirements.
Report mechanical faults, damage or other concerns immediately to the supervisor.
Ensure that vehicle servicing and repairs are undertaken as scheduled and properly documented.
Keep the assigned vehicle clean and in good working condition.
Maintain required vehicle documents and ensure that they are available and valid.
Ensure that the vehicle has the necessary emergency equipment, tools, and spare tire.
Maintain accurate vehicle log sheets, fuel records, mileage records, and other required documentation.
Report accidents, incidents, traffic violations or vehicle damage promptly and in accordance with organizational procedures.
Logistics and Field Activity Support
Provide basic logistical support during workshops, trainings, meetings, field visits, and other organizational activities.
Assist with the collection, transportation, loading, unloading and arrangement of equipment and materials required for activities.
Support venue preparation, including arranging materials and basic equipment before activities begin.
Assist with transportation and coordination of participants where required and authorized.
Collect and deliver documents, supplies, equipment and other materials as assigned.
Support staff in ensuring that logistical requirements are confirmed before field activities commence.
Assist with purchasing or collecting approved supplies and ensure that relevant receipts and supporting documentation are submitted.
Support the movement and safe handling of organizational assets and equipment.
Provide practical support to program and administrative teams during field activities as required.
Planning and Coordination
Confirm transport and logistical requirements with the relevant staff member before an assignment.
Plan journeys and logistical activities to ensure that tasks are completed within the required timelines.
Communicate effectively with staff, participants, suppliers, venues and other relevant persons when carrying out assigned duties.
Inform the supervisor of any logistical challenges that may affect an activity and propose practical solutions where possible.
Prioritize tasks appropriately when handling multiple assignments.
Maintain flexibility when program activities or travel arrangements change.
Safety and Security
Prioritize the safety of passengers, staff, equipment and other organizational assets at all times.
Follow InformAction’s security and safety procedures during travel and field assignments.
Exercise appropriate judgment when driving in unfamiliar, remote or challenging locations.
Report security concerns, road incidents, and other risks to the relevant supervisor.
Avoid driving when conditions or the vehicle present an unreasonable safety risk and immediately report such concerns to the supervisor.
Support staff in following applicable security and safety procedures during field activities.
Accountability and Compliance
Maintain accurate records relating to vehicle use, fuel, mileage, servicing and other assigned logistical activities.
Account for any funds provided for authorized purchases or logistical activities and submit the required receipts and balances.
Ensure that organizational vehicles, equipment, and other resources are used only for authorized purposes
Comply with InformAction’s policies and procedures, including those relating to safeguarding, PSEAH, fraud prevention, whistleblowing, data protection, security and occupational health and safety.
Maintain professional conduct when representing InformAction during official travel and field activities.
Report any suspected misuse, loss, damage or unauthorized use of organizational resources through the appropriate channels.
General Support
Provide reasonable administrative and operational support to the organization when required and where such duties are consistent with the position.
Work collaboratively with programme, finance, administration and other teams to support smooth implementation of organizational activities.
Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor that are consistent with the objectives of the position.
Qualifications
A valid Kenyan driving license appropriate for the vehicles assigned to the position.
A diploma in social sciences or related fields. A degree would be an added advantage.
A minimum of three years’ professional driving experience, preferably within an NGO, development organization, private sector company or other institution.
Demonstrated experience driving, including rural and difficult road conditions, preferably a resident in one of the focus counties with extensive knowledge of the road network.
Basic knowledge of vehicle maintenance and troubleshooting.
Basic computer literacy.
Basic understanding of logistics and administrative support.
Experience supporting workshops, trainings, meetings, field activities or similar events is an added advantage.
A valid Certificate of Good Conduct may be required at the appropriate stage of the recruitment process.
Knowledge of Kenya’s road network
Basic knowledge of occupational health, safety and security practices relevant to driving and field travel.

Job Description:
Responsibilities
Access, Security, and Accountability
Hold and secure the laboratory room keys and administer authorized biometric access in accordance with hospital policy.
Arrange and document temporary access for scheduled workshops, faculty, residents, and visiting groups; maintain an accurate access list and promptly remove access that is no longer required.

Ensure that equipment and consumables do not leave the laboratory without documented authorization and a clear return plan.
Equipment, Inventory, and Repairs
Maintain a current master inventory of cameras, monitors, instruments, trainers, recording equipment, accessories, consumables, and other laboratory assets, including identification number, condition, location, and service status where applicable.
Keep equipment organized, labeled, clean, securely stored, and ready for use.
Complete daily equipment checks; perform safe first-line operational troubleshooting within training and authority and escalate technical or clinical concerns promptly.
Coordinate preventive maintenance and repair, vendor or biomedical support; track unresolved repairs to completion.
Monitor consumable levels and anticipated demand, and submit restocking or replacement needs early enough to prevent avoidable training interruption.
Scheduling and Training-Group Preparation
Maintain the authoritative laboratory schedule and confirm bookings before communicating them to users; prevent double-booking and identify conflicts early.
Maintain and update the visiting-groups calendar. Contact each expected group at least monthly, and again as needed, to confirm dates, participant numbers, training objectives, faculty, equipment, specimen, recording, and access requirements.
Coordinate the lab schedule with faculty and residents.
Prepare training stations, instruments, consumables, checklists, sign-in materials, audiovisual systems, and other materials before each session or workshop.
Support training trips and off-site projects by preparing documented equipment and materials, confirming transport and return arrangements, and reconciling all items after the activity.
Attendance, Training Records, and Video Management
Maintain complete and accurate attendance and sign-in records for all laboratory sessions, workshops, and visiting groups.
Label, organize, quality-check, and upload training videos to the designated system promptly; maintain an index of uploaded recordings.
Protect training records and videos from unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or loss, and follow approved retention and deletion processes.
Maintain learner progress records required by the LAPP program and provide accurate data for reports and program review.
Specimens, Cleanliness, and Safe Practice
Coordinate approved logistics for animal organs or other specimens used in training, including timing, quantity, transport, receipt, storage, preparation, and availability for the scheduled session.
Follow hospital requirements for infection prevention, personal protective equipment, biological-material handling, decontamination, waste segregation, and disposal; obtain guidance when requirements are unclear.
Maintain laboratory cleanliness, orderly work surfaces, and good laboratory practice before, during, and after all activities.
Perform daily checks to confirm that equipment, sharps, specimens, waste, and surfaces have been handled safely and that the laboratory is ready for the next group/session.
Learner and Faculty Support
Develop and maintain practical competence in the laboratory's laparoscopic skills, equipment setup, simulation tasks, assessment tools, and training workflow under designated faculty guidance.
Orient every participant to the LAPP program and skills laboratory before training, including program objectives, laboratory access and layout, equipment-handling expectations, safety and cleanliness procedures, recording requirements, and participan
Enroll each participant in the LAPP program.
Observe training activity videos and provide timely, specific, actionable, and respectful feedback to faculty and residents using LAPP objectives, checklists, and proficiency standards.
Distinguish operational and skills-lab feedback from independent clinical judgment; refer clinical questions, disputed assessments, or significant learner concerns to the responsible faculty member or Medical Education Programs Coordinator.
Collect feedback from users and recommend practical improvements to lab flow, equipment readiness, training materials, data quality, and learner experience.
Reporting
Submit a weekly report to the Medical Education Programs Coordinator covering sessions completed and planned, learner training progress, attendance, inventory status, consumable needs, equipment downtime or repairs, incidents, unresolved risks, and a
Submit a monthly report on LAPP projects and trips, including activities completed, participants, outcomes, equipment and materials used, unresolved issues, lessons learned, and the next month's planned activities.
Notify the Medical Education Programs Coordinator immediately of significant equipment loss or damage, access or confidentiality breaches, safety incidents, specimen-handling concerns, or any issue likely to cancel or materially disrupt training.
Requirements
Demonstrated critical-thinking and problem-solving ability, including the capacity to identify causes, test practical solutions, and escalate issues appropriately.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate several schedules, training groups, equipment needs, and deadlines at the same time.
High personal integrity and accountability in managing restricted access, confidential information, and expensive, delicate equipment.
Clear written and oral communication skills, including the confidence and professionalism to give constructive feedback to surgeons, faculty, residents, and other learners.
Curiosity and self-directed learning, with willingness to learn laparoscopic equipment, simulation tasks, training workflows, and the LAPP skills curriculum.
Practical digital skills for calendars, spreadsheets, electronic records, video recording, file naming, uploading, and routine troubleshooting.
Ability to work independently, prioritize urgent operational needs, follow through on unresolved matters, and report risks early.
Ability to collaborate respectfully with clinical faculty, residents, visiting groups, Medical Education staff, and hospital support departments.
Education, training, or work experience that demonstrates the competencies above.
Experience in a skills laboratory, simulation center, training program, clinical environment, technical workshop, equipment service setting, events operation, or comparable role.
Experience maintaining inventories, coordinating repairs, supporting audiovisual systems, or managing digital training records.
Familiarity with infection-prevention practices, personal protective equipment, and safe handling and disposal of biological training specimens.

Job Description:
About the role
Digital Green is seeking a MEL & Research Manager based in Nairobi to support monitoring, evaluation, research, and learning for our work in Kenya and Nigeria, with a particular focus on FarmerChat, Digital Green’s AI-powered agricultural advisory platform.
This is a hands-on research and analytics role at the intersection of agriculture, digital technology and AI. The MEL Research Manager will help us understand who is using FarmerChat, how farmers engage with the platform, whether the information and advisory they receive is useful and trusted, how farmers act on that information, and ultimately whether FarmerChat contributes to meaningful improvements in farmers’ practices, productivity, income, as well as agency and resilience.
The role will combine traditional MEL and research methods with analysis of digital product data and experimentation with new approaches to measurement and learning. This may include designing and analyzing farmer surveys, conducting qualitative research, developing sampling strategies, and linking self-reported outcomes with FarmerChat backend data to better understand patterns of adoption, engagement, and impact.
At the same time, we want to test new ways of collecting data and learning from farmers—including voice-based methods, AI-enabled or agentic MEL approaches, alternative survey formats, and different approaches to incentivizing participation. The MEL Research Manager should be curious and willing to experiment, while also thinking critically about the strengths, limitations, biases, data quality, cost, farmer experience, and ethical implications of different methods. We are looking for someone who can help us test what works, learn from what does not, and identify when a new approach offers real advantages over more traditional methods.
The Manager will report to the Director of MEL and work closely with Digital Green’s Kenya program, product, user insights/ux research, and technology teams, as well as external research and implementation partners.
We are looking for someone who has already developed a strong foundation in MEL or applied research but is eager to continue developing their technical and leadership skills. This is an opportunity for a curious and ambitious researcher to take increasing ownership of research and evaluation while contributing to Digital Green’s broader evidence agenda for FarmerChat.
What you will do
Design research and measurement for FarmerChat
Support the design and implementation of MEL studies and evaluations that assess FarmerChat’s reach, engagement, user experience, behavior change, and outcomes for farmers.
Translate program and product questions into clear research questions, hypotheses, indicators, and measurement approaches.
Design high-quality quantitative survey instruments covering areas such agricultural practices, relevance and trust of advisory, adoption of recommendations, productivity, costs, income, agency, resilience, and other farmer outcomes
Design qualitative interview and focus group guides to explore farmers’ experiences with FarmerChat, including how and why they use it, what they find useful, barriers to engagement, and how advisory influences their decisions.
Contribute to research design decisions, including sampling approaches, sample-size calculations, statistical power, comparison groups, and timing of measurement.
Support experimental and quasi-experimental studies, including randomized evaluations and A/B tests, where appropriate.
Help design and test alternative approaches to data collection, including voice-based research, AI-enabled or agentic MEL, shorter or adaptive survey formats, and different approaches to participant incentives.
Assess the trade-offs between different methods, including validity, representativeness, bias, cost, response rates, data quality, and participant experience.
Analyze farmer and product data
Clean, manage, and analyze quantitative data using Excel and Stata and/or R.
Analyze FarmerChat backend and product-usage data alongside survey and qualitative data to build a richer understanding of farmer engagement and outcomes.
Examine patterns such as frequency and intensity of FarmerChat use, types of questions farmers ask, agricultural value chains of interest, retention and drop-off, and differences across farmer segments, including gender based analysis
Conduct descriptive and inferential statistical analysis, including significance testing, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and subgroup analysis.
Link survey responses with FarmerChat usage data where appropriate to explore relationships between digital engagement, adoption of advisory, and farmer outcomes.
Work closely with product and data colleagues to define meaningful metrics and ensure that data generated through FarmerChat can support MEL and research questions.
Compare findings across different data-collection approaches and help determine which methods are most appropriate for different research questions.
Lead high-quality field research
Coordinate quantitative and qualitative data collection with farmers in Kenya and Nigeria, including working with field teams, enumerators, and external research firms.
Develop sampling plans and support recruitment of farmers for research.
Train and support enumerators and research teams on survey instruments and research protocols.
Monitor incoming data and conduct systematic data-quality checks throughout data collection.
Conduct or support farmer interviews, focus groups, and other qualitative research.
Pilot new data-collection approaches and document lessons on what works, for whom, and under what conditions.
Ensure research is conducted ethically and that farmers’ privacy and data are appropriately protected.
Turn evidence into learning and action
Synthesize quantitative, qualitative, and FarmerChat usage data to answer practical questions for Digital Green.
Produce clear research briefs, presentations, reports, and other materials for internal teams, partners, and donors.
Translate findings into practical recommendations for FarmerChat product development and program implementation.
Work with program teams to understand whether and how FarmerChat is contributing to changes in agricultural knowledge, practices, productivity, costs, income, and other outcomes.
Contribute evidence and analysis for donor reporting, proposals, learning agendas, and strategic decision-making.
Document not only successful approaches but also experiments that do not work, so that learning can inform future research and product decisions.
Build strong research systems and documentation
Maintain rigorous documentation of research designs, survey instruments, sampling decisions, datasets, codebooks, analysis files, statistical code, assumptions, and methodological decisions.
Develop reproducible and well-organized analytical workflows, so that analyses can be reviewed, updated, and built upon over time.
Document pilots of new MEL approaches, including methodology, implementation challenges, data-quality issues, results, and recommendations.
Help strengthen Digital Green’s MEL systems and approaches for measuring the performance and impact of digital and AI-enabled agricultural advisory.
Ensure that lessons from individual studies are captured and used to improve future research and measurement.
What we are looking for
Required qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in economics, statistics, public policy, development studies, project management, agricultural economics, social sciences, or another relevant quantitative or research-oriented field, with approximately 3–5 years of relevant experience in MEL, applied research, or evaluation; or a relevant Master’s degree with approximately 1–3 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience designing quantitative surveys and other research instruments.
Strong analytical skills, including proficiency in Excel and working proficiency in Stata and/or R or related software
Solid understanding of applied statistics, including descriptive statistics, confidence intervals, statistical significance, and hypothesis testing.
Understanding of sampling methods and sample-size calculations; familiarity with statistical power and power calculations.
Experience cleaning, managing, and analyzing survey or program datasets.
Experience conducting or supporting qualitative research, including interviews and/or focus groups.
Strong attention to data quality and experience developing or implementing data-quality checks.
Excellent documentation skills, including the ability to clearly document research methods, instruments, datasets, analytical decisions, and findings.
Ability to translate data and research findings into clear insights and recommendations for colleagues who are not researchers.
Ability to work effectively across teams, particularly with program, product, and data/technology colleagues.
Strong written and spoken English + local language
Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn new tools, analytical approaches, and research methods independently.
Ability to travel (X days per month) in the field.
Nice to have
Experience working in agriculture or with smallholder farmers in Kenya or East Africa.
Experience conducting MEL or research for digital products, digital advisory services, AI-enabled tools, or other technology-for-development programs.
Experience analyzing product or administrative data in addition to traditional survey data.
Experience linking survey data with digital usage or transactional datasets.
Experience with SurveyCTO, KoboToolbox, ODK, or similar digital data-collection platforms.
Experience with randomized evaluations, A/B testing, quasi-experimental methods, and impact evaluation.
Experience with voice-based research, conversational surveys, AI-enabled research tools, or other emerging approaches to data collection.
Experience testing participant incentives or other approaches to improving participation and response rates.
Experience managing external research firms, enumerators, or field research teams.
Knowledge of Kenya’s agricultural sector and smallholder farming context.

Job Title: Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer,Power Partnership
Job Description:
Job overview
The Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer coordinates quality and learning across the six POWER country programs. The role works through country WPE and program teams, POWER’s women-led and local partners, and the WPE Global Practice, and coordinates with the Award Management Unit (AMU), which leads the donor relationship with Irish Aid. It is accountable for technical quality assistance against IRC core WPE standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards for the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, and for tracking and reporting delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six countries so that deviation is identified early. The position contributes to the partnership’s advocacy pillar and to the design of the next partnership phase.
Major responsibilities
The role holds the technical quality of POWER delivery to IRC's WPE standards, keeps the partnership and the WPE Global Practice in two-way exchange ,rather than a one directional flow of standards downward, and tracks delivery across six countries against scope, timeline and budget so that deviation is flagged early enough for adaptive management
Provide quality oversight across the six country programs, so that survivor-centered response, case management, women and girls' safe spaces, clinical and MHPSS referral pathways, and social norms work meet IRC WPE technical standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
Serve as the connective role between the POWER partnership and the WPE Global Practice, translating core standards into partnership contexts and carrying partnership-generated practice back into the core.
Support the sequencing of prevention and social norms activities to context, so they are introduced only where women-led community analysis confirms the preconditions for safe implementation are met.
Maintain coherence of approach across the six countries without flattening contextual difference, identifying where a shared standard applies and where local adaptation is warranted.
Track and report on delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six country programs, flagging deviation early enough for adaptive management rather than end-of-cycle correction.
Ensure MEAL and program data feed directly into program adaptation, so that what the data shows changes what the program does, not only what it reports.
Connect program data and implementation evidence to wider sector trends and debates, including comparable protection and GBV programming elsewhere.
Learning, evidence, and the partnership learning agenda
The role leads the program's learning function, treating implementation learning as a legitimate evidence pathway rather than a lesser substitute for external research. It also support the partnership’s advocacy pillar, so that evidence generated with the partners informs partners’ own advocacy and IRC’s policy positioning.
Lead the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, coordinating cross-country learning cycles, documentation, and structured reflection between IRC and partners.
Position women-led safety audits as community-generated risk analysis, and strengthen the pathway from that analysis into local decision-making and adaptive management.
Build the program's evidence base on what enables and constrains change in protracted crisis settings, surfacing failure modes honestly, including referral systems that exist on paper but not in practice, and norms work that shifts survey scores without shifting community behavior.
Ensure learning is co-owned with partners and feeds their own institutional positioning, not only IRC's reporting obligations.
Steward the POWER advocacy pillar, supporting partners to carry community-generated analysis into local, national, and global advocacy where they hold standing in their own right.
Work with advocacy and policy colleagues so the partnership's evidence informs IRC positioning toward donors, multilaterals, and normative bodies.
Strengthening the core and surge capacity of women-led and local organizations
The role supports partners on two distinct fronts, their institutional core and their capacity to surge in emergencies, resisting the pattern where localization language coexists with authority still held by the international actor.
Support partner institutional strengthening across governance, financial systems, safeguarding, and MEAL in ways partners define and lead, consistent with the PEERS principles and the direct funding commitment.
Strengthen partner surge and emergency response readiness under the emergency response pillar, so local organizations hold a credible role when crises escalate rather than being displaced by international surge.
Advance the shift of analytical and decision-making authority toward partners with genuine institutional standing, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, co-designing tools and thresholds with them rather than imposing them.
Support the broader civil society and women's movement ecosystem the partnership connects to, recognizing partners as governance and coordination actors in their own right.
Strategic focus on women and girls in conflict settings
The role keeps women and girls in active conflict and protracted displacement at the center of the partnership, including where conflict-related sexual violence is a feature of the context.
Ensure program design and adaptation are anchored in the realities faced by women and girls across the six contexts, several of which are shaped by active conflict and large-scale displacement.
Support conflict-related sexual violence sensitive practice where relevant, including safe and consent-based documentation, clinical pathways, and Do No Harm decisions taken at closest proximity to violence, with pattern awareness fed upward.
Keep adolescent girls visible as a distinct group rather than folded into a general women-and-girls category.
Partnership and donor relationship management
The role supports coherence of technical delivery across countries and reporting cycles, contributing technical content into the strategic relationship with Irish Aid, which AMU stewards and holds overall.
Serve as a central program coordination point for the POWER partnership, supporting planning, adaptive management, amendments, and quality reporting to Irish Aid in coordination with the European DE & Frameworks team (Irish Aid).
Feed technical content on program direction, learning, and strategic opportunities into AMU's communication with Irish Aid and the Department of Foreign Affairs. .
Coordinate across the six country teams and the relevant IRC technical, advocacy, awards, and finance functions to keep the partnership coherent and its commitments met.
Contribute technical input to AMU's design and negotiation of the next Strategic Partnership phase (post-2027), including program scope, theory of change, and the monitoring, evaluation and learning framework, coordinating input from WPE pillar leads, country teams, and partners, under AMU's overall lead on negotiation, timeline, and the donor relationship.
Key working relationships
Works closely with:
AMU, Global and VPRU Advocacy; VPRU MEAL/METAL Unit.
Country WPE and program leads across the six POWER countries; POWER women-led and local partners, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya; IRC Awards Management Unit (AMU); VPRU Business Development; Irish Aid and Department of Foreign Affairs counterparts.

Demonstrated skills and competencies:
Strong technical grounding in WPE practice and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
Practical experience in feminist partnership and localization, including working with women-led organizations as partners rather than subgrantees.
Learning and MEAL capability, with the judgment to treat implementation learning as evidence and to surface difficult findings.
Program and grant management across multiple countries, including tracking and reporting r delivery against scope, timeline, and budget, and the systems to flag deviation early.

Job Description:
About the role
The Customer Operations Associate will report to the Customer Operations Lead. As we launch our operations in Tanzania, this role will be based in Kenya while exclusively serving the Tanzania market, using our Kenya office as a strategic operational hub. The ideal candidate must be Tanzanian, whether currently living in Kenya or Tanzania. Candidates currently based in Tanzania must be willing to relocate to Kenya for the role.
The Customer Operations Associate is Turaco's direct point of contact with our customers and is accountable for what those customers experience. This contact reaches customers through several channels, including phone, WhatsApp, other approved digital channels, and in person in the field. The Associate is expected to work across all of these channels, explaining insurance products, benefits, and payment methods clearly; guiding customers through claims accurately and on time; and spending regular, planned time at partner branches and in the communities our customers come from, supporting partner teams and bringing back insights from the field.
Where Turaco's approved AI tools support customer and claims work, the Associate will be expected to use these tools while also checking and reviewing their output before it reaches a customer, and escalating recurring errors to help improve the tools over time.
The role covers the full breadth of Customer Operations work, and this breadth is central to the position rather than incidental. Claims administration, customer surveys and Voice of Customer activities, outbound and IVR campaigns, backlog clearance, and partner engagement are all core responsibilities. The Associate is expected to be able to take on any of these activities and move between them as Customer Operations priorities require, with the appropriate training, tools, and support provided.
Roles and responsibilities
Contact Center
Explain product features, benefits, eligibility, claims requirements, and other relevant information to potential and existing customers.
Respond to customer inquiries through phone, WhatsApp, and other approved customer support channels.
Understand and strive to meet or exceed agreed Customer Operations service levels and performance metrics.
Learn and maintain strong knowledge of all relevant Turaco products and partnerships.
Register and update customer information accurately in TACO and other approved systems.
Address customer inquiries relating to products, policies, claims, and customer support within agreed timelines.
Respond efficiently and accurately to customers, provide clear solutions, and ensure customers feel valued.
Follow up on unresolved customer issues and escalate cases that cannot be resolved at first contact.
Maintain accurate notes and records of customer interactions.
Support inbound and outbound customer campaigns as assigned.
Customer Engagement and Outbound Activities
Contact customers for onboarding, education, product awareness, claims follow-up, and other approved Customer Operations campaigns.
Support upsell or cross-sell activities where these form part of an approved customer campaign.
Follow up on initial customer contacts where further action is required.
Use approved scripts while adapting communication appropriately to the customer's needs.
Meet agreed activity, response and completion targets for assigned campaigns.
Support customer surveys, feedback collection and other Voice of Customer activities.
Support IVR and other customer communication campaigns, including follow-up where required.
Claims Administration
Initiate, investigate and process claims reported by customers.
Communicate with customers, next of kin, medical service providers, partners and colleagues to obtain information required to process claims.
Follow up on missing claims documentation and help customers understand what is required.
Review claim information, policy details and supporting documentation in line with approved claims processes.
Support claims assessment and settlement decisions in line with approved guidelines and authority levels.
Keep claims records, notes and statuses accurate and up to date in TACO.
Follow up on aged, pending and stuck claims and escalate blockers promptly.
Support claims verification activities, including customer, provider or document verification where required.
Detect and escalate suspected fraud or unusual claims activity while safeguarding customer dignity.
Ensure claims are handled within agreed turnaround times and Customer
Operations service standards.Operational and Team Support
Support backlog clearance and other priority Customer Operations activities when required.
Work across customer support, claims and other Customer Operations activities based on workload and business priorities.
Support other Turaco markets or teams where additional capacity is required and appropriate training has been provided.
Participate in product launches, customer onboarding activities and operational projects where Customer Operations support is required.
Raise recurring customer, claims, or process issues to the Customer Operations
Lead for resolution.
Follow agreed SOPs, escalation processes, and operating procedures.
Complete assigned actions and operational follow-ups within agreed timelines.
Field and Partner Support
Participate in branch, partner, agent, DSR, Loan Officer or customer field activities as required.
Spend regular, planned time at partner branches and offices, and in the communities where Turaco customers are based.
Train, coach and support partner staff at their own locations on Turaco products, customer handling and claims documentation requirements.
Observe firsthand where claims get stuck or where customers struggle with Turaco processes, and bring those findings back to the Customer Operations Lead so that they can be addressed.
Support product and claims education during approved field engagements.
Assist with customer sensitisation, surveys, customer follow-up and feedback collection during field visits.
Capture and escalate customer, agent and partner feedback identified during field activities.
Support post-launch and refresher activities where required.
Turaco will provide the required approvals, logistics and reasonable resources for assigned field activities.
Quality, Performance and Compliance
Meet agreed Customer Operations performance standards, including service
levels, productivity, claims turnaround time and quality measures.
Maintain accurate customer, claims and operational records.
Participate in QA reviews, coaching, refresher training and product knowledge assessments.
Apply feedback from QA and coaching sessions to improve performance.
Escalate customer, fraud, compliance, legal or operational risks promptly.
Maintain confidentiality and handle customer information in line with Turaco policies and applicable requirements.
Key Performance Measures
Performance will be assessed using relevant Customer Operations measures, which may include:
Customer response and resolution turnaround times.
Inbound call service levels.
WhatsApp service levels.
Claims turnaround time.
Claims processed per associate.
Aged and pending claims.
Quality assurance scores.
Customer satisfaction and feedback.
Accuracy of TACO and customer records.
Completion of assigned campaigns and follow-ups.
Attendance and schedule adherence.
Completion of agreed actions and operational tasks.

Job Summary
The Specialist, Financial Reporting (Actuarial) is responsible for the timely, accurate and compliant execution of actuarial valuations, financial reporting, regulatory reporting and management information for the life insurance business. AIFRS 17 Reporting

Prepare actuarial information required for annual financial statements and external reporting.
Support responses to IFRS 17 audit and stakeholder queries, maintaining complete working papers and evidence.

Perform calculations and analysis supporting valuation of insurance liabilities for group and individual life business.
Review actuarial assumptions and investigate variances in valuation results.
Validate actuarial data, assumptions and valuation outputs and escalate material issues to the Manager, Capital Management and Reporting for review and approval routing.
Monitor actuarial reserves and emerging experience trends and recommend further investigation or action.

Monitor trends affecting product profitability and actuarial assumptions.
Analyse the performance and profitability of existing and newly launched products.
Provide actuarial insight and recommendations to support business decision-making.
Investigate business performance variances and emerging actuarial risks.
Product Development and Pricing Support

Assess the financial implications and sustainability of new product proposals.
Support product reviews to assess continued competitiveness, customer value and profitability.
Assist with user acceptance testing and actuarial validation of products configured in administration and valuation systems.
Monitor product performance and recommend enhancements through the Manager.
Expense Analysis, Budgeting and Forecasting

Provide actuarial projections and analysis for budgeting, forecasting and business planning.
Contribute actuarial input to long-term financial projections and scenario analysis.
Regulatory Reporting and Compliance
Prepare actuarial returns and regulatory submissions required by the Insurance Regulatory Authority and other relevant authorities for review and approval.
Operate in accordance with the Insurance Act, applicable actuarial and financial reporting standards, regulatory requirements and internal policies.
Support implementation of regulatory and reporting changes affecting assigned activities.
Provide information to the external or appointed actuary and internal stakeholders through the Manager.
Support responses to regulatory reviews and information requests.
Data Governance and Quality Assurance
Perform data validation, reconciliation and quality-assurance checks for actuarial reporting.
Investigate and resolve data anomalies affecting calculations and reporting, escalating material or recurring issues.
Maintain evidence of data checks, controls, exceptions and resolution.
Recommend improvements to actuarial data quality, ownership and governance.
Model Governance and Controls
Maintain, test and enhance actuarial models used for valuation, pricing and financial reporting within approved access and change controls.
Comply with model governance standards, documentation requirements and independent review arrangements.
Participate in model testing, validation and controlled implementation of changes.
Identify and escalate model risks, limitations and control weaknesses.
Investment-Linked Fund Administration Support
Review unit pricing calculations and supporting controls in accordance with approved governance processes.
Verify the accuracy and completeness of unit pricing information before submission through the approval process.
Investigate pricing exceptions or discrepancies and document resolution.
Adhere to established mandates, controls and escalation requirements for investment-linked fund administration.
Audit, Risk and Governance
Support internal and external audits relating to actuarial and financial reporting activities.
Implement assigned audit recommendations and corrective actions within agreed timelines.
Identify, assess, document and escalate actuarial, reporting and operational risks.
Maintain documentation supporting actuarial review, audit and regulatory inspection.
Promote adherence to actuarial governance standards, company policies and internal controls.
Collaboration and Continuous Improvement
Work closely with Finance, Risk, Investments, Operations, IT and Data teams to deliver integrated and reliable reporting.
Provide technical guidance to analysts or colleagues where delegated, without assuming formal people-management accountability.
Identify opportunities to automate and simplify reporting while preserving appropriate review and controls.
Maintain current technical knowledge and share relevant learning with the actuarial team.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering or a related quantitative discipline.
Progress toward qualification with a recognised actuarial professional body such as IFoA, ASSA, SOA or equivalent.
Minimum seven actuarial examinations pass or an equivalent level of progress toward professional qualification.
Demonstrated experience in actuarial valuations, financial reporting and experience investigations.
Exposure to regulatory reporting, actuarial governance, modelling and reporting systems.
Experience
Minimum 5 years of relevant actuarial experience in life insurance, financial services or actuarial consulting.

Financial Reporting and IFRS 17
Actuarial Valuation
Experience Investigations
Data Analysis and Interpretation
Product Profitability and Pricing Analysis
Regulatory Reporting
Actuarial Modelling and Scenario Testing
Risk, Governance and Control Awareness
Behaviourial Competencies
Analytical Thinking
Attention to Detail
Commercial Acumen
Problem Solving
Accountability
Stakeholder Management
Planning and Organizing
Effective Communication
Team Collaboration

JOB PURPOSE
We are seeking an experienced Senior Programme Officer to lead the implementation and growth of the Calestous Juma Science Leadership Fellowship (CJF), a flagship leadership development programme that nurtures and empowers accomplished African scientists to become influential leaders capable of shaping science, policy, innovation, and sustainable development across the continent.
The Senior Programme Officer – CJ Fellows will support the implementation and visibility of the Calestous Juma Science Leadership Fellowship (CJF), with primary responsibility for science communication, knowledge dissemination and Fellow visibility. The role will translate complex scientific, leadership and programme content into clear, engaging and accessible communications for diverse audiences, while supporting effective delivery of Fellowship activities.
The role will work closely with Fellows, faculty, programme teams, Science Communications, funding partners and other stakeholders to develop high-quality communication products, strengthen Fellow thought leadership and visibility, document programme outcomes and support communication across the Fellowship lifecycle. It will also contribute to programme coordination, stakeholder engagement, reporting and learning as required.
The position requires strong science communication and storytelling capability, excellent writing and editing skills, an understanding of scientific and research environments, ideally grounded in academic or professional training in a scientific or public health discipline and the ability to work effectively across diverse stakeholders and African contexts.
SFA Foundation is committed to fostering a culture grounded in Respect, Accountability, Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI), and Excellence. We seek individuals who embody these values in their work and interactions.
PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Science Communication Strategy and Planning
Contribute to the development and implementation of communication plans for the CJ Fellowship in alignment with programme and organisational priorities.
Identify key audiences, messages and appropriate communication channels for Fellowship activities, research, leadership outcomes and impact.
Translate scientific, technical and leadership content into clear, accessible and compelling communications for diverse audiences.
Contribute to content calendars, communication workplans and campaign planning for Fellowship activities and milestones.
Provide technical communication input to programme teams and advise on effective approaches to communicating scientific and programme outcomes.
Content Development, Storytelling and Knowledge Products
Develop and coordinate high-quality Fellowship content, including impact stories, profiles, case studies, blogs, articles, briefs, newsletters, presentations and other knowledge products.
Develop compelling stories that demonstrate the achievements, leadership journeys, research contributions and impact of Fellows and alumni.
Support the packaging of programme evidence, learning and results into accessible content for internal and external audiences.
Lead or support editorial processes, ensuring accuracy, clarity, tone and alignment with SFA Foundation standards and approved messaging.
Work with Fellows and faculty to identify and develop opportunities for publications, speaking engagements, thought leadership and other visibility opportunities.
Fellow Visibility, Thought Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement
Support Fellows to strengthen their professional and scientific visibility through appropriate media, speaking, publication and digital opportunities.
Build effective working relationships with Fellows, alumni, faculty, programme teams, grantees, funders, media and other relevant stakeholders.
Coordinate communication engagement with Fellowship partners and contribute to positioning the Fellowship as a platform for African scientific leadership.
Support advocacy, outreach and thought leadership activities that amplify the Fellowship’s contribution to science, policy, innovation and development.
Represent the Fellowship at relevant communication, programme and stakeholder engagements when required.
Digital, Media and Event Communications
Coordinate with Science and Corporate Communications teams to support timely publication of approved Fellowship content across relevant digital platforms.
Support website, social media and other digital content related to Fellowship activities, achievements and milestones.
Support media engagement and identify appropriate opportunities to generate accurate and positive coverage of the Fellowship and its Fellows.
Develop and coordinate pre-, during- and post-event communication materials for workshops, conferences, learning sessions and other Fellowship events.
Coordinate photography, media, social media amplification and other communication logistics for key Fellowship activities.
Programme Coordination, Reporting and Learning
Contribute to planning and implementation of Fellowship activities and workplans, ensuring communication requirements are integrated into programme delivery.
Support preparation of programme, partner and funder reports, including communication, visibility, outcomes and impact sections.
Track communication outputs, reach, engagement and outcomes and provide periodic updates to inform programme learning and decision-making.
Document lessons, success stories and good practices arising from the Fellowship and support knowledge sharing across Fellows, alumni and partners.
Maintain organised records and archives of communication products, media coverage, publications and relevant programme documentation.
Quality Assurance, Capacity Building and Collaboration
Review communication outputs for quality, accuracy, accessibility and consistency with SFA Foundation brand and editorial guidelines.
Provide technical guidance to programme colleagues and relevant partners on science communication and knowledge dissemination.
Share good practice and support learning on effective science communication approaches across the Fellowship and wider Foundation.
Work collaboratively with Communications, Programmes, M&E and other professional services teams to deliver high-quality outputs.
Budget and Operational Support

Support monitoring of communication-related expenditure and deliverables within approved plans and budgets.
Support coordination of external communication vendors and consultants, where required.
PERSON SPECIFICATIONS
Academic Qualifications
A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Science, Public Health, Science Communication, Communications, Journalism or a related discipline from a recognised institution.
A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. Candidates with a science or public health background combined with demonstrated science communication experience are particularly encouraged to apply.

Experience
At least 5 years of progressive experience in science communication, strategic communications, science journalism, research communication or a related field, preferably within science, health, research, innovation or the non-profit sector. Job Title: M-Pesa Africa: Senior Solutions Architect (Digital Platforms)
Job Description:
Key Responsibilities
Super App & Digital Platform Architecture
Own the end-to-end architecture of the M-PESA Super App, including its mini-app platform, SDK, and marketplace ecosystem, across all six markets.
Own the design, versioning, and lifecycle governance of M-PESA's SDKs (mini-app SDK, payment SDKs, and partner/developer-facing SDKs), ensuring consistency, backward compatibility, and developer experience across platforms.
Define and govern the technical standards for mini-app onboarding, integration, security review, and lifecycle management.
Architect the Super App's core and service layer to support scalable, secure, and performant digital experience delivery.
Drive the transition to modern digital platform architectures: composable UI patterns, micro-frontends, headless/BFF (backend-for-frontend) design, and cloud-native deployment aligned to M-PESA's infrastructure strategy.
Digital Platform Governance & Standards
Establish and champion architecture governance frameworks, design review standards, and reference architectures for digital and mobile platforms across all six markets.
Define UX-to-architecture standards, mini-app certification criteria, and release governance, ensuring traceability from partner/developer submission through to production release.
Partner with Compliance, Legal, Risk, and Market teams to ensure digital platform architectures meet local regulatory obligations, data protection, and app store/marketplace requirements.
Digital Payment Channels
Own the architecture of M-PESA's digital payment channels, including QR payments, hosted payment pages, and NFC/Tap-to-Pay, ensuring consistent design standards across the Super App and other consumer touchpoints.
Define channel-level security, tokenisation, and merchant integration standards for QR, hosted payment page, and NFC acceptance flows.
Architect the technical roadmap for emerging and converging payment channels, ensuring interoperability with core wallet, switching, and settlement systems.
Integration & Ecosystem Architecture
Architect integration patterns between the Super App, core M-PESA systems, third-party mini-app developers, and partner platforms.
Collaborate with API gateway and platform engineering teams to define event-driven, API-first exchange patterns aligned with the integration layer strategy.
Design and govern the mini-app SDK, developer portal, and sandbox/testing environments to support a scalable third-party developer ecosystem.
Own the SDK release process: versioning strategy, deprecation policy, and documentation standards; for internal engineering teams and external partner/merchant developers.
Performance, Security & Resilience Enablement
Design digital platform architectures that ensure app performance, offline resilience, and graceful degradation across varied network conditions and device profiles.
Define security architecture for the Super App and mini-app ecosystem, including sandboxing, permission models, and secure inter-mini-app communication.
Partner with the Risk and Security teams to embed fraud prevention and abuse detection into the mini-app onboarding and runtime experience.
Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as the senior digital platforms architecture voice in Architecture Review Boards, design forums, and group-level governance bodies.
Mentor and coach mid-level and junior architects across markets, building digital platform architecture capability within the team.
Produce executive-ready architecture artefacts, including C4/Mermaid diagrams, ADRs, and digital platform strategy presentations for CTO/CIO audiences.
Lead vendor evaluations for mini-app platforms, mobile development frameworks, and digital experience technologies.
Qualifications
Skills & Competencies
Key Technical Competencies
Strong understanding of Super App and mini-app architecture patterns, including hybrid/WebView runtimes, mini-app SDKs, and marketplace/platform governance models.
Extensive experience with mobile and web application architecture, including native, hybrid, and cross-platform frameworks, and cloud platforms on AWS and/or Azure.
Working knowledge of native iOS and Android platform constraints (app lifecycle, distribution/app store requirements, platform-specific security models), sufficient to guide architectural decisions across both ecosystems.
Proven experience designing, versioning, and maintaining SDKs for external developers or partners, including API contract design, backward compatibility, and developer documentation.
Proficiency in integration patterns including REST/GraphQL APIs, event streaming (Apache Kafka), and backend-for-frontend (BFF) design for consumer-facing platforms.
Strong knowledge of digital platform architecture patterns including micro-frontends, composable UI, headless architecture, and offline-first/resilient mobile design.
Experience with digital platform security architecture including app sandboxing, permission models, secure SDK design, mTLS, and OAuth2/OpenID Connect.
Working knowledge of digital payment channel architecture, including QR code standards (EMVCo/static/dynamic), hosted payment page design, and NFC/HCE-based Tap-to-Pay acceptance.
Knowledge of platform documentation and governance practices including ADRs, C4 modelling, developer portal design, and architecture review board processes.
Key Behavioral Competencies
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex digital platform concepts.
Analytical, structured thinker with strong problem-solving ability.
Collaborative and influential across multi-market teams.
Self-driven, accountable, and delivery focused.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related field.
8+ years of experience in solutions/platform architecture, mobile or digital engineering, or closely related technical disciplines, with at least 3 years in a senior or lead capacity.
Proven track record designing enterprise-scale digital or Super App platforms in financial services, fintech, or telecommunications.
Demonstrated ownership of a super app / mini-app platform architecture, including SDK design and third-party mini-app governance, at scale.
Track record owning SDK strategy for external developers or partners, versioning, backward compatibility, and deprecation at enterprise scale.
Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and mobile/web application architecture.
Proficiency in integration patterns: event streaming, API gateway design, and BFF/composable architecture.
Strong understanding of app platform security and governance frameworks (OWASP MASVS, app store/marketplace policies, or equivalent).
Experience with high-availability architecture and performance optimisation for high-traffic consumer-facing platforms.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in mobile money, payment systems, or digital financial services platforms in emerging markets.
Familiarity with mini-app engine technologies (e.g., WeChat Mini Programs, Alipay GMP, or equivalent hybrid mini-app runtimes).
Exposure to AI/ML-driven personalisation, in-app recommendation engines, or conversational/agentic interfaces.
Experience operating across multi-country regulatory environments in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Professional certifications: TOGAF, AWS/Azure Solutions Architect, or equivalent.
Familiarity with developer ecosystem programmes, including partner onboarding, certification, and marketplace monetisation models.

This Senior Data Scientist role is broad – we are looking for someone who can sit at the intersection of data engineering, ecological data science, and technical product ownership. As Senior Data Scientist, you will be responsible for day-to-day data management and the building of automated data processing pipelines and visualizations. You will also be involved in applying discriminative machine learning and ecological modeling approaches to processing and analyzing biodiversity data and designing and building ecological decision support tools within our Natural State Analytics platform.
This role owns data pipeline design, requirements, testing, and validation. Pipeline implementation may be carried out by you, the Technology team, or collaboratively depending on the project. This will include designing dynamic, structured field survey forms (in ODK) and data ingestion pipelines that ensure raw field data are cleaned, processed, and joined correctly to become analysis-ready datasets that can be exported for different end users. Your role will also include analyzing field datasets into decision-support metrics that can be displayed on platform dashboards and be used to generate project reports, under guidance from Project Delivery and Biometrics.
Our Project Delivery and Biometrics teams decide how data collection should be done, what quality checks matter, and what data dashboards need to show. You will turn these requirements into precise, buildable specifications for the Technology team to implement on the platform and then verify what gets built. You will not need to write all the backend code yourself, Natural State's Technology team owns most implementation, but you do need to be comfortable building data pipelines (in SQL) and writing and executing data analysis functions (in Python or similar). Most importantly, you need to understand the Natural State science database and principles deeply enough to specify exactly what should be built, ask the right questions before it's built, independently check the result once its built, and communicate that information clearly to external technical and non-technical audiences.
There is a lot of scope for growth within this role. We envision the first 6-12 months to be heavily focused on creating and improving data management pipelines. Once those systems become less time consuming to maintain, we hope you will bring your imagination and expertise to help us build data tools within the Natural State Analytics platform that inform better decision making and help us achieve our mission of Restoring the Natural World.
This role is for you if...
You have a strong technical background and are wanting to use your skills on real-world, applied biodiversity conservation and restoration projects.
You have ideas about how biodiversity data can be leveraged to make better decisions and you are excited to implement these.
You are detail-oriented and diligent, with a keen understanding of the importance of well-curated data and a passion for creating pipelines to support this.
You thrive in a remote work environment and are able to effectively manage your own workload without needing too much top-down direction.
You enjoy working in a small, high-performance team and pitching in where you’re needed.
Requirements
Must have: 5+ years of work experience and a degree in data science, computer science, statistics, mathematics, quantitative ecology or a related field plus experience working with ecological/biodiversity data (e.g. camera trap images, passive acoustic monitoring recordings, vegetation surveys, animal surveys, species lists, soil carbon, biomass, remote sensing observation, climate etc.).
Must have: Strong Python for scientific data work - pandas or polars for data handling, plus the analysis stack (numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn or equivalent). Comfortable writing validation scripts that catch schema mismatches early and explain clearly what broke.
Must have: Strong statistical reasoning, including an understanding of concepts such as confidence intervals, uncertainty estimation, GLMs, and discriminative machine learning models.
Must have: Confident in SQL, joins, CTEs, window functions.
Must have: Comfortable investigating data issues independently in pgAdmin, DBeaver, or similar.
Strongly desired: Able to handle spatial data in PostGIS, QGIS, and GeoPandas - raster algebra, coordinate reference systems and reprojection, vector versus raster, and the common ways location data breaks.
Strongly desired: Experience working with remote sensing data.
Nice to have: Experience with ODK, KoboToolbox, Survey123, or a comparable field data collection platform (ODK Central admin experience is a plus).

You will work closely with leadership, auditors, tax advisors and lenders to keep the numbers accurate, the filings on time and the business well informed.
