Own the month-end close and group reporting. Oversee close, multi-entity and multi-currency consolidation, and IFRS statutory financial statements across our entities. Review key schedules, journals and reconciliations.
Lead audits, tax and statutory compliance. Coordinate external audits, manage auditors and tax advisors, and ensure timely and accurate tax and statutory filings across the Group.
Own the Group’s tax agenda. Manage direct and indirect taxes (corporate income tax, VAT, withholding and payroll taxes) across jurisdictions, and oversee the Group’s transfer pricing arrangements and intercompany charges.
Manage regulatory and business compliance. Oversee AML, licensing, business permits and other regulatory requirements across the Group, and keep compliance calendars and filings on track.
Run treasury and cash management. Oversee cash flow movements and liquidity management, FX exposure and banking relationships. Collaborate on cash flow forecast.
Drive budgeting and performance analysis. Lead the budget process, track actuals against plan, and give leadership clear insight into performance and outlook.
Own preparation of lender, investor and board reporting. Produce reporting packs, monitor covenant compliance, maintain debt schedules and respond to information requests.
Supervise and further develop a small, experienced accounting, compliance and investor relations teams. Set clear objectives, ownership and accountability across finance processes.
Automate with AI. This role is designed around AI-enabled ways of working — much of Apollo’s reporting, reconciliation and analysis is already automated, and you are expected to run, extend and improve that tooling so a lean team can cover a broad scope.
You might be a fit if you:
Have 7+ years of finance and accounting experience with increasing responsibility over time, including running a month-end close and reporting process
Hold a professional accounting qualification (K-CPA, ACCA, or equivalent)
Have strong experience with consolidation, IFRS statutory accounts and external audits
Have solid direct and indirect tax knowledge (CIT, VAT, WHT) with hands-on KRA/iTax and eTIMS experience; group transfer pricing exposure is a strong plus
Are comfortable across budgets and forecasts — as well as core accounting
Use AI tools in your daily work and are genuinely excited to automate your own job while maintaining a deep understanding of all materials you and your team produce
Are hands-on, organized and strong on follow-through, with the judgement to know what matters
Communicate clearly with senior stakeholders, auditors and lenders
Nice to have:
Experience across multiple jurisdictions or multi-entity groups
Exposure to external investor/lender reporting
Hands-on experience with Xero, Fathom or other cloud finance systems
Experience in fintech, lending, financial services or agriculture

Work in cross-functional teams where finance is expected to be practical, collaborative and close to the business. We operate across multiple countries and value ownership, sound judgment, and people who help solve problems while maintaining the right controls.
Care about outcomes, not ego. We hold ourselves and each other to a high bar, and we all roll up our sleeves to make the work excellent.
Move fast, take smart risks, and build with urgency, because our customers' livelihoods depend on what we deliver.
Listen deeply, debate openly, and collaborate across boundaries, because the best ideas often come from unexpected places.
Offer competitive compensation, meaningful ownership, and the chance to grow on a team that takes your work and your development seriously.

Objectives of the Position
The overall objective of the position is to provide high-level technical and programmatic support to the Ministry of Health and national stakeholders in strengthening tobacco control policies, legislation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation in Kenya.
The officer will contribute to advancing WHO FCTC implementation, strengthening national coordination mechanisms, enhancing surveillance and research, supporting enforcement and compliance efforts, and integrating tobacco control into broader NCD and health promotion strategies. The position will also support reporting to regional and global frameworks and facilitate alignment with global best practices and WHO technical guidance.
Roles and Responsibilities
Under the overall guidance of the WHO Representative and the technical supervision of the Cluster Lead Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control (DPC), the Public Health Officer, Tobacco Control will undertake the following responsibilities:
The officer will provide technical support to the Ministry of Health in reviewing, developing, and implementing tobacco control policies, strategies, and regulations consistent with WHO FCTC provisions and global best practices. This will include supporting regulatory frameworks for smoke-free environments, tobacco advertising bans, packaging and labelling requirements, taxation measures, and regulation of emerging nicotine and tobacco products.
The officer will support national coordination and multi-sectoral engagement, including collaboration with government ministries, civil society organizations, academia, and development partners to strengthen implementation of tobacco control measures.
The officer will contribute to strengthening tobacco surveillance systems, including supporting implementation of population-based surveys, monitoring of tobacco use trends, and analysis of data to inform policy decisions. This includes contributing to national reporting obligations under the WHO FCTC.
Provide technical assistance for operationalization of the Kenya reference laboratory for testing tobacco products.
Support the Ministry of Health in establishment and implementation of quality and integrated tobacco cessation services withing the general health care system in collaboration with multi-stakeholders.
Provide technical support to multi-stakeholders for implementation of alternative livelihoods project in the targeted Counties.
The officer will assist in building national and county-level capacity through development of training materials, organization of workshops, and provision of technical guidance to strengthen enforcement, compliance monitoring, and cessation services integration into primary health care.
The officer will prepare technical briefs, policy notes, donor reports, and strategic documents to support advocacy and resource mobilization. The officer will also contribute to broader NCD prevention initiatives and ensure integration of tobacco control within universal health coverage and primary health care frameworks.
The officer will perform other related duties as assigned by WHO management in line with organizational priorities.
Education Requirements
Essential qualifications:
A Bachelor’s Degree in Public Health, Medicine, Epidemiology, Health Policy, Health Promotion, Global Health, Health Economics, or a related discipline from a recognized university.
Desirable qualifications:
A Master’s Degree in Public Health, Medicine, Epidemiology, Health Policy, Health Promotion, Global Health, Health Economics, or a related discipline from a recognized university.
Training in tobacco control, noncommunicable disease prevention, public policy analysis, health law, or implementation science. A postgraduate qualification with demonstrated research or policy experience in NCDs or tobacco control is an added advantage.
Work Experience
Essential;
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible professional experience in public health, including at least three years of demonstrated experience in tobacco control, noncommunicable disease prevention, health policy, or public health programme management.
Demonstrated experience in policy analysis, programme planning and implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and coordination of public health interventions.
Demonstrated experience in working with government institutions including National and County and/or other relevant stakeholders in the implementation of public health programmes.
Desirable
;
Professional experience working with United Nations agencies, international organizations, development partners, or other multilateral institutions.
Experience in legislative and policy processes, multi-sectoral coordination, and the development of technical guidance, policy briefs, reports, and other normative documents.
Experience in public health surveillance, including the use of digital surveillance tools and electronic health information systems.
Experience in data analysis, research coordination, and evidence generation to inform public health policy and programming.
Familiarity with Kenya’s devolved health system and county-level governance structures would be an advantage.
Experience supporting tobacco control policy implementation and coordination at national and/or subnational levels would be an added advantage.
Language Requirements
Expert knowledge of English is essential, with demonstrated ability to draft technical documents, policy briefs, and reports.
Working knowledge of Kiswahili is desirable to facilitate effective engagement with national and subnational stakeholders.
IT Knowledge
The incumbent must demonstrate proficiency in standard office software applications including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Advanced skills in data analysis and visualization using tools such as Excel advanced functions, STATA, SPSS, Power BI, or similar software are desirable.
Familiarity with virtual collaboration platforms, digital reporting tools, and online data management systems is required.
Remuneration
The position will be recruited under WHO’s Special Service Agreement (SSA) category, subject to applicable WHO Staff Rules and Regulations.
Remuneration will align with the WHO salary scale for Kenya, commensurate with qualifications and years of relevant experience.

Job Title: Senior Manager, Supply Chain Digitalization Benchmarking and Pilots
Job Description:
Job Overview/Summary
The TWG's work is organized around four results: a multi-stakeholder governance framework (Result 1), a common data standards and shared taxonomy (Result 2), a data-sharing and interoperability blueprint (Result 3), and a mapping of complementary initiatives already underway across the sector (Result 4). In the second half of the project, Results 1, 2, and 3 each move from design into live testing through a dedicated pilot: a governance pilot, a data standards pilot, and an interoperability pilot.
The Program Officer will lead the benchmarking work that underpins the data standards pilot and will support the design and delivery of all three pilots - governance, data standards, and interoperability -helping translate research and sector mapping into practical input for how each is built. This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role spanning three of the TWG's four workstreams, for someone who wants to help a sector-wide coalition move from agreement in principle to evidence in practice.
The position is funded through the HLGSC Digitalization TWG action (DG ECHO-funded), through project close in December 2027. The Program Officer, Supply Chain Digitalization Benchmarking and Pilots works closely with data.org, the TWG's facilitation partner, and reports to the Deputy Director for Business Development and Program Delivery within IRC's Global Supply Chain team.
Major Responsibilities
Benchmarking (Result 2)
Lead benchmarking with the 3 TWG member organizations assessing their data systems against the TWG's agreed minimum viable data standards.
Consolidate benchmarking results into a clear, decision-ready evidence base that directly informs the Result 2 data standards pilot.
Pilot design, delivery & documentation (Results 1–3)
Support the design and launch of three pilots: a governance pilot (testing the endorsed governance framework, including rotating co-chair and decision procedures), a data standards pilot (testing the agreed taxonomy across benchmarked organizations), and an interoperability pilot (testing data-sharing and anonymization protocols across organizations at varying levels of digital maturity).
Document each pilot as it unfolds, capturing lessons learned to support real-time, adaptive management.
Author the pilot completion reports, prepared in a format agreed in advance with DG ECHO.
Support identification of pilot opportunities under Result 3, working directly with participating organizations.
Research translation (Result 4)
Translate findings from the Result 4 mapping report into concrete design inputs for the Results 1–3 pilots.
Coordination & reporting
Participate in TWG meetings and relevant sub-group sessions.
Provide regular progress updates to TWG co-leads.
Help prepare materials for co-leads meetings and, where relevant, the HLGSC Coordination Board.
Job Requirements
Education
Bachelor's degree required in Supply Chain, Project Management, Data Science, International Development or related field required; Master's degree is an advantage.
Work Experience
3-6 years' experience in humanitarian supply chain, program monitoring and evaluation, or data systems work required, including direct responsibilities in pilot design or the testing of new operational mechanisms.
Demonstrated Skills and Competencies
Required:
Strong project management skills, with the ability to keep multiple concurrent workstreams on track and within scope.
Comfort working with data standards, benchmarking frameworks, or data governance concepts.
Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to translate research and technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for a non-technical audience.
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple organizations and stakeholder groups.
Fluency in English required; French or Arabic language skills is an advantage.
Desirable:
Prior experience with data standards frameworks such as GS1 or UNSPSC.
Experience working with multi-stakeholder coalitions, working groups, or coordination bodies.

The role ensures regulatory, conduct and financial crime requirements are translated into consistently executed operational processes supported by effective supervision, quality management, timely escalation and reliable management information. Working closely with Level 2 Compliance, Business, Operations and Technology, the role drives control effectiveness, service-level performance, system and scenario effectiveness, remediation delivery and sustainable compliance outcomes while preserving clear accountability between execution and independent oversight.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the Level 1 Compliance function and establish clear operating standards, accountabilities, service levels, quality thresholds and escalation protocols across all units.
Oversee transaction monitoring and financial crime surveillance, including automated and manual alert review, investigation, disposition, suspicious activity referral, escalation of Suspicious Transaction Reports to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and completion of post-investigation actions.
Oversee real-time and T+1 name screening, transaction and payment screening, sanctions investigations, periodic and ongoing screening, and timely escalation of potential sanctions matches and control failures.
Ensure effective governance of financial crime systems and scenarios, including data-quality monitoring, scenario performance reviews, tuning support, change implementation, user requirements and timely resolution of operational defects.
Lead Customer Due Diligence and Enhanced Due Diligence advisory, including high-risk and complex onboarding, politically exposed persons and sensitive clients, beneficial ownership, passport screening and verification, high-risk customer reviews and specialized due diligence.
Oversee correspondent banking and partnership due diligence, requests for information, questionnaires, risk assessments, ongoing reviews and escalation of material concerns.
Lead Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act and Common Reporting Standard processes, data remediation, operational controls and reporting support.
Oversee execution of Regulatory Compliance and Anti-Bribery and Corruption controls, including gifts and entertainment, hiring practices, sponsorships and donations, manual payments, third-party assessments and other assigned conduct controls.
Oversee customer, product, channel, geography, third-party, sanctions, conduct and compliance risk assessments, ensuring consistent methodology, complete evidence, clear ownership and timely treatment of identified risks.
Ensure implementation, monitoring and enforcement of Compliance and Financial Crime Compliance policies, standards and procedures within Level 1 operations, with prompt escalation of breaches, exceptions and control failures.
Promote an evidence-based compliance culture focused on demonstrable control effectiveness, timely action, customer protection, strong documentation and audit readiness.
Own the Risk and Control Self-Assessment for Level 1 compliance controls and maintain accurate risk, control, issue and action records supported by current evidence.
Provide practical compliance and financial crime advisory to Business and support functions, while seeking Level 2 interpretation or challenge where matters are material, novel or outside approved guidance.
Drive timely execution of remediation programmes arising from regulatory inspections, compliance testing, internal audit, quality assurance, system reviews and management-identified control weaknesses.
Establish robust quality management through supervisory reviews, operational quality checks, root-cause analysis, coaching and recurring-error prevention.
Develop accurate and forward-looking management information, operational dashboards and key risk indicators covering volumes, ageing, backlogs, productivity, quality, breaches, emerging risks, capacity and remediation status.
Ensure material risks, significant backlogs, service-level breaches, suspicious activity, sanctions concerns and control failures are escalated promptly to the Head of Compliance and relevant Level 2 owners.
Lead implementation of regulatory change, procedure updates, new controls, system enhancements and training requirements within Level 1 operations.
Coordinate with Technology, Operations, Data, Business and other stakeholders to improve automation, data quality, workflow efficiency and sustainable control performance.
Lead workforce planning, succession, capability development, performance management and deployment of staff across Level 1 units, ensuring adequate capacity for risk and workload demand.
Qualifications
Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in Law, Business, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, Information Systems or a related field.

The position combines strategic commercial leadership, category expertise, sales management, marketing strategy, and operational execution to strengthen the organization's position within the edible oils and fats market.

Commercial & Category Leadership
Develop and implement the commercial strategy for the Edible Oils & Fats category in line with overall business growth and profitability objectives.
Own the category P&L, driving performance across pricing, product mix, margins, and volume.
Lead business planning and forecast alignment with Production, Supply Chain, Finance, and other key functions.
Identify opportunities for category growth through core portfolio optimization, innovation, value-added products, and premium segments.
Monitor market trends, competitor activity, consumer behavior, and category dynamics to inform commercial decisions.
Sales & Route-to-Market Excellence
Lead national sales teams and regional sales heads to achieve revenue, distribution, volume, and profitability targets.
Develop and optimize route-to-market strategies to strengthen market coverage, product availability, and cost efficiency.
Drive sales execution through clear KPIs, performance dashboards, structured business reviews, and accountability mechanisms.
Build and manage strategic distributor relationships, ensuring strong performance, profitability, and sustainable partnerships.
Identify opportunities to improve sales productivity and channel effectiveness.

Lead integrated marketing and communication strategies to strengthen brand awareness, consumer relevance, and market positioning.
Work closely with R&D and cross-functional teams to identify and develop new product and category growth opportunities.
Strengthen consumer trust and brand differentiation through effective positioning, communication, and innovation.
Ensure marketing investments are aligned with commercial priorities and measurable business outcomes.
Trade Marketing & Channel Development
Lead trade marketing strategies and programs to strengthen brand visibility, distribution, and in-store execution.
Develop channel-specific activation strategies across General Trade, Modern Trade, and other relevant channels.
Optimize promotions, pricing, and pack architecture to maximize commercial returns.
Partner with Finance and Sales Operations to monitor trade spend, promotional effectiveness, and ROI.
Strengthen execution standards and visibility across key customer and distribution channels.
Digital & Data Enablement
Champion the adoption and effective use of BI tools, CRM systems, and digital dashboards to improve commercial decision-making.
Leverage data analytics to inform pricing, promotions, customer segmentation, distribution, and sales strategies.
Use market and consumer data to identify emerging opportunities and risks.
Explore e-commerce and digital trade opportunities to complement traditional routes to market.

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing commercial team with clear objectives and performance standards.
Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, and continuous improvement.

Job Purpose:
The core responsibility of an auditor within Absa is to execute audit assignments in accordance with the Group Audit Plan and relevant policies, procedures and quality standards.

Audit Delivery and Issue Assurance
Develop an in- depth knowledge of the methodology, by attending training sessions and using knowledge gained during audits, use this proactively in executing audit activities.

Develop and maintain relationships with key audit contacts on each audit by attending continuous stakeholder meetings. In addition, engage closely with stakeholders during
assignments and encourage open discussion and interaction with business on the risks associated in their environment.
Engage proactively with Internal Audit colleagues during assignments and request technical assistance where required. Technical assistance may be requested for the review of the risks and controls to be tested, audit working papers and audit report.

Support the Senior Audit Manager in the identification of risks to be tested by participating in planning sessions.

Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of controls and document all working papers in Audit Bond for review by the Senior Audit Manager.
Ensure all audit observations and planned actions are factually agreed with management as soon as they arise and increase the speed of report issuance. Provide suggestions to stakeholder management on how they can address the control issues identified.
Document all working papers in line with methodology requirements. The working papers must be accurate, reflective of work performed and support conclusions drawn.
Display professional skepticism, raising and discussing contentious observations with management and provide evidence to support all issues identified.
On an ongoing basis throughout the audit, discuss and agree the factual accuracy of audit observations with the Senior Audit Manager and Chief Audit Executive.

Job Title: Senior Officer, Corporate and Business Partnerships
Job Description:
Position Summary
The African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) is an Africa-based conservation organization protecting wildlife and their habitats as essential to a modern and prosperous Africa. We articulate a unique vision of African-led conservation, focusing on solutions that create opportunity for people — not at the expense of wildlife and their habitats, but because of them.
The goal of AWF’s work with business is to shape strategic relationships that align with AWF’s mission and vision and that support AWF’s work from a programmatic and financial perspective.
The Senior Officer, Corporate and Business Partnerships will report to the Senior Manager, Corporate and Business Partnerships, and work with colleagues in the Institutional Partnerships Team to build and maintain relationships with corporate and business partners.
In partnership with other teams, the incumbent will lead the full fundraising cycle for assigned portfolio of corporate prospects/partners, including prospect research, outreach, relationship cultivation, proposal development, negotiation, contracting support, stewardship, renewal, and scale-up. The Senior Officer will be responsible for meeting fundraising targets. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing organization at a critical time for conservation on the African continent.
Key Responsibilities
New Business Development (35%)
Build, qualify, and manage a robust pipeline of prospective corporate and strategic business partners whose ESG and CSR commitments, sustainability practices, and business models align with AWF’s priorities.
Prepare thoughtful partnership strategies aligned with organizational income targets and strategic priorities.
Identify opportunities for partnerships and calls for proposals.
Secure new revenue streams, including through corporate grants, cause-related marketing, event sponsorship, matched funding, gifts in kind, and strategic alliances, to grow overall support from corporate and business partnerships from $1m to $3 million/year by 2030.
Proposal and Content Development (15%)
Develop and deliver briefings, presentations, and customized collateral for prospective partners.
Prepare Opportunities Review documents for Senior Management, complying with AWF’s Account Management Framework.
Work with Technical, Program, Design, and Finance teams to identify fundable projects, budgets, results frameworks, and evidence of impact.
Interface with Senior Management, Design Team, and assigned partners to support the development of tailored partnership concepts, proposals, sponsorship packages, and funding concepts.
Partnership Management and Stewardship (25%)
Coordinate internal award management processes, including organizing the project’s kickoff meeting and representing the partner’s interests in account management committees.
Manage a portfolio of assigned corporate and business partners, serving as the liaison between partners and AWF program teams to ensure strategic alignment, mutual value, timely communication and engagement, and the prompt delivery of acknowledgments and stewardship materials.
Develop stewardship plans that demonstrate impact, strengthen engagement, and maximize partnership retention and growth.
Review partner reports and coordinate with field staff and the Finance Team to ensure accurate and timely technical and financial reporting, ensuring quality control and compliance with partner and AWF requirements and quality standards.
Support the preparation and negotiation of grant amendments, no-cost extensions, budget revisions, scope changes, and other agreement modifications, ensuring approvals are obtained before implementation.
Coordinate partner site visits, field trips, and impact reporting to demonstrate conservation outcomes.
Work with Program and Finance Teams to ensure closeout requirements are completed, including final reports, reconciliations, documentation archiving, and lessons learned.
Data Management and Internal Reporting (10%)
Maintain accurate prospect, contact, opportunity, and revenue records in AWF’s CRM (Raiser’s Edge) and content management and file-sharing platform (Box).
Track partnership performance, deliverables, and revenue targets.
Prepare regular reports on fundraising progress and partnership impact on assigned portfolios for internal leadership.
Collaborate with the Research Team to undertake due diligence assessments using dedicated databases such as RepRisk to inform the suitability of prospects and prevent reputational damage to AWF, complying with AWF’s Corporate Giving Policy.
Representation and Networking (5%)
Maintain a schedule of industry conferences, business forums, and other events to be considered for networking purposes.
Represent AWF at corporate forums, sustainability events, and industry meetings to enhance visibility and partnership opportunities.
Build relationships with relevant networks, including CSR platforms, business councils, and sustainability alliances.
Internal Collaboration, Administrative and Other Responsibilities (10%)
Schedule and coordinate internal and external meetings involving stakeholders in different time zones, including agenda preparation, minute-taking, and follow-up on action items.
Coordinate with the Communications Team on partner visibility, campaigns, brand use, media opportunities, and public announcements.
Participate in team and cross-team meetings.
Manage logistics for corporate partner engagements, including travel arrangements, event planning, and hospitality coordination.
Provide general administrative support to the Corporate & Business Partnerships team, including filing and data cleaning.
Key Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or higher in environmental studies, international development, business, marketing, communications, finance, or a related field desirable.
Minimum of 3 years relevant experience in corporate fundraising, business development, partnership management, or sponsorship sales, preferably within an NGO or conservation context.
Demonstrated ability to cultivate and manage corporate relationships and contribute to fundraising targets.
Good understanding of business trends relating to AWF’s core agenda of nature and people to inform partnership strategies.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including proposal writing and presentation delivery.
Demonstrated strength in organizational and project management skills, with an appetite for action and results. Must be a natural self-starter, self-disciplined, with excellent time management skills.
Collegial, collaborative team player with exceptional interpersonal and networking skills, with a demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships. Ability to work in a multicultural environment with diverse stakeholders.
Proficiency with standard apps (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and office equipment. Familiarity with Raisers Edge or other CRM software a plus. Comfortable and nimble in learning new systems, processes, and protocols.
Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
Intellectual curiosity to remain up-to-date on industry trends.
Global or regional experience in conservation, international development, or related field strongly preferred. Keen interest or experience in Africa’s wildlife, land, and people.
Experience working with multinational and African-based corporations is highly desirable.

Job Description:
What this role actually is
This is a hands-on, high-ownership position. You will be the finance lead for a standalone entity — the person responsible for the monthly management reporting pack, the CFO-level executive commentary, the IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss model, the lender and treasury compliance, and the unit economics that inform commercial decisions across multiple OEM brands.
You'll manage the end-to-end monthly close: accruals, prepayments, intercompany, depreciation, FX. You'll produce the variance analysis that isolates brand-mix effects from one-off items. You'll monitor the loan book, analyse repayment behaviour by cohort, and own provisioning and bad debt trends. You'll lead lender reporting and covenant compliance, manage drawdown documentation, and support due diligence processes.
And then — because this is Mobility — you'll also be a commercial partner. You'll sit alongside the commercial team to interrogate OEM economics, model new product launches, assess new supply agreements, and build the financial cases for board presentations and grant proposals.
This is not a role where the strategy happens upstairs and the finance team keeps score. You'll shape both.
What makes it different
Most finance roles at this level have inherited structures, established processes, and reporting cadences that largely run themselves. This one doesn't. The tools, the workbooks, the ways of working — these are yours to design. You'll identify automation opportunities, build controls from scratch, and ensure IFRS compliance in areas where judgement genuinely matters: IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, revenue recognition, IFRS 18 readiness.
You'll also have direct exposure to development finance and climate finance — two fast-growing fields where M-KOPA's electric mobility business sits at an increasingly interesting intersection. Lender relationships here aren't purely commercial. They span impact investors, development finance institutions, and climate finance structures. That's a professional education you can't buy.
What you bring
Qualified Chartered Accountant (CPA(K), ACCA, CA or equivalent), with a demonstrable track record in finance management or a senior finance role, including hands-on ownership of statutory and management reporting cycles.
Deep, applied IFRS knowledge — particularly IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IAS 21, and revenue recognition — and proven ability to manage audit processes end-to-end, from file preparation to auditor queries.
Exceptional financial modelling and communication skills: you can build a complex multi-scenario model in Excel and present its conclusions clearly to a CFO or a lender in the same week.
Big 4 training (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) is a strong advantage. Working knowledge of the East African electric mobility sector is a plus, though not required — curiosity and commercial instincts matter more.
The reality check
This role will ask a lot of you. The entity is scaling fast, the reporting obligations are real, and the lender relationships require precision. There will be months where the close feels tight and the audit feels relentless. You'll be operating across strategic and operational levels simultaneously — and some days the most important thing on your plate will be debugging an ECL model, not presenting to the board.
If that sounds manageable, it probably is. If it sounds energising — you're probably the right person.

Maintain a professional, respectful and compassionate approach when interacting with patients and their families, ensuring confidentiality and privacy of patient information throughout the diagnostic process.

Experience working in a hospital, specialist clinic or multidisciplinary healthcare environment will be an added advantage.
SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES
Strong technical knowledge of neurological and neurophysiological investigations.
Demonstrated competence in EEG procedures and operation of relevant diagnostic equipment.
Good understanding of patient preparation, safety and infection prevention requirements.
Ability to accurately acquire, record and maintain diagnostic information and patient records.
Good troubleshooting and equipment-handling skills.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to interact professionally with patients and clinical teams.
High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with neurologists and other healthcare professionals.
Strong commitment to patient confidentiality, safety and professional ethics.
Calm, compassionate and professional when dealing with patients, including those requiring specialised neurological care.

Job Description:
What this role is
This is an early-career product role for someone with 2 to 4 years of experience who wants to become a product manager and has the raw material for it. You will join our product team, work alongside our senior product owners, and take ownership of a slice of one of our product areas from your first quarter.
Most of what we build is internal: the tools our buyers, warehouse staff, pickers, riders, finance and customer service team use every day, and the customer app and website they all feed into.
Our engineering is in-house and so is our product thinking.
What you will work on
You will be assigned to one of our product teams and given real problems inside it.
Depending on where the need is, that could be:
Inventory & Waste. Receiving, put-away, transfers between sites, counting, expiry and waste. Keeping what the system says we have in line with what is on the shelf. The apps used by people on their feet in a cold room, and the printers, scanners and scales behind them.
Last Mile Delivery. Picking, packing, dispatch, routing, delivery slots, the rider app and proof of delivery. Getting the right order to the right door at the right time, and knowing straight away when we have not.
Commercial Excellence. How much we buy, of what, and when. Product master data, pricing, promotions, supplier terms and margin. The tools our buying team uses to run their categories and to see whether a decision made money.
Scale & Compliance. The back-office processes that carry volume: order to cash, procure to pay, finance close, controls and audit trails. Assets, facilities and quality, including temperature records and food safety. Making each process cheaper per transaction and less dependent on one person knowing how it works.
Customer Value. The app and website, search, checkout, substitutions and retention. How we tell a customer what actually happened to their order, and what brings them back for the next one.
In every one of these you will do the same things: understand the workflow as it really happens, find the structural problem behind the recurring symptom, write it up so an engineer can build it, ship it, and check whether it moved the number.
How you will work
You report to a product owner and work day to day with your engineering squad. You will not be alone, but you will be expected to own your problems rather than be handed solutions.
You spend real time where the work happens: the receiving bay, the pick aisle, the rider hub, the customer service desk. Every process here is judged on the floor, and the best specs come from having watched the thing go wrong.
You write. Short, clear problem statements and specs that an engineer can build from and an operations lead can challenge. If it cannot be explained on one page, it is not understood yet.
You prioritise a backlog and you can say why the thing at the top is at the top.
You use AI tools to prototype small internal tools and analyze yourself. Turn data into insight into action quickly, without waiting for a full engineering cycle every time.
You make sure the team actually uses what you build. If they do not, it is on you to figure out why.
What we are looking for
2 to 4 years of experience in a demanding role. Many of the people who fit this description are developers who have found they care more about whether the right thing gets built than about building it themselves. Others come from operations, data or analytics, consulting, or a start-up where you wore several hats.
Technically literate. You can read SQL, sketch a data model, follow an engineering discussion and have an opinion on the trade-offs.
You have already been the person who fixed something nobody asked you to fix. A report people came to rely on, a script that removed a manual step, a process you rewrote because the old one kept breaking. We want to hear about it.
You know how a product team is meant to work. Problem discovery, solution discovery, then delivery, in that order (Marty Cagan, Inspired). You do not need to have run it end to end yet, but you should recognise the difference between a team that ships features it was handed and a team that finds the problem, tests a few ways to solve it, and only then builds. If you have not read the book, read it before the interview.
Curious about why. When a number looks wrong, your instinct is to go and find out, rather than correct it and move on.
Comfortable with people who are not like you. A warehouse supervisor, a rider and a backend engineer will all need to trust you, and none of them are impressed by the same things.
Commercially aware. You do not need to have owned a P&L, but you should be able to connect a feature to margin, availability, working capital or customer retention, and be curious when you cannot.
Decisive with incomplete information. You would rather ship a decent fix this month and correct it than wait for certainty.
Low ego. You listen, you ask good questions, and you are willing to be on the floor at 6am when that is where the answer is.
What makes people succeed in this job
They accept being judged on outcomes. A developer is judged on what they built. A product manager is judged on whether it was the right thing and whether anyone uses it. Some people find that shift liberating and some find it uncomfortable. The first group does well here.
They distrust stated requirements. What a user asks for is a clue. The good ones watch the work, ask the second and third question, and often end up building something smaller and more useful than what was requested.
They write clearly because they think clearly. Short documents with the problem, the evidence, the proposed change and the number it should move.
They say no, and explain it. A backlog with no noes in it is a wish list. Prioritisation is the actual job.
They close the loop. They go back after shipping to see whether it worked, and they say so plainly when it did not.
They stay close to the floor after they have stopped needing to. The ones who drift into meetings and dashboards lose the feel for the work within a quarter.
If you are a developer thinking about this
This is a real option for the right engineer, and we want to be straight about what changes. You will write far more than you code. You will spend hours with people who do not care how elegant a solution is, only whether it works on a wet floor at 6am. You will hand your best ideas to other engineers to build, and you will be measured on what they ship. In return you get to decide what gets built, which is the part most engineers wanted all along.
What success looks like after a year
You own a product area, or a substantial part of one, end to end, and the operations team treats you as the person to call when something in it is not working.
You have shipped several things that are used by choice, because they are faster than the workaround.
You can point to at least one number you were accountable for and show what you did to move it.
Do not apply if
You want the plan handed to you. You will get support and a senior product owner to learn from, but nobody is going to write your backlog for you.
You want to keep being a developer with a different title. You will prototype, but the production code will be written by your squad.
You think product management is about managing people. You will have no direct reports and a great deal of influence, and you will need to earn all of it.
You would rather be thorough than moving. We will take a decent fix shipped this month over a perfect one next quarter. You will often decide with about 70% of the information and correct the course later.

Job Description:
Job Summary
We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own product strategy and execution for financial technology products end to end: discovery, spec, delivery, launch, and the metric that follows. You will work across the product lines we operate today and the ones we stand up next, and you will partner with senior leadership on where the next bet goes.
This is not a traditional product role. We operate in an AI-native environment. The team uses Claude Code, Claude Design, Codex, and similar tools to spec, prototype, and ship. The Senior PM is expected to write product and technical specifications that AI agents can execute against, drive delivery end to end, ship small PRs directly when it is faster than handing off, coordinate the stakeholders that turn a product into a business, and own the outcomes those products generate. The bar is moving 10x faster without sacrificing quality.
Responsibilities
The role spans two domains.
Own the roadmap across your product lines, which may include credit and lending, savings and deposits, payments and foreign exchange, and new products in development.
Run customer discovery directly with target segments, from individual borrowers and savers to SMEs, business operators, and freelancers.
Size opportunities, instrument funnels, and validate hypotheses against production data. You do not wait for an analyst.
Make prioritisation calls across very different product lines (a credit policy tweak vs. a new payments corridor vs. a deposit campaign) and defend them with numbers.
Track competitor moves in the markets you operate in and translate them into product decisions.
Execution and Delivery
Write product and technical specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can implement directly. Tight, unambiguous, testable.
Prototype in Claude Design to validate concepts before committing engineering time.
Code and ship small PRs yourself with Claude Code when it is faster than handing off. PMs here live in the codebase.
Drive delivery end to end. Own scope, timeline, and quality.
Run delivery in Linear, our product and project management surface.
Run the cadence with Engineering: standups, sprint reviews, unblocking, bug triage, and trade-off calls when things slip.
Coordinate across stakeholders: leadership, Engineering, Data, Credit, Operations, Risk, Compliance, and Marketing.
Align scope, ship dates, and trade-offs across teams that have different incentives.
Own outcomes, not output. Tie every initiative to a revenue, growth, or risk metric. Track it post-launch and iterate until the metric moves.
Review AI-generated implementations, prototypes, and analyses for correctness, edge cases, and business fit.
Build feedback loops: customer signal, spec, AI-assisted build, metric, next spec. Compress the cycle.
Own launch comms and internal enablement.
Qualifications and Experience
5+ years in product management.
Direct experience shipping consumer or SME products in fintech, banking, lending, or payments.
Track record of owning outcomes. You measure yourself by the metric that moved (revenue, active users, default rate, deposit growth), not by what was planned or shipped.
Strong stakeholder coordination. You drive alignment across the cross-functional set above without losing your own thread.
Strong written communication. You can write a spec a senior engineer does not need to ask questions about.
Comfortable reading production data yourself. SQL fluency, or willing to get there in week one.
Demonstrated proficiency with AI tools in your daily workflow (Claude Code, Claude Design, Codex, and similar). You have shipped real work with them, not just experimented.
Comfortable reading and writing code, enough to ship a small PR with Claude Code.
High agency. You move from problem to validated solution to shipped product without waiting to be told.
Able to read financial regulatory guidance in the markets you operate in and translate it into product requirements.
Highly Preferred
Experience with credit products (origination, scoring, collections) and deposit products (rate strategy, treasury, funding).
Exposure to foreign exchange, cross-border payments, stablecoins, or virtual account infrastructure.
Experience working with engineering teams that use AI coding agents in production workflows.
Prior work in emerging markets, particularly Africa, SEA, or LATAM fintech.
Bonus
Founder or 0 to 1 product experience.
Familiarity with trade finance instruments (invoice factoring, LPO financing, purchase order financing).

Company Details:
WHO WE ARE
Rafiki wa Maendeleo Trust is a charitable organization working in the rural area of Rarieda sub-County in Siaya County, Kenya. Our vision is people believing in themselves and working together to build a vibrant and progressive community. Our mission is to empower communities and build t...read moreheir capacities to create positive change for children and youth within their community. Our values guide our mission:
We promote sustainable environmental and socio-economic development to enhance future well being.
We encourage creativity and innovation for continuous adaptation, learning and growth.
We believe participatory approaches ensure communities own their development.
We advocate for human rights to promote dignity, diversity and respect.
We encourage accountability and transparency to assure integrity and credibility.

HOW WE STARTED
Rafiki started as a community development founded by the Director Michele Ostertag and her two friends, Monica and Solomon Ochieng. Touched by the hardships faced by children and villagers, the founding friends began with health treatment and education to the villagers. During the first two years, it became increasingly clear that given the socio-economic hardships of the area, one could not focus on treatment of diseases alone.

In September 2003, the initiative was registered as a Community Based organization (CBO) called Lusi Community Orphans Project. The CBO emphasized self-help through income generating initiatives such as chicken and dairy farming, beekeeping and crafts. The profits from these ventures were used to support up to 83 orphaned children with breakfast, school uniforms and weekend psycho-social activities. 

In 2006 the group decided that a stronger organizational structure and a more robust legal framework was required in order to grow the project into a professional organization. The Lusi Community Orphans Project was therefore reconstituted into Rafiki wa Maendeleo Trust (RWMT), which officially began operating in June 2006.

Job Description
Job Purpose:
The role is accountable for driving sustainable revenue growth, active customer penetration, and lifetime value across Retail and Business Banking by:
Owning the end-to-end transactional banking franchise (Payments, Branch-led transactions & FX-led transactions).
Leading Customer Value Management (CVM) strategy across acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and monetization.
Translating customer behavior and data into commercial outcomes, while ensuring regulatory, risk, and operational resilience.
The role combines P&L ownership, customer lifecycle leadership, and data-driven execution to scale active customers and transaction intensity.
Key Accountabilities
Transactional Banking Strategy & P&L Ownership (20%)
Own and deliver the transactional banking revenue and profitability targets, including Account services, Payments (domestic, cross-border, & Value-Added Services), Cash management & Transaction-led FX
Define and execute a multi-year transactional banking growth strategy aligned to Retail & Business Banking objectives.
Drive transactional primacy by positioning the bank as the customer’s main operating account.
Continuously optimize product economics, margins, and cost-to-serve.
Own the strategic partnerships agenda for Transactional Banking and CVM, with clear accountability for value creation, revenue impact, and customer adoption.
Own transactional bundles, pricing tiers, and related value propositions.
Align transactional propositions to customer life-stage, business maturity, and usage behavior.
Ensure transactional propositions integrate seamlessly with lending, savings, insurance, and investment.
Customer Value Management (CVM) Leadership (15%)
Own the CVM framework across the full customer lifecycle: Acquisition, Onboarding & activation, Usage growth, Retention & reactivation, and Value deepening
Define and manage Key Value Drivers (KVDs) such as: Net Active Customers, Digital Actives, Transaction frequency & value, Product holding, Dormancy and churn
Design and govern Always-On CVM programmes, event-based triggers, and segment-specific plays.
Ensure CVM execution is measurable, prioritized, and commercially justified.
Lead customer segmentation across Retail and Business Banking (e.g. mass, affluent, SMEs), leveraging advanced analytics to segment the customer base and predict behaviors, preferences, and needs.
Design and manage cross-segment loyalty programs that increase customer retention and incentivize repeat engagement.
Optimize customer onboarding, activation, and retention through tailored engagement strategies.
Increase cross-product holdings and product usage over time through lifecycle management.
Implement churn management programs to retain customers and win back lost clients.
Drive long-term relationships by offering proactive solutions that fit customer needs.
Data, Analytics & Insights (10%)
Champion a data-led operating model for transactional banking and CVM, leveraging targeted campaigns to increase product penetration and maximize customer lifetime value.
Work with Data & Analytics teams to:
Define standardized CVM metrics and dashboards
Enable near-real-time performance tracking
Translate insights into targeted actions
Use behavioral data to inform: Pricing, Campaign design, Channels optimization, Fraud and risk mitigation decisions (in partnership with Risk)
Use data-driven insights to identify cross-sell and upsell opportunities across the customer base.
Work with the Product Data to gather actionable insights to inform decision-making.
Continuously monitor customer feedback, behavior, and trends to refine the overall customer engagement approach.
Use retention data to proactively engage at-risk customers and prevent churn.
Provide regular reports on customer metrics and engagement outcomes to segment heads, product owners and management teams.
Digital & Channel Enablement (15%)
Drive growth of digital transactional journeys (app, online, USSD).
Increase self-service adoption while reducing manual and branch-dependent processes.
Partner with Technology and Operations too:
Modernize transactional platforms
Improve reliability, uptime, and scalability
Support straight-through processing where feasible
Continuously innovate to enhance digital product offerings based on customer feedback and evolving needs.
Collaborate with IT and digital teams to improve user interfaces and remove friction points in digital banking.
Track and drive adoption rates for digital products, ensuring key performance indicators (KPIs) are met.
Ensure that digital onboarding is seamless, efficient, and customer centric.
Pricing, Commercialization & Revenue Assurance (20%)
Own transactional pricing strategy, discount frameworks, and commercial guardrails.
Ensure pricing is, Competitive, Risk-adjusted, Margin-protective
Govern revenue leakage management, fee integrity, and pricing compliance.
Lead commercial approvals for transactional deals within delegated authority.
Use data to drive personalized offers and customer engagement strategies that maximize value generation and customer retention.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize payment, platform, fintech, ecosystem, and enterprise partners that accelerate, Transaction volume and velocity, Customer acquisition and activation and new use-cases across retail and business segments
Risk, Compliance & Operational Resilience (10%)
Ensure all transactional and CVM activities comply with:
Central bank prudential guidelines
AML/CFT and financial crime controls
Data protection and consumer protection regulations
Partner with Risk, Compliance, and Fraud teams to, balance growth with control and introduce intelligent controls within the transactional banking & customer value management domains.
Accountable for operational resilience of transactional services, including incident response and remediation.
Continuously assesses improvements for related processes and procedures relating to transactional banking and CVM.
Owns the internal risk management and compliance activities to manage open risks, known management issues and audit findings.
Stakeholder & People Leadership (10%)
Set clear performance goals for team members and ensure accountability for results.
Act as a single point of accountability for transactional banking and CVM strategy execution across:
Distribution (Branches, RMs, Workplace Banking)
Marketing
Technology & Operations
Finance
Risk & Compliance
Build and lead a high-performance team with strong commercial, analytical, and execution capability.
Embed a culture of commercial discipline, customer centricity, and data-driven decision making.
Facilitate training and development for team members to enhance skills and ensure continuous improvement.
Foster a collaborative and innovative environment to encourage customer-focused strategies for the transactional banking and CVM function.
Preferred Qualification
Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, Economics, or related field
Postgraduate qualification (MBA or equivalent) preferred
Preferred Experience
5 to 10 years’ experience in transactional banking, payments, or retail/business banking.
Proven P&L ownership and delivery in a complex banking environment.
Demonstrated leadership in CVM, analytics-driven growth, or customer lifecycle management.
Strong understanding of payments, cash management, and transaction-led FX.
Experience working with regulators and managing risk-intensive products.
Knowledge and Skills
Knowledge and skills for the role include, expert-level understanding of transactional banking (payments, cash management, digital channels and transaction-led FX) and Customer Value Management (end-to-end lifecycle design, KVDs, triggers, and always-on execution), supported by strong P&L ownership, pricing and commercial structuring, and the ability to originate and govern strategic partnerships and commercial initiatives that deliver measurable revenue and customer outcomes.
The role requires advanced capability in applying data and analytics to decision-making, together with sound regulatory, risk, and operational resilience understanding.
Behaviorally, the role demands senior leadership presence, commercial drive, stakeholder influence, customer-centric judgement, accountability, and the ability to lead change at pace.
Cognitively, it requires strategic and systems thinking, strong analytical reasoning, and high-quality decision-making with disciplined commercial judgement in complex, regulated environments.

Lead client engagement initiatives, reviews, and retention strategies to strengthen long-term partnerships.

Job Description:
INTRODUCTION TO THE ROLE
The Communications Manager at Girls Not Brides plays a crucial role turning organisational priorities and communications vision into coordinated, impactful, and audience-focused communications delivery.
The Communications Manager ensures that communications operates as an integrated function, connecting strategic direction with day-to-day implementation across media, editorial, digital and storytelling. The role will provide leadership across communications planning, messaging, and quality assurance, ensuring outputs are consistent, impactful, and aligned with Girls Not Brides’ strategic objectives.
Working closely with the Head of Communications and colleagues across the organisation, the Communications Manager will ensure communications approaches support organisational influence, fundraising, partnership development and engagement with priority audiences.
ABOUT YOU
We are seeking an experienced communications professional who combines strategic thinking with strong operational leadership. You will enjoy translating organisational priorities into practical communications approaches and bringing together different teams, perspectives and disciplines to achieve shared objectives.
You will have excellent judgement, strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and consistency. You will be confident working across teams, building trusted relationships, and supporting colleagues to use communications effectively to achieve goals. You will be a collaborative and supportive manager who is committed to developing others and creating a positive, accountable and high-performing team culture.
You will share Girls Not Brides’ values and demonstrate a commitment to ethical, inclusive and audience-focused communications.
Salary range
Market competitive based on a detailed survey by the Birches Group of comparable national NGO salaries in selected location. Payments will be made in local currency of where it is located.
Contract
This is a fixed-term contract for 2 years
The successful candidate must have the right to work in Kenya at the time of applying, and for the full duration of the two-year initial contract
KEY RESPONSIBILTIES
Communications strategy operationalisation and delivery leadership
Translate organisational strategy, influencing priorities, and audience needs into integrated communications approaches for priority engagements, and moments.
Support the Head of Communications to turn strategic priorities into coordinated approaches and delivery across the Communications Team.
Lead collaborative and impactful communications planning for organisational priorities, publications, events and influencing moments, bringing together the right communications expertise, channels and products to achieve the intended outcomes.
Coordinate delivery across the communications functions, overseeing workflows, timelines, dependencies and priorities to ensure communications activity is integrated, strategically aligned and delivered to a high quality.
Provide coordination and oversight across strategic communications and corporate communications workstreams, ensuring alignment, identifying dependencies and risks, and ensuring high-quality delivery.
Strengthen communications processes, workflows and ways of working to improve team effectiveness and responsiveness.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with colleagues and external partners, supporting the operational delivery of strategic communications partnerships and initiatives.
Support the Head of Communications to identify and prioritise opportunities to strengthen Girls Not Brides’ profile and external positioning, ensuring these opportunities are appropriately translated into coordinated team activity.
Messaging, quality and consistency
Develop and maintain messaging and narrative approaches, with the Head of Communications, ensuring they are applied consistently across communications.
Ensure communications outputs are accurate, consistent, high-quality, audience-focused and aligned with organisational positioning and priorities.
Provide editorial and brand oversight, review and sign-off across written, creative, and storytelling outputs, ensuring quality, consistency and alignment with organisational positioning and visual brand identity.
Support colleagues across the organisation to communicate effectively with external target audiences.
Work with the Head of Communications to strengthen organisational narratives and ensure key messages are reflected across communications channels and products.
Communications Team management, integration, and organisational support
Manage, support and develop line-reports, providing clear direction, prioritisation, feedback and support for effective workload management and performance.
Foster effective collaboration across communications disciplines, ensuring expertise is connected, duplication is minimized, and the team operates as an integrated function.
Coordinate strategic communications, media, editorial, digital and multimedia expertise to ensure specialist inputs contribute to integrated communications approaches.
Work with internal teams to understand organisational, national and influencing priorities, identifying communications opportunities, and ensuring communications is is built into key initiatives from the outset.
Work collaboratively as part of cross-functional project teams, partnering with colleagues to develop communications plans, approaches and outputs that support organisational objectives, engage priority audiences and contribute to outcomes.
Oversee communications monitoring and evaluation using performance and audience insights to strengthen future planning and delivery.
Contribute to other communications activities as required.
Wider Organisational Responsibilities
Support copywriting, proofreading and translation of communications outputs across our core languages as required
Commit to the mission and vision of Girls Not Brides, putting these at the forefront of all planning, work and actions.
Uphold the core values of Girls Not Brides in all areas of work and interactions with colleagues, members, partners, and other stakeholders.
Comply with Girls Not Brides’ policies and processes, including for safeguarding, diversity and inclusion, the code of conduct and data protection.
Ensure that internal databases and monitoring information are kept fully up-to-date.
Commit to ongoing personal development and learning.
Fulfil any other reasonable requests for the advancement of Girls Not Brides.
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
Essential
Significant professional experience in communications, strategic communications, advocacy communications, public affairs or related roles in the not-for-profit sector, an international/intergovernmental organisation, a social movement, or social enterprise.
Strong ability to translate organisational and influencing priorities into clear communications approaches, plans and activity that achieve defined audience outcomes.
A proven track record of developing and delivering successful integrated, multi-channel communications approaches that effectively engage and influence target audiences.
Experience coordinating complex communications projects or campaigns, managing multiple priorities, deadlines, dependencies and stakeholders.
Significant professional experience managing, developing and coordinating teams, including providing direction, feedback, mentorship and support, delegating effectively, and fostering a collaborative, inclusive and high-performing team culture across remote-working, cross-cultural and international environments.
Experience working across communications disciplines, bringing together editorial, digital, media, multimedia or other specialist expertise to deliver integrated communications.
Strong organisational, project management and coordination skills, with the ability to work independently, identify risks and dependencies, solve problems, manage workflows, manage competing priorities, and coordinate people and projects to deliver shared objectives.
Strong leadership, interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work collaboratively as part of a team, build trusted working relationships across an organisation, and effectively liaise with colleagues and stakeholders to translate priorities into coordinated action.
Strong editorial judgement and writing skills, with experience reviewing and quality-assuring communications across different formats and channels.
Ability to prioritise effectively and manage multiple competing deadlines.
A strong commitment to the mission and values of Girls Not Brides.
Desirable
Experience working within thematic areas of child marriage, girls’ education, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), and related fields.
Proficiency in additional languages, especially French and Spanish.
Experience supporting organisational influencing or fundraising objectives.
Experience managing communications transformation or change processes.
Company Details: Girls Not Brides was initiated in September 2011 by The Elders, a group of independent global leaders working together for peace and human rights, as part of their efforts to more attention to the harmful practices that hold girls and women back, and to encourage and empower others to work to cre...read moreate a world without child marriage. Girls Not Brides became an independent charity in 2013. Archbishop Desmond Tutu, Mrs Graca Machel and Sonita Alizadeh are Girls Not Brides Global Champions and advocates to end child marriage.Girls Not Brides is a global partnership of more than 1300 civil society organisations from over 100 countries committed to ending child marriage and enabling girls to fulfill their potential. Members are based throughout Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and the Americas. We share the conviction that every girl has the right to lead the life that she chooses and that, by ending child marriage, we can achieve a safer, healthier and more prosperous future for all. Stronger together, Girls Not Brides members bring child marriage to global attention, build an understanding of what it will take to end child marriage and call for the laws, policies, and programmes that will make a difference in the lives of millions of girls.

Job Description:
Your opportunity
The role of an FSE (Field Service Engineer) Manager offers a unique opportunity to lead, develop, and inspire a team of highly skilled engineers while driving operational excellence
Your Mission
First Point of Escalation: Serve as the primary point of contact for FSEs in case of any issues or challenges that arise on-site during interventions.
Intervention Preparation: Collaborate with the requester and the FSE to ensure all aspects of the intervention are well-prepared, including technical requirements, timing, and resource allocation.
Support to Planning Team: Provide the planning team with a list of FSEs suitable for specific interventions based on skillsets and availability.
Communicate Key Messages & Company Strategy: Act as a conduit for key messages and company strategies, ensuring that FSEs understand and align with the overall organizational goals.
Salary and Compensation Review: Conduct reviews of salary and compensation packages to ensure they are competitive and in line with company policy.
APA (Annual Performance Assessment): Set and monitor KPIs for FSEs, including conducting mid-year and end-of-year performance reviews to track progress and development.
In Case of Accident on Site: Lead the Root Cause Analysis (RCA) of any accidents occurring on-site, in collaboration with the HSE team, to identify preventive measures and ensure safety standards are upheld.
Leave Management: Oversee and manage FSE leave requests, ensuring that they align with workload demands and avoid operational disruptions.
Expenses Approval: Check and approve FSE expenses, addressing any discrepancies or deviations in collaboration with the finance team.
Post-Intervention Report Review: Review intervention reports to ensure completeness and accuracy of the data provided, addressing any gaps with the FSE.
Training Standards & Multi-Skill Development: Ensure that FSEs are continuously developing their skills, including multiskilling, to meet changing operational needs.
HSE Training Compliance: Ensure all FSEs are up to date with required Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) training and certifications.
Provide Necessary Tools / PPE & Monitor with Finance: Ensure that all necessary tools and PPE are provided to FSEs for their interventions and collaborate with the finance team to monitor and manage the associated costs.
Recruitment: Lead recruitment efforts to identify and onboard new FSEs, ensuring they meet the technical and cultural requirements of the company.
Feedback Collection & Action: Gather feedback from FSEs after interventions, addressing any concerns or issues raised to improve processes and working conditions.
Collaboration with Competence and Development Manager: Work closely with the Competence and Development.
Manager to ensure that FSEs are properly qualified and have the necessary skills for interventions.
Ensure FSE Occupation: Monitor the workload and ensure the optimal occupation of FSEs to meet business needs and individual career growth.
Your Profile
This role requires strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills to maintain the efficient functioning of the FSE team and ensure alignment with company objectives.
Technical knowledge on beverage is a must.

Job Description:
What makes this different
Most Senior Manager, Communications roles at this level sit above the work — reviewing, approving, delegating.
This one doesn't.
You'll draft the media pitch yourself. You'll sit with a Country MD and work through group positioning. You'll counsel senior stakeholders on how to navigate a sensitive issue. You'll work alongside marketing to make sure campaigns, brand and corporate reputation are telling the same story. You'll partner directly with People/HR on a sensitive change narrative.
You'll also build relationships with the people who matter beyond the organisation — from media and partners to government stakeholders and regulators across the markets in which we operate.
And when something goes wrong, you'll be one of the people in the room figuring out what happens next.
Because reputation doesn't stop at the press release. It lives in the decisions a business makes, the way leaders communicate, the relationships it builds and how it responds when circumstances get complicated.
And in the same week, you might chase a purchase order and reconcile a budget line, because there's no one else to hand that to.
It's a rare mix of strategic counsel, integrated communications, reputation management and genuine hands-on ownership — and because M-KOPA doesn't have dedicated in-market communications teams, you'll be the connective tissue holding Group positioning and market execution together across the region.
What you'll need to bring
A communications career, not just communications exposure. You've built your expertise in corporate communications, integrated communications or a similarly broad communications environment, and understand how media, reputation, brand, internal communications and stakeholder engagement connect.
Strong strategic instincts. You can take a business objective, understand what matters to different audiences and turn it into a communications strategy that leaders can actually use. You're as comfortable giving counsel as you are executing the work yourself.
Deep experience in reputation and issues management. You've operated in situations where the stakes are high and judgement matters. You understand that protecting reputation isn't simply about controlling a message — it's about understanding the business, anticipating risk and knowing how to communicate when there isn't an obvious answer.
Crisis communications experience that goes beyond a playbook. You've had to think clearly under pressure, advise leaders, coordinate stakeholders and communicate externally when the circumstances weren't neatly packaged. You know that a crisis rarely arrives in the format you prepared for.
Multi-market experience, ideally across Africa. You've managed reputation and communications across different geographies, cultures, regulatory environments and stakeholder landscapes. You understand that what works in one market may not work in another — and can balance local relevance with a consistent Group narrative.
Stakeholder confidence. You'll work with Country MDs, senior executives, government stakeholders, regulators, media and other external partners. You need to be able to build trust quickly, navigate different agendas and provide clear counsel — particularly when the answer isn't straightforward.
Strength across external and internal communications. External communications will be a significant part of the role, but you'll also need to understand employee communications, leadership messaging, organisational change and culture — and how the two worlds influence each other.
Excellent writing. You can turn complexity into clarity. You know when a message needs precision, when it needs personality and when it needs both. Whether you're writing a press statement, executive briefing, leadership speech, crisis response or employee communication, the quality of your thinking should come through in the quality of your writing.
Experience in complex, fast-moving environments. You may have worked in a fintech, technology business, high-growth company, agency or another matrixed organisation. What matters is that you've learned to operate across functions, influence without always having direct authority and get up to speed quickly when the context changes.
Comfort operating lean. You don't need a large team around you to get things done. You know when to bring in an agency or specialist, when to solve the problem yourself and how to keep momentum without unnecessary layers.
Operational ownership. Agencies, suppliers and budgets aren't someone else's problem. You're comfortable taking work from strategy through to execution — including procurement, POs, spend tracking and the finance administration that keeps the function moving.
