Company Details: Ol Pejeta is the largest black rhino sanctuary in east Africa, and home to three of the world’s last remaining northern white rhino. It is the only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, in a Sanctuary established to rehabilitate animals rescued from the black market. It has some of the highest...read morepredator densities in Kenya, and still manages a very successful livestock programme. Ol Pejeta also seeks to support the people living around its borders, to ensure wildlife conservation translates to better education, healthcare and infrastructure for the next generation of wildlife guardians. In 2004, the ranch was purchased by the U.K.-based conservation organisation, Fauna &Flora International (FFI), with the financial backing of the Arcus Foundation, a private international philanthropic organisation founded by Jon Stryker. The land purchase was wholly funded by a $15 million donation from the Arcus Foundation, which worked in tandem with FFI and the Lewa Wildlife Conservancy to secure the 90,000 acres of open Savannah grassland and convert it to a national land trust. The conservation of the natural habitat, located in Kenya’s Laikipia Plateau, ensured the protection of existing rhino, elephant, and other wildlife populations in addition to captive chimpanzees living in a 300-acre sanctuary. The Arcus Foundation also gave $12 million to fund capital and institutional development costs at the conservancy. That initial injection of funding allowed Ol Pejeta Conservancy to fulfill its business model as a Kenyan-owned operation benefiting local community development and economic growth in addition to its impact on conservation. Today, the Arcus Foundation continues to support the conservancy through its membership on the Board of Trustees and the funding of various initiatives. In 2014, Ol Pejeta achieved IUCN Green List status, one of only two conservancies in Africa to be awarded this. IUCN Green Listing aims to define excellence in managing valuable natural areas. We have also been awarded the TripAdvisor Certificate of Excellence three years running - a testament to the incredible experiences treasured by all who visit Ol Pejeta. In 2015, we published our 2020 Management Plan - which was developed by our staff in consultation with a range of stakeholders, and sets out our vision for the years leading up to 2020, outlining the major projects that will help us to deliver our vision. We want to become an innovative and sustainable model that conserves biodiversity (particularly endangered species) and contributes to economic growth and the improvement of the livelihoods of rural communities.

Job Title: Head of Engineering, POS Application Platform
Job Description:
What you'll get to do
Own the technical strategy and architecture for the POS Application Platform, acting as the domain CTO for everything that runs on our POS devices.
Build and govern the four core platform pillars across the organisation: developer experience (tools, libraries, SDKs), platform reliability (observability, uptime, quality standards), foundational frameworks (architecture, coding standards, testing and release pipelines), and squad adoption (driving uptake of platform tooling across all embedded POS engineers).
Define and enforce engineering standards across all POS device types and OEM manufacturers, ensuring architectural consistency and quality across a heterogeneous device fleet.
Functionally lead POS engineers embedded across Payments, Onboarding, VAS, Savings, and Loans squads - setting the bar for engineering quality and providing the platform layer above all of them.
Own POS observability end-to-end: monitoring, alerting, and incident response frameworks that ensure platform health across all devices and squads.
Drive the architecture for how Moniepoint supports multiple POS device types, including defining how new devices are onboarded, governed, and integrated with the platform.
Collaborate with OEM partners and the POS hardware team when new device types are introduced, ensuring the application layer is ready to support them from day one.
Build and scale the POS platform team, including hiring, mentoring, and structuring for growth as the platform expands internationally.
Translate platform decisions into business impact, working closely with Product, Payments, and Business leadership across markets.
Establish and continuously improve engineering processes, tooling standards, CI/CD pipelines, and developer productivity metrics across the POS engineering community.
To succeed in this role, we think you should have
A minimum of 10 years of hands-on software engineering experience, with at least 6 years leading engineering teams through meaningful growth phases, ideally in multi-national or large VC-backed companies.
Direct, hands-on experience building software that runs on Point-of-Sale terminal devices. This means engineering on the device itself — the application layer — not server-side integrations with POS systems. This is a non-negotiable requirement and candidates without it will not be considered.
Strong working knowledge of EMV standards (Europay, Mastercard, Visa) and experience navigating payment certification processes such as PCI DSS and P2PE. Candidates without this will not be considered.
Deep Android engineering expertise in Kotlin and Java. The POS application layer at Moniepoint is Android-based and there are no exceptions to this requirement.
Proven experience building internal engineering platforms, shared libraries, developer tooling, or foundational frameworks used by other engineering teams — not just consumer-facing feature products.
Experience governing or architecting across multiple POS device types from different hardware manufacturers, with an understanding of how OEM integrations and device management work at scale.
Experience building or maturing platform engineering functions, including establishing engineering processes, tooling strategies, and cross-squad governance structures.
Demonstrated ability to scale engineering teams and build the organisational layer beneath you — leaders who can grow into and around the role you are hiring into.
Experience at a company processing high volumes of financial transactions in a regulated environment. Fintech background is strongly preferred.
Familiarity with terminal management systems and device observability tooling is a strong advantage.
Backend engineering experience in Java or Spring Boot is a strong plus given the breadth of the platform and the integration surface it sits on.
Experience working directly with OEM vendors on hardware specification and integration is a bonus.
Exposure to C or C++ is a plus — one of our device variants uses C.
Experience at Series A or B stage startups alone is unlikely to reflect the scale and complexity required for this role.
Cultural Alignment
We assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation.
Customer Obsession: Deep empathy for the people depending on the platform — whether that is a merchant in Lagos trying to accept a payment, or a POS engineer blocked by missing tooling. You solve problems quickly and intuitively. You close loops by fixing root causes, not just tickets.
Craft: You have mastered your domain at the fundamentals level. You make trade-offs explicit, reason from first principles, and consistently produce solutions that are better than typical.
Systemisation: You convert recurring decisions into repeatable mechanisms. You reduce cognitive load for others. You strengthen institutional memory and improve engineering quality at scale.
Urgency: You move with disciplined speed. You act without waiting for permission when you are within scope. You escalate early when risk exceeds your authority. You remove friction and close loops.
Ownership: You treat the platform as yours to solve regardless of job description boundaries. You take responsibility without being asked. You follow through on commitments without being reminded.
No Ego: You put the mission ahead of personal status. You credit others genuinely, welcome challenge, and never protect your position at the expense of collective outcomes.
Candour: You surface reality early, clearly, and completely — especially when it is uncomfortable. You name risks before they become crises. Intelligent failure is acceptable; concealment is not.
Integrity: Truthfulness and ethical consistency in everything. You adhere to rules and obligations. You never perform under intimidation or corrosive behaviour. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.
Some of the technologies you'll work with
Android (Kotlin, Java) - primary platform for all POS application development
EMV payment standards and PCI/P2PE certification frameworks
Multiple POS device types and OEM manufacturers, including Topwise and Telpo
Terminal management systems and device observability tooling
Java, Spring Boot — backend services and integration layer
Docker and Kubernetes
PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, Elasticsearch
Microservices architecture on AWS

Supporting branches in packaging credit proposals to ensure clarity for faster approval and adoption.

Confirming borrower’s credit worthiness as presented by Relationship managers

Confirming suitability of collateral offered.
Ensuring credit risks and breaches are identified & mitigation measures proposed.

The role is responsible for efficiently handling high-volume and complex cash and non-cash financial transactions while ensuring strict compliance, zero cash differences, and superior customer service. Responsibilities and Accountabilities;
Customer Satisfaction
Maintain high and unparalleled customer service standards at the branch through timely and accurate processing of routine and complex customer transactions according to laid-down SLAs and documented procedures.
Promptly resolve customer inquiries and handle initial escalations of front-line complaints before referring complex matters to the Customer Service Manager (CSM).
Provide guidance to junior tellers on efficient queue management and professional handling of demanding customer interaction
Operational Efficiency and Escalation Support

Drive cross-selling initiatives by identifying client needs and generating qualified leads/referrals for deposit accounts, loan products, foreign exchange (FX), and digital banking channels (e.g., B-Mobile, Internet Banking).

Job Description:
Job Purpose:
To design and document technology solution architectures that meet business requirements, comply with the Bank’s Enterprise Architecture standards, and deliver secure, scalable, and cost-effective outcomes. The Solution Architect works closely with project managers, business analysts, QA teams, and integration engineers to translate business and functional requirements into well-defined architectural designs, ensuring that all solutions are fit for purpose and aligned to the Bank’s technology roadmap.
Key Responsibilities:
Solution Design & Documentation
Design and document end-to-end solution architectures for assigned ICT projects and technology changes.
Produce High-Level Design (HLD) and Low-Level Design (LLD) documents, architecture decision records, data flow diagrams, and integration specifications.
Evaluate alternative solution options and recommend the most appropriate architecture based on business needs, cost, and risk.
Ensure all solution designs are reviewed and approved by the Solution Architecture Lead before submission.
Maintain architecture artefacts throughout the project lifecycle and update documentation post-implementation.
Enterprise Architecture Alignment
Ensure all designed solutions comply with the Bank’s Enterprise Architecture framework, standards, and guidelines.
Identify and flag deviations from EA standards to the Solution Architecture Lead.
Contribute to the maintenance and evolution of the architecture repository.
Apply established reference architectures and design patterns in solution design work.
Project & Stakeholder Engagement
Engage with Business Analysts to understand and translate business requirements into technical architectures.
Collaborate with System Integrators, developers, and QA teams to ensure architecture designs are accurately implemented.
Participate in project meetings, technical design reviews, and architecture workshops.
Provide technical guidance to development and integration teams throughout the build phase.
Prepare and present solution architecture designs to the Solution Architecture Lead and project governance forums
Security & Compliance
Incorporate security controls, data protection requirements, and compliance considerations into all solution designs.
Coordinate with the Information Security team to conduct architecture security reviews for assigned solutions.
Ensure designed solutions comply with CBK technology regulations and the Bank’s ICT policies.
Change Impact Assessment & Continuous Improvement
Assess the architectural impact of proposed technology changes and provide input for Change Approval Board submissions.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of architecture standards, templates, and methodologies.
Stay current on emerging technologies, architecture patterns, and industry trends relevant to banking.
Participate in team knowledge-sharing and professional development activities
Academic & Professional Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field (required).
TOGAF Foundation certification is an added advantage.
Cloud architecture certification (AWS, Azure, or GCP – Associate or Professional level) is an added advantage.
ITIL Foundation certification is an added advantage.
Experience Requirements
Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in solution architecture, systems design, or software development.
Demonstrated experience in designing technology solutions for banking or financial services environments.
Experience in integration design and API architecture.
Exposure to cloud architecture and hybrid deployments.
Experience producing architecture documentation (HLDs, LLDs, architecture diagrams).

Job Purpose
:
To design, develop, implement, and maintain system integration solutions that enable seamless interoperability between the banking applications, digital channels, third-party systems, and external platforms. The System Integration Officer applies technical expertise in integration technologies, APIs, and middleware platforms to deliver reliable, secure, and high-performing integration solutions, supporting the Bank’s operational efficiency and digital banking objectives.
Key Responsibilities:
Integration
Development & Implementation
Design, develop, and implement integration solutions using the Bank’s integration platforms (ESB, SOA, REST APIs, and Microservices).
Build and configure API connections, message routing, data transformation, and orchestration workflows on assigned integration projects.
Develop and maintain integration specifications, API contracts, and technical documentation for all assigned integrations.
Participate in technical design reviews and ensure integration solutions comply with Enterprise Architecture standards.
Implement integrations in line with the Bank’s CI/CD pipeline and version control standards.
Conduct unit testing of integration components before handover to QA for formal testing.

Provide Level 2 support for integration-related incidents, diagnosing and resolving failures within agreed SLAs.

Contribute to DR planning and testing for critical integration systems.
Continuous Improvement & Innovation

Contribute to automation of integration deployment and monitoring tasks.
Participate in team knowledge-sharing and professional development activities

ITIL Foundation certification is an added advantage.
Experience Requirements
Minimum 2–4 years’ experience in system integration, API development, or middleware development.
Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing integration solutions using ESB, SOA, or API platforms.
Experience in REST and SOAP API development and management.
Experience in integration testing and defect resolution.
Working experience in a banking or financial services environment is an added advantage.

Job Title: Senior Officer, Corporate and Business Partnerships
Job Description:
Position Summary
The African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) is an Africa-based conservation organization protecting wildlife and their habitats as essential to a modern and prosperous Africa. We articulate a unique vision of African-led conservation, focusing on solutions that create opportunity for people — not at the expense of wildlife and their habitats, but because of them.
The goal of AWF’s work with business is to shape strategic relationships that align with AWF’s mission and vision and that support AWF’s work from a programmatic and financial perspective.
The Senior Officer, Corporate and Business Partnerships will report to the Senior Manager, Corporate and Business Partnerships, and work with colleagues in the Institutional Partnerships Team to build and maintain relationships with corporate and business partners.
In partnership with other teams, the incumbent will lead the full fundraising cycle for assigned portfolio of corporate prospects/partners, including prospect research, outreach, relationship cultivation, proposal development, negotiation, contracting support, stewardship, renewal, and scale-up. The Senior Officer will be responsible for meeting fundraising targets. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing organization at a critical time for conservation on the African continent.
Key Responsibilities
New Business Development (35%)
Build, qualify, and manage a robust pipeline of prospective corporate and strategic business partners whose ESG and CSR commitments, sustainability practices, and business models align with AWF’s priorities.
Prepare thoughtful partnership strategies aligned with organizational income targets and strategic priorities.
Identify opportunities for partnerships and calls for proposals.
Secure new revenue streams, including through corporate grants, cause-related marketing, event sponsorship, matched funding, gifts in kind, and strategic alliances, to grow overall support from corporate and business partnerships from $1m to $3 million/year by 2030.
Proposal and Content Development (15%)
Develop and deliver briefings, presentations, and customized collateral for prospective partners.
Prepare Opportunities Review documents for Senior Management, complying with AWF’s Account Management Framework.
Work with Technical, Program, Design, and Finance teams to identify fundable projects, budgets, results frameworks, and evidence of impact.
Interface with Senior Management, Design Team, and assigned partners to support the development of tailored partnership concepts, proposals, sponsorship packages, and funding concepts.
Partnership Management and Stewardship (25%)
Coordinate internal award management processes, including organizing the project’s kickoff meeting and representing the partner’s interests in account management committees.
Manage a portfolio of assigned corporate and business partners, serving as the liaison between partners and AWF program teams to ensure strategic alignment, mutual value, timely communication and engagement, and the prompt delivery of acknowledgments and stewardship materials.
Develop stewardship plans that demonstrate impact, strengthen engagement, and maximize partnership retention and growth.
Review partner reports and coordinate with field staff and the Finance Team to ensure accurate and timely technical and financial reporting, ensuring quality control and compliance with partner and AWF requirements and quality standards.
Support the preparation and negotiation of grant amendments, no-cost extensions, budget revisions, scope changes, and other agreement modifications, ensuring approvals are obtained before implementation.
Coordinate partner site visits, field trips, and impact reporting to demonstrate conservation outcomes.
Work with Program and Finance Teams to ensure closeout requirements are completed, including final reports, reconciliations, documentation archiving, and lessons learned.
Data Management and Internal Reporting (10%)
Maintain accurate prospect, contact, opportunity, and revenue records in AWF’s CRM (Raiser’s Edge) and content management and file-sharing platform (Box).
Track partnership performance, deliverables, and revenue targets.
Prepare regular reports on fundraising progress and partnership impact on assigned portfolios for internal leadership.
Collaborate with the Research Team to undertake due diligence assessments using dedicated databases such as RepRisk to inform the suitability of prospects and prevent reputational damage to AWF, complying with AWF’s Corporate Giving Policy.
Representation and Networking (5%)
Maintain a schedule of industry conferences, business forums, and other events to be considered for networking purposes.
Represent AWF at corporate forums, sustainability events, and industry meetings to enhance visibility and partnership opportunities.
Build relationships with relevant networks, including CSR platforms, business councils, and sustainability alliances.
Internal Collaboration, Administrative and Other Responsibilities (10%)
Schedule and coordinate internal and external meetings involving stakeholders in different time zones, including agenda preparation, minute-taking, and follow-up on action items.
Coordinate with the Communications Team on partner visibility, campaigns, brand use, media opportunities, and public announcements.
Participate in team and cross-team meetings.
Manage logistics for corporate partner engagements, including travel arrangements, event planning, and hospitality coordination.
Provide general administrative support to the Corporate & Business Partnerships team, including filing and data cleaning.
Key Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or higher in environmental studies, international development, business, marketing, communications, finance, or a related field desirable.
Minimum of 3 years relevant experience in corporate fundraising, business development, partnership management, or sponsorship sales, preferably within an NGO or conservation context.
Demonstrated ability to cultivate and manage corporate relationships and contribute to fundraising targets.
Good understanding of business trends relating to AWF’s core agenda of nature and people to inform partnership strategies.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including proposal writing and presentation delivery.
Demonstrated strength in organizational and project management skills, with an appetite for action and results. Must be a natural self-starter, self-disciplined, with excellent time management skills.
Collegial, collaborative team player with exceptional interpersonal and networking skills, with a demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships. Ability to work in a multicultural environment with diverse stakeholders.
Proficiency with standard apps (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and office equipment. Familiarity with Raisers Edge or other CRM software a plus. Comfortable and nimble in learning new systems, processes, and protocols.
Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
Intellectual curiosity to remain up-to-date on industry trends.
Global or regional experience in conservation, international development, or related field strongly preferred. Keen interest or experience in Africa’s wildlife, land, and people.
Experience working with multinational and African-based corporations is highly desirable.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
As a member of the Global DREF Team and in alignment with DREF Procedures, the Regional DREF Delegate will support all DREF-related processes and support in the Africa Region. The role will support timely, compliant, and well-coordinated processing, documentation, and reporting of DREF requests, while providing expert technical and compliance analysis and guidance throughout the DREF cycle.
Acting as a technical focal point on DREF to African National Societies, IFRC delegations, and regional staff, the role supports criteria-compliant submissions, contributes to the eligibility review of requests, and provides technical support on the appropriate and strategic use of DREF funds—ensuring operational relevance and alignment with procedures. In addition to compliance, the DREF Delegate support the technical review and quality assurance of DREF operations in the region, ensuring performance is aligned with IFRC KPIs, risk thresholds, and strategic frameworks. From that oversight position, the DREF Delegate provides ongoing analysis and technical support to inform operational decision-making in Delegations, the Regional Office, and National Societies across the full DREF cycle, including proactive monitoring and escalation of compliance or performance issues as needed.
The DREF Delegate supports the Africa DCC team in operations coordination, contributing to the oversight of operational quality beyond the compliance role. A key responsibility is to support the implementation of the regional DREF capacity strengthening plan, supporting African National Societies (ANSs), IFRC staff, and Partner National Societies (PNSs) through training, coaching, tools development, and knowledge sharing. Finally, the role contributes to strategic learning by generating and consolidating evidence, insights, and lessons from DREF operations, to inform continuous improvement of the mechanism globally and regionally.
Job Duties and Responsibilities
Technical
Enable Quality, Timely and Compliant DREF Operations
Monitor the Risk Watch and provide timely and tailored guidance to National Societies, Country Cluster Delegations, Country Delegations Offices and the Regional Office on the timeliness and appropriate use of DREF modalities; preparation of DREF allocation requests, including support to operationalise contingency planning and readiness of at-risk National Societies through access to DREF funds for anticipatory actions.
Provide technical guidance and support on the use of DREF grants, include under Emergency Appeals (EAs), ensuring compliance with DREF procedures. Advise on the eligibility of the proposed operations and compliance with DREF Procedures to regional and country cluster delegations or through participating on joint task force calls and providing advice on the eligibility or not of the proposed requests and advising on DREF grant or loan procedures according to the Emergency Response Framework.
Support alignment of DREF grants with Emergency appeals processes; documentation and reporting flows to avoid duplication or inconsistencies. Where applicable, advise on the management of DREF grants under the EA in accordance with revised operational circumstances.
Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)
Support the DREF approval process by facilitating the collection and consolidation of technical inputs from regional technical and support services teams (Health, Disaster Climate and Crisis, WASH, logistics, NSD, PMER, finance, Log etc.); include liaising with DCC Dept. in Geneva for quality control and sign off.
Support the application of review, validation, and sign off processes for DREF allocations, include to EAs, including eligibility checks, technical and quality control, regional validation.
Closely collaborate with the DREF operation project managers for operations coordination and to maintain an overview of DREF compliance across the operation cycle, revision of operation plans where necessary and timely and transparent financial and narrative reporting on the use of DREF funds.
Promote and support the systematic application of Result Based Management(RBM)Minimum Requirements in DREF operations, including CEA and PGI standards, by providing direct technical guidance to National Societies and IFRC teams—ensuring coordination with PMER for effective implementation of RBM tools.
The DREF Delegate provides operational support for all DREF operations across the Africa Region and works in close coordination with operation coordinators, project managers and technical team at Country, Regional and Global levels.
Capacity strengthening of users ANSs and IFRC staff
Provide hands-on coaching and mentoring to strengthen DREF capacities in Africa, offering proximity support for the development of DREF requests, ensuring process compliance and quality against regional performance standards and SoPs.
Contribute to capacity strengthening activities through training, coaching and knowledge-sharing initiatives and mentoring to National Societies, Partner National Societies, IFRC delegations, and Regional units across Africa.
Reporting and learnings
Support the review of DREF operation final reports, supporting the quality oversight of DREF Final Reports, including compliance and integration of minimum DREF requirement for RBM/CEA/Lesson Learnt Workshop (LLW)findings
Collect and analyse data from DREF reports on performance management targets and maintain database on quality and timeliness of DREF reporting for measurement of progress and monitoring of performance in the Africa Region
Representation
The DREF Delegate supports engagement with DREF partners and may represent DREF in technical discussions as delegated (donors, PNSs, Movement partners, external stakeholders) in Africa.Relationships
The DREF Delegate is part of the Global DREF team, with a focus on the Africa Region. As such, the DREF Delegate reports to the DREF coordinator who oversees daily operations, manages performance, lead the daily technical decisions and manage the HR processes while DREF Senior Officer DREF in Geneva, can continue to advise on technical issues and DREF parameters.
The DREF Delegate also works under the management of the Regional Coordinator of Operations which unit seats under the Disasters, Climate and Crises (DCC) Unit in an advisory role to ensure that DREF Guidelines and Procedures are adhered to
Works in close collaboration with Regional, Cluster and Country Operation and Disaster Management coordinators and colleagues of the various thematic sectors to promote an integrated approach in disaster response operations and ensure coordinated regional support.
Education
Degree level (or equivalent qualification) in Disaster Management, International Development, or other relevant subject(Required)
IMPACT course or equivalent training/knowledge(Preffered)
Experience
3–5 years of progressively responsible experience in disaster management, specifically disaster response operations across multiple country contexts, including rapid‑onset emergencies and complex, protracted crises(Required)
Previous experience of monitoring and evaluation, preferably in the humanitarian/development context(Preferred)
Previous experience of using IFRC planning, reporting and finance tools(Required)
Experience of programme design, project management and reporting, preferably in relation to disaster response(Required)
Practical experience and understanding in sectors that link with disaster response (i.e. relief, food security, health, WASH, logistics)(Required)
Experience supporting emergency operations in the African context, demonstrating familiarity with regional risk patterns, operational challenges, and National Society capacities(Required)
Knowledge, Skills and Languages
Expertise in emergency response systems, operational compliance, and funding mechanisms, ideally with direct experience in DREF or similar rapid funding tools.(Required)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with ability to formulate operational recommendations based on operational trends. (Required)
Proficiency in RBM tools and quality standards (CEA, PGI, PMER), with ability to support National Societies and IFRC teams in their application. (Required)
Strong facilitation and training skills, with ability to deliver capacity-building activities to varied audiences (NSs, PNSs, IFRC delegations). (Required)
Team coordination and networking skills. Able to work effectively across departments, regions, National Societies, IFRC reference centres and external partners. (Required)
Strong cultural awareness and sensitivity, with the ability to work and communicate efficiently in a multi-cultural, multi-lingual and cross-functional team setting, including remote/dispersed teams. (Required)
Knowledge of the IFRC Emergency Response Framework (ERF), DREF Procedures 2024+, and SoPs for emergency operations. (Required)
Understanding of financial compliance controls in humanitarian operations. (Required)
Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants. (Required)
Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values. (Required)
Fluent spoken and written English(Required)
Good command of another IFRC official language (French, Spanish or Arabic)(Preferred)

Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Company Accountant is responsible for the efficient management of the company’s financial resources, ensuring accuracy in financial reporting and compliance with legal standards. The role involves developing and maintaining accounting principles, practices and procedures to support strategic decision making. The role collaborates with various departments to establish budgets and forecast activities, monitor financial performance, implement cost control measures and coordinate year-end organizational audits.
Key Responsibilities
Cash Management
Maintain accurate and organized records of all cash transactions.
Process and record incoming cash receipts including customer payments.
Maintain accurate and organized records of all incoming and outgoing cash transactions.
Accurate account allocation and ensuring exchange gains/losses are approved before posting
Implement and manage collection strategies to minimize overdue accounts.
Issue petty cash after verifying and reconciliation of the expenses.
Post petty cash vouchers on a timely manner.
Support the cash flow planning and forecasting.
Perform regular reconciliations of accounts receivable ledgers with general ledger accounts.
Assist in the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports.
Filing the cash records in Edocs and CW1
Overhead Costs Control and Management
Ensure proper allocation and posting of overhead expenses on CW1 system.
Ensure adherence to internal controls and company policies in relation to overhead expenses.
Analyse and reconcile overhead related general ledgers monthly.
Review overheads trends.
Produce, as required, any ad hoc financial reports as requested by the Management in relation to overhead expenses.
Financial Reporting and Analysis
Prepare accurate and timely annual financial statements, including income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements.
Conduct financial analysis to identify trends, variances, and opportunities for improvement.
Assist the Financial Controller with statutory reporting ensuring compliance with accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Respond to inquiries made by the Financial Controller and other managers regarding financial results and special reporting requests.
Produce, as required, any ad hoc financial reports as requested by the Management.
Budgeting and Forecasting
Collaborating with other departments, develop, implement and monitor budgets.
Provide budget utilization and contribution analysis reports to assist the various departments to manage and monitor their performance in line with the allocated budgets.
Analyse budget variances and recommend corrective actions.
Internal Controls and Risk Management
Work with Financial Controller and Heads of Department across the whole organization to ensure financial risks are identified.
Develop and implement mitigation strategies of the identified risks.
Develop and implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls.
Tax Management and Compliance
Ensure compliance with all tax regulations and timely submission of tax returns i.e. PAYE, VAT, Withholding tax etc.
Ensure compliance with the relevant tax laws
Working with Financial Controller and others, coordinate organization annual audit and ensurea clean audit report.
Provide analysis and advice to the Financial Controller on the potential implications of proposed changes in accounting rules/policies and legislation/government rules.
Financial Systems and Processes
Oversee the development and implementation of new procedures and features to enhance the workflow of the department.
Monitor and analyse department work to develop more efficient procedures and use of resources while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
Ensure the integrity and reliability of financial data.
Other
Coach and mentor staff regarding the handling of non-routine reporting transactions.
Develop and implement financial policies and procedures.
Participate in system improvement processes and initiatives.
Oversee the receivables section of the finance department in collaboration with the Receivables Officer.
Any other responsibility as delegated by management.
Minimum Knowledge, Qualifications and Experience required for this role
Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance
Minimum of 8 years working experience
Proficiency in computer skills
Knowledge of Cargo wise system (Added advantage)
Certification/Membership
CPA (K)
Role Related Competencies (Behavioural Indicators):
Creativity and innovation
Multi-tasking
Prioritization of different tasks
Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills
Excellent communication skills (Verbal & written)
Excellent organizational and planning skills
Ability to work as part of a team in a pressured environment.
Attention to detail and ability to maintain confidentiality.
Demonstrate problem solving skills.
High level of integrity and work ethics
Key Performance Indicators
Efficiency of cash flow management
Adherence to tax compliance and timely filing of returns
Effectiveness of the internal controls in preventing errors and loss
The accuracy and reliability of financial reports prepared.
Number of process improvements implemented.
Budget implementation and monitoring
Team management – efficiency and productivity of the team

The job holder will provide strategic leadership and technical oversight for Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), evidence generation and programme communications across Concern Kenya, ensuring robust systems, credible data and evidence are used to strengthen programme quality, accountability, learning and decision-making. Support the tracking of MEL, accountability and reporting commitments throughout the grant cycle.
Provide timely, accurate and quality-assured data and analysis to support donor reporting, grant reviews and programme performance updates.
Ensure grant-level MEAL, accountability, learning and evidence commitments are monitored, and support programme teams to use performance data, findings and participant feedback to inform grant management and programme adaptation.
Capacity Building, Localization and Learning

Strengthen the capacity of local partners, government and communities to participate in and lead MEAL, accountability and learning processes.
Promote localization, local ownership and the use of locally generated evidence in programme design and decision-making.
Lead documentation and sharing of lessons, good practices, innovations and learning across programmes.
Lead the development and implementation of programme learning agendas and structured reflection processes to identify strategic learning priorities and inform programme improvement.
Promote an organisational culture of continuous learning, reflection and adaptive management, ensuring programmes respond to emerging evidence, changing contexts and the priorities and feedback of programme participants.

Ensure effective management of digital data collection and MEAL platforms, databases, dashboards and other information management systems.

Ensure timely analysis, visualisation and presentation of programme data through dashboards, reports and other appropriate information products to support programme monitoring and evidence-based decision-making.
Work with relevant teams to strengthen the integration, accessibility and use of programme data and information across programmes and grants.
Communications, Evidence and Visibility
Provide strategic oversight and line management to the Communications Officer.
Work with programme teams to identify results, evidence, learning and stories for communication and advocacy.
Ensure evidence and learning are translated into clear products such as briefs, infographics, case studies, success stories and presentations.
Ensure communications are accurate, ethical, appropriately consented and aligned with Concern standards.
Ensure that programme evidence, learning, participant perspectives and feedback are appropriately incorporated into communications and advocacy products, while maintaining ethical standards, informed consent, confidentiality and responsible data use.
Stakeholder Engagement and Representation
Maintain effective relationships with government, donors, partners, research institutions and other stakeholders.
Represent Concern Kenya in relevant national MEAL, survey, research, nutrition and technical forums.
Provide strategic representation and technical leadership in relevant national and international MEAL, accountability, research and programme quality forums.

Set objectives, monitor performance and coordinate workloads across the team.
Promote effective coordination, collaboration and evidence-based decision-making across MEAL, accountability, learning, information management and communications functions.

Required to actively participate in any emergency response as and when required.
Ensure that ethical principles, confidentiality, informed consent, data protection and responsible data management are applied in all assessments, research, monitoring and communication activities.

Ensure that MEAL, accountability, learning and communication functions are appropriately integrated into emergency preparedness and response activities.
Ensure MEAL, accountability, FCRM and information management systems are adapted and operational during emergency response to support timely decision-making and accountability to affected people.

Contribute to organisational strategy, programme design and decision-making by ensuring evidence, learning, accountability and locally generated knowledge are systematically considered.

Undertake any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the Line Manager.

Master’s degree in Statistics, Epidemiology, Monitoring and Evaluation, Project Management, Social Sciences, Economics or a related field.
At least five (5) years’ progressive experience in MEAL, including MEAL systems, surveys, assessments, evaluations and research.
Strong experience in MEAL design, information management, data quality, analysis and reporting, using digital data systems.
Experience in survey and assessment methodologies, including SMART, SQUEAC, LQAS and quantitative and qualitative approaches.
Experience in developing theories of change, logical frameworks, indicators and monitoring plans, and contributing to proposals and donor reporting.
Experience in accountability, localization and capacity strengthening of staff, local partners, government and communities.
Experience supporting grant management and use of evidence for programme adaptation and decision making.
Strong analytical, communication, report writing, presentation and stakeholder engagement skills, with proficiency in relevant data analysis and Microsoft Office tools and fluency in English and Kiswahili.

About the Project
AFIDEP is implementing a three-year initiative to generate policy-relevant evidence on how governments, private sector actors, civil society organisations and communities can strengthen economic integration for migrant and displaced youth in East and West Africa. The project combines mixed-methods research, policy engagement, capacity strengthening and regional learning.
Role Overview
AFIDEP is seeking an experienced Research and Policy professional to coordinate and lead the day-to-day technical implementation of the Inclusive Economic Integration for Migrant and Displaced African Youthproject. The Project Manager will be responsible for delivering project research, coordinating partners and country teams, supporting policy engagement, supervising project outputs, and ensuring timely implementation of approved work plans and milestones.
The successful candidate will have a combination of strong applied research skills, practical project coordination, and evidence-to-policy experience.
Key Responsibilities
Lead Applied Research Delivery
Research Design:
Coordinate development of research protocols, survey instruments, qualitative tools, sampling plans and analytical frameworks.
Data Collection & Analysis:
Lead or support mixed-methods data collection, analysis and synthesis in collaboration with the technical team.
Fieldwork Supervision:
Supervise fieldwork preparation, enumerator training, data-quality checks and documentation.
Ethics & Compliance:
Ensure compliance with approved ethics, safeguarding and data-protection procedures.
Reporting & Publications:
Draft and coordinate technical reports, country analyses, comparative studies and manuscripts
Coordinate Project Implementation
Workplan Coordination:
Coordinate day-to-day implementation of the approved project workplan and deliverables schedule.
Planning & Tracking:
Develop detailed activity plans, implementation trackers and inputs for annual workplans and budgets.
Team & Partner Coordination:
Coordinate staff, partners, consultants and country-level collaborators.
Risk Monitoring:
Monitor progress, risks and dependencies and escalate strategic or material issues to the leadership.
Meeting Management:
Organise project management, technical and partner meetings and maintain action trackers.
Support Policy Engagement & Evidence Uptake
Engagement Strategy:
Work with the project team to implement the policy engagement and evidence uptake strategy.
Policy Materials:
Develop stakeholder maps, policy briefs, technical presentations and briefing materials.
Stakeholder Convening:
Coordinate consultations, validation workshops, policy dialogues and regional learning activities.
Stakeholder Relations:
Maintain relationships with technical officers, implementing partners, youth organisations and other project stakeholders.
Evidence Tracking:
Track evidence use, policy influence, stakeholder commitments and follow-up actions.
Manage Monitoring, Learning & Reporting
Monitoring Data:
Maintain project monitoring data and coordinate routine reporting against indicators, milestones and deliverables.
Donor Reporting:
Develop quarterly, annual and donor narrative reports for review

Company Details:
In 2009, the African Institute for Development Policy (AFIDEP), an African-led, regional non-profit policy think tank, was established to help bridge the gaps between research, policy and practice in the areas of population change and sustainable development, and health systems strengthening in Afri...read moreca. The purpose of AFIDEP’s work is to contribute to sustainable socio-economic development by enabling the formulation of policies and programme interventions that are informed by sound research evidence in these focus areas.

Our Context

In spite of on-going efforts to improve the utilisation of research evidence in decision-making in Africa, there remain major challenges. Available research is largely fragmented in different scientific publications and not appropriately packaged for use by decision-makers. Furthermore, the evidence often does not fully meet the policy and programme needs of decision-makers since they rarely contribute to the initial identification of the knowledge gaps that the evidence seeks to fill. Use of evidence is particularly weak in closing the big gap between policies and implementation, which remains one of the most critical development challenges in Africa. This is partly because there is limited research evidence to inform effective design and implementation of interventions that have the best potential to improve lives.

Define clear roles, accountabilities, decision rights, escalation routes and assurance responsibilities at Board, ELT, global, regional, country, programme and partner levels.

Company Details:
We rebuild tropical fisheries with coastal communities
Blue Ventures develops transformative approaches for catalysing and sustaining locally led marine conservation. We work in places where the ocean is vital to local cultures and economies, and are committed to protecting marine biodiversity in w...read moreays that benefit coastal people.
Our story started over a decade ago, surveying coral reefs in the Mozambique channel. Vezo communities in southern Madagascar were concerned about the decline of their fisheries, so we supported one village to experiment with closing off a small section of their octopus gleaning area for a few months, to see whether this might boost productivity.

When the closure was re-opened, communities experienced a huge increase in octopus landings and fisher incomes. As news of this remarkable fishery boom spread, neighbouring communities started copying this approach. Crucially, this sparked interest in more ambitious coastal management efforts, leading to the creation of the country’s first Locally Managed Marine Area (LMMA) governed by a small network of fishing villages.

Since then, this temporary fishery closure model has gone viral along thousands of kilometres of Madagascar’s coastline, spawning a grassroots marine conservation revolution with 64 more LMMAs established to date. Today, 11% of the island’s seabed is managed by communities, for communities.

Our work is about much more than octopus. These experiences have guided our journey searching for new approaches to demonstrate that marine conservation can be in everyone’s interest, and that taking less from our ocean can give us much much more.

Job Description:
Position overview
As a Client Success Manager, you will play a key role in supporting the success of Tana’s client partnerships and helping drive client satisfaction and retention. You will work closely with our day-to-day stakeholders at client organisations, acting as the bridge between clients and internal teams, including Recruitment, Training, and Talent Success, to ensure strong alignment and empower our talent to thrive in their roles. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role where you’ll be deeply involved in relationship management and problem-solving day-to-day, while also contributing to internal initiatives that strengthen our approach and improve process efficiency as we scale.
Responsibilities
Client onboarding: Onboard clients by helping them understand the Tana model, by translating client requirements into clear, actionable briefs for the Recruitment and Training teams, by reviewing and refining candidate profiles ahead of interviews, and by ensuring Day 1 readiness for talent placements.
Client relationship management: Run regular check-ins with client managers to gather feedback, problem-solve, and ensure expectations are consistently met, while acting as the bridge between clients and the Talent Success team by sharing context, feedback, and priorities and ensuring clear follow-through.
Account health and retention: Monitor client satisfaction, contract renewals, performance concerns, and retention risks, proactively identifying and addressing issues before they escalate and working closely with internal teams to help resolve them.
Growth and expansion
:
Support long-term success by reflecting with clients on the impact of our partnership, by identifying ways to add value and spotting opportunities to expand relationships, whether through new teams, new roles, or referrals.
Process improvement and documentation: Contribute to scaling Tana by helping standardise and automate Client Success processes, while maintaining clear documentation of client feedback, contract renewals, and key account milestones to support proactive follow-up and smooth execution.
Requirements
5+ years in client-facing roles such as Client Success, Account Management, Consulting, B2B Sales, or Project Management, with proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders.
Experience working with clients in North American and/or European markets. Bonus points if you’ve lived or worked abroad in those geographies.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills with internal and external stakeholders.
Strong judgment and problem-solving, particularly in high-stakes and ambiguous situations.
Highly organised, proactive, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Location
This is a hybrid position based in Nairobi, Kenya (3 days a week in-office).

Job Description:
About the Position:
Axmed is building a B2B marketplace that changes how quality medicines are procured across low and middle income countries (LMICs), alongside logistics SaaS and trade financing that connect healthcare providers, governments, NGOs and pharmaceutical manufacturers through one data-driven platform. Quality is the promise that makes the marketplace work: buyers need to trust every product and every supplier on it.
As Quality Lead you are the hands-on owner of day-to-day quality assurance and quality control operations. You will run external audits and quality checks in the system to prevent issues, maintain and improve the Quality Management System (QMS), write and update SOPs, manage CAPAs, qualify suppliers and products, and keep Axmed ready for regulatory and customer audits. You will work closely with Commercial, Operations, Tech, Legal and Regulatory colleagues to make quality practical for a lean, remote-first team, and you will report to the Head of Quality once that role is filled.
What you'll own
Run quality assurance day to day: supplier and product quality checks, documentation review, consignment release and non-conformance handling in line with GDP and GMP principles.
Support internal and external audits and inspections: prepare documentation, assess current processes against requirements, advise on readiness plans, and recommend and track corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) through to closure.
Develop and maintain SOPs so they reflect WHO MQAS and Good Distribution Practice (GDP) standards and how Axmed works.
Monitor and improve the QMS: evaluate the existing system, recommend improvements aligned to industry standards, and work with stakeholders to implement them.
Qualify and monitor suppliers and logistics partners: collect and review quality documentation, run risk assessments and support supplier audits.
Design and deliver training on GDP and quality systems at axmed for internal teams, and maintain the records that demonstrate compliance.
Provide ongoing, practical regulatory and quality guidance to Commercial, Tech, Legal and Regulatory colleagues, and stay current with evolving guidance so processes keep pace.
Skills:
Hands-on application of GDP and GMP in a pharmaceutical, medical device or health supply chain setting. Particular focus to WHO MQAS framework.
Working knowledge of stringent regulatory authority quality requirements (FDA, EMA or Swissmedic) and WHO guidance, and how they apply to distribution and procurement.
SOP writing, document control, deviation and CAPA management, and QMS maintenance (ISO 9001, ISO 13485 or equivalent).
Strong and consistent digital and AI exposure
Audit preparation and execution: internal audits, supplier audits and supporting regulatory or customer inspections.
Clear written and verbal communication; able to simplify complex regulatory topics into accessible guidance and training.
Experience
4 to 7 years in quality assurance or quality control, ideally within pharma, medical devices or health supply chain.
Demonstrated hands-on execution: audits, quality checks, documentation, GDP or GMP application, rather than oversight only.
Experience operating with limited internal infrastructure, for example in a lean team, a startup or a field-based supply chain role.
Experience preparing for regulatory audits and inspections.
Exposure to humanitarian or global health supply chain organisations, or to a Swiss or European pharma distributor, is a strong plus. Experience designing and delivering compliance training is also valued.
Traits
Self-starting and organised: comfortable owning a quality workload end to end without a large team around them.
Pragmatic and risk-based, with high attention to detail where it matters.
Collaborative and approachable; makes quality feel like support rather than policing.
Adaptable to remote, asynchronous working across time zones.
Digital first

Job Description:

You are responsible for developing and managing a portfolio of investments (grants and contracts) aimed at improving primary health care through health systems design and financing.

What You'll Do
Negotiate, execute, and manage a complex portfolio of grants or performance-based contracts.
Review letters of inquiry and grant proposals and provide clear, concise, and insightful written analyses and recommendations for funding.
Consult with grantees and other partners to maximize project impact and ensure grants are meeting strategy goals. This may include site visits, providing operational guidance, and convening meetings of key stakeholders.
Develop, manage, resource, and implement a program that aligns with foundation strategy and is operationally integrated with other foundation programs. Contribute to the design of new strategies, collaborations, and implementation plans to ensure long-term sustainability and impact.
Manage relationships with multiple government counterparts holding distinct mandates (e.g., implementation vs. policy bodies), ensuring all engagement remains strictly non-partisan and technical in nature, consistent with foundation advocacy guidelines.

Coordinate and monitor implementation across multiple subnational sites/regions simultaneously, working through in-country consultants and mentorship networks to maintain visibility and momentum.
Provide rigorous analysis and thoughtful solutions to complex systems problems for both internal and external audiences, drawing on working knowledge of national health information and financial management systems (e.g., DHIS2, PlanRep, FFARS, eLMIS) and how interoperability across these systems supports performance management.
Coordinate with disease-specific technical teams (e.g., malaria, MNCH) to ensure system-strengthening investments translate into measurable service-delivery outcomes for tracer programs.
Communicate strategy effectively and make linkages as needed to support the work through key collaborations and partnerships, including leading development of results-oriented narratives and data packages for high-level strategic reviews — working backward from key milestones to define what evidence and storylines are needed and when.
Manage internal processes and portfolio progress while ensuring appropriate documentation, grant budgeting, and reporting, including a pipeline of investments at different stages (active implementation, design, and approval) simultaneously, ensuring consistent strategic alignment across all of them.
Support inclusive culture through modeling behaviors and actions; escalate issues in a timely fashion to appropriate stakeholders, working closely with an extended support network including in-country consultants, strategy/portfolio management colleagues, and technical specialists to ensure continuity of institutional knowledge and coordinated delivery.

Significant project management experience.
Strong knowledge and expertise across relevant technical areas of health systems strengthening, health financing, insurance/pooling, benefits packages, health technology assessment, or strategic purchasing.
Strong analytical, writing, and verbal skills for communicating with a broad and diverse audience.
Strong understanding of shaping and managing sustainable and scalable ventures.
Understanding of strategies for automating the process of data collection in a variety of settings and sites.

Experience with financial planning software and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.

Job Title: Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager - Africa Region
Job Description:
What We Can Achieve Together:
The Content Strategy & Storytelling Manager is responsible for shaping and driving TNC Africa Region's content vision, editorial strategy, and storytelling agenda. This role serves as the primary architect of compelling narratives that showcase conservation impact, elevate partner and community voices, strengthen donor engagement, expand influence, and deepen audience connection with the organization's mission across Africa.
This is a highly specialized content leadership position requiring exceptional editorial judgment, narrative development expertise, and demonstrated experience translating complex conservation, scientific, and community-based work into compelling stories that inspire action and support. Through exceptional writing, editing, interviewing, and production, this role will help TNC Africa demonstrate conservation impact and deepen connections with strategic stakeholders and audiences.
The position leads the development of strategic content plans and manages the end-to-end storytelling process, from story identification and field reporting to writing, editing, multimedia production, publishing, and performance analysis.
The role collaborates closely with conservation, policy, philanthropy, and Marketing and Communications experts, both regionally and globally, to ensure content aligns with organizational priorities and engages audiences through powerful, authentic, and evidence-based storytelling. In partnership with creative agencies, photographers, and videographers, the incumbent will identify, develop, produce, and publish high-quality storytelling assets. Nature.org will be the primary delivery platform, complemented by video productions, blogs, podcasts, photo stories, and other creative multimedia formats.
The role reports to the Director Marketing & Communications - Africa and shall be based in any country where TNC has offices, in Kenya, Tanzania, Gabon, Zambia, South Africa, Angola. No employment visas or assistance is being offered with this position except for the local labour employment requirements.
We’re Looking for You:
Are you a strong writer, editor, producer, and creative storyteller who can transform complex conservation science into clear and memorable content? Are you excited by the opportunity to report from some of Africa’s irreplaceable landscapes, work with partners, communities, and conservation teams, create donor-focused stories, and help expand influence in written, visual, video, and audio formats?
We are looking for someone with excellent editorial judgment, a strong portfolio, and the ability to manage content from initial idea through publication. By joining the Africa Marketing and Communications team, you will help bring our Big 5 Irreplaceable Landscapes story to life and connect donors with the people, places, and conservation outcomes their support makes possible.
Role Scope & Key responsibilities
Content Strategy & Editorial Leadership
Develop and own the Africa content and storytelling strategy aligned with regional priorities, conservation objectives, philanthropic engagement goals, and organizational brand standards.
Establish an editorial vision and annual storytelling roadmap that identifies priority themes, narratives, audiences, and content opportunities across Africa.
Lead content planning processes to ensure a consistent pipeline of high-impact stories throughout the year.
Define storytelling frameworks, editorial standards, voice, tone, and content governance practices.
Advise leadership and program teams on strategic storytelling approaches that strengthen audience engagement and showcase impact.
Identify emerging stories, trends, and content opportunities that support regional priorities and strategic objectives.
Story Development & Narrative Creation
Serve as the lead storyteller, writer, and editor for the Africa region.
Identify, source, research, and develop compelling stories from landscapes, communities, Indigenous Peoples, conservation practitioners, scientists, donors, partners, and staff.
Transform complex scientific, technical, and conservation information into clear, engaging, audience-centered narratives.
Produce feature stories, long-form articles, case studies, donor stories, scripts, blogs, and impact reports.
Conduct interviews and gather firsthand information to build authentic, evidence-based narratives.
Ensure all content reflects diverse voices, local perspectives, and ethical storytelling practices.
Multimedia Storytelling & Content Production
Lead the conception and development of multimedia storytelling projects, including video, photography, audio, and digital content.
Travel to field sites to conduct reporting, interviews, story gathering, and content production activities.
Develop creative briefs and storytelling concepts for visual and multimedia projects.
Collaborate with photographers, videographers, designers, editors, and production partners to produce high-quality storytelling assets.
Oversee content production workflows and ensure consistency with editorial and storytelling objectives.
Maintain a library of approved stories, photographs, video assets, and supporting content resources.
Audience Engagement & Content Performance
Monitor content effectiveness using audience insights, analytics, and engagement metrics.
Evaluate storytelling performance across channels and recommend improvements based on data and audience behavior.
Apply audience research and engagement data to strengthen narrative approaches and content decisions.
Measure the effectiveness of storytelling initiatives in supporting donor engagement, partnership development, and organizational visibility.
Content Collaboration & Internal Consulting
Partner with philanthropy, conservation, science, policy, country, and digital teams to identify strategic storytelling opportunities.
Provide editorial guidance and storytelling support to colleagues across the Africa region.
Review, edit, and strengthen content created by internal contributors and external partners.
Serve as a subject matter expert on storytelling best practices and content development.
Building the network and collaborations to ensure Africa stories are elevated for global showcases.
Desired Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in in Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English related field and a minimum 7 years related experience or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Exceptional writing, editing, interviewing, and narrative development skills.
Demonstrated experience developing content strategies and managing editorial pipelines.
Experience producing content across multiple formats, including written, digital, visual, and multimedia platforms.
DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English, or related field.
8+ years of professional experience in content strategy, editorial leadership, journalism, storytelling, publishing, or multimedia content development.
Experience working in conservation, environmental, development, sustainability, or nonprofit sectors.
Background in journalism, documentary storytelling, or editorial publishing.
Experience producing stories for donor, philanthropic, and partnership audiences.
Knowledge of digital content performance metrics and audience engagement strategies.
Experience working across multiple African countries and cultures.
Strong understanding of ethical storytelling, representation, and inclusive narrative practices.
Strong portfolio demonstrating impactful storytelling and editorial leadership.
Experience gathering stories through direct field reporting and stakeholder interviews.
Excellent project management skills with experience managing multiple content initiatives simultaneously.
Excellent relationship-building and collaboration skills, with experience working across cultures, functions, locations, and time zones.
Fluency in written and spoken English.
The position has indicative 20% travel

Company Details:
We work with local communities, governments and organizations to conserve Africa’s important places.

Africa is special. Its wild lands and waters are home to incredible numbers and diversity of species living close to people. For most rural Africans, connection to place takes on unique meaning,...read moremore so than anywhere else on Earth because their daily existence depends on the productivity of their natural resources.
Challenges in Africa

Some 60 percent of Africa’s lands and waters - community property, in a sense - are managed by the people who live on them. These people are undoubtedly the most vulnerable on Earth. A continuing threat is their lack of control over the communal lands and waters they depend on for survival.

And as the people struggle, so too does the wildlife that relies on the same resources. An absence of strong institutions and governance further compounds these challenges.

Therefore, our work in Africa is focused on perfecting and exporting the best examples of community-led conservation across the continent’s vast shared lands and waters. These examples are ones that provide tangible benefits to people. Conservation has to pay to be successful.

Job Description:
Kebarick Ventures is looking for a talented, practical and product-minded Full-Stack Software Engineer to help design, build and continuously improve our growing portfolio of digital platforms.
This role is for someone who enjoys solving real business problems with technology — not simply writing code.
You will work on systems used across business, healthcare, HR, recruitment and digital operations, helping turn ideas and operational challenges into secure, reliable and easy-to-use software.
WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON
The successful candidate will contribute to solutions such as:
SaaS business applications
Healthcare and HMIS platforms
HR, Payroll, Attendance and Workforce Management systems
Recruitment and Applicant Tracking Systems
Business websites, customer portals and internal platforms
APIs, integrations and third-party services
Databases, reporting and business intelligence features
Authentication, permissions and multi-user workflows
Mobile-ready and cloud-based applications
System improvements, automation and performance optimisation
WHAT YOU WILL DO
You will be expected to:
Design and develop frontend and backend application features
Build clean, responsive and intuitive user interfaces
Design and maintain reliable databases and data models
Develop and integrate APIs and external services
Troubleshoot bugs, performance issues and production problems
Improve existing systems without disrupting working functionality
Translate business and user requirements into practical technical solutions
Write maintainable, secure and scalable code
Test features thoroughly before deployment
Participate in architecture, product and workflow discussions
Document important technical decisions and system behaviour
Continuously improve system performance, usability and reliability
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You may be a strong fit if you:
Have solid full-stack software-development skills
Are comfortable working across frontend, backend and databases
Understand APIs, integrations and modern web application architecture
Can work with an existing codebase as confidently as building something new
Pay attention to user experience and interface quality
Can debug problems methodically and solve them without creating new ones
Understand security, data integrity and access-control principles
Can translate a real-world business process into a working software workflow
Are curious, adaptable and willing to learn new technologies when necessary
Take ownership of the quality of what you build
THE KIND OF ENGINEER WE WANT
We are not looking for someone who only waits for detailed technical instructions.
We want an engineer who can look at a problem and ask:
What is the user trying to achieve? What is the simplest reliable solution? How should we build it — and how do we make sure it keeps working as the system grows?
You should be able to think beyond individual screens and features and understand how the user experience, business process, data, integrations and underlying architecture fit together.
If you enjoy building software that people actually depend on, we would like to hear from you.

Job Description:
The Opportunity
We are seeking a structured and execution-focused Commercial Lead to own the commercial execution rhythm across our customer growth, compliance, pipeline conversion, and repeat demand functions.
This is not a traditional sales management role. You will be the engine room of our commercial operations—translating strategy into weekly and monthly execution, driving accountability, and ensuring that activity converts into real movement: orders, repeat demand, cash, and customer progression.
You will coach and build the Customer Growth team, strengthen cross-functional execution, and reduce dependency on any single person. If you are someone who thrives on structure, follow-through, and turning pipeline into performance, we want to hear from you.
Core Responsibilities
Customer Growth & Pipeline Discipline
Own the customer growth rhythm and pipeline follow-up. Drive conversion, repeat demand, and customer issue closure.
Translate strategy into weekly and monthly execution plans with clear owners, dates, blockers, and decisions.
Commercial Execution & Compliance
Align compliance, dispatch, receivables, and internal blockers to ensure seamless order-to-cash execution.
Hold the team to movement, not activity: orders, repeat demand, cash, customer progression, market insight, and decisions.
Team Coaching & Capability Building
Coach the Customer Growth team to improve performance, accountability, and commercial discipline.
Build leadership depth by clarifying accountability and reducing dependence on one person.
Data-Driven Decision Making
Use data, customer feedback, pipeline, GP, cash, stock, and market learning to make faster, better decisions.
Strengthen cross-functional execution with Finance, Operations, Production, HRD, and other teams where needed.
Key Deliverables
Customer Growth team operating rhythm established and maintained
Pipeline follow-up and conversion visibility improved
Repeat customer discipline strengthened
Reduced customer and internal execution issues
Role outputs delivered with clear evidence
Actions closed or escalated with owner and date
Quarterly improvement shown in capability, discipline, and impact
Operating Rhythm
Daily: Identify what moved, what is blocked, what was learned, and what decision is needed
Weekly: Review role KPIs, customer/product/market movement, cash or stock blockers, and actions due
Monthly: Review performance, customer/market/product health, recovery decisions, and resource needs
Quarterly: Review KPI delivery, behaviour, growth, capability, and next-quarter focus
What You Bring (Skills & Competencies)
Commercial Operations: Experience managing commercial execution, customer growth, and pipeline discipline.
Team Coaching: Ability to coach, develop, and hold a team accountable for results.
Problem-Solving & Judgement: Ability to separate activity from real movement and make practical decisions.
Communication & Follow-Through: Clear communication and practical follow-through on commitments.
Systems Proficiency: Ability to use trackers, Excel, SAP, S&S Connect, or equivalent tools accurately.
Commercial Understanding: Strong grasp of revenue, GP, cash, stock, customer quality, and risk.
Cross-Functional Maturity: Ability to coordinate across functions without blame or delay.
Our Expectations
At S&S, we look for individuals who don't just do a job, but who live our values. You will be expected to:
Understand and passionately execute the Company's strategy.
Be commercially focused and driven by customer growth.
Be a collaborative problem-solver and a supportive team player.
Ultimately, be self-driven and accountable for realizing the company's goals.
