Job Description:
Main purpose of this Role:
Coordinates and continuously improves the day-to-day operational activities of the company (including logistics, documentation, warehouse, and supply-chain processes), ensuring efficiency, quality, and compliance with local regulations and company standards.
Key responsibilities:
Manage and oversee day-to-day operational activities, including shipment coordination,documentation, and warehouse or distribution workflows.
Ensure all shipment documentation is complete and accurate, and that shipments comply with local regulations of the receiving country.
Ensure local operations meet agreed service levels, cost targets, and quality standards.
Implement and follow standardised operating procedures issued by the management, adapting them where necessary to local legal or market requirements.
Ensure compliance with local regulatory requirements, customs procedures, and shipping/trade documentation standards (Incoterms, certificates of origin, import/export licences, etc.) applicable in the country.
Maintain accurate, up-to-date records within the company's internal data and ERP systems for all local operations.
Coordinate and support local staff, contractors, and third-party service providers (carriers, forwarders, warehouses, customs agents) operating in the country.
Oversee warehouse operations including stock receipts, storage, bagging, repacking, mixing activities where applicable, inventory accuracy and dispatch readiness.
Oversee inventory shrink control, HSE (Health, Safety, and Environment) standards and safety management
Manage clearing agents, port/border customs procedures, and transit logistics optimization.
Coordinate routine maintenance, servicing and operational readiness of local production and warehouse equipment.
Monitor local operational performance and report regularly to the direct manager and dotted-line/functional manager.
Analyse local performance data and propose improvements to increase efficiency, reduce cost, and improve customer satisfaction.
Proactively identify and help resolve operational issues arising in the country, informing relevant parties in a timely manner.
Escalate unclear situations or problems, as well as matters beyond individual authority to the direct manager and/or dotted-line / functional manager.
Share local market knowledge and experience with colleagues, contributing to shared, more effective ways of working across the region.
Perform other duties as reasonably assigned by management – including Country Manager, dotted-line/functional manager and other management representatives.
Additional Requirements:
Perform duties independently while maintaining the highest standards of integrity, professionalism and ethical conduct.
Use clear, solution-oriented, and professional language with all internal and external stakeholders.
Contribute to a positive, collaborative environment, resolving workplace conflicts constructively through established management channels.

Teachers and school leaders
Besides a student’s socio-economic background, the quality of teaching and school leadership has the biggest impact on educational achievement. Therefore, we are strongly committed to the professional development of these important actors.

Capacity development
We offer technical solutions in the form of technical assistance that reinforces the capacity of the government and local education authorities. This mainly concerns departments in the ministries of education and institutions that provide professional development opportunities to teachers and school leaders. We offer practical and technical education expertise as well as process support, and simultaneously make sure that our partners increasingly take the lead as the programme progresses. Four educational subsectors: goals
Teachers and school leaders in early education (and in the transition to primary education) provide an equal start to all learners to ensure their full development during their future education.
 
Teachers and school leaders in primary education use appropriate pedagogical and didactic methodologies to improve literacy, numeracy and life skills in all learners.
 
Teachers and school leaders in general secondary education (and in the transition to it) ensure all learners acquire the necessary 21st century skills.
 
Teachers and school leaders in technical and vocational education and training prepare all learners to the needs of society and decent work.
 
Equity, and gender equity in particular, is a common thread in all our activities.

Job Description:
Job Purpose/Objective
The Community Health Assistant (CHA) is responsible for supporting the delivery of primary healthcare services at the community level. This includes immunization, health promotion, maternal and child health support, disease prevention, and facilitating effective linkages between households and health facilities. The CHA plays a key role in coordinating and supervising Community Health Promoters (CHPs), supporting the implementation of the Kenya Community Health Strategy, and ensuring accurate reporting and data management. The position reports directly to the Health Manager.
Key Responsibilities
Service Delivery and Health Promotion
Provide basic health services including immunization, health education, and management of common illnesses such as diarrhea and malaria.
Support maternal and child health, including promoting antenatal/postnatal care and breastfeeding.
Educate communities on healthy behaviors, including hygiene, sanitation, nutrition, and water safety.
Conduct household visits for health education, surveillance, and disease prevention.
Facilitate community dialogue days, action days, and health campaigns.
Promote the uptake of preventive health services such as family planning and safe water use.
Community Mobilization and Engagement
Work with Community Health Committees (CHCs), CHPs, and other stakeholders to implement health strategies and work plans.
Strengthen community participation in health programs and support referrals between communities and health facilities.
Collaborate with local leaders, NGOs, and MOH structures to enhance health outcomes.
Conduct routine follow-ups of patients defaulting on immunization, HIV, nutrition, and chronic illness services.
Supervision and Capacity Building
Oversee and support the performance of CHPs, ensuring clear roles and household assignments.
Organize and conduct training, mentorship, and on-the-job support for CHPs.
Develop training curricula and contribute to training manuals in collaboration with the CHP team.
Ensure annual training and biannual supervision of CHPs is carried out effectively.
Data Management and Reporting
Maintain accurate records of services delivered at the community level.
Ensure timely and accurate data collection, compilation, and reporting using MOH tools and digital platforms.
Analyze and utilize data for performance monitoring and decision-making.
Submit regular reports to the health facility and relevant stakeholders.
Program Implementation and Coordination
Support the rollout and implementation of the national community health strategy.
Coordinate implementation of community health action plans and participate in program reviews and health surveys.
Attend facility-level meetings and provide guidance on community health issues.
Participate in camp-wide health surveys and intersectoral coordination meetings.
Other Duties
Undertake any other duties as assigned by the Health Manager or Program Manager to support health programming.
Key Result Areas
Effective supervision and coordination of CHPs.
Timely and accurate reporting of community health data.
Increased community participation and improved health outcomes.
Consistent training and capacity building of community health workforce.
Strengthened linkage between the community and health facilities.
Required Qualifications and Experience
Education:
Diploma in Community Health, Public Health, Environmental Health, or a related field.
Registered with a recognized regulatory body.
Experience and Competencies:
Minimum of 2 years’ experience in community health or public health.
Experience working with or supporting the MOH in implementing the Kenya Community Health Strategy and Community Health Policy is a MUST have.
Ability to design community engagement and BCC strategies to foster positive change and sustainable impact in the community.
very good understanding of how the MOH and county health department’s function.
Excellent communication (oral and written) and interpersonal skills.
Strong team player with cultural sensitivity and adaptability to challenging environments.
Previous experience working in low-resource or refugee settings is an advantage.

Job Description:
Position Overview
The Civil Engineer will be responsible for the planning, coordination, supervision and technical execution of civil and infrastructure works at Magnate City, ensuring that construction activities are delivered in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, statutory requirements, quality standards, budgets and project timelines.
The role will provide day-to-day technical oversight of site activities, including earthworks, roads, drainage, water and sewer infrastructure, structural works, utilities and associated external works, while coordinating contractors, consultants, suppliers and other project stakeholders.
The Civil Engineer will also monitor quantities, workmanship, material utilisation, project progress, variations, defects and compliance with occupational health and safety requirements.
Key Roles and Responsibilities
Construction & Site Supervision
Supervise and coordinate day-to-day civil and infrastructure works at Magnate City.
Ensure construction is undertaken in accordance with approved architectural, structural and civil drawings, specifications, Bills of Quantities (BQ), method statements and applicable standards.
Supervise earthworks, excavation and filling; roads, pavements, kerbs and parking areas; storm-water drainage; water reticulation and sewer systems; foundations and reinforced concrete works; structural and masonry works; utility ducts; landscaping-related civil works and other external works.
Conduct regular site inspections and identify workmanship, quality or technical deficiencies requiring corrective action.
Verify setting-out, levels, dimensions and coordinates before and during construction.
Monitor contractor performance against approved work programmes and project milestones.
Technical Coordination
Review civil and structural drawings, specifications and technical documents before execution and identify discrepancies or constructability concerns.
Coordinate with architects, structural engineers, quantity surveyors, MEP consultants, contractors and other specialists to resolve technical and site coordination issues.
Participate in site meetings, technical meetings and project progress reviews.
Prepare and/or review method statements, technical submissions, Requests for Information (RFIs), inspection requests and material approvals.
Ensure all revisions to drawings and specifications are properly communicated and implemented on site.
Maintain accurate as-built information and support preparation of final as-built drawings and project handover documentation.
Quality Assurance & Quality Control
Ensure materials delivered to site comply with approved specifications and quality requirements.
Coordinate and witness relevant field and laboratory tests, including concrete, soil compaction, aggregate and other construction-material testing.
Inspect works before subsequent activities proceed and ensure defective or non-conforming work is rectified.
Maintain appropriate inspection, testing and quality-control records.
Monitor snagging and defects and ensure closure before handover.
Project Planning & Progress Monitoring
Monitor actual construction progress against approved programmes and milestones.
Prepare daily, weekly and monthly progress reports, including photographs, completed works, outstanding works, constraints and corrective actions.
Identify potential delays, technical risks and construction bottlenecks and recommend mitigation measures.
Track contractor resources, including labour, equipment and materials, against planned requirements.
Support preparation and review of construction schedules and short-term work programmes.
Escalate significant delays, defects, cost implications or technical risks to management promptly.
Cost, Quantities & Material Control
Work closely with the Quantity Surveyor/Project Manager to monitor project costs against approved budgets.
Verify quantities and measurements of completed civil works for purposes of contractor valuation and certification.
Review requests for variations and provide technical justification before approval.
Monitor material utilisation and minimise wastage, loss and unnecessary rework.
Verify materials required against drawings, BQs and construction programmes before requisition.
Support procurement by preparing or reviewing technical specifications and evaluating the technical suitability of proposed materials and suppliers.
Contractor & Stakeholder Management
Coordinate civil contractors and subcontractors and monitor compliance with contractual and technical requirements.
Provide technical direction and clarification to site teams where required.
Monitor contractor productivity, workmanship, staffing and equipment deployment.
Liaise with consultants, authorities, utility providers and other stakeholders on technical matters affecting the project.
Participate in contractor performance evaluations.
Maintain professional working relationships while ensuring contractors remain accountable for quality, cost, safety and timelines.
Health, Safety, Environment & Statutory Compliance
Ensure civil works comply with applicable occupational health, safety and environmental requirements.
Work closely with the Health & Safety team to identify and control construction-related hazards.
Ensure contractors implement approved safety procedures, method statements and risk assessments.
Stop or escalate unsafe or materially non-compliant works where necessary.
Support compliance with relevant permits, approvals, building regulations, environmental requirements and applicable Kenyan construction standards.
Ensure required inspections and approvals are obtained from relevant authorities at the appropriate project stages.
Documentation & Handover
Maintain comprehensive site records, including drawings, inspection reports, test results, site instructions, RFIs, progress reports and correspondence.
Maintain records of changes and variations arising during construction.
Participate in practical completion inspections, snagging and defects-liability inspections.
Ensure all identified defects are properly documented, assigned and closed.
Support compilation of the project's technical handover documentation, including as-built drawings, test certificates and relevant approvals.
Academic & Professional Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering from a recognised university.
Registered as a Graduate Engineer with the Engineers Board of Kenya (EBK) or otherwise appropriately registered in accordance with applicable Kenyan requirements.
Minimum 5 years' relevant post-graduate experience in civil engineering and construction/site supervision.
Demonstrable experience in residential, commercial, mixed-use or infrastructure development projects.
Strong knowledge of construction methods, civil works, structural drawings, specifications and quality-control procedures.
Proficiency in AutoCAD and other relevant engineering/project software.
Ability to interpret architectural, structural, civil and services drawings.
Working knowledge of Bills of Quantities, construction programmes, contractor valuations and variation management.
Good understanding of applicable Kenyan construction, safety and regulatory requirements.
Added Advantage
Professional Engineer registration with EBK.
Membership in the Institution of Engineers of Kenya (IEK).
Experience in large-scale real-estate or mixed-use development projects.
Experience with Civil 3D, MS Project, Primavera or similar project-management/design applications.
Experience Profile
Site supervision and civil construction management.
Roads, drainage, sewer, water and external infrastructure works.
Concrete, structural and foundation works.
Setting-out and interpretation of engineering drawings.
Contractor and subcontractor supervision.
Quality assurance and construction-material testing.
Project planning and progress monitoring.
Quantity verification and measurement of works.
Cost, variation and material control.
Preparation of technical and progress reports.
Snagging, defects management and project handover.
Construction health, safety and environmental compliance.
Core Competencies & Personal Attributes
Strong technical and engineering judgement.
Excellent numerical and analytical ability.
Strong attention to detail.
Ability to identify technical problems and develop practical solutions.
Strong planning and project-coordination skills.
Ability to manage multiple contractors and work fronts simultaneously.
Cost and commercial awareness.
Strong quality-control orientation.
Good understanding of construction risk.
Effective written and verbal communication.
Strong reporting and documentation skills.
Negotiation and stakeholder-management skills.
Leadership and supervisory capability.
Ability to work under pressure and meet demanding project deadlines.
High integrity and professional accountability.
Proactive approach to identifying and resolving site issues.
Career Progression
Potential progression: Civil Engineer → Senior Civil Engineer → Project/Construction Manager → Head of Projects/Development.

Company Details: Ol Pejeta is the largest black rhino sanctuary in east Africa, and home to three of the world’s last remaining northern white rhino. It is the only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, in a Sanctuary established to rehabilitate animals rescued from the black market. It has some of the highest...read morepredator densities in Kenya, and still manages a very successful livestock programme. Ol Pejeta also seeks to support the people living around its borders, to ensure wildlife conservation translates to better education, healthcare and infrastructure for the next generation of wildlife guardians. In 2004, the ranch was purchased by the U.K.-based conservation organisation, Fauna &Flora International (FFI), with the financial backing of the Arcus Foundation, a private international philanthropic organisation founded by Jon Stryker. The land purchase was wholly funded by a $15 million donation from the Arcus Foundation, which worked in tandem with FFI and the Lewa Wildlife Conservancy to secure the 90,000 acres of open Savannah grassland and convert it to a national land trust. The conservation of the natural habitat, located in Kenya’s Laikipia Plateau, ensured the protection of existing rhino, elephant, and other wildlife populations in addition to captive chimpanzees living in a 300-acre sanctuary. The Arcus Foundation also gave $12 million to fund capital and institutional development costs at the conservancy. That initial injection of funding allowed Ol Pejeta Conservancy to fulfill its business model as a Kenyan-owned operation benefiting local community development and economic growth in addition to its impact on conservation. Today, the Arcus Foundation continues to support the conservancy through its membership on the Board of Trustees and the funding of various initiatives. In 2014, Ol Pejeta achieved IUCN Green List status, one of only two conservancies in Africa to be awarded this. IUCN Green Listing aims to define excellence in managing valuable natural areas. We have also been awarded the TripAdvisor Certificate of Excellence three years running - a testament to the incredible experiences treasured by all who visit Ol Pejeta. In 2015, we published our 2020 Management Plan - which was developed by our staff in consultation with a range of stakeholders, and sets out our vision for the years leading up to 2020, outlining the major projects that will help us to deliver our vision. We want to become an innovative and sustainable model that conserves biodiversity (particularly endangered species) and contributes to economic growth and the improvement of the livelihoods of rural communities.

Job Title: Group Principal Privacy & Digital Business Auditor
Job Description:
Job Description
Airtel Africa is seeking a Group Principal Privacy & Digital Business Auditor to provide independent assurance and practical advisory insight over privacy, data protection, home broadband and digital business risks across Group and operating company environments. The role will lead complex, multi-country audits, translate regulatory and technical requirements into clear control expectations, and influence senior stakeholders to deliver sustainable remediation.
Responsibilities
Plan and lead risk-based audits over data privacy, data protection, home broadband, fixed and digital business processes.
Assess compliance with applicable data protection laws, Airtel’s Group Privacy Policy and regulatory obligation management requirements.
Evaluate controls over personal data handling, including collection, consent, lawful basis, retention, access, transfer, storage and deletion.
Review privacy governance activities such as RoPA, DPIA, privacy notices, consent mechanisms and data subject request handling.
Audit home broadband and fixed business controls covering network roll-out, provisioning, billing, revenue assurance, partner management, customer experience and service quality.
Deliver management reviews and advisory engagements on emerging risks, transformation initiatives and recurring control issues.
Prepare clear, business-focused audit reports and Board / Audit & Risk Committee reporting inputs.
Coach audit teams, co-sourced specialists and OpCo stakeholders to strengthen privacy, digital risk and audit capability.
Qualifications
Required Experience and Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Law, Accounting, Engineering or a related discipline.
6–10 years’ relevant experience, including at least 4 years in internal audit, external audit, risk or compliance within telecommunications, technology, financial services or a Big 4 environment.
Experience leading data privacy or data protection audits in a multi-jurisdiction environment.
Practical exposure to telecom, ISP, fixed broadband, FTTH or fixed wireless access operations is preferred.
Relevant professional certification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT, CISA, CIA, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27701 / 27001 Lead Auditor, ACCA or CPA.
Key Competencies
Strong privacy, data protection and regulatory judgement.
Digital and data fluency, with the ability to understand data flows, platforms and technology-enabled business models.
Excellent audit execution, analytical and report-writing skills.
Ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive practical, sustainable remediation.
High integrity, independence, ownership and delivery discipline.
Coaching mindset and ability to build capability across diverse teams

Job Title: Global Portfolio Manager, Maternal Newborn Health & Nutrition (MNHN)
Job Description:
About the role
The Global Portfolio Manager (GPM) will support the growing portfolio of the Maternal Newborn Health and Nutrition (MNHN) portfolio. The GPM is a crucial position within the Programs Unit responsible for supporting the Global Portfolio Director (GPD) in the grant management of projects within the portfolio.
The GPM will work with a global cross-functional team of internal resources in Head Office, Africa and Asia, to ensure projects are delivered on time, on scope and on budget. The GPM will ensure all projects delegated to their authority within the MNHN portfolio are managed effectively and delivered according to their contractual obligations.
The Global Portfolio Manager will be an inclusive leader with a proven ability to manage public health/ nutrition grants and lead and motivate teams and foster a respectful and innovative team environment. They will report to the Global Portfolio Director for Maternal Newborn Health and Nutrition and will work closely with all team members in the portfolio and country offices as well as other portfolio teams within Nutrition International.
This position is open to Kenyan nationals and offers a four (4) year contract, renewable based on performance.
Key responsibilities
Portfolio Management
Work with the Global Portfolio Director to put in place effective project management mechanisms to ensure quality implementation and implementation of a set of projects within a portfolio, in collaboration with colleagues in HQ, the regional offices in New Delhi and Nairobi, and in countries of operation and according to Nutrition International policies and ways of working.
Ensure program data is up to date, quality assured by the Monitoring, Data and Learning (MDL) and portfolio teams and is available to leadership and to the communications team.
Grant Management
Working with regional and country colleagues, ensure grants under their management have clear annual plans, activity plans and budgets and are implemented on time and to a high quality.
For all the grants under their management, ensure that all donor, technical and financial reports are completed in a timely fashion to a quality that meets Nutrition International monitoring and reporting standards.
Carry out monitoring to ensure projects are on track to meet corporate and grant performance targets (program and finance) and take corrective action in a timely way
Manage the overall programmatic budget:
Cross Unit/Program Coordination and Representation
Support and provide capacity building to project teams when and where required on project cycle management processes and tools.
Work with Corporate Services and Program unit colleagues to improve modalities, including processes, tools and ways of working to make improvements that drive program quality and/or cost savings.
Represent Nutrition International, as requested, at partner meetings and other forums
Resource Mobilization
Support the development of project proposals.
Requirements
Education/Professional Designations/Experience:
A master’s degree in public health, nutrition, international development, or a similar field or significant experience in lieu.
A minimum of 7 years’ experience managing large, complex, development programs in an international NGO/UN agency (or similar) that spans multiple geographies in Asia and/or Africa and from multiple and diverse donors.
Experience working in the public health/nutrition sector in Asia and Africa; understanding of health systems.
Experience managing field research projects an asset.
Demonstrated experience and/or personal commitment to promoting gender equality within development work.
Previous experience working in maternal and newborn health and nutrition programming is highly valued for this position.
Demonstrated skills and experience in proposal writing, external representation and effective donor stewardship.
Superior written and spoken English; able to work with a team to put together complex documents that clearly articulate the organization’s work.
Previous experience of grant management and/or PMP certification will be an asset
Above average ability in Excel and able to make sense of complex spreadsheets that support the development of better data management and program monitoring.
Experience and comfort working within a matrixed team structure
Other Specific Skill Requirements
Strong ability to identify, rank and mitigate risks, and manage complex time sensitive problems.
Able to work as part of multi-cultural global team in a dynamic and growing organisation.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint.
Excellent communications skills (oral and written) including good report writing and presentation skills.
Excellent communications skills (verbal and written).
Demonstrated understanding of results-based management, performance measurement frameworks and fundamentals of program monitoring and donor reporting.
Demonstrated experience in project start up processes.
Demonstrated understanding and/or experience operationalizing child safeguarding principles and policy.
Fluency in English - both reading and writing – is essential.
A working knowledge of French is an asset.
Key Competencies
Organization: Exceptional organizational and planning skill with a proven ability to prioritize and work in a dynamic fast paced environment.
Leadership: Confident leader with a proven ability to motivate and support project teams.
Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate with internal teams and external stakeholders.
Relationship Building: Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with team members, project stakeholders and partner organizations.
Cultural Sensitivity: Ability to navigate diverse cultural environments and tailor solutions to country and regional contexts.
Project Management: Strong project management skills, with experience in the direct management of international development projects.
Analytical: Ability to analyze and interpret data for decision-making, program improvement, and donor reporting.

Job Description:
Overall purpose of the role:
DRC is recruiting a highly qualified Roving Safety Officer to oversee safety matters related to DRC personnel, assets and facilities within DRC Kenya offices and operations. The Roving Safety Officer is responsible for ensuring proper application of DRC’s Safety Risk Management System (SRMS) and the Global Safety Policy. The Roving Safety Officer, in close collaboration and technical oversight by the Country Safety Coordinator, is responsible for managing known and unknown safety risks, and leading on day-to-day safety management under his/her jurisdiction as per the terms of reference.
Duties & Responsibilities:
Lead in identifying and minimizing potential safety risks to staff, facilities and assets.
Regularly update the Local Safety Rules (LSR) and share with all staff.
Update the SRAs in the different field locations under his/her jurisdiction.
Prepare weekly and monthly safety updates and share with CSC.
Respond to safety concerns raised by staff in different locations under his/her jurisdiction.
Responsible for safety clearance on staff movements
In consultation with the CSC, conduct internal HEIST training for DRC Staff.
Ensure all DRC staff are aware of the safety policies and rules.
Keep Record of Emergency Data (RED) list updated and ensure all new staff submit their forms.
Update and brief all DRC staff and visitors regarding security and context situations.
Support the CSC in Organizing for statutory OSHA audits and Fire Audits and thereafter implement their recommendations.
Maintain safety upgrade plans and develop Safety Improvement Plan (SIP) based on the Office needs.
Establish communication trees and update it frequently.
Ensure all vehicles are equipped as per required standards and vehicle SOPs.
Act as the focal point for supervising the day/night guards across DRC Locations.
Ensure all fire extinguishers and first aid kits are refilled/serviced on time.
Support in managing Critical incidents within DRC Locations.
Any other tasks as delegated by the Country Safety Coordinator.
Experience and Technical Competence
Minimum 5 years’ experience working as a Safety Officer for an NGO or equivalent in a high risk/conflict zone (or equivalent role).
Proven experience in context/security analysis, documentation and advisory in humanitarian & development settings.
Proven in-country experience liaising with UN missions or agencies.
Fluent English, and strong interpersonal, communication, and networking skills.
Proven ability to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines under pressure.
Computer literate, able to use common software packages.
Ability to diffuse tension and always remain calm and particularly following an incident.
Ability to encourage, motivate and guide team members to approach safety and security issues with confidence especially during crises.
Proven ability to work effectively with minimal supervision.
Education
A degree in a relevant field, or equivalent experience.
Other security management related trainings/qualifications (desirable)

English – excellent written and verbal skills
Swahili – excellent verbal skills

Job Description:
ROLE SUMMARY
The Training Admissions and Engagement Coordinator is an enabling role within the Leadership and Learning Department, responsible for the systems, administration and coordination that support the Centre’s programmes and participant journey. This includes admissions and enrolment, participant engagement, university and learning partner outreach, bursary administration, and learning and participant management systems.The role supports the Head of Centre and the Department’s Training, Learning Design, Indigenous Knowledge and Innovation, MEL, and Operations units, and liaises with Fundraising, Communications and Partnerships and other Natural State departments as required.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:
Admissions and Participant Engagement
Manage applications, admissions, enrolment and participant onboarding across Leadership and Learning programmes.
Act as a key contact for prospective and enrolled participants, providing timely information on programme requirements, fees, bursaries, schedules and next steps.
Maintain accurate applicant and participant records and coordinate selection administration, confirmations, waiting lists and completion documentation.
Manage participant communications before, during and after programmes, including engagement between modules, post-programme follow-up, and ongoing communities of practice.
Work with FCP and programme colleagues to support programme promotion and participant recruitment.
University and Learning Partner Engagement
Support outreach and relationship management with universities, colleges, training institutions and other relevant learning partners.
Research and maintain a pipeline of priority institutions and contacts and coordinate meetings, visits, information sessions and follow-up.
Support institutional relationships that contribute participants, expertise, research connections, placements or other learning opportunities.
Work with the Head of Centre, relevant Leadership and Learning colleagues and Fundraising, Communications and Partnership to coordinate partner engagement and track agreed actions.
Training Bursary Fund Administration
Administer the centre’s training bursary fund in line with approved criteria, budgets and procedures.
Coordinate applications, eligibility checks, assessment administration and communication of approved decisions.
Maintain accurate records of awards, beneficiaries, commitments and available balances, working with Finance on related financial administration.
Track bursary utilisation and prepare routine summaries and information for internal and donor reporting.
Final bursary and financial approvals remain with the appropriate authorised decision-makers.
Learning Systems and Training Administration
Support day-to-day administration of the LMS and other admissions, participant and engagement platforms, including learner accounts, enrolment, access and records.
Maintain the training calendar, participant databases, attendance, completion records, programme files and standard administrative tools.
Provide first-line support for basic learner platform issues and escalate technical matters to the appropriate system owner.
Support online and blended programme administration and maintain accurate, secure and consistent information across systems.
Support adoption and improvement of learning and participant management systems as the Centre grows.
Programme Coordination and Operations Interface
Provide the Centre’s Operations/Facilities unit with timely participant numbers, schedules, arrival and departure details, accommodation, dietary and other programme requirements.
Support participant registration, orientation and programme readiness for residential, in-person and field activities.
Coordinate participant-facing travel and logistical information and communicate changes promptly to relevant teams.
Support the CNE Operations/Facilities unit with accommodation, catering, transport, facilities and site operations.
MEL and Reporting Support
Work with the MEL Manager to administer agreed participant surveys, feedback tools and programme data collection.
Maintain accurate admissions, demographic, attendance, completion, bursary and engagement data and provide agreed information for MEL and departmental reporting.
Support participant and alumni follow-up and data-quality checks as required.
Departmental and Head of Centre Administrative Support
Provide administrative and coordination support to the Head of Centre, including meeting bookings, calendars, agendas, briefing materials, action tracking and follow-up.
Provide administrative support to the Training, Learning Design, and Indigenous Knowledge and Innovation units and other departmental workstreams as required.
Maintain departmental files, correspondence, contact lists, calendars and shared information resources.
Support departmental meetings, events, partner visits, travel, routine budget tracking, invoices and other administrative requirements, coordinating with relevant Natural State functions.
Professional Relationships and Communication
Maintain clear, open, and timely communication with the line manager, raising any concerns or risks promptly.
Collaborate effectively with colleagues across the Leadership and Learning department and the wider organisation, including HR, communications, and operations teams.
Act as a role model in upholding the organisation's core values, contributing to a positive, professional, and inclusive working culture
Person Specification
Must Have
Experience
At least five years’ relevant experience in training or programme administration, admissions, participant engagement, education administration or a comparable coordination role.
Demonstrated experience managing applications, admissions, enrolment and participant records.
Experience coordinating multiple programmes, schedules, meetings, deadlines and administrative processes.
Experience communicating with participants and engaging with external organisations or institutional partners.
Experience using digital systems to manage records, applications, communications or programme administration.
Knowledge & Skills
Excellent organisational and administrative skills, with strong attention to detail and follow-through.
Strong written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
Strong digital capability, including Microsoft Office and confidence using databases, online forms, shared platforms and digital systems.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and coordinate effectively across teams.
Sound judgement and discretion when handling confidential participant, bursary and organisational information.
A proactive, flexible and service-oriented approach, with a commitment to a high-quality participant experience.
Education
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant qualification in business administration, education, programme management, communications, community development or a related field.
Candidates with an appropriate diploma or professional qualification combined with substantial relevant experience will also be considered.
Nice to Have
Experience working within a university, training institution, professional education provider or similar learning environment.
Experience engaging with universities, training institutions or other learning partners.
Experience administering bursaries, scholarships or participant financial support.
Experience using an LMS, CRM, admissions or participant management system.
Experience supporting residential, blended, vocational or community-based learning programmes.
Experience supporting participant or alumni engagement, including communities of practice.
Experience administering participant feedback, surveys or MEL data collection.
Experience working in conservation, restoration, sustainable development or the nature economy.
Knowledge of Laikipia and/or relevant Kenyan language skills.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The Global Financial Shared Services Manager will lead IPA's newly established Shared Services Center within the Global Finance team. The role is responsible for building the center from the ground up — designing processes, developing a team of up to five staff, and serving as the primary point of contact for country office finance teams and headquarters leadership. The Shared Services Manager will ensure timely, accurate, and compliant processing of accounts payable, journal entries, expense reports, intercompany transactions, and bank and balance sheet reconciliations across all IPA entities worldwide.
Responsibilities
Operations and Service Delivery
Lead day-to-day operations of the Shared Services Center, covering accounts payable, journal entry processing, intercompany transactions, and bank and balance sheet reconciliations for all IPA offices.
Establish and monitor service-level agreements (SLAs) with country offices and headquarters, including processing turnaround times, accuracy rates, and query resolution timelines.
Coordinate with country office finance staff to resolve queries, address missing documentation, clear reconciliation discrepancies, and ensure completeness of month-end close activities.
Provide coverage to country office finance teams during periods of staff transition.
Support all offices with audit requests as needed.
Process Design and Continuous Improvement
Identify opportunities for automation, system improvements, and process simplification, and lead implementation in coordination with IT and Global Finance teams.
Develop performance dashboards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for the Shared Services function, and report results to senior finance leadership on a regular cadence.
Build team capacity to take on additional responsibilities with a consistent level of excellence.
Team Leadership and Talent Development
Recruit, onboard, and supervise a team of up to three Shared Services staff.
Set individual performance objectives, conduct performance reviews, and support professional development.
Design and deliver training for junior staff on accounting tasks, reconciliation procedures, NetSuite operations, and country-specific requirements; maintain training documentation for knowledge continuity.
Monitor individual and team workload across country assignments; adjust capacity allocation and escalate resourcing needs proactively.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Compliance and Controls
Ensure all transactions comply with IPA policies, donor requirements, and relevant accounting standards.
Support internal and external audits by providing required documentation.
Maintain clear segregation of duties between the Shared Services Center and country office banking and treasury functions.
Stakeholder Engagement and Reporting
Serve as the primary liaison between the Shared Services Center, country office finance teams, and headquarters Global Finance.
Oversee generation of monthly financial reports for distribution to country office finance teams and leadership.
Lead regular check-ins and reporting meetings with country office finance leads, providing updates on month-end close status, outstanding issues, and team performance.
Communicate process changes, training requirements, and service updates to all stakeholders.
Contribute to cross-functional projects related to finance transformation and other global initiatives as needed.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance.
Minimum seven years of progressive experience in accounting, including at least three years of direct supervisory experience.
Demonstrated experience leading or working in a shared services, business process outsourcing (BPO), or centralized finance environment.
Full professional proficiency in English and Spanish, written and spoken.
Strong working knowledge of accounts payable processes, general ledger accounting, and internal controls.
Proficiency with ERP systems, preferably NetSuite, and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Proven ability to collaborate across time zones and cultures, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience supporting multi-currency and multi-country accounting operations.
Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Chartered Accountant (CA), or equivalent professional certification. (preferred)
Master's degree in accounting, finance, or business administration. (preferred)
Experience with nonprofit, international development, or donor-funded organizations, including familiarity with USG and FCDO requirements. (preferred)
Demonstrated experience designing or improving accounting processes across multiple entities or geographies. (preferred)

Job Title: Kenya Market Research & Business Development Executive, Marketing
Job Description:
Before we sell a single t-shirt, we want to understand the market properly. We are looking for a sharp, curious, Nairobi-based researcher and business developer to be our eyes and ears on the ground — first to map how t-shirts actually move through Kenya, and then to turn that knowledge into a pipeline of real potential buyers and partners. You will work directly with the founders and help shape how an established international textile house launches its own premium brand in Kenya.
The role at a glance
This is a two-part engagement.
Part 1 is research: understand the distribution and wholesale network for t-shirts in Kenya — who imports, who sells, who buys, and from where.
Part 2 is business development: use that market picture to build a verified list of potential buyers and partners, mapped by category. You'll move from “how does this market work?” to “here are the people worth talking to.”
Part 1 — Understand the market
Map how t-shirts flow through Kenya, from origin to end-buyer, and give us an evidence-based read on the best way to enter. You will investigate:
The distribution network — how t-shirts reach the market: importers, wholesalers, distributors, and the traders and hubs (e.g. Nairobi's wholesale districts) that move volume.
Where product comes from — which countries supply Kenya's t-shirts (China, India, Turkey, Bangladesh, second-hand “mitumba”, local manufacture), at what quality tiers and rough price points.
Who buys and who sells — the players at each step of the chain, how they buy, in what quantities, and how often.
Route-to-market comparison — weigh the options for a premium brand like ours: selling through the existing wholesale/distributor network versus going retail-direct. Tell us, with reasons, which looks stronger and why.
Buyer categories — break the demand side into segments (for example hospitality, corporate and promotional/branding, retail store owners, institutions, and online sellers) and size up which are the most realistic and valuable targets for us.
The competitive picture
—
what's already on the shelves, at what quality and price, so we understand where a premium cotton tee fits.
Part 2 — Build the pipeline
Turn the research into a practical, verified list of people worth contacting. You will:
Build a target list of potential buyers and partners across every realistic buyer category identified in Part 1.
Identify and verify named contacts — real, currently-employed decision-makers — with accurate contact details, not guesses or scraped data.
Capture how each type buys: volumes, buying frequency, and what they look for in a supplier.
Keep a clean, well-organized record of your findings and sources in a shared workbook we provide.
Share what you're learning with the founders on regular check-in calls, so we can steer the work as it develops.
Qualification
Based in Nairobi and able to do both online (desk) research and in-person fieldwork across the city.
3–5 years' experience in market research, B2B sales/business development, distribution, or the textile/apparel trade.
Strong local knowledge of Nairobi — comfortable navigating both the textile/production zones on the outskirts (e.g. the EPZ) and the downtown wholesale and retail districts where t-shirts are traded.
A genuine researcher's instinct — resourceful, curious, and able to find answers by talking to real people, not just Googling.
Fluent English and conversational Kiswahili, so you can hold useful conversations across the trade.
Organised and evidence-led — you record what you find clearly and can back it up. We value verified, first-hand information over volume, and do not accept AI-generated or scraped data.
Self-directed, comfortable owning a scope of work and reporting progress without close supervision.

Job Description:
About the Position
Namati is entering a critical new phase. As we deepen our impact across the globe, we seek a strategic and relationship-driven Partnerships Manager to secure funding for Namati’s work in Africa.
As Namati’s fundraising strategy evolves, we’re shifting much of our global Resource Mobilization (RM) team to prioritize multi-program and thematic awards spanning several countries or global initiatives. To complement this global team, we’re looking for a Manager to focus squarely on single-program awards for our programs in Kenya and Sierra Leone. That means cultivating funders whose interests are rooted in a specific country or a program, such as embassies, local offices of development agencies, and foundations funding in-country civil society initiatives.
The Manager will drive the full lifecycle of program-specific fundraising, from prospect identification and cultivation to securing awards to stewarding relationships for longevity and growth. This role will report to the Senior Advisor for the time being.
This is a unique opportunity for a skilled fundraiser to embed in the work of locally-rooted country teams, working side-by-side to resource their essential work during a time of global instability, while benefiting from close collaboration with a professional, global fundraising team.
Key Responsibilities include:
Pipeline development & strategy
Build and maintain a robust pipeline of funding opportunities for Namati’s programs in Africa, with particular attention to embassies, local foundations, global foundations with country-specific grantmaking strategy, and in-country offices of bilateral and multilateral agencies.
Track donor trends and identify opportunities that align closely with near-term program priorities as well as supporting longer-term country strategies.
Collaborate with U.S.-based colleagues to ensure program-specific fundraising complements and aligns with broader thematic and multi-country strategies.
Proposal development & reporting
Lead the drafting, coordination, and submission of concept notes, proposals and reports for program-specific opportunities in tight collaboration with program and finance teams.
Ensure compliance with donor requirements and internal processes, meeting all commitments to funders on time and at the highest quality.
Donor cultivation & stewardship
Develop strong relationships across diverse stakeholders ranging from embassy staff to local donor representatives to foundation program officers, positioning Namati as a trusted partner.
Represent Namati at external meetings, events, and donor convenings in Nairobi and (occasionally) Freetown or elsewhere, including regional or continental convenings such as the Africa Philanthropy Forum.
Cultivate opportunities to build multi-country relationships with donor agencies whose embassies fund across more than one Namati country.
Internal collaboration
Work hand in hand with our Sierra Leone and Kenya program leads to understand their strategies, priorities, and funding needs, and to provide funding outlook insights to inform country strategy.
Support program teams to deeply understand donor goals and perspectives while ensuring that our fundraising efforts focus on aligning funders to our mission and values, rather than bending our programs to match funder priorities.
Provide the RM team and global leadership with regular analysis of local trends, opportunities, and risks in African philanthropy and bilateral giving, highlighting emerging themes that could affect both program-specific and thematic fundraising.
Fundraising systems & learning
Collaborate with fundraising operations team members to ensure timely entry of all proposals, opportunities, and donor interactions into Namati’s fundraising management systems (HubSpot, Asana, Google Drive).
Monitor key pipeline and renewal metrics, ensuring that day-to-day fundraising efforts lead to measurable progress toward strategic fundraising goals.
Contribute to team-wide learning about effective program fundraising approaches, sharing insights about country programs and in-country donor landscapes with the global RM team.
Here’s what you might have tackled last week:
Drafted a proposal to the European Union delegation in Nairobi, in partnership with Namati Kenya’s Citizenship team, to strengthen inclusion of marginalized groups in civic processes related to elections.
Traveled to Freetown to join the Sierra Leone team for a meeting with the Dutch Embassy, and helped craft a follow-up memo to secure an invitation to apply for a grant focused on strengthening community land tenure.
Conducted prospect research in collaboration with fundraising operations team members to add new embassy opportunities to the fundraising pipeline, revising likelihood-of-success ratings and sharing new insights with colleagues in Asia who are pursuing similar embassy relationships.
Partnered with the land, environment, and climate justice (LECJ) team in Kenya, as well as the finance team, to draft and refine a budget narrative for a $100,000 proposal for a U.S. funder.
Attended a donor roundtable at the Canadian High Commission in Nairobi, and initiated follow-up conversations with three program officers about potential collaboration.
Coordinated with U.S.-based RM team to ensure your chosen messaging for a Sierra Leone-specific proposal aligns with broader organizational communications and global funding strategies.
About You
Must-Haves
Fundraising experience: At least 7 years of professional fundraising or business development experience in the nonprofit or development sector, with a strong track record of securing institutional awards in Africa.
Deep familiarity with the African donor landscape, especially in East or West Africa.
Relationship-builder: Demonstrated success cultivating relationships with embassies, foundations, or donor agencies with professionalism, warmth, and credibility.
Program fluency: Capacity to quickly learn and speak compellingly about Namati’s varying strategies across our African country programs.
Communication skills: Excellent writer and communicator, able to produce persuasive proposals and reports, and to adapt messaging to different audiences.
Collaborative spirit: A team player who thrives on close collaboration with program and fundraising colleagues across countries and time zones.
Organized and systems-oriented: Skilled at managing multiple projects simultaneously, meeting deadlines, and maintaining accurate records in shared systems.
Nice-to-Haves
Prior experience in legal empowerment, human rights, or international development.
Public speaking skills, including experience representing organizations at philanthropic or global policy events.
Location and Travel
This role will be based in Nairobi, Kenya, with occasional travel to Sierra Leone, other parts of Africa, and other global locations as required (approximately 10–15% of the time). When not traveling, the successful candidate will follow Namati’s hybrid work policy, which requires staff to work from the office two days per week.
Candidates must already be legally eligible to work in Kenya; Namati is unable to sponsor a work permit for this role.
The successful candidate will also be expected to occasionally work outside standard working hours to accommodate colleagues across different time zones, particularly as most of the members of the RM team are based in the United States.

Job Description:

Monitor actual, committed, and forecast costs against approved project budgets.
Identify cost overruns, budget variances, and margin erosion at an early stage.

Provide Project Managers with timely financial information to support corrective decisions.

Strengthen accountability by ensuring project teams understand the financial impact of their decisions.

Qualifications, Experience & Skills
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.
CPA, ACCA, CMA, or equivalent professional qualification, or demonstrable progress towards one, is a must.
Minimum of 2 years' relevant experience in cost accounting or project cost management.
Experience in project/product costing, inventory reconciliation, cost allocation, variance analysis, and margin monitoring.
Experience working collaboratively with Finance, Procurement, Operations, and Project teams to control costs and improve profitability.
Experience working across multiple concurrent projects is highly desirable.
Prior exposure to the technology sector will be an added advantage.
Proficiency in ERP/accounting systems and advanced Microsoft Excel.
Experience with Zoho is an added advantage.
Excellent attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
Strong variance analysis and root-cause investigation skills.
Ability to translate financial data into practical and actionable business insights.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Strong ownership and accountability.
Ability to work independently and meet strict deadlines.

Job Description:
Role Overview
The Program Delivery Associate Trainee is an entry-level development role designed to prepare individuals for full operational responsibility in implementing Tap2Eat program delivery across a cluster of schools.
During the six-month traineeship, the trainee will work closely with experienced Program Delivery Associates and Regional Program Delivery Officers to gain hands-on exposure to school operations, data management, customer engagement, and program monitoring.
The program is designed to build the trainee’s operational capability, professionalism, and leadership readiness, preparing them to transition into the Program Delivery Associate (PDA) role responsible for managing approximately 30 schools within a cluster.
Key Responsibilities
School Operations Support
Assist with daily school operations including queue management, food receipt verification, tapping, and tag replacement.
Accompany Program Delivery Associates during school visits to observe and learn operational workflows.
Support monitoring of school-level hygiene practices, portion control, and service standards.
Help ensure adherence to Tap2Eat Standard Operating Procedures during daily operations.
Program Utilization & Data Processes
Learn to track key operational metrics such as registrations, activations, utilization, and tapping performance.
Assist in collecting, entering, and verifying school-level operational data.
Support the identification and documentation of performance gaps in assigned schools.
Participate in data reconciliation activities and follow-ups with underperforming schools.
People & Stakeholder Support
Support School Leads, Coordinators, Tappers, and Kitchen Officers in executing daily operational duties.
Assist in communicating program updates and operational changes to school teams.
Learn how to build professional relationships with school administrators, parents, and community stakeholders.
Support the resolution of simple operational issues under supervision.
Customer Experience & Engagement
Observe and practice handling parent or school concerns in a professional and empathetic manner.
Coordinate with Customer Engagement teams to ensure consistent messaging and issue resolution.
Assist in gathering feedback from parents, students, and school administrators to improve service delivery.
Inventory & Logistics Support
Assist in monitoring availability of tags, devices, and personal protective equipment (PPE) across assigned schools.
Support basic inventory tracking and reporting under the supervision of the Program Delivery Associate.
Help document asset usage and report shortages or replacement needs.
Reporting & Documentation
Support daily school reporting and operational documentation.
Participate in compiling summaries and preparing reports for internal use.
Maintain structured notes and logs during school visits to support learning and operational review.
Training Expectations – Learning While Executing
The traineeship is designed as a hands-on operational training program, where learning takes place through real program execution.
During the training period, trainees may be assigned a small group of schools within a cluster to support and gradually manage under the guidance of the Regional Program Delivery Officer and experienced Program Delivery Associates.
This approach ensures trainees gain practical experience while contributing to daily program delivery.
Key expectations during the traineeship include:
Supporting and eventually managing operations in a designated group of schools during training
Conducting regular school visits to observe and improve operational performance
Working directly with School Leads, Coordinators, and Tappers to ensure smooth daily operations
Monitoring tapping, utilization, registrations, and activation trends in assigned schools
Identifying operational gaps and proposing improvements with guidance from supervisors
Participating actively in coaching, feedback sessions, and operational reviews
The goal is for trainees to build operational confidence while delivering real program outcomes.
Expected Outcomes (Post-Traineeship Capability)
By the end of the training period, the trainee should be capable of independently performing the responsibilities of a Program Delivery Associate, including:
Managing Tap2Eat operations across 30+ schools within a cluster
Supervising School Leads, Coordinators, Tappers, and Kitchen Officers
Monitoring and improving key program performance indicators such as utilization, activation, penetration, and tapping accuracy
Ensuring adherence to hygiene, food safety, and operational compliance standards
Resolving escalations from parents, school administrators, and school-level teams
Maintaining accurate operational data including tag assignments, tapping records, attendance, and feeding reports
Managing inventory of program assets including tags, devices, and operational supplies
Coordinating with internal teams such as Customer Engagement, Tech, and Utilization to support program performance
Conducting structured school visits and coaching frontline teams to improve service delivery
Generating timely operational reports and flagging system or data issues to relevant teams.

Preparing project proposals and reports for funding to donor individuals and organizations.
Managing all conservancy logistics to ensure compliance with conservancy regulations and efficiencies.
Maintaining conservancy assets at a serviceable level.
Undertaking capacity building of the various conservancy Board committees.

Enhancing conservancy visibility.
Leading peace-building initiatives.
Reinforcing the role of women and youth in bringing about peace and collaboration.
Any other duties as may be assigned from time to time.

A Bachelor’s degree in Conservation, Natural Resource Management, Wildlife Management, Rangelands Management, Community Development or a related field from a recognised university.

Demonstrated ability to think creatively and solve problems effectively.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Kiswahili.

A firm understanding of pastoralist customary livestock practices and community engagement processes.

Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to establish and maintain effective partnerships and working relationships.
Strong understanding of pastoralist customary practices and community engagement processes.

The ability to build and lead effective teams.

Job Title: Programme Policy Officer Assurance Coordinator CST II
Job Description:
Assurance Objective
The objective is to provide management with reasonable, evidence-based assurance that material CP-related risks are identified and appropriately managed; key controls are suitably designed and operating as intended; compliance obligations are being met; significant findings are addressed within agreed timelines; and the Country Office maintains adequate evidence to demonstrate effective oversight to internal and external oversight bodies. The assignment will apply a risk-based approach, with assurance effort proportionate to risk exposure, funding and materiality, donor sensitivity, geographic and operational complexity, prior findings, control maturity and other relevant risk indicators.
Scope of Assurance
The assurance scope will cover CP-related governance, risk management, compliance and internal controls across the CP management lifecycle, including, as applicable:
due diligence, capacity assessment and risk classification;
partner selection and governance arrangements;
financial and programme controls relevant to CP implementation;
segregation of duties and approval controls;
monitoring, spot checks, verification and supporting evidence;
implementation of agreed risk mitigation measures and management actions;
follow-up of audit, investigation, assurance and monitoring findings;
data quality, record retention and audit trail adequacy;
compliance with applicable WFP policies, procedures, CP management requirements and donor conditions; and
emerging or systemic CP-related risks identified through data analysis, field work, management reporting or oversight activity.
The scope of individual reviews will be defined in an approved risk-based assurance work plan or review terms of reference. The coordinator will not provide assurance over matters for which the role has direct operational responsibility.
Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities
CP governance and internal controls
Assess the design and operating effectiveness of key CP governance and internal control arrangements, using documented criteria and sufficient appropriate evidence.
Identify control gaps, ineffective or inconsistently applied controls, segregation-of-duties weaknesses, recurring process failures and other control deficiencies.
Assess whether identified controls address the relevant risks and whether control owners can demonstrate that controls operated during the period under review.
Recommend practical corrective actions that address root causes and assignable control weaknesses.
Risk assessment and due diligence oversight
Independently review CP due diligence, capacity assessments, risk ratings and mitigation measures for completeness, consistency, evidence and alignment with applicable requirements.
Maintain a consolidated view of high-risk CP engagements within the assigned portfolio, including material risk exposures, mitigation status and overdue actions.
Provide documented constructive challenge where risk assessments, ratings or mitigation plans are weak, incomplete, outdated or unsupported by evidence.
Escalate material changes in CP risk exposure through established governance channels.
Risk-based assurance planning
Develop and maintain a documented, risk-based CP assurance plan for the assigned Area Office portfolio, subject to management approval through established governance arrangements.
Prioritize assurance activity using defined risk factors, including risk rating, funding/materiality, donor sensitivity, geography, operational complexity, prior audit or assurance history, control maturity and unresolved findings.
Maintain sufficient assurance coverage of high-risk engagements and periodically reassess the plan in response to significant changes in risk exposure.
Align CP assurance activities with the Country Office assurance plan, risk register, audit readiness priorities and relevant governance forums.
Assurance reviews, testing and independent verification
Conduct assurance reviews, spot checks, walkthroughs, sample-based testing and independent verification for selected high-risk CP engagements or locations.
Define the objective, scope, criteria, sampling approach, evidence requirements and review period for each assurance exercise.
Assess evidence for relevance, reliability, completeness and traceability, and retain sufficient working papers to support conclusions.
Document exceptions and control deficiencies clearly, including the condition observed, applicable criterion, risk/impact, root cause where established, supporting evidence and agreed management action.
Prepare concise assurance reports with findings, risk implications, recommendations, responsible owners and agreed target dates.
Audit readiness and oversight follow-up
Support preparedness for internal audits, external audits and CP-related oversight reviews by maintaining an up to-date evidence trail and status of material findings.
Maintain a consolidated tracker of audit observations, assurance findings, investigation-related actions where applicable, spot-check findings and management actions.
Validate, on a risk basis, evidence submitted to close or remediate findings before closure is reported.
Monitor overdue, recurring or high-risk findings and escalate significant unresolved matters through established governance channels.
Coordinate factual inputs and evidence retrieval for oversight responses without assuming management ownership of the response.
Risk monitoring, data analytics and reporting
Analyse Partner Connect, UN Partner Portal, monitoring, audit, assurance and other available data to identify trends, anomalies, concentration risks and early warning indicators.
Maintain a portfolio-level dashboard covering high-risk CPs, assurance coverage, material findings, overdue actions, repeat findings and audit-readiness indicators.
Provide periodic assurance updates to management and contribute evidence-based CP risk inputs to the Country Office risk register and management briefings.
Escalate systemic or cross-cutting control weaknesses where remediation requires management action beyond an individual CP or Area Office.
Continuous improvement
Strengthen assurance tools, checklists, templates, sampling approaches and review methodologies based on lessons learned and emerging risks.
Promote consistent documentation and assurance practices across Area Offices.
Support cross-functional learning on CP risk and controls while maintaining the distinction between second-line assurance and first-line management.
Methodology and Minimum Evidence Standards
All assurance work shall be documented sufficiently to permit an independent reviewer to understand what was reviewed, against which criteria, using what evidence, with what sampling or testing approach, how exceptions were evaluated, and how the conclusion was reached.
Each review shall have a defined objective, scope, criteria, period under review and risk rationale.
Testing shall be risk-based and proportionate to the significance of the control and the exposure under review.
Evidence shall be sufficiently appropriate, relevant, reliable and traceable to the conclusion reached.
Working papers shall identify the population reviewed, sample selected where applicable, tests performed, evidence obtained, exceptions identified and conclusion reached.
Findings shall distinguish clearly between fact/evidence, applicable requirement or control criterion, risk/impact, root cause where supported, and recommended corrective action.
Management actions shall have a clearly identified owner and target completion date and shall be tracked to closure.
Where evidence is insufficient to support closure or an assurance conclusion, the matter shall remain open or be explicitly qualified and escalated as appropriate.
Reporting, Escalation and Governance
The Assurance Coordinator reports functionally to the Risk and Compliance Unit and coordinates with Area Office management and relevant technical units for planning, evidence gathering and follow-up.
Significant control deficiencies, material compliance concerns, suspected systemic weaknesses and overdue high-risk actions shall be escalated promptly through established governance channels.
Assurance reports shall be factual, evidence-based, balanced and sufficiently documented to withstand management, audit and oversight scrutiny.
The Coordinator shall maintain professional objectivity and shall not approve, own or implement controls that are subsequently subject to the Coordinator’s assurance assessment.
Access to relevant records, systems, personnel and locations shall be obtained through established Country Office arrangements and in accordance with applicable confidentiality, data protection and access requirements.
Role boundaries and independence The Assurance Coordinator
will not:
manage CP contracts or administer Field Level Agreements (FLAs);
lead routine CP onboarding or manage day-to-day CP relationships;
perform first-line programme, finance, supply chain, monitoring or CP management functions;
approve CP risk ratings, management actions or control decisions on behalf of first-line owners;
assume ownership for implementing corrective actions arising from assurance work; or
provide assurance over controls for which the Coordinator has direct operational responsibility.
The role provides independent second-line assurance, constructive challenge, verification, reporting and escalation. Management retains responsibility for risk acceptance, control operation, corrective action and achievement of programme objectives
.
Deliverables and Minimum Outputs
Risk-Based CP Assurance Plan: approved and periodically refreshed assurance coverage for the assigned portfolio, with documented risk rationale.
Assurance Review Reports: reports supported by documented criteria, evidence, testing, findings, root-cause analysis where established, risk implications and agreed actions.
Quarterly CP Assurance Reports: portfolio-level assessment of key risks, control weaknesses, assurance coverage, recurring findings, overdue actions and emerging trends.
CP Risk and Assurance Dashboard: current view of high-risk CPs, assurance coverage, material findings, overdue actions and audit-readiness status.
Corrective Action Tracker: consolidated tracking of audit, assurance, monitoring and spot-check actions, including ownership, due dates, status and evidence of closure.
Audit Readiness File: organized evidence trail supporting material CP assurance activities and follow-up.
Annual CP Assurance Opinion: concise, evidence-based management assurance statement on the adequacy of CP governance, risk management and key controls within the assigned portfolio, including material limitations or qualifications where applicable
Risk Register Inputs: documented, evidence-based CP assurance inputs for Country Office risk and assurance reporting.
Performance Indicators
Percentage of planned risk-based assurance activities completed within the approved assurance cycle.
Percentage of high-risk CP engagements covered by assurance in accordance with the approved plan.
Percentage of material findings with documented owners, target dates and evidence-based closure status.
Ageing and recurrence of overdue or repeat material findings.
Timeliness and completeness of assurance reports and management updates.
Percentage of sampled assurance work with complete supporting working papers and traceable evidence.
Qualifications and Experience
Education:
Advanced university degree in risk management, internal audit, compliance, finance, accounting, governance, operations management or a related field. Relevant professional certification is desirable.
Experience:
5–7 years of relevant experience in assurance, audit, compliance, risk management, internal controls or oversight. Experience with NGOs, implementing partners, humanitarian operations or audit readiness is desirable.

Top risks
