Job Description:
Job Summary:
We are seeking a dynamic and motivated Program Director to lead the anticipated five-year AgEMERGE (Agricultural Enterprise-led Market Ecosystems for Resilience, Growth and Equity) program in Kenya, based in Nairobi.
AgEMERGE is a market-led program that deploys a delivery model that combines direct technical assistance and Dutch commercial partnerships with a Local Investment Facility. The Program Director will manage this milestone-based grants facility and co-investment portfolio, including awards to local businesses. The PD will also lead the consortium, liaising with the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN), coordinating with sub-national regional leadership and in-country partners, supervising the project teams, and overseeing implementation and resource management in project offices. This role includes financial and administrative oversight and accountability, reporting, risk management and monitoring and evaluation of the project.
Program Overview:
AgEMERGE is a five-year, €15 million Food and Nutrition Security program funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN) in Kenya. Implemented by a consortium led by TechnoServe, AgEMERGE takes a catalytic, market-led approach centered on the middle of the value chain, strengthening the midstream businesses (aggregators, processors, traders, and logistics providers) that connect farms to markets. A Market Systems Development approach will be adopted to maximise localisation and sustainability. A strong emphasis on inclusive value chains, women’s empowerment and creating economic opportunities for youth will be a cross-cutting priority.
Working across three market corridors and 14 predominantly Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) counties, the program will reach approximately 85,000 farmers, pastoralists, and MSMEs (at least 50% women and youth). AgEMERGE will crowd in commercial investment and Dutch partnership to build a market-driven, climate-resilient, and inclusive agri-food system.
Primary Functions & Responsibilities:
Lead overall implementation and management of the program, from inception to close-out, ensuring that the program achieves established goals, objectives and targets.
Provide strategic guidance, leadership, management and general technical oversight of the program.
Drive the program’s catalytic, market-led strategy across the three corridors (Commercial Growth, Adaptive Crops, and Coastal-Northern) and five activity pathways, adjusting intensity and sequencing to market maturity.
Oversee the Local Investment Facility and its grant windows (Local Systems & Delivery; Local Trade & Investment; and Local Research, Innovation & Learning), ensuring milestone-based disbursement, cost-share, due diligence, and compliance.
Cultivate and activate Dutch commercial partnerships and the investment pipeline — working with European development finance and government credit agencies such as EKN, RVO, FMO, and Dutch firms to connect Kenyan market actors to Dutch knowledge, technology, and capital.
Ensure integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), climate resilience, and nutrition as market-system priorities across all activity pathways and grantee engagements.
Continuously develop operational efficiencies and drive innovations in delivery.
Oversee development and submission of project deliverables on time and within budget.
Recruit, lead, manage, and supervise delivery teams comprising long- and short-term team members and consortium partners.
Serve as the primary liaison with the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN), the Government of Kenya (national and county) entities and all counterparts, implementing partners, and stakeholders involved with the program.
Act as a spokesperson for the program and present its work regionally/globally.

Produce content that works for Reuters' global clients and digital audiences.
Identify opportunities for exclusive pictures, deeper visual storytelling and longer-term photographic projects.
Build and maintain strong relationships with sources, photographers, editors and other stakeholders across Kenya and the wider region.

Candidates must have strong technical photography skills, including:
Professional digital photography and camera skills.
Digital image editing and processing.
Accurate captioning and metadata management.
Fast and reliable picture filing and transmission from the field.
The ability to work with professional photography equipment and modern image-management and transmission systems.
A strong understanding of photographic ethics, accuracy and Reuters' editorial standards.

Experience covering major breaking news, political, business, sporting or humanitarian events in East Africa or other complex reporting environments, with a demonstrated ability to deliver exclusive and agenda-setting visual journalism
Experience working in an integrated newsroom environment, collaborating closely with text, video and digital teams to deliver coordinated, multi-format coverage for global audiences and clients.

INTRODUCTION TO THE ROLE
Girls Not Brides is seeking a talented Development Officer to join a small, high-performing team and support fundraising delivery across prospecting, proposal development, donor stewardship and team operations. The Development Officer will keep the fundraising engine running by coordinating the key processes and systems that underpin effective operations. Additionally, they will help identify new funding opportunities, coordinate and contribute to high-quality funding proposals and donor reporting and support the management of donor relationships. This is a varied and collaborative role offering excellent development opportunities for an early-career fundraiser looking to build experience across the full fundraising cycle. The role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail, excellent communication skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and global environment.
ABOUT YOU
We are seeking an efficient and proactive fundraising professional with excellent communication and relationship-building skills, alongside strong coordination and operational capabilities. A true team player, you maintain composure and sound judgement in a fast-paced environment, and you approach challenges with optimism and pragmatism. You excel at managing deadlines, systems and processes, and enjoy researching and identifying new funding opportunities and supporting the development of compelling fundraising proposals, donor communications and stewardship activities.
You are comfortable working with a range of stakeholders and can manage multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail. You are collaborative, curious and motivated to learn, and you take a solutions-focused approach to your work. You are committed to Girls Not Brides' mission and values and are excited by the opportunity to contribute to an ambitious fundraising strategy that supports efforts to end child marriage globally.
Job location
Nairobi (Kenya) or New Delhi (India)
Working as a global team, all Girls Not Brides’ team members may from time to time be expected to work outside normal working hours (e.g., early morning or early evening); this is not a regular occurrence and is only to accommodate collaboration of teams across different time zones. This role may require occasional international travel to support events, as necessary.
Accountable To
Development Manager
Salary range
Market competitive based on a detailed survey by the Birches Group of comparable national NGO salaries in selected location. Payments will be made in local currency of where it is located.
Contract
This is a fixed term contract for 2 years. The successful candidate must have the right to work in India or Kenya at the time of applying, and for the full duration of the two-year contract.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Fundraising Coordination, Systems & Delivery
Ensure effective fundraising delivery by tracking deadlines and reporting requirements, maintaining accurate donor and prospect records, and supporting high-quality data, reporting and workflow management across fundraising systems (Excel, Monday.com).
Contribute to the identification, development and continuous improvement of team systems, tools, and processes.
Support the preparation and implementation of donor-facing and fundraising-related events, including developing briefing materials and coordinating logistics.
Coordinate updates and inputs from the Development Team for internal communications, including the Whole Team Newsletter, and organise inductions sessions for new starters.
Prospecting, Pipeline Development & Conversion
Research, identify, and monitor prospective funders aligned with Girls Not Brides’ strategy and funding priorities, supporting relationship development and cultivation activities.
Contribute to prospect qualification and ranking, providing recommendations for pursuit and/or prioritisation.
Maintain and update prospect pipeline records, ensuring prospect information, engagement activities and next steps are accurately captured and monitored.
Conduct due diligence on prospective donors to ensure value alignment.
Carry out desk-based research, including monitoring and analysing child marriage and gender equality funding trends, to inform prospecting, positioning and organisational understanding of funding landscape.
Coordinate and support non-grant income opportunities including individual/partnership donations, engaging relevant stakeholders and providing recommendations for pursuit.
Donor Relationship Management
Support the stewardship of a portfolio of philanthropic donors, acting as a trusted and consistent point of contact as required.
Contribute to the development and submission of high-quality funding proposals and concept notes, working closely with relevant team members from across the organisation to coordinate technical, financial and MEL inputs.
Contribute to the renewals of existing grants, coordinating inputs from relevant teams.
Support donor compliance for restricted and unrestricted funding, ensuring timely, accurate and high-quality narrative and financial reporting.
Ensure contractual and policy obligations are met across the organisation (e.g. branding, PSEAH, safeguarding reporting), working with teams to support compliance.
Contribute to shared communications and updates with the wider donor community.
Support representation of Girls Not Brides in donor and partner meetings, briefings and events, contributing to relationship building and positioning.
Wider Organisational Responsibilities
Commit to the mission and vision of Girls Not Brides, putting these at the forefront of all planning, work and actions.
Uphold the core values of Girls Not Brides in all areas of work and interactions with colleagues, members, partners and other stakeholders.
Comply with Girls Not Brides’ policies and processes, particularly around safeguarding, diversity and inclusion, the code of conduct and data protection.
Commit to ongoing personal development and learning.
Fulfil any other reasonable requests for the advancement of Girls Not Brides.
PERSON SPECIFICATION
Essential
Experience in a development, fundraising, or partnerships role in the not-for-profit sector.
Strong organisational and project management skills, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple workstreams, priorities and deadlines.
Experience using CRM systems, databases or fundraising tracking tools.
Experience contributing to funding proposals, donor reports or other fundraising communications.
Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information and present it clearly and persuasively for different audiences.
Excellent interpersonal and relationship-management skills, with the ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders across a global team and engage external stakeholders and internal colleagues.
Strong research and analytical skills, including experience gathering and interpreting information from a range of sources.
Strong commitment to the mission and values of Girls Not Brides.
Proactive, solutions‑focused, and able to exercise sound judgement and discretion.
Comfortable working flexibly across time zones and priorities.
Desirable
Experience working on child marriage, girls’ rights or gender equality.
Understanding of charity fundraising and trends within the broader development and philanthropic landscape.

Job Description:
Role purpose
To provide strategic leadership and operational integration across AGRA’s corporate-services portfolio—including Finance, People & Culture, Procurement, Administration, Information Technology, Grants Management, Facilities and Enterprise Risk Management—to enable efficient, effective and sustainable delivery of AGRA’s mission and strategic objectives.
The role ensures that corporate-service strategies, systems, processes, resources, and performance priorities are integrated and aligned with the approved operating model, while preserving the functional accountability, professional independence, and delegated authorities of the respective functional leaders.
Role Summary
The Chief Operating Officer at AGRA provides strategic and operational leadership to strengthen organisational effectiveness and ensure the seamless delivery of corporate services that enable programmatic impact across Africa. Reporting to the President and serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO leads integrated operational planning, cross-functional performance and delivery of the approved operating model across the corporate-services portfolio.
Operating through a matrix-management model, the COO provides executive coordination and operational-performance oversight across Finance, People & Culture, Procurement, Administration, Information Technology, Grants Management, Facilities and Enterprise Risk Management. The CFO and Chief People & Culture Officer retain functional leadership, professional independence, delegated authority and accountability for their respective mandates, including appropriate direct access and escalation to the President and relevant Board or Board Committee structures.
The COO leads initiatives to improve resource utilisation, operational efficiency, digital and business transformation, enterprise risk management and compliance with donor, regulatory and organisational requirements. The role ensures the timely coordination, escalation and implementation of agreed actions on material operational, financial, people, risk, compliance, audit and control matters, in accordance with AGRA’s delegated-authority, governance and Board-reporting frameworks. Internal Audit remains independent of management and retains its direct reporting and escalation access to the Board or relevant Board Committee.
Key Measures of Performance
The performance of this role holder will be assessed based on the achievements made on:
Operational Excellence & Service Delivery: Ensure effective delivery of corporate services by achieving agreed service-level standards, improving operational efficiency, and implementing process optimization initiatives that enhance organizational performance.
Governance, Risk & Compliance: Maintain robust governance, enterprise risk management, and compliance frameworks across corporate functions, ensuring strict adherence to organizational policies, donor requirements, regulatory obligations, and the swift, systematic resolution of internal and external audit and control findings while respecting Board assurance independence.
Financial Stewardship & Budget Discipline: Drive organizational cost optimization, strict budget adherence, and value-for-money outcomes in close operational matrix partnership with Finance, enforcing proactive cost-control mechanisms and operational efficiency across all corporate service units.
Technology, AI & Business Transformation: Lead operational and digital transformation initiatives, leveraging AI-enabled tools, data, and modern business systems alongside appropriate risk and governance frameworks to strengthen organizational capabilities, efficiency, and business continuity.
Grant Prudence & Effectiveness: Ensure effective stewardship of grant resources through strong grant management, compliance, monitoring, and reporting practices, maximizing the impact, efficiency, and accountability of donor-funded investments.
People & Culture Leadership: Foster a high-performing, inclusive, and value-driven culture by overseeing operational HR execution, talent development, workforce planning, and employee engagement, while supporting executive and FHRC governance priorities.
Leadership & Stakeholder Effectiveness: Build and sustain high-performing teams, foster a culture of accountability and collaboration, and maintain strong stakeholder satisfaction through responsive, reliable, and effective operational support services.
Major Duties and Responsibilities
Purpose – Advance
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of AGRA’s operational functions, ensuring alignment with organizational strategy, growth objectives, and program delivery priorities.
Lead the development and implementation of operational strategies, frameworks, policies, and systems that strengthen organizational effectiveness and sustainability.
Oversee enterprise-wide operational excellence initiatives, driving continuous improvement, efficiency gains, and service quality across corporate functions.
Direct the development and implementation of governance, risk management, compliance, and business continuity frameworks to safeguard organizational assets and reputation.
Lead organization-wide operational transformation and digital enablement initiatives to improve service delivery, decision-making, and scalability.
Oversee resource planning and optimization to ensure effective utilization of financial, human, technological, and physical resources.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Executive Leadership Team on operational performance, organizational capacity, and emerging risks.
Build and maintain strategic partnerships with donors, development partners, regulators, and service providers to strengthen AGRA’s operational capabilities.
Provide executive coordination and oversight of enterprise workforce and organisational-capability priorities, ensuring that people strategies, workforce plans, leadership pipelines and culture initiatives are aligned with AGRA’s strategy, operating model and resource plans.
Champion a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and operational excellence across the organization.
Develop leadership capability and succession pipelines within operational and corporate services functions.
Support change management, executive onboarding, and ensure operational continuity during top-level leadership transitions.
Enable integrated planning across Finance, People & Culture and other corporate-service functions, ensuring alignment of workforce plans, budgets, organisational design, capacity requirements and operational priorities.
Hold the corporate-services portfolio accountable for agreed enterprise outcomes, service standards, cross-functional dependencies and delivery of approved operational plans, without displacing the functional mandates or delegated authorities of the CFO and Chief People & Culture
Escalate material operational, financial, people, compliance and delivery risks to the President and relevant governance structures in accordance with AGRA’s approved escalation and delegated-authority framework.
Engagement – Position
Lead and coordinate operational support functions, including administration, procurement, facilities, information technology, grants management, and enterprise risk management.
Collaborate with business units and program teams to ensure operational services effectively support program delivery and organizational priorities.
Drive cross-functional initiatives aimed at improving business processes, service delivery, and stakeholder experience.
Provide executive coordination across Finance, People & Culture and Program teams to ensure integrated organisational planning, aligned resource allocation, workforce capacity and effective execution of AGRA’s strategy.
Build strong relationships with country, regional, and headquarters teams to ensure consistent and effective operational support.
Guide the implementation of operational policies, procedures, and standards across the organization.
Foster collaboration and knowledge sharing across operational functions to promote organizational learning and continuous improvement.
Lead and mentor high-performing operational teams, ensuring alignment with AGRA’s culture and values.
Ensure effective stakeholder engagement and communication on operational priorities, risks, and performance.
Work through the CFO and Chief People & Culture Officer to align financial, people and operational plans; resolve cross-functional dependencies; monitor delivery against agreed priorities; and escalate material issues that require executive or Board-level attention.
Maintain a matrix relationship with the CFO and Chief People & Culture Officer that balances enterprise integration and operational accountability with their functional leadership, professional independence and delegated decision-making authority.
Support the President in ensuring that the CFO and Chief People & Culture Officer have appropriate access to the Board, FHRC and other relevant Board committees on matters within their functional remit.
Coordinate management’s response to material audit, risk, compliance and control findings, while ensuring that Internal Audit retains independence from management and direct reporting and escalation access to the Board or the relevant Board committee.
Delivery – Corporate Planning
Lead the development and monitoring of the operational strategy and annual operational plans in alignment with AGRA’s strategic objectives.
Oversee operational budgeting, resource allocation, and performance monitoring across corporate functions.
Establish and monitor key operational performance indicators, service standards, and organizational effectiveness metrics.
Drive the implementation of operational improvement initiatives and track realization of efficiency and cost optimization benefits.
Lead scenario planning, risk assessments, and business continuity preparedness to enhance organizational resilience.
Ensure operational priorities, investments, and initiatives are aligned with AGRA’s growth ambitions and long-term sustainability goals.
Develop management dashboards and operational reports to support executive decision-making.
Monitor emerging trends, technologies, and leading practices to identify opportunities for innovation and enhanced operational effectiveness.
Evaluate the effectiveness of operational systems and processes and implement improvements where required.
Ensure timely reporting on operational performance, risk, compliance, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership and governance bodies.
Lead an integrated annual planning and performance-management cycle across corporate services, ensuring alignment between organisational strategy, budgets, workforce plans, operating plans, service standards and risk-management priorities.
Ensure that Finance and People & Culture performance plans, budgets and key measures are integrated into enterprise planning and reviewed through the agreed management-performance cycle, while technical and professional accountability remains with the respective functional leader.
Review, with the CFO, enterprise financial performance, forecasts, resource utilisation, budget variances and cost-management actions; ensure timely executive attention and corrective action on material issues.
Review, with the Chief People & Culture Officer, workforce capacity, leadership capability, succession, employee engagement, performance and culture indicators; ensure that material workforce risks and organisational-capability gaps are addressed through agreed actions.
Ensure that material financial, people, operational, risk, compliance, audit and control matters are appropriately escalated to the President, Executive Leadership Team and relevant Board or Board Committee structures in line with approved governance protocols.
Profile
Education
Master’s degree in business administration (MBA), Operations Management, Public Administration, Finance, Supply Chain Management, Organizational Leadership, International Development, or a related field.
Relevant Experience
Minimum 20 years of progressive leadership experience in operations, corporate services, business management, or organizational effectiveness.
At least 15 years in a senior leadership role managing multiple operational functions.
Demonstrated experience leading large and geographically dispersed teams in a multi-national development organization, international NGO, foundation, multilateral institution, or private-sector organization of comparable complexity.
Proven experience overseeing one or more of the following functions: finance, procurement, administration, technology, facilities, grants management, risk management, and business continuity.
Experience driving organizational transformation, operational excellence, business process improvement, and digital transformation initiatives.
Strong track record in governance, risk management, compliance, and operational performance management.
Experience managing organizational budgets, resource planning, and performance reporting.
Proven track record in enforcing organizational budget discipline, cost optimization, and successfully resolving complex audit and control findings in international or development environments.
Experience operating within the non profit sector, scaling development initiatives through government systems, or managing the operational complexities of climate/agri-food funding structures.
Demonstrated ability to influence executive leadership, Boards, donors, and other senior stakeholders.
Experience operating in Africa and working across multiple countries and cultures.

Company Details: Médecins sans frontières (MSF) or Doctors Without Borders, is an international humanitarian-aid non-governmental organization (NGO) and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, best known for its projects in war-torn regions and developing countries facing endemic diseases. It was founded in Fra...read morence in response to the Biafran War. The organization is known in most of the world by its localized name or simply as MSF; in Canada and the United States the name Doctors Without Borders is commonly used. In 2015 over 30,000, mostly local, doctors, nurses and other medical professionals, logistical experts, water and sanitation engineers and administrators provided medical aid in over 70 countries. Job Description:
Main Purpose
Lead an antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) program in a medical and surgical humanitarian hospital. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) / Doctors Without Borders has increased its focus on the problem of antibiotic resistance. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is growing rapidly in low and middle-income countries and MSF faces ongoing challenges managing antibiotic resistant infections in hospitalized patients particularly in patients with burns, trauma, hospital infections and in pediatric and neonatal care. AMR threatens patient outcomes, makes hospitals less safe and increases costs. MSF is committed to responding and one part of this response is to increase efforts to conserve the effectiveness of antibiotics through antibiotic stewardship.
Accountabilities
Medical doctors tasks In addition to Antimicrobial Stewardship Focal Point tasks
Leading, promoting and supporting antimicrobial stewardship efforts in the healthcare facility(s) across the spectrum of healthcare.
Establish and participate in a multidisciplinary Antimicrobial Stewardship (AS)committee (that meets regularly with Terms of Reference).
Identify antimicrobial stewardship priorities together with the AS committee and the mission.
Monitor, collect and analyze the antimicrobial data reported to the multidisciplinary AS committee.
Conduct regular audits relevant to stewardship priorities. This might include audits of antibiotic use, treatment of select conditions, indications for microbiology testing, and communication of results.
Provide feedback to the project and the mission regarding results of audits and plan improvements.
Co-ordinate and deliver education to other medical, nursing and pharmacy staff around stewardship.
Support other clinical staff regarding antibiotic choices and regularly participate in clinical rounds.
Liaise with the laboratory for timely communication of results (where relevant), interpretation of results and feedback to clinicians.
Collaborate with lab + IPC to prospectively monitor pathogens of concern and respond to hospital outbreaks including outbreaks of multidrug resistant organisms/bacteria (MDRO).
Identify opportunities to improve stewardship in the project (e.g., therapeutic drug monitoring, OPAT).
Participate in relevant project level committees (e.g., IPC, Quality improvement, Morbidity + Mortality reviews).
In collaboration with IPC and the clinical team, participate in detection, management and prevention of healthcare associated infections.
Requirements
Education:
Essential: Medical Doctor degree registered with the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council (KMPDC) with a valid practicing licence.
Desirable: Completed on-line training in Antimicrobial stewardship [e.g. BSAC (British Society of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy) and/or WHO (World Health Organisation)]
Experience:
Essential: At least 5 years’ experience in working as a medical doctor in inpatient settings.
Desirable: Experience in reviewing medical records/reviewing appropriateness of antimicrobials
Languages:
English Essential & Swahili Desirable
Knowledge:
Essential: Have a working understanding of key pathogens, their usual antibiotic susceptibilities, typical clinical presentations, and empiric or targeted treatment.
Have a working understanding of the modes of action of antimicrobials including their spectrum of activity.
Have a working understanding of the key principles of infection prevention and control (IPC) and the relationship between IPC and AMR (Antimicrobial Resistance).
Have a working understanding of the appropriate use of antimicrobials to prevent the emergence of resistance and avoidance of adverse effects.
Have a working understanding of the use of diagnostic tests in the investigation and management of infectious diseases. How to use data for feedback and reporting.
Desirable:
Understanding of behaviour change principles.
Able to provide face to face feedback to prescribers about antibiotic prescriptions.

Job Title: RFP-Development of AI Powered Entrepreneur Training Support Platform
Job Description:
Objective of the Assignment
Inkomoko is transitioning from a human-mediated service delivery model to a digitally scaled service model, to improve the client experience, enhance the quality and consistency of entrepreneur training, and reduce the operational burden currently placed on frontline Business Advisors, trainers, and support staff.
Clients and staff currently rely heavily on Relationship Managers, trainers, and support staff for:
Basic product and policy questions
Loan balance and repayment enquiries
Training in products and systems
Routine support issues
This dependency leads to delays, inconsistent messaging, and a high manual workload on Inkomoko’s field and support teams — constraining the organisation’s ability to scale its entrepreneur programs across new regions and cohorts.
Inkomoko is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to design, develop, commission, and provide ongoing maintenance and support for an AI-powered platform (the “Platform”) that will:
Deliver structured, interactive AI-driven training that guides entrepreneurs progressively through the four stages of the Inkomoko entrepreneur journey: Ideation, Investment Readiness, Business Planning and Market Entry;
Provide 24/7 automated customer support and FAQ handling;
Respond securely to loan and financial product enquiries;
Integrate with Inkomoko’s core systems (including the Core Banking System (CBS), Inkobook, and the PBI reporting dashboard);
Enforce role-based access, data privacy, and full audit control.
Scope of Work
The Platform being procured through this RFP must digitise and scale Inkomoko’s existing, field-tested Program Design. This design guides an entrepreneur through a structured, sequential journey of training modules paired with in-person or remote consulting visits. Each module builds on the previous one, combining skills training with structured advisory data collection that informs the client’s next stage of readiness.
Idea-Stage Track (Primary Focus of this Platform)
The Idea-stage track takes an entrepreneur from a business idea to market entry across four sequential modules; each paired with a consulting visit:
Module 1 – Business Ideation
Module 2 – Investment Readiness
Module 3 – Business Planning
Module 4 – Market Entry
Existing Business (Growth) Track — Future Scalability Context
Inkomoko also runs a parallel Existing Business (EB) track across five (5) consulting visits namely:
Investment Readiness
Bookkeeping
Business Model Canvas
Sales
Marketing
While the primary scope of this RFP is the Idea-Stage journey, the Platform's information architecture, content model, and workflow engine must be designed so that the EB track and any future cohort tracks can be configured and onboarded without requiring a re-architecture of the Platform. Vendors should describe in their proposal how their solution supports this configurability (see Section 6.5).
Supporting Tools in the Current Program
Inkomoko's current program relies on the following tools, which the Platform must be capable of integrating or interoperating with:
Inkobook – training attendance and consulting record system
PBI Dashboard – reporting and analytics
Digital Bookkeeping tools
Analog Bookkeeping (booklet-based) records, for clients without digital access

Job Description:
THE ROLE
TREES is seeking a dynamic, entrepreneurial leader to build and deploy our market integration strategy. This role bridges the gap between farm-level programming and viable market access, ensuring smallholder farmers have the information and resources needed to meet market demands (product / variety, quality, timing, and volume) for high-margin agricultural products while advancing long-term land restoration outcomes. The Director will help identify and navigate tradeoffs between commercial opportunity and environmental objectives, ensuring both farmer prosperity and landscape regeneration remain central to program design. Beyond setting strategy, the Director will guide the design, implementation, and evaluation of market integration partnerships across all of our programs.
We partner with over 30,000 smallholder farmers in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, delivering extension services, inputs, and financing through our network of last mile project officers. As we expand our impact, we are integrating market mechanisms to ensure farmers not only grow sustainably but thrive economically. The ideal candidate brings private sector experience aligning commercial agricultural opportunities with the needs and perspectives of smallholder farming communities, a track record of developing market access partnerships in multiple value chains, financial acumen, and an existing network within East African agricultural markets.
This is a full-time, individual contributor role reporting to the Technical Director, Programs Department, and partnering closely with peers in each country. Frequent regional travel is required, and existing permanent work authorization in one of Kenya, Tanzania, or Uganda is required.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Strategy & Pilot Development
Assess our current programs, including farmer engagement models, types of farmers, existing market touch points, and long-term aims of farmers and the organization vis-a-vis our carbon financing program, and develop a fit-for-purpose strategic approach to market integration.
Evaluate the implications of market integration opportunities on both farmer profitability and restoration outcomes, and recommend approaches that optimize long-term value across both objectives.
Design and lead TREES’ market integration roadmap across East Africa, in coordination with country program teams and technical advisors, to ensure integration with country-level programmatic approach, on-the-ground reality, and farmer and market readiness.
Identify and prioritize market intervention entry points (i.e. financing, inputs access, offtake aggregation, transport, cold chain, branding), and develop and execute rapid pilots to get to proof of concept (or disprove concepts).
Collaborate with in-country Markets and Value Chain staff, Country Directors, Field Program Leads, research and evaluation staff, and other relevant teams to embed market thinking into core programming; pilot and evaluate new ideas and solutions, and identify high-potential options to scale up.
Farmer Economics & Financial Leadership
Develop tools and analyses (e.g. simplified farmer-level P&L models and organizational-level business propositions) that assess both farm enterprise performance and restoration impacts to support strategic investment and program decisions.
Support the design of bundled financial products (e.g. input financing, insurance, forward contracts) to facilitate end market access.
Analyze deal structures, leverage regular farmer input and feedback, and negotiate contracts with buyers, processors, and service providers as a trusted partner to farmers.
Partnerships & Ecosystem Engagement
Build strategic partnerships with cooperatives, exporters, agri-tech firms, and buyers.
Engage with private sector actors to co-create structural market access approaches.
Represent TREES in value chain forums, trade associations, and other relevant industry networks.
Data & Market Intelligence
Identify, create, or otherwise activate market data collection systems to ensure TREES and the farmers we serve understand demand, price points, volume requirements, and quality standards to inform agricultural programming.
Integrate market and restoration performance data to inform recommendations on crops, production systems, and market opportunities.
Work closely with training and agricultural extension teams to ensure market intelligence is adequately translated and disseminated to farmers, and that extension staff have the information and know-how to support farm-level decision-making in line with market requirements.
WHO YOU ARE
An enthusiastic advocate for TREES’ mission and values. You are inspired to work alongside farming families building vibrant regional economies, thriving food systems, and a healthier planet. You thrive on a close-knit team that values shared integrity, inclusive collaboration, sustainable resilience, and continuous learning.
A commercially seasoned agribusiness professional. You understand how buyers, processors, exporters, and service providers actually make decisions, and you know how to make a case that holds up on both sides of a deal.
A connector who puts farmers at the center. You carry an existing network of relevant agribusiness actors in the region and negotiate as a trusted partner to farmers, grounding every deal in their input, feedback, and long-term interest.
Financially fluent and comfortable with numbers. You can build a simple farmer-level model and a credible organizational business proposition and use both to make a clear recommendation.
A strategist who balances prosperity with restoration. You can hold two objectives at once, demonstrating the ability to balance farmer profitability with land restoration goals and to make sound, transparent recommendations where tradeoffs exist. You look for the approaches that create long-term value across both.
An entrepreneurial builder who learns by testing. You combine strategic thinking with detailed orientation to connect strategy to on-the-ground implementation. You design rapid pilots, get proof of concept quickly, and are equally willing to disprove an idea and move on.
A strong communicator and relationship builder. You are a natural collaborator with the ability to lead through influence across diverse teams, geographies, and cultures. You have a warm, energetic, and authentic personality that translates to lasting relationships with farmers, colleagues, and commercial partners alike.
ROLE REQUIREMENTS
Required
8+ years of experience in private sector engagement within key agricultural value chains in East Africa.
Demonstrated combination of strategic thinking, the ability to drive change at a program level, and detail orientation to connect strategies to on-the-ground implementation.
Proven track record in connecting smallholder farmers to durable market opportunities, and an existing network of relevant agribusiness actors in the region.
Commercial financial skills: P&L modeling exposure, deal structuring, and contract negotiation.
Excellent stakeholder engagement and partnership-building skills; a natural collaborator and communicator with the ability to lead with influence across diverse teams and cultures.
Preferred
Demonstrated ability to balance farmer profitability with land restoration objectives and make sound recommendations where tradeoffs exist.
Experience with agricultural product differentiation and certifications, i.e., regenerative agriculture, organic certification, or carbon neutral claims.
Exposure to digital traceability or agri-tech platforms.
MBA, Master’s in Agribusiness, Economics, or a related field.

Job Description:
Role Purpose
Power Financial Wellness is seeking a Group Financial Controller to own the group’s reporting engine across a multi-entity fintech: a Delaware parent (PFW Inc.) over operating entities in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and India, plus partnership and JV markets across Africa. This role owns the US parent-entity accounting, the monthly multi-entity consolidation and intercompany, and — critically — the accurate and complete booking of JV and partnership revenue. You will be the person who makes the numbers come together correctly each month across every entity, working directly with the Group CFO and CEO.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role at the center of a lean finance team, with real ownership from day one as the group scales through Series A and beyond. Because the team is deliberately lean, the role is broad — beyond the reporting core it takes on planning, cash-flow and treasury coordination, with support from the CFO.
You will partner with — but not manage — the country finance managers (Kenya, Uganda) and accountants (Tanzania, Rwanda) and our outsourced India provider, collating their submissions on the group timetable. You report to the Group CFO, which keeps sign-off on the consolidated and US numbers independent of any single country.
Key Responsibilities
US Entity & Parent-Company Close
Own PFW Inc. (Delaware) accounting end-to-end — booking intercompany funding, holding-company costs and accruals, and running US payments.
Keep the parent ledger tidy and audit-ready, with clear working papers.
JV & Partnership Revenue
Own the accurate and complete booking of JV and partnership revenue and income across the group — with lenders, Sacco’s, banks, and other partners — recognized in the right entity, period, and account.
Reconcile partner statements and settlement data to the ledger and resolve differences, so revenue and revenue-share are correctly recorded; maintain clear audit trails for every arrangement.
Act as the central reporting home for partnership and JV markets where the group serves customers but has no local entity.
Group Consolidation & Reporting
Run the monthly group consolidation — collating entity submissions into the consolidated income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow.
Own intercompany and eliminations, foreign-currency translation, and reconciling intercompany balances so they clear cleanly across entities.
Help prepare the monthly board and investor pack — group KPIs, revenue mix, cash, burn and runway — and maintain robust reconciliations for group cash, the loan book, and third-party debt.
Product-Line Reporting
Maintain group reporting by product line — Pay, Borrow, Save, and Insurance / Protect — tracking revenue, margin and KPIs, and standing up reporting for each new product from launch (chart-of-accounts mapping, recognition treatment, disclosures).
Close, Audit, & Series A
Run the group month-end close to a fixed timetable, hit deadlines, and help tighten the calendar over time.
Prepare supporting schedules and evidence for the annual group and entity audits and support Series A diligence and the data room.
Planning, Treasury, & Process
Help build and maintain the group budget and rolling forecast with monthly variance analysis; own the short-term (13-week) cashflow forecast and track runway.
Help keep the group model and investor five-year plan current and build unit-economics and KPI reporting.
Support cash and treasury across entities and currencies; coordinate local tax and statutory filings and transfer-pricing documentation with country teams and advisors; strengthen controls and processes in Microsoft Dynamics 365.
Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is a qualified accountant who has worked hands-on across multiple entities and is comfortable being the sole technical owner of the group numbers in a lean team. They are accurate, organized, and diligent, genuinely bothered by items that don’t reconcile, and keen to take on more as the group scales.
Essential
Qualification: A bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field, together with a completed professional accounting qualification (CPA(K), ACCA, CA, or equivalent). Candidates who are finalists and close to completing their professional qualification may also be considered.
Experience: around 6 – 9 years, including hands-on exposure to multi-entity consolidation and intercompany — having owned a consolidation end-to-end is a strong plus.
Accounting: solid IFRS knowledge including revenue recognition, and confidence with multi-currency / FX translation.
Close discipline: a demonstrable track record of hitting month-end close deadlines to a fixed calendar.
Tools & rigor: strong Excel and a controls / audit-trail mindset; experience in leveraging AI
Desirable
Experience booking partnership / revenue-share or JV income, ideally in fintech, lending or banking.
US entity / US GAAP or Delaware parent-company exposure; Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365); FP&A and financial modelling; and experience across African markets in a high-growth or start-up environment.

Job Description:
About the role
The Senior Technical Program Manager owns end-to-end delivery of technology initiatives and raises the standard for how we plan, build, and ship. Taking a structured, data-driven view of the delivery lifecycle, you'll re-engineer how teams prioritise, build, test, and release to drive predictability and consistency , bringing clear plans, honest reporting, managed risk, and a focus on unblocking teams.
Contribution & Impact
This role is critical to the efficient, predictable, and high-quality delivery of our core lending, value store & transfer, and data platforms. The role will improve delivery velocity, predictability, and the timely deployment of growth-enabling capabilities. It does this by improving how our systems and processes fit together, and by coordinating execution across teams and dependencies rather than owning a single delivery lane. Success will be measured by on-time and cost-effective delivery of key initiatives, improved delivery cycle times, effective management of dependencies and risks, platform stability and performance, and maintaining architectural alignment towards a shared and scalable target state.
Key responsibilities
Project leadership and delivery orchestration
Own the delivery of large, multi-team technology programs from definition through to production, including platform modernisation, data initiatives, cloud and AI-enabled systems.
Define, document and agree program deliverables, requirements, resourcing and success criteria with technology and business stakeholders.
Coordinate across Engineering, QA, Platform, teams to sequence work, manage dependencies and remove blockers.
Maintain a clear, honest view of delivery health, surfacing risks and issues to Technology leadership early and with a recommended course of action.
Establish technical governance frameworks that balance delivery speed with long-term architectural scalability.
Architectural direction and technical standards
Work with the Technology Delivery Director to define and communicate the target architecture for the lending, data and customer value platforms, and translate it into a sequenced, deliverable roadmap.
Ensure non-functional requirements (resilience, high availability, performance, security, observability, data quality) are designed in and delivered.
Identify systemic architectural risk and technical debt, make its cost visible, and get remediation into the plan.
Evaluate and pilot emerging technologies and practices, including AI-enabled and cloud-native tooling, where they serve the business.
Transform manual or fragmented delivery processes into scalable, data-driven systems that empower teams to ship with confidence.
Process engineering and Agile enablement
Champion the adoption of Agile practices across Technology and partner business teams, adapting them pragmatically to Ezra's context rather than applying frameworks by the book.
Introduce and facilitate the ceremonies that matter – planning, reviews, retrospectives – and coach teams and stakeholders on the principles behind them.
Diagnose where the delivery system is failing: handoffs, approval bottlenecks, unclear ownership, weak requirements, poor estimation — and redesign the process to fix it.
Define and monitor delivery metrics (throughput, cycle time, predictability, escaped defects) and use them to drive real improvement, not reporting theatre.
Drive consistency in documentation, workflows and technical decision-making across programs.
Team leadership and mentorship
Mentor and support engineers and technical leads in planning, estimation, risk management and stakeholder communication.
Foster a culture of transparency, accountability, technical rigor and continuous improvement.
Stakeholder communication and reporting
Develop and agree stakeholder and communication plans for each major program.
Provide structured, decision-useful updates on progress, risk and dependency to leadership and, where relevant, to partners and customers.
Manage expectations and maintain alignment between technical teams and business stakeholders, including when the message is unwelcome.
Governance, risk and compliance
Establish and run appropriate governance forums, with proportionate rigor enough control to be safe, not so much that delivery stalls.
Proactively identify systemic delivery and operational risk, drive alignment on categorization and treatment, and co-own the outcome.
Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT or a related field.
7+ years of experience in technical program, project or delivery management , Architecture, team management within software or platform engineering environments, including experience running multi-team programmes.
An engineering background, significant time spent as a software engineer, architect or technical lead, with strong expertise in at least one and familiarity with several programming languages.
Demonstrated ability to lead and improve delivery processes, including guiding teams or organizations through Agile adoption or similar change.
Solid understanding of Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, XP) and the judgement to know when and how to apply them.
Proficiency with project and service management tooling (e.g. Jira, Confluence)
Experience leading or mentoring others, formally or informally.
Exceptional communication, facilitation and influencing skills, with a track record of driving complex technical decisions across multiple teams.
Preferred qualifications
Experience in a regulated FinTech, payments or financial services environment.
Experience delivering in high-volume, high-availability transactional environments.
Experience working across multiple countries, time zones or partner organizations.
Lifecycle Management: Experience driving end-to-end technical projects, managing product development lifecycles from conception/prototype to release or end-of-life
The ideal candidate is someone who
Think architecturally. Understands systems, not just schedules. Can define a target state, reason about how the pieces fit together, and see where the real technical and delivery risk sits.
Is technically credible. Earns the respect of senior engineers because they understand the work and have done it, not because of the title.
Engineers the process. Sees ways of working as a system to be diagnosed and improved, and has the discipline to measure whether the change worked.
Handles ambiguity. Comfortable being handed a poorly-defined problem, a hard deadline and competing stakeholders, and turning that into a plan.
Leads without needing authority. Builds alignment across engineering, product and business by influence, clarity and follow-through.
Is direct and honest. Surfaces bad news early with a recommendation attached. Does not manage an optimistic status report.
Develops people. Takes real satisfaction in growing a team and lifting the standard around them.
Embraces evolution. Stays current with industry practice and helps the organisation adopt new approaches — including AI and cloud-native tooling — without destabilising the core platform.

Job Description:
Trócaire seeks to recruit a dedicated Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Coordinator to support the organization’s MEAL and research functions, and other duties as assigned. The MEAL Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring a systematic approach to Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) in the Sudan Country Programme and will facilitate the development. The MEAL Coordinator will lead the design, coordination and continuous improvement of the Sudan Country Programme's MEAL system, ensuring that programme teams and partners collect, analyse, use and report high-quality evidence in a consistent way, while promoting accountability and learning to improve programme quality and impact, and implementation of the country programme MEAL system. Additionally, s/he will work closely with Trocaire partners’ MEAL Officers and will be responsible for supporting baseline surveys, formative and operational research, development of project MEAL plans, community feedback and accountability mechanisms and development of programme MEAL reports. The candidate will be able to provide responsive technical and programme support to partners operating in complex and access-constrained environments, identifying and supporting practical and innovative solutions to monitoring and data challenges. S/he will ensure that these tasks are functional and well grounded, strengthening coordination and collaboration with all programme team and partner staff, while ensuring that MEAL is visible within projects.
Key Responsibilities
MEAL System Design, Stewardship, and Management
·The MEAL Coordinator leads the design, implementation and continuous improvement of the country programme's MEAL system to ensure the consistent collection, analysis and use of quality evidence across all projects.
This includes:
Developing and maintaining the country programme MEAL framework, with accompanying relevant processes, tools and guidance.
Supporting the design of and quality assure project logframes, MEAL plans, indicator frameworks and IPTTs.
Establishing and maintaining tools and approaches (such as common indicators or priority approaches) for data collection, management, analysis and reporting.
Supporting the use of Kobo Toolbox as Trócaire’s digital data collection platform and support the use of other information management systems.
Ensuring programme monitoring systems are aligned with organisational requirements, donor expectations and sectoral standards (such as SPHERE, GBViE, CHS).
Supporting the Programme Team on measuring people reached as part of the organisational reporting.
Generate, manage, and support the use of key MEAL templates (such as Output Trackers, Indicator Tracking Tables, and Report Templates)
Programme Quality, Monitoring and Evidence Generation
The MEAL Coordinator ensures that project data is accurate, reliable and useful.
This includes:
Supporting routine monitoring and performance tracking across projects, including through supporting project leads and partner MEAL officers in maintaining Indicator Tracking Tables and other performance documentation.
In collaboration with Program Coordinators, conduct field visits to monitor programme activities against established quality frameworks through qualitative and quantitative methods. Generate and share reports with Programme Manager and the program team, supporting the use of data.
Leading or supporting data quality assessments and validation processes and providing recommendations for improvement to programme teams.
Supporting the design and management of project assessments, reviews and evaluations.
Analysing and synthesising data to identify trends, gaps, risks and opportunities.
Supporting programme teams to use monitoring data to adapt implementation and improve results.
Partner Support and Capacity Strengthening
The MEAL Coordinator works closely with partners to strengthen their MEAL capacities and support their MEAL practices.
This includes:
Conducting partner MEAL capacity assessments and supporting capacity strengthening plans (through existing resources and potential development of new resources).
Providing technical advice, coaching and mentoring on MEAL approaches, tools and systems.
Supporting partners to develop results frameworks and apply Results Based Management approaches in project documents and programme management.
Supporting partners in the use of digital data collection and analysis tools (primarily through Kobo Toolbox).
Strengthening partner capacity in data quality, evidence generation, reporting and learning.
Supporting joint planning, monitoring and reflection processes with partners.
Ensuring quality data collection through inclusive and representative strategies and the use of Washington Group short set practical tools, and other inclusion tools.
Accountability and Community Feedback
The MEAL Coordinator supports the strengthening of systems that enable communities and programme participants to provide feedback and hold the programme accountable.
This includes:
Support partners to operationalise community accountability in MEL mechanisms and forums as guided by the Field Coordinator.
Establishing and monitoring Trócaire Complaints and Response Mechanism in all sectors and components of the operations in the programme locations.
Managing complaints and feedback data and supporting appropriate referrals and follow-up through proper data management.
Assessing and strengthening community feedback systems through training.
Promoting the use of community feedback to improve programme quality and responsiveness.
Learning, Adaptation and Knowledge Management
This includes:
Embedding learning throughout the project cycle.
Facilitating reflection, learning and programme adaptation processes.
Identifying and promoting innovative and effective MEAL approaches. Learn from other organisational and external documented learning in rolling out new approaches and methods (e.g. digital data monitoring and innovative participatory M&E methods) and explore how to apply these in the region context.
Documenting and disseminating lessons learned, good practices and evidence of impact.
Supporting the development of case studies, learning products and knowledge-sharing resources.
Ensuring learning informs programme design, implementation and strategic decision-making.
Support the updating of programme data on Salesforce.
Adaptive Programming and Remote Partner Support
The MEAL Coordinator supports partners to maintain effective monitoring, accountability and learning systems in complex, insecure and rapidly changing operating environments.
This includes:
Providing technical support through both in-person and remote modalities.
Supporting partners to adapt MEAL approaches where access, security or operational constraints affect implementation.
Developing practical and innovative solutions to data collection, verification and learning challenges.
Ensuring evidence generation remains feasible, ethical and context appropriate in constrained environments.
Supporting programme teams and partners to use evidence for timely and adaptive decision-making.
Other Duties
Any other reasonable and relevant area of work that, in the opinion of management, is consistent with the role of MEAL Coordinator

Company Details: Established in 1952, the Aga Khan Hospital in Kisumu is part of the Aga Khan Health Services (AKHS). It is a 61-bed acute care facility managed by qualified professionals who include experienced, full-time resident doctors and consultants. The hospital's objectives are to provide high quality...read more, cost-effective health care to the population of Western Kenya and neighbouring countries. The Hospital provides general medicine services, specialist clinics and high-tech diagnostic services and has a well-equipped 24-hour emergency Casualty Department. It is also part of the AKHS international referral system, with links to the Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi and Karachi respectively. History On 26 February 1951, Prince Aly Khan laid the foundation for the Aga Khan Dispensary and Maternity Home. The home had an 8-bed general ward. In 1960, the dispensary was extended to incorporate two general wards with a total of 17 beds and an outpatient department. A small laboratory was established in 1975 and a portable X-ray machine purchased. Patient activity levels continued to increase. By 1979, the average bed occupancy was over 100 percent, which indicated a need for expansion. In 1991, the hospital had 55 beds, piped oxygen gas was available, an administration block was completed and physiotherapy services were introduced. By 1992, the bed capacity was increased to 76 with a paediatric ward, a VIP wing and an acute care unit. Presently the hospital offers services in the areas of Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, Obstetrics & Gynaecology and Acute Care. It also provides 24-hour emergency / ambulatory services. This is further supported by basic to intermediate specialised investigations both in laboratory and radiology and a well-stocked pharmacy, all on a 24-hour basis. The Hospital has introduced haemodialysis, dental, ophthalmology, endoscopy, histopathology and imaging services, including image-guided non-vascular intervention, CT scans and Doppler ultrasounds. The significant strengthening of the diagnostic departments has been through the recruitment of expatriate consultants from India a radiologist and a pathologist. Aga Khan Health Services AKHS has facilities in Kenya and Tanzania that provide care to over 600,000 patients annually in both rural and urban, and preventive and curative contexts. Its hospitals provide an increasingly comprehensive range of high-quality clinical services. Healthcare Activities of the Aga Khan Development Network AKHS activities are conducted in concert with other health-related activities of the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN). The overall aim is to raise the health status of people in East Africa and elsewhere in the developing world. In current projects, emphasis is on strengthening health systems development. The Aga Khan Foundation (AKF), with branches in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, works with a variety of grantees, including AKHS, to improve the health of vulnerable population groups, especially mothers and children, and promote health services development on the national and regional levels. AKF and AKHS have been joined in their work in health care in East Africa by the Aga Khan University's Faculty of Health Sciences, which offers accredited professional training, especially for nurses and doctors, and conducts a variety of research programmes focused on the health problems of developing nations. The AKDN aims to assist countries in the building of effective, sustainable health systems linking different kinds of services and levels of care. Company Details:
Longhorn Publishers limited is a public limited liability company wholly-owned and run by Kenyans. It was incorporated in Kenya in May 1965 as Longmans of Kenya a wholly owned subsidiary of Longman Group International of the United Kingdom. At that time, it was mainly a sales promotion office handli...read moreng Longman publications published in UK. In December 1969, the company changed name to Longman Kenya Limited. During the 1970s, a limited local publishing programme was started and, around the same time, a few Kenyans were invited to join the Board of Directors.

Following the opening up of Eastern Europe after the fall of the Berlin Wall, many multinationals shifted their focus from Africa to the new markets. In addition, in the 1990’s, Kenya’s then Minister for Education banned the importation of textbooks. This forced multinationals to consider other ways of supplying the Kenyan market, including licensing, which drastically reduced their margins (as compared to supplying stock). As a result, in the 1980s Longman UK sold 40% of its shareholding to Kenyans with a further 20% being sold in 1991. Finally.in 1993, Longman UK fully divested from the company when it sold its remaining 40% shareholding to Kenyans. As a result of this divestiture, the company changed its name to Longhorn Kenya Limited.

In 2006, Longhorn undertook a rebranding exercise aimed at revitalizing the company’s image through the publishing of non-textbook reading materials. To this end, in 2007, the company launched its Sasa Sema Imprint after acquiring the intellectual property of Sasa Sema Publications Limited. Sasa Sema provides reference books, creative works, biographies and general knowledge books to cater for the unmet needs within the general readership space and thus provide a balanced diet. This initiative was in line with the company’s strategy of diversifying its product range to Include books for general readership. Longhorn is the only publisher with full approval by the Ministry of Education in 12 key subjects for secondary and primary schools.

Job Description:
Job purpose:
The Total Rewards Associate is responsible for the accurate and timely execution of monthly payroll processing, statutory payment administration, third-party payment coordination, and benefits scheme operational support for all staff and Financial Advisors across the Group. The role is the operational engine of the Total Rewards team, ensuring that every payroll input is correctly captured, every statutory obligation is met, every third-party payment is processed on schedule, and every employee and FA query is handled professionally.
Key responsibilities:
Monthly Payroll Processing
Receive monthly payroll variation data from all stakeholders (HR, Finance, FA Operations, BU HR teams); sense-check data for accuracy and correct format before acceptance.
Return incomplete or incorrect variation files to originators with clear written guidance on what requires correction; follow up to obtain corrected files within the processing timeline.
Upload all approved monthly variation data into the payroll ERP module accurately and on schedule.
Perform pre-payroll processing checks, verifying that all inputs have been captured, that deductions are calculating correctly, and that the payroll is ready for the Senior Total Rewards Analyst review.
Extract post-payroll reports and prepare voluntary and statutory payment files for Finance; PAYE, SHIF, NSSF, SACCO savings, staff loans, and other deductions for review and approval.
Send approved post-payroll files to Finance and follow up to confirm payment processing within statutory deadlines.
Prepare monthly payroll reconciliations, balance sheet accounts and bank account reconciliations and submit to the Senior Total Reward Analyst for review and approval before sharing with Finance.
Statutory Compliance Administration
Log onto all applicable statutory online platforms; file monthly returns for NSSF, SHIF, and other applicable deductions per jurisdiction, within regulatory deadlines.
Prepare and share e-slips with Finance for payment of statutory liabilities immediately following payroll approval.
Monitor the validity of all statutory compliance certificates (NSSF, SHIF, NITA, and others); initiate the renewal process ahead of expiry and track through to receipt of the renewed certificate.
Conduct KRA PIN verification for all new staff and FA joiners; update the PIN register in the payroll ERP system promptly.
Manage SHIF card contribution queries, investigating missing deductions, liaising with the relevant authority, and confirming resolution within the agreed SLA.
Implement notified legislative changes affecting payroll and statutory deductions promptly upon instruction from the Supervisor.
Third-Party Payments & Schedules
Prepare accurate and timely monthly schedules for all third-party payroll deductions; SACCO savings, bank loan deductions, pension contributions, insurance premiums, and any other authorized deductions and submit to Finance for payment by the due date.
Follow up with Finance on all pending third-party payments; obtain and file payment confirmations.
Prepare out-of-payroll payment files as directed, loan cash cover, cashier bonds, final dues, Directors' fees, FA payments, and off-cycle salary advances and submit to the Supervisor for approval before passing to Finance.
FA Payroll & Scheme Administration
Prepare and share the monthly FA payroll register summary with the Total Rewards Analyst for commission validation.
Process routine FA payroll deductions and scheme updates in the payroll system as directed by the Total Rewards Analyst.
Respond to daily FA phone, email, and walk-in queries related to payroll deductions, benefits administration, and payment timelines; escalate compensation and commission queries to the Total Rewards Analyst.
Administer the annual FA loan and scheme deduction data in the payroll system, ensuring accuracy against the register maintained by the Total Rewards Analyst.
Payroll Variance Analysis Support
Prepare a monthly payroll variance summary, comparing current month to prior month across all entities and submit to the Total Rewards Analyst for analytical review and commentary.
Flag movements that appear anomalous e.g. unusual salary changes, unrecognized deductions, unexpected joiner or leaver counts at the point of preparation.
This first-pass commentary is the Analyst's starting point for the formal variance analysis submitted to the Supervisor, the Associate's active engagement with the data improves the quality of the full analysis.
Payroll Document Management
Ensure all monthly payroll records, variation files, payroll run reports, statutory payment evidence, reconciliations, and sign-off documentation are fully signed off and filed securely in the designated payroll folder on the day of completion.
Prepare and submit the monthly payroll filing schedule to the Supervisor; coordinate the transfer of physical / electronic documents to the registry by the approved schedule.
Maintain the payroll document register; ensure all records are retrievable for audit and management requests within the agreed turnaround time.
Support internal and external payroll audits; retrieving records, compiling documentation, and confirming completeness of payroll files as directed by the Supervisor.
Payroll Query Management
Serve as the first point of contact for routine employee payroll queries; deduction queries, payslip requests, P9 questions, and benefit deduction confirmations, resolving within the agreed SLA.
Escalate complex payroll queries the Senior Total Rewards Analyst with a clear summary of the issue.
Maintain a query log; track open items to resolution; report recurring query themes to the Supervisor monthly.
Any other duties that may be assigned from time to time
Knowledge, experience and qualifications required
Bachelor's Degree in Human Resources, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
Professional qualification in Finance or HR (e.g. CHRP, CPA, or equivalent).
2-4 years' experience in payroll administration, with demonstrated responsibility for the monthly payroll processing cycle and statutory filings.
Working knowledge of Kenyan statutory deduction requirements - NSSF, SHIF, HELB, Housing Levy, NITA.
Proficiency in payroll ERP systems and statutory online platforms (iTax, NSSF portal, SHIF portal).
Understanding of the payroll maker role within an internal controls framework.
Preferred
Experience processing payroll for a workforce of 500+ employees across multiple entities.
Exposure to FA payroll and commission deduction administration in an insurance or financial services environment.
Familiarity with GL reconciliation processes and payroll-to-Finance reporting.
Prior experience in a structured HR Shared Services or Total Rewards team.
Technical/ Functional competencies:
Payroll processing and statutory deduction administration - Kenya and Group entities.
Statutory compliance execution
FA payroll and scheme administration
Third-party payment processing
Payroll-to-Finance reconciliation support
HRIS and payroll ERP module administration
MS Office - intermediate to advanced Excel (payroll reconciliation, variance summaries); Word and Outlook proficiency.

The Operations Assistant is a practical, hands-on role supporting the day-to-day running of Natural State’s Centre for Nature Economy. Responsibilities will span facilities maintenance, cleaning and housekeeping, accommodation preparation, access and visitor management, programme and event set-up, stock and inventory management, supplies and deliveries, vehicles and transport, hospitality support and general operational administration.
The role requires someone who is dependable, organised, resourceful and comfortable undertaking practical and physical work as well as maintaining accurate operational records.
The postholder will help ensure that the Centre’s standard operating procedures, checklists and day-to-day operational controls are consistently followed.
The Operations Assistant will work closely with the Operations & Facilities Manager and wider Centre team, responding to operational needs as they arise and taking responsibility for completing assigned tasks to a high standard.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Centre Operations, Access & Visitor Support
Support the smooth day-to-day operation of the Centre and ensure facilities are ready for staff, learners and visitors.
Carry out routine opening, closing and operational checks and promptly report or address issues.
Manage day-to-day access to Centre facilities, including the secure issue and return of keys and maintenance of the key register.
Ensure visitor, contractor and supplier sign-in and sign-out procedures are followed and the visitor log is kept accurate and up to date.
Receive and direct visitors, contractors, suppliers and deliveries and provide appropriate site information.
Complete required operational checklists, logs and records and follow established Centre SOPs.
Facilities Maintenance & Upkeep
Carry out routine checks of buildings, accommodation, equipment, grounds and essential facilities and identify maintenance requirements.
Undertake basic maintenance and minor repairs within the postholder’s skills, including general repairs, minor painting, furniture repairs and replacement or adjustment of fittings.
Monitor water, electricity, sanitation and other essential facilities and promptly report faults.
Support planned and preventative maintenance and assist technicians and contractors undertaking specialist work.
Maintain tools, maintenance equipment and materials safely and in good order.
Maintain records of reported faults, maintenance requirements and completed work.
Cleaning, Housekeeping & Facility Preparation
Undertake cleaning and housekeeping of accommodation, classrooms, offices, bathrooms, communal areas and other Centre facilities.
Prepare and reset guest accommodation, including making beds, changing linen and replenishing supplies.
Prepare classrooms, meeting rooms and other spaces for training programmes, meetings, events and visitors, including arranging furniture and equipment.
Assist with laundry, linen management, waste management and general upkeep of Centre facilities and surrounding areas.
Support catering and hospitality activities, including setting up, serving, clearing and washing-up where required.
Maintain consistently clean, tidy and welcoming facilities.
Inventory, Stock, Stores & Supplies
This can absorb much of the duplication currently spread across sections 5, 6 and 10.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date inventory and stock records for Centre assets, equipment, consumables and supplies.
Receive and check deliveries, record stock received and issued, and ensure items are stored safely and appropriately.
Monitor stock levels and ensure replenishment requirements are identified in good time.
Carry out routine stock counts and support periodic inventory verification and reconciliation.
Ensure assets and equipment are appropriately recorded, labelled and accounted for and report missing, damaged or unserviceable items.
Maintain clean, secure and well-organised stores and storage areas.
Assist with approved local purchases, collections and deliveries and maintain relevant receipts and supporting documentation.
Vehicles, Transport & Operational Logistics

Carry out routine vehicle checks and report faults, damage or servicing requirements.
Ensure Centre vehicles are clean, appropriately equipped and ready for approved use.
Where appropriately licensed and authorised, drive Natural State vehicles for approved operational activities.
Undertake operational errands, collections and deliveries and assist with moving people, equipment and supplies as required.
Support practical logistics for programmes, meetings, events and other Centre activities.
Safety, Procedures & General Operational Support
Follow and implement Centre SOPs, health and safety requirements, security procedures and operational checklists.
Identify and promptly report hazards, incidents, unsafe conditions, security concerns and other operational issues.
Help ensure emergency equipment, first-aid supplies and safety signage are available and report servicing or replacement requirements.
Maintain accurate operational records and update relevant inventory, asset, maintenance and other systems as required.
