Job Description:
PURPOSE OF THE ROLE
BBC World Service is creating a new Horn of Africa Language Services Unit in Nairobi, bringing together BBC Amharic, BBC Afaan Oromo, BBC Tigrinya and BBC Somali under a single editorial leadership structure for the first time.
BBC Amharic is a trusted source of independent journalism for millions of Amharic speakers across Ethiopia and across a significant global diaspora.
WHY JOIN THE TEAM
As a Senior Journalist, you will play a leading role in shaping and delivering BBC Amharic's journalism across digital, video, audio and social platforms. Working closely with the Assistant Editor and colleagues across the Horn of Africa services, you will contribute to the service's digital transformation, helping to grow audiences while maintaining the highest editorial standards and audience trust.
This role combines strong journalistic judgement, creative storytelling and digital ambition. You will commission, create and deliver distinctive journalism that serves audiences with accuracy, impartiality and innovation across multiple platforms.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Contribute to BBC Amharic’s transition to a digital-first, video-led service by supporting a culture of editorial excellence, innovation, collaboration and continuous learning.
Produce, edit, commission and publish high-quality journalism across digital, video, social, audio and radio platforms, creating content that meets audience needs and platform behaviours.
Support the delivery of major news stories, special coverage, investigations, explainers and original journalism, helping to ensure timely, engaging and impactful output.
Use audience insights, analytics and performance data to inform content decisions and improve reach, relevance and audience engagement.
Work closely with colleagues across the Horn of Africa services and wider BBC teams to coordinate coverage, share knowledge and contribute to collaborative storytelling projects.
Support the development of digital storytelling, visual journalism and emerging content formats, particularly those that engage younger and underserved audiences.
Apply BBC Editorial Guidelines at all times, ensuring content meets the highest standards of accuracy, impartiality, fairness and compliance, and contribute to editorial decision-making within agreed parameters.
SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE
ESSENTIAL CRITERIA
Significant experience producing high-quality journalism in a fast-paced, multimedia news environment, with the ability to deliver accurate and engaging content to tight deadlines.
Strong editorial judgement and the ability to identify, develop and tell distinctive stories that resonate with target audiences.
Proven experience creating content for digital-first audiences, with a strong understanding of video, social media and mobile journalism.
Ability to use audience insights, analytics and performance data to inform content decisions and maximise audience reach and engagement.
Good knowledge of major digital and social platforms, including YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, WhatsApp and BBC digital products.
Experience editing, producing and publishing content across a range of formats and platforms.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues across teams and services, alongside a sound understanding of BBC Editorial Guidelines and a commitment to accuracy, impartiality and fairness.
DESIRABLE
Experience of reporting on Ethiopia and the wider Horn of Africa region.
Experience in data journalism, investigative reporting or visual storytelling.
Experience presenting content on video, audio or live digital platforms.
Knowledge of audience growth strategies, SEO and content optimisation techniques.
Company Details: The BBC World Service is the world's largest international broadcaster, broadcasting radio and television news, speech and discussions in 29 languages to many parts of the world on analogue and digital shortwave platforms, Internet streaming, podcasting, satellite, FM and MW relays. It was announced...read morein November 2016 that The BBC World Service will start broadcasting in Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba and Amharic among others in its biggest expansion since the 1940s. The World Service reached 210 million people a week (TV, radio and online) on average in 2015. The English-language service broadcasts 24 hours a day.

Knowledge of Zendesk.

Job Description:
About the role:
Acumen has international and institutional funders that provide both grants and returnable capital for its funds. This role sits at the center of safeguarding across the Green RISE, Pioneer, and Academy programs. Approximately half of the role will focus on managing safeguarding activities across Green RISE — owning the safeguarding framework, leading safeguarding due diligence, and monitoring safeguarding risks. The remaining half will primarily support Pioneer and the Academy, with additional support for Acumen’s returnable capital funds. The Manager will work closely with investment teams, external partner organizations, social enterprises, and other stakeholders, and will report on safeguarding to Acumen’s funding partners.
Accountabilities include:
Managing Acumen’s safeguarding framework across Green RISE, including safeguarding policies, procedures, and standards
Leading safeguarding due diligence on prospective and existing funding recipients, fellows, and partners
Monitoring safeguarding risks across the Green RISE portfolio, and escalating and managing safeguarding incidents as they arise
Owning and managing Green RISE’s grievance and safeguarding reporting mechanisms, including accessible reporting channels, confidential case management, survivor-centered and trauma-informed response and referrals, escalation and investigation coordination, and monitoring implementation across external partner organizations
Supporting Pioneer and the Academy on safeguarding integration, with additional support for Acumen’s returnable capital funds
Supporting Pioneer’s investing strategy, including integrating ESG into pipeline development, investment diligence, and post-investment portfolio support
Supporting Acumen’s returnable capital funds on ESG, including diligence, risk monitoring, and reporting to fund investors and partners
Supporting external partner organizations, investees, and other stakeholders with safeguarding capacity building, training, and resources
Co-developing new safeguarding resources across funds, including trainings and templates
Reporting on safeguarding performance, risks, and incidents to Acumen’s funding partners
Synthesizing safeguarding data and narrative into clear insights, supported by evidence, with recommendations for action
Qualifications
Minimum of 8 years of experience in safeguarding, ESG, impact investing, or sustainable finance; demonstrated safeguarding experience is essential
Direct experience designing, managing, or implementing safeguarding frameworks, policies, and due diligence processes, ideally with investees or partners in Africa
Experience investigating safeguarding incidents with a survivor-centered approach
Strong understanding of safeguarding standards, gender lens investing, gender equality and social inclusion strategies, risk-management practices, and due diligence, alongside ESG policies, procedures, and metrics across sectors
Bachelor's degree with a focus on social enterprise, sustainable finance, or international development.
Strong ability to take initiative with research and analysis and produce valuable results in conditions of uncertaint
An investigative mind and an ability to synthesize disparate data to draw conclusions and propose recommendations
A sense of proportionality in determining practical approaches to requirements with a focus on substantive value add and beneficiaries
Strong project management and stakeholder management skills and experience managing internal teams towards a common objective
Strong organizational skills and an ability to set up efficient systems for managing data, processes and information
Strong writing and presentation skills
Commitment to and enthusiasm for the organization’s mission to change the way the world tackles poverty, and respect for our core values: generosity, accountability, humility, audacity, listening, leadership, integrity, and respect
Ability to thrive when there is ambiguity, remain cool-headed when there are unexpected obstacles, and withstand the tests of a rapidly changing environment with resilience and resolve

Job Title: Programme Manager - Social Determinants of Health
Job Description:
ABOUT THE PROGRAMME
The Wellcome Trust Climate, Health & Mental Health Programme supports Amref Health Africa's work across three interconnected areas: Climate and Health, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support, and Global Health Leadership. The programme brings together research, policy, advocacy and implementation to generate African-led evidence, strengthen policy influence and advance solutions that respond to emerging health and social determinant priorities.
Within Amref, the programme is anchored in the Social Determinants of Health Unit and works across technical teams, country offices and external partners. Effective programme management is therefore critical to ensuring that technical and advocacy ambitions are translated into coordinated workplans, compliant grant delivery, sound resource stewardship and timely results.
JOB PURPOSE
The Programme Manager is responsible for the effective planning, coordination and operational delivery of the Social Determinants of Health portfolio, with primary responsibility for ensuring that grant-funded programmes are implemented on time, within approved budgets and in accordance with donor and organisational requirements.
Working closely with the Director, Social Determinants of Health and programme leads, the role translates programme priorities into integrated workplans, budgets, implementation schedules, management systems and reporting processes. The Programme Manager provides oversight across the Climate and Health, Mental Health and Global Health portfolios; coordinates delivery across technical, advocacy and support teams; anticipates and manages implementation risks; and ensures that leadership has timely information for decision-making and course correction.
The role is expected to bring strong programme management discipline, sound judgement and a solutions-oriented approach to a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio. It will work closely with Finance, Procurement, Legal, Human Resources, country offices, consultants and external partners to strengthen accountability, compliance, operational efficiency and quality of delivery.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
Programme Planning and Delivery (25%)
Lead the development, consolidation and monitoring of annual and quarterly workplans across the SDOH portfolio, ensuring alignment with approved grant objectives, budgets and delivery timelines.
Translate programme priorities into clear implementation schedules, milestones, responsibilities and management trackers, and maintain visibility of progress across workstreams.
Coordinate programme start-up, implementation reviews, re-planning and close-out processes, ensuring timely completion of required actions and documentation.
Monitor delivery against agreed milestones and proactively identify dependencies, bottlenecks and emerging implementation risks, escalating material issues to the Director with practical recommendations.
Coordinate programme governance and review meetings, ensuring decisions are documented, actions are assigned and follow-up is completed within agreed timelines.
Promote consistent programme management standards, tools and ways of working across the portfolio.
Grant Management and Donor Compliance (20%)
Coordinate grant administration throughout the programme lifecycle, ensuring contractual obligations, donor conditions, reporting requirements and internal controls are understood and met.
Maintain a consolidated view of grant deliverables, reporting deadlines, contractual commitments and compliance requirements, and follow up with responsible teams to ensure timely action.
Coordinate operational and management inputs into donor reports, grant reviews, amendments and other submissions, working closely with technical leads and support functions.
Ensure programme records, grant files, approvals and supporting documentation are complete, current and audit-ready.
Coordinate preparation for audits, donor reviews and grant close-out processes, and follow through on management actions arising from reviews or assurance activities.
Provide programme teams with practical guidance on applicable donor and organisational requirements, escalating areas requiring specialist advice.
Financial and Resource Stewardship (20%)
Lead programme budgeting, forecasting and periodic budget review processes in collaboration with the Director, programme leads and Finance.
Monitor expenditure, burn rates, commitments and budget utilisation against approved plans, identifying variances early and coordinating corrective action.
Coordinate budget revisions, reforecasts and resource allocation discussions to support delivery priorities while maintaining donor compliance and value for money.
Maintain oversight of procurement plans, consultant and service contracts, and other programme commitments to support timely implementation and appropriate use of resources.
Work with Finance and programme teams to strengthen financial accountability, documentation quality and timely resolution of outstanding financial actions.
Identify opportunities to improve resource efficiency and ensure programme resources are deployed in line with agreed priorities.
Risk, Quality and Performance Management (15%)
Maintain and regularly review programme risk registers, ensuring risks, mitigating actions, owners and escalation points are clearly documented and actively managed.
Monitor programme performance against agreed indicators, milestones and management commitments, drawing attention to areas requiring intervention or course correction.
Coordinate quality checks on programme management processes, documentation and delivery systems to strengthen consistency, reliability and compliance.
Support the Director and programme leads to assess implementation options, trade-offs and operational implications when plans or external conditions change.
Ensure key management decisions, changes and lessons are captured and reflected in subsequent planning and implementation.
Promote continuous improvement through periodic review of programme systems, processes and ways of working.
Stakeholder and Cross-functional Coordination (10%)
Coordinate implementation across SDOH technical and advocacy teams, Amref country offices, consultants, partners and relevant support functions.
Build effective working relationships with Finance, Procurement, Legal, Human Resources and other corporate teams to ensure programme needs are anticipated and addressed in a timely manner.
Facilitate clear information flow between programme leadership and delivery teams, ensuring priorities, decisions and dependencies are understood.
Coordinate consultant and service-provider engagement from an operational perspective, including workplans, deliverables, timelines, contracting interfaces and follow-up.
Support the planning and operational coordination of key programme meetings, partner engagements, convenings and strategic events where required.
Reporting, Learning and Operational Improvement (10%)
Prepare concise programme management updates, dashboards and decision-support information for the Director and programme leadership.
Coordinate periodic portfolio reviews and contribute programme management analysis to annual planning, donor reviews and management discussions.
Document implementation lessons and operational insights and ensure these inform future planning, risk management and process improvement.
Maintain fit-for-purpose programme management systems, dashboards and trackers that provide reliable and timely information for decision-making.
Promote effective use of digital collaboration and programme management tools to improve visibility, coordination and efficiency across the portfolio.
Qualifications
Education and Experience
Master's degree or equivalent in Public Health, International Development, Project or Programme Management, Business Administration, Social Sciences or a related field.
At least eight (8) years of relevant experience in programme or project management, including at least three (3) years in a managerial or programme leadership capacity. Experience working at the intersection of
climate and health
will be considered an added advantage.
Proven experience managing complex donor-funded programmes, preferably within health, international development or a multi-country environment.
Demonstrated experience in programme planning, grant management, budgeting, financial monitoring, procurement coordination, risk management and donor reporting.
Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams, country offices, consultants and external partners across multiple workstreams.
Knowledge, Skills and Competencies
Strong programme and project management capability, with the ability to translate strategic priorities into practical plans, systems and delivery milestones.
Sound financial and resource management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, expenditure monitoring and value-for-money considerations.
Strong understanding of grant and donor compliance requirements, programme controls, risk management and audit readiness.
Ability to analyse complex programme information, identify risks and dependencies, and make sound recommendations to support management decisions.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical teams, support functions, country offices, partners and donors.
Ability to coordinate multiple priorities and deliverables simultaneously while maintaining quality, timeliness and attention to detail.
Proven ability to improve systems and processes and to use digital tools, dashboards and data to strengthen programme visibility and decision-making.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare concise management reports, presentations and donor-facing documentation.
High levels of integrity, accountability and judgement, with a strong commitment to organisational policies, safeguarding, equity and inclusion.
Ability to work independently, exercise initiative and remain effective in a fast-moving and evolving programme environment.

Job Title: Administrative and Operations Officer - Health Systems Strengthening
Job Description:
ABOUT THE PROGRAMME
The Wellcome Trust Climate, Health & Mental Health programme brings together three interconnected pillars within the Social Determinants of Health (SDoH) Unit: Climate and Health, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), and Global Health Leadership. The programme combines research and evidence generation, policy and advocacy, partnership building, knowledge translation and institutional learning to strengthen African-led responses to emerging health challenges and influence regional and global policy agendas.
JOB PURPOSE
Reporting to the Director, Social Determinants of Health, the Administrative & Operations Officer provides cross-cutting operational and administrative support to the SDoH Unit, ensuring the efficient day-to-day functioning of a multi-country technical portfolio and the timely delivery of programme activities.
The role coordinates unit administration, procurement, travel and logistics, consultant and vendor processes, financial administration, event support, documentation and selected people-operations activities. Working closely with programme staff and corporate support departments including Finance, Procurement, HR, Legal, ICT and Administration, the position helps translate technical workplans into well-organised operational delivery while ensuring compliance with Amref policies and donor requirements.
The incumbent is expected to execute established operational processes accurately and on time, maintain reliable systems and records, analyse and report routine operational information, identify practical improvements and resolve day-to-day issues within delegated authority while escalating exceptions appropriately.
PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Unit Administration & Executive Support (~20% LoE)
Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Director, SDoH and the wider Unit, helping organise priorities, schedules and routine information flow.
Coordinate calendars, meetings, travel schedules and internal communications, anticipating dependencies and ensuring relevant materials are available in advance.
Prepare agendas, meeting packs, minutes and action trackers, and follow up agreed actions to support timely closure.
Maintain organised unit filing systems, shared drives, contact lists, templates and document repositories with appropriate access and version control.
Coordinate onboarding and administrative arrangements for staff, consultants and interns in collaboration with HR, ICT and line managers.
Programme Operations, Workplanning & Coordination (~15% LoE)
Support translation of annual and activity workplans into operational schedules, trackers, procurement plans, travel plans and logistical requirements.
Maintain operational trackers for key programme activities, deadlines and dependencies and provide routine status updates to the Director and relevant team members.
Coordinate operational communication between the SDoH Unit, country offices, partners and corporate support functions, ensuring requests are complete and followed through.
Support programme start-up, implementation reviews and close-out activities by ensuring required documentation, approvals and administrative steps are completed.
Compile routine operational inputs for programme reviews, donor reports, presentations and management updates.
Procurement, Contracts, Consultants & Compliance (~20% LoE)
Coordinate procurement requests in accordance with Amref policies, delegated authority and donor requirements, ensuring specifications, approvals and supporting documentation are complete.
Support preparation, processing and tracking of consultancy contracts, service agreements, purchase orders and related documentation.
Maintain procurement, contract, consultant and vendor trackers, proactively flagging upcoming expiries, pending actions and documentation gaps.
Liaise with Procurement, Finance, Legal and programme teams to ensure timely processing and resolution of routine queries.
Support due diligence, vendor onboarding and administrative compliance processes for consultants and service providers.
Maintain complete audit trails and support responses to routine compliance, audit and document requests.
Travel, Logistics & Event Support (~20% LoE)
Coordinate international and domestic travel including flights, accommodation, visas, insurance, travel approvals, per diems and itinerary documentation.
Provide end-to-end logistical support for workshops, meetings, conferences, field missions and partner convenings, both virtual and in-person.
Coordinate venues, participant invitations and registrations, materials, transport, equipment and other event requirements in line with approved budgets and procurement procedures.
Support operational planning for major convenings including COP, UNGA, WHA, AHAIC and other regional or global events, working with technical leads and external partners.
Maintain accurate travel, participant and logistical records and support post-event reconciliation and documentation.
Financial Administration & Budget Support (~15% LoE)
Prepare purchase requisitions, payment requests, advance requests, expense documentation and other routine financial paperwork accurately and on time.
Monitor operational expenditures against approved activity budgets and maintain expenditure and commitment trackers in collaboration with Finance and programme colleagues.
Support budget monitoring, reconciliation, forecasting and follow-up of outstanding advances, invoices or supporting documents.
Verify that financial documentation is complete, accurate, properly approved and audit-ready before submission.
Support consultants, vendors and programme colleagues with routine guidance on required finance and administrative documentation.
People Operations, Systems & Continuous Improvement (~10% LoE)
Coordinate selected administrative aspects of recruitment, onboarding, leave planning, induction, consultant engagement and staff transitions in collaboration with HR and line managers.
Maintain unit dashboards, operational tools and routine data required for planning and management oversight.

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE
The HR Generalist supports the HR Business Partner, HQ in delivering reliable, responsive and employee-centred human resource services across the employee lifecycle. The role combines strong day-to-day people operations with future-focused HR practices by coordinating recruitment and onboarding, employee relations and experience, performance and talent processes, learning and future skills, workforce analytics, digital HR solutions and compliance. Through accurate service delivery, practical guidance, data-informed insights and continuous improvement, the role helps create an inclusive, agile and digitally enabled workplace while ensuring HR programmes and processes are implemented in line with organisational policies and applicable employment requirements.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
HR Operations, Employee Lifecycle and Service Delivery

Prepare accurate and timely employment documentation, employee correspondence and HR confirmations, and maintain trackers for contracts and other time-bound actions.
Maintain complete, accurate and confidential employee records in the HR information system and personnel files, in line with data protection and records-management requirements.

Talent Acquisition, Onboarding and Workforce Planning Support

Coordinate recruitment processes from approved requisition through appointment, including job posting, application management, shortlisting administration, interview scheduling, candidate communication, pre-employment checks and appointment documentation.
Support hiring managers to apply fair, inclusive and competency-based selection processes and maintain complete recruitment records in line with organisational policy.
Coordinate onboarding and induction, including pre-boarding arrangements and scheduled follow-up, to help new employees integrate quickly and understand performance, culture, safeguarding and compliance expectations.

Support development of talent pools for recurring and critical roles in line with approved workforce priorities.
Employee Relations, Experience, Wellbeing and Culture

Support fair and consistent implementation of employee relations processes, including attendance, conduct, grievance and performance-related matters, within established procedures.
Coordinate employee listening, engagement, wellbeing and recognition initiatives; analyse feedback and track agreed actions with relevant leaders and teams.
Gather feedback at key moments in the employee journey and use it to recommend improvements to employee experience and HR service delivery.
Promote an inclusive, respectful and psychologically safe workplace by reinforcing organisational values, equity and inclusion, safeguarding expectations and relevant people policies.
Performance, Talent, Learning and Future Skills
Coordinate key stages of the performance management cycle, including goal setting, check-ins, review periods, documentation, completion tracking and follow-up with managers and employees.
Support talent review, succession and employee development processes under the guidance of the HR Business Partner and relevant specialist teams.
Coordinate learning-needs inputs and learning activities, including nominations, logistics, attendance, evaluation and maintenance of accurate training records.
Track individual development plans, career-development actions and agreed learning commitments and provide completion and impact updates.
Support initiatives that build future-relevant capabilities, including digital fluency, data literacy, collaboration, adaptability and people-management skills.

Compile and analyse workforce data, identify patterns and emerging risks, and prepare concise reports and insights for the HR Business Partner and management decision-making.

Significant experience producing high-quality journalism in a fast-paced, multimedia news environment, with the ability to deliver accurate and engaging content to tight deadlines.

Job Title: Women’s Economic Empowerment Manager – Regional Livestock Programme (RLP)
Job Description:
General Position Summary
The Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) Manager for the Regional Livestock Programme will use their in-depth contextual understanding, technical and practical expertise and relationship building skills to lead the collective delivery of a gender transformative program for women’s economic empowerment in the drylands of Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya.
The WEE manager will lead the design, implementation, and oversight of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy within a Market Systems Development (MSD) framework, ensuring that women, youth, and other marginalized groups benefit equitably from market opportunities. The role will provide technical leadership to integrate gender-transformative and socially inclusive approaches across all program components in targeted corridor, strengthen the quality and effectiveness of WEE interventions, and ensure that program strategies are informed by robust market systems, gender, and social inclusion analyses. Working closely with technical team, partners, and Monitoring and Results Measurement (MRM) teams, the WEE Manager will drive the generation and use of evidence to support adaptive management, learning, and decision-making; oversee the development of gender-responsive Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems; and contribute to knowledge sharing, impact measurement, and external engagement to advance sustainable, inclusive, and scalable program Women Economic Empowerment outcomes.
Essential Job Responsibilities
VISION AND STRATEGY
Set strategic direction and provide leadership for the program’s Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) agenda across target livestock trade corridors, ensuring women and youth are recognized, engaged, and benefit as key economic actors within livestock market systems. The role will strengthen the capacity of program teams and partners to integrate gender-transformative approaches across livestock value chains and supporting sectors, including animal health, feed and forage, livestock trade, business development services (BDS), and financial inclusion (FI).
Lead the implementation and continuous refinement of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy, ensuring that gender-transformative approaches are effectively embedded across priority interventions and market system activities. Working closely with Corridor Managers, the Deputy Director/Technical Lead, the Investment Manager, and the NRM Lead, the role will provide technical oversight and strategic guidance to address systemic gender constraints, strengthen inclusive market outcomes, and enhance women’s participation, leadership, agency, and economic benefits within livestock market systems.
Support the Program Leadership Team in engaging and influencing key stakeholders, including government institutions, private sector actors, development partners, donors, and civil society organizations, to advance the program’s WEE objectives. She/he will support strengthen multi-stakeholder partnerships, donor engagement and resource mobilization efforts directed to WEE, contribute to policy dialogue and advocacy initiatives, and promote collaborative actions that expand sustainable, inclusive, and market-driven economic opportunities for women.
Lead the development and implementation of the GESI/WEE learning, evidence, and knowledge management agenda to support adaptive management, advocacy, and thought leadership. This includes refining annual learning priorities and questions based on emerging evidence and program needs; leading qualitative and quantitative analysis to inform decision-making, donor reporting, stakeholder engagement, and capacity strengthening; and overseeing the development of internal and external communication products that highlight WEE achievements, lessons, and impact.
Promote innovation, learning, and adaptive management by identifying emerging opportunities, encouraging innovative approaches to overcome barriers to women’s economic participation, and fostering an environment where diverse perspectives are valued. The role will champion a culture of continuous learning, reflection, and evidence-based adaptation to strengthen program effectiveness and WEE outcomes
TECHNICAL Leadership FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Matrix accountability with program director for overall performance, quality, and results of RLP’s WEE and GESI portfolio across all countries and trade corridors
Lead the implementation of Mercy Corps’ Global Minimum Standards for Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) across the RLP, ensuring consistent integration of GESI principles throughout program design, implementation, monitoring, and learning processes.
Provide strategic and technical leadership for the design and implementation of GESI and Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) interventions, investments, and activities across all program components. Ensure interventions are informed by robust gender and social inclusion analyses, technically sound, market-driven, and aligned with donor requirements and recognized good practices.
Set annual WEE strategic priorities with program director
Guide and support program teams and partners to effectively integrate GESI considerations across interventions, ensuring women, men, youth, and other marginalized groups are meaningfully included, participate equitably, and benefit from program outcomes within livestock market systems.
Strengthen the capacity of program teams, partners, and stakeholders through training, coaching, mentorship, and technical support to foster ownership of GESI and WEE approaches and promote the application of gender-transformative and inclusive development practices.
Provide technical oversight for field monitoring, learning, and adaptive management related to GESI and WEE, including leading periodic qualitative reviews to assess progress, identify emerging opportunities and challenges, and inform strategic adjustments to interventions.
Lead the analysis, interpretation, and use of sex-, age-, and diversity-disaggregated data to generate evidence, strengthen program learning, and inform WEE strategies, intervention design, partnership development, and adaptive management decisions.
Contribute to high-quality donor and program reporting, ensuring that progress, lessons learned, and evidence of gender-transformative change, social inclusion, and inclusive market development outcomes are effectively documented and communicated.
Champion the integration of GESI across program operations, systems, and organizational practices, ensuring that internal policies, procedures, and ways of working reflect inclusive and gender-responsive principles.
Serve as the RLP Safeguarding Focal Point, promoting safeguarding awareness, strengthening compliance with Mercy Corps policies, supporting prevention and risk mitigation efforts, and ensuring safeguarding concerns are appropriately managed and addressed
MANAGEMENT & COORDINATION
Provide matrix management through technical supervision and mentorship of RLP’s GESI Focal Points and wider program team.
Lead and coordinate cross-country GESI community of practice to share learning and best practices across corridors.
Lead planning and coordination of WEE investments, in collaboration with budget holders to ensure GESI interventions are fully resourced. .
Provide technical sign-off on WEE grants, investments and partnerships as appropriate
Monitor value for money and effectiveness of WEE investments
Ensure that program and country staff understand, are familiar with, and have the skills to contribute to the integration of Mercy Corps’ GESI Minimum Standards.
Liaise with key external stakeholders to include their input on GESI, youth, and WEE perspectives in all aspects of program activities.
Engage with the global GESI team and relevant internal communities of practice to share and benefit from lessons and best practices across the organization.
EXTERNAL REPRESENTATION
Identify strategic influence opportunities to represent RLP’s learning on GESI and MSD with donors, peers, policy makers, and private sector actors
Design compelling, evidence-based presentations and learning products to share externally
Represent Mercy Corps and the program with donors and government and community leaders, as well as peer-oriented meetings and events, including in MSD and GESI-related networks and coordination bodies.
Lead publication of regional learning products on GESI and MSD in close collaboration with the Director Evidence & Learning Resilient Dryland Production Systems
Prepare and deliver presentations to stakeholders about program approaches, best practices, and learnings related to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion.
Security
Work closely with the country team’s security focal point to promote and maintain systems that promote the safety and security of all team members. Ensure that gender specific needs and interests of program staff in relation to safety and security are identified and responded to appropriately.
SAFEGUARDING
Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work
Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members
Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.
Supervisory Responsibility
Provides matrix leadership, technical supervision, performance input, and work-planning oversight to GESI focal points and relevant technical staff across Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia.
Accountability
Reports Directly To:
Program Director
Works Directly with RLP Staff including:
Within the RLP
: Deputy Director/Technical Lead, Monitoring and Results Measurement Manager, Director of Evidence & Learning RDPS, Trade Corridor managers, Inclusive Finance and Investment Manager, and the Communication and Knowledge Management Manager and wider RLP program team.
National, Regional and Global
: S/He will collaborate with the National Gender advisor(s) within the 3 countries if that role exists, the Regional Gender Advisor, and Global GESI and MSD technical advisors and MEL team members for strategic support to the RLP, her/his own professional growth, and to share insights and progress to others in Mercy Corps and beyond.
To Beneficiaries
Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our beneficiaries and to international standards guiding international relief and development work, while actively engaging beneficiary communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.
Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC's policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.
Minimum Qualifications & Transferable Skills
Master’s degree in Gender Studies, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Economics, Rural Development, Agricultural Economics, Livestock sector or a related field, with at least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including 5 years in a senior GESI/Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) leadership role. Experience in Market Systems Development (MSD), livestock value chains, and/or private sector development is highly preferred.
Proven experience leading the design and implementation of GESI and WEE strategies within large development programs, with demonstrated success in integrating gender and youth into livestock market systems, and economic development programming.
Strong experience working with the private sector to identify, test, and scale innovative business models, technologies, and market-based solutions that address barriers to women’s and youth’s economic participation and empowerment.
Demonstrated experience working on matrix teams and managing staff and budgets.
Demonstrated ability to build the capacity and commitment of program teams, partners, government institutions, and other stakeholders to apply gender-transformative approaches and promote women’s economic empowerment.
Proven technical leadership in the design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and learning of GESI/WEE interventions, including mentoring multidisciplinary teams and supporting adaptive management processes, preferably within an international NGO or donor-funded program.
Experience implementing women’s economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, youth employment, and livelihoods programs, preferably in pastoralist and agro-pastoralist contexts. Experience in the Horn of Africa is highly desirable.
Strong analytical and learning skills, including the ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and utilize qualitative and quantitative data to inform strategy, learning, advocacy, and decision-making.
Experience working with major donors such as SDC, Sida, AFD, the World Bank, and similar development partners, including donor compliance, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.
Excellent facilitation, communication, networking, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence diverse audiences and foster collaboration across sectors.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and adaptive management skills, with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in complex and evolving environments.
Demonstrated cultural sensitivity, diplomacy, and ability to work effectively within multicultural and multidisciplinary teams.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Willingness and ability to travel regularly to field locations (30-50%) as required

About the Role
We are hiring a data engineer to design the models behind client reporting and to present the results to the client directly. Source systems are rarely clean, and requirements rarely arrive complete.
What You Will Do
Design and build the ingestion, transformation, and modelling layers that client reporting depends on.
Own data models end to end: grain, keys, relationships, history, and testing, with the reasoning documented.
Profile, clean, and reconcile source data before it reaches the reporting layer.
Build the analytics layer that answers the client's questions, and interpret what the results indicate for their business.
Present designs, findings, and recommendations directly to client stakeholders, including non-technical audiences, and contribute to scoping at the pre-sales stage.
Excellent communication and presentation skills
Self-Starter – Motivated – Customer-focused
What You Have
Minimum 3 years building and maintaining production data pipelines that other teams relied on.
Undergraduate coursework, university and personal projects do not count toward this.
Certification required: a current cloud certification within the data, analytics, or machine learning track.
Certifications outside that track do not satisfy this requirement.
Snowflake SnowPro Core, production Snowflake experience, and machine learning deployed to production are each an advantage.
Advanced SQL: window functions, CTEs, set logic and aggregation at the correct grain, with the ability to read a query plan and explain a performance problem.
Relational database and modelling depth: normalisation, grain, key relationships, slowly changing dimensions, and judgement on when to denormalise.
dbt in a production setting: incremental models, snapshots, tests, and a project structure you designed rather than inherited.
Python for data work: analysis, automation, and acquiring data from databases, APIs, and files, including scraping where no interface is provided.
Data cleaning as an engineering discipline rather than a one-off task: profiling a source, reconciling it against a system of record, and holding it to that standard as it changes.
Quantitative and logical reasoning: statistics sufficient to validate a result, and the discipline to justify a design decision under questioning.
Presentation of data: turning a result into a clear chart, a written finding, and a recommendation that a non-technical audience can act on.
Where AI tools form part of how you work, you are expected to explain and defend every line of output you deliver. We regard them as an accelerator, not a substitute for understanding.
What We Want to See in Your CV
The databases, platforms, and tools you worked on directly, the scale of the data, and your own contribution rather than the team's.
At least one data model you designed: its grain, why you selected that grain, and what you deliberately excluded.
One instance where source data arrived incomplete, duplicated, or inconsistent, and what you did to make it reliable enough to report on.
Analytics or reporting you delivered, the question it answered, and how the business used it.
The hardest query or performance problem you have solved, rather than a stated proficiency level.
Certifications held, with the awarding body and current status.
What We Offer
The opportunity to work with the leading global OEMs and their technologies.
Ongoing professional development, with certifications supported and funded.
Career growth within a rapidly expanding technology consulting firm.

Phones are core to how GiveDirectly delivers cash — recipients need one to receive mobile money — and we buy close to a million of them a year across our country programs. That means constant coordination: what each country needs and when, which suppliers can deliver it, whether the price is fair, and what happens when a batch arrives damaged or a shipment runs late.
This role owns that end-to-end: forecasting demand with Programs, managing supplier relationships and orders, and keeping price, delivery, and quality on track across every country we operate in.
Reports to: Senior Manager, Global Supply Chain
What you’ll do:
Forecasting & planning
Partner with Programs and country Operations & Procurement Managers (OPMs) to build and maintain rolling phone demand forecasts by country and model
Translate forecasts into purchase timelines that avoid both stockouts and overstock
Sourcing & supplier management
Own supplier communication for feature phones and smartphones
Run RFQ/RFP processes to bring on new suppliers where needed, in coordination with country procurement teams
Track supplier performance and address quality, pricing, or reliability issues directly with vendors
Order & payment management
Process and track purchase orders from request through delivery
Coordinate with Finance on vendor payments, invoice discrepancies, and budget tracking
Manage returns, warranty claims, and defective-device resolution with suppliers
Reporting & continuous improvement
Track and report OTIF, cost savings, and Programs satisfaction on a regular cadence
Flag emerging risks — price increases, supply shortages, customs delays — before they affect delivery
Work with the Phone Inventory System Lead and Global Supply Chain on inventory visibility as new tooling comes online
What you’ll bring:
Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve.
Language Requirement: English
2+ years in procurement, supply chain, or vendor/category management; electronics, telecom, or hardware sourcing experience is a strong plus
Experience with demand forecasting and purchase order management
Strong negotiation skills and a track record of managing supplier relationships, including resolving commercial disputes like returns and warranty claims
Comfort coordinating across multiple African countries, time zones, and stakeholder groups (Programs, Finance, country OPMs)

Job Description:
About this role
GiveDirectly’s Emergency Cash team delivers rapid, technology-enabled cash assistance to people affected by crises. The Technical Program Manager (TPM), Emergency Cash will build, configure, and manage the technology used for those responses - including systems for data collection, verification, payments, and monitoring - and ensure they are reliable, replicable, and ready for rapid deployment.
In this role, you’ll translate emergency response needs into actionable technical requirements, coordinate cross-functional teams during activations, and strengthen our global readiness by improving tools and surfacing technical gaps to inform the product and technology roadmap.
The Emergency Cash team is a remote-first team built around trust, ownership, and flexibility. Because this role supports emergency responses, the TPM may need to provide surge capacity and work across multiple timezones during activations, in line with pre-established on-call schedules.
This position is ideal for someone who thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, can bridge the gap between technical teams and field realities, and is motivated to redefine how humanitarian responses leverage technology.
Reports to:
Senior Product Manager, Solutioning, Emergency Cash
What You'll Do:
Lead Technical Program Delivery for Emergency Responses:
Embed (remotely or on-site) with the emergency response team during activations to manage end-to-end technical program delivery - leading scoping, requirements gathering, system configuration and implementation, QA and testing, troubleshooting, and closeout.
Collaborate with Product, Tech, Research, Engineering, Data, Payments, and Programs teams to ensure systems are aligned with programmatic objectives and work seamlessly in field conditions.
Ensure all systems comply with GD’s standards for data protection, privacy, and financial controls.
Manage technical training and onboarding for surge staff, collaborators, and local partners.
Strengthen Rapid Response Technical Readiness:
Maintain and improve technical documentation, deployment guides, and incident-response protocols to ensure consistency and speed in future responses.
Partner with Programs and Engineering to develop product roadmaps and requirements, and prioritize and implement improvements that enhance emergency response scalability and reliability.
Track and report on technical readiness metrics (e.g. uptime, deployment speed, integration failures, data quality, testing coverage).
Lead and document technical design and implementation retrospectives, lessons learned and root cause analyses after each response to drive continuous improvement and contribute to product development strategies.
Support technical assessments, evaluations, testing and adoption of new products and solutions that strengthen emergency response technical capabilities.
Drive Safety,
Risk
Management, and Systems Resilience:
Support risk assessments for systems and data flows in high-risk operating environments.
Identify and mitigate technical risks - including connectivity, data loss, device theft, fraud, system misuse - before and during activations.
Contribute to incident reviews to improve our safety and resilience protocols.
What You'll Bring
:

:
Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve.
Professional Experience:
5+ years of professional experience; we welcome a wide range of relevant backgrounds (e.g. technical program management, product management, data analytics, software engineering, international development, emergency response, or management consulting).
Experience managing timelines, operational risk, stakeholders, and complex deliverables across multiple workstreams.
Proven ability to operate in fast-paced and ambiguous settings, exercising sound judgment to balance speed, risk, and quality.
Technical Skills:
Experience owning technical decisions when no predefined playbook exists, including evaluating novel technologies, system designs, and risks.
Working proficiency with a programming or statistical language (e.g. Python, R, Matlab, Java, Apex) - this role involves building automation and business logic, but it is not an engineering or data science role.
High attention to detail and strong instincts for analysis and validating data and code creatively and rigorously.
Structured approach to problem-solving and a drive to uncover and fix root causes rather than surface-level issues.
Ability to clearly communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders across varied cultural, national, and social backgrounds.
Fluency in English.

Preferred, not required: Experience with data visualization.
Contextual Understanding:
Understanding, or interest in learning, how technology enables emergency response operations (e.g. CVA platforms, identity verification, data collection tools, payment systems, mobile apps).
Preferred, not required: Experience working in humanitarian or emergency response contexts.

Job Title: Consultancy: Facilitation of Capacity Building Sessions During the Africa Team Retreat
Job Description:
Scope of Work
The consultant is expected to:
Hold preparatory meetings, review background materials, and develop the retreat agenda and facilitation plan.
Facilitate Work Planning for 2027 sessions. Guide the team through collaborative work planning to develop clear workstreams, activities, deliverables, dependencies, timelines, and individual accountabilities for 2027.
Guide country focal teams to present their contexts and support the team to reach portfolio and priority decisions.
Design and facilitate team building integration of new colleagues, and communication sessions.
Capture all decisions and outputs, photograph the sessions, and submit the post-retreat report.
Deliverables
A comprehensive facilitation plan, including methodology, detailed agenda, session designs, and activities, agreed with the Africa Team ahead of the retreat.
Africa Team's 2027 Work Plan using the agreed work planning template, with clear workstreams, activities, deliverables, dependencies, timelines, and individual accountabilities.
Country Portfolio and Strategic Priorities document with documented decisions on regional focus areas for 2027.
Power-Shifting Framework document defining how powershifting will be operationalized across hiring, governance, partnerships, and member engagement
A retreat report summarising discussions, decisions, insights, outcomes, and recommendations, alongside pre- and post-retreat evaluations to document baseline expectations, outcomes, learnings, and participant feedback.
All supporting materials, presentations, templates, and resources used during the retreat.
Photographs capturing team members during team-building activities and sessions.
Duration and location
The Africa Team Retreat is scheduled to take place on the week of 29th September 2026 in Nairobi, Kenya.
The consultant is expected to be available for preparatory meetings, retreat facilitation, and post-retreat reporting.
Qualifications and Expertise
The ideal consultant should have:
Proven experience in team facilitation and organisational development, including facilitating strategy operationalisation and change processes.
Demonstrated experience designing and facilitating working sessions and workshops that produce concrete decisions and documented outputs.
Expertise in team building, communication, and collaboration strategies, including integrating new staff into established teams.
Understanding of organisational values and dynamics of remote and distributed teams across diverse regional contexts.
Familiarity with power-shifting and localisation approaches in international development and understanding of how these principles shape organizational practice.
Experience working with international development organisations, ideally in Africa or with Africa-focused teams.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work sensitively across diverse country contexts and build psychological safety for open dialogue and decision-making.
Full computer literacy and fluency in English both written and spoken are essential.
Application Process
Interested individual consultants or companies are invited to apply. Please provide details of similar projects undertaken. Applications must not exceed five pages and should include the following:
Technical capacity of the consultant/s in terms of their qualifications and competencies for the assignment. Please attach detailed C.Vs.
Clear understanding of the assignment/interpretation of the TORs.
Methodology to be used during the assignment.
Work plan indicating the maximum time/duration required for the assignment, including a detailed financial proposal.
Duration of Assignment
This is a 6-day assignment that will consist of 2 days of pre-retreat, 3 days equivalent of retreat facilitation, and 1 day of post retreat that includes retreat reporting and recap. The Africa Team retreat is scheduled for the week of 29th September 2026.

The Debt Collections Officer will be responsible for managing and recovering outstanding B2B receivables while maintaining strong and professional relationships with customers.
The role will focus on ensuring timely collection of customer debts, reducing overdue balances and bad debts, resolving account-related disputes, and supporting the company's cash-flow and working-capital objectives.
The successful candidate will work closely with Finance, Sales, Customer Service, Operations, and customers to ensure invoices are accurately followed up, disputes are resolved promptly, and agreed payment terms are adhered to.
Key Responsibilities
Debt Collection & Receivables Management
Manage an assigned portfolio of B2B customer accounts and ensure timely collection of outstanding balances.
Monitor customer accounts and ageing reports to identify overdue and high-risk accounts.
Conduct regular collection follow-ups through telephone calls, emails, meetings, and written correspondence.
Establish and maintain effective collection schedules for overdue accounts.
Secure clear payment commitments from customers and follow up to ensure commitments are honoured.
Escalate severely overdue or high-risk accounts in accordance with company credit-control procedures.
Maintain accurate records of all collection activities, customer commitments, disputes, and payment arrangements.
Customer Account Reconciliation
Reconcile customer accounts and statements regularly.
Investigate discrepancies between company records and customer statements.
Follow up on unallocated payments, short payments, credit notes, and invoice discrepancies.
Ensure customer accounts accurately reflect invoices, payments, credit notes, and adjustments.
Work with the finance team to resolve account reconciliation issues promptly.
Invoice & Dispute Resolution
Follow up on unpaid invoices and establish reasons for delayed payment.
Identify and escalate invoice disputes, pricing issues, missing documentation, purchase-order issues, and service-related queries.
Liaise with Sales, Operations, Customer Service, and Finance to resolve customer disputes.
Ensure legitimate disputes are resolved quickly to prevent unnecessary delays in payment.
Track disputed invoices until resolution and payment.
Credit Control
Monitor customer credit exposure and payment behaviour.
Identify customers whose payment patterns indicate increased credit risk.
Provide recommendations regarding credit limits, payment terms, and collection actions where appropriate.
Ensure customers comply with agreed credit terms.
Support the implementation of credit-control policies and procedures.
Recommend escalation, credit holds, or legal recovery action for accounts that remain persistently unpaid, subject to management approval.
Reporting & Performance Monitoring
Prepare regular debt collection and accounts-receivable reports.
Provide updates on outstanding balances, overdue accounts, collection commitments, disputes, and recovery progress.
Monitor key collection metrics and ageing trends.
Highlight accounts requiring management intervention.
Provide accurate collection forecasts to the Finance Manager.
Maintain up-to-date collection notes and supporting documentation.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Work closely with Sales teams to resolve customer payment issues without compromising commercial relationships.
Coordinate with Operations and service teams on customer disputes relating to delivery or service performance.
Liaise with Finance and Accounts Receivable teams regarding invoicing, allocations, reconciliations, and account adjustments.
Support customer onboarding and credit assessment by providing information on payment history where required.
Customer Relationship Management
Maintain professional relationships with customers throughout the collection process.
Communicate firmly but diplomatically when pursuing overdue debts.
Understand customer payment processes, including purchase orders, approval workflows, invoice submission requirements, and payment cycles.
Develop effective relationships with customer finance, procurement, and accounts-payable teams to facilitate timely payment.
Required Skills & Competencies
Strong understanding of B2B credit control and debt collection processes.
Good knowledge of accounts receivable and customer account reconciliation.
Strong numerical and analytical skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong negotiation and persuasion skills.
Qualifications
Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related field.
Professional qualifications such as CPA (K), ACCA, or equivalent will be an added advantage.
Relevant training in credit management or debt collection is desirable.
Qualifications & Experience
At least 3 years of relevant experience in B2B debt collection, credit control, accounts receivable, or a related finance role.
Experience managing collections from corporate, institutional, industrial, or commercial customers.
Demonstrable experience handling overdue and disputed accounts.
Experience with customer account reconciliations and ageing analysis.
Experience dealing with finance, procurement, and accounts-payable departments within corporate customer organisations.

Job Description:
Position Overview
The Unit Accountant will oversee the property's daily financial operations. During the pre-opening phase, you will design financial workflows, implement accounting systems, and manage initial procurement tracking. Post-launch, you will lead budgeting, financial reporting, payroll, tax compliance, and cash flow management. This role reports directly to the General Manager.
Key Responsibilities
Pre-Opening Phase
Set up property management (PMS) and accounting systems integration.
Establish internal controls and operating procedures for all departments.
Track pre-opening expenses against the approved launch budget.
Assist in vendor registration and procurement validation.
Daily Operations & Reporting
Prepare monthly financial statements, profit and loss accounts, and balance sheets.
Manage accounts receivable and payable, ensuring timely vendor payments and guest billing.
Oversee daily night audit reconciliations and bank reconciliations.
Supervise income audit processes for rooms, food and beverage, and other revenue streams.
Compliance & Strategy
Ensure full compliance with KRA tax regulations, including VAT, PAYE, and withholding tax.
Manage payroll processing and statutory deductions.
Coordinate internal and external audits annually.
Analyze financial data to provide the management team with actionable cost-saving insights.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related business field.
Certified Public Accountant (CPA-K) or ACCA qualification.
Minimum of 3–5 years of accounting experience, specifically within the hospitality sector (hotels or serviced apartments).
Proficiency in hospitality software (e.g., Opera, Fidelio, or Sun Systems) and standard accounting packages (QuickBooks, Sage).
Strong understanding of Kenyan tax laws and statutory compliance.
Excellent analytical, Excel, and communication skills.
Hospitality pre-opening experience – added advantage
What We Offer
Competitive salary and benefits package.
Opportunity to shape a financial department from the ground up.
Career growth within an expanding hospitality brand.

In line with her vision of being a Premier Technological University excelling in Quality Education, Research and Technology transfer, DeKUT has put up expansive and well equipped Engineering workshops and supporting Physics and Chemistry laboratories.

DeKUT intends to establish a Science and Technology Park as per the Ministry of Education’s Master Plan for Science and Technology Parks in Kenya, the second of the kind will be established at Konza City. This new development will help build on the existing University Innovation and Incubation Hub (DeHUB) to a very great extent and take the University to a point of strength in living her Vision.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The Assistant Manager, Carbon Markets will support the delivery of FSD Africa’s carbon markets strategy and portfolio, working closely with the Manager and Lead, Carbon Markets and colleagues across FSD Africa and FSD Africa Investments. The ultimate goal is to enable Africa to seize the opportunity presented by carbon markets to accelerate its green economic transition and mobilise finance towards sustainable development. The role will provide technical, analytical, project management and coordination support across FSD Africa’s Carbon Markets portfolio, supporting the identification, design and implementation of carbon market programmes and investments and directly managing defined projects and workstreams. Working across FSD Africa’s organisational pillars, the Assistant Manager will support cross-pillar coordination and the integration of carbon market opportunities into wider FSD Africa programmes and investments.
Contract Type -
1 year fixed-term
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND ROLE REQUIREMENTS
Strategy & Programme/Investment Design
Support the implementation of FSD Africa’s Carbon Markets strategy and portfolio:
Monitor local, regional and international carbon market developments, including regulatory changes, market trends, financing developments, emerging technologies, opportunities and risks, providing timely analysis and inputs to Carbon Markets strategy, annual business planning and portfolio reviews.
Undertake research and market analysis to deepen understanding of how carbon markets can contribute to Africa’s green economic transition and financial market development, providing technical inputs to colleagues across FSD Africa on carbon finance, market mechanisms, policy and regulation, project development, financial institution engagement and emerging market opportunities.
Support the identification and assessment of potential carbon market programmes, investments and partnerships, undertaking initial research, stakeholder mapping, needs assessments and market diagnostics to inform programme and investment design.
Support the preparation of concept notes, business cases, Investment Committee papers, Terms of Reference and other programme documentation.
Support the identification of opportunities to integrate carbon finance into wider FSD Africa and FSDAi programmes and investments.
Project Cycle Management
Manage defined carbon market projects and workstreams and support the wider Carbon Markets portfolio so that agreed results are achieved, risks are managed and high-quality outputs are delivered:
For projects/workstreams under direct management:
Support the identification, procurement and onboarding of consultants and implementing partners, including drafting Terms of Reference and supporting procurement processes; work with implementing partners to translate approved concepts into detailed implementation plans, budgets, milestones, deliverables and risk management frameworks.
Coordinate day-to-day project implementation, maintaining effective working relationships with implementing partners and project trackers covering activities, milestones, budgets, risks, procurement requirements and Development Impact indicators.
Review project deliverables for quality, completeness and consistency with agreed objectives, providing feedback to implementing partners and organising and participating in project meetings, monitoring visits and stakeholder consultations.
Identify implementation issues and emerging risks at an early stage, escalating material issues to the Manager or Lead, Carbon Markets as appropriate, and support project amendments and extensions in accordance with FSD Africa policies and procedures.
Support project closure processes in accordance with FSD Africa policies and procedures, capturing project learning and ensuring relevant lessons are shared across the Carbon Markets team and wider organisation.
For projects managed by other pillars or cross-pillar colleagues:
Provide technical and coordination support for carbon market components, including reviewing project concepts, Terms of Reference, implementation plans and deliverables from a carbon markets perspective.
Participate in project meetings and stakeholder engagements where appropriate.
Maintain an up-to-date inventory of FSD Africa and FSDAi carbon market programmes, investments and pipeline opportunities.
Support colleagues to identify practical opportunities for integrating carbon markets and carbon finance into wider programmes and investments.
Financial Management, Risks & Resources
Support effective financial and risk management of projects and workstreams:
Prepare and maintain detailed project budgets, forecasts and implementation trackers, monitoring expenditure against approved budgets and flagging variances or implementation risks.
Support due diligence and contracting processes for implementing partners, consultants and potential investees, undertaking financial, market and risk analysis as required to support programme and investment design.
Liaise with FSD Africa support functions to ensure projects comply with internal policies, donor requirements and relevant statutory requirements.
Support assessment of Value for Money and Development Impact across projects.
Contribute to fundraising activities through research on prospective funding opportunities and preparation of technical inputs, workplans, budgets and proposal materials, including project and programme documentation required for internal approval and donor reporting.
Development Impact & Learning
Work closely with the Development Impact team and project colleagues to support evidence-based programme delivery and learning:
Support the development of Development Impact theses, results frameworks, indicators and data collection tools, ensuring implementing partners understand and comply with agreed reporting and data requirements.
Collect, review and analyse quantitative and qualitative project information, following up with stakeholders where information is incomplete and maintaining accurate records of project outputs, outcomes and lessons.
Contribute to periodic portfolio and project reviews to assess performance and identify areas requiring adjustment.
Support analysis of lessons emerging from carbon market interventions and translate these into practical recommendations for future programme design.
Contribute to the preparation of reports, briefing materials and presentations for FSD Africa management, donors and other stakeholders.
Influencing and Communicating for Impact
Support the Carbon Markets team’s communication, influencing and knowledge-sharing activities:
Maintain stakeholder maps for priority carbon markets, including governments, regulators, financial institutions, investors, project developers, buyers and other key market actors, and support the organisation and delivery of workshops, webinars, roundtables, training programmes and other stakeholder engagements.
Support the preparation of briefing notes, presentations, reports, case studies, articles and other communication materials, working with the Communications team to identify opportunities to disseminate project learning and market insights.
Contribute technical content to FSD Africa’s annual and quarterly reporting and wider Carbon Markets communications.
Represent FSD Africa at relevant meetings, workshops and external forums as appropriate, behaving at all times in a manner consistent with FSD Africa’s brand and values.
Support the development and dissemination of practical knowledge products that build understanding and capacity within financial institutions and the wider carbon market ecosystem.
Relationship Management
Build and maintain effective working relationships across FSD Africa and with external partners:
Develop relationships with relevant carbon market actors including government agencies, regulators, financial institutions, project developers, investors, buyers, technical experts, development partners and implementing organisations, supporting stakeholder consultations, market engagement and partnership development.
Coordinate effectively with colleagues across FSD Africa and FSDAi to support cross-pillar carbon market interventions, identifying emerging partnership and programming opportunities and bringing these to the attention of the Manager and Lead, Carbon Markets.
Maintain regular communication with implementing partners and other project stakeholders to support timely delivery and problem-solving.
Support capacity-building and knowledge-sharing activities for internal and external stakeholders.
Coordinate consultants engaged on specific projects or workstreams and ensure delivery against agreed outputs and timelines.
Carry out any other duties or special assignments as assigned by the Management
.
COMPETENCIES
Competencies describe the key behaviours that drive success in all of FSD Africa’s roles, regardless of technical specialism. They have been derived from systematic research correlating performance with personal attributes.
Competency Levels
Level 1: Basic
Level 2: Foundation
Level 3: Specialist
Level 4: Senior Specialist
Level 5: Leading Expert
Level 6: Executive
This position requires competency at
Foundation Level
for all the competencies listed below:
Requirements
PERSON SPECIFICATIONS
Qualifications and Education
Master’s degree and at least three years of relevant professional experience, or bachelor’s degree and at least four years of relevant professional experience.
At least one to two years’ direct experience working on carbon markets, climate finance, sustainable finance or closely related initiatives.
Excellent written and spoken English.
Essential Experience, Knowledge, and Skills
Good understanding of carbon markets, climate finance and sustainable development, including familiarity with key carbon market trends, actors and policy developments.
Understanding of the role of financial institutions, investors and other capital providers in supporting carbon market development.
Experience undertaking research, market analysis and preparation of high-quality written materials.
Good understanding of project cycle management and experience coordinating projects or complex workstreams.
Ability to develop and maintain project plans, budgets, trackers and risk registers.
Sound analytical skills, including the ability to assess financial, market and implementation information and draw practical conclusions.
Understanding of basic financial and investment principles and an interest in developing innovative financing approaches for carbon markets.
Understanding of risk, compliance and due diligence processes.
Experience working with multiple stakeholders and coordinating delivery across different organisations or teams.
Strong written communication and presentation skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information into clear and practical outputs.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and meet deadlines while maintaining attention to detail.
Strong interpersonal skills and an ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
Knowledge and skill in relevant ICT programmes, including Microsoft Office.
Desirable
Experience working with financial institutions, investors, project developers, government agencies or development partners.
Experience working on carbon project finance, carbon market policy/regulation, Article 6, voluntary carbon markets or related climate finance areas.
Experience working in African markets.
Experience working in a multi-cultural environment.
Knowledge of donor policies and procedures.
Previous experience working on FCDO-funded projects.
Experience supporting programme design, investment analysis or fundraising.
Languages: French and/or African languages.
