Job Description:
Job Summary
The Assistant Manager will work closely with the Senior Manager, Adaptation & Resilience Programmes, and the Senior Project Manager, AFIYA, to provide day-to-day programme management, reporting, and coordination support for the AFIYA programme – a multi-country programme funded by the Mastercard Foundation to expand access to gender-intentional agricultural insurance and complementary financial services for young women smallholder farmers and agri-preneurs.
The Assistant Manager is the engine room of AFIYA's programme management function.
This means keeping AFIYA's project tracking systems current and accurate (Monday.com), maintaining the reporting calendar and compiling inputs for Mastercard Foundation and internal management reports, maintaining budget-versus-actuals (BVA) trackers across the programme budget, and coordinating operational inputs from implementing and delivery partners across AFIYA's continental activities and country-level implementation (Kenya, Nigeria, and Senegal in phase 1). In doing so, the Assistant Manager enables the Senior Manager and the AFIYA programme team to focus on programme delivery, partner management, and impact.
The Assistant Manager also supports monitoring, evidence, and learning across the programme, working with the Development Impact team and delivery partners to ensure that data required for AFIYA's results framework and resilience measurement is collected, validated, and reported on schedule. While line management of the A&R Programme Assistants and Analysts sits with the Senior Manager, the Assistant Manager supports the day-to-day coordination of Assistants allocated to AFIYA, helping to track workload, maintain quality standards, and ensure consistent use of FSD Africa's templates, processes, and project management tools.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND ROLE REQUIREMENTS
Programme Operations & Reporting Support
Support the operational management infrastructure for the AFIYA programme, ensuring reporting, tracking, and coordination tasks are delivered accurately and on time:
Maintain the AFIYA reporting calendar, tracking all reporting obligations including Mastercard Foundation narrative and financial reports, internal management reports, and partner reporting deadlines; flag upcoming deadlines and coordinate timely inputs.
Keep Monday.com (or equivalent project management platform) current and accurate as the single source of truth for AFIYA project status, milestones, deliverables, and risk flags across continental and country-level workstreams, including data entry, quality checks, and routine updates.
Compile and quality-assure inputs from the AFIYA programme team, implementing and delivery partners, and country workstreams for progress updates, risk registers, and milestone reports, ensuring submissions are complete and on schedule.
Prepare first drafts of funder and internal reports for review by the Senior Manager and Senior Project Manager, ensuring consistency with FSD Africa's templates and the Mastercard Foundation's reporting requirements.
Support the development and maintenance of standardised templates and processes for AFIYA project reporting, risk escalation, and operational coordination.
Liaise with the Finance & Operations, Development Impact, and Corporate Services teams on routine operational and administrative matters for the AFIYA programme.
Workplan, Milestone & Delivery Tracking
Maintain comprehensive, accurate visibility of AFIYA workplans, milestones, and deliverables across continental activities and country implementation:
Keep AFIYA workplan and delivery trackers current and accurate across all programme components, from planning through to completion, covering both continental activities and country-level implementation.
Collect and verify progress data from the AFIYA programme team and delivery partners on a regular cycle, ensuring trackers reflect the latest status, expected milestones, and delivery timelines.
Track programme milestones and deliverables against the approved workplan and results framework, flagging delays or risks to the Senior Manager and Senior Project Manager in a timely manner.
Support the preparation of programme governance documentation, including materials for steering and oversight meetings, by compiling accurate status and supporting data.
Budget Monitoring & Financial Administration
Support effective budget management across the AFIYA programme, in compliance with FSD Africa policies and Mastercard Foundation grant requirements:
Maintain budget-versus-actuals (BVA) trackers across the AFIYA programme budget on a monthly basis, covering FSD Africa-managed activities and partner disbursements, preparing variance analysis for review by the Senior Manager and flagging discrepancies early.
Liaise with the Finance & Operations team to reconcile programme expenditure, track partner disbursements and financial returns, and support accurate forecasting.
Support the preparation of resourcing plans, procurement plans, and budgets for AFIYA activities and workstreams.
Support compliance with the Mastercard Foundation's financial reporting requirements, assembling documentation and following up on outstanding items.
Partner Coordination & Compliance Support
Support effective coordination of AFIYA's implementing and delivery partners, ensuring partners are onboarded, briefed, and compliant with programme requirements:
Support partner onboarding processes, including due diligence documentation, contracting follow-ups, and integration of new partners into AFIYA's reporting and tracking systems.
Help ensure implementing and delivery partners (including insurtechs, insurers, reinsurers, and research and delivery organisations) are briefed on reporting expectations, data collection requirements, quality standards, and compliance with risk management and accountability requirements, following up on outstanding items.
Coordinate the collection of partner reports and deliverables, tracking submission status and quality-assuring inputs before consolidation.
Support the organisation of partner meetings, workshops, and programme events, including scheduling, logistics, preparing materials, and capturing actions and follow-ups.
Coordinate inputs and follow-ups with consultants engaged on AFIYA programme management tasks.
Monitoring, Evidence & Learning Support
Support the collection, validation, and management of programme data required for AFIYA's results framework and resilience measurement:
Work with the Development Impact team and delivery partners to coordinate the collection of monitoring data against AFIYA's results framework, including outreach, adoption, and resilience indicators.
Quality-assure and validate data submissions from partners, flagging gaps or inconsistencies and following up on corrections.
Maintain AFIYA's programme data and documentation electronically, ensuring records are complete, current, and audit-ready.
Support the preparation of learning products, case studies, and evidence summaries drawing on programme data and partner reporting.
Team Coordination & Quality Support
Support the smooth functioning of the AFIYA programme team and the Programme Assistants allocated to AFIYA:
Support the Senior Manager in tracking the workload and task allocation of Programme Assistants and Analysts allocated to AFIYA, flagging capacity constraints and bottlenecks.
Help maintain consistent quality standards across the Programme Assistants and Analysts' work on AFIYA, including adherence to FSD Africa's templates, reporting formats, procurement procedures, and record-keeping requirements.
Support the induction and training of Programme Assistants and Analysts in AFIYA's project administration processes and the use of project management tools.
Work collaboratively with the AFIYA programme team, the wider A&R pillar, and cross-functional teams to ensure smooth information flows and effective coordination.
Carry out any other duties or special assignments as assigned by the Management.
COMPETENCIES
Competencies describe the key behaviours that drive success in all of FSD Africa’s roles, regardless of technical specialism. They have been derived from systematic research correlating performance with personal attributes.
Competency Levels
Level 1: Basic
Level 2: Foundation
Level 3: Specialist
Level 4: Senior Specialist
Level 5: Leading Expert
Level 6: Executive
This position requires competency at
Foundation Level
for all the competencies listed below:
PERSON SPECIFICATIONS
Qualifications and Education
Relevant Master's degree and 3 years of experience or Bachelor's degree from a recognised university and 4 years of experience, working in programme management, development finance, financial sector development, or a related field.
Excellent skills in written and spoken English.
Essential Experience, Knowledge, and Skills
Practical experience in programme or project management support within a complex, multi-stakeholder environment, including managing reporting deadlines and coordinating inputs across teams.
Strong data management and organisational skills, with demonstrated ability to maintain project tracking systems, workplan trackers, and reporting trackers to a high standard of accuracy.
Experience supporting funder reporting cycles for grant-funded programmes (experience with philanthropic funders such as the Mastercard Foundation desirable), including narrative and financial reporting.
Good skills in data analysis, financial tracking (budget versus actuals), and budget administration, with strong attention to detail.
Strong coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines simultaneously and follow up systematically across diverse workstreams.
Proficiency with project management tools (Monday.com, MS Project, or equivalent) and strong skills in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
Ability to manage data and documentation electronically and work effectively with digital platforms and tools.
Excellent communication skills; a collaborative team player.
Desirable
Experience working in inclusive or agricultural insurance, climate finance, adaptation finance, or financial sector development in Africa.
Experience supporting gender-intentional or youth-focused programming.
Experience coordinating implementing partners across multiple countries.
Experience of working in a multi-cultural environment.
Experience working with funders, including knowledge of grant compliance policies and procedures.

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE.
Lead World Vision's applied research, evidence generation and learning translation function, using child data across the partnership - Annual Impact Measurement (AIM/AIM+), programme monitoring, evaluations, operational research and commissioned studies - to produce decision-useful, externally credible evidence. The role commissions and leads applied research, evidence synthesis and university partnerships; translates findings into actionable learning and strategic insight; and ensures evidence informs programme quality, fundraising, policy influence and senior leadership decisions. Child Data Analytics & Insights retains ownership of analytics, dashboards, data products and analytical services.
KEY RESPONSIBILITES
Applied Research, Evidence Synthesis & Child Data Insights
Lead applied research and evidence synthesis using child data from AIM/AIM+, programme monitoring, evaluations, operational research, commissioned studies and other evidence sources.
Deliver the annual AIM/AIM+ insight narrative as a research/learning product, translating WVI’s Global Strategy - Our Promise, Phase 3 (OP3) and senior-leadership questions into answerable research questions, data stories and decision-use products.
Commission and/or lead secondary analyses of the 400,000+ household AIM data set and other datasets to generate cross-country insights across child wellbeing, resilience, vulnerability, equity and integrated sector outcomes.
Set interpretation standards for child-data research, including methods, uncertainty, claim boundaries, reproducibility and responsible use of sensitive data.
Coordinate with Design Monitoring Evidence Accountability and Learning (DMEAL) and data governance on data availability, quality, extracts and analytical constraints.
OP3 Applied Research Portfolio & Commissioned Studies
Translate the OP3 research agenda into a sequenced portfolio of studies across Integrated Child Wellbeing Pathways, Christian Faith/Spiritual Nurture/Child Flourishing, Climate Stress and Child Resilience, Long-Term Community Transformation, and Local-to-Global Systems Transformation.
Commission, scope, lead and quality assure research studies, evidence syntheses, secondary analyses, mixed-methods, ex-post/longitudinal and quasi-experimental or comparative designs.
Ensure research designs address cross-sector programming questions across health, nutrition, WASH, livelihoods, child protection, resilience, climate, faith and development, systems transformation, and humanitarian/nexus contexts.
Develop or approve research questions, theories of change, protocols, TORs/RFPs, analysis plans, sampling approaches, ethics/IRB pathways, data-use agreements, publication plans, technical review processes and acceptance criteria.
Coordinate with Field Office and Regional Office (FO/RO) teams, Support Offices, sector leads, Grants Acquisition and Management (GAM), Advocacy and External Engagement (A&EE), Disaster Management (DM), universities and external researchers so commissioned studies are rigorous, feasible, field-grounded and operationally usable.
External Research Partnerships, Publications & Funding
Develop university and research-institution partnerships that strengthen methodology, credibility, peer review, publication potential and access to specialists.
Shape joint research through co-PI models, advisory groups, fellowship/student pipelines, data access protocols, authorship plans, dissemination and workplans.
Build publication and dissemination pathways, including peer-reviewed outputs, working papers, evidence briefs, donor-facing research products and public learning products.
Agree partnership scope, deliverables, data-use arrangements, ethical requirements, acceptance criteria and dissemination expectations with legal, data governance, safeguarding and line management as needed.
Mobilise technical and funding leverage by matching WV data assets, field presence and OP3 priorities with external expertise in child wellbeing, faith and development, health/nutrition, climate, systems and longitudinal research.
Represent WV research and evidence agenda with academic partners, donors, Support Offices, foundations and external evidence networks.
Learning Translation, Influence & Research Uptake
Translate research findings and child-data findings into leadership-ready insight products, Research Board materials, executive briefs, donor-facing narratives, programme design implications, influence products and practical learning tools.
Define an evidence-to-decision pathway for each major research product, identifying the decision owner, intended use, audience, timing, format and measure of uptake before products are commissioned or produced.
Facilitate interpretation and uptake with programme, sector, FO/RO, Support Offices (SO), GAM, advocacy, communications and senior leadership teams so findings inform design, adaptation, fundraising, policy influence and external positioning.
Track whether research improves decisions, is used by external actors, or contributes to resource mobilisation, aligned with the OP3 success metrics of impact, influence and income.
Ensure public-facing and donor-facing evidence claims are accurate, proportionate and defensible.
Research Governance, Team Leadership & Capability Building
Lead a leveraged research and learning platform that includes core researchers, Health/Nutrition and Faith/Development research capabilities, commissioned researchers, university partners, sector specialists and time-bound working groups.
Set the annual workplan, quality standards, technical review cadence, escalation process and product standards for applied research, evidence synthesis, AIM/AIM+ insight narratives and OP3 research outputs.
Line-manage and/or matrix-manage research staff and consultants as assigned, setting priorities, coaching technical quality, managing delivery and ensuring accountability for outputs.

Company Details:
The 1st Steiner-Waldorf Kindergarten opened in 1998...

...in a small house along the Magadi Road on the outskirts of Nairobi. It was led by 3 teachers from Germany (Florian, Vojko and Irmgard).
The following year the school moved to Mbagathi extending the kindergarten to a 1st Grade primary clas...read mores. The Mbagathi Steiner school continues to run successfully; now a fully fledged kindergarten and primary school known as the Rudolf Steiner School, Mbagathi, transitioning their children successfully into Kenyan Curriculum Secondary schools.
In 1994 a new Waldorf Kindergarten opened its doors in a beautiful residential suburb - the Kileleshwa Kindergarten. This was initiated by a group of parents who had been impressed by the Mbagathi kindergarten but needed something in a more central area.
As the new millennium approached, another parent group around a core of Kileleshwa parents, now more familiar with the Waldorf philosophy and its practical results, felt a great need to continue the initiative into the primary level. Both the Kenyan and British institutions were offering instruction that was wholly formal from such a young age, promoting 'The Hurried Child' syndrome.
Media reports about school unrest were pandemic and views from other parents clearly indicated dissatisfaction with the lack of creativity in education. Some of their children were already feeling stressed and unhappy in school. There was a very conscious feeling that Waldorf education would not only benefit the families and their own children, but would contribute towards the ultimate transformation of education in Kenya for the better.

About the role
You will be responsible for marketplace health and pricing efficiency for Bolt’s ride-hailing marketplace in Kenya. Your role will involve balancing rider experience, including pickup ETA, search coverage and cancellations, with driver earnings, supply availability and retention through data-driven pricing, category and supply interventions.
Your role will have a direct and tangible impact through continuous improvement of the rider and driver experience by ensuring a healthy marketplace, competitive pricing and an effective balance between supply and demand.
You will be working alongside other Operations team members and cross-functional stakeholders across Growth & Analytics, Product, Driver Growth, Driver Engagement, Riders, Fleet & Vehicles, Compliance and Customer Support. You will play a key role in translating marketplace data into actions, adapting global marketplace playbooks to Kenya’s specific dynamics and driving initiatives from analysis through to implementation.
Main tasks and responsibilities
Own marketplace performance by monitoring core KPIs including pickup ETA, Search Coverage, Partner Acceptance Rate, Order-to-Finish Rate, Utilization and Rider Cancellation Rate, running the weekly Marketplace Health Review and translating insights into actions that improve rides and GMV.
Design and execute pricing strategies through regular competitive price benchmarking, pricing simulations and adjustment proposals, while owning category-level pricing across Non-LTO categories, EV, motorbike/2-wheeler, CBD, short-distance pricing and category laddering.
Improve supply quality and marketplace efficiency by managing driver-quality programmes, addressing completion and offline-trip behaviour, investigating dispatch and matching issues, and optimizing geographic polygons and search categories.
Own competitive intelligence by monitoring competitor pricing, promotions, incentives, market share, ASP and net rates, and translating market developments into recommendations for Bolt’s pricing, incentive and marketplace strategy.
Own marketplace reporting and performance tracking by continuously improving the Marketplace Operations Tracker, automating recurring checks, tracking driver incentive spend and ROI, and preparing weekly, monthly and quarterly marketplace performance reviews.
Lead cross-functional marketplace initiatives from planning to execution, collaborating closely with Growth & Analytics, Product, Driver Growth, Driver Engagement, Riders, Fleet & Vehicles, Compliance, Customer Support and Central Operations, while supporting ad hoc fraud and risk investigations affecting marketplace performance.
About you
You have 5 -7 years of experience in Operations, Consulting, Analytics, Strategy, Marketplace Operations, a start-up or another fast-paced environment with a strong quantitative component.
You have a Bachelor's Degree or higher in Business Management, Economics, Engineering, Finance, Statistics or related fields.
You are highly analytical and comfortable using data to diagnose marketplace challenges, identify opportunities and drive strategic and operational decision-making.
You have strong project management skills and experience translating analysis into implemented actions, managing multiple priorities and leading cross-functional initiatives.
You are a strong collaborator and communicator with excellent English communication skills (both verbal and written), and you are comfortable working with stakeholders across Product, Analytics, Growth and Operations.
You demonstrate strong ownership, independence and attention to detail, with the ability to work towards ambitious goals and continuously improve and automate operational processes.
Why you’ll love it here
Accelerate your professional growth with unique career opportunities.
Enjoy a rewarding salary and stock options, knowing that as Bolt succeeds, so do you.
Take care of your physical and mental health with our wellness perks.
Celebrate 5 years at Bolt with a 1-month paid sabbatical to recharge.
Connect with colleagues at annual company events and smaller team gatherings.
Balance flexibility and in-person collaboration with our hybrid model, including at least 12 monthly in-office days.

Job Description
The role is responsible for maintaining strong client relationships and ensuring a seamless client experience across the company’s investment and wealth management products and services.

Client Relationship Management
Develop and maintain strong, professional relationships with clients and proactively identify their needs, concerns and service requirements.
Serve as a key point of contact for clients, providing prompt and accurate responses to enquiries and requests.
Maintain a strong understanding of Moran Capital Management’s products, services, processes and client service standards.
Provide clients with regular updates and relevant information regarding their investments, accounts and transactions.
Identify potential client service issues and ensure timely resolution or escalation where necessary.
Client Onboarding & Account Management
Coordinate the onboarding of clients across investment products, including Money Market Funds, Equities, Pensions, Local Fixed Income and International Investment Products.
Ensure that required client documentation and information are accurately captured, maintained and updated in accordance with company and regulatory requirements.

Coordinate with relevant internal teams to ensure that client accounts and investment instructions are processed accurately and within agreed timelines.
Ensure that financial consultants are kept informed of relevant client transactions, account activities and service requests.
Investment & Transaction Support

Client Service Excellence
Implement and maintain high standards of client service in line with Moran Capital Management’s client service objectives.
Coordinate client service excellence initiatives and support continuous improvement of client-facing processes.
Gather and communicate client feedback to relevant management and recommend improvements to enhance the client experience.
Maintain confidentiality and exercise a high level of discretion when handling client, financial consultant and company information.
Prepare and maintain relevant client service reports and records as required by management.
Compliance, Risk & Escalation
Ensure that client interactions and service activities are undertaken in accordance with approved company policies, procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.
Escalate complex, sensitive or high-risk client matters to the Finance & Strategy Director or relevant department promptly.
Maintain proper documentation and audit trails for client transactions, requests and communications.
Identify recurring service issues and recommend practical solutions to minimise operational and client-service risks.
Teamwork & General Responsibilities
Work collaboratively with the Operations, Finance, Wealth Advisory and other relevant teams to ensure seamless delivery of client services.
Support the implementation of process improvements and automation initiatives aimed at improving efficiency and client experience.
Perform any other duties reasonably assigned by the supervisor or management in line with the requirements of the role.

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Commerce, Investment Management, or a related field.
Professional qualifications in finance, investment, customer service or a related discipline will be an added advantage.
3–5 years of relevant client service experience in investment, wealth management, financial services or insurance industry.
Experience dealing with investment or wealth-management clients will be an added advantage.
Demonstrable experience in client onboarding, account administration, transaction processing and client relationship management.
PREFERRED SKILLS
Strong understanding of client service principles and practices.
Good understanding of investment and financial products.
Good knowledge of client onboarding and account administration processes.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant client/investment management systems.
Strong customer orientation and ability to manage demanding clients professionally.

Job Title: Senior Associate- Food Systems, Agriculture and Climate Resilience Management
Job Description:
Role Purpose
Busara's FaRM team applies behavioral science to some of the most complex challenges in food systems, smallholder agriculture, and climate resilience across the Global South. As a Senior Associate, you will work closely with the Engagement Director to lead the delivery of rigorous research and advisory projects for donors, governments, NGOs, and private sector clients working on food security, climate adaptation, and agricultural market systems.
You are a skilled researcher and project executor, someone who can take a well-scoped engagement and drive it forward with rigor, initiative, and attention to detail. You bring deep qualitative research expertise, genuine sector knowledge, and the organizational ability to keep complex, multi-method projects on track.
You translate behavioral evidence into actionable recommendations, backed by the credibility that comes from real field experience and methodological depth. You are comfortable representing Busara's work in client settings and holding your own in a room with a senior government official or seasoned development economist while knowing when to loop in senior leadership.
This is not a role for generalists. We are looking for someone who has spent meaningful time in the field and understands the lived realities of smallholder farmers and agri-food value chains. In this role, you will take ownership of project deliverables and client relationships, directly manage project staff, and coordinate effectively across Busara's internal teams to ensure engagements are executed to the highest standard.
Key Accountabilities/Responsibilities:
Senior Associates will work closely with Busara offices and directly with academic researchers and advisory clients to perform a variety of tasks, including, but not limited to:
Client & Advisory Leadership
Own the client relationship across the full engagement lifecycle — from scoping and contracting through delivery and dissemination.
Lead senior-level conversations with donors, implementing partners, ministries, and private sector clients; anticipate needs, navigate complexity, and manage expectations proactively.
Translate client problems into well-defined research and advisory briefs; push back constructively when questions are ill-formed or scope is misaligned.
Develop proposals, concept notes, and pitch decks; contribute to business development within the food systems and climate resilience space.
Represent Busara at conferences, technical working groups, and client convenings — presenting findings with clarity and confidence to non-specialist and expert audiences alike.
Qualitative Research & Technical Execution
Design and lead qualitative research components — including in-depth interviews (IDIs), focus group discussions (FGDs), ethnographic observation, and participatory methods — with rigor and cultural sensitivity.
Synthesize qualitative evidence into coherent, actionable narratives; identify behavioral drivers and barriers embedded in complex social and institutional contexts.
Apply behavioral science frameworks (e.g., COM-B, dual process theory, social norms models) to agricultural and climate adaptation challenges.
Oversee mixed-methods research design, ensuring qualitative and quantitative workstreams are well-integrated and mutually reinforcing.
Maintain quality control across all research outputs — guides, transcripts, codebooks, analysis memos, and final reports.
Project & People Management
Own project timelines, budgets, deliverables, and staffing plans; escalate risks early and manage scope proactively.
Directly manage and mentor Analysts and Project Leads embedded on your engagements; build their research and advisory skills through active coaching.
Coordinate across Busara's Data, Programming, and Operations teams to ensure smooth execution of field and remote research activities.
Contribute to onboarding and knowledge management so institutional learning is captured and usable.
Organizational Contribution
Contribute to FaRM team strategy and knowledge development — including internal research, sector thought pieces, and methodology innovation.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, and performance management of junior team members.
Champion a culture of intellectual rigor, constructive feedback, and psychological safety within your project teams.
Knowledge, Skills and Experience
Required
5–8 years of experience in research, advisory, or program design roles with a meaningful focus on food systems, agriculture, or climate resilience in sub-Saharan Africa or comparable contexts.
Deep expertise in qualitative research methods — IDIs, FGDs, thematic analysis, and synthesis with strong fieldwork experience in low-resource settings.
Demonstrated ability to manage senior client and partner relationships with confidence, clarity, and professional maturity.
Proven track record leading complex, multi-stakeholder projects from inception to delivery.
Strong analytical and synthesis skills, you can turn messy qualitative data into a crisp, defensible argument.
Excellent written and verbal communication in English; able to write for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (Social Sciences, Development Studies, Agricultural Economics, Public Policy, or related).
Strongly Preferred
Master's degree in a relevant field.
Experience applying behavioral science formally or informally to agricultural extension, climate adaptation, or food value chains.
Familiarity with quantitative methods and data analysis tools (Stata, R, or Python); comfort interpreting quantitative findings even if not the primary analyst.
Experience with experimental or quasi-experimental designs (RCTs, difference-in-differences, etc.) as a research lead or collaborator.
Existing networks within the East or West African food systems or climate finance ecosystem.

Job Description:
Purpose of the Role
The Psychosocial Support Officer will provide specialized professional expertise to safeguard participant well-being throughout the assignment, with a particular focus on identifying, preventing, and responding appropriately to emotional distress or unforeseen crises that may arise during sensitive interviews, surveys, or other field interactions. The role will also support the wider field team in maintaining a safe, ethical, and trauma-informed approach to engagement with participants
Key Responsibilities
Monitor participants for signs of distress, trauma, anxiety, or emotional overwhelm during sessions.
Provide immediate emotional support and grounding techniques to help distressed participants regain a sense of safety and stability.
Protect participants’ privacy by treating personal stories and mental health information with the highest level of confidentiality.
Prepare data collectors to recognize and respond appropriately to emotional stress in themselves and others during the data collection exercise.
Facilitate brief daily debriefs to help the team reflect on difficult experiences and support one another after demanding field days.
Offer practical guidance and brief supportive counseling to staff members who may feel overwhelmed.
Apply established safety protocols and ethical guidelines when engaging on sensitive topics.
Escalate any significant safety concerns or incidents to lead researchers immediately.
Contribute to adjustments in field plans when new emotional risks emerge during implementation.
Prepare an incident report at the end of the data collection exercise, summarizing any incidents identified and the mitigation and referral measures implemented in line with Mastercard Foundation’s Safeguarding policies.
Indicative Deliverables
A financial proposal/quote itemizing the services to be provided.
A brief psychosocial support plan outlining participant safety measures, distress response procedures, and escalation pathways for field activities.
Field support notes or debrief summary capturing key wellbeing concerns, actions taken, and any follow-up needs identified during the assignment.
An incident and referral log documenting any psychosocial risks, responses provided, and referrals made in line with safeguarding protocols.
A concise end-of-assignment report summarizing psychosocial support activities, key observations, mitigation measures, and recommendations for future fieldwork.
Required Qualifications and Experience
A bachelor’s degree in social sciences, psychology, gender studies, development studies, community development, or a related field from a recognized institution in Kenya; a master’s degree is an added advantage.
At least 5–7 years of professional experience in psychosocial support, safeguarding, gender-responsive programming, inclusive fieldwork, or related work in Kenya, preferably in development or humanitarian settings and with vulnerable groups such as refugees, displaced persons, women, youth, or persons with disabilities.
Demonstrated experience supporting qualitative fieldwork or participant engagement, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to apply trauma-informed, culturally sensitive, and ethical approaches when working with diverse communities.
Working knowledge of safeguarding principles, confidentiality, duty of care, and referral pathways in the Kenya context, including the ability to respond appropriately to sensitive disclosures.
Strong communication and facilitation skills in English and Kiswahili; knowledge of additional Kenyan local languages or experience working effectively with interpreters is an advantage.
Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations, field research, or program reviews is an added advantage.

Job Title: Thematic Expert- Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development (Kenya)
Job Description:
Purpose of the Role
The Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development Thematic Expert brings specialist expertise in entrepreneurship, financial sector development, MSME finance, and inclusive finance mechanisms (including credit guarantees, digital financial services, and value chain finance) relevant to Kenya and the East Africa region. On this assignment, the expert leads the analysis of financial inclusion outcomes, assesses contribution to system- and ecosystem-level change in the financial sector, and contributes substantively to final review reports. The expert will support Busara and Mastercard Foundation Kenya to establish:
How trends in Kenya’s entrepreneurship, enterprise development, financial inclusion, and MSME sector are impacting youth employment opportunities where the strategy is active in Kenya.
The extent to which the strategy partnerships and investments are positioned to respond to and capitalize on these trends.
The barriers, gaps, and opportunities for meaningful participation of young women, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and refugee communities in entrepreneurship and enterprise development.
Opportunities, risks, and gaps in the strategy’s entrepreneurship, enterprise development, financial inclusion, and MSME sector positioning, and practical, prioritized recommendations to strengthen it.
Key Responsibilities
Review literature, strategy documents, partner reports, and results data on entrepreneurship, enterprise development, financial inclusion, and MSMEs in Kenya.
Analyze sector trends, key actors, and ecosystem dynamics, and benchmark Kenya’s context against relevant East African strategies.
Conduct key informant interviews and stakeholder consultations with ecosystem actors, partners, and other informed respondents.
Assess program relevance, coverage, and alignment with national priorities, with attention to youth employment, skilling, and participation by young women, PWDs, and refugee communities.
Identify barriers, gaps, opportunities, and priority partnerships, delivery models, and sub-sectors to strengthen youth participation and outcomes.
Evaluate how sector knowledge dissemination contributes to dignified and fulfilling work and improved financial outcomes for youth.
Provide technical guidance on evaluation design, sampling, data collection tools, analytical frameworks, and enterprise-related theory of change and assumptions.
Support the design and interpretation of POA indicators, with particular attention to enterprise-based pathways and progress.
Assess participant experiences and outcomes related to enterprise establishment, growth, market access, productivity, resilience, financial inclusion, and business continuity.
Provide technical input on enterprise finance and financial inclusion pathways, including access to finance, investment decisions, loan use, repayment, and progression dynamics.
Support development of enterprise performance frameworks that reflect informal, emerging, and growth-oriented businesses.
Interpret enterprise outcomes across participant segments, including youth-owned enterprises, women-owned enterprises, refugee-owned enterprises, persons with disabilities, MSMEs, and SMEs.
Review quantitative and qualitative findings and synthesize evidence into actionable recommendations for program improvement, systems strengthening, and ecosystem development.
Review and quality-assure inception reports, analytical frameworks, interim deliverables, strategic review outputs, and final evaluation reports.
Produce a final report with findings, learnings, and recommendations, and a prioritization framework for Busara and Young Africa Works stakeholders.
Indicative Deliverables
An inception report covering the methodology, work plan, and budget.
Key Informant Interview (KII) discussion guides tailored to various stakeholders.
Audio recordings and notes from Key Informant Interview (KII) discussions.
A draft narrative report including an executive summary, findings, learnings and recommendations, and a prioritized action matrix.
A PowerPoint slide deck for presentation to the Foundation.
Hold a validation and dissemination session with the Foundation.
A final PowerPoint slide deck incorporating input from the validation and dissemination session.
Participate in sensemaking sessions with the Foundation, Implementing Partners, and other relevant ecosystem actors, as required.
A final narrative report incorporating input from the validation, dissemination, and sensemaking sessions.
Required Qualifications and Experience
Advanced degree in economics, finance, development studies, entrepreneurship, business administration, enterprise development, agricultural economics, private sector development, or a related field.
At least 8–10 years of experience in financial sector development, MSME finance, inclusive finance, enterprise development, entrepreneurship promotion, market systems development, private sector development, or livelihoods programming in Kenya or East Africa.
Demonstrated experience with one or more of the following: digital financial services, value chain finance, enterprise finance, or inclusive finance mechanisms.
Proven experience analyzing financial inclusion or enterprise development outcomes for underserved groups, including youth, women, refugees, and persons with disabilities.
Proven track record and consulting experience conducting strategic reviews, evaluations, or advisory assignments for donor-funded or foundation-funded entrepreneurship and enterprise development programs.

Sales & Business Development

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE
The Fleet Coordinator Intern will support the day-to-day coordination and administration of the company’s fleet and logistics operations. The role will assist in monitoring vehicle movements, maintenance schedules, fuel usage, driver activities, documentation, deliveries, and other logistics activities to ensure efficient and cost-effective operations.
The intern will gain practical experience in fleet management, logistics coordination, record keeping, reporting, and operational support.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Fleet Coordination
Assist in coordinating the daily allocation and scheduling of company vehicles.
Monitor vehicle movements, assignments, and utilization.
Maintain an updated fleet register and vehicle records.
Assist in tracking vehicle mileage, fuel consumption, servicing, and repairs.
Follow up on scheduled vehicle servicing, inspections, insurance, and other statutory requirements.
Assist in reporting vehicle breakdowns, accidents, and maintenance issues.
Monitor vehicle availability and communicate any operational challenges to the supervisor.
Driver Coordination
Assist in coordinating drivers and daily vehicle assignments.
Maintain updated driver records and documentation.
Follow up on driver schedules, routes, and assignments.
Assist in monitoring compliance with company fleet policies and procedures.
Support communication between drivers, operations, and other departments.
Logistics Support
Assist in planning and coordinating deliveries, collections, and dispatches.
Support route planning and scheduling to improve efficiency.
Track deliveries and provide updates on their status.
Assist in coordinating movement of goods between branches, customers, suppliers, and other locations.
Escalate delays, delivery challenges, or other logistics issues to the relevant supervisor.
Fuel & Expense Monitoring
Maintain accurate records of fuel usage and vehicle-related expenses.
Assist in reconciling fuel records, mileage, and vehicle usage.
Monitor fuel consumption and flag unusual variances.
Assist with preparation of fleet-related expense reports.
Documentation & Record Keeping
Maintain organized physical and electronic fleet and logistics records.
Assist in ensuring vehicle files contain valid and updated documentation.
Capture and update fleet information in Excel or the company’s fleet management system.
Maintain records of maintenance, fuel, repairs, accidents, insurance, and vehicle inspections.
Ensure logistics documentation is properly filed and easily accessible.
Reporting & Data Management
Prepare routine fleet and logistics reports as required.
Assist in tracking key fleet performance indicators.
Update daily, weekly, and monthly fleet trackers.
Analyze basic fleet data and highlight trends, variances, or areas requiring attention.
Support preparation of management reports.
General Operational Support
Support the Fleet & Logistics Coordinator in implementing operational procedures.
Assist with fleet audits and physical vehicle inspections.
Participate in stock, vehicle, and logistics-related reconciliations where required.
Perform other duties related to fleet and logistics operations as assigned by the supervisor.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
The intern's performance will be assessed based on:
Accuracy and completeness of fleet records.
Timely updating of fleet and logistics trackers.
Accuracy of fuel and mileage records.
Timely follow-up on vehicle servicing and maintenance schedules.
Efficiency in tracking vehicle movements and deliveries.
Accuracy and timeliness of logistics reports.
Proper filing and maintenance of fleet documentation.
Responsiveness to drivers and internal stakeholders.
Adherence to company procedures and safety requirements.
Demonstrated learning, initiative, and ability to work independently.
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
Diploma or Bachelor's Degree in Logistics & Supply Chain Management, Transport Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
Recent graduate or student seeking practical internship experience.
Basic knowledge of fleet, transport, or logistics operations is an added advantage.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word.
Good numerical and data-entry skills.
Previous exposure to fleet management or logistics is an advantage but not mandatory.
REQUIRED SKILLS & COMPETENCIES
Good organizational and coordination skills.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Good communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to maintain accurate records.
Basic analytical and problem-solving skills.
Good knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
Ability to multitask and prioritize activities.
Ability to work under minimal supervision.
Team-oriented and willing to learn.
High level of integrity and accountability.
Proactive approach to work.
End Date 30th September 2026

Job Description:

Job Title: One-to-One Elementary Teacher Assistant – French & English Speaking
Job Description:
Nature & Scope
We are seeking a caring, flexible, and experienced French- and English-speaking educator to provide one-to-one support for an elementary-aged student. This temporary position is designed to help the student successfully adjust to an English-speaking school environment while supporting academic progress, communication, social-emotional development, and day-to-day school routines.
The ideal candidate will be a patient and encouraging educator who can work closely with the student, classroom teachers, support staff, and family to help create a successful transition and increase independence at school.
Key Responsibilities
Provide individualized one-to-one support throughout the school day.
Assist the student in understanding classroom instruction, expectations, assignments, and routines.
Provide French-English translation and interpretation when needed to support communication and understanding.
Help the student develop English language skills in an encouraging and age-appropriate manner.
Reinforce classroom learning and provide additional explanation or practice when necessary.
Support the student's adjustment to a new school, classroom, language, and cultural environment.
Assist with organization, transitions between classes or activities, and completion of assigned work.
Help the student develop confidence in communicating with teachers and peers.
Encourage positive peer relationships and participation in classroom and school activities.
Work collaboratively with classroom teachers to adapt or clarify learning activities when appropriate.
Communicate observations, progress, and areas of concern with the appropriate teachers and school staff.
Gradually encourage greater independence as the student's confidence and English-language abilities develop.
Maintain confidentiality and follow all school child-safeguarding policies and procedures.
Qualifications and Skills
The successful candidate should:
Be fluent in both French and English, with strong verbal communication skills in both languages.
Have experience working with elementary-aged children.
Have teaching, tutoring, learning-support, EAL/ESL, or similar educational experience.
Demonstrate patience, compassion, flexibility, and strong interpersonal skills.
Be able to explain academic concepts in developmentally appropriate ways.
Understand that translation should support the student's transition while also encouraging increasing use of English.
Be comfortable collaborating with classroom teachers and other members of a student-support team.
Be dependable, organized, professional, and responsive to student needs.
Preferred: A teaching qualification, education degree, EAL/ESL experience, learning-support experience, or previous experience supporting multilingual students in an international school setting.
Contract
This is a temporary position beginning as soon as possible and continuing through December 2026. There is a possibility of extending the position beyond December, depending on the student's needs and the success of the arrangement

Job Description:

The Marketing, Communications & Fundraising Officer strengthens Kahawatu Foundation's visibility, donor engagement and resource mobilization by turning programme evidence and field experience into clear, compelling communications and fundraising materials. Communications, storytelling & publications

Work with programme and MEL teams to translate technical updates and evidence into accessible content for donors, partners and public audiences.
Ensure consistent branding, messaging and editorial quality across organizational publications and fundraising materials.
Website, social media & field content

Build productive relationships with donors, partners, producers, cooperatives, field teams and relevant service providers.

Bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, international development, business administration or a related field.
Four to six years of relevant experience in communications, fundraising, business development or donor relations, preferably within an NGO or development organization.
Demonstrated experience producing external communications and supporting proposals, donor research and fundraising initiatives.
Skills & Capabilities
Excellent English writing, editing, interviewing and presentation skills, with the ability to make technical information accessible to varied audiences.
Strong proposal-writing, donor-research, planning and information-management skills, with close attention to quality and deadlines.
Proficiency with website content management, social media publishing tools, Microsoft 365, digital analytics and SEO.
Ability to work independently and confidently in field environments; photography, video or graphic design capability is an advantage.
Strong judgment, initiative, organization and relationship-building skills across teams and cultures.
Fluency in Swahili and/or another language used in the Foundation's countries of operation is an advantage.
Experience managing website and social media content and working across cultures; East African experience is strongly preferred.
Familiarity with coffee value chains, responsible sourcing, sustainability or rural livelihoods is an advantage.
Additional Information
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Communications calendar maintained and agreed activities delivered on time.
Two to four high-quality impact stories or case studies produced monthly and four newsletters delivered annually.
Website reviewed monthly and substantive digital content published at least twice per month, with performance reviewed quarterly.
Ten to fifteen relevant funding opportunities researched or supported annually, with the donor pipeline kept current.
Proposal and donor-communication inputs delivered to agreed quality standards and deadlines.
Content and consent records from field activities accurately captured, archived and made accessible.

Job Title: Child Development and Disability Experts Opportunity
Job Description:
Are you an experienced professional in child development, disability, mental health, or family support? We are looking for people like you to join Whole Family Collective's Core Curriculum Adaptation Team, the group leading the adaptation of the World Health Organization's evidence-based Caregiver Skills Training (CST) package for Kenyan families of children with developmental delays or disabilities.
From this team, a smaller group will train as Master Trainers, leading CST delivery, facilitator training and quality assurance. Core Curriculum Adaptation Team members are engaged for approximately six months; Master Trainers selected from the group will be engaged in the programme through Year 1.
As part of this team, you will help translate a globally validated intervention into practice for Kenyan families: reviewing and critiquing the CST materials, contributing your expertise alongside a multidisciplinary group, working through stakeholder consultations, and helping test and refine the adapted package through a pre-pilot phase.
Key responsibilities
Core Curriculum Adaptation Team
Undertake a detailed individual review and analysis of the CST training materials.
Identify linguistic, cultural and contextual considerations relevant to adapting the package for Kenya.
Participate in adaptation workshops and work collaboratively to reach consensus on proposed adaptations.
Contribute expertise on child development, mental health, disability, caregiving and/or the Kenyan service and community context.
Contribute to stakeholder consultations with caregivers, service providers and other relevant stakeholders.
Help identify and address barriers to participation and implementation.
Contribute to the adaptation of examples, terminology, activities and other materials where appropriate.
Participate in the pre-pilot field test of the adapted CST package.
Support observation, feedback collection and documentation of the pre-pilot.
Contribute to decisions about whether and how the adapted CST package can be implemented within existing services and community settings.
Master Trainers
Participate in CST Master Trainer training.
Develop a strong working knowledge of the CST package and its core components.
Participate in supervised practice to develop CST training and facilitation competency.
Deliver the CST program directly to caregiver groups, leading facilitation of sessions.
Train additional CST facilitators during the broader rollout.
Lead facilitator supervision and fidelity monitoring.
Provide technical support and mentorship to CST facilitators.
Contribute to monitoring implementation quality and caregiver outcomes during Year 1.
Who we are looking for
We are particularly interested in professionals with backgrounds in:
Psychology / mental health
Psychiatry
Occupational therapy
Speech and language therapy
Social work
Child development / early childhood development
Public health
Education
Developmental disability
Other relevant health, social care or child/family disciplines
Essential
A relevant university degree and professional experience in the fields mentioned above.
Experience working with children with developmental delays or disabilities and their families.
Knowledge of child development, mental health, disability, or caregiver/family support.
Strong understanding of the Kenyan cultural and community context.
Fluency in English and Kiswahili.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Ability to review and critically engage with structured training materials.
Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team and contribute constructively to consensus-based decision-making.
Availability to participate consistently throughout the adaptation and pre-pilot process.
Desirable
Experience delivering parenting, caregiver, psychosocial, disability or early childhood interventions.
Experience training, mentoring or supervising other professionals, community workers or facilitators.
Experience working with community-based programmes or non-specialist service delivery.
Experience in programme adaptation, implementation research or implementation of evidence-based interventions.
Experience conducting or contributing to focus groups, interviews or other qualitative consultations.
Expectations
Consensus-based collaboration:
We expect all our team mates to engage constructively, share their expertise openly, and work toward consensus, including when views differ.
Confidentiality:
All team mates must maintain strict confidentiality when handling information about caregivers, children and families, in accordance with WFC’s safeguarding and confidentiality requirements.
Openness to observation and feedback:
Observation, reflection and structured feedback are integral to our CST process. We expect all team members to be open to receiving and providing constructive feedback to support programme quality and continuous improvement.
Time commitment
This is a project-based, part-time opportunity and not a full-time employment position. Exact dates and time commitments will be communicated to shortlisted candidates.
Compensation
Successful candidates will be compensated for agreed project activities and time commitments. Successful candidates will also be required to complete a background/police clearance check prior to engagement, given the nature of this work with children and families.

Job Description:
Job Summary: –
The Direct Sales Representatives will contact potential customers; contact potential clients, and work to sell them products and services offered by the Bank. They will also be required to handle basic customer issues and escalate where and when necessary.
Key Responsibilities: –
Actively sell and cross-sell the Bank’s products and services, targeting both new and existing customers to enhance the Bank’s market reach and product uptake.
Persuade clients to open accounts with the Bank, following up on dormant or unfunded accounts to encourage active usage and retention.
Maintain and update customer sales databases regularly, ensuring thorough follow-up on referrals to generate potential leads and convert them into clients.
Conduct market research during field assignments to gather valuable insights and feedback from customers, reporting findings to the sales managers / supervisors.
Actively participate in the promotion of new products and services, supporting marketing activations and campaigns to increase product visibility and customer engagement.
Prepare and submit daily, weekly, and monthly sales reports, tracking prospective business pipelines to provide management with updated sales trends.
Conduct presentations to potential customers to effectively communicate the benefits of opening accounts with Premier Bank Kenya (PBK), aiming to secure new account openings.
Undertake any other duties assigned by management to support overall business objectives and goals.
Qualifications:
Hold a Diploma in Sales & Marketing; A bachelor’s degree in business administration, Marketing, Public Relations preferred.
Professional Sales qualifications and/or experience a plus.
Have a minimum of one (1) year relevant work experience in a similar position with a proven result oriented track record.
Have strong sales, business development and customer service orientation/experience.
Competencies & Attributes:
Personality: A go-getter, enthusiastic, results oriented with excellent communication and social skills. A forward planner with clear focus, mature, reliable, hardworking and able to work without supervision.
Sound knowledge of the Bank’s products and services; CBK Prudential Guidelines (KYC and account opening requirements).
Job skills:
Knowledge in and understanding of markets and customer needs/trends
Have a high sense of professionalism, diplomacy and patience.
Passion for championing superior level of customer service.
Ability to network, build and maintain excellent relationships with customers and colleagues.
Ability to convince and close deals customers.
Have good PR/interpersonal skills, have outstanding reporting skills, problem analysis, time management and listening ability.
Computer skills: Must be adept in use of Ms Word, Excel, Access, power-point, Internet and email.
Honest and with high integrity.

Job Description:
Key Responsibilities:
Support the Laboratory Director and Principal Investigators in the overall leadership, planning, coordination and day-to-day operation of the Clinical Research Centre Laboratory.
Lead the implementation, maintenance and continuous improvement of the laboratory Quality Management System (QMS), in line with ISO 15189, GCLP, approved study protocols, institutional policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
Ensure accurate, reliable and timely laboratory results by overseeing pre-examination, examination and post-examination processes, including specimen collection/phlebotomy, testing and technical supervision as required.
Able to drive risk assessment processes across pre-examination, examination, and post-examination processes, and implementing corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) plans.
Serve as the primary laboratory point of contact for clinical teams, investigators and collaborators on laboratory operations, results, interpretation within scope, specimen flow and logistics.
Establish and maintain effective laboratory workflows, roles, escalation pathways and communication structures to support safe, efficient and accountable service delivery.
Conducting protocol for specific laboratory tests & procedures and writing and implementing laboratory analytical plans for newly implemented research studies.
Responsible for providing Laboratory Audit oversight by directing internal and external quality audits, managing non-conformity investigations, root-cause analyses, and ensuring timely audit closures.
Be able to establish, track, and report Quality Indicators (QIs) and key metrics (e.g., Test Turnaround Time (TAT), critical result reporting compliance, customer feedback, etc).
Coordinate shipment of biological specimens, including required approvals and documentation, compliant packaging, courier liaison, shipment tracking and confirmation of receipt with collaborating laboratories.
Liaise closely with clinic teams and strengthen the laboratory-clinic interface to support specimen quality, timely communication of results, participant safety and adherence to study protocols.
Coordinate laboratory regulatory and compliance activities, inspections, mandatory training and documentation, and maintain ongoing inspection and accreditation readiness.
Oversee reagents and consumables supply-chain control, including forecasting, procurement, inventory management, lot-to-lot verification, expiry monitoring, critical storage conditions and mitigation of stock-outs.
Manage participation in External Quality Assessment (EQA) / Proficiency Testing (PT) programs and ensure proper evaluation and corrective action for out-of-range outcomes
Responsible for all the laboratory equipment, instruments, analytical methods, and Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) and to ensure that the equipment undergo proper calibration, maintenance, validation, and verification before clinical use.
Maintaining laboratory records, data management and good documentation practices.
Ensures adherence to study protocols and enforce biosafety guidelines, chemical safety protocols, waste disposal regulations, and occupational health standards incident-reporting and emergency-response requirements.
Conduct staff supervision and competency by recruiting, onboarding, evaluating and mentoring laboratory staff. This includes documenting annual staff performance and appraisals, orientation and training of new employees.
Manage staffing levels, schedules, duty rotas to ensure uncompromised daily service delivery, as well as promoting continuous education, training programs, and safety updates for technical and administrative personnel.
Coordinating collaborations with other laboratories and technical interfaces with other laboratories, research teams and partner institutions.
Serve as liaison to internal and external investigators and collaborators and referral laboratories, ensuring clear communication of laboratory requirements, timelines and deliverables.
Oversee service level agreements (SLAs), equipment maintenance contracts, and third-party referral laboratory arrangements.
Ensures on-going integrity of laboratory samples by overseeing all handling and repository projects while assuring accurate documentation and adherence to protocols and to timelines.
Advise the Laboratory Director and Principal Investigator on technical, quality, staffing, biosafety and resource issues, and undertake other laboratory management duties as assigned.
Vacancy Requirements:
Possess a degree in Medical Laboratory Sciences or related discipline. Mandatory
Master's degree in a relevant science or laboratory-related field. Mandatory
At least seven (7) years’ experience in a busy clinical research laboratory. Mandatory
At least five (5) years’ experience in a management position. Mandatory
Experience working in an ISO 15189 accredited laboratory. Mandatory
Experience in carrying out laboratory testing for research and/or clinical trials. Mandatory
Experience in usage of Laboratory information Management systems (LIMS). Mandatory
Must possess a scientific imagination commensurate with the independent execution of research projects. Mandatory
Training in Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP); Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and Human Subjects Protection training are an added advantage. Added Advantage
Experience in laboratory audit processes. Mandatory
Strong technical troubleshooting, analytical thinking, data interpretation and problem-solving skills. Skills & Competencies
Demonstrated ability to supervise, mentor and develop laboratory staff, interns and students, and to manage competing operational priorities. Skills & Competencies
Strong leadership, communication, interpersonal, organizational and stakeholder-management skills. Skills & Competencies
Proficiency in standard office applications and the ability to analyse and trend laboratory quality-control and operational performance data. Skills & Competencies

Job Title: HR Director, Manufacturing Europe and Africa
Job Description:
As
HR Director Manufacturing Europe & Africa
, you will lead the People agenda across BIC’s manufacturing operations in Europe and Africa, encompassing 10 manufacturing sites located across France, Greece, Spain, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and potential other manufacturing locations in the region. You will partner closely with regional and site leadership teams to ensure that talent, organization, culture, and workforce strategies support business performance, operational excellence, manufacturing excellence, and long-term growth.
A key aspect of the role will be to elevate all manufacturing sites to BIC’s highest standards in leadership, culture, people practices, workforce capability, and organizational effectiveness. Through a combination of talent strategy, capability building, and organizational transformation, you will help build a world-class manufacturing organization and support the continuous development of manufacturing excellence across the network.
The role will also contribute to the evolution of BIC’s manufacturing footprint through productivity, optimization, acquisition, integration, expansion, consolidation, or restructuring initiatives, ensuring that people and business considerations are at the center of strategic decision-making.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the HR strategy and execution across manufacturing facilities in Europe and Africa, ensuring alignment with business priorities and operational objectives.
Act as a trusted advisor to regional and site leadership teams on organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, talent, culture, engagement, and change management.
Drive the regional people development agenda, including talent reviews, succession planning, leadership development, and high-potential programs.
Lead capability-building initiatives from assessment through deployment, ensuring the organization develops the skills required to support future manufacturing and business needs.
Partner with Manufacturing leaders to build a culture of manufacturing excellence by strengthening leadership capabilities, workforce effectiveness, operational discipline, and people practices across all sites.
Drive the harmonization and continuous improvement of HR practices across the region, ensuring all factories progressively operate at BIC standards in talent management, employee engagement, labor relations, safety culture, leadership effectiveness, and organizational performance.
Support strategic workforce planning and organization design initiatives to ensure the manufacturing network is equipped with the capabilities required to deliver future business objectives.
Lead the people strategy and execution for manufacturing footprint evolution initiatives, including network optimization, site start-ups, expansions, transfers of production, acquisitions, integrations, restructuring programs, and factory transformations. Ensure organizational readiness, workforce capability, effective change management, and sustainable employee engagement throughout the journey.
Lead the annual people cycle across the region, including goal setting, performance management, talent reviews, succession planning, and compensation processes.
Support manufacturing teams in delivering productivity, efficiency, and flexibility programs while ensuring sustainable people practices.
Oversee employee and labor relations across all sites, coaching local HR leaders and supporting constructive relationships with unions, employee representatives, and works councils.
Partner with local HR teams and Centers of Excellence to attract, develop, engage, and retain top talent.
Champion a strong culture of health, safety, well-being, inclusion, and accountability across all manufacturing operations.
Ensure the effective implementation of global HR programs, processes, and policies throughout the region while balancing local business and regulatory requirements.
Build strong relationships with senior leaders across functions, divisions, and geographies, providing strategic counsel on complex people and organizational challenges.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of HR professionals while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Identify, develop, coach, and mentor high-potential talent across the manufacturing organization.
Continually assess and improve HR programs, policies, and practices to ensure competitiveness, operational effectiveness, and alignment with business needs.
Ensure compliance with applicable labor laws, regulations, and company policies across all countries within the scope, minimizing legal and operational risks.
Partner with internal and external legal counsel on complex employment matters, strategic workforce initiatives, and organizational transformations.

THE ROLE PURPOSE
The role provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of staff benefits, and Payroll administration across all Group entities in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, South Sudan, and DRC Congo. It ensures the effective management of HR costs, benefits programs, supports payroll accuracy, statutory compliance, account reconciliations, productivity metrics, and service delivery standards. The role is responsible for optimizing employee cost structures, managing Group Life, Medical, GPA, Pension and Benevolent schemes, ensuring automation of key Reward processes, strengthening internal controls, and maintaining audit-ready documentation. It further ensures alignment with regulatory requirements across multiple jurisdictions while supporting subsidiaries to achieve consistency, accuracy, and operational excellence in Total Rewards execution.
THE KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Manage HR benefits structures, spearhead staff cost leadership initiatives, Ensuring benefit terms are fully in line with for Group policies.
Oversee multicountry payroll support functions, ensuring SLA adherence, reduced error rates, and timely delivery of annual review exercises.
Maintain accurate benefits administration processes including Group Life updates, GPA claims, medical membership management, and pension administration.
Support in monthly reconciliations of HR-related financial accounts including Oracle disbursement, 100% accuracy of medical database and pension trustee accounts.
Support in the automation initiatives such as benevolent benefit management processes, and other benefits-related workflows in liaison with all the key stakeholders.
Ensure compliance with statutory obligations across all operating countries, achieving zero penalties and operational losses.
Maintain complete, audit-ready documentation and support all internal/external audit processes.
Drive risk awareness, internal controls, and maintenance of an updated risk log across benefits.
Provide continuous staff education on benefits, ensuring at least two sensitization sessions per quarter.
Ensure timely service delivery on benefits SLAs and working closely with the medical team to ensure complete coverage of staff on the medical benefit and timely staff query resolution.
CORE ACCOUNTABILITIES AND DELIVERABLES
Financial Accountabilities
Achieve zero penalties and zero operational losses through strong compliance and financial controls.
Ensure accurate reconciliations of all HR benefits accounts by the 5th of every month.
Maintain accurate GL postings, financial schedules, and audit-ready documentation for benefits.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
The EHS Specialist will be responsible for supporting the implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) standards within the factory. The role involves conducting routine workplace inspections, identifying hazards, assessing risks, implementing corrective actions, supporting incident investigations, and promoting a strong safety culture across all departments.
Key Responsibilities
Workplace & Factory Inspections:
Conduct daily workplace, production area, warehouse, machinery, and factory inspections to identify hazards, unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, and HSE non-compliance.
Monitor compliance with company EHS policies, procedures, safe work practices, and applicable statutory requirements.
Document inspection findings and prepare reports for management.
Follow up on identified hazards and ensure corrective actions are implemented and effectively closed.
Risk Assessment & Hazard Control
Identify workplace hazards and participate in risk assessments for different work activities and processes.
Recommend appropriate control measures based on the hierarchy of controls.
Monitor the effectiveness of implemented controls and recommend improvements where necessary.
Support Job Safety Analysis (JSA/JHA) and safe work procedure development.
Safety Awareness & Communication:
Conduct daily or scheduled toolbox talks and safety briefings before work activities.
Conduct safety awareness sessions and campaigns for employees and contractors.
Promote positive safety behavior and encourage employees to report hazards, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
Incident & Accident Management
Assist in investigating workplace accidents, incidents, near misses, and unsafe occurrences.
Collect relevant information, interview witnesses, document findings, and support root-cause analysis.
Assist in developing corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
Monitor implementation and closure of incident investigation recommendations
EHS Training
Assist in conducting EHS induction and refresher training for new and existing employees.
Support training on PPE use, fire safety, manual handling, machine safety, chemical safety, working at height, and other relevant safety topics.
Maintain accurate records of EHS training and employee attendance.
EHS Documentation & Reporting
Maintain accurate EHS records, inspection checklists, incident reports, risk assessments, training records, and corrective action registers.
Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly EHS reports as required.
Monitor safety performance indicators and highlight areas requiring management attention.
Ensure EHS documentation is properly maintained and readily available for audits and inspections.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Monitor proper use of PPE within the factory and other designated work areas.
Identify PPE requirements based on workplace hazards.
Report PPE non-compliance and support corrective action.
Assist in maintaining PPE inspection and issuance records where applicable.
Qualifications & Requirements
Diploma or Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Health and Safety, Environmental Health, Safety Management, or a related field.
3- 5 years of Relevant EHS/HSE experience in a manufacturing, industrial, construction, or factory environment will be an advantage.
NEBOSH certification is an added advantage.
