Meru University of Science and Technology (MUST) was established by the Kenya Government under Legal Notice No. 103 of 18th July 2008 as a constituent college of Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology.

The idea of establishing a University goes back many years to the time when Nj...read moreuri Ncheke (Council of elders of Meru people) conceived an idea of establishing an institution of higher learning in Meru. Consequently, the NJURI NCHEKE ELDERS set aside 641 acres of land near the Njuri Ncheke’s Shrine at Nchiru for the same. In the mid-1960s, the elders initiated the process of establishing an institution of higher learning. It was decided that the Meru community raise funds for establishment of a College of Technology. As a result, Meru College of Technology (MECOTECH) was founded and opened its doors to its first batch of students in 1983 with an intake of fifty four (54) students all of whom were enrolled in Agriculture. In 1985 Motor Vehicle Engineering and later in 1987 building courses were introduced. MECOTECH offered diploma and certificate courses in automotive engineering, agriculture and extension, information technology, accounting, electrical engineering, building and masonry and business administration, among others.

MUCST had its first intake in May 2009, admitting forty five (45) students in three (3) degree programmes: Bachelor of Commerce (B-COM), Bachelor of Business Information Technology (BBIT), and Bachelor of Science in Information Technology (Bsc. IT). The institution has since grown to offer four (4) Masters programmes, thirteen (13) Degree programmes, eight (8) Diploma and five (5) Certificate programmes.
MUCST was formally launched by His Excellency Hon. Mwai Kibaki C.G.H., M.P., President and Commander-In-Chief of the armed forces of the Republic of Kenya on Saturday 17th April, 2010

The objective of the University is to play a leading role in the development and expansion of opportunities for higher education and research in Agriculture, Forestry, Mining, Energy, Water and Environmental Science and arid and semi-arid lands. The University aims at becoming a regional leader in the discovery, preservation and dissemination of knowledge in the area of Science and technology and related disciplines.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Facility supervisor will be responsible for the day-to-day operations of the data center. The Facility Supervisor will support in managing the installation, repair, and maintenance of critical facility systems, equipment and buildings.
The job holder will support the Facility Manager in leading the operations team, plan, execute projects to upgrade and improve our critical / non-critical infrastructure systems and develop the tools, processes, and safety culture necessary to effectively scale up.
Position and Job Magnitude
Latitude-This role reports to the Facility Manager. The job holder works in the Operations team in collaboration with other departments. External contacts include Clients, Contractors and Suppliers.
Level of Impact-The role is critical in maintaining the reliability and efficiency of data center operations.
Duties and Responsibilities.
Management Support
Assist the Facility Manager in identifying training needs for the Operations Team and coordinating relevant training and mentorship programs.
Manage and oversee sub-contracted workforce to ensure quality and compliance with standards.
Assign, prioritize, and review work plans, including providing estimates and inspections as required.
Support the Facility Manager on designated projects and initiatives.
Provide technical consultation and leadership on facility-related projects, reviewing system specifications within areas of expertise and monitoring implementation.
Plan and manage work schedules, including shift rotations and leave planning for the Operations Team.
Act as the Operations team lead in the absence of the Area Facility Manager.
Maintenance and Repair works
Execute preventive and corrective maintenance of buildings and equipment to minimize downtime.
Conduct daily surveillance and proactive monitoring of all data center systems and equipment.
Support the Facility Manager in planning and executing data center and equipment maintenance schedules.
Accurately document all maintenance and repair activities in a timely manner.
Oversee and document repairs and maintenance performed by contractors, ensuring quality and compliance with standards.
Proactively monitor SLA indicators, identify gaps, and implement corrective measures.
Provide input on power usage, capacity planning, and infrastructure optimization.
Serve as the first point of contact for the Customer Service Centre on technical requests.
Act as the first line of response for alarms, resolving or escalating issues according to established guidelines.
Customer Implementation and Service Delivery
Participate in the 24/7 call-out roster to ensure continuous operational support.
Execute the physical customer implementation process within the data center.
Collaborate with the Customer Implementation Department to install or supervise the commissioning and decommissioning of customer equipment, ensuring complete documentation of the process and outcomes.
Deliver Value-Added Services (VAS) to customers in line with agreed standards and timelines.
Procurement
Maintain an up-to-date asset register of all equipment within the data center.
Evaluate, coordinate, and submit purchase requests for materials and supplies for approval by the Facility Manager.
Research and recommend materials, coordinate with external vendors and contractors, and provide informal cost estimates or work sequencing updates to the Facility Manager as required.
Health and Safety
Collaborate with the Facility Manager and Health & Safety Manager to develop and implement safety plans for the data center.
Enforce iColo’s safety policies, procedures, and training programs, ensuring safe work practices are consistently applied.
Conduct regular safety training sessions for staff and contractors.
Monitor equipment and installations to ensure compliance with safety standards and regulations.
Support the Facility Manager and the Health and Safety Manager in developing and maintaining comprehensive emergency response plans and procedures for the data center.
Support in investigation of accidents and incidents, conducting regular safety inspections across the facility and common areas to ensure activities are carried out safely and appropriately.
Additional Responsibilities
Maintain accurate and up-to-date operational documents and reports.
Analyse operational data and reports, providing recommendations and decisions in consultation with the Facility Manager.
Establish and improve tools and procedures for monitoring, continuously integrating additional iColo systems into service monitoring as they become available.
Track utility consumption and propose efficiency improvement initiatives.
Maintain and update monitoring scripts to ensure accuracy of thresholds and alerts.
Develop and refine alert mechanisms and escalation procedures in line with management-defined SLAs.
Share knowledge and industry best practices by building close working relationships with operations teams and supervisors across the company.
Conduct working methods and initiatives to maintain and improve agreed PUE levels.
Support sustainability initiatives by monitoring energy consumption, identifying efficiency opportunities, and contributing to green data center practices.
Perform any other duties as assigned by the line manager or senior management.
Hard Skills
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
At least 8 years of progressive engineering experience, with a minimum of 4 years in a data center or other mission-critical operations environment.
Proven leadership experience with the ability to guide, empower, and develop technical teams.
Good understanding of data center technologies, industry best practices, and familiarity with construction and project management processes.
Strong technical expertise in the maintenance and operation of critical data center infrastructure, including UPS systems, generators, transformers, power distribution panels, and fire suppression systems.
Proficient in advanced Microsoft Office Suite (including MS Project) and AutoCAD, with the ability to quickly adapt to other applications and software used within iColo.io.
Soft Skills
Proactive, customer-oriented mindset with a commitment to operational excellence.
Strong attention to detail, combined with a practical, hands-on approach to problem-solving.
Effective leadership and team management capabilities.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively across teams and organizational levels.
Resilient and resourceful, with the ability to remain composed and solution-focused in challenging situations.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with sound judgment and the confidence to make timely and effective decisions.
Self-Motivated.
Ability to work independently while being a positive team player.

Job Description:
The Opportunity
We are looking for two people to join us as Quality Assurance Interns for three months. You will work directly with the QA Officer, getting a real look at how a QA function operates day to day— reviewing performance, monitoring task interactions, checking how member and staff requests are handled, and producing the reports that keep the organization accountable.
This is not a passive placement. The pathway — for those who earn it — is intern, then Assistant QA, then QA Officer. It starts here.
We are not looking for someone who already knows everything. We are looking for someone who pays attention, follows through, and is serious about building a career in quality assurance or operations.
What You Will Be Doing
Your time will be split across five areas. You will start by observing and supporting, and gradually take on more independently as the months go on. The two interns will each be assigned a set of staff portfolios to review, working in parallel under the QA Officer rather than on identical tasks.
Performance Monitoring
Every day, the QA function reviews how the team is tracking against their KPI targets. You will learn what the numbers mean, how to spot patterns, and what to flag before it becomes a bigger problem. By month three, you will be running the morning performance check yourself.
Task Interaction Review
Staff are assigned tasks through our internal system, and each task carries a record of what was done and when. You will learn to review these interaction logs — checking whether tasks were picked up on time, actioned correctly, and closed with the right outcome recorded. When something is off, you will flag it.
Member and Staff Request Review
Members submit requests — for loans, account changes, exits, and other services. Staff also raise internal requests, such as task corrections, data amendments, and exception approvals. You will learn to track both types from submission to resolution, checking that the right steps were followed, the right people were involved, and nothing sat without a response.
Reporting
The QA function produces daily, weekly, and monthly reports. You will learn to draft a few of them —starting with sections and, building up to full first drafts. Clear, factual writing is one of the core skills you will develop here. At the end of month three, you will also write a short personal self-assessment covering what you learned, how far you came, and where you still want to grow.
Staff Meeting Facilitation and Follow-up
The QA Officer chairs a weekly staff meeting with the full team. You will attend from day one, help prepare agendas and materials, and gradually take on facilitation of specific sections under the QA Officer's oversight. By month three, you will facilitate a full meeting — with the QA Officer present but letting you lead. You will also conduct follow-up check-ins with individual team members to see whether agreed actions have been taken.
How the Three Months Are Structured
Month 1 — Learn the Ground
You spend month one understanding how everything works. You shadow the QA Officer, read the SOPs, attend all meetings, and review real interaction and request logs with guidance. By the end of month one, you should be able to explain the QA function — and why it matters — to someone walking in off the street.
Month 2 — Start Doing
Month two is about trying things with a safety net. You draft reports, run the morning performance check, flag task and request issues before being prompted, and begin conducting follow-up check-ins independently. The QA Officer reviews your work and gives you direct feedback. You act on it.
Month 3 — Work Independently
By month three, the QA Officer should be reviewing your work rather than correcting it. You lead the morning performance check, submit reports on time, manage your own interaction and request review tasks, and facilitate a full staff meeting under the QA Officer's oversight. At the end of the month, you write a short self-assessment on where you started and where you ended up.
Who We Are Looking For
You do not need prior QA experience. You do need to be someone who pays attention, follows through, and takes their work seriously.
You are a good fit if you:
Are comfortable working with numbers and reading performance data.
Write clearly and precisely — no padding, no jargon.
Can keep track of multiple things at once without things falling through.
Take feedback well and act on it quickly.
Handle sensitive information with discretion.
Are genuinely interested in quality assurance or operations — not just looking for any placement.
It helps if you have:
Some exposure to Sacco operations, microfinance, or financial services.
Experience with Excel or Google Sheets.
A background in business, finance, social sciences, or a related field.
Experience in a coordination, monitoring, or administrative role — even informally.
We care more about attitude and aptitude than qualifications. If this sounds like you, we want to hear from you.
Where This Can Take You
This internship is the entry point to a defined progression: intern, then Assistant QA, then QA Officer. We built it this way because the best person to eventually run the QA function is someone who learned it from the ground up. Candidates who demonstrate real growth and consistent performance over the three months will be considered for an Assistant QA role at Mombo Sacco.

Although the Teachers Service Commission was established in 1967, its history dates back to the 1950s when teachers led by retired President Daniel T Moi vigorously fought for the formation of one teacher body.
 

Following the formation of the first teachers union in Kenya - the Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) in 1957 there was sustained agitation for the creation of an umbrella body to manage the affairs of all teachers. At the time, teachers were employed by either; missionaries, local authorities or the Central Government which led to a great disparity in remuneration and other terms and conditions of service. In 1964, The Kenya Education Commission Report (The Ominde Report) strongly supported the need for a competent, respected and contented teaching force. As a result of these factors, the Teachers Service Commission was formed in July 1967 through an Act of Parliament to give teachers one employer and uniform terms and conditions of service. It was charged with the mandate of registering, employing, promoting, disciplining and paying teachers.

The Role Purpose:
To lead the development, implementation, and oversight of a robust risk and regulatory compliance framework tailored to the dynamic environment of investment banking. This role ensures EIB’s capital markets, corporate finance, advisory, trading, and asset management activities comply with local and international regulations while proactively identifying, assessing, mitigating, and reporting on financial, operational, market, credit, liquidity, and reputational risks. The position acts as a key strategic partner to business lines, providing expert advice on regulatory interpretation, new product approvals, transaction structuring, and risk appetite alignment to support sustainable growth in a competitive investment banking landscape.
Key Responsibilities:
Risk Management:
Develop and maintain enterprise-wide risk frameworks, including Risk and Control Self Assessments (RCSA), Risk Registers, Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and scenario analysis specific to investment banking (market volatility, counterparty credit, operational resilience in trading systems).
Conduct risk assessments for high-impact activities such as underwriting, proprietary trading, and structured products.
Monitor risk appetite and limits; escalate breaches with remediation plans.
Collaborate with first-line business teams on risk identification in deal pipelines and trading books.
Support stress testing, capital adequacy (ICAAP), and recovery planning aligned with Basel
requirements.
Regulatory Compliance Leadership
Oversee the bank’s compliance program across investment banking activities, including deal origination, equity/debt capital markets and trading (equities, fixed income).
Monitor and interpret evolving regulatory requirements (e.g., prudential standards, market abuse, insider trading, conflicts of interest, client suitability, best execution) and ensure timely implementation.
Lead regulatory reporting, interactions with regulators (CMA, FRC, UFAA, IRS, KRA etc.), and management of inspections/audits.
Advise on new products, services, and transactions for regulatory risks and obtain necessary approvals.
Embed a strong compliance culture through training, policies, and awareness programs.
Support group-wide compliance initiatives including policy updates, compliance training, and culture enhancement.
Governance, Monitoring & Reporting
Participate in Risk & Compliance Committees; prepare reports for Board, Executive Risk Committee, and senior management.
Implement and test controls for key risks (e.g., Chinese walls, surveillance for market manipulation, AML in cross-border deals).
Lead or support internal audits, external reviews, and gap analyses.
Drive continuous improvement through technology (regtech, surveillance tools, automated reporting).
Intellectual Property & Data Protection
Maintain and protect EIB trademarks and other IP assets.
Monitor IP infringements and support renewal processes.
Support implementation of Data Protection policies and assist in breach management processes.
Stakeholder Management & Advisory
Provide proactive, practical advice to Front Office, Legal, Finance, and Operations on compliance and risk matters.
Build strong relationships with regulators, industry bodies, and peers.
Support business growth by balancing risk mitigation with commercial objectives.

Equity Bank’s business model and its visionary leadership has continued to earn local, regional and global accolades and recognition. The model is also studied in some of the leading business schools in the world, as other developing countries in Africa and Asia seek to learn from Equity’s low margin, high-volume model.

Equity Bank in 2010 established the Equity Group Foundation. This innovation and creative vehicle has fully transformed the concept of philanthropy and corporate social responsibility. While Equity Group Foundation champions the socio-economic transformation of the people of Africa and seeks partnerships along six cluster thematic areas, Equity Bank provides the infrastructure of delivery, hence reducing the operational costs for the Foundation and increasing the rate of return on any social investment. Job Title: Head of Investment Operations and Enterprise Sourcing
Job Description:
About the Opportunity
Our client is a leading African-based development organization that leverages the power of the private sector to address systemic challenges related to rural poverty, employment and sustainable development across the continent.
The organization supports innovative and high-impact commercial businesses, particularly within the agribusiness and renewable energy sectors, to develop and scale solutions that increase agricultural productivity, expand energy access, create employment opportunities and improve the livelihoods of low-income households.
Operating across frontier markets, fragile contexts and high-risk environments, the organization works with bold enterprises and partners to address climate risks, expand opportunities for women and young people, and build resilient communities.
We are seeking to recruit an experienced, strategic and highly analytical professional for the position of
Head of Investment Operations and Enterprise Sourcing
.
The Role
The Head of Investment Operations and Enterprise Sourcing will lead the development and management of the organization's investment operations platform, including the frameworks, systems and analytical capabilities required to support the construction and delivery of high-performing investment portfolios.
The successful candidate will bring strong investment discipline, financial analysis and process rigour across the full investment lifecycle, including enterprise sourcing, competition management, due diligence, financial structuring and Investment Committee processes.
The role will be responsible for ensuring that investment decisions are supported by high-quality analysis, consistent processes, effective governance and timely execution.
Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Sourcing and Competition Management
Lead enterprise sourcing competitions from end to end, including competition design, marketing, application management, scoring and shortlisting.
Ensure the integrity, quality, efficiency and effectiveness of enterprise sourcing processes.
Continuously improve competition design using pipeline yield data, applicant quality and conversion-to-investment insights.
Develop and manage complementary sourcing channels through proactive outreach, ecosystem partnerships and co-investor referrals.
Manage sourcing infrastructure, including CRM systems, pipeline tracking tools, marketing campaigns and application management platforms.
Ensure pipeline data is accurate, current, well-organized and readily available to support portfolio and investment decision-making.
Investment Analysis and Deal Team Support
Provide strong financial modelling, investment analysis and structuring expertise to support deal teams during due diligence and transaction structuring.
Act as a strategic thought partner and constructive challenger to sector and investment teams.
Strengthen investment discipline and analytical rigour throughout the investment process.
Build and manage strong analytical capability within the Investment Operations function to support investment activities across multiple sectors.
Investment Committee Process and Governance
Serve as the process owner for Investment Committee activities, including scheduling, agenda management and submission coordination.
Ensure the quality and consistency of Investment Committee memoranda and other decision-making documentation.
Confirm that all investment submissions meet the required standards for decision-readiness.
Track Investment Committee decisions, conditions precedent and post-approval actions.
Coordinate post-Investment Committee follow-through and documentation.
Portfolio Analytics, Systems and Reporting
Lead the development and management of portfolio analytics, performance dashboards and investment data infrastructure.
Ensure portfolio performance information is visible, accurate, timely and comparable across sectors.
Lead systems automation and digitization initiatives to improve efficiency, transparency and speed across the investment lifecycle.
Analyze portfolio-wide trends, patterns and lessons to strengthen investment decision-making and programme design.
Process Discipline and Continuous Improvement
Monitor and improve cycle times across the investment lifecycle, from enterprise origination through Investment Committee approval, disbursement and milestone delivery.
Identify bottlenecks and implement operational improvements without compromising investment quality and rigour.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives across investment operations and portfolio delivery.
Investment Frameworks and Standards
Develop, maintain and continuously improve frameworks and standards governing the investment lifecycle.
Develop and maintain due diligence templates, structuring playbooks, Investment Committee memorandum standards, valuation methodologies, financial analysis frameworks and risk assessment tools.
Ensure the consistent application of investment frameworks across sectors.
Refine investment standards based on lessons learned and portfolio performance.
Lead the ongoing development and refinement of catalytic capital frameworks, including guidance on the appropriate use of grants, repayable grants and concessional debt.
Team Leadership and Capability Building
Lead, mentor and develop the Investment Operations team.
Build investment and analytical capability across the wider organisation through training, coaching and structured development programmes.
Foster a collaborative, high-performance and investment-led culture.
Support analysts, associates and other team members to strengthen their investment and portfolio management capabilities.
Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate should possess:
A Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related field.
A professional qualification such as CFA, ACCA or an equivalent qualification.
At least
8 years of investment experience
across the full investment lifecycle, including sourcing, due diligence, structuring, Investment Committee processes and portfolio management.
Experience within impact investing, blended finance, development finance or related investment environments will be an added advantage.
Deep expertise in catalytic capital instruments, including grants, repayable grants and concessional debt.
Demonstrated experience designing and managing investment platforms, systems, processes and operational frameworks.
Experience designing and managing structured enterprise sourcing programmes, competitions or cohort-based investment pipelines.
Strong experience in financial analysis, financial modelling, valuation, investment structuring and Investment Committee processes.
A demonstrated ability to support and enable deal teams, sector leads or portfolio managers in a centre-of-excellence or platform capacity.
Experience working with early-stage portfolios and complex multi-stakeholder environments, including donors and concessional capital providers.
Strong leadership, people management and team development skills.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management and interpersonal skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
A high level of integrity, professionalism and sound investment judgement.
Key Competencies
The ideal candidate should demonstrate:
Strong investment and commercial acumen.
Strategic and analytical thinking.
Financial modelling and structuring expertise.
Process design and operational excellence.
Strong leadership and people development capability.
Excellent stakeholder management skills.
Ability to manage complex and multiple priorities.
High attention to detail and commitment to quality.
Ability to work effectively within complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
A collaborative and performance-driven approach.

Job Description:
Role Overview
The Sales Manager is responsible for driving sustainable revenue growth across the Synkron Group by developing new business, expanding existing client accounts, strengthening the sales pipeline, and improving the conversion of commercial opportunities across the Group's portfolio.
The role involves proactive market development across Synkron's industrial engineering and technical solutions, building strong client relationships, understanding client operational and technical requirements, and working closely with engineering, operations, projects, logistics, and OEM partners to develop commercially viable solutions.
The Sales Manager will also support the commercial growth of the Synkron Training Center by generating training opportunities, following up prospective learners and corporate clients, supporting learner and client onboarding, and developing long-term commercial partnerships. The role requires a commercially driven individual with strong business development, technical solution selling, strategic account management, and sales execution capabilities.
Key Responsibilities
Sales Strategy & Revenue Growth
Develop and execute Synkron's sales plan in line with approved revenue objectives. Translate revenue targets into clear sales priorities, pipeline requirements, and account plans while identifying opportunities to increase recurring revenue through services, maintenance, spare parts, training, and long-term client relationships.
New Business Development & Market Expansion
Build and maintain a strong pipeline of qualified new-business opportunities. Proactively identify and engage prospective clients through direct outreach, referrals, networking, industry events, OEM relationships, and strategic partnerships. Develop opportunities from initial engagement through qualification, solution development, proposal, negotiation, and conversion.
Strategic Account Management & Client Growth
Develop and maintain strategic relationships with existing clients. Identify cross-selling, upselling, repeat-business, and account-growth opportunities across projects, equipment, services, spare parts, and training. Conduct regular account reviews and work with operational teams to ensure effective delivery of commercial commitments.
Technical Solution Selling
Understand Synkron's engineering, automation, and technical solutions and engage clients to understand their operational and technical requirements. Work with engineers, technical specialists, OEM partners, and project teams to develop appropriate solutions and value propositions.
Proposal, Tender & Commercial Management
Coordinate commercial proposals, quotations, tender responses, and client presentations. Ensure proposals address client requirements, scope, deliverables, timelines, and commercial terms. Support negotiations, coordinate internal approvals, monitor submission deadlines, and ensure successful handover of won opportunities.
Pipeline, CRM & Sales Performance Management
Maintain accurate and up-to-date sales pipeline information within the approved CRM. Track opportunity values, stages, probabilities, closure dates, and next actions. Conduct regular pipeline reviews and prepare weekly, monthly, and quarterly sales forecasts and reports.
OEM, Partner & Channel Development
Build productive commercial relationships with OEMs and technology partners. Identify joint opportunities, coordinate client engagements and demonstrations, leverage partner relationships for lead generation, and support joint go-to-market initiatives.
Services, Spare Parts & Recurring Revenue Growth
Develop opportunities for preventive and corrective maintenance, technical support, system upgrades, spare parts, service agreements, and other recurring commercial arrangements. Work with technical teams to convert recurring client needs into structured commercial solutions.
Training Center Sales & Learner Onboarding Support
Drive commercial growth of Synkron Training Center programs among corporate and individual learners. Generate corporate training opportunities, follow up enquiries and prospective learners, support clients through available training pathways, and identify opportunities for repeat training and additional enrolments.
Cross-Functional Commercial Coordination
Collaborate with Engineering, Operations, Projects, Logistics, Procurement, Finance, Marketing, and regional teams to ensure commercially viable and deliverable solutions. Provide visibility of upcoming opportunities, support effective handovers, and share market and client feedback to inform product and service development.
Requirements
Education Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Commerce, Marketing, Sales, or a related field.
An Engineering or technical qualification combined with strong commercial experience is highly advantageous.
A postgraduate qualification in Business Administration, Sales, Marketing, or a related field is an added advantage.
Relevant professional sales, key account management, or commercial certifications are desirable.
OEM or industrial technology certifications are an added advantage.
Experience
Minimum of 5–7 years' progressive experience in B2B sales, business development, key account management, or technical sales.
Demonstrated track record of achieving significant revenue and sales targets.
Experience selling industrial, engineering, automation, manufacturing, technology, or other complex B2B solutions is strongly preferred.
Proven experience developing new business and managing enterprise or strategic client relationships.
Demonstrated experience managing substantial opportunity pipelines and complex sales cycles.
Experience developing proposals, tenders, quotations, and managing commercial negotiations.
Experience working collaboratively with engineering or technical teams to develop client solutions.
Experience with OEM relationships, industrial equipment, automation, technical services, or spare parts is highly advantageous.
Experience within African industrial and manufacturing markets is advantageous.
Experience selling training, certification, or professional development solutions is an added advantage.

DELIVERY
Identify and support the development of new funding opportunities and strategic partnerships that strengthen Kenya's carbon market ecosystem and expand GGGI's carbon finance portfolio
Deliver high-quality project outputs on time and within budget that meet program objectives, donor requirements and government requirements.
Quickly absorb and apply sufficient technical knowledge on Article 6 concepts, requirements, frameworks and approaches.

Job Description:
About the Position:
We have a bold ambition that will impact the lives of billions of patients. We are looking for an exceptional communications leader to make sure the world knows it and convince the relevant stakeholders to join our mission. This is a senior individual-contributor role for a builder and operator. This role comes with significant autonomy, direct access, and an equal high bar for ownership and impact. You will have the mandate to shape how Axmed shows up in the world. You will own our communications strategy, creative ambition, narrative, brand presence, thought leadership, and external visibility.
This is a sleeves-up, hands-on, high-energy role. We expect roughly 70–80% of this role to be hands-on execution, supported by strong strategic judgment and ruthless prioritisation. You will set the strategy and personally bring much of it to life: writing, editing, publishing, building decks, shaping campaigns, developing executive content, briefing agencies and partners, improving our digital presence, testing new formats and channels, using data to understand what works, and continuously shipping.
The mandate is simple: make Axmed impossible to ignore among the audiences that matter to our mission and growth.
The Person We’re Looking For:
You are passionate about what you do and an unusually strong communicator and exceptionally skilled storyteller who combines strategic judgment with very high execution capacity.
You can zoom out far enough to shape a company narrative and zoom in close enough to obsess over a headline, slide, caption, sentence, or call to action.
You thrive in fast-paced, tech-first environments and are comfortable operating without a large team, large budget, or elaborate process. Faced with ambiguity, you create clarity. You would rather test a strong idea, learn from the response and improve it than spend weeks perfecting a communications plan nobody sees. You have worked in healthcare before and are intellectually curious enough to become genuinely expert in the subjects Axmed has a right to lead on.
You should bring:
Extreme ownership, pace, curiosity, resourcefulness, and attention to detail.
Exceptional writing, editing, messaging, and storytelling ability.
A strong instinct for what makes an idea interesting, credible, distinctive, and shareable.
Experience building communications, brand, content, or thought leadership in a fast-moving startup.
The ability to translate technical or complex subject matter into communication that senior stakeholders can quickly understand.
Experience working directly with CEOs or senior executives on thought leadership and external positioning.
Strong digital and social instincts and an understanding of how content actually travels.
Comfort with communications analytics and using evidence to improve performance.
High proficiency with modern AI tools and a desire to build agentic and automated ways of working.
Experience in global health, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, technology, marketplaces , or another complex multi-stakeholder environment would be highly valuable.
What Success Looks Like:
The right people know Axmed and why it matters. We build awareness and recognition as a leading global health procurement infrastructure player.
Axmed has a distinctive voice. Our narrative is clear, memorable and associated with the issues we want to lead.
Our ideas travel. We earn media coverage, partner amplification, speaking opportunities and engagement from influential stakeholders.
Our leaders are influential voices. Their perspectives earn attention, invitations and opportunities from the right audiences.
Major moments break through. Launches, partnerships, market entries, fundraising and other milestones reach and influence priority audiences.
Communications drives growth. Our work generates partner, commercial, platform, investor and donor opportunities.
We achieve disproportionate output. AI, automation and strong systems enable greater speed and quality than our team size would suggest.
We know what works. Data guides which narratives, formats, channels, audiences and campaigns we invest in.
What you'll Own:
Narrative, Positioning & Brand
Own and continuously sharpen Axmed's overarching narrative and positioning.
You will:
Define and evolve the story of Axmed: what we believe, what we are building, why it matters, and why Axmed is uniquely positioned to deliver it.
Translate Axmed's value proposition for different audiences, including procurers, governments, donors, suppliers, pharmaceutical manufacturers, investors, and ecosystem partners.
Protect the quality and coherence of the Axmed brand across external and high-value internal touchpoints.
Content, Thought Leadership & Distribution
Build and run Axmed's external communications engine.
You will:
Own the end-to-end editorial and content strategy across Axmed's owned channels.
Own the right mix of owned, earned, paid and partner distribution to get Axmed’s ideas and company moments in front of the audiences that matter.
Personally create and edit high-quality content including articles, social posts, executive communications, case studies, presentations, reports, launch materials, partner stories, video concepts, and other formats.
Identify the ideas, insights, data, customer stories, and market developments Axmed has a right to speak about and turn them into compelling content.
Own Axmed's social media presence and execution across priority platforms.
Experiment continuously with formats, hooks, channels, and distribution strategies to expand reach and engagement.
Use partner channels, leadership networks, ecosystem platforms, events, and collaborators to extend Axmed's reach beyond our owned audience.
Be data centric and track communications performance and continuously improve what we create, where we distribute it, and how we communicate.
CEO & Leadership Communications
Turn Axmed's leadership into a strategic communications asset.
You will:
Build a distinctive and credible external voice for Axmed's CEO and other priority leaders.
Translate leadership ideas, experiences, and points of view into high-quality social content, articles, presentations, talking points, interviews, and other communications.
Proactively identify moments where Axmed's leaders should have a point of view rather than waiting for content requests.
Develop a repeatable executive communications cadence rather than treating thought leadership as a series of one-off posts.
Campaigns, Launches & Ecosystem Moments
Make important Axmed moments land.
You will:
Design and execute integrated communications around product launches, market entries, strategic partnerships, fundraising announcements, company milestones, and major commercial initiatives.
Build communications plans that connect narrative, content, social, partner channels, leadership voices, events, and earned opportunities.
Shape Axmed's participation in high-value conferences, panels, roundtables, and ecosystem moments.
Work with external agencies and partners where useful while remaining accountable for the thinking, quality, speed, and final output.
Lead end-to-end PR campaigns
Commercial Enablement
Ensure our communications make it easier for Axmed to win.
You will:
Work closely with Commercial to translate Axmed's proposition into excellent customer- and partner-facing materials.
Create and continuously improve pitch decks, one-pagers, partner briefs, case studies, leave-behinds, presentations, and other high-value collateral.
Build modular content and messaging that teams can quickly adapt for different markets, audiences, and use cases.
Ensure communications is involved early in product launches, market entries, partnerships, and strategic initiatives rather than brought in at the end to "make it look good."
Surface stories, proof points, customer insights, and evidence from across the business that strengthen Axmed's external narrative
Build an AI-Native Communications Function
Use AI and automation to give Axmed disproportionate communications leverage.
You will:
Build AI-enabled workflows and agents that accelerate research, monitoring, content development, repurposing, distribution, analytics, and communications operations.
Establish systems that help Axmed identify relevant conversations, ecosystem developments, partner activity, emerging narratives, and content opportunities quickly.
Help establish responsible ways for teams across Axmed to use AI while maintaining accuracy, judgment, confidentiality, and a distinctive human voice.

Sales & Revenue Delivery

Drive new customer acquisition, existing account growth, and SKU penetration across Nairobi, Central, Rift Valley, Western, Coast, and Eastern regions.
Lead key account management for top-tier customers — commercial farmers, poultry aggregators, and institutional buyers.

Drive product mix optimisation toward higher-margin SKUs and specialty feed lines.

Lead trade marketing execution: visibility, merchandising, shelf share, farmer field days, demo farms, and promotional cycles.

Lead customer satisfaction tracking and NPS where relevant.

Scope and monitor export and regional expansion opportunities beyond Kenya (EAC, COMESA, and the Gulf) across DOCs, hatching eggs, and feed — covering regulatory requirements, logistics feasibility, and potential customer or distributor partners — to build an options pipeline ahead of any future strategic decision to expand outside Kenya, notwithstanding that this is not an immediate priority.

Manage marketing budget and ROI reporting.

Work with Finance on credit control, pricing, profitability analysis, and monthly commercial reporting.
Work with Supply Chain and Logistics on cold chain integrity, delivery performance, and fleet utilisation.

Lead, coach, and develop the commercial team across sales, key accounts, trade marketing, and customer service.
Set KPIs, run monthly performance reviews, and build a succession pipeline.
Design, implement and monitor Commission based incentives for Regional sales teams

WHO WE ARE
Rafiki wa Maendeleo Trust is a charitable organization working in the rural area of Rarieda sub-County in Siaya County, Kenya. Our vision is people believing in themselves and working together to build a vibrant and progressive community. Our mission is to empower communities and build t...read moreheir capacities to create positive change for children and youth within their community. Our values guide our mission:
We promote sustainable environmental and socio-economic development to enhance future well being.
We encourage creativity and innovation for continuous adaptation, learning and growth.
We believe participatory approaches ensure communities own their development.
We advocate for human rights to promote dignity, diversity and respect.
We encourage accountability and transparency to assure integrity and credibility.

HOW WE STARTED
Rafiki started as a community development founded by the Director Michele Ostertag and her two friends, Monica and Solomon Ochieng. Touched by the hardships faced by children and villagers, the founding friends began with health treatment and education to the villagers. During the first two years, it became increasingly clear that given the socio-economic hardships of the area, one could not focus on treatment of diseases alone.

In September 2003, the initiative was registered as a Community Based organization (CBO) called Lusi Community Orphans Project. The CBO emphasized self-help through income generating initiatives such as chicken and dairy farming, beekeeping and crafts. The profits from these ventures were used to support up to 83 orphaned children with breakfast, school uniforms and weekend psycho-social activities. 

In 2006 the group decided that a stronger organizational structure and a more robust legal framework was required in order to grow the project into a professional organization. The Lusi Community Orphans Project was therefore reconstituted into Rafiki wa Maendeleo Trust (RWMT), which officially began operating in June 2006.

Job Description:
Role Summary
Nariana Enterprises Ltd. is seeking an experienced
Site Accountant
to support the financial and accounting activities of our civil engineering construction projects.
The successful candidate will be based at a construction project site and will be responsible for maintaining accurate site financial records, managing petty cash and imprests, tracking project expenditure, processing supplier and subcontractor documentation, monitoring labour and payroll costs, reconciling materials and fuel usage, and preparing regular site financial reports for Head Office.
Previous accounting experience within a construction, civil engineering, contracting, road works, or similar project-based construction company is mandatory for this position.
The ideal candidate should be comfortable working independently at a construction site while coordinating closely with the Site Agent, Project Manager, Procurement, Stores, Plant Department, suppliers, subcontractors, and the Head Office Finance Department.
Key Responsibilities
Site Accounting & Financial Records
Maintain complete and accurate accounting records for the assigned construction project.
Record and track all site related expenditure and ensure expenses are allocated to the correct project and cost category.
Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly site financial records and reports.
Maintain proper supporting documentation for all site transactions.
Prepare and process payment vouchers, expense vouchers, and other accounting documentation.
Verify supplier invoices against LPOs, delivery notes, quotations, and goods received.
Maintain schedules of outstanding supplier invoices, payments, advances, and other site liabilities.
Ensure all financial transactions are properly supported, authorised, and recorded.
Petty Cash, Imprest & Site Expenses
Manage site petty cash, imprests, and cash advances in accordance with company procedures.
Maintain accurate petty cash registers and supporting documentation.
Ensure cash advances and imprests are properly accounted for and surrendered within the required timelines.
Monitor site expenses and identify unusual, unsupported, or excessive expenditure.
Submit timely expense reports and supporting documents to Head Office Finance.
Labour, Wages & Payroll Support
Maintain accurate records of site labour and casual workers for payroll purposes.
Verify attendance and other payroll related information together with the relevant site personnel.
Assist with preparation and verification of labour wages and payroll schedules.
Maintain proper supporting documentation for labour related expenditure.
Track labour costs against project activities and approved budgets.
Assist Head Office with payroll reconciliations and statutory payroll information where required.
Materials, Fuel & Plant Cost Control
Track the financial value of construction materials received, issued, and consumed at site.
Work closely with Storekeepers and site personnel to reconcile material records and identify discrepancies.
Monitor and reconcile fuel purchases, fuel issues, and fuel consumption for construction plant, machinery, vehicles, and equipment.
Maintain records of plant, equipment, and vehicle related expenditure.
Assist in identifying abnormal fuel consumption, material variances, or unexplained expenditure.
Support periodic physical stock counts and reconciliation of materials held at site.
Project Cost Control
Track project expenditure against approved budgets and cost allocations.
Maintain project cost schedules showing actual expenditure and outstanding commitments.
Assist in monitoring project expenditure against budgets and BOQs.
Identify significant cost variances, abnormal expenditure, or potential cost overruns and report them promptly.
Work closely with the Project Manager, Site Agent, Quantity Surveyor, Procurement, and Head Office Finance on project cost control.
Support the preparation of project cost information required for management reporting and IPC related records.
Supplier & Subcontractor Accounts
Maintain accurate records of supplier and subcontractor transactions at site.
Verify supplier and subcontractor invoices against approved documentation and work completed.
Maintain records of outstanding supplier and subcontractor payments.
Assist with supplier statement reconciliations.
Maintain records of subcontractor certificates, payments, advances, and deductions where applicable.
Follow up on missing invoices, delivery notes, receipts, or other supporting documentation.
Reconciliations & Reporting
Perform regular cash, petty cash, supplier, material, fuel, and site account reconciliations.
Prepare monthly site expenditure and cost reports for Head Office Finance and project management.
Provide regular updates on cash requirements, outstanding payments, site advances, and financial commitments.
Ensure all balances and supporting records are reconciled before monthly reporting deadlines.
Assist with internal and external audits by providing site accounting records and supporting documentation when required.
Documentation & Internal Controls
Maintain an organised filing system for invoices, receipts, payment vouchers, LPOs, delivery notes, payroll records, petty cash documentation, and other financial records.
Ensure all financial documents are properly approved before processing.
Ensure compliance with company accounting procedures, approval processes, and internal controls.
Maintain confidentiality of company, employee, supplier, subcontractor, and project financial information.
Report financial discrepancies, missing documentation, irregular transactions, or control concerns promptly to management.
Qualifications & Experience
The ideal candidate should have:
Bachelor’s Degree or Diploma in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, or a related field.
CPA (K), ATD, ACCA, or progress towards a recognised professional accounting qualification will be an added advantage.
Minimum 4
years of relevant accounting experience.
Previous accounting experience in a construction, civil engineering, road construction, contracting, or similar construction company is mandatory.
Practical experience working with site accounts, project costs, suppliers, petty cash, imprests, labour costs, and construction related expenditure.
Experience working with supplier invoices, LPOs, delivery notes, payment vouchers, reconciliations, and project cost records.
Familiarity with Kenyan taxation and statutory deductions.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, spreadsheets, reconciliations, and data analysis.
Experience using Tally.
Ability and willingness to work at a construction project site, including sites located outside major towns where required.

Job Description:
Mission Description
The Change Relay plays a key role in the successful adoption of DRIVE 2030 new solutions within the country. Acting as the local change-management focal point before and throughout the deployment lifecycle, the Change Relay connects the Central Change Team, local country management, and users to ensure that business and operational impacts are understood, communication remains continuous, and local adoption needs are addressed. The role combines change impact coordination, local communication, stakeholder engagement, and adoption monitoring, with a strong focus on translating DRIVE 2030 changes into clear, practical, and operational guidance for local teams.
Based in Nairobi and reporting to the MD - Kenya, the successful candidate will be responsible for:-
Build and maintain a good understanding of the DRIVE 2030 ecosystem, deployment & change strategies, and key project milestones
Onboard local teams on the DRIVE 2030 program and its projects (DRIVE, DECLARE, CARLO...) and support early awareness and engagement though the organization of dedicated meetings and workshops and through the usage of a change kit provided by the DRIVE Central Change Team.
Participate in organization workshops and help assess impacts on roles, ways of working, organization, and local operations
Coordinate the DRIVE 2030 local Ambassadors' network. He/She is responsible for their onboarding and training, through the referential provided by the Central Change team. DRIVE 2030 ambassadors aims at supporting the Change Relays in their daily change activities and act as the DRIVE 2030 influencers.
Supports local HR teams and coordinates with central teams as part of the recruitment process deployment roles (with priority on Deployment Officers' recruitment).
Provides support to all DRIVE 2030 + STREAMLINE local project managers on change activities.
Ensure clear and regular communication on DRIVE locally, through the adaptation of the DRIVE communication kit and deploying of the DRIVE communication plan.
Monitor change adoption throughout the project using Change Surveys and other feedback mechanisms. Identify and escalate to the central change team any change-specific needs, risks, and resistance points that may affect user readiness or adoption
Work closely with the Deployment Officer, Training Coordinator, and local management to align change, training, and operational readiness
Maintain reinforced on-site presence during Go-Live and Hypercare to support managers and users
Profile
Strong knowledge of local operational processes and legacy systems
Experience with IT solutions and digital tools; TMS knowledge is a plus
Proven experience in change management, stakeholder engagement and internal communication
Skills & Competencies
Good understanding of the DRIVE 2030 ecosystem
Strong listening and stakeholder-engagement skills, with credibility among managers and users.
Strong communication, facilitation, and presentation skills
Ability to work effectively with central and country teams in a multi-cultural environment
Ability to animate a network of Ambassadors
Fluent in English

Job Title: Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery
Job Description:
Job Overview
The Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery is a senior global role responsible for making IRC's supply chains fit for scale across its most ambitious health and humanitarian programming commitments. The role is designed to translate strategic program targets into operational supply chain solutions that work at country level and ensuring country realities shape global supply chain strategy in return.
The role has three integrated areas of responsibility.
It serves as a primary GSC lead and contributor to business development: identifying, designing, and positioning supply chain funding opportunities with institutional and non-traditional donors, and leading supply chain sections of competitive proposals.
It provides support across IRC's Impact at Scale (I@S) thematic supply chains, driving end-to-end performance from demand planning and forecasting through sourcing, pre-positioning, and last-mile delivery.
It builds country and regional capacity to sustain health supply chain improvements over time, providing direct technical support, deploying to high-priority contexts, and harmonizing tools and SOPs across country programs in collaboration with Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs) and other relevant Global Supply Chain (GSC) units and IRC stakeholder departments.
Reporting to the Director of Emergency and Health Supply Chain, the Deputy Director works in close collaboration with the Health Technical Unit, Global Procurement, Regional Supply Chain Directors, Country Programs, IT, Finance, and external partners including UNICEF, WHO, ECHO, and peer INGOs.
Key Responsibilities
Leadership for Program Delivery
The Deputy Director plays an active role in GSC’s business development (BD) function. Supply chain is an increasingly fundable programming area, with institutional donors such as ECHO, SIDA, Gates and non-traditional donors explicitly framing requirements around operational efficiency, commodity management, and supply chain innovation. Additionally, private and corporate donors have expressed specific interest in funding the optimization of health and emergency supply chains.
Act as the primary GSC focal point within I@S agile working groups and cross-functional scaling teams, ensuring supply chain planning is embedded in program design from the outset and not treated as a downstream implementation task.
Implement the strategic direction for cross-cutting supply chain enablers including pooled procurement, global pre-positioning frameworks, harmonized delivery models, and digital systems and oversee their development and rollout across priority country programs.
Provide supply chain leadership and oversight for the addition of any new I@S Ready to Scale thematic areas, ensuring new commodities and delivery models are integrated into IRC's global supply chain architecture without creating fragmentation or duplication.
Serve as GSC's coordinating focal point with the Research and Innovation Department, contributing to supply chain innovations including AI-enabled solutions.
Business Development & Resource Mobilization
Is responsible for operationalizing the BD strategy, assembling inputs to create compelling bids, gap filling in the BD process as needed/relevant, and driving ultimate bid success through correct donor intel and positioning, strong bid submission, and effective cross-functional collaboration.
Flag, track and route relevant funding opportunities to GSC Leadership and work closely with internal stakeholders to plan for staff needs and business development capacity requirements to successfully write and budget for winning bids based on the pipeline
Lead or co-lead the technical design of supply chain sections for proposals where GSC has a primary role, including narrative writing, logical framework development, and supply chain costing.
Collaborating with program and business development leads to embedding supply chain considerations into program design, with specific attention paid to Impact at Scale initiatives
Contribute to bid assessment, probability-of-winning analysis, and positioning strategy for supply chain funding opportunities with specific focus on I@S thematic areas
Develop and maintain GSC supply chain capability statements and value propositions relevant to I@S programming areas, for use in capture and proposal development.
Participate in the BD review cycle for proposals with significant supply chain components, ensuring technical quality and alignment with IRC’s global supply chain strategy.
Mobilize opportunities with non-traditional partners such as Airlink to improve program delivery and increase cost savings
Take the lead with External relations and other fundraising teams to enable increased use of GIK goods and services, enabling program delivery whilst making IRC more cost effective.
Build and maintain donor intelligence on supply chain funding streams
Support pre-award activities including donor engagement, capture visits, and key personnel recruitment where relevant to I@S supply chain opportunities.
Coordinate with Regional Supply Chain Directors and country programs to ensure country-level supply chain needs and evidence are reflected in proposals.
Contribute to after-action reviews following award decisions to capture lessons and improve future supply chain BD submissions.
Identify and evaluate opportunities for business development & partnerships with academic or research centers, with Research & Innovation colleagues as appropriate.
Implementation of Strategic Initiatives Supporting Impact @ Scale
Strengthening global forecasting and demand planning systems for key health commodities.
Collaborate with Global Procurement to define sourcing strategies, monitor supplier performance, and ensure security of supply.
Lead global visibility efforts by consolidating country-level data on demand, pipeline status, consumption, and stock risks. Collaborate with GSC Systems and Data to digitalize as many aspects of this as possible in a timely manner.
Work with country teams to improve quantification, storage, distribution planning, and last-mile delivery.
Translate I@S targets into actionable supply chain plans with milestones, KPIs, and risk controls.
Design and support the rollout of cross-country improvements (e.g., pooled procurement feasibility, centralized pre-positioning, LMIS integration, preferred vendor strategies, emergency surge mechanisms, harmonized delivery models).
Support the implementation of the supply chain I@S bodies of work.
Escalate and advise GSC Leadership on global priorities, risks, and mitigation strategies impacting success of I@S activity plans.
Capacity Building, Country Support & Operational Strengthening
Provide specialized technical support to country supply chain and health teams.
Strengthening country practices in forecasting, contingency planning, supplier management, and stock-out prevention.
Support countries facing pipeline risks or operational bottlenecks; deploy to high-priority locations as needed.
Promote best practices and harmonize tools, guidance, and SOPs across all countries, regions and departments.
Train country and departmental staff as required. Develop e-training as funding permits.
Monitoring, KPIs, Reporting & Knowledge Management
Develop supply chain KPIs aligned to IRC’s LMIS, BD and I@S objectives.
Produce timely reports on global health supply chain performance, risks, and mitigation actions.
Document lessons learned and drive continuous improvement.
Maintain updated knowledge of global markets, procurement trends, supplier landscapes, regulatory shifts, and donor funding priorities relevant to supply chain programming.
Qualifications
Education
Master's degree in public health, pharmacy, supply chain management, strategy development, , international development, international relations, or relevant field or equivalent combination of education and work experience background is required or related field.
Work Experience
Experience in supply chain management in humanitarian settings, preferably with demonstrable experience in health supply chains, especially immunization, nutrition and sexual and reproductive health (SRH).
Proven experience in departmental or organizational strategy development in operations / supply chain in humanitarian organizations.
Expertise in forecasting, strategic sourcing, procurement, quality assurance, and distribution of health commodities including in the context of vaccine storage and distribution.
Experience in conducting assessments and evaluations of supply chain systems.
Experience engaging in business development processes, including writing and project design, proposal development, donor positioning, or capture for supply chain or health programming is strongly preferred.
Experience in developing and managing project concepts and funding proposals for humanitarian / development work with the ability to turn concepts and strategy into measurable action
Strong capacity to understand the humanitarian system and operating context and coordinate the relevant technical inputs from within and outside GSC
Familiarity with donor landscapes for supply chain programming (e.g., ECHO, SIDA, USAID, Gates) and ability to contribute to donor engagement and positioning.
Familiarity with managing large-scale, complex portfolio and experience using strategic insights and data from varied sources to support portfolio management, pivoting and alignment to organizational and sectoral goals
Experience in building partnerships for development and humanitarian funding as well as negotiation of programmatic and financial contractual arrangements with donors and partners
Experience and comfort interrogating partnership practices and familiarity with emerging developments including growing attention to power-shifting, localization and technical assistance models for INGOs
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
Proficiency in data analysis, visualization tools (Power BI), and performance monitoring.
Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills and ability to analyses trends based on a diverse set of data and insights
Digital supply chain literacy: familiarity with LMIS platforms, supply chain technology ecosystems, and data interoperability standards in humanitarian or low-resource settings. Experience with using AI-enabled solutions preferred.
Ability to identify fundable supply chain programming opportunities and experience in business development writing and proposal design
Ability to translate operational supply chain experience into compelling proposal narratives and capability statements.
Demonstrated ability to work with stakeholders at multiple levels and influence decision making
Knowledge of public and private fundraising - appetite and curiosity about building collaborative pathways with philanthropy and private sector
Fluent in English (required); proficiency in French, Spanish or Arabic.
Competencies
Strong project management and coordination skills.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in supply chain optimization.
Good organizational skills and ability to prioritize competing priorities effectively.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities; skills; ability to work cross-functionally and across cultures.
A sense of curiosity about how things can be done, and a willingness to get creative on solutioning.
Attention to detail and ability to identify and address potential risks proactively.
Commitment to ethical standards and accountability.
Additional Information
Frequent travel to program countries will be required up to 20%.
This position may involve collaboration with government agencies, international NGOs, private-sector partners, and institutional donors.
The role actively participates in IRC’s BD process, including pipeline monitoring, capture, and proposal development for supply chain funding opportunities.
Working Environment
Remote work / standard office (location dependent)

Job Title: Customs & Forwarding Subject Matter Expert (Short Term Consultancy Services)
Job Description:
Background & Objectives
Chwezi is Africa's integrated cross-border trade platform, built to serve the Great Lakes corridor and the East and Central African trade belt. The platform replaces fragmented ecosystems with a trusted digital infrastructure connecting importers, licensed clearing agents, and professional transporters. Before executing final Quality Assurance, an industry expert is required to conduct a strategic, operational review of the current staging environment to identify missing logistical requirements, compliance gaps, and process misalignment.
Scope of Work
Strategic Workflow & System Review: Assess the practical flow of operations across the Client, Clearing Agent, and Transporter portals, ensuring real-world variables like freight types and Incoterms are captured.
Compliance & Document Audit: Verify that the Digital Compliance & Document Vault and duty payment portals satisfy operational requirements for key revenue authorities (KRA, URA, RRA, DGDA, and OBR).
Milestone & Escrow Evaluation: Analyze GPS milestone checkpoints for operational realism and review automated escrow triggers to ensure they do not expose parties to undue risk.
Critical Gap Analysis: Identify missing steps or edge cases (e.g., extended customs holds) and provide a prioritized list for the development team before final QA.
Transit Cargo Checklist: Develop a comprehensive checklist of transit cargo requirements for the Kenya/Uganda, Kenya/Uganda/Rwanda, Kenya/Uganda/Burundi, and Kenya/Uganda/Rwanda/DRC corridors.
Deliverables
Pre-Launch Gap Analysis Report: A document detailing every missing operational requirement and workflow misalignment in the current build.
Resolution Roadmap: Actionable, prioritized recommendations for the development team to address identified gaps before code freeze.
Dispute & Edge-Case Advisory: A framework advising administrators on handling realworld escrow disputes and logistical delays using current tools.
Transit Cargo Requirements Checklist: A compiled guide detailing the necessary documentation and regulatory conditions for transit cargo crossing the specified regional border points.
Qualifications & Engagement Logistics
Experience & Mastery: 7+ years in cross-border freight forwarding and customs clearance along the Northern Corridor, with a deep understanding of EAC Single Customs
Territory procedures and national systems.
Vision & Communication: Ability to identify deviations from on-the-ground operational reality and translate complex logistics into clear directives for software engineers.
Engagement Details: This is a short-term, immediate-start role (remote or hybrid in East Africa), where the consultant will receive access to live staging links and demo accounts.
Access: The consultant will be provided access to the live staging links for the Customer Portal, Admin Portal, and demo accounts for the Client, Clearing Agent and Transporter.

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE
The Customer Care Supervisor is responsible for supervising and coordinating the customer care function to ensure that all customers receive timely, accurate, professional, and consistent service.
The role will lead the day-to-day customer care team, monitor customer enquiries and complaints, coordinate with Sales, Production, Warehouse, Logistics, Finance, Quality, and other departments to resolve customer issues, and ensure that all customer requests are properly followed through to closure.
The Customer Care Supervisor will also establish and maintain a structured
customer/project information management system
, ensuring that customer orders, production status, stock availability, dispatches, deliveries, payments, damages, claims, and complaints are accurately recorded and easily accessible.

CUSTOMER CARE TEAM SUPERVISION

Allocate customer enquiries, complaints, and follow-up tasks to team members.
Monitor team performance and ensure agreed customer service standards are maintained.
Coach and guide Customer Care Officers on effective communication, problem-solving, and customer handling.
Monitor response times and ensure customer enquiries are attended to promptly.
Review unresolved customer issues and ensure appropriate follow-up.
Conduct regular team briefings to communicate priorities, operational updates, and recurring customer concerns.
Identify training and development needs within the team.
Promote teamwork, accountability, professionalism, and customer-focused behaviour.
CUSTOMER ENQUIRY MANAGEMENT

Establish and monitor agreed customer response-time standards.
Ensure customers receive accurate information regarding:
Product availability
Orders
Stock
Production
Dispatch
Delivery
Payments
Damaged goods
Claims
Product information
Complaints

Monitor high-priority and urgent customer enquiries until resolution.
Ensure communication with customers is professional, clear, and consistent.

Product quality
Delivery delays
Incorrect quantities
Damaged products
Missing products
Product specifications
Installation concerns
Payment issues
Service quality
Ensure customers receive regular updates until their complaints are resolved.
Escalate serious, recurring, or unresolved complaints to management.
Analyze recurring complaints and recommend corrective and preventive actions.

Deliveries

Complaints
Customer communication
Resolution history

Delivery information
