Job Description:
Role description
BOMA is seeking qualified and experienced Mentors to deliver day-to-day implementation of the SOIL Program in Marsabit County. This is a field-based role whereby the mentor is responsible for program delivery by providing participants with monthly coaching, mentorship, facilitation, training, linkages to markets and follow-up activities to ensure the effective and quality implementation of the SOIL program towards the achievement of nutrition, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, savings, resilience, and child well-being outcomes. The mentor must be a member of the community/villages where the project is being implemented with clear understanding of the community culture, language and geographical coverage. The will serve as a frontline link between BOMA and participating households and community structures.
Reporting to the Field Officer, the Mentor will take lead in participant mobilization, targeting and enrolment, VSLA group formation and strengthening, capacity building, business coaching, monitoring progress of interventions and data collection. He/she will ensure smooth collaboration with key stakeholder in the community including the government structures relevant for the program deliver outcomes. The mentor delivery the expected roles with adherence to BOMA's program quality, policies, safeguarding, and accountability standards.
Responsibilities
KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Program Delivery and Participant Mentorship
Develop a strong understanding of BOMA's nutrition-sensitive poverty graduation approach, the SOIL Program design, and the Mentor's role in delivering the program in accordance to the approved program design, workplans, implementation guidelines, quality standards, and timelines.
Build trusted relationships with participants and provide practical, participant-centered coaching and mentorship based on individual and household needs.
Conduct monthly mentorship sessions with assigned participants, Business Groups (BGs), Savings Groups/VSLAs, and households, ensuring that agreed actions are followed up
Track participant progress, identify households or groups that are falling behind, and provide targeted support or escalate issues to the Field Officer.
Facilitate household visioning and action planning to help participants set realistic livelihood, nutrition, savings, and well-being goals and monitor progress towards them.
Ensure that program activities are delivered efficiently and contribute to agreed participant and program-level results and targets.
Use BOMA's digital systems, tablets, monitoring platforms, and program tools to plan, document, track, and report implementation.
Identify implementation challenges and recommend practical adaptations to improve participant engagement, program quality, and results.
Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development
Deliver trainings to the participants on lifeskills, entrepreneurship, agri-nutrition, market linkages and financial literacy in accordance with the training manuals and standards
Guide participants to identify viable, context-specific and market-driven livelihood and enterprise opportunities based on local resources, skills, demand, risks, and household circumstances.
Support participants to start and strengthen viable enterprises across appropriate livelihood opportunities, including livestock trading, food production and trading, value addition, regenerative agriculture, service businesses, and nature-based enterprises.
Coach participants in developing and implementing simple business plans, including business objectives, start-up requirements, costing, pricing, sales, cash-flow management, and profitability.
Strengthen participants' practical business management skills, including record keeping, stock management, customer management, cash management, and business performance tracking.
Coach participants on profit management, savings, reinvestment, and responsible use of business income to support enterprise growth and household well-being.
Conduct monthly enterprise follow-up to assess business performance, identify challenges, and support participants to develop practical solutions.
Facilitate linkages between participants and relevant markets, buyers, suppliers, aggregators, financial service providers, business development services, and other market actors.
Identify opportunities for participants to diversify income sources and promote enterprises that can contribute to improved household access to nutritious foods and strengthen the local food system.
Savings and Financial Inclusion
Support the formation, strengthening, and effective functioning of Savings Groups/VSLAs, in line with BOMA's approved approach and standards.
Facilitate group sessions on savings, responsible borrowing, household budgeting, financial planning, and appropriate use of loans.
Coach participants to set savings goals and use savings strategically for productive investments, enterprise development, household needs, and resilience-building.
Monitor Savings Group performance and identify governance, participation, record-keeping, or financial management challenges requiring additional support.
Support viable Savings Groups and participants to establish linkages with appropriate formal financial institutions and other financial service providers.
Promote responsible financial decision-making and discourage borrowing that may increase household vulnerability.
Food Security, Nutrition and Child Well-being
Deliver the SOIL nutrition resilience package through regular household and group-level training, coaching, follow-up, and practical demonstrations.
Facilitate monthly agri-nutrition sessions covering food production, food utilization, dietary diversity, nutrition-sensitive livelihoods, and household resilience.
Provide practical nutrition education and counselling within the Mentor's scope, with appropriate referrals to qualified health and nutrition service providers where required.
Support households to understand the link between income, food production, food access, dietary diversity, nutrition practices, and child well-being.
Promote consumption of diverse, locally available, affordable, and nutritious foods, including indigenous and traditional foods.
Support households to establish and maintain kitchen gardens, poultry, and other appropriate nutrition-sensitive activities, taking into account water availability, climate, land access, household capacity, and local conditions.
Conduct household follow-up to assess adoption of recommended food security and nutrition practices and provide practical support to address barriers.
Facilitate household dialogues on nutrition, food security, livelihoods, budgeting, caregiving practices, and child well-being, including household action planning.
Support nutrition screening and identification of children or household members requiring referral, in collaboration with Community Health Promoters (CHPs) and qualified health and nutrition actors.
Ensure identified cases requiring health, nutrition, protection, or other specialized services are appropriately referred and followed up in accordance with program protocols.
Support households to translate improved livelihood and income opportunities into improved food consumption, dietary diversity, and child well-being outcomes.
Household Resilience, Regenerative Practices and Community Engagement
Support households to identify key livelihood, food security, nutrition, climate, and economic risks affecting their well-being.
Coach households to develop practical actions to prepare for, manage, and recover from shocks.
Promote appropriate regenerative agriculture, sustainable natural resource management, and climate-resilient livelihood practices at household and community level.
Support participants to adopt practical approaches that improve household productivity while protecting and restoring natural resources.
Mobilize and engage community members in relevant SOIL activities and promote ownership of program interventions.
Build effective working relationships with community leaders, Location Committees, CHPs, government extension officers, schools, health facilities, and other relevant stakeholders.
Promote appropriate participation of men, youth, and other household members in livelihood, nutrition, food security, and child well-being activities.
Identify and nurture community champions who can demonstrate good practices and encourage peer learning and adoption among other households.
Monitoring, Data Management and Reporting
Collect and submit accurate, complete, timely, and verifiable program data using approved BOMA digital and reporting tools.
Maintain accurate records of participant, household, Business Group, and Savings Group activities and progress.
Update participant records and digital systems promptly following mentorship, training, household visits, and group sessions.
Monitor individual and household progress against agreed goals, milestones, and program graduation or outcome indicators.
Use available participant data to identify households requiring additional coaching, follow-up, referral, or escalation.
Report implementation progress, emerging risks, participant concerns, and significant challenges to the Field Officer in a timely manner.
Document success stories, innovations, adaptations, lessons learned, and good practices for program learning.
Participate in program reviews, data quality checks, learning sessions, and reflection meetings as required.
Ensure that all data collected is accurate and that participant information is handled confidentially and in accordance with BOMA's data protection requirements.
Program Quality, Accountability and Safeguarding
Implement all activities in accordance with BOMA's program standards, policies, safeguarding requirements, accountability commitments, and ethical standards.
Treat all participants with dignity, respect, and fairness and ensure inclusive participation in program activities.
Explain BOMA's feedback, complaints, and safeguarding mechanisms to participants and ensure they know how and where to raise concerns.
Promptly report safeguarding, protection, fraud, exploitation, abuse, or other serious concerns through established reporting channels.
Maintain strict confidentiality of participant information and only collect, use, or share information for authorized program purposes.
Identify and escalate implementation risks that may affect participant safety, program quality, or achievement of results.
Support BOMA's commitment to Do No Harm, inclusion, gender equality, and protection of vulnerable participants.
Field Operations and Resource Management
Plan and organize daily field activities and maintain accurate movement plans, fuel, mileage, and activity records in accordance with BOMA procedures and policies
Ensure effective use of assigned program resources, including tablets, phones, training materials, motorcycles, and other equipment.
Maintain assigned equipment in good working condition and report loss, damage, faults, or maintenance requirements promptly.
Submit required activity, fuel, movement, airtime, data bundles and other operational documentation within agreed timelines.
Use program resources responsibly and ensure activities are delivered in a cost-effective manner without compromising quality.
Comply with BOMA's field security, health and safety, travel, and operational procedures.
Teamwork and Coordination
Work closely with the Field Officer, Program Manager, Community Health Promoters, technical teams, and other departmental staff to ensure coordinated delivery of the SOIL program package.
Participate actively in team meetings, supervision sessions, trainings, coaching sessions, and program review meetings.
Share field-level insights, participant feedback, emerging risks, and implementation lessons with the program team.
Support other team members during major program activities, participant mobilization, assessments, trainings, and community events as required.
Contribute to a positive team culture based on accountability, collaboration, respect, learning, and continuous improvement.
Other Responsibilities
Perform any other duties reasonably assigned by the Field Officer or Program Manager that contribute to the effective implementation and achievement of SOIL Program objectives.
Requirements
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIRED COMPETENCIES
At least a Diploma in Business Administration, Entrepreneurship, Agribusiness, Agriculture, Community Development, Nutrition, Community Health, Public Health, Social Work, Development Studies, Project Management or another relevant field.
At least 2 years of relevant experience in community-based programme implementation, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, nutrition, agriculture, economic inclusion, financial inclusion or resilience programming.
Demonstrated experience in community mobilization, participant mentorship, business coaching or savings group facilitation.
Experience working with women, pastoralist communities or other vulnerable and rural populations is highly desirable.
Experience using digital data collection tools and Microsoft Office is desirable.
Good interpersonal and communication skills.
Good coaching and facilitation skills.
Ability to work independently with minimum supervision.
Motivated, self-driven and accountable.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Must be a resident of the respective SOIL program implementation location/village.
Fluency in English and Kiswahili.
Fluency in the relevant local language spoken in the assigned location.
Strong basic computer and digital literacy.
Ability to work in remote and challenging environments.
Must have a Valid motorcycle riding license Class A1/A2. This is mandatory because the mentor is required to ride a motorcycle daily as he/she delivers the program activities in the field.

Company Details: Ol Pejeta is the largest black rhino sanctuary in east Africa, and home to three of the world’s last remaining northern white rhino. It is the only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, in a Sanctuary established to rehabilitate animals rescued from the black market. It has some of the highest...read morepredator densities in Kenya, and still manages a very successful livestock programme. Ol Pejeta also seeks to support the people living around its borders, to ensure wildlife conservation translates to better education, healthcare and infrastructure for the next generation of wildlife guardians. In 2004, the ranch was purchased by the U.K.-based conservation organisation, Fauna &Flora International (FFI), with the financial backing of the Arcus Foundation, a private international philanthropic organisation founded by Jon Stryker. The land purchase was wholly funded by a $15 million donation from the Arcus Foundation, which worked in tandem with FFI and the Lewa Wildlife Conservancy to secure the 90,000 acres of open Savannah grassland and convert it to a national land trust. The conservation of the natural habitat, located in Kenya’s Laikipia Plateau, ensured the protection of existing rhino, elephant, and other wildlife populations in addition to captive chimpanzees living in a 300-acre sanctuary. The Arcus Foundation also gave $12 million to fund capital and institutional development costs at the conservancy. That initial injection of funding allowed Ol Pejeta Conservancy to fulfill its business model as a Kenyan-owned operation benefiting local community development and economic growth in addition to its impact on conservation. Today, the Arcus Foundation continues to support the conservancy through its membership on the Board of Trustees and the funding of various initiatives. In 2014, Ol Pejeta achieved IUCN Green List status, one of only two conservancies in Africa to be awarded this. IUCN Green Listing aims to define excellence in managing valuable natural areas. We have also been awarded the TripAdvisor Certificate of Excellence three years running - a testament to the incredible experiences treasured by all who visit Ol Pejeta. In 2015, we published our 2020 Management Plan - which was developed by our staff in consultation with a range of stakeholders, and sets out our vision for the years leading up to 2020, outlining the major projects that will help us to deliver our vision. We want to become an innovative and sustainable model that conserves biodiversity (particularly endangered species) and contributes to economic growth and the improvement of the livelihoods of rural communities.

Familiarity with External Quality Assurance/Proficiency Testing (EQA/PT) schemes, RTCQI/LCQI processes, and laboratory accreditation preparation (e.g., SLIPTA).

Strong technical writing, data analysis, and report-writing skills.
Excellent interpersonal, mentorship, and stakeholder-engagement skills, with the ability to work effectively with county government officials, FBO facility leadership, and national reference institutions.
High level of integrity, sound judgement, and commitment to CHAK’s mission and values.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and meet milestone-linked deadlines under a results-based (Fixed Amount Award) funding model.
Strong computer literacy, including proficiency with laboratory and health data systems and standard office software.

Job Description:
Job Purpose:
The role holder is responsible for handling Card Issuing and acquiring business disputes as per VISA and MasterCard Rules and Regulations and existing Bank Operational procedures.
Roles & Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities:
Investigate and initiate financial disputes raised by internal and external bank clients as mandated by scheme rules and procedures.
Follow up on disputes process as per the scheme (Mastercard and VISA) manuals to manage correct resolution with no financial loss is experienced.
Collecting evidence, determination of the validity of a dispute and based on findings making decisions and engagement of key stake holders’ merchants and banks clients.
Internal Stakeholder (branches, Call Center, and Complaints Handling Unit) Engagement with an aim of ensuring that dispute management is understood, and correct procedures are appropriately followed when raising the complaints.
Tracking card disputes raised and received from other banks.
Review of Outstanding Card Reconciliation Exceptions to ensure no outstanding reconciliation items beyond SLA.
Analyze card related disputes to identify thematic issues that could portray fraudulent attack for reporting/escalation. Work closely with the card fraud monitoring team on the same.
Ensure timely submission of monthly reports to the bank stakeholders, regulators, and quarterly reports submission to the Card Schemes.
Processing of incoming and outgoing files from Card schemes portals into/from the bank Card management system within the set SLAs.
GL and Loyalty file generation for processing into the core banking systems.
Ensuring all card scheme settlement obligations are posted in core banking and remittances sent to Visa and Mastercard settlement banks.
Upskilled to ensure that analyst keeps up with scheme mandated rules which enhances the ability to manage both external and internal stakeholders.
Academic Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Banking or related field.
Work Experience Required:
At Least one (1) year relevant experience.
Competencies:
Planning & Organizational skills.
Analytical skills and attention to detail.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Interpersonal skills to manage stakeholders at all levels.
Ethics and integrity.
Excellent judgment and analytical abilities and impeccable integrity.
Strong commercial awareness and an ability to connect to business goals.
Experience in Business Continuity Planning and Disaster recovery.
Risk management skills.

Job Description:
Role Overview
AFIDEP is seeking to recruit an experienced
Head of Finance and Operations (HoFO)
to join its Senior Management Team. The HoFO is a critical leadership role responsible for the financial health, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance of the Institute across all its country offices and programmes.
The successful candidate will be a strategic, results-oriented leader who combines deep technical expertise in finance and accounting with the ability to manage diverse operational functions — including administration, procurement, ICT, and facilities — and to lead and develop a multifunctional team. The HoFO will serve as the Institute’s primary financial steward, ensuring that resources are managed with rigour, transparency, and accountability to donors, the Board, and the communities AFIDEP serves.
This is a senior leadership role. Candidates must demonstrate both the strategic vision to drive institutional financial planning and the operational rigour to ensure robust systems, controls, and compliance across a complex, multi-donor, multi-currency environment.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Financial Leadership
Institutional Financial Strategy:
Contribute to the development of AFIDEP’s institutional strategic plans, translating organisational priorities into multi-year financial plans and resource frameworks.
Annual Planning & Budgeting:
Lead the annual institutional planning and budgeting process, including financial resource allocation, cash flow projections, and cost recovery planning across all projects and country offices.
Resource Mobilisation Support:
Contribute to institutional resource mobilisation efforts by developing budgets for new grant proposals, reviewing donor agreements for financial feasibility, and advising on cost structures and indirect cost recovery rates.
Financial Performance Oversight:
Monitor and report on financial performance against approved plans and budgets; provide the Executive Director and Senior Management Team with timely, actionable financial analysis and risk insights.
Policy development and implementation oversight
:
Lead the development, review and execution of financial management, grant management, cost allocation, procurement, and related policies for input by the Senior Management Team and approval by the Board.
Financial Management & Reporting
Finance & Accounting Operations:
Oversee all finance and accounting functions, including general ledger management, accounts payable and receivable, payroll, bank reconciliations, and month-end and year-end close processes.
Treasury & Cash Management:
Manage treasury operations including foreign currency management, banking relationships, investment of institutional reserves, and maintenance of adequate liquidity across all country offices.
Financial Reporting:
Ensure the preparation and timely submission of accurate financial reports for the Board, Executive Director, donors, and statutory authorities, in compliance with applicable accounting standards (IFRS) and donor requirements.
Board & Audit Committee Engagement:
Present financial reports, budget updates, and risk assessments to the Board and Finance/Audit Committee on a regular basis; serve as a trusted financial adviser to Board-level governance structures.
External Audits:
Coordinate and manage the annual external audit process, maintaining audit-readiness throughout the year and implementing audit recommendations in a timely manner.
Payroll & Tax Compliance:
Ensure accurate and timely payroll processing and compliance with statutory deductions, tax obligations, and labour law requirements in Kenya and Malawi, and any other jurisdictions where AFIDEP operates.
Grants & Donor Compliance
Grants Management:
Provide oversight of the full grants management lifecycle — from award acceptance and budget activation through expenditure tracking, financial reporting, and grant close-out — ensuring strict adherence to donor-specific financial requirements.
Donor Compliance:
Extensive experience managing finances in a complex multi-donor environment, with knowledge of the requirements of bilateral, multilateral and private foundation donors.
Sub-Grantee Management:
Oversee financial due diligence, contracting, monitoring, and capacity building for sub-grantees and implementing partners.
Donor & Partner Relations:
Maintain strong, trust-based financial relationships with donors and partners, managing financial queries, facilitating donor financial reviews, and proactively communicating on budget variances or compliance matters.
Risk Management & Internal Controls
Internal Control Environment:
Design, implement, and continuously improve financial and operational internal controls to safeguard institutional assets, prevent fraud and conflict of interest, and ensure compliance with applicable policies, laws, and regulations.
Asset Management:
Maintain an accurate and up-to-date institutional asset register; ensure appropriate insurance coverage for all institutional assets and operations.
Risk Management:
Lead the identification, assessment, and mitigation of financial and operational risks; maintain the institutional risk register and report risk status to the Senior Management Team and Board.
Audit & Compliance Oversight:
Provide administrative line management to the Audit and Compliance Officer, supporting the effective functioning of the internal audit function while safeguarding its independence. Ensure timely implementation of internal audit recommendations.
Operations Management
Administration & Facilities:
Provide strategic oversight of institutional administration, including facilities management, office operations, lease agreements, and vendor contracts across all AFIDEP offices.
Procurement:
Ensure the development and consistent application of transparent, value-for-money procurement policies and procedures, including supplier prequalification, tendering, and contract management.
ICT Governance:
Oversee AFIDEP’s ICT infrastructure and systems, ensuring that technology investments support institutional effectiveness, data security, and business continuity.
Policy and
Systems Development:
Lead the continuous development, refinement, and upgrading of financial and operational management policies and systems to ensure robust, efficient, and audit-ready institutional infrastructure.
Team Leadership & Development
Team Management:
Recruit, lead, mentor, and develop the Finance and Operations team across all AFIDEP locations, fostering a high-performance, collaborative, and learning-oriented culture.
Capacity Building:
Build the financial management and operational capacity of non-finance staff across the Institute, ensuring that programme teams understand and adhere to financial and compliance requirements.
Succession & Continuity:
Identify and develop internal talent to ensure continuity of key finance and operations functions and build organisational resilience.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential
Education:
A Master’s degree and Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a closely related field from a recognised university.
Professional Certification:
A full, current professional accounting qualification is mandatory — CPA, ACA, ACCA, ACMA, CFA, or equivalent.
Professional Membership:
Current membership in good standing with a recognised professional accountancy body (e.g. ICPAK in Kenya, ICAM in Malawi, ACCA, ICAEW, or equivalent).
Senior Experience:
A minimum of 10 years’ progressive professional experience in finance and operations, with at least 5 years in a senior, multifunctional leadership role — preferably as Head of Finance, Director of Finance and Operations, or equivalent — within an international NGO, research organisation, or development institution.
Multi-Donor Environment:
Extensive experience managing finances in a multi-donor environment, with demonstrated hands-on familiarity with the financial regulations and compliance requirements of major international development
Multi-Country & Multi-Currency:
Demonstrated experience managing financial operations across multiple country offices and currencies, including foreign exchange risk management and consolidated multi-currency reporting.
People Leadership:
Proven ability to lead, manage, and develop high-performing, multifunctional teams; experience building team capacity and managing staff across geographically dispersed locations.
Financial Systems:
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central or a comparable ERP system, Microsoft Excel and financial modelling. Experience with Power BI or similar reporting tools would be an advantage.
Regulatory Knowledge:
Working knowledge of statutory and regulatory environments in Kenya and/or Malawi, including NGO governance requirements, tax compliance, labour law, and relevant financial reporting obligations.
Board-Level Communication:
Demonstrated ability to prepare and present complex financial information clearly and confidently to Board members, donors, and non-financial stakeholders.
Desirable
Audit Management:
Experience managing internal and external audit processes, including donor financial reviews and statutory audits in multiple jurisdictions.
ICT Governance:
Experience providing strategic oversight of institutional ICT infrastructure, systems security, and digital transformation initiatives.
HR Administration:
Familiarity with HR administration, compensation and benefits management, and employment law compliance in East or Southern Africa.
Grant Management Systems:
Experience with grants management platforms such as Salesforce, Fluxx, or similar tools.
Procurement Systems:
Experience establishing or strengthening institutional procurement policies and supply chain management in an NGO context.
Competencies
The following competencies are integral to success in this role:
Strategic Leadership:
Ability to think and plan strategically across a complex, multi-function portfolio; translate institutional strategy into operational and financial plans.
Financial Acumen:
Deep technical mastery of financial management, accounting standards, and donor compliance requirements; ability to identify financial risks and develop practical solutions.
People Management:
Commitment to developing others; ability to build cohesive, high-performing teams across functions and geographies, and to manage performance constructively.
Communication & Influence:
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to present complex financial and operational information clearly to diverse audiences, including Boards, donors, and programme colleagues.
Integrity & Accountability:
The highest standards of personal and professional ethics; a visible champion for financial transparency and institutional accountability.
Problem-Solving:
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities; ability to diagnose complex operational and financial challenges and design pragmatic, sustainable solutions.
Relationship Management:
Ability to build and maintain effective, trust-based relationships with donors, partners, auditors, and internal stakeholders.
Adaptability:
Comfortable working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment; able to manage competing priorities and adapt approaches in response to evolving organisational needs.

Our Context

In spite of on-going efforts to improve the utilisation of research evidence in decision-making in Africa, there remain major challenges. Available research is largely fragmented in different scientific publications and not appropriately packaged for use by decision-makers. Furthermore, the evidence often does not fully meet the policy and programme needs of decision-makers since they rarely contribute to the initial identification of the knowledge gaps that the evidence seeks to fill. Job Description:
Role Overview
AFIDEP is seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Grants Manager to lead the effective management of the Institute’s grants portfolio, from pre-award due diligence through to award close-out. The Grants Manager will work closely with the Finance and Programmes teams to ensure that all grants are managed in full compliance with donor requirements and AFIDEP’s policies. He/she will play a key role in strengthening the Institute’s systems for grants and sub-grants management.
The successful candidate will be a meticulous, results-oriented professional who combines deep technical expertise in grants and contracts management with strong donor compliance knowledge. The Grants Manager will serve as a key link between AFIDEP and its donors, ensuring that grants are managed with rigour, transparency, and accountability to donors, the Board, and stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
Grants Strategy
Grants Portfolio Planning:
Contribute to institutional planning by tracking the grants pipeline, funding gaps and renewal timelines across all projects and country offices.
Proposal Budgeting:
Develop and review budgets and budget narratives for new funding proposals, in collaboration with programme teams.
Financial Feasibility Review:
Review donor solicitations and draft agreements to assess financial feasibility, flag unfavourable terms, and advise on cost structures and indirect cost recovery rates.
Cost Recovery Planning:
Support the application of AFIDEP’s cost allocation and indirect cost recovery methodology across new and existing grants.
Grants & Donor Compliance Management
Award Set-up & Activation:
Lead the review and activation of new awards, ensuring donor terms and conditions are understood and translated into internal budgets and compliance checklists.
Donor Compliance:
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the compliance requirements of bilateral, multilateral and private foundation donors, and ensure grant implementation adheres to these at all times.
Grant Close-out:
Coordinate timely and compliant close-out of completed awards, including final financial reporting, asset disposition and documentation archiving.
Donor & Partner Relations:
Serve as a key point of contact for donors on grants administration matters, managing financial queries and facilitating donor financial reviews.
Financial Monitoring & Reporting
Budget Monitoring:
Track grant expenditure against approved budgets, flag variances, and work with project teams to ensure spending remains on track and within donor rules.
Donor Financial Reporting:
Coordinate the preparation and timely submission of accurate financial reports to donors, in compliance with donor requirements and applicable accounting standards (IFRS).
Management Reporting:
Provide the Finance and Programme leadership with timely, actionable analysis of grants portfolio performance, burn rates and compliance risks.
Audit Support:
Support internal and external audits related to grants and contracts, maintaining audit-ready documentation and helping implement audit recommendations.
Sub-Grants & Partner Management
Due Diligence:
Lead financial and organisational due diligence assessments of prospective sub-grantees and implementing partners.
Sub-Agreement Management:
Draft and manage sub-grant and sub-contract agreements, ensuring donor flow-down clauses are correctly applied.
Disbursement & Compliance Monitoring:
Track sub-grantee disbursements, review partner financial reports, and monitor compliance with agreed budgets and donor rules.
Partner Capacity Building:
Build the financial management and compliance capacity of sub-grantees and partner institutions through training and ongoing support.
Risk Management & Systems Development
Grants Risk Management:
Identify, assess and escalate financial and compliance risks across the grants portfolio, and maintain an up-to-date grants risk log.
Internal Controls:
Support the design and consistent application of internal controls over grant income, expenditure and sub-grant disbursements.
Grants Management Systems:
Maintain an accurate, up-to-date grants tracking system and ensure accessible records of all active and closed awards.
Policy Development:
Contribute to the continuous review and improvement of AFIDEP’s grants and sub-grants management policies and procedures.
Identify and escalate risks in grant implementation and contribute to the continuous improvement of AFIDEP’s grants management policies and procedures.
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Essential
A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, International Development or a related field.
At least [5–7] years of relevant progressive experience in grants and contracts management, preferably within the NGO sector or donor-funded environment.
Strong working knowledge of the compliance requirements of major donors
Demonstrated experience managing sub-grants or sub-contracts to partner organisations.
Professional accounting or grants management qualification (e.g. CPA, ACCA, CIMA) is an added advantage.
Excellent analytical, organisational and financial management skills, with high attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain compliance requirements clearly to non-specialists.
Proficiency in financial and grants management software and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

Experience supporting internal and external audit processes, including donor financial reviews and statutory audits across multiple jurisdictions.

Familiarity with grants and financial data systems, with an appreciation of data security and system controls relevant to grants management.

Familiarity with staff costing as it relates to grant-funded staffing, including donor rules on staff costs, benefits and compliance.

Familiarity with procurement policies and processes as they relate to donor compliance and grant-funded purchases in an NGO context.

Job Description:

AFIDEP seeks to recruit an experienced
Audit
and Compliance Officer
to join its team on a fixed-term contract. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring the Institute’s financial and operational integrity by establishing and operating a risk-based internal audit and compliance function that provides independent assurance to AFIDEP’s leadership and Board.
The role carries an institute-wide mandate, covering all departments, projects, and country offices, to ensure adherence to international accounting standards, donor-specific financial regulations, statutory obligations, and internal AFIDEP policies.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Planning & Management
Annual Risk-Based Audit Plan:
Develop and obtain Board Audit Committee approval for an annual internal audit plan based on a systematic risk assessment of the Institute’s activities, projects, and processes.
Audit Execution:
Lead and conduct audits in accordance with IIA standards, producing formal audit reports with clear findings, root causes, management responses, and agreed corrective actions and timelines.
Follow-up:
Track implementation of audit recommendations and escalate unresolved or high-risk findings to the Board Audit Committee.
Financial & Accounting Compliance
Financial Records Audit:
Conduct rigorous audits of all financial records to ensure compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), AFIDEP’s financial policies, and applicable statutory requirements in Kenya and Malawi.
Donor Compliance:
Demonstrated, hands-on familiarity of complex multi-donor environment, with knowledge of the requirements of bilateral, multilateral and private foundation donors
Internal Controls:
Evaluate, monitor, and recommend improvements to financial and operational internal controls to safeguard institutional assets and prevent fraud, waste, and abuse.
Risk Management
Enterprise Risk Assessment:
Maintain and periodically update AFIDEP’s institutional risk register using recognised frameworks (e.g. COSO, ISO 31000), and work with management to ensure appropriate risk mitigation measures are in place.
Fraud Prevention & Response:
Establish and communicate fraud risk policies and whistleblower mechanisms; lead or support investigations into suspected financial irregularities.
Risk & Compliance Databases:
Identify and curate relevant financial data and evidence to maintain internal risk and compliance tracking systems.
Systems & Operational Review
ERP & Financial Systems:
Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of AFIDEP’s financial management and ERP systems, including IT general controls and access management, to ensure data integrity and security.
Policy & SOP Development:
Design and operationalise tools, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and processes to ensure institutional policies are consistently applied across all departments and country offices.
Operational Efficiency:
Identify inefficiencies and recommend process improvements that strengthen value for money across institutional operations.
Governance & Reporting
Regulatory Compliance:
Monitor and ensure compliance with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements in all countries where the Institute is registered (currently Kenya and Malawi, USA), including NGO regulations, tax obligations, and labour law provisions relevant to AFIDEP’s operations.
Capacity Building
Staff Training & Mentorship:
Design and deliver targeted, practical training for staff across all departments to build sustainable in-house understanding of financial compliance, internal controls, and accountability requirements.
Compliance Culture:
Promote a culture of proactive compliance and ethical conduct across the Institute, acting as a visible champion for accountability standards.
Qualifications and Experience
Education:
A Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a closely related field.
Professional Certification:
A current, full professional certification is mandatory — CPA, ACCA, CIA, or equivalent. CIA certification (Certified Internal Auditor) is particularly desirable given the nature of this role.
Experience:
A minimum of 8 years’ progressive professional experience in internal audit, financial management, or compliance, with at least 5 years in an international NGO, research organisation, or development institution operating within a multi-donor environment.
Donor Compliance Knowledge:
Demonstrated, hands-on familiarity of complex multi-donor environment, with knowledge of the requirements of bilateral, multilateral and private foundation donors.
Regulatory Knowledge:
Working knowledge of statutory and regulatory environments in Kenya and/or Malawi, including NGO governance, tax compliance, and relevant financial reporting obligations.
Financial Systems:
Demonstrated experience designing and managing financial control systems or audit software within complex, multi-project environments; proficiency with ERP systems and advanced use of Microsoft Excel.
Risk Frameworks:
Familiarity with recognised risk management frameworks such as COSO or ISO 31000, and experience maintaining institutional risk registers.
Audit Standards:
Demonstrated working knowledge of IIA International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) or equivalent internal audit standards.
Desirable
IT/Systems Audit:
Experience in IT general controls review, ERP access management audits, or cybersecurity compliance assessments.
Grants Management Systems:
Experience with grants management platforms.
Multi-country Experience:
Prior experience working across multiple country offices or managing compliance in a geographically dispersed organisation.
Competencies
The following competencies are integral to success in this role:
Professional Integrity & Independence:
The highest standards of personal and professional ethics; ability to maintain objectivity and independence under pressure.
Analytical Rigour:
Strong capacity to interpret complex financial data, identify patterns, and reach well-reasoned audit conclusions.
Communication & Influence:
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical audit findings clearly and persuasively to non-financial stakeholders — including senior management and Board members
Relationship Management:
Ability to build trust and constructive working relationships with colleagues across the Institute while maintaining the professional scepticism required of an independent audit function.
Attention to Detail:
Meticulous approach to documentation, evidence, and reporting, with a commitment to accuracy.
Initiative & Self-Management:
Ability to plan and prioritise a complex workload independently, adapt to shifting priorities, and deliver to deadlines without close supervision.
Data Literacy:
Ability to organise, interpret, and present complex financial information clearly, including proficiency in data visualisation tools for communicating audit findings.

Job Description:
Purpose of the role
This role keeps the company’s technology running: the laptops, accounts, network and licences that every other department depends on to do their work.
It sits close to every function but reports centrally. It owns the systems that keep people equipped, connected and secure, and is accountable for how quickly problems get resolved and how well the company’s devices, licences, access and data are protected.
Key Responsibilities
The asset register. Maintain a live, accurate record of every device the company owns: who holds it, its condition, its repair history, and when it is due for replacement. This register is the basis for every hardware procurement and budget decision.
Software licensing. Track every licence and subscription the company holds – what it costs, when it renews, and who is actually using it. Flag unused licences before they renew, and flag any system running without a valid licence before it becomes a compliance problem.
The helpdesk. Own the support queue end to end: log every request, resolve it within agreed turnaround times, and escalate what you can’t fix yourself. Set up new joiners and retrieve equipment from leavers on the day it happens, not the day after.
Network and WiFi. Keep the office network and WiFi running reliably and securely. Segregate guest traffic from company traffic, and be the first call when connectivity drops, liaising with the ISP where the fault sits outside the office.
Accounts and access. Create, change and remove user access across every system the company uses, in step with who joins, changes role, or leaves. No one should hold access they no longer need, and every account should be traceable to a person.
Security. Run the baseline controls – endpoint protection, patching, backups, multi-factor authentication and be the person who notices and responds when something looks wrong. Keep company practice in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019.
How success is measured
Every measure is a before-and-after comparison, with the baseline recorded at the start of the work.
Helpdesk turnaround falls. Time from ticket raised to ticket resolved drops and stays down.
The asset register holds up. A spot audit of devices matches the register without exceptions.
Licence spend is clean. No licence renews unused, and no system runs without a valid licence.
Network uptime rises. WiFi and network outages fall in frequency and duration.
Access matches reality. An access review turns up no account that should already have been removed.
No repeat security finding. The same control gap does not show up in consecutive reviews.
Qualifications
Required
Three or more years in IT administration, systems administration, or a helpdesk role with hands-on ownership, not just ticket-passing.
Practical experience with Windows/macOS environments and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace administration.
Working knowledge of networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN) and hands-on experience configuring routers, switches and WiFi access points.
Understanding of security fundamentals: endpoint protection, firewalls, backups, access control.
Clear written English. Tickets, procedures and the asset register are the main record of this role’s work.

What We Do

We have successfully introduced market leading express delivery and logistics services to the Middle East and other emerging economies. As a leading global provider of comprehensive logistics and transportation solutions, our breadth of services include express courierdelivery, freight forwarding, logistics, supply chain management, e-commerce and record management services.

How We Do It

Our unique, asset-light business model underlies all of the strategic decisions we make. It has proved highly successful, allowing Aramexus to swiftly adapt to challenging market conditions, execute last-mile delivery solutions and quickly respond to changing customer preferences.

Innovation in technology is critical to maintaining our asset-light business model and leveraging the Aramex global network. Instead of investing heavily in infrastructure, we acquire or partner with domestic-focused logistics companies that have strong local networks, knowledge and transportation solutions already in place for efficient and effective last-mile delivery. This approach has proven to have significant benefits for both our business and customers and why we consider ourselves a technology enterprise, selling transportation and logistics solutions without being encumbered by heavy investments in assets. We also believe that investing in and sourcing new technologies in the field of e-commerce in particular is core to a swifter, more efficient movement of goods and services globally and maintaining our market leadership position.

We also recognize that to continue to grow a truly sustainable business we must serve and develop the markets and communities where we operate. Our "Delivering Good” sustainability platform is active in over 180 educational, social and environmental projects worldwide and we have partnered with a number of international and local organizations devoted to similar causes. We are proud of the close ties we have with the communities where we operate and the contributions we have made to their sustainable economic development.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Executive, Credit Risk Management or designate, this position is responsible for ensuring the Bank's overall credit risk exposure is maintained at prudent levels and within the risk appetite parameters set by the Board of Directors.
Duties and Responsibilities
The duties and responsibilities of the role include but are not limited to:
Evaluate the financial performance of borrowers and based on a variety of credit risk and other factors, determining an appropriate risk rating for assigned portfolios.
Own the risk appetite by monitoring, evaluating and reporting on credit limits, exposures, and portfolio characteristics of all clients to adequately provide for any expected credit losses.
Develop and review credit risk management policies and procedures to guide risk taking practices and decision making.
Conduct Risk Reviews/Risk Opinions on credit applications and reviews to ensure there is independent and expert scrutiny of credit risks and rewards, mitigations and provide feedback to busines development officers during the structuring phase of credit facilities.
Present the Risk Reviews, opinions, and recommendations on residual risks to relevant Credit Committees for consideration in risk taking decisions.
Implement (internal & external) audit findings or recommendations within agreed timeframe.
Oversight of the Credit and Political Risk Insurance Portfolio to ensure applicable exposures are adequately mititgated for; Process renewals on existing insurance covers, make applications to acquire new insurance where required and prepare Insurance Portfolio Reports.
Actively identify early warnings signals at client level and portfolio level to prevent weak assets from crystallizing into unmitigated losses; Conduct annual and interim reviews of existing credit facilities and monitor financial and non-financial convenants and recommend corrective action plans.
Collect timely, credible and accessible data on country, sector and obligor exposures to provide decision makers with appropriate information to inform risk taking decisions.
Contribute to the department's periodic risk reporting process by ensuring timely submission of data to inform corporate reporting.
Act as Secretary to the Credit Committee to keep record of deliberations and ensure meetings are held in a structured manner by sending invitations and agenda for Credit Committee meetings to Members, Presenters & Observers.
Train and mentor credit analysts to equip them with knowledge and skills to effectively perform their role.
Qualifications and Competencies
A Master's degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, or any other relevant field from a recognized university.
Relevant professional qualification/certification such as ACIB, ACCA, CPA, CA, CIA, FRM, or PRM.
Membership of a recognized professional body as an added advantage.
A minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience and proven track record in a Commercial/Development Banking or Financial institution environment.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of corporate and sovereign credit risk management concepts and international standards relating to credit risk.
Enabler to the business deal teams and cross functional taskforces through an entrepreneurial mindest for optimal win-win solutions for both the client and the Bank without compromising on risks.
Experience in trade finance as well as project & infrastructure finance structures.
Strong interpersonal skills with ability to work in different environments and with culturally diverse teams.
Solid track-record in developing and nurturing talent and managing diverse teams to drive engagement and performance.

Reporting administratively to the Chief Executive Officer and with appropriate functional accountability to the Board and relevant Board Committees on governance and risk matters, the Chief Legal & Risk Officer / Corporation Secretary will serve as NIF’s principal legal, governance and enterprise risk adviser. General Counsel, Chief Legal Officer, Head of Legal or comparable senior position involving personal responsibility for complex transactions.

Non-recourse or limited-recourse project-finance transactions.
Negotiating significant construction or EPC arrangements, preferably including FIDIC-based contracts.
Negotiating concessions, leases, implementation agreements, offtake/ revenue agreements, O&M contracts and other material infrastructure project agreements.
Negotiating financing documents involving commercial banks, development finance institutions or other sophisticated lenders.
Equity investments, shareholder agreements, joint ventures and investment SPVs.
Legal due diligence and transaction risk assessment.
Managing legal conditions precedent and achieving financial close.
Engaging Government institutions and navigating statutory and regulatory approvals affecting major commercial or infrastructure transactions.
Managing Kenyan and international external counsel on complex transactions.
Managing significant contractual claims, disputes, arbitration or other dispute-resolution proceedings.
Supporting investments through portfolio management, restructuring, refinancing and exit.
Advising Boards and Board Committees at senior executive level.
Corporation/company secretarial and governance responsibilities.
Experience in infrastructure, project finance, investment management, private equity, development finance, banking, capital markets or institutional investment will be particularly relevant.

Leading solution design and delivery end-to-end: Rolling up your sleeves as an individual contributor- writing production code, designing and evaluating methods and models, and building and deploying solutions (including APIs, UIs, CI/CD, etc.); while also working alongside other data scientists to shape the overall approach, synthesize findings, and communicate results.
Establishing standards and best practices: Bringing experience in writing quality code, conducting code reviews, and providing feedback on technical and non-technical documentation. Setting the bar for engineering rigor and project management on the team.
Coaching and mentoring: Upskilling junior data scientists on methods and approaches, and providing structured feedback on both technical and delivery skills.
Providing thought leadership in your specialty: Leading the org through deep expertise in a subset of the following (machine learning, deep learning, GenAI/LLMs, NLP, optimization, geospatial analytics, backend development, frontend development, DevOps, or MLOps) — and drawing on broad familiarity across methods to make sound judgment calls on which approach fits which problem.
Shaping the sector: Identifying trends and gaps in the AI-for-Good space; proposing products or services that could address these gaps; and contributing thought leadership on how data science and AI can be deployed responsibly and for the right problem types.

Real-time feedback and structured reviews are regularly provided to maximize each data scientist’s expertise. IDinsight’s entrepreneurial culture allows roles and career progression to be tailored to individual strengths, interests, and goals. Employees have the opportunity to increase responsibilities, and high performers will have the opportunity to move up in the organization along technical, managerial, or client-facing paths.

Intermediate-to-advanced Python skills / experience working on complex codebases.

Are you a strategic communicator and compelling storyteller who can turn complex ideas, programme evidence and results into powerful content that inspires people to engage and act? Do you know how to build organisational visibility and reputation across digital, media and other influential platforms, while positioning leaders and technical experts as credible voices? This is an opportunity to shape how Solidaridad East & Central Africa communicates its impact, strengthens its brand and brings its work to life for the audiences that matter.
Solidaridad East & Central Africa is seeking an experienced Regional Communications Manager to lead the regional communications, marketing, visibility and storytelling agenda. Working across countries, programmes and teams, you will translate organisational priorities, evidence, results and learning into compelling stories and communications for donors, partners, governments, businesses, media and other key stakeholders. You will also support programme and PMEL teams to turn learning into impactful products, while partnering with Business Development and leadership to develop strong institutional communications, marketing materials and positioning content that strengthen Solidaridad’s influence and reputation across the region.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the Regional Communications, Marketing and Visibility Strategy — Develop and implement the regional communications and marketing strategy and annual plan, translating organisational priorities into integrated campaigns, messaging and communications initiatives.
Strengthen Brand, Positioning and Reputation — Lead Solidaridad’s brand positioning, visibility and external reputation across East and Central Africa, identifying opportunities to strengthen organisational influence and profile with regional and global audiences.
Lead Strategic Storytelling and Thought Leadership — Translate programme evidence, results, learning and technical expertise into compelling stories, publications, knowledge products and thought leadership that demonstrate impact and strengthen Solidaridad’s voice and credibility.
Drive Digital, Media and External Communications — Provide strategic direction for digital communications, social media, multimedia, publications, media engagement and other influential platforms to expand reach, audience engagement and organisational visibility.
Strengthen Leadership and Stakeholder Positioning — Advise the Managing Director and Regional Leadership Team on strategic messaging, positioning and leadership communications, while positioning senior leaders and technical experts as credible voices across relevant platforms.
Support Resource Mobilisation and Institutional Communications — Partner with Business Development, programmes and leadership to develop high-quality donor and partner communications, pitch decks, capability statements, presentations, organisational profiles and other marketing collateral that strengthen institutional positioning and resource mobilisation.
Drive Programme Evidence and Learning Communications — Work closely with programme, technical and PMEL teams to transform evidence, results and learning into accessible and influential communications and knowledge products for donors, partners, policymakers and other priority audiences.
Lead Internal Communications and Organisational Alignment — Strengthen internal communications, leadership messaging and information flow across regional and country teams to promote alignment, engagement and understanding of organisational priorities and achievements.
Provide Functional Leadership and Quality Assurance — Lead the regional communications function and strengthen the capacity of country communications focal points and programme teams, establishing standards, approaches and quality assurance for communications and storytelling.
Manage Communications Resources and Reputational Risk — Oversee communications budgets, agencies and external service providers, while proactively advising leadership on sensitive communications, emerging reputational risks and crisis communications.
The person we are looking for
You are a strategic communicator and compelling storyteller who can turn complex ideas, technical evidence and programme results into clear, engaging and influential narratives. You combine strategic thinking with strong execution and are confident advising senior leaders, shaping organisational positioning, developing campaigns and strengthening content. You are curious, creative and audience-focused, with a strong understanding that communication is about more than content; it is about building visibility, strengthening reputation, influencing audiences and demonstrating impact. You thrive in a multicultural, multi-country environment and bring sound judgement, collaboration, initiative and integrity.
Key Competencies
Strategic Communication & Judgement – Ability to translate organisational priorities into clear, impactful communications and make sound decisions about audiences, messages and channels.
Storytelling & Content Excellence – Exceptional writing, editing and storytelling skills, with the creativity to make complex issues accessible, compelling and memorable.
Influence & Executive Advisory – Confidence and credibility to advise senior leaders and influence stakeholders on messaging, positioning and reputation.
Digital & Media Leadership – Strong understanding of digital communications, social media, multimedia, media relations and evolving audience engagement platforms.
Stakeholder & Relationship Management – Ability to build trusted relationships with donors, partners, media, governments, businesses and other influential stakeholders.
Collaboration & Cross-Cultural Leadership – Proven ability to work effectively across countries, cultures, disciplines and diverse teams.
Results Orientation & Accountability – Focus on measurable impact, quality, timely delivery and continuous improvement.
Creativity, Agility & Integrity – Curious, proactive and innovative, with the resilience, discretion and integrity required to navigate complex communications and reputational issues.
What Success Looks Like
Success means stronger visibility, influence and reputation for Solidaridad ECA, with compelling communications that showcase impact, engage priority audiences and position the organisation and its experts as credible voices.

Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Marketing or a related discipline. A Master’s degree is an advantage.
8–10 years of progressive experience in strategic communications, marketing, public relations, journalism, development communications or a related field.
At least 3 years’ experience in a managerial, regional or strategic communications role.
Proven experience developing and implementing organisational, regional or multi-country communications strategies.
Strong track record in content development, storytelling, digital communications, media engagement and thought leadership.
Experience strengthening organisational brand, visibility, reputation and external positioning.
Experience supporting donor, partner and business development communications.
Experience advising senior leadership on communications and reputational matters.
Experience working across multiple countries, cultures and diverse teams is highly desirable.
Experience in international development, sustainability, agriculture, climate or related sectors is an added advantage.

Zeno is looking for a driven Network Operations Specialist to be the frontline for riders who depend on our battery swap network every day. When a driver hits a swapping or charging issue, you're the person who gets them moving again — fast. You'll respond to inbound queries across phone, WhatsApp, and in-app chat, troubleshoot remotely, and coordinate with our field and product engineering teams to resolve issues at the root.
This is the first hire of its kind at Zeno, so you won't just be answering tickets—you'll help shape how our network operations support function works as we scale. You'll report to the Network Operations Lead and work closely with field technicians and our product engineering team.

Rapid Response & Customer Satisfaction
Provide technical support to customers to get them back on the road quickly.
Make sure no driver is left standing still due to network-related issues—drive every case to resolution.

Diagnose battery swap hardware and software issues remotely, working methodically to identify root causes.
Triage and escalate cases that need hands-on attention—coordinating field technicians through our Deployment team and relaying feedback back to customers.
Escalate fundamental product issues to our product engineering team and follow through until resolved.
Process & Continuous Improvement
Help build and refine support processes, playbooks, and SLAs from the ground up.
Keep accurate records of issues, resolutions, and recurring patterns.
Surface trends and recommend improvements to reduce repeat issues and improve network reliability.
Requirements
A strong service mindset and the drive to keep our growing customer base happy—someone who goes above and beyond and won't stop until every rider is back on the road.
Ability to work methodically and follow process to root-cause issues.
Strong coordination skills to drive results with partner teams (field and product), plus solid admin and record-keeping so we can analyze and improve.
Fluency in English and Swahili.
Comfort with technical troubleshooting and support and monitoring tools — you can get to the bottom of a hardware or software problem, explain it clearly and document for follow-up.
Willingness to work flexible hours, including evening rush periods (centered around 6pm) when demand peaks. Over time, this role may move to shift-based coverage.
Qualifications
1+ years in customer support, technical support, or a technically-oriented operations role—or a strong technical background with the customer instinct to match.
An academic engineering background is a plus. We're open to fairly junior candidates with the right drive.
Comfort learning technical systems quickly—battery swap hardware, mobile app, and backend tools.
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
Clear, empathetic communication under pressure.

Competitive salary.
Company-sponsored healthcare.

Contractor Management Plan.

Develop practical safeguards tools, checklists, SOPs, and guidance materials.

Company Details: The Mater Hospital was opened in 1962 by the Sisters of Mercy, a Catholic Order of Nuns originating from Ireland, three years after registering themselves as the Registered Trustees of an entity under the Perpetual Succession Act (the succeeding legislation after independence). The "Sisters...read moreof Mercy" first set up a 60 bed general hospital to cater mainly for the poor, indigenous Kenyans, with the primary mission being general healthcare. The colonial authorities granted 12 acres of land in a swampy, mosquito-infested area, which has since become the Industrial Area of Nairobi. In 1970, a 60-bed maternity ward was opened with antenatal, postnatal and immunization clinics attached in order to upgrade the quality of maternity healthcare available to the poorer segments of the Nairobi population. In 1972, in recognition of the contribution of the hospital in training midwives to assist births in rural areas, Mater was chartered as a School of Midwifery. In 1975, a consultant’s block of 6 offices was opened enabling specialised consultants to practice on site and deliver significantly better medical services to the patients. In 1986, the hospital opened its own pharmacy, physiotherapy and laboratory services and, in 1990, opened its counselling centre for inpatients, outpatients and staff who needed advice and guidance on family planning, HIV, and other concerns of a psychological and/or physical nature. In 1995, in a major building expansion programme, the hospital opened a larger and more efficient Casualty, Accident and Emergency Department, an Intensive Care Unit and a Cardiac Unit where open-heart surgery is performed. The missionary role of the Sisters of Mercy has spread to other parts of Kenya and the Mater Hospital has become a private hospital that charges a fee-for-service to a patient population that has developed locally to a much higher level of affluence compared with other parts of Kenya. The financial objective of the hospital is to provide affordable healthcare to as many people as possible but also attempt to meet all of its costs, including depreciation, in order to replace and upgrade medical equipment.
