Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Graphic Designer exists to give visual form to the DIB Kenya brand ensuring that everything the bank produces, publishes, or presents is designed to the highest standard of quality, brand consistency, and visual impact. In a sector where trust, credibility, and professionalism are built as much through perception as through performance, the visual quality of every communication matters. This role sits at the intersection of brand governance and creative production. The Graphic Designer is not simply an executor of requests; they are a creative partner to the Marketing, Brand & Communications team, elevating every campaign, every corporate document, and every event with design that reflects DIB Kenya’s ambition to be the leading Islamic bank in Kenya. The role is responsible for all visual output from social media graphics and campaign assets to Board presentations, event branding, and branch materials and is the in-house design capability that enables the bank to produce world-class communications rapidly, consistently, and at significantly lower cost than full agency dependency.
Key Responsibilities
Creative Design & Campaign Assets Design all marketing campaign assets including social media graphics, digital banners, email templates, out-of-home advertising materials such as billboards and digital screens, print advertisements, and above-the-line materials. Develop campaign visual concepts in collaboration with the Brand Marketing Manager and Digital & Content Officer, from initial mood board through to final production-ready files. Produce high-quality visual content for all Islamic calendar campaigns, Ramadan, Eid Al-Fitr, Eid Al-Adha, Muharram, and Mawlid reflecting both the cultural significance of the occasion and the distinctive DIB Kenya brand aesthetic. Prepare already artwork files for print vendors and digital platforms, ensuring correct specifications, bleed, resolution, and color profiles for each medium.
Brand Identity & Governance Maintain and enforce DIB Kenya’s Brand Identity System, ensuring all visual output produced in-house and by external parties adheres to brand guidelines covering typography, colour palette, logo usage, imagery standards, and overall visual tone. Develop and maintain the brand asset library, keeping all templates, logo files, fonts, approved imagery, and brand elements organized, up to date, and accessible to the team. Review and quality-control all externally produced design work from agency creative submissions to third-party co-branded materials ensuring they meet DIB Kenya’s brand standards before approval. Support the development of new brand assets, product visual identities, and sub-brand design elements as the bank’s portfolio and business lines grow.
Digital Design Design all social media visual content including post graphics, Stories, Reels overlays, profile assets, and highlight cover across all active platforms, consistent with the brand and content calendar. Design email marketing templates ensuring they are responsive, brand-consistent, and visually effective across desktop and mobile platforms. Design all website visual elements including banners, hero images, product page graphics, and landing page visuals, in close coordination with the Digital & Content Officer. Support the production of motion graphics and animated social content using Adobe After Effects, Canva, or equivalent tools as required by the content strategy. Corporate & Internal Design Design all corporate materials including executive presentations, annual reports, Board papers, stakeholder communications, and official bank publications. Produce all HR and internal communications design including staff posters, internal newsletters, culture campaign materials, and employer brand visuals. Design all customer-facing collateral including product brochures, promotional flyers, rate cards, customer welcome kits, and branch materials. Produce all internal signage, office environment branding, and workspace visual elements to maintain a consistent, professional, and brand-aligned physical presence Event Design Design all event branding and collateral including stage backdrops, pull-up banners, event programmes, speaker name badges, branded merchandise, and promotional giveaways. Manage event artwork production and liaise directly with print vendors to ensure all event materials are produced to specification and delivered within required timelines. Design pop-up booth materials, exhibition stands, and activation materials for community events, branch openings, sponsorship activations, and trade shows. Photography & Visual Asset Management Manage DIB Kenya’s photography and image library, curating a bank of high-quality, culturally appropriate, and Shariah-consistent visual assets for use across all communications. Brief and coordinate external photographers and videographers for campaign shoots, product photography, and event coverage. Ensure all visual assets used across channels, including photography, illustrations, icons, and stock imagery, are brand-consistent, culturally appropriate, and properly licensed.
Dimensions / Context (scope of the job – responsibility for managing) The role holder is expected to produce multiple design assets per month across all formats and channels, maintain a turnaround time consistent with business needs, and manage multiple concurrent briefs without compromising on brand quality or production accuracy. The role requires strong self-management, the ability to prioritise effectively under pressure, and a disciplined approach to the briefing and approval process. The role has no direct reports and no budget management authority but carries responsibility for briefing and coordinating external print vendors, photography suppliers, and production houses within approved parameters. As the guardian of the bank’s visual identity, the Graphic Designer also plays an important governance function reviewing and quality-controlling all design work produced externally by agencies or third-party partners and maintaining the brand asset library that underpins the bank’s visual communications.
Key Relationship (Internal & External)
Internal All departments and departments heads External Vendors/Suppliers Advertising Agencies Print Vendors & Production Houses — Artwork submission, proofing, and print production management. Photography & Videography Suppliers External Creative Agencies — Collaboration on major campaigns where agency supports in-house design; brand standards enforcement across all externally produced materials.
Job Specification
Education
Bachelor’s Degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communications, Fine Art, or a related creative discipline. Other relevant formal qualification/Certification from a recognized design institution is preferred.
Key Skills
Training & Skills Full proficiency across the Adobe Creative Suite including Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign, Premiere Pro, and After Effects Microsoft Office design proficiency including PowerPoint and Word to an executive presentation standard Digital design specifications for social media platforms, web, and email. Motion graphics and basic animation for social media content are preferred.
Professional Certifications Adobe Certified Professional is preferred but not mandatory. Short course qualifications in motion graphics, UX/UI design, or brand management are advantageous.
Work Experience
Minimum 3-5 years of commercial graphic design experience in a professional environment. Demonstrable portfolio covering a range of design formats including social media, print campaigns, corporate presentations, and event collateral is required. Experience producing print-ready artwork and managing artwork through print production, including direct liaison with print vendors. Experience designing for a banking, financial services, professional services, or other corporate brand is highly preferred. Experience working with brand guidelines and producing design within a structured brand identity system. Experience producing executive-level presentations and corporate publications such as annual reports or stakeholder reports. Portfolio demonstrating experience with Islamic or culturally sensitive design is a significant advantage.
Competencies
Brand Identity & Visual Systems: Expert knowledge of brand architecture, with the discipline to apply it consistently on a scale. Typography & Layout Design: Mastery of typographic hierarchy, spatial design, and layout principles across print and digital. Adobe Creative Suite: Full, expert-level proficiency across all core applications. Print & Digital Production: Ability to independently manage artwork from concept through to final production-ready file for both print and digital media. Campaign & Corporate Design: Demonstrated ability to design compelling visual communications across both marketing campaigns and formal corporate publications.
Complexity/ Judgement While the Graphic Designer works under management direction, the role requires significant independent creative judgement and a consistent standard of self-quality-control. The complexity of the role stems from several factors: Brand consistency at volume: Producing multiple design assets per month while maintaining absolute brand consistency requires a deep internalization of the brand guidelines and a disciplined, systematic approach to design. Production accuracy: In a banking environment, design errors are not merely aesthetic inconveniences. A wrong interest rate, a misspelled product name, or incorrect regulatory disclaimer on a printed brochure can create compliance, legal, and reputational problems. The role holder must apply meticulous attention to detail to every piece of artwork before it goes to production. Cultural and religious design sensitivity: DIB Kenya’s brand has a strong Islamic heritage, and a significant proportion of its visual output relates to Islamic banking products, Shariah-compliant values, and Muslim cultural occasions. Managing multiple concurrent briefs: The role holder will regularly be managing multiple design briefs simultaneously, at varying stages of completion, for different internal clients. This requires excellent personal organization, clear communication about timelines and priorities, and the judgement to know when to escalate conflicting demands. Balancing creative ambition and practical constraints: The role holder must be capable of producing work that is genuinely beautiful and brand-elevating, while also working within production timelines, budget constraints, and format specifications that are non-negotiable.
Behavioral Expectations
Craft & Attention to Detail — Is pixel-perfect in every piece of work submitted. Never allows alignment errors, colour inconsistencies, or off-brand treatments to pass through uncorrected. Reliability —Delivers on deadlines without exception. Communicates proactively if a timeline is at risk rather than missing it silently. Creative Ambition — Is not content with the functional minimum. Consistently seeks to push the quality and visual impact of DIB Kenya’s communications higher. Collaborative Receptivity — Receives creative feedback professionally, views revisions as improvements rather than criticisms, and produces better work as a result. Brand Ownership — Treats the DIB Kenya brand as a personal responsibility. Finds off-brand materials genuinely troubling and takes initiative to correct them. Cultural Intelligence — Demonstrates genuine sensitivity to Islamic design traditions, Arabic visual culture, and the aesthetic expectations of a Shariah-compliant financial institution.

The rich flora and fauna within the forest coupled with mountain climbing are a great potential for tourist activities. The county has six major rivers namely; Sagana, Nyamindi, Rupingazi, Thiba, Rwamuthambi and Ragati, all of which drain into the Tana River. These rivers are the principal source of water in the county. The water from these rivers has been harnessed through canals to support irrigation at the lower zones of the county. The county has a tropical climate and an equatorial rainfall pattern. The climatic condition is influenced by the county position along the equator and its position on the windward side of Mt Kenya. The county has two rainy seasons, the long rains and the short rains. Administratively, the county is divided into five districts namely; Kirinyaga East, Kirinyaga West, Mwea East, Mwea West and Kirinyaga Central. The districts are subdivided further into 12 divisions, 30 locations and 81 sub-locations.The county has four constituencies namely Mwea, Ndia, Kirinyaga Central and Gichugu. Kirinyaga County has twenty (20) wards. From the Kenya Population and Housing Census 2009 report, the population of the county stood at 528,054 persons with an annual growth rate of 1.5 percent. The population is projected to be 595, 379 in 2017. Kerugoya, Sagana and Wang’uru are the only towns in the County while Kagio and Kagumo comprise the urban centres. The town with the highest population is Wang’uru with a population of 18,437; followed by Kerugoya with a population of 17,122; the least populated town is Sagana with a population of 10,344. The urban centre with the highest population is Kagio with a population of 3,512 followed closely by Kagumo with a population of 3,489. The population of Wang’uru is highest because it has a lot of economic activities, mainly rice farming while Kerugoya town had long been the District administrative headquarters. The total road network of in the county is 1,109.11 Km, out of which 106.5 Km is bitumen, 462.05 Km is gravel and 540.5 Km is earth surfaced roads. The county has an established road network with 7 tarmac roads passing through it namely Makutano – Embu road, Kutus – Karatina road, Baricho road, Kiburu road, Kutus – Sagana road, Kutus – Kianyaga road and Kabare – Kimunye road. There is only a 5km of railway line and one railway station in the county located in Ndia Constituency but currently not in use. There is one airstrip located in Mwea constituency. The mobile phone coverage stands at 99 percent while the number of fixed lines stands at 693 units. There are 5 sub- post offices and 14 cyber-cafes. There is also an increase in the usage of computers and internet in government offices, private businesses and homes due to availability portable modems and affordability of computers and laptops.

Key Responsibilities
Facilities Maintenance and Operations
Oversee preventive and corrective maintenance of university buildings, infrastructure, and equipment.
Ensure timely response to maintenance requests across academic, administrative, and residential facilities.

Auxiliary Services Management

Ensure cost-effective utilization of resources while maintaining service quality.
Monitor expenditures and provide regular financial and operational reports.
Asset Management

Maintain an updated inventory of facilities, equipment, and assets under maintenance.
Ensure proper lifecycle management, including maintenance, repair, and replacement planning.
Stakeholder Engagement
Work closely with academic departments, student services, housing, and administration to address facility and service needs.

Membership in a relevant professional body.
Proficiency in computer applications and facilities management systems.
Experience

Experience in managing outsourced services and contractors.

Job Specification
Officers are responsible to the Head of their Directorate for providing Board Secretarial and related services to the Board of Directors and ensure effective and efficient management of contract administration, company insurance, legislative drafting and compliance with legal and regulatory legislation including provision of legal advice to members of management.
Duties and responsibilities
Ensure compliance with national, county and international legal instruments governing metropolitan transport affairs, including monitoring implementation and providing periodic compliance reports and advisory.
Provide strategic legal and corporate advisory services to the Board and Management, including interpretation of laws, preparation of legal opinions and timely guidance on legal and regulatory matters.
Provide effective Board secretariat services, including coordinating Board business, preparing and maintaining records of proceedings, and implementing or facilitating decisions as directed by the Board.
Develop, review and maintain the Authority’s legal and regulatory framework, including policies, codes, rules, regulations, guidelines, by-laws, directives and treaties, and facilitate their approval and gazettement.
Coordinate and oversee the Authority’s representation in courts, tribunals and other judicial or quasi-judicial bodies, safeguarding the Authority’s interests and ensuring effective defence of its legal position.
Manage all litigation and dispute-resolution matters, including monitoring outstanding cases, instructing and supervising external advocates, and ensuring that legal proceedings are handled in the Authority’s best interests.
Establish and oversee the Authority’s Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) framework, including promoting preventive legal strategies, building stakeholder capacity and facilitating engagement with national and international ADR mechanisms.
Draft, review, negotiate and vet contracts and other legal instruments, including leases, licences, service-level agreements, memoranda of understanding and business transaction documents, to protect the Authority’s interests and manage contractual risks.
Undertake legal due diligence and provide legal advice on proposed transactions, approvals, licences, partnerships, leases and other relationships involving the Authority, its tenants, licensees, partners and third parties.
Conduct and coordinate legal and regulatory compliance audits and risk assessments, identify potential legal risks and ensure that appropriate mitigation and corrective measures are implemented.

Provide legal guidance on enforcement, regulatory approvals and operational requirements, including maintaining records of enforcement and compliance activities and establishing appropriate legal accountability mechanisms.
Promote legal awareness, ethics and governance across the Authority, including interpretation and dissemination of legal requirements, staff training, implementation of Mwongozo and the Code of Conduct and Ethics.

A minimum of ten (10) years in relevant work experience and at least four (4) years in management in the Public or Private Sector;

Master’s Degree in any of the following disciplines; Law, Metropolitan transport or equivalent qualifications from a recognized institution;
Postgraduate Diploma in Law from the Kenya School of Law;
Admitted as an Advocate of the High Court of Kenya;

Management course lasting not less than four (4) weeks from a recognized institution.

Job Description
The Corporate Finance & Treasury Analyst is a dual-mandate role supporting the Corporate Finance Manager through a mix of analytical, deadline-driven tasks (financial modeling, covenant compliance, investor/lender reporting) and fixed operational routines (managing d.light's funding structures and daily/weekly/monthly group liquidity). Designed for an analytically strong, highly organized professional, the position offers exposure to structured and off-balance-sheet finance, debt capital markets, and multi-market treasury management, requiring comfort with both project-based analysis and strict calendar obligations.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Stream A — Corporate Finance
Financial Modelling & Analysis
Develop and maintain robust financial models to support fundraising, strategic planning and investment decisions.
Conduct macroeconomic research and maintain up-to-date financial model assumptions.
Perform scenario analysis, sensitivity testing and stress testing to assess financial risks and opportunities.
Prepare financial forecasts and valuation models for strategic initiatives.
Build and maintain the medium- and long-term liquidity and funding plan.
Track actual business outcomes against strategic objectives, highlighting adverse deviations for timely corrective action.
Covenant Compliance & Lender Reporting
Calculate, track and forecast financial covenant compliance across all facilities.
Prepare compliance certificates and other reporting deliverables required under funding agreements.
Prepare regular reports, presentations and dashboards for lenders, investors and financial partners.
Ensure compliance with financial reporting requirements arising from funding agreements.
Fundraising & Investor Support
Support the execution of debt and equity fundraising activities.
Prepare investor presentations, investment memorandums and due diligence materials.
Maintain the data room and coordinate responses to investor and lender information requests.
Model the impact of proposed facility terms, pricing and structures on the group’s capital
structure, cash flows and covenant headroom.
Roles & Responsibilities: Stream B — Treasury Operations
Receivable Finance & SPV Operations
Manage the monthly sale of new receivables into the receivable financing SPVs across Kenya,
Tanzania, Uganda, Nigeria and Zambia to unlock cash receipts in a timely fashion.
Ensure daily cash sweeps to the SPVs are executed in compliance with the related agreements and maintain the supporting compliance evidence.
Support receivable eligibility testing and proactively work to maximize the advance rate against eligible receivables.
Liquidity Framework & Cash Discipline
Consolidate OpCo cash submissions into the group rolling cash flow forecast, challenge the inputs, and explain variance against forecast.
Maintain cash generation and cash conversion KPI reporting by country and channel, making cash flow drivers visible to OpCo finance leads and management teams as well as the Group ExCo.
Produce the weekly liquidity flash reports, liquidity governance pack and supporting cash dashboards to country financial controllers and management teams.
Continuously monitor minimum cash thresholds and escalation triggers and immediately escalate projected shortfalls.
Debt, FX & Banking Administration
Maintain the group debt register, including facility terms, drawdown schedules, pricing and repayment calendars.
Calculate and schedule interest and principal payments, and ensure timely settlement of all debt service obligations.
Monitor foreign exchange exposures and execute currency conversions and hedging instruments strictly within the Board-approved hedging mandate, maintaining complete hedge documentation.
Administer bank accounts, mandates, signatories, KYC documentation and banking platform access across the group.
Monitor counterparty exposure against approved limits and bank charges against agreed tariffs.
Requirements
Bachelors Degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration or a related field.
CFA/CPA/ACCA/CA or equivalent qualification is mandatory.
A treasury qualification (ACT CertT/AMCT, CTP or equivalent) is a strong added advantage.
5 - 8 years of experience spanning both corporate finance analysis and treasury or finance operations.Candidates with depth in only one of the two streams are unlikely to succeed in this role.
Strong experience in financial modelling, valuation and corporate finance principles.
Hands-on experience operating banking platforms and executing settlement and treasury transactions in a controlled and automated environment.
Experience working across multiple currencies, entities and banking jurisdictions.
Exposure to structured, securitization or receivables financing structures, and to lender covenant reporting, is strongly preferred.
Experience in emerging markets, and familiarity with mobile money and local currency control regimes, is an advantage.
Benefits
Competitive Remuneration
Medical Cover
Pension Scheme

Daniel Arap Moi C.G.H., M.P. (th...read moreen Vice-president) launched the Harambee Fund Raising Drive at the request of Kirinyaga people. Kirinyaga County Council set aside 200 acres of land for the institute at Kutus and 50 more acres were also acquired at Kangaita area on the slopes of Mt. Kenya. The Institute opened doors to the first students on 2nd March 1977 when 72 students were enrolled, 48 of these students were admitted in the building and construction department while the remaining 24 were enrolled in the clothing and textile technology department. Job Title: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Thematic Expert
Job Description:
Purpose of the role
The TVET Thematic Expert brings extensive knowledge and expertise in Uganda’s TVET sector, as well as the ability to assess current approaches, outcomes, and gaps, and recommend actionable strategies to strengthen youth employment and enterprise development through TVET skilling and institutional capacity building. The expert will help Busara and Mastercard Foundation Uganda establish:
How trends in Uganda’s TVET sector are impacting youth employment opportunities where the strategy is active in Uganda.
The extent to which the strategy, partnerships, and investments are positioned to respond to and capitalize on these trends.
Opportunities, risks, and gaps in the strategy’s TVET positioning, and practical, prioritized recommendations to strengthen it.
Key Accountabilities/Responsibilities
Conduct literature review on the TVET ecosystem and review relevant Young Africa Works Strategy documents, reports, and results data of Uganda’s implementing partners.
Provide technical input to assessments and reviews related to TVET system indicators.
Map sector actors and current trends in Uganda’s TVET sector relevant to youth employment and upskilling, and benchmark against relevant associated strategies in East Africa.
Conduct Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and consultations with relevant stakeholders and ecosystem actors.
Assess the extent to which current programs address critical TVET sector challenges: access to TVET institutions, the cost of institutional learning, the impact of technology on the sector, among others.
Assess the TVET sector relevance and positioning of Young Africa Works Strategy in Uganda’s current partner portfolio and flagship interventions, including alignment with national TVET policy priorities.
Identify barriers and opportunities for youth participation in the TVET sub-sectors, to strengthen skilling outcomes, including potential new partnerships, delivery models, priority sub-sectors, or areas of focus.
Evaluate the effectiveness of TVET skilling, mentorship, and linkages to dignified and fulfilling work, and finances for the youth participants.
Produce a report with findings, recommendations, and a prioritization framework for dissemination to Busara and the Young Africa Works stakeholders.
Indicative Deliverables
An inception report covering the methodology, work plan, and budget.
Key Informant Interview (KII) discussion guides tailored to various stakeholders.
Audio recordings and notes from Key Informant Interview (KII) discussions.
A draft narrative report including an executive summary, findings, learnings and recommendations, and a prioritized action matrix.
A PowerPoint slide deck for presentation to the Foundation.
Hold a validation and dissemination session with the Foundation.
A final PowerPoint slide deck incorporating input from the validation and dissemination session.
Participate in sensemaking sessions with the Foundation, Implementing Partners, and other relevant ecosystem actors, as required.
A final narrative report incorporating input from the validation, dissemination, and sensemaking sessions.
Required Qualifications
The expert should possess
An advanced degree in TVET, Education, Vocational Training, or a related field.
Minimum 8-10 years of experience in TVET program design, delivery, or evaluation in Uganda, ideally within youth employment or skilling programs serving refugee or host community populations.
Demonstrated experience designing and conducting qualitative fieldwork (IDIs, FGDs, KIIs), including lifejourney/storytelling techniques, with TVET trainees, instructors, and institutions.
Working knowledge of Uganda’s TVET/BTVET policy framework, competency-based training and assessment, and institutional accreditation processes.
Familiarity with Uganda’s refugee response context (including major refugee-hosting districts) and labor market systems relevant to TVET graduates is strongly preferred.
Strong facilitation skills in relevant Ugandan local languages, or demonstrated experience working effectively through local language facilitators and interpreters.
Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations or strategic reviews, ideally within mixed methods, Made in Africa evaluation-aligned designs, is an advantage.

Job Title: Thematic Expert- Gender, Inclusion and Safeguarding
Job Description:
Purpose of the Role
The Gender, Inclusion and Safeguarding Expert brings expertise in gender-responsive evaluation, inclusive programming for structurally excluded groups, and safeguarding practice. Across assigned Strategic Reviews, the expert leads disaggregated analysis across gender, refugee status, and disability status; oversees qualitative data collection with these populations; ensures safeguarding standards are upheld throughout fieldwork; and ensures inclusion perspectives are reflected across all review deliverables.
Key Accountabilities/Responsibilities
Lead disaggregated analysis of quantitative and qualitative findings across gender, refugee status, and disability status for each assigned review, examining how outcomes in reach, access, progression, and quality of life differ across these inclusion population groups.
Oversee the design and quality of qualitative instruments (IDI, FGD, and KII guides) to ensure they are gender-responsive, trauma-informed, and appropriate for engagement with refugees, young women, and persons with disabilities, adapted to the specific population and geography of each assignment.
Directly oversee Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), In-Depth Interviews (IDIs), and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with refugee youth, young women, and other structurally excluded groups, with FGDs conducted single-sex to support open and honest sharing, in locations and languages appropriate to each assignment.
Ensure all fieldwork involving refugees, PWDs, and young women applies appropriate adaptations to interview environment, pace, and logistics, consistent with safeguarding commitments and POA inclusion and equity principles.
Serve as the review team’s primary safeguarding focal point during fieldwork for each assignment: ensuring informed consent procedures are properly followed, identifying and managing any safeguarding risks or disclosures that arise during data collection, and ensuring a clear referral pathway is in place and communicated to field teams before data collection begins.
Examine the extent to which gender, safeguarding, disability inclusion, and refugee protection were integrated into the Implementing Partner’s program design and delivery, and how this influenced inclusion outcomes (POA Question Area 1).
Lead analysis of system-level changes supporting greater inclusion of young women and marginalized groups, and of unintended positive or negative effects on these groups (POA Question Areas 3 and 4).
Train or brief Research Coordinators, Senior Field Officers and Field Officers on gender-responsive and safeguarding-sensitive data collection practices ahead of fieldwork for each assignment.
Co-author the gender, inclusion, and safeguarding sections of each Strategic Review's final report, ensuring inclusion perspectives are integrated throughout, not confined to a standalone section, and contribute to recommendations for strengthening inclusive design in future programming.
Indicative Deliverables
Inception report with methodology and work plan.
Technical input to the Strategic Review instruments relating to gender, inclusion, and safeguarding indicators and disaggregation strategy.
Desk review synthesis input on gender, inclusion and safeguarding relevant to the Implementing Partner’s sector and geography.
Administering Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), In-depth Interviews (IDIs) and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with documented adaptations for refugee, PWD, and young women respondents relevant to the assignment.
A short safeguarding briefing note and referral pathway for field teams, finalised before data collection begins.
Oversight of qualitative fieldwork as scheduled for the assignment, with field notes or summaries as agreed with the review’s lead.
Disaggregated analysis note covering gender, refugee status, and disability status across POA outcome areas.
Interim findings presentation to the Foundation team.
Final report (max 40 pages, excluding annexes) including executive summary, digital economy analysis chapter, recommendations, and a prioritized action matrix.
Drafted sections of the final Strategic Review report covering gender, inclusion, safeguarding integration, and related recommendations.
Participation in sensemaking and validation sessions with the Mastercard Foundation and the relevant Implementing Partner, as required.
Required Qualifications
The expert should possess
Advanced degree in gender studies, social sciences, development studies, or a related field.
Minimum 8-10 years of experience in gender-responsive evaluation, inclusive programming, or safeguarding in development or humanitarian contexts in Uganda, ideally including direct work with refugee or displaced populations and persons with disabilities.
Demonstrated experience designing and conducting qualitative fieldwork (IDIs, FGDs, KIIs) with structurally excluded groups, including trauma-informed and culturally appropriate facilitation techniques.
Working knowledge of safeguarding frameworks and referral pathways appropriate to the Uganda context, including experience handling sensitive disclosures during fieldwork.
Familiarity with Uganda’s refugee response context (including major refugee settlement areas) and with national gender and disability inclusion policy is strongly preferred.
Strong facilitation skills in relevant Ugandan local languages, or demonstrated experience working effectively through local-language facilitators and interpreters.
Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations or strategic reviews, ideally within mixed-methods designs, is an advantage.

The Financial Inclusion and MSME Expert brings specialist expertise in financial sector development, MSME finance, and inclusive finance mechanisms (including credit guarantees, digital financial services, and value chain finance) relevant to Uganda and the East Africa region. Examine enterprise progression along the growth spectrum (micro to small to medium), including which combinations of interventions generate the strongest results for enterprise growth and job creation.

Contribute to each review’s desk review by assessing the Implementing Partner's financial inclusion approach against comparable and alternative inclusive finance models operating in Uganda and the East Africa region.
Support the development and review of qualitative Inquiry content and analytical frameworks relating to financial capability, financial behavior, and enterprise outcomes.
Lead Key Informant Interviews with Implementing Partner leadership, technical teams, and ecosystem actors (financial regulators, sector associations) relevant to financial inclusion.
Co-author the financial inclusion, MSME outcomes, and systems contribution sections of each Strategic Review's final report, and contribute to actionable recommendations for future access-to-finance programming.

Technical input to the Strategic Review Questions relating to financial inclusion and MSME indicators.
Desk review synthesis input on financial inclusion and comparative inclusive finance models relevant to the Implementing Partner’s sector and geography.

Technical analysis notes on financial inclusion outcomes, financing mechanism effects, and enterprise progression.
Interim findings presentation to the Foundation team.

Participation in sensemaking and validation sessions with the Mastercard Foundation and the relevant Implementing Partner, as required.

Advanced degree in economics, finance, development studies, or a related field.
Minimum 8-10 years of experience in financial sector development, MSME finance, or inclusive finance programming in Uganda or East Africa, including experience with at least one of: digital financial services or value chain finance.
Demonstrated experience analyzing financial inclusion outcomes for underserved populations, including youth, women, refugees, and PWDs, within the Uganda or East African context.
Prior experience contributing to or leading evaluations, strategic reviews, or assessments for development programs, ideally within mixed-methods (quantitative and qualitative) designs.
Strong analytical and report-writing skills, with the ability to translate technical financial data into actionable findings for non-specialist audiences including donors and implementing partners.

Availability for flexible, short-term deployment across multiple assignments within the Uganda portfolio over the engagement period.

All leonine contracts created by I&M Bank Limited that employ standardized, non-negotiated/non-negotiable provisions.
All Contracts between the Bank and Service Providers or Vendors including but not limited to License Agreements, Maintenance Agreements, Service Level Agreements, etc.

Continuous scrutiny and review of the Bank’s Contract Management Policy in line with new laws and applicable industry practice.
Periodic review and update of the Bank’s General Terms and Conditions and all other internal terms and conditions.

Company Details: Kirinyaga County borders Nyeri County, Murang’a County and Embu County.It covers an area of 1,478.1 square kilometers. Kenya which lies on the northern side grea...read moretly influences the landscape of the county as well as other topographical features. The snow melting from the mountain forms the water tower for the rivers that drain in the county and other areas that lie south and west of the county. The county can be divided into three ecological zones; the lowland areas, the midland areas and the highlands. The county is well endowed with a thick, indigenous forest with unique types of trees covering Mt. Kenya. Mt. Kenya Forest covers 350.7 Km2 and is inhabited by a variety of wildlife including elephants, buffaloes, monkeys, bushbucks and colourful birds while the lower parts of the forest zone provides grazing land for livestock. The rich flora and fauna within the forest coupled with mountain climbing are a great potential for tourist activities. The county has six major rivers namely; Sagana, Nyamindi, Rupingazi, Thiba, Rwamuthambi and Ragati, all of which drain into the Tana River. These rivers are the principal source of water in the county. The water from these rivers has been harnessed through canals to support irrigation at the lower zones of the county. The county has a tropical climate and an equatorial rainfall pattern. The climatic condition is influenced by the county position along the equator and its position on the windward side of Mt Kenya. The county has two rainy seasons, the long rains and the short rains. Administratively, the county is divided into five districts namely; Kirinyaga East, Kirinyaga West, Mwea East, Mwea West and Kirinyaga Central. The districts are subdivided further into 12 divisions, 30 locations and 81 sub-locations.The county has four constituencies namely Mwea, Ndia, Kirinyaga Central and Gichugu. Kirinyaga County has twenty (20) wards. From the Kenya Population and Housing Census 2009 report, the population of the county stood at 528,054 persons with an annual growth rate of 1.5 percent. The population is projected to be 595, 379 in 2017. Kerugoya, Sagana and Wang’uru are the only towns in the County while Kagio and Kagumo comprise the urban centres. The town with the highest population is Wang’uru with a population of 18,437; followed by Kerugoya with a population of 17,122; the least populated town is Sagana with a population of 10,344. The urban centre with the highest population is Kagio with a population of 3,512 followed closely by Kagumo with a population of 3,489. The population of Wang’uru is highest because it has a lot of economic activities, mainly rice farming while Kerugoya town had long been the District administrative headquarters. The total road network of in the county is 1,109.11 Km, out of which 106.5 Km is bitumen, 462.05 Km is gravel and 540.5 Km is earth surfaced roads. The county has an established road network with 7 tarmac roads passing through it namely Makutano – Embu road, Kutus – Karatina road, Baricho road, Kiburu road, Kutus – Sagana road, Kutus – Kianyaga road and Kabare – Kimunye road. There is only a 5km of railway line and one railway station in the county located in Ndia Constituency but currently not in use. There is one airstrip located in Mwea constituency. The mobile phone coverage stands at 99 percent while the number of fixed lines stands at 693 units. There are 5 sub- post offices and 14 cyber-cafes. There is also an increase in the usage of computers and internet in government offices, private businesses and homes due to availability portable modems and affordability of computers and laptops.

Job Description:
POSITION PROFILE
In response to the shifting humanitarian financing landscape, IMPACT is placing greater emphasis on producing comparable, decision-oriented analysis products to inform humanitarian prioritization. This position will be working on the second round of the Acute Needs Analysis (ANA) – a flagship analytical output that summarizes available data to provide a concise, actionable understanding of risk of loss of life across geographies and population groups within a crisis in order to feed into key decision-points, such as the HPC and donor allocations.
The (Senior) Analyst – Acute Needs Analysis will be responsible for producing this analytical product at country level. This includes reviewing and synthesizing data, conducting structured analysis using IMPACT’s global analytical guidance, and producing a short, high-impact external brief. The analyst will work closely with GIS, data, and design colleagues to incorporate visual elements into the final output. The final analytical product will play a key role in informing humanitarian prioritization decisions.
RESPONSIBILITIES
DEVELOPMENT OF ANALYTICAL PRODUCT – ACUTE NEEDS ANALYSIS
Lead the implementation and delivery of the analysis project at the country level, in coordination with the HQ programme team.
Align the rollout with global schedules and ensure adherence to IMPACT’s analytical standards.
Develop and maintain a strong stakeholder mapping and a network of collaborators at country level to enhance contextual understanding / monitoring.
Ensure development of user-centered products and, where relevant, support joint analysis with relevant stakeholders.
DATA REVIEW AND CONSOLIDATION
Collect and synthesize relevant secondary data from REACH assessments, UN agencies, INGOs, and public datasets (e.g., OCHA, FEWS NET, IPC), including via building and maintaining necessary relationships.
Evaluate data reliability and identify critical gaps.
Support decisions on the need for targeted, light-touch primary data collection.
ANALYTICAL PROCESS AND INTERPRETATION
Apply IMPACT’s global analytical guidance to produce structured, consistent, and context-relevant analysis of acute needs analysis.
Use defined frameworks (e.g. Risk of Excess Mortality) to identify areas at risk of large-scale loss of life and estimate the number of people experiencing life-threatening conditions
Clearly document assumptions, limitations, and analytical reasoning.
OUTPUT PRODUCTION AND DISSEMINATION
Draft the Acute Needs Analysis brief using standardized global templates and language.
Collaborate with GIS and design colleagues to include maps, caseload tables, and other visual aids.
Ensure internal review and validation of the product before dissemination.
Present findings to clusters, working groups, and donors as needed.
As needed, support the development of Global Key Messages based on country level findings.
LEARNING, INNOVATION, AND QUALITY ASSURANCE
Participate in lessons-learned reviews and propose improvements to global analysis processes and guidance.
Contribute to organisational learning on running analysis workstreams and contribute to reflections and development of additional analytical workstreams, in collaboration with country and global counterparts.
Support internal knowledge sharing and analytical training at the country level.
Stay updated on sectoral best practices and innovations in humanitarian analysis.
The (Senior) Analyst will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.
REQUIREMENTS
Note, roles can be at Senior Analyst or Analyst level, based on the experience of the candidate.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as analysis, assessments, monitoring and evaluation and research design etc. with direct in-country experience;
Excellent academic qualifications, including a master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. international development studies / international relations, humanitarian response, data science, political science, etc.);
TECHNICAL SKILLS:
Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills with experience of interpreting complex data and producing clear, actionable insights.
Strong writing skills and experience producing clear, concise briefs for external audiences.
Proficiency in Excel, with experience of an additional analytical tool (e.g. PowerBI, SPSS, R, STATA, or Python) and an understanding of basic GIS processes and outputs an asset.
Familiarity with different qualitative and quantitative research methods, with the ability to evaluate the quality of different data sources.
Understanding of humanitarian coordination systems, including HPC and inter-agency needs analysis and assessments.

Job Description:
APHRC is recruiting a Multimedia Officer for its Synergy Unit’s Policy Engagement and Communications Program. The Officer will lead the creation of visual, audio, and digital content to translate complex research findings and policy messages into accessible, engaging products. This position requires a creative professional skilled in multimedia production, research communication, digital storytelling, and audience engagement.
Key Responsibilities
Multimedia production and storytelling
Conceptualize and produce multimedia content in formats including videos, documentaries, animations, podcasts, webcasts, photography, digital stories, online galleries, infographics, slide presentations and interactive products.
Translate research findings, policy messages and technical information into accessible and compelling visual and audio-visual narratives.

Conduct and record interviews with researchers, policymakers, programme participants, partners and other stakeholders.
Capture high-quality photographs, video footage and audio during APHRC activities, field visits, conferences and stakeholder engagements.
Produce human-interest stories and other multimedia products that demonstrate the relevance and impact of APHRC’s work.
Video, audio and photography
Manage the complete video and audio production process, including concept development, scripting, filming, recording, editing, post-production, subtitling and distribution.
Provide professional photography and videography support for institutional and programme activities.
Set up and operate cameras, lighting, sound and related production equipment.
Coordinate external production companies, photographers, videographers, animators and other multimedia service providers when required.
Ensure that multimedia productions meet APHRC’s editorial, technical, ethical and safeguarding standards.
Obtain and manage appropriate consent for photography, video, audio and personal stories.
Graphic design and data visualization
Design high-quality products for digital and print use, including infographics, reports, policy briefs, factsheets, event materials, social media assets, presentations, banners and exhibition materials.
Work with researchers and policy engagement teams to present data and evidence through accurate and accessible visualizations.
Develop creative concepts, templates and visual assets that strengthen consistency across APHRC products.
Apply sound principles of typography, colour, composition, accessibility and information hierarchy.
Ensure that all visual products comply with APHRC’s brand guidelines and relevant partner requirements.
Digital platforms and events
Produce and adapt multimedia content for APHRC’s website, social media platforms, newsletters, digital campaigns and other communication channels.
Support the planning and technical delivery of webinars, livestreams, hybrid meetings, conferences, exhibitions and other institutional events.
Provide audio-visual support, including presentation management, recording, streaming and post-event editing.
Optimize content for different platforms, audiences, devices and internet environments.
Monitor emerging multimedia formats, tools and audience trends and recommend appropriate innovations for APHRC.
Multimedia asset management
Maintain organized institutional databases and archives for photographs, videos, audio recordings, graphics, consent forms and other digital assets.
Develop and apply clear systems for naming, classifying, storing, retrieving and backing up multimedia files.
Maintain an inventory of audio-visual equipment and coordinate its appropriate use, storage and maintenance.
Ensure that multimedia assets are properly licensed, credited and used in accordance with copyright, data protection and consent requirements.
Support the development and implementation of institutional multimedia production standards and procedures.
Planning, collaboration and quality assurance
Work closely with the Synergy Unit, programme teams and other institutional functions to identify multimedia needs and develop appropriate products.
Contribute multimedia activities, timelines and resource requirements to communications and policy engagement plans.
Manage multiple production assignments while meeting agreed deadlines and quality standards.
Review and quality-assure multimedia products developed internally or by external service providers.
Support the procurement and management of multimedia consultants, vendors and production services.
Track the reach, engagement and use of multimedia products and contribute to communications performance reporting.
Provide multimedia guidance and basic capacity strengthening to staff and partners.
Perform other related duties assigned in support of the Synergy Unit and APHRC’s institutional objectives.
Required qualifications and experience
Bachelor’s degree in Multimedia Production, Film and Television Production, Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Digital Media, Journalism, Communications or a related field.
At least three years of relevant professional experience in multimedia production, preferably within a research, policy, international development, non-governmental or similar organization.
A strong portfolio demonstrating experience in video production, photography, graphic design, visual storytelling and digital content development.
Demonstrated experience managing video production from concept and scripting through filming, editing and final delivery.
Experience producing multimedia content for websites, social media, digital campaigns, webinars and live or hybrid events.
Experience translating research, data or technical information into accessible visual products is highly desirable.
Experience working with researchers, policymakers, development partners or diverse multicultural teams will be an added advantage.
Technical Skills
Advanced proficiency in relevant multimedia production and design applications, such as Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Audition or comparable professional tools.

Strong video-editing, colour-correction, sound-editing, motion-graphics and post-production skills.
Knowledge of data visualization, information design, typography, colour theory and layout.
Familiarity with content-management systems, social media publishing tools and digital asset-management systems.

Creativity and strong visual judgment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong storytelling and interviewing abilities.
Attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to interpret complex research and policy information.
Strong planning, organization and time-management skills.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and work under deadlines.
Initiative, adaptability and a solution-oriented approach.
Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills.
Sensitivity when working with diverse communities and vulnerable populations.
Commitment to ethical, inclusive and culturally appropriate communication.
Ability to work independently and as part of multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.

Job Description:
JOB PURPOSE
Reporting to the METAL Coordinator, technically supported by the Regional MEAL Technology Coordinator and working closely with the TeachWell MEAL Advisor, the Senior MEAL Technology Officer leads MEAL technology delivery for the entire IRC Kenya country programme, including the TeachWell project. The allocation of the position's time and responsibilities between country
programme support and TeachWell will be agreed through work planning and elaborated in routine reporting.
Within the METAL framework, the Senior MEAL Technology Officer provides technical leadership for the country programme's digital and technology work, leading the design, delivery, integration and continuous improvement of its data systems and holding accountability for their quality, timeliness, interoperability and readiness for handover to government and partners.
Technical authority, systems standards and decision-making on the country programme's digital data architecture rest with the METAL Coordinator; the Senior MEAL Technology Officer designs ,implements, maintains and advances these systems and is accountable for the quality and timeliness of the technology deliverables.
The position carries out database management; expert-level design and administration of electronic data collection in CommCare; configuration of project indicators using Power Apps; management and development of the Project Indicator Dashboard (PID), TeachWell dashboard, Strategy dashboard and other Power BI products; development of a CommCare-based logframe tracking platform; administration of the Electronic Medical Records (EMR) system across IRC-supported health facilities; systems integration and interoperability between IRC, partner and government systems; including alignment of the EMR to Taifa Care, adoption of licensed AI for data quality, reporting and analysis under agreed governance data quality and protection; and user training and support.
Working closely with the METAL Coordinator, the role builds the capacity of users of various applications within the programmes to cascade technology integration from reporting to data sources
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Country programme MEAL technology support
Serve as the country programme's focal point for MEAL technology delivery across all projects and sectors, including the TeachWell project, working under the guidance and direction of the METAL Coordinator.
Support the TeachWell MEAL Advisor in overseeing IRC and partner MEAL technology requirements and in designing and managing the technology components project MEAL framework and results tracking across components, leveraging qualitative and quantitative methods; co-design indicators, measurement tools and monitoring responsibilities.
Conduct regular MEAL technology needs assessments across the IRC Kenya programme and propose a costed digital systems roadmap and standards, and apply and maintain the agreed standards across projects.
Implement and maintain the database architecture set, ensuring system integrity, security, version control, documentation and business continuity across the portfolio.
Design and implement transition plans for programmes migrating to new data collection tools, and manage migration/transformation of existing project and country-level data into standard data structures.
Collaborate with programmes, IT and Supply Chain to plan procurement, configuration and lifecycle management of devices and licenses for data management.
Deployment of technologies for data collection, management, analysis and visualization
Design, build, test, deploy and adapt CommCare applications across the country programme (including TeachWell data collection tools), applying advanced case management (case
hierarchies, parent–child and extension cases, case sharing, longitudinal client tracking), complex form logic (multi-language forms, validation, calculated questions, repeat groups, lookup tables), workspace administration (users, permissions, location hierarchies, versioning and releases), data services (Data Export Tool, CommCare APIs, live connections to Excel and Power BI), and performance optimization for field users on low-bandwidth connections.
Configure and deploy surveys and programme assessments in commcare and mobile applications through elaborate testing, user training and roll-out
Build and maintain the TeachWell teacher professional development case management system with teacher profiles, electronic attendance registers and classroom observation modules per training module, ongoing teacher support, communities of practices, digital learning and and harmonize it with partner school databases to link teacher and learner data.
Recommend and document improvements to CommCare use across the programme: reusable templates, standardized case structures, workflow automation and adoption of new platform features
Develop, document and roll out a CommCare-based digital logframe / results-framework tracking platform, modelling indicators, targets, baselines, and disaggregation, linking routine data collection to the corresponding indicators.
Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards across all sectors and projects for technical and non-technical audiences, including the PID, TeachWell dashboard and Strategy dashboard
Administer the Power BI service (workspaces, refresh, gateways, row-level security); document all dashboards so no product depends on a single individual or external consultant; and contribute analysis to routine reporting cycles.
Create system architecture that mirrors TeachWell partner capture systems for ease of seamless data sharing.
Develop spatial/GIS visualization of programme coverage and results across counties and camps.
EMR functional administration and support (in collaboration with the IT Manager)
The Senior MEAL Technology Officer is the programme's focal point for the functional administration, data quality and reporting of the EMR system. Infrastructure administration — including server management, backups and restore testing, software updates and patches, business continuity and disaster recovery, hardware lifecycle, and vendor and SLA management — is led by the IT Manager, with functional input from this position.
Manage EMR functional administration across IRC-supported health facilities: user accounts, roles, permissions and organization unit hierarchies; maintain functional documentation (configuration guides, data dictionaries, SOPs and audit logs).
Lead the EMR's alignment to Taifa Care and the national digital health ecosystem: coordinate the vendor's Digital Health Agency certification so the EMR becomes Taifa Care-compatible by the September 2026 deadline, secure interoperability with eCHIS and KHIS/DHIS2, and support Social Health Authority readiness so that IRC-supported facilities can be empanelled and claim.
Manage EMR data flows and integration with national reporting platforms (eCHIS, KHIS/DHIS2, iRHIS), ensuring reporting is accurate, timely and compliant with Ministry of Health requirements, and configuring aggregate exports that eliminate double-entry for facility staff.
Serve as the EMR training focal point for IRC health staff and partner facility staff: design and deliver role-specific training and job aids (in English and Swahili where appropriate), and provide first-line functional user support, escalating system and infrastructure issues to the IT Manager.
Lead user acceptance testing (UAT) for new EMR modules and enhancements; capture and prioritize enhancement and customization requests from clinical and MEAL staff, and channel them through the IT Manager and vendor for implementation and validation.
Design, build and maintain EMR reports and dashboards for programme, donor and Ministry of Health reporting, including indicator-level reports aligned to project logframes and patient/cohort-level analytics for clinical decision-making and defaulter tracking; train supervisors on their use.
Ensure EMR data practices comply with patient confidentiality requirements, IRC data protection policy and the Kenya Data Protection Act (2019), including consent capture, role-based access, data masking and retention schedules.
Data management, quality, protection and analysis
In close collaboration with the METAL Coordinator, undertake data analysis, data quality assurance and data reviews, and ensure findings inform programming and adaptive management.
Integrate data quality assurance mechanism in MEAL systems and provide feedback to MEAL team for management action
Lead routine and automated data quality checks across the portfolio, follow up remediation with data owners and partners, and verify that data is uploaded in line with SOPs and is complete, timely and accurate.
Ensure all tools, databases and integrations comply with IRC data protection policy, the Kenya Data Protection Act (2019), government data governance requirements and donor data quality guidelines.
User needs, training and support
Provide system training and ongoing end-user support to IRC and partner staff on databases, tools and dashboards, prioritizing partners with limited METAL capacity.
Gather user feedback during and after deployment, lead requirements capture and UAT for new tools, and ensure user needs are reflected in system design.
Responsible AI integration and innovation
Provide technical enablement for the country programme's flagship AI pilots, including the survivor-support and community feedback channels and geospatial targeting, and prepare each pilot for scale-up across hub offices once it is proven.
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Education
University degree in Information Technology, Database Development, Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Health Informatics or a related field.
Relevant professional certification (e.g., CommCare, Microsoft Power BI, DHIS2 fundamentals/implementation, data engineering and other related quantitative field) is an added advantage.
Experience and technical skills (required)
Minimum 5 years' experience in project database development, systems integration and data management, with a substantial portion in MEAL functions of humanitarian or development programmes.
Demonstrable CommCare competence is essential: advanced case management, complex form logic, CommCare HQ administration and data export/API configuration, including the ability to design indicator/results-tracking structures linked to routine data collection.
Advanced Power BI skills: data modelling, Power Query, DAX and service administration, evidenced by a portfolio of dashboards in active use, including managing an inherited indicator dashboard.
Working experience in tool development related to research, MEAL and other development utilities from origination, data collection analysis and use
Working in multisectoral / consortium projects is an added advantage
Note:
Technical competence is a core selection criterion. Shortlisted candidates will be required to complete a hands-on practical assessment at interview covering both CommCare application development and Power BI/dashboard development, including demonstrating an application and a dashboard they have built.
Demonstrated understanding of health information systems (eCHIS, KHIS/DHIS2, HMIS, EMR), their reporting workflows, and the confidentiality requirements of patient-level data.
Strong proficiency with mobile data collection (CommCare, ODK, Kobo) and data analysis software such as advanced Microsoft Excel, SPSS, STATA, R or Python, and GIS tools.
Working knowledge of data protection and responsible data practices in humanitarian settings.
Willingness to travel to field-level offices (up to 50%).
Knowledge of MEAL functionality across different thematic areas is an added advantage.
Desirable
Experience administering an EMR or comparable facility-based health information system, including user management, backups and vendor coordination.
Experience standardizing tools across a multi-sector portfolio.
Experience taking over, documenting and improving systems built by third-party consultants or departing staff.
Experience digitizing client feedback / accountability mechanisms.
Skills and abilities
Excellent interpersonal, time-management and communication skills, both verbal and written.
Ability to work independently, and under own initiative with a proactive approach to problem solving.
Proven skills in making empirical data accessible for different audiences through different channels and media.
Self-motivated and result-driven, with the ability to build and manage networks and relationships and issue resolution.

Company Details: The Mater Hospital was opened in 1962 by the Sisters of Mercy, a Catholic Order of Nuns originating from Ireland, three years after registering themselves as the Registered Trustees of an entity under the Perpetual Succession Act (the succeeding legislation after independence). The "Sisters...read moreof Mercy" first set up a 60 bed general hospital to cater mainly for the poor, indigenous Kenyans, with the primary mission being general healthcare. The colonial authorities granted 12 acres of land in a swampy, mosquito-infested area, which has since become the Industrial Area of Nairobi. In 1970, a 60-bed maternity ward was opened with antenatal, postnatal and immunization clinics attached in order to upgrade the quality of maternity healthcare available to the poorer segments of the Nairobi population. In 1972, in recognition of the contribution of the hospital in training midwives to assist births in rural areas, Mater was chartered as a School of Midwifery. In 1975, a consultant’s block of 6 offices was opened enabling specialised consultants to practice on site and deliver significantly better medical services to the patients. In 1986, the hospital opened its own pharmacy, physiotherapy and laboratory services and, in 1990, opened its counselling centre for inpatients, outpatients and staff who needed advice and guidance on family planning, HIV, and other concerns of a psychological and/or physical nature. In 1995, in a major building expansion programme, the hospital opened a larger and more efficient Casualty, Accident and Emergency Department, an Intensive Care Unit and a Cardiac Unit where open-heart surgery is performed. The missionary role of the Sisters of Mercy has spread to other parts of Kenya and the Mater Hospital has become a private hospital that charges a fee-for-service to a patient population that has developed locally to a much higher level of affluence compared with other parts of Kenya. The financial objective of the hospital is to provide affordable healthcare to as many people as possible but also attempt to meet all of its costs, including depreciation, in order to replace and upgrade medical equipment.

The East Africa Border Security Programme (BSP) takes a multifaceted approach – integrating ‘prevention’, ‘prepare/protect’ and ‘pursue’, working closely with national governments, partners and local communities to disrupt the criminal networks that facilitate human trafficking and smuggling across the land borders of the East Africa

Company Details:
In Kenya, Oxfam works with others to alleviate poverty and inequality. We work with the most vulnerable communities in the dry and remote northern regions, and in the impoverished slums of the capital, Nairobi.

In Kenya, the highest poverty levels are in the northern pastoralist districts - in so...read moreme areas 95% of people fall below the poverty line.

Like many developing countries, Kenya is undergoing rapid urbanisation. It’s estimated that by 2050 half the Kenyan population will be living in urban areas. This high presents a myriad of challenges. 34% of the 17 million poor Kenyans are urban poor and most of them live in informal urban settlements.

Oxfam in Kenya

Since starting work in Kenya in 1963, Oxfam has:

provided long-term development aid and emergency relief, for example supporting refugees;
promoted peace and managed conflicts between communities;
campaigned for better governance and equitable access to services.
We aim to help citizens stand up for their rights, and we work with others from government, civil society, communities, international development actors and the private sector.

Working with dry-land communities

In Turkana and Wajir we develop market-based alternative and complementary livelihoods, supporting fishermen and traders.

Working with poor urban communities

In the capital, Nairobi, we work with partners to run water kiosks, "bio-centers” that turn human waste into usable energy and improve sanitation, and recycling plants for unemployed youth. Our social protection programs provide cash to help poor families cope with rising costs of food and water and kickstart small businesses.

Peace-building and conflict management

We focus on enhancing communities’ capacity to resolve conflicts and co-exist peacefully. We also influence national policy through the National Steering Committee on Peace-Building and Conflict Management, under the Office of the President.

Climate change

We’re working closely with others, supporting local civil society to hold the Government accountable for its response to climate change. We’re also generating relevant climate change data to inform advocacy positions locally and internationally.

Governance

All of Oxfam’s work in Kenya is rooted in promoting better governance - at local, regional and national levels - by strengthening poor people’s ability to defend and demand their rights. We work to ensure that our partners and the communities we work with have their voices and concerns heard, and that the Government fulfils its responsibilities to poor Kenyans.

Job Description:
Purpose of the Job
The Internal Inspector is responsible for assessing the compliance of each group member, production unit, and collection center with organic production rules, according to the EU Regulations (2018/848),USDA/NOP, Regenerative Organic Standards, Fair For life standards and other standards. The role ensures that the members adhere to the Internal Control System (ICS) procedures, conducting effective farm inspections and providing clear, objective reports. The inspector must uphold the integrity of the certification process by avoiding any conflicts of interest. The role be required to build strong relationships with farmers supplying the company, ensuring that the Client is constantly aware of the evolving needs of its smallholder farmers, and that the company is offering solutions to meet these evolving needs in an effort to drive and grow farmer loyalty to the Client.
Additionally, the role will implement the approved yearly work plan and work closely with the field officers, buying clerks to ensure that the coconut requirements of the company are met in terms of quality and quantity.
It is a requirement that the role maintains high level of integrity, ethics and responsibility while ensuring compliance with the Clients organic and fair-trade standards.
Roles and Responsibilities
Internal inspection
Perform internal inspections of farms, production units, and collection centers in line with the ICS procedures and organic certification standards- USDA/NOP and EU 2018/848.
Review and verify farm compliance with EU organic regulations, including production methods, field management, and harvesting practices.
Carry out yield estimation and balance verification exercises, ensuring data accuracy.
Ensure that all documentation, including checklists and reports, is accurately completed and submitted on time and submitted to the ICS data clerk
Ensure that all internal inspections are carried out in accordance with the clients Grower Group Quality Manual and the annual work plan.
Identify any non-compliance and provide guidance on corrective actions for all the farmers assigned to you.
Accompany field officers during field visits and assist with monitoring and evaluation of farm activities.
Farmer Support
Work closely field officers with farmers to educate them on organic and Fair-Trade standards and practices.
Support farmers in meeting the Kentaste coconut quality requirements by ensuring traceability of coconuts at farm level
Provide on-site guidance to farmers on organic input requirements, proper harvesting methods, and other farming activities to meet Organic standards.
Training
Train field officers, buying clerks, receiving clerks and other staff on the inspection process and compliance requirements.
Participate in initial and ongoing training sessions on organic farming regulations and the ICS processes.
Keep up-to-date with changes in EU and USDA/NOP organic regulations and ensure compliance
during inspections.
Documentation and Reporting
Prepare detailed reports after each internal inspection, including observations, compliance status, and any necessary follow-up actions for assigned farmers.
Ensure all inspection reports are submitted to the data clerk in a timely manner.
Maintain accurate records of farmer compliance status and provide updates for the Approved Farmers List (AFL).
Assist with compiling data and reports for external inspections and certification bodies.
Communication
Communicate inspection findings and compliance requirements to farmers and field officers.
Ensure that all updates and decisions from the ICS Approvals Committee are conveyed to farmers promptly.
Collaborate with the Sustainability and Compliance Manager (S&C Manager to create and follow the annual internal inspection schedule.
Attend regular meetings to update the S&C Manager on inspection outcomes and potential issues within the group
Compliance Monitoring
Evaluate members' ongoing compliance with the ICS and EU regulations throughout the year and report any non-compliance or violations immediately to the S&C Manager and the Data Clerk.
Provide recommendations for corrective actions and follow-up on their implementation.
Monitor the implementation of corrective actions by farmers and follow up on areas identified for improvement.
Assist in managing compliance with organic and Fair Trade standards during each stage of production and harvesting, collection, transportation and holding.
Work closely with the Field officers, supervisors and S&C Manager to ensure continuous improvement in farmer practices and performance.
Maintain impartiality during inspections and declare any potential conflicts of interest (e.g.,family relations with members, previous work relationships).
Ensure compliance with conflict-of-interest rules: inspectors cannot audit their own parcels of land or members they have personal ties with.
Other Responsibilities
Support the field officers in the recruitment and onboarding of new farmers.
Collaborate with the Field Officers to ensure smooth communication and workflow between farmers and the ICS.
Ensure inspections align with ICS manuals and procedures, including maintaining farm documentation (e.g., maps, input registers).
Be familiar with the group’s internal risk assessment and conduct inspections based on risk categorization (low, medium, high).
Participate in any additional duties as required by the S&C Manager.
Update the office on external partners’ activities and engagement at the village level. When needed, attend events as advised by the office and give feedback as required.
Take part in data gathering exercises as required by the management
Attend the monthly ICS reviews as planned by your supervisor:
To discuss the work plan
Previous month performance vs targets
Current month targets (financial and non-financial), timelines and milestone objectives.
Metrics
Smallholder Farmer internal inspections(compliant small holder farmers as a % of the total) All relevant data required of smallholder farmers
Develop monthly inspection schedules
100% farmer inspections within workplan period
Maintain the groups assigned to you;
100% farmer training attendance across at least two trainings annually
100% supply of projected coconuts to the Client.
95% collection of advances within guidelines set in the policy
100% Organic farmers certified as per the work plan
100% accuracy to yield projections – within reasonable conditions
100% coverage on all trainings.
Accurate and timely monthly reports as per approved templates and work plan
Requirements
A Diploma in Agriculture
Two years of work experience
Excellent knowledge and understanding of farming practices including Organic standards, Fair trade, Climate smart farming techniques.
Computer proficiency: Moderate computer skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint
Ability to communicate effectively with people across all literacy levels.
Ability to use smart gadgets in data collection and doing surveys
Confident public speaker
Willingness to spend long hours in the field riding and walking in the farms.
Ability to speak fluently in English and Swahili
Motorcycle riding experience with a valid license

Assist business growth in a sustainable and profitable manner by ensuring optimization of targeted profitability and compensation leveraging on risk-based pricing and fee models.

Monitoring of covenants and Risk Triggers on the assigned portfolio and carrying out periodic reviews in order to make appropriate recommendations to management so as to improve and maintain a quality of the portfolio.
Undertake periodic Customer visits to support business growth opportunities in structuring deals
Closely liaise with Credit Monitoring & Control and Business Support Units to facilitate early reporting, intervention and turnaround of deteriorating exposures.
Regularly engage RMs for timely annual review of facilities and closure of control items and covenants.
Recommend best practices and Identify opportunities to improve processing efficiencies to enhance Customer experience and make the customer journey an exciting experience.
Credit Approvals

A logical and solution-oriented thinker with a practical approach to problem-solving and delivering outcomes.

Clear and professional communication skills, with a good command of both spoken and written English.
