Job Description:
Job Purpose:
The Senior Associate Database Administrator (DBA) is responsible for the reliable and efficient operation of the Bank’s database environments, playing a lead role in day-to-day database administration while providing guidance to junior DBA staff.
The role encompasses the installation, configuration, monitoring, maintenance, and security of enterprise database systems, ensuring availability, performance, and integrity of data that underpins critical business applications.
Operating within the Data Center & BCP Section, the Senior Associate DBA works closely with development, infrastructure, and business support teams to uphold database management best practices and drive continuous improvement.
Roles & Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities:
Install, configure, and maintain relational database systems including Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL across development, test, and production environments.
Create and manage database objects such as tables, indexes, views, and stored procedures, ensuring alignment with schema design standards.
Apply and manage bug fixes, security patches, and software upgrades in accordance with change management procedures.
Maintain comprehensive documentation of database configurations, procedures, changes, and operational standards.
Administer Data Guard for database protection, failover, and standby operations, including setup, configuration, and ongoing management.
Support RAC administration to ensure continuous high availability of critical database services.
Manage, test, and validate database backup, restore, and recovery procedures to meet defined recovery time and point objectives.
Maintain and enhance disaster recovery capabilities in alignment with BCP frameworks and Bank requirements.
Proactively monitor database performance using Enterprise Manager and other toolsets, identifying and addressing issues before they impact operations.
Collaborate with development teams to review and optimize database queries, execution plans, and schema designs.
Conduct regular database audits to verify data integrity, consistency, and compliance with performance benchmarks.
Manage database security through administration of user accounts, roles, and access privileges in line with least-privilege principles.
Implement and enforce data security controls to protect sensitive and regulated information in accordance with Bank policy.
Support compliance with data security and regulatory requirements through periodic access reviews, audits, and reporting.
Provide technical support across the full development lifecycle including development, testing, performance tuning, and production deployments.
Troubleshoot and resolve database issues efficiently, acting as an escalation point for junior DBA staff.
Lead or support data migration and replication initiatives, ensuring minimal disruption to business operations.
Monitor and maintain database hardware, software, and interface health, escalating complex issues as appropriate.
Academic Qualifications & Work Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field.
Minimum 2-3 years of hands-on experience in database administration, with demonstrated expertise across at least one enterprise-grade RDBMS and exposure to
high-availability and recovery operations.
Preferred Certifications include Oracle OCA (Oracle Certified Associate) or OCP (Oracle Certified Professional), Microsoft SQL Server certification (e.g., DP-300), MySQL Database certification and/or AWS Certified Database (Specialty or equivalent cloud database certification).
Technical Skills:
Skilled in Oracle Database operations including Data Guard, RAC, and Oracle Enterprise Manager (OEM) and advanced configuration and administration, Microsoft SQL Server, including administration, configuration, and performance tuning and security hardening, MySQL and/or PostgreSQL, including installation, configuration, and operational management.
Experience with Cloud database platforms including AWS RDS and/or Azure SQL Database administration and management.
Advanced proficiency in SQL and database query languages, including query optimization and execution plan analysis.

Company Details:
The NCIC is a statutory body established under the National Cohesion and Integration Act (Act No.12 of 2008).

The Commission was borne out of the realization that long lasting peace, sustainable development and harmonious coexistence among Kenyans requires deliberate normative, institutional and...read moreattitudinal processes of constructing nationhood, national cohesion and integration.

The Commission draws its existence from the National Dialogue and Reconciliation Agreement signed in Nairobi on 1 February, 2008 by the Government; Party of National Unity (PNU) and Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) delegations, and witnessed by H.E. Kofi A. Annan for the Panel of Eminent African Personalities.

This Agreement formed the basis of the National Accord that H.E. President Mwai Kibaki and the Rt. Hon. Prime Minister Raila Amolo Odinga signed on 28 February, 2008 when the dialogue was officially launched.

The dialogue sought to provide a peaceful solution to the political impasse and violence that had engulfed the country, following the December 2007 Local, Parliamentary and Presidential Elections and had four (4) main agendas:
 Agenda No. 1 - Immediate action to stop violence and restore fundamental rights and liberties.
 Agenda No. 2 - Immediate measures to address the humanitarian crisis, promote reconciliation, healing and restoration.
 Agenda No. 3 - How to overcome the current political crisis.
 Agenda No. 4 - Long term measures and solutions (such as constitutional, institutional and legal reforms; land reform; poverty and inequity; unemployment, particularly among the youth; consolidating national cohesion and unity; and transparency, accountability and addressing impunity).

Agenda No. 4 under which the Commission was formed, recognized that long term issues with regard to poverty, inequitable distribution of resources and perceptions of historical injustices and exclusion of segments of the Kenyan society were among the underlying causes of the prevailing social tensions, instability and the cycle of violence recurrent in electoral processes in Kenya.

Discussions under this Agenda item therefore examined and proposed solutions to longstanding issues such as :
 Undertaking constitutional, legal and institutional reforms
 Tackling poverty and inequality as well as combating regional development imbalances
 Tackling unemployment, particularly among the youth
 Consolidating national cohesion and unity
 Undertaking land reform
 Addressing lack of accountability and transparency among leaders and clipping impunity.

Company Details: In 2008, the Government of Kenya approved the creation of Konza Technology City as a flagship Kenya Vision 2030 project. Vision 2030 aims to create a globally competitive and prosperous nation with a high quality of life by 2030. As part of this vision, Konza will be a sustainable, world class te...read morechnology hub and major economic driver for Kenya. Konza was initially conceived to capture the growing global Business Processing Outsourcing and Information Technology Enabled Services (BPO/ITES) sectors in Kenya. BPO/ITES business produced US$110 billion in revenues in 2010. Revenues from this industry are expected to increase three-fold to US$300 billion by 2015. Africa attracts about 1% of the total revenues accruing from this growing industry. Only a few African countries, including South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Ghana and Mauritius, have made an effort to develop their BPO/ITES industries. Given the robust tech industry already in Nairobi, Kenya has a unique opportunity to capture a sizable amount of the growing global BPO/ITES industry. In 2009, the Government of Kenya hired the International Finance Corporation, a member of the World Bank, to advise on the development and implementation of a world-class technology city, which would grow the BPO/ITES and other technology industries in Kenya. The Government commissioned feasibility studies that demonstrated the viability of Konza, the focus on BPO/ITES, and its potential contributions to local economic development. The studies conducted include a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment, Legal and Regulatory Due Diligence, and a Demand Assessment. The initial feasibility and concept master plan was prepared by Deloitte and Pell Frischmann, a United Kingdom based consultancy. Pell Frischmann proposed the establishment of Konza, a technology park with world class infrastructure that will be sustainable and have inclusive growth as key drivers. In 2009, The Konza Technology City project was initiated with the procurement of a 5,000 acre parcel of land at Malili Ranch, 60km south east of Nairobi along Mombasa-Nairobi A109 road. With this, the realization of Africa’s Silicon Savannah officially launched. In 2012, the Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology retained a team of consultants led by New York City based HR&A Advisors, Inc. to prepare a detailed business plan and master plan for Phase 1. The Master Development Partner1 (MDP1) team included SHoP Architects, Dalberg, Centre for Urban and Regional Planning, OZ Architecture, and Tetra Tech. The MDP team held extensive interviews with stakeholders, business leaders, potential investors, and led 5 workshops with government officials over nearly a year to develop a comprehensive plan for Konza. The first phase of Konza City is expected to create over 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The city will be developed as a public private partnership, in which the Government will take a minimal role, developing the public infrastructure and regulatory guidelines.

The current rail network in Kenya is the metre gauge commonly referred to as 'The Lunatic Line’. It was initially named the 'Uganda Railway’ after its destination. Its construction began in the Port city of Mombasa in 1896 and was completed in 1901 at the lines terminus in Kisumu. Operations on...read morethe line commenced in 1903. The Lunatic Line links Kampala in Uganda with the Indian Ocean town of Mombasa.

Branch lines were built to Thika in 1913, Lake Magadi in 1915, Kitale in 1926, Naro Moru in 1927 and from Tororo to Soroti in 1929. In 1929, the Uganda railway became Kenya Uganda Railways & Habours. In 1931, a branchline to Mount Kenya was completed and the main line was extended from Nakuru to Kampala in Uganda.

The line is 1,000 mm and is a single track all through with occasional sidings and passing points to deal with opposing traffic. Construction was carried out by labourers brought in from India. After completion, some of the Indians remained behind thus creating the Indian community in East Africa.

The line was a huge logistical achievement and became strategically and economically vital for Kenya, linking the Indian Ocean with Lake Victoria and the East African interior. Branch lines were built and the railway became an essential part of safari adventures in the early decades of the 20th Century.

Job Description:
IDinsight’s Associates and Senior Associates are high-performing early-career professionals passionate about experiencing the front-line realities of evidence-informed decision-making. These roles provide a rich, varied experience with responsibilities ranging from client interactions and management, in-depth research and analysis, data collection management, and team building. We seek intellectually curious, resilient, and team-oriented individuals who – in addition to developing professional and technical skills – are highly motivated to grapple with the difficulties and unpredictability of trying to improve lives at scale.
Associates and Senior Associates are responsible for the following areas of work:
Managing project team workflow, systems, deliverables
Driving the day-to-day execution of the project work according to project plans and leading internal coordination efforts for their team
Conducting and supporting fit-for-decision and right-fit research design, data collection or acquisition, technical analysis, and results visualization/packaging, etc. for project tasks
Creating client deliverables, including reports, slide decks, and oral presentations to inform decisions and actions of clients
Developing strategic communications to build awareness of IDinsight projects and learnings, contribute to sectoral knowledge, and shift the sector towards more evidence-informed policy and practices
Supporting their team in developing strong client relationships
Engaging with client and stakeholder relationships
Contributing to client development, including developing proposals and concept notes
Leading data collection activities
Overseeing all data collection activities to ensure quality, including managing data collection teams
Traveling to project sites, IDinsight offices, embedded client locations, and other areas as per project needs
Contributing to internal team building
Developing, piloting, and implementing internal systems or other organizational contributions (e.g., event management) for IDinsight, in coordination with functional teams such as Operations, Communications, Finance, etc.
Contributing to office life and culture building, such as facilitating All Hands Meetings; leading team building efforts at team retreats; participating in Social Cultural Committee events; and engaging with the DEI Working Group.
Associates learn professional, technical and life skills while working on some of the world’s most critical problems. No two experiences are the same. Some work deeply on one project for their entire program commitment, while others work across a variety of projects. Workstreams can immerse Associates in remote, front-line program contexts, deep statistical analyses, and/or high-level, strategic interactions.
Associates and Senior Associates will be staffed on IDinsight projects according to various factors including organizational need, timeline and availability, team dynamics, skills optimization, and professional growth and development. While we aim to factor in individual preferences whenever possible to staffing decisions, they are one of many factors in the project staffing process.
Career development
Skill and career development are core to IDinsight's values and long-term impact strategy. Associates and Senior Associates receive significant mentorship from IDinsight leadership, support from talented peers, and considerable autonomy in their work. They maintain professional development plans and are given "stretch" opportunities designed to strengthen a variety of skills. Real-time feedback and structured reviews are regularly provided to enable maximum professional growth. Additionally, Associates and Senior Associates have access to an annual professional development stipend that they are encouraged to utilize to explore their career interests and develop their skills.
Qualifications
IDinsight Associates and Senior Associates come from a wide range of disciplinary backgrounds, including economics, data science, policy research, development projects, engineering, environmental science, political science, public policy, literature and more. Given that no Associate or Senior Associate comes in with the same exact background as another, we’re typically looking for candidates with a broad range of qualifications and previous experiences. Here are some examples of the key qualifications most successful candidates should possess:
Knowledge, skills, and abilities
Strong analytical skills, with exposure to (either via professional work experience or academic coursework) the basics of econometrics, data, and research analysis tools, and quantitative and qualitative research processes or an ability to quickly understand these topics.
Strong writing skills with the ability to translate technical jargon into well-structured, writing-based deliverables (e.g., policy briefs, project memos, analytical reports, external blog posts, and more).
Ability to understand complex concepts and topics quickly even with limited prior knowledge or exposure and a willingness to invest in learning new concepts, skills, and methods without being prompted.
Behaviors and mindsets
Highly organized, attentive to deadlines, and able to manage a high volume of work with efficiency.
Excellent interpersonal skills, can effectively engage with stakeholders ranging from school children to senior government officials to internal colleagues, and places a high value on being a team player.
Intellectually curious and a willingness to share your opinions with the team, question the status quo, and encourage others to expand their perspectives
Excels in diverse team environments, consistently treating colleagues across our global organization with respect.
Deeply passionate about combating poverty worldwide and improving lives in disadvantaged populations.
Willingness to travel for extended periods of time where safety precautions and restrictions allow, including to remote and rural areas.
Additional preferred qualifications
Proficient in statistical analysis and data collection software, such as Stata, SPSS, R, SurveyCTO, and/or Open Data Kit.
Familiarity with local context and working proficiency in the relevant local languages of the placement state or regio

We are looking for a professional, experienced, trustworthy, and hardworking Private Household Che
f

, Ruiru
.

All activities will be aligned with the UNHCR Global Strategy for Sustainable Energy, the Kenya Multi-Year Energy Strategy 2026-2030, the Shirika Plan, and the Kalobeyei Integrated Socio-Economic Development Plan (KISEDP).
Roles and responsibilities:
Activity Monitoring and Implementation Follow-up (35%)
This constitutes the core function of the role. The Senior Energy Associate will:
Conduct regular field visits across Kaku ma refugee camp (area 1-4) _and the Kalobeyei Integrated Settlement to monitor the progress of all ongoing energy projects, including solar electrification of health facilities, schools, and community centres, as well as electric cooking initiatives and O&M contracts.
Maintain an updated activity tracker and work plan dashboard for all energy activities across the operational area, proactively flagging delays, risks, and proposed mitigation measures.
Monitor the quality of implementation of contractor and partner activities, including solar installations, electric cooking device deployment, and associated training programmes.
Verify the effective functioning of O&M contracts and escalate issues related to system downtime or maintenance gaps to the Senior Energy Officer in a timely manner.
Monitor the operationalization and performance of newly installed solar systems at health facilities, schools, market areas, and UNHCR field facilities across both Kakuma and Kalobeyei.
Ensure systematic data collection and documentation across all field activities, including beneficiary counts, energy production data, and system performance records.
Prepare weekly and monthly technical monitoring reports for submission to the Head of Office and Senior Energy Officer and for contribution to the operation's Situation Reports (SitReps).
Project Implementation Support (35%)
Supervise and coordinate the training of local youth - from both refugee and host community backgrounds - in the operation and maintenance of solar systems and electric cooking devices, ensuring meaningful knowledge transfer and sustained local capacity development.
Support the rehabilitation of existing energy systems that have become non-functional due to maintenance deficits or unavailability of spare parts.
Collaborate closely with the WASH section to support the solarization of boreholes and strategic water infrastructure across both sites.
Support the piloting and scale-up of market-based energy approaches in Kalobeyei, including engagement with private sector actors and the development of micro­enterprise models for energy service delivery.
Technical Guidance and Capacity Building (15%
Provide technical guidance and support to UNHCR implementing partners engaged in energy and environment projects across the Kakuma-Kalobeyei area.
Support the capacity development of UNHCR Kakuma Sub-Office staff and implementing partners on sustainable energy concepts, monitoring methodologies, and reporting tools.
Contribute to the design and delivery of awareness-raising sessions for refugee and host community beneficiaries on the safe use and maintenance of energy technologies.
Support the implementation and scale-up of market-based renewable energy and clean cooking solutions, informed by field assessments, with a focus on investment readiness, gender-responsiveness, and long-term sustainability.
Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement (15%)
Act as UNHCR's field-level energy focal point in Kakuma-Kalobeyei, maintaining regular engagement with NGO partners, government counterparts (including Turkana County officials and the State Department for Refugee Services), private sector actors, and community representatives.
Participate actively in relevant field-level working groups and coordination forums related to energy, environment, WASH, and integrated settlement planning.
Engage with private sector energy service providers, social enterprises, and financial institutions exploring investment opportunities in the Kakuma-Kalobeyei energy market.
Maintain regular structured communication with the Senior Energy Officer in Nairobi, contributing field-based evidence and operational updates to country-level strategy discussions.
Monitoring and Progress Controls
The Senior Energy Associate will be expected to produce the following regular outputs throughout the assignment:
Produce structured weekly field monitoring reports covering activity progress, challenges, risks, and recommendations across both Kakuma and Kalobeyei.
Monthly activity progress report, encompassing project tracker updates, key performance indicators, operational challenges, and recommendations for both sites.
Contribution to the energy section of the UNHCR Kakuma-Kalobeyei Situation Report
(SitRep).
Ad hoc technical notes, field visit reports, and assessment summaries as required by the Sub-Office Management or Senior Energy Officer.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date project documentation, including contracts, technical specifications, as-built drawings, and training records.
Document and compile lessons learned and best practices from Kakuma-Kalobeyei energy interventions, with particular attention to the Kalobeyei integrated model, to inform Kenya­wide and global energy strategies.
End-of-assignment report summarizing key achievements, lessons learned, and strategic recommendations for the continuation and scale-up of energy activities across Kaku ma and Kalobeyei.
Qualifications and Experience:
Education
Bachelors with 4 years relevant experience or master's degree with 2 years relevant work experience in Renewable Energy, Energy Engineering, Environmental Science, Sustainable Development, or a closely related field.
Work Experience

Experience in a humanitarian, development, or integrated settlement context is a strong asset.
Demonstrated familiarity with solar energy systems, including design, installation, and O&M, is required.
Experience with clean cooking technologies, productive use of energy (PUE), and/or market-based energy approaches is a significant advantage.
Prior experience working in refugee settings, integrated development contexts, or remote, arid operational environments is desirable.
Knowledge of the Kalobeyei Integrated Socio-Economic Development Plan (KISEDP) and refugee self-reliance frameworks is an asset.
Key Competencies
Strong monitoring, data collection, and analytical skills, with the ability to translate field data into actionable recommendations.
Sound understanding of humanitarian and development energy needs, encompassing electricity access, clean cooking, greening of operations, and market-based approaches.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, multi-cultural, and multi-disciplinary team environment.
Demonstrated capacity to perform under pressure in stressful, remote, and resource­constrained settings.
Proficiency in standard ICT tools and energy data collection and visualisation software.

Heifer International's mission is to work with communities to end world hunger and poverty and to care for the Earth.
Dan West was a farmer from the American Midwest and member of the Church of the Brethren who went to the front lines of the Spanish Civil War as an aid worker. His mission was to pr...read moreovide relief, but he soon discovered the meager single cup of milk rationed to the weary refugees once a day was not enough.
And then he had a thought: What if they had not a cup, but a cow?
That "teach a man to fish" philosophy is what drove West to found Heifer International. And now, nearly 70 years later, that philosophy still inspires our work to end world hunger and poverty throughout the world once and for all.

HOW IT WORKS
We empower families to turn hunger and poverty into hope and prosperity - but our approach is more than just giving them a handout. Heifer links communities and helps bring sustainable agriculture and commerce to areas with a long history of poverty. Our animals provide partners with both food and reliable income, as agricultural products such as milk, eggs and honey can be traded or sold at market.
When many families gain this new sustainable income, it brings new opportunities for building schools, creating agricultural cooperatives, forming community savings and funding small businesses.

The Junior Trainer delivers classroom, practical, virtual and field-based training; supports curriculum and training material development; facilitates trainee assessments; maintains learning records; supports LMS administration; prepares training equipment and laboratories; and assists in monitoring the effectiveness of training interventions.

Programme design and feasibility assessment:
Collaborate with country teams to ideate and surface new programme concepts. Produce feasibility assessment memos that make clear recommendations and flag what we need to believe for the programme to work. Speed and judgment matter as much as comprehensiveness.
Community engagement & social accountability design:
Design community engagement from programme inception. This includes pre-implementation dialogue with communities about programme rationale and design, feedback and grievance mechanisms, and social accountability frameworks. Ensure communities understand we are serious about listening. Produce community engagement plans that go to country leadership teams (and other stakeholders) before implementation begins.
Implementation readiness planning:
Before a new programme launches, produce a launch readiness plan covering partnership agreements, monitoring and feedback loops, risk mitigation strategies, maintenance arrangements (especially for infrastructure), and ESG narrative. Identify what could derail this programme and outline mitigation. Your plan will signal to all stakeholders that we’ve thought through implementation challenges and accounted for them.
Collaboration with country teams and impact team colleagues.
Work closely with country teams on contextualisation and adaptation, ensuring research insights translate into locally-grounded programme design. Partner with research associates on qualitative and quantitative feedback loops during programme execution and community learning. You represent implementation reality and community voice in programme design discussions. Surface tensions between research evidence, feasibility concerns, and implementation reality for resolution. Help articulate programme theory, implementation approach, and learning strategy to donors and partners.
Flexible contribution to urgent priorities.
As part of the Impact team, you pitch in where needed across our research, monitoring, evaluation, and investment functions. This might include supporting fieldwork on an urgent evaluation, helping with community due diligence for an investment decision, or contributing to a time-sensitive analysis. You respond quickly to evolving priorities and can maintain flexibility to handle what's urgent as well as what's planned.
Ideal Profile
Bachelor's or master's degree in development economics, public policy, social sciences, or a related field. Strong academic record.
5+ years designing and managing programmes, community engagement, or implementation with an NGO, bilateral donor, or government. Experience launching new programmes and managing budgets, timelines, and teams. Experience in fragile or conflict-affected contexts.
Conversant with development economics literature and evidence-based programme design. You understand what works in your sector (e.g., water, education, skills training, etc.). You can engage substantively with research findings and help translate them into feasible programme design.
Creative problem-solver. You help design solutions that are both grounded in evidence and adapted to local context. You're comfortable proposing alternatives when the standard approach won't work. You draw from multiple sectors and contexts to inform your thinking.
Financial literacy. You can build basic programme budgets, model simple financial projections (e.g., programme NPV, cost per beneficiary, etc.), and understand cash flow implications of programme design. You may not identify as a financial modeler, but you can plug numbers and flag when the math doesn't work.
East Africa experience (ideally Somaliland, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya, or similar). You understand the operating environment and are not learning it from scratch.

You operate independently. You can receive a brief, define your assessment approach, spend time in the field, and deliver a polished output without being closely managed.
You work with urgency, moving fast with imperfect information while making defensible judgments and flagging uncertainties honestly.
Curious and mission-aligned. You want to understand how things work and care whether our programmes create impact. You are willing to push back when evidence warrants it.

Job Description:
Job Purpose:
Lead the delivery of Britam’s major technology programmes on behalf of the business. The first and largest is the Group ERP and HRIS implementation across the operating markets including all other programmes of similar scale. Set up each programme before design begins: governance, plan, budget, architecture and controls. Hold accountability for scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, vendor performance, adoption and benefits through go-live, hypercare and handover to business as usual. Lead the in-house software teams that build the integrations, extensions and self-service journeys around the core platforms, applying the delivery method suited to the work. Keep the sponsor, business owner, design authority, vendor and assurance roles distinct, and provide one agreed view of programme status.
Key responsibilities:
Programme leadership and governance
Mobilise each programme before design begins: secure approval of the charter, scope, governance, decision rights and success measures, and validate the business case, resources and market sequencing before baselining the plan.
Act as the single client-side point of accountability, run the governance forums covering design authority, delivery, market readiness and risk, escalate unresolved decisions early with options and a recommendation, and codify what each programme produces into reusable Group delivery standards.
Planning and delivery control
Own the integrated plan across every workstream, from solution build, integration and custom development through data migration, testing, change, security, cutover and market deployment.
Operate stage-gated control for vendor-delivered implementation alongside iterative release cycles for extensions and front-ends. Track schedule, cost, scope, quality, risk and benefits against approved baselines, and recover performance that moves outside tolerance.
In-house software delivery and engineering standards
Lead the teams building integrations, extensions, reports and self-service journeys around the core platforms, with named business product owners holding backlog authority and acceptance, and one prioritised backlog so that no parallel change queue forms.
Protect configuration-first design, with every extension carrying a rationale, a named owner and an assessed support cost, and enforce engineering standards covering source control, peer review, automated build, deployment and regression testing, and secure coding. No release bypasses design authority approval or segregation-of-duties review.
Design, data, security and go-live
Chair the client design authority, challenge unnecessary customisation on evidence, and drive a group-first design with controlled local variation for statutory, tax, payroll, language and currency requirements. No programme replicates inefficient legacy processes in a new platform.
Own data migration and reconciliation end to end, coordinate integration with the core insurance, banking, payroll, payments, procurement, identity and reporting platforms, and ensure access management, segregation of duties, audit trails, cybersecurity, data privacy and recovery requirements are built and tested.
Set the testing strategy with auditable entry and exit criteria and business sign-off, block progression through any stage gate where evidence, controls or readiness is incomplete, own cutover and go/no-go, lead hypercare to agreed exit criteria, and hand over to the permanent support organisation.
Vendor, commercial and financial control
Manage systems integrators, software vendors and third parties against contracts, milestones, service levels and acceptance criteria; challenge estimates, change requests and claims independently; and lead corrective action, contractual notice and dispute resolution.
Control budget, forecast, contingency and total cost of ownership, including the run cost of custom-built components, and validate invoices and milestone payments against accepted deliverables with Finance and Procurement.
Change, adoption, benefits and people
Align process redesign, communications, training and adoption with the technical plan, track readiness by market, function and user group, and hold business owners accountable for process decisions, data quality, user acceptance and post-go-live performance. Training completion is an input to adoption, not evidence of it.
Define benefit owners, baselines and realisation plans, and lead a cross-functional, cross-market team of internal staff, engineers, consultants and vendor personnel: clarify accountabilities, secure ring-fenced capacity and coach workstream and squad leads.
Knowledge, experience and qualifications required:
Academic qualifications and certifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business Technology or a related field; a Master’s degree is desirable.
Mandatory:
Current PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, MSP Practitioner, PgMP or equivalent.
Preferred: a recognized agile certification, cloud ERP or HRIS product certification on the platform selected by Britam, and ITIL, COBIT, CISA or CRISC.
Experience:
At least 8 years in enterprise technology delivery, including at least 3 years leading complex multi-workstream programmes and at least 5 years in ERP, HRIS or comparable enterprise applications.
Personal leadership of at least two full cloud ERP implementations from inception through go-live, hypercare and transition to business as usual, of which at least one carried HRIS or payroll scope in a regulated financial services environment.
Leadership of in-house software teams under both stage-gated and iterative methods, and of a multi-country implementation across at least four countries or jurisdictions with global-template design and controlled localization. Delivery of a further programme of a different type, for example core insurance replacement, digital channels, contact center or cloud migration, is preferred.
Accountability for a budget at or above the Group Procurement threshold for major technology investment, and management of a software vendor, a major systems integrator and third parties under outcome-based contracts and milestone acceptance.
Working knowledge of financial services regulation, technology risk, information security, data privacy and internal control, with Africa or emerging multi-regulatory market experience preferred.
Technical Skills and Behavioral Competencies
Technical:
Programme delivery and control: stage-gated, iterative and hybrid methods and the interlock between them, critical-path analysis, earned value, forecasting, commercial change control, vendor performance management, RAID and decision governance, and benefits realization.
Cloud ERP and HRIS implementation lifecycle, including vendor release management, environment strategy and regression impact; functional coverage across finance, procurement and planning and across core human resources, payroll, talent, compensation and absence; and the enterprise structures, ledgers and statutory reporting that connect them.
Enterprise and integration architecture, data migration, and software engineering practice covering source control, peer review, continuous integration and deployment, automated testing and release management. Security and control design covering access management, segregation of duties, privileged access, audit trails and privacy by design, with end-to-end and non-functional testing, operational readiness and cutover management.
Behavioral:
Enterprise leadership and ownership: acts with personal accountability for outcomes, connects plans and controls to daily execution, resolves ambiguity, and holds momentum through intense delivery periods without bypassing controls.
Independent judgement, commercial acumen and control orientation: tests assumptions and vendor claims without becoming adversarial, and protects governance, evidence and value for money.
Executive influence and cross-cultural leadership: presents complex issues with the options and decisions required, builds alignment across markets, and coaches workstream and squad leads.

Company Details: Space for Giants is an international conservation organisation that protects the great wildlife landscapes that Africa's remaining elephants need to survive and thrive. These landscapes give homes to giants, but they also bring great value to people and nations: biodiversity, livelihoods and...read moreenterprise, new medicines, carbon storage, even the very oxygen we breathe. But they are under threat. Criminals kill endangered animals for tusks, horns, scales and skins. Farmers needing more land to feed their families expand into wildlife habitat. When wild animals then damage their crops, they retaliate.Space for Giants grew out of pioneering research in the early 2000s into how to encourage the co-existence of people and wildlife in modernising Africa. Since then, we have spent close to two decades working in these landscapes, studying how people and wild animals live together, and how that relationship is changing. We understand that to survive, these landscapes and their wildlife must prove that they bring value now and long into the future. Then they become assets people and governments fight to protect. We also understand that time is short. While we work to demonstrate this value, we must also act now to preserve these landscapes so that they don't disappear before it's too late.

Job Description:
The role
Post-harvest losses cost African farmers a share of everything they grow. That is an engineering problem, and it is the problem this role exists to work on.
We are looking for a recent mechanical engineering graduate to join our hardware team on a six-month internship. You will help standardise our Smart Solar Dryer product line: the drawings, the bills of quantities, the quality control and the field performance data that every deployment depends on.
We are a small, fast paced, innovative team. What we design is fabricated, installed and judged in the field within weeks, not years. You will spend real time on site in places like Kericho, Nyandarua, Makueni and Kisumu, and your work will directly determine whether what we install performs for the farmer.
If you want your engineering to be used rather than filed, this is that role.
What you will do
Prepare and maintain engineering drawings for our standard product range, under proper version control
Document drying chambers, airflow paths, ventilation, and fan and component selection
Instrument installed dryers and collect temperature, humidity and airflow data, then tabulate and present it clearly
Detail drying beds, racks and materials handling arrangements
Support thermal and drying performance testing across different crops and regions
Produce accurate quantity take-offs and bills of quantities from approved designs
Produce fabrication drawings and jig documentation for our workshop and subcontractor partners
Inspect sites against written quality control checklists, and record and close out defects
Verify materials on delivery against specification
Prepare as-built documentation and closeout packages for every deployment
Submit a written weekly report on your sites, on the agreed day, without being asked
How you will be supported
You will not carry unsupervised design responsibility. Fan and airflow sizing, thermal assumptions, structural member sizing, and any change to an approved design are reviewed and signed off before anything goes to fabrication, site or client.
We are explicit about this because it is how you learn properly, and because it is how our customers stay safe.
What we are looking for
A recent graduate — BSc in Mechanical Engineering, completed within the last two years. Agricultural or Biosystems Engineering with a strong thermal and fluids grounding also works. Candidates awaiting conferment may apply with a transcript
Competent in AutoCAD. SolidWorks, Inventor or equivalent is a plus
Comfortable in Excel for take-offs, schedules and data
Willing to travel to rural field sites at short notice
Clear written English — a large part of this job is documentation other people rely on
Someone who shows their working. When you give us a number, you can tell us where it came from
Someone who says 'I don't know yet' and then goes and finds out
Genuinely interested in agriculture and in farmers doing better
What we offer
A monthly stipend of KES 20,000 gross (statutory deductions apply; we will confirm the net figure in your offer)
Six months of real engineering work on products that go into the field, with honest feedback and clear goals
Field travel and related costs on company business covered
A certificate of internship and a reference on successful completion
Please note: this is a fixed six-month internship. It does not automatically extend or convert into a permanent role. If a permanent position opens and is funded, you are welcome to apply for it on its merits.

Company Details: The Mater Hospital was opened in 1962 by the Sisters of Mercy, a Catholic Order of Nuns originating from Ireland, three years after registering themselves as the Registered Trustees of an entity under the Perpetual Succession Act (the succeeding legislation after independence). The "Sisters...read moreof Mercy" first set up a 60 bed general hospital to cater mainly for the poor, indigenous Kenyans, with the primary mission being general healthcare. The colonial authorities granted 12 acres of land in a swampy, mosquito-infested area, which has since become the Industrial Area of Nairobi. In 1970, a 60-bed maternity ward was opened with antenatal, postnatal and immunization clinics attached in order to upgrade the quality of maternity healthcare available to the poorer segments of the Nairobi population. In 1972, in recognition of the contribution of the hospital in training midwives to assist births in rural areas, Mater was chartered as a School of Midwifery. In 1975, a consultant’s block of 6 offices was opened enabling specialised consultants to practice on site and deliver significantly better medical services to the patients. In 1986, the hospital opened its own pharmacy, physiotherapy and laboratory services and, in 1990, opened its counselling centre for inpatients, outpatients and staff who needed advice and guidance on family planning, HIV, and other concerns of a psychological and/or physical nature. In 1995, in a major building expansion programme, the hospital opened a larger and more efficient Casualty, Accident and Emergency Department, an Intensive Care Unit and a Cardiac Unit where open-heart surgery is performed. The missionary role of the Sisters of Mercy has spread to other parts of Kenya and the Mater Hospital has become a private hospital that charges a fee-for-service to a patient population that has developed locally to a much higher level of affluence compared with other parts of Kenya. The financial objective of the hospital is to provide affordable healthcare to as many people as possible but also attempt to meet all of its costs, including depreciation, in order to replace and upgrade medical equipment.

Reporting to the facility inhcharge, the MCH nurse will be tasked to provide high-quality maternal, newborn, and child health services, ensuring optimal health outcomes for women, infants, and children Including Overseeing the Child Welfare Clinic (CWC) and Expanded Program for Immunization (EPI) programs in the Facility.
Key Responsibilities:
Maternal Health:
Provide comprehensive antenatal care, including health assessments, counseling, and education.
Assist with normal deliveries and conduct emergency deliveries for clients presenting in second stage at the clinic.
Provide postnatal care, including counseling on breastfeeding, family planning, and newborn care.
Identify and manage and/or refer high risk conditions during pregnancy and postpartum periods.
Perform essential procedures such as blood pressure monitoring, fetal heart rate monitoring, and vaginal examinations.
Provide Maternal EPI services (Tetanus injections) as per schedule.
Offer family planning counseling and services, including long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs).
Provide post-abortion care and cervical cancer screening and treatment services.
Neonatal Health:
Monitor newborn health and identify any potential complications.
Monitor breastfeeding and offer guidance on other nutrition options.
Provide linkage with Nutrition for vulnerable Neonates as per assessment.
Administer essential neonatal interventions, such as treatment of common ailments and vaccinations.
Child Health:
Provide immunization services according to the Expanded Program of immunization (EPI) schedule.
Manage common childhood illnesses, such as diarrhea, pneumonia, and malaria.
Conduct growth monitoring and promote optimal child development through child welfare clinic (CWC).
Provide nutritional counseling and support.
Record Keeping:
Maintain accurate and up-to-date medical records for all patients.
Submit timely reports on maternal, newborn, and child health indicators.
Training and Supervision:
Participate in training and capacity-building activities to enhance skills and knowledge.
Supervise and mentor junior staff.
Participate in Facility Clinical audits
Attend an participate in Facility CMES
Community Outreach:
Conduct in-facility health education sessions on maternal, newborn, and child health topics.
Participate in community outreach activities to promote health-seeking behaviors on needs basis.
Together with the nurse and clinician, organize for adequate clinic coverage when required.
Carry out any other additional duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.
Key Result Areas:
Reduced maternal and neonatal mortality rates
Increased uptake of antenatal and postnatal care services
Increased uptake of EPI services
Reduction of malnutrition through monitoring of children at the child welfare clinic
Improved family planning utilization rates
Strengthened community -facility linkage.
Effective supervision and mentorship of junior staff
Required Qualifications:
KRCHN, KRN/KRM.
Registration with the Nursing Council of Kenya
Required Experience & Competencies:
At least 1 years of experience in a busy maternal child health department/clinic.
Emergency Obstetrics and Newborn Care / Respectful maternal newborn competency trainings highly desirable.
Strong clinical skills and knowledge of maternal and child health
Ability to work under pressure and in challenging environments
Good communication and interpersonal skills.

Job Description:
Job Overview:
Airbel Ventures is the IRC's impact investing arm, launched in July 2025 to bridge humanitarian need and private-sector innovation. It invests in seed-stage businesses across Africa and parts of MENA that can help reach more people, faster, and at lower cost in humanitarian contexts, with a focus on climate, health, education, and economic opportunities. Airbel Ventures is a separate entity, wholly owned by the IRC, governed by a Board and an Investment Committee.
The Investment Manager will play a central role in sourcing, evaluating, and managing investments in early-stage companies that deliver both strong impact and financial returns. The role reports to the Managing Partner of Airbel Ventures and works closely with IRC's Country Programs and technical teams to build traction for portfolio companies within humanitarian markets.
The Investment Manager is expected to leverage AI tools strategically to enhance effectiveness and efficiency in research and analysis, ensuring all AI-generated content is reviewed for accuracy, quality, and alignment with the IRC's mission and values.
Major Responsibilities:
Deal Sourcing: Identify and cultivate relationships with relevant startups, accelerators/incubators, and investors across Africa.
Due Diligence: Lead due diligence processes, including market analysis, financial modeling, impact assessment, and risk evaluation. Develop Investment Memos (IMs) to present to the Investment Committee.
Portfolio Management: Support portfolio companies post-investment through strategic guidance, fundraising support, and impact assessments, and build traction and use cases in humanitarian markets in coordination with IRC's Country Programs and technical teams.
Strategy: Contribute to deepened sector mapping and refine investment theses across Airbel Ventures' focus sectors, sub-sectors, and verticals.
Partnerships & Ecosystem Engagement: Represent Airbel Ventures in regional investor networks, events, and conferences, strengthening its visibility and partnerships in the African venture ecosystem.
Internal Stakeholder Engagement: Manage relevant IRC internal stakeholders through the full investment cycle and post-investment, including when building use cases and traction in humanitarian contexts.
Other Support: Support the Managing Partner on fundraising, overall portfolio strategy, and broader internal stakeholder engagement within the IRC.

Work Experience:
Right to work in Kenya required.
6–8 years of experience in venture capital, impact investing, development finance, or management consulting, with project experience in impact investing.
Experience managing due diligence processes from sourcing to closing.
Experience within African startup ecosystems, with existing networks across the African startup ecosystem.

Excellent financial analysis skills, including financial modeling.
Excellent analytical skills.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
To provide technical agricultural extension services and support to farmers to improve farm productivity, crop quality, sustainable farming practices, and reliable supply of quality raw materials to the company.
The Field Extension Intern will serve as the link between the company and farmers by conducting farm visits, providing technical advice, monitoring crop development, supporting farmer training, collecting field data, and ensuring compliance with the company's agricultural and quality standards.
Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Farmer Engagement and Support
Develop and maintain good working relationships with farmers and farmer groups.
Register and maintain updated farmer records within the assigned area.
Conduct regular farm visits and assess farmers' production practices.
Identify farmers' challenges and provide appropriate technical recommendations.
Respond to farmer inquiries and provide timely feedback.
Mobilize farmers for company programmes, trainings, meetings and field activities.
Support farmer group formation and development where applicable.
Agricultural Extension Services
Provide farmers with technical advice on recommended crop production practices.
Advise farmers on land preparation, planting, pruning, nutrition, pest and disease management, harvesting and post-harvest handling.
Demonstrate good agricultural practices through farm demonstrations and field days.
Conduct farmer training on productivity, quality and sustainable agricultural practices.
Monitor adoption of recommended agricultural practices.
Provide guidance on safe and responsible use of agricultural inputs.
Identify pest, disease and other crop-related challenges and escalate serious cases to the relevant technical personnel.
Farm Monitoring and Field Assessments
Conduct scheduled and routine farm inspections.
Monitor crop health, farm productivity and expected harvest volumes.
Assess farmer compliance with company requirements and applicable agricultural standards.
Identify risks that may affect crop quality or supply.
Prepare farm visit reports and document observations and recommendations.
Follow up on previously identified issues to ensure corrective actions are implemented.
Quality and Post-Harvest Management
Educate farmers on proper harvesting and post-harvest handling practices.
Promote practices that minimize contamination, deterioration and physical damage to produce.
Monitor farmer compliance with quality requirements.
Advise farmers on proper drying, storage and handling of produce where applicable.
Support traceability of produce from the farm to the company's collection or receiving points.
Report any quality concerns or suspected cases of contamination or non-compliance.
Data Collection and Reporting
Collect accurate farmer, farm and production data.
Maintain updated records of farm visits, farmer activities, acreage, crop condition and estimated yields.
Monitor and report estimated crop volumes within the assigned area.
Prepare weekly and monthly field activity reports.
Provide management with information on farmer performance, crop conditions and emerging challenges.
Maintain accurate records of farmer training and extension activities.
Use company-approved digital tools or systems to capture and submit field data.
Farmer Training and Capacity Building
Organize and facilitate farmer training sessions.
Develop practical demonstrations to improve farmer understanding and adoption of recommended practices.
Train farmers on good agricultural practices, food safety, quality and environmental sustainability.
Support awareness programmes on climate-smart agriculture and sustainable farming.
Evaluate farmer understanding and adoption of training recommendations.
Supply and Harvest Coordination
Support the Agriculture/Procurement team in estimating expected crop volumes.
Monitor crop maturity and harvesting timelines.
Communicate expected harvest volumes and timing to relevant departments.
Support coordination between farmers, collection centers and the company.
Identify potential supply gaps and communicate them to management in advance.
Compliance and Sustainability
Promote compliance with applicable agricultural, environmental, food safety and company standards.
Promote responsible use of water, fertilizers and crop protection products.
Encourage environmentally sustainable farming practices.
Support implementation of company sustainability and traceability programmes.
Report any serious cases of non-compliance, unsafe practices or environmental risks.
Other Duties
Participate in agricultural field days, farmer meetings and company events.
Support surveys, research and pilot agricultural projects.
Work closely with Quality, Procurement, Production and other relevant departments.
Perform any other duties as may reasonably be assigned by the supervisor.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
Number of farmers actively supported and monitored.
Number of farm visits conducted against target.
Farmer adoption rate of recommended agricultural practices.
Farmer training sessions conducted.
Accuracy and completeness of farmer and farm records.
Accuracy of estimated crop yields and supply forecasts.
Improvement in farmer productivity and crop quality.
Reduction in rejected or poor-quality produce.
Compliance with company agricultural and quality standards.
Timeliness and quality of field reports.
Farmer satisfaction and engagement levels.
Traceability and documentation compliance
Core Competencies
Strong agricultural and crop production knowledge.
Good farmer engagement and relationship management skills.
Training and facilitation skills.
Good report-writing and documentation skills.
Data collection and analytical skills.
Knowledge of Good Agricultural Practices (GAP).
Knowledge of food safety and quality requirements.
Academic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or Diploma in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agricultural Extension, Crop Production or a related field.
Additional training in agricultural extension, agribusiness, sustainability or related areas will be an added advantage.

With a history spanning over 150 years, Nestlé did not become the world leading food and beverages brand by chance. Monitor plan execution and resolve production exceptions.
Materials Planning and Inventory Management_
Ensure availability of raw, imported bulk and packaging materials to satisfy production requirements.
Manage purchase orders, supplier follow-up and stock cover.
Manage inventory within targets while ensuring supply and minimizing redundancy.
Warehouse and Stakeholder Coordination_
Support warehouse compliance and operational performance.
Collaborate with production, procurement, suppliers and planners.
Support Supply Planner with preparation and hosting the Weekly Production Review
What Will Make You Successful
Bachelor's degree in Production, Supply Chain or related discipline.
Minimum 2 years planning and/or MRP experience.
SAP/APO knowledge and strong Excel skills.
Factory planning experience in FMCG manufacturing required.
Strong numeracy and problem solving skills
Excellent communication and organizational skills

Job Description:
About the role
IDinsight Managers and Senior Managers are dynamic leaders who drive evidence-informed decision-making at scale. These roles provide diverse, high-impact experiences spanning strategic client advisory, technical excellence, team leadership, and organizational growth. We seek intellectually curious, resilient, and team-oriented individuals who, in addition to developing professional and technical skills, are highly motivated to grapple with the difficulties and unpredictability of trying to improve lives at scale.
Managers and Senior Managers are responsible for the following areas of work:
Leading client engagements and building trusted advisor relationships
Overseeing all aspects of client projects to deliver high-quality outputs that drive social impact
Providing strategic counsel and establishing themselves as experts and trusted advisors to senior leaders in governments, foundations, NGOs, and socially impactful businesses
Managing client expectations, navigating complex stakeholder dynamics, and maintaining strong relationships throughout project lifecycles
Driving technical excellence across projects
Directing project teams' technical work and leading evaluation design, research methodology, and analytical approaches tailored to client needs and decision contexts
Engaging internal and external technical experts to strengthen project quality and rigor
Developing a deep understanding of econometrics, data science, field experiment, and qualitative methods to guide appropriate tool selection
Creating and reviewing high-quality deliverables, including policy briefs, technical reports, presentations, and strategic communications that translate evidence into actionable insights
Managing project execution and team coordination
Overseeing project management systems, timelines, budgets, and deliverables to ensure efficient execution
Ensuring quality control throughout all project phases from design through final delivery
Managing full project budgets, strategically allocating resources to maximize impact and efficiency, and anticipating budget risks early and offering solutions to stay on track
Managing project and office-related safety and security risk management for team members
Adapting project plans in response to field realities, client needs, and emerging challenges
Mentoring and developing junior staff
Professionally developing Associates and Senior Associates by providing regular coaching, feedback, and growth opportunities aligned with individual development paths
Building high-performing, cohesive teams that deliver exceptional results
Contributing to organizational growth and development
Contributing to client development and external communications by identifying opportunities, generating ideas, and leading concept note and proposal creation
Contributing to IDinsight's organizational evolution by refining methodologies, piloting new approaches, and improving internal systems
Engaging in knowledge sharing, internal training, and cross-office collaboration
Managers will be staffed on IDinsight projects according to various factors including organizational need, timeline and availability, team dynamics, skills optimization, and professional growth and development. While we aim to factor in individual preferences whenever possible to staffing decisions, they are one of many factors in the project staffing process.

Graduate degree (Master's or PhD) in economics, statistics, public policy, development studies, or related quantitative/social science fields
6-10 years of progressive work experience in international development, research and evaluation, data analytics, consulting, or program management, with demonstrated leadership responsibilities
Knowledge, skills, and abilities
Advanced analytical and methodological expertise, with proven ability to design and oversee rigorous econometric analyses, mixed-methods research strategies, and complex evaluation frameworks
Exceptional writing and communication skills with the ability to synthesize complex technical findings into strategic recommendations for diverse audiences, including executive leadership, donors, and policymakers
Strategic thinking capabilities with demonstrated ability to identify emerging trends, anticipate challenges, and translate organizational priorities into actionable research and programmatic agendas
Proven ability to mentor and develop junior staff, providing technical guidance and building analytical capacity within teams

Strong project and people management skills, with ability to oversee multiple workstreams simultaneously, delegate effectively, and ensure timely delivery of high-quality outputs
Excellent stakeholder management and relationship-building skills, with experience navigating complex partnerships across government agencies, donor organizations, implementing partners, and senior leadership
Demonstrated strategic leadership as a proactive problem-solver who anticipates obstacles, develops innovative solutions, and drives initiatives forward independently
Deeply passionate about combating poverty worldwide and improving lives in disadvantaged populations
Additional preferred qualifications
Fluency in the local language(s) of country placement and/or prior in-country management experience
Track record of peer-reviewed publications, policy influence, or thought leadership in international development
Experience managing budgets, grants, or donor relationships

Job Description:
About the Job
Reporting to the Group Head of Technology, the AI & Data Transformation Lead is the strategic and technical guide of the section, combining deep domain knowledge of reinsurance with expertise in programming, AI usage, business analysis methodologies, and enterprise process transformation and automation.
The AI & Data Transformations Lead will also design and operate secure, reliable, and scalable data platforms that support AAR Insurance Kenya Ltd operations in Kenya and that of its subsidiaries. The role enables claims analytics, fraud detection, regulatory reporting, actuarial analysis, and operational dashboards, while ensuring data quality and compliance.
Duties & Responsibilities
Lead business analysis across all 18+ departments to map current-state processes, identify pain points, design future-state automated workflows and drive their implementation.
Develop and maintain the organization's AI roadmap, including use-case identification, feasibility analysis, and phased deployment.
Engage with external partners, brokers, and technology vendors to benchmark transformation initiatives against global best practice.
Mentor the Transformation Officer and coordinate ICT resource requests (servers, databases, APIs, cloud compute).
Data Quality, Security & Governance:
Implement data quality checks, validation rules, and anomaly detection.
With support from the Systems Administrators, enforce secure data access using IAM, encryption, and role-based controls.
Ensure compliance with Kenya Data Protection Act (2019) and healthcare confidentiality standards.
Assess AI-related risks (model bias, data drift, explainability, regulatory non-compliance) and recommend mitigation controls.
Review and recommend updates to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to accommodate AI-driven decision support and automated processes.
Chair the monthly Data Lock and Backup process, ensuring immutable snapshots are captured at midnight on the last day of each month.

The role is accountable for shaping FSDAi's approach to ESG risk management and impact, ensuring ESG considerations strengthen investment decision-making, portfolio performance and long-term development outcomes, while remaining aligned with evolving market practice, investor expectations and organisational priorities.
As FSDAi's strategic ESG lead, the role provides leadership on complex and high-risk transactions and works across FSDAi and FSD Africa with the Investment, Corporate Risk and Development Impact functions to embed responsible investment practices throughout the investment lifecycle.
The role also strengthens FSDAi's ESG positioning through engagement with governance bodies, funders, co-investors and industry partners, builds ESG capability across the organisation and its partners, and contributes to the continued development of the Gender Lens Investing Strategy and Framework to enhance the organisation's influence and leadership in responsible investment across Africa.

ESG Strategy & Governance

Lead the periodic review and enhancement of FSD Africa's Environmental and Social Performance Management (ESPM) Manual, ESG Policy and exclusion list, ensuring continued alignment with applicable standards, donor requirements and evolving industry best practice.
Lead the continuous improvement of FSDAi's ESPM system against strategic initiatives, including climate finance, nature finance and Gender Lens Investing (GLI).
Benchmark FSDAi's ESG approach against comparable Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) and emerging market practice, recommending enhancements that strengthen the organisation's responsible investment approach.
Monitor emerging ESG macro trends, particularly in climate, nature, biodiversity and gender, assessing their implications for FSDAi's investment approach and ESG system.
Recommend enhancements to the ESPM System that strengthen governance, organisational effectiveness and responsible investment.

Lead ESG due diligence for complex, high-risk and strategically significant investment transactions, providing quality assurance over ESG due diligence undertaken by the ESG team and external consultants.
Review ESG risk categorisation, exclusion list screening, safeguarding assessments and gender lens assessments, ensuring ESG risks and opportunities are appropriately reflected in investment recommendations.
Lead the development of ESG action plans, investment conditions and reporting requirements, ensuring ESG commitments are effectively embedded within investment documentation and transaction implementation.
Present ESG risks, opportunities and recommendations to the Investment Committee, Executive Committee and other governance forums, supporting informed investment decision-making.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
Under the direction of the Deputy Regional Director, the Manager, Disasters, Climate and Crises (DCC) provides strategic leadership and manages the Africa Regional DCC Department, which encompasses three core pillars: (i) Coordination of Operations; (ii) Coordination of Programmes; and (iii) Technical Services, including Anticipatory Action, Climate, Disaster Risk Reduction, Community Engagement and Accountability, Migration and Cash and Voucher Assistance.
The position holds overall responsibility for shaping and driving the strategic vision for disaster, climate and crisis related work across the Africa Region, in close collaboration with Geneva, IFRC Country and Cluster Delegations as well as National Societies. It ensures that IFRC-supported operations and programmes are coherent, high quality, locally anchored and aligned with Strategy 2030, the Renewal and the Africa Unified Plan.
The Manager, DCC, ensures that continental and multi-country programmes and operations are designed to scale, are effectively governed, and are managed with the highest standards of accountability and performance. It guarantees that emergency operations are efficient, timely and impactful, and that National Societies are positioned as first responders through strong preparedness, readiness and surge systems.
The Manager embeds the Ways of Working across all DCC functions—promoting shared leadership, localisation, simplification, evidence-based decision-making and a relentless focus on impact at country level.
In coordination with the IFRC HQ and regional teams, the role positions IFRC Africa as a leading humanitarian and resilience actor on the continent, shaping regional agendas on preparedness, anticipatory action, climate adaptation, migration and integrated resilience.

Strategic Leadership of the DCC Department in the Africa
Lead and manage the DCC Department across its three core pillars:
Coordination of Operations (emergency response, surge, DREF, operational intelligence)
Coordination of Programmes (pan-African and multi-country initiatives)
Technical Services (Anticipatory Action, Climate, DRR, CEA, Migration, CVA)
Provide clear strategic direction, performance management and coherence across these pillars.
Ensure that operational excellence, programmatic scale-up and technical services reinforce each other.

Country/Cluster Delegations and external partners.

Priorities and enablers of the IFRC Strategy 2030 and the five shifts of IFRC Renewal, with a focus on deepening localisation and accountability and sharpening the humanitarian focus. Ensure that pan
African and multi-country programmes and operations are designed for scale, supported by appropriate governance models, and managed in line with IFRC Programme and Project Management (PCM) standards.

Job Description:
Job Summary
Our client is seeking a practical, hands-on, and results-driven Farm Manager to oversee the day-to-day operations of two farms in Kisii, covering both dairy and crop production. The ideal candidate will be responsible for ensuring efficient farm operations, healthy and productive livestock, strong crop yields, proper use of farm inputs, effective supervision of farm workers, and accurate farm records.
The role requires someone who can plan and coordinate activities across both farms, monitor productivity and costs, identify operational issues early, and ensure the farms are run efficiently, safely, and sustainably.
Key Responsibilities
Farm Operations & Planning
Oversee the daily operations of both farms and ensure all planned farm activities are completed on time.
Develop weekly and monthly farm work plans covering dairy, crop production, labour, maintenance, and input requirements.
Coordinate activities between the two farms and ensure proper allocation of labour, equipment, feeds, fertilizer, seeds, chemicals, and other farm inputs.
Monitor farm productivity, operational costs, and resource utilization and recommend practical
improvements.
Maintain accurate daily and monthly farm records and submit regular updates to management.
Dairy Farm Management
Oversee feeding, watering, milking, breeding, housing, hygiene, and general welfare of dairy cattle.
Monitor milk production per cow and maintain accurate milk production and sales records.
Ensure proper feeding programs, feed storage, rationing, and availability of fodder throughout the year.
Coordinate routine animal health activities including vaccinations, deworming, disease prevention, treatment, and veterinary visits.
Maintain breeding, calving, health, medication, and livestock movement records.
Ensure milking areas, equipment, storage containers, and animal housing are kept clean and hygienic.
Crop Production Management
Plan and supervise land preparation, planting, weeding, fertilization, spraying, irrigation where applicable, harvesting, and post-harvest handling.
Prepare seasonal crop plans and ensure planting and harvesting activities are completed within the required timelines.
Monitor crop health, pests, diseases, soil condition, and weather-related risks and take timely corrective action.
Ensure correct application and safe handling of fertilizer, pesticides, herbicides, and other crop inputs.
Track crop yields, losses, input usage, and storage levels and recommend ways to improve production and reduce wastage.
Coordinate production and conservation of fodder crops to support the dairy operation.
Oversee coffee plantation management, including pruning, fertilization, pest and disease control, harvesting, and post-harvest handling.
Farm Staff Supervision
Supervise farm workers across both locations and allocate daily duties based on operational priorities
Monitor attendance, punctuality, productivity, and quality of work and address performance or discipline concerns promptly
Train and guide workers on animal handling, milking hygiene, crop production, equipment use, safety, and good farming practices.
Promote accountability, teamwork, proper use of farm resources, and adherence to farm rules and procedures.
Inventory, Maintenance & Cost Control
Maintain accurate stock records for feeds, veterinary supplies, seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, fuel, tools, and other farm inputs.
Monitor consumption of farm inputs and prevent misuse, loss, theft, and unnecessary wastage.
Coordinate routine servicing and maintenance of farm equipment, machinery, water systems, fencing, sheds, and other farm infrastructure.
Support procurement by identifying farm requirements in advance and verifying deliveries against approved orders.
Track farm expenses and provide management with accurate information to support budgeting and cost control.
Compliance, Safety & Reporting
Ensure the farms operate in line with applicable agricultural, animal welfare, environmental, health, and safety requirements.
Ensure safe storage and use of veterinary medicines, chemicals, farm tools, and protective equipment.
Maintain proper records including livestock registers, crop records, input registers, production reports, sales records, mortality records, and staff attendance.
Prepare weekly and monthly farm performance reports highlighting production, challenges, expenses, losses, and required actions.
Escalate disease outbreaks, major crop losses, equipment breakdowns, security issues, or other significant operational risks immediately.
Qualifications & Experience
Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agribusiness, Animal Science, Dairy Technology, Crop Production, or a related field.
Over 3 years of practical farm management or supervisory experience, preferably involving both dairy and crop farming.
Strong practical knowledge of dairy cattle management, animal nutrition, breeding, milking hygiene, and basic herd health.
Good knowledge of crop production, pest and disease control, input application, harvesting, and post-harvest handling
Experience supervising farm workers and coordinating multiple farm activities at the same time.
Good record-keeping, planning, budgeting, and basic reporting skills.
Ability to identify farm problems early and make practical decisions with minimal supervision.
High integrity, accountability, reliability, and willingness to work hands-on in a farm environment.
